text: Police Squad Lieutenant Frank Drebin is on vacation in Beirut when he disrupts a conference of America's enemies who are trying to conceive a terrorist plan to humiliate the U.S. In Los Angeles, Officer Nordberg attempts to bust a heroin operation run by businessman Vincent Ludwig but is shot by Ludwig's henchmen. Frank returns to LA and is briefed on the case before visiting him in the hospital. Nordberg provides cryptic clues, including a picture of Ludwig's ship, where the deal took place. Frank also learns that Nordberg's jacket tested positive for heroin. Police Squad is put in charge of security for the impending visit of Queen Elizabeth II to Los Angeles, so Frank is given 24 hours to clear Nordberg before the press finds out and detracts from the Queen's arrival. When Frank visits Ludwig to inquire about the ship, he accidentally reveals that Nordberg is still alive. Ludwig asks his assistant Jane, who is unaware of Ludwig's criminal activities, to get close to Frank to see what he knows. She provides Frank with the information he requested and they begin to fall in love. Ludwig meets with Pahpshmir, from the Beirut meeting, to discuss an assassination plot against the Queen. Ludwig agrees to do it for $20 million and explains that he will use a beeper that uses hypnosis to turn anyone into an assassin. Ludwig attempts to have Nordberg killed at the hospital by hypnotizing his doctor, but Frank successfully protects him. The doctor is killed in a comical fashion before Frank can interrogate him. Frank breaks into Ludwig’s office and finds a note confirming his suspicions, but accidentally sets it—and the office—on fire. Frank later confronts Ludwig with his allegations at a reception for the Queen's arrival. He misinterprets Ludwig's presentation of a musket to the Queen as an attack and tries to protect her, but only makes things worse and gets fired from Police Squad. Jane learns the plan will go down at a baseball game, with one of the players as the assassin. She tells Frank, who sneaks in disguised. Police Squad arrives at the stadium after Frank tells them about the plot. Frank knocks the home plate umpire out and takes his place in order to frisk the players for weapons while they are at bat. Ludwig eventually activates his unwitting assassin, Reggie Jackson, using the hypnotic beeper. Jane warns Frank, who tackles Jackson, triggering a bench-clearing brawl that lets him get away. Ludwig holds Jane at gunpoint and begins to leave the stadium while the hypnotized Jackson takes aim at the Queen. Frank tries to tranquilize Jackson, but misses and hits a woman on the upper deck—who falls and lands on Jackson, crushing him and saving the Queen. Frank follows Ludwig to the top of the stadium and shoots him with another dart. Ludwig falls over the side of the stadium and is struck by a passing bus, run over by a steamroller, and finally trampled by a a marching band. Some of the band members inadvertently step on Ludwig's beeper, triggering Jane to attempt to kill Frank. He breaks Jane's hypnosis by confessing his love for her and proposing. Frank is reinstated to Police Squad and a recovered Nordberg congratulates him. Unfortunately, Frank accidentally pushes Nordberg's wheelchair down the stadium stairs and launches him onto the field.

text: Adam Shankman's Stop That Train is a campy action comedy disaster film that blends drag performance with high stakes chaos following two best friends who must save a runaway luxury train headed straight into a deadly storm. The story follows Tess and Dee, two out of work train stewardises who sneak aboard the glamorous Glam Amazonian Express disguised as staff only to find themselves caught in a spiraling disaster. As the train barrels toward Florida, its brakes fail and a massive storm dubbed Stormaganza looms ahead, threatening a catastrophic crash into a nuclear site. At the US train command center, dispatcher Donna Dusk discovers the danger, but struggles to convince her superiors, while President Judy Gagwell reles her own traumatic train past in comedic flashbacks. On board, Tess clashes with rival stewardist Amber while Dee grows closer to co-conductor Cal as they attempt to steer the train through a haunted tunnel to avoid destruction. Chaos escalates with Scorpion bites. Passengers turning against Tess and Dee and Cal's shocking disappearance, leaving the heroins to improvise their way through disaster. The film revels in parody, mixing slapstick gags, musical interludes, and drag queen camp with disaster movie tropes, ultimately delivering a finale where Tess and DD prove themselves as unlikely heroes. With its ensemble cast of drag icons and celebrity cameos, Stop that Train embraces over-the-top silliness while celebrating friendship, resilience, and queer joy, earning praise for turning the disaster genre into a fabulous spectacle. Where Estella is distracting Baroness. Horace gets in the house, whereas Jasper is hacking the cameras Baroness enters with her dogs. Where Estella’s childhood friend has come as a reporter Baroness insults her. Estella then enters as Cruella. She comes in with a dress on fire! It has become a breaking news. Now cruella is back on her job being Estella So she can keep an eye on Baroness. The day of presenting spring collection has come. Everyone’s taking Baroness’ pictures. Estella designs a beautiful dress for Baroness to get in her good books Baroness is impressed but she’s yet busy in her own praises. We see cruella back in senses. She’s in Baroness’ assistant John’s apartment John had saved her. She didn’t want anything come in front of her because she was a self-obsessed lady She ordered John to kill Estella but John couldn’t do it. Because she considers her, her mother and love her so much. She’ll now show it to Baroness that what true craziness is. Estella goes and saves Horace and Jasper from Police’s custody. She’s distracting Police Whereas she sends dog with the key. Estella shares the truth with them And convinces them once again for help by emotionally saying that they’re her only family She then goes to Artie who’s already ready for Estella’s help. They’re working on a new plan at John’s home. Whereas Baroness is preparing for her annual party In which she had killed Catherine. Inspector reaches there and tells her that they didn’t find Cruella Baroness is now anxious. Estella and her team including John, send costumes to Baroness’ guests They’re exactly like Estella’s dress. Saying, that they all should come wearing it in the memory of Cruella Cruella has called police at Baroness’ house as well. Baroness’ guards are attacking at every guest Baroness is shocked to see everyone in the same dress and gets scared as well Jasper has called all the guards to the library. Where Horace has locked them down Cruella reaches Baroness in the party and takes the whistle from her hand by poking a needle She then reaches the same cliff, being Estella. Form where baroness had pushed Catherine She whistles and calls the dogs. Baroness reaches there too Jasper, Artie, and John say that Baroness’ is calling all the guests outside. होती है और सबसे कहती है, मैंने ही उसे आने के लिए कहा था। मून फेस वह तुम्हारे लिए एक तोहफा भी लेकर आई है। फ्रैन भी जो खिलौना लाई थी उसे दिखाती है तो वह उसे बहुत पसंद आ जाता है। वह उसके साथ खेलने लगता है और उसे वहीं रहने की इजाजत दे देता है। इसके बाद सिल्की अपने दोस्त सॉस्पैन से मिलवाती है। उसे खाना पकाने के बर्तनों से कपड़े पहनना बहुत पसंद है। इसके बाद वे स्वर्ग जैसी दिखने वाली इस पेड़ की दुनिया को दिखाने लगते हैं। तभी एक महिला कपड़े धोने का पानी नीचे फेंकती है। सिल्की के एक और दोस्त भाट्स [संगीत] हिज नेम से भी परिचय कराया जाता है। दरअसल वह अपना नाम ही भूल गया है। इसलिए उसका नाम वाट्स हिज नेम रख दिया गया है। इसके बाद वे ऊपर आते हैं। कपड़े धोने वाली इस महिला का नाम स्टेसी है। सच कहा जाए तो इस दुनिया में कई सारे साम्राज्य हैं। हर दिन अलग-अलग साम्राज्य में जाया जा सकता है। उन साम्राज्यों के बारे में स्टेसी बहुत अच्छी तरह जानती है। इसके बाद वे एक साम्राज्य में जाने के लिए गाना चलाकर नाचते हुए एक [संगीत] विशाल सीढ़ी दिखाते हैं। फ्रैन भी उनके साथ सीढ़ी पर चढ़ने लगती है। वे जिस साम्राज्य में जा रहे हैं, उसका नाम पान लैंड ऑफ द गुडीज है। वे इस साम्राज्य में जैसे ही प्रवेश करते हैं एक गार्ड कहता है कोई भी लालच मत करना क्योंकि इस साम्राज्य में जहां भी [संगीत] देखो सिर्फ चॉकलेट और कैंडीज ही उसके पास आकर कहता है फोन की बैटरी खत्म हो गई है। अब क्या करूं? तब टिम्मी कहता है बाहर जाकर बच्चों के साथ खेलो। ठीक उसी समय टिम्मी को याद आता है कि फ्रैन सुबह से घर ही नहीं आई है। इधर लैंड ऑफ द गुडीज मार्शमेलो उसके हाथ को जकड़ लेते हैं। तब गार्ड कहता है, मैंने तो कहा था लालच मत करना। इधर टिम्मी और पॉली फ्रैन को हर जगह ढूंढ रहे होते हैं। इसके बाद सिल्की [संगीत] और उसकी टीम आकर बड़ी मुश्किल से फ्रैन को बचाकर सुरक्षित वहां से नीचे ले आती है। जिसके बाद तैयार हो जाओ कहकर उसे एक छेद के अंदर भेज देते हैं। वह भी रोलर कोस्टर की तरह मजे करते हुए पेड़ से नीचे उतर आती है। यहां टिम्मी और पॉली बहुत चिंता में पड़ गए थे। चाहे जो हो जाए फ्रैन को ढूंढना ही होगा। वे यही कोशिश कर रहे थे। ठीक उसी समय फ्रैन के वापस आने से उनमें जैसे फिर से जान आ जाती है। कहां गई थी? पूछने पर उसके साथ जो कुछ हुआ वह सब बता देती है। इसलिए वे कहते हैं इसके बाद से तुम अगर कहीं भी जाना चाहोगी तो बेथ और जो को भी साथ लेकर जाना। फ्रैंक की इन बातों पर वे ज्यादा ध्यान नहीं देते। उसने जो बात की उसी से वे बहुत खुश हो जाते हैं। इसके बाद टिम्मी किसानों की तरह जीवन जीने लगता है। यह उसे बहुत पसंद आने लगता है। उसके इस हर काम में पॉली उसकी [संगीत] मदद करती है। वे दोनों मिलकर बहुत खुशी-खुशी टमाटर की खेती करने की तैयारी करने लगते हैं। हां, टमाटर की खेती करके ही वे अपना जीवन बिताएंगे। ऐसा उन्होंने सोचा है। लेकिन बेथ को यह सब बिल्कुल पसंद नहीं है। वह अपनी नानी यानी पॉली की मां को एक चिट्ठी लिखती है। हम सभी गांव में फंस गए हैं। आकर ले जाओ। इसके बाद हमें बेथ की नानी को दिखाया जाता है। वह बहुत अमीर है। बेथ की लिखी चिट्ठी उसके पास पहुंच जाती है। इन सबके बीच फ्रैन बेथ से गुजारिश करती है। मेरे साथ जंगल में चलो। वह भी राजी हो जाती है। फ्रैन जो और बेथ को लेकर जंगल में प्रवेश करती है। फिर पार अवे ट्री के पास आकर कहती है। आंखें बंद करके तीन बार कहो मैं जादू में विश्वास करती हूं। उन्हें इन सब बातों पर भरोसा नहीं था। फिर भी वे आंखें बंद करके लापरवाही से ठीक है कह देते हैं। ऐसा कहते ही उनकी आंखों के सामने जो जादू होता है उस पर वे खुद विश्वास [संगीत] नहीं कर पाते। पहले की तरह ही इस बार भी तीन तकिए आते हैं। वे तीनों बैठते ही तकिए उन्हें ऊपर ले जाते हैं। पहले वे पिक्सी को [संगीत] देखते हैं। इसके बाद फ्रैन उन दोनों को अपने दोस्तों के पास ले जाकर उनसे मिलवाती है। वे सभी उन दोनों को दोस्त के रूप में अपना लेते हैं। तभी सिल्की वहां आकर बेथ को देखकर उसे अपनी बहुत करीबी दोस्त बनाना चाहती है। लेकिन बेथ को यह पसंद नहीं आता। ठीक उसी समय स्टेसी [संगीत] गलती से ऊपर से उस पर पानी डाल देती है। जिसके बाद आज अनलैंड ऑफ द बर्थडे बी नाम के एक साम्राज्य नाम के जीव रहते [संगीत] हैं। वे कहते रहते हैं इस जगह पर तुम जो भी मांगोगे वह पूरा हो जाएगा। इसे आजमाने के लिए सॉस पैन कहता है, मैं साधारण कपड़ों में रहना चाहता हूं और तुरंत ही उसके बर्तनों वाले कपड़े गायब हो जाते हैं। इसके [संगीत] बाद जो भी कहता है, मैं गेम का कैरेक्टर बनना चाहता हूं, वह भी ठीक उसी तरह एक गेम के कैरेक्टर [संगीत] या खिलौने में बदल जाता है। इसी तरह सिल्की भी कहती है, मैं एक बहुत ही सुंदर परी बनना चाहती हूं। वह भी छोटे पंखों वाली एक बहुत सुंदर परी बन जाती है। उसी तरह फ्रैन भी कहती है, "मुझे अपनी आवाज पसंद नहीं है। मुझे दूसरी आवाज चाहिए।" देखा जाए तो उसकी आवाज आदमियों जैसी हो जाती देखती है कि वे लोग अभी तक वापस नहीं आए हैं तो वह भी जाने लगती है। स्टेसी कहती है मैंने कपड़े धोए हैं। यह एल्फ लोगों को दे देना। यह कहकर वह कपड़े उसके हाथ में दे देती है। वह भी सीढ़ियां चढ़ते-चढ़ते एल्फ कहते हैं यहां बेसमेंट में एक आदमी है। उसके पास जाओ। वह तुम्हारी मदद करेगा। वे सभी बेसमेंट में आते हैं। यहां बूम बूम नाम का एक आदमी रहता है। वह छोटी परी बनी सिल्की को देखकर बहुत खुश होता है और सभी पहले की तरह नॉर्मल हो जाएंगे। लेकिन वह एक शर्त रखता है। तुम सबको अंदर भेजने के लिए मुझे वह परी चाहिए यानी सिल्की। कोई भी इसके लिए राजी नहीं होता। तब वह कहता है परी मेरे लिए नहीं है। क्रिसमस के दिन सबके लिए तोहफे लाने वाले सांता क्लॉज़ को परी देने का मैंने वादा किया था। उनके लिए है। अभी भी कोई तैयार नहीं हो रहा था। लेकिन सिल्की सबको नॉर्मल करने के लिए खुद को सांता क्लॉज़ के पास भेजने के लिए तैयार हो जाती है। सबका बहुत मन उदास हो जाता है। इसके बाद वे सभी ठीक है कहकर राजी हो जाते हैं। इस दरवाजे के अंदर आते ही एक-एक करके सब नॉर्मल होने लगते हैं। लेकिन यहां देखा जाए तो वह सिल्की को सांता क्लॉज़ के पास नहीं भेज रहा है। वो जो स्टेसी ने बेथ को बताया था ना कि एक साम्राज्य में नहीं जाना चाहिए। वहां डम स्नेप नाम की बुरी रानी रहती है। वह सिल्की को उसी के पास भेजने की तैयारी कर रहा था। यह बात बेथ को text: It all starts with a little kid named Steve, who shows us the wild world of Minecraft. The story begins in the Overworld—a huge land full of blocks, animals, and endless adventures. Even as a child, Steve dreamed of being the best miner ever. He loved building, digging, and discovering new things. But every time he tried to enter the local mine, a grumpy old man stopped him. The rule was clear: kids weren’t allowed, only adults. Years passed, and Steve finally grew up. But life didn’t go the way he wanted. He ended up working a boring job—selling door knobs. Every day felt the same, and he felt like his dream was slipping away. One day, while eating lunch alone, he remembered that dream. Something inside him sparked. He decided to go back to the mine. This time, he wouldn't let anything stop him. The old man was still there, but Steve pushed past and began digging like crazy. Deep in the mine, he found two strange cubes: a crystal cube and the creation cube. When he put them together a portal opened to a magical world: the Overworld. There, he met a pink sheep. Using its wool, he built three amazing houses and started living the life he always wanted. One day, a wild wolf tried to attack him. Steve gave it a juicy bone and made it his friend. He named the wolf Dennis. From then on, they were best buddies. Together, they built cool things, made peace with animals, and created a beautiful world. Time passed. Steve kept building and exploring. One day, he found some old ruins. Inside a chest, he discovered another portal—this one led to a dark place called the Nether. It was full of mean pig-like creatures called piglins, who followed an evil sorceress named Malgoia. Malgoia had a sad past. She wanted to be a dancer, but her people laughed at her and kicked her out. Angry and hurt, she turned mean and now wanted the creation cube to control all worlds. Steve escaped with the orb and gave it to Dennis. He told him to hide it where no one would ever find it. Dennis ran across worlds and buried it under Steve’s water bed. The main world was safe… for now. Years later, a young guy named Garrett Garrison became super famous for starring in a video game. He was called “The Trash Man” because he could throw garbage with perfect aim. He got rich and had it all—until he suddenly got evicted. Just like that, he lost everything. Broke and desperate, Garrett went to an auction to find something he could sell. But Auction manager told him about a strange artifact that might be valuable. He bought it for $900, hoping to sell it for cash. But when he opened the box, it looked empty. He thought he got scammed and slammed it shut—without realizing the creation cube was hidden inside. Later, we meet Henry and his big sister Natalie. Their mom had passed away, and they had just moved to the city. Natalie got a small job to pay rent, and a kind real estate agent named Dawn helped them settle in. The next morning, Natalie made pizza for Henry to take to school and even gave him cologne as a gift. Henry didn’t say much—he was still sad and nervous. While walking, he stopped by Garrett’s shop. He offered him a slice of pizza for advice. Garrett, always joking, said he charged $50 an hour for life lessons. When Garrett tries to explain Henry ignores him and leaves to school. There, the Vice principal told him about her sad marriage and gave him a name tag. In class, the sarcastic teacher asks them to draw a Banana and an apple . But Henry tries to draw a rocket with those, teacher scolds him, Seeing this Henry’s classmate make fun off him, To prove it Henry starts building a rocket. But Henry messed up while helping with a jetpack model, and it went flying out of control—crashing into the building where Natalie worked! The principal called for Henry’s guardian. Henry panicked and called Garrett, asking him to pretend to be his uncle. Garrett agreed—for $26 in cash. Garrett saved Henry from the principal, and the two of them went to Garrett’s shop. While they were there, Henry saw a strange cube on a table and asked what it was. Garrett said he wasn’t sure. There was a note on a page nearby. It clearly said: “Do not combine the cubes.” But Garrett and Henry didn’t listen. Curious, they went to an old mine to test it. At the same time, Natalie realized Henry was missing and asked Dawn for help. Dawn tracked his phone, and they rushed to the mine. When they got there, the cube was glowing. It pulled Henry in. Natalie and Dawn grabbed him—and all of them got sucked into the portal! Now in the Overworld, Garrett bragged about being a game legend. They met the pink sheep, but also noticed a villager had followed them through the portal, crossing into Earth. Back in the Nether, Malgoia was angry. Her piglins couldn’t find gold, and she threatened to turn them into pork chops. Suddenly, she felt a signal—the orb was active again. She visited Steve, who was still her prisoner. She offered him a deal: give back the orb, or Dennis would suffer. In the Overworld, Garrett was trying to impress the pink sheep, but it soon turned to night. Suddenly, Dennis showed up, growling. The sheep got scared and ran away. Then monsters started to come—skeletons, spiders, zombies, and creepers! Everyone ran. Henry stayed calm and started building defenses. Garrett hid—until a creeper exploded near him. He screamed, giving away his spot. The pink sheep was captured. Just in time, Steve arrived and saved them all with amazing skill. When the sun rose, the zombies burned away. Steve told them he needed the Orb of Dominion. He said he would help them get home—but he would keep the orb. They had a problem: the crystal cube was missing. Without it, there was no way back. They had to find it or try another way. Meanwhile, the group found a peaceful village with nice villagers, a wise llama, a strong iron golem, and a legendary pig. They ate roast chicken to relax. Steve warned them it was cooked over lava—still super hot. Garrett ate it anyway to show off. In the Nether, Malgoia had had enough. She called her strongest general—Chungus, a powerful but kind piglin. She gave him a magic nether wart to keep him safe from turning into bacon. His mission: get the orb, no matter what. Back in the Overworld, the group headed to the mansion. They found Steve’s magic inventory full of tools and gear. Garrett used the Ender Pearl (without knowing it was the last one). Steve showed them how to craft tools. Garrett made a weird one, but it kind of worked. Henry made a gadget using real-world stuff and Minecraft blocks. Garrett later asked Steve about a hidden message he found in the orb. Steve admitted he had diamonds, but they were deep in a mine. So, off to the mine they went. But just before they left Piglins attacked. General Chungus met Steve and introduced himself politely—but with a serious tone. Steve tried to lead, but Garrett jumped in, trying to be a hero. He missed his attack and hit Steve instead. Chungus didn’t even flinch. A big fight broke out. The group got split up—Natalie and Dawn went one way, Garrett and Henry went another. Before they ran, they all agreed to meet again at the mansion. To help everyone escape, Steve handed out some flying wings—but he only had two pairs. So, in a surprise move, he tackled Garrett and took off, flying through the sky together. Next came a crazy air chase. They flew through walls, dodged attacks, and escaped from the piglin army. Finally, Steve and Garrett used their water-drop move and splashed safely into a lake—completely unharmed. Back on Earth, the villager who crossed through the portal got hit by the principal’s car. She panicked and invited him to dinner to avoid a lawsuit. Meanwhile, in the Overworld, Steve talked about Malgoia. Long ago, she wanted to be a dancer. She was amazing—her moves were beautiful. But her father didn’t like it and kicked her out. After that, she gave up on anything creative. Now, if she gets the orb, she’ll destroy the Overworld and everyone in it. But Steve was torn—he needed the orb to save his beloved wolf, Dennis, who was still trapped by Malgoia. Back in the Nether, Malgoia was angry. Chungus had failed her, and she was done being patient. She released her most powerful weapon: the Great Pig—a huge beast with a new brain. It woke up in a rage and crushed General Chungus in one stomp. Elsewhere, Natalie and the real estate agent, Dawn, met someone surprising: Dennis, Steve’s wolf. Dawn offered him a bone, and he trusted her. Knowing he belonged to Steve, the girls decided to follow him. Underground, the guys finally found the diamond cave. But Steve smelled something awful—it was nether wart. That could only mean one thing: the Great Pig had arrived. Steve told the others to head to the safe room. They jumped in minecarts and took off. But right when they needed power, the redstone ran out. The carts stopped in front of their creeper farm. Then the Great Pig showed up—angry and roaring. With no way out, Steve and Garrett made a bold choice—they activated all the creepers. The explosion shook everything. They made it out alive—but just barely. Afterward, Henry yelled at Garrett for losing the diamonds. Garrett went quiet. Back on Earth, the school principal was on a surprise date with the villager she had hit with her jeep. Over dinner, she shared that she was recently divorced—her ex-husband just didn’t have a personality. Then they started planning a mansion break-in. Steve said the mansion had three levels: First, strong villagers who were trained to fight. Next, evokers—dark wizards who could summon monsters. And at the top, the Enderman crystal, guarded by the Enderman himself—a quiet but dangerous protector. Before they could act, the villagers captured the adults and threw them into an underground fight club. Garrett got pushed into the ring. His opponent? A tiny zombie riding a fierce chicken. It looked silly but fought like crazy. At the same time, Henry snuck to the top floor and met Enderman. It was dark, creepy—and they had to battle. But Henry won. His prize? A teleportation sphere. It lets him jump across the world instantly. After escaping the mansion, the group ran into Malgoia. She used her magic to take the creation cube and the Enderman crystal. Then she disappeared into the Nether. Steve and Henry tried to run. Steve set off a huge explosion—his last chance to stop Malgoia. The blast threw everyone in different directions. Steve woke up because Dennis helped him. Henry was hurt but still alive. Not far away, they saw a small mushroom house—Dawn had built it as a safe place to rest. Reunited with Natalie and Dawn, they saw how bad things had gotten. Malgoia’s darkness was spreading fast. It was time to fight back. They made stronger tools. Henry upgraded the iron golems with speed boosters. Now they had a fast, powerful army. The war began. Malgoia sent out the Great Pig again. But the heroes had their own secret weapon: a giant golem made from a super-strong metal. The two monsters battled, shaking the whole world. Steve faced Malgoia in diamond armor with a massive sword. She used dark magic, but he stood strong. Elsewhere, Henry fought toward the orb. Natalie got trapped. The Great Pig charged her. Then Dawn appeared, standing tall with a pack of wild wolves. She whistled, and the wolves attacked the pig in a furious battle. But then, the Great Pig blasted Henry with a powerful beam. He fell. Everything went quiet—until Garrett returned. He rushed in, grabbed Henry, and pulled him to safety. With their last bit of strength, the heroes worked together. They destroyed Malgoia’s machines and threw the orb into the abyss. Light came back. The Overworld was healing. But then, the Great Pig caught the orb. Hope faded—until the ultimate golem landed one final blow, smashing the beast and taking back the orb. Now came the final fight. Steve stood in front of Malgoia. She was weak. She tried to fool him three times, but Steve stopped every attack. In the end, he didn’t hurt her. He turned and walked away, leaving her to live with her loss. With peace restored, Steve said goodbye to his friends. He asked Henry to stay in the Overworld, but Henry smiled and said he was going home. Steve nodded and gave Dennis to Dawn. He hugged Garrett, thanked Natalie and Dawn, and watched them walk through the portal. Then Steve turned, took a deep breath—and stepped through the portal to Earth. Days later, everything changed. Garrett's shop was booming. He became a business and gaming pro. The whole group made a new video game based on their adventure. Life was awesome. Dawn stopped working in real estate and started going on adventures full-time with Dennis by her side. Natalie opened a self-defense school and became a hero in her town. Henry? He finally built his jetpack and flew across the skies—living his dream. At the end Turns out the villager and the principal fell in love. Now he speaks human, and she speaks villager. One night, he got down on one knee and asked her to marry him. She said yes.

text: Nocturnal recaps here. Today, I'm going to tell you about a 2023 tragicomedy called "Poor Things". An eccentric surgeon transplants the brain of an unborn child into the body of her dead mother. Fate had brought me a dead body and alive infant. It was obvious A girl in a blue dress stands on the edge of a bridge and then goes into free fall. The picture turns black and white, and we are transferred to a piano. A girl named Bella Baxter awkwardly taps the keys with her hands and feet while a man with a disfigured face named Godwin Baxter watches her. At lunch, Bella eats with her hands and spits out unpalatable food like a spoiled child. Finished with the meal Godwin kisses the girl on the forehead and goes to work. Bella sees Godwin off, awkwardly following him and calling him Papa. Godwin, being one of the best surgeons in London, passes on his knowledge to his students, most of whom are much more interested in the teacher's appearance than in his lessons. Only a young student named Max admires the hereditary surgeon whose father built the place. Godwin notices Max's diligence and invites him to become his assistant in one project. Back at the house, in which Bella is entertained by breaking dishes, the girl joyfully jumps on Godwin, after which punches Max in the nose instead of shaking hands. Seeing Max's misunderstanding, Godwin explains that the girl is now recovering from a brain injury and despite her age, her developmental level is now at the level of a two-year-old. Godwin suggests that Max observe Bella and note her progress, to which Max eagerly agrees. The next day, Max follows Bella relentlessly, noting down everything she does, from what she ate to how many words she learned today. One day, while reading Bella a bedtime story, Godwin tells her that he took her in after her parents died in South America. This sparks the girl's interest in the outside world, and she eagerly looks at maps in Max's company. Wanting more, Bella climbs the stairs to look out over the city. Impressed by what she sees, Bella throws Godwin a tantrum, demanding to go for a walk and he reluctantly agrees. They travel to the countryside in a mechanical carriage where Bella wallows in leaves, having never seen anything like it before. As they sit down for a picnic, Godwin tells them why his body is so disfigured. It turns out that his father often did experiments on little Godwin, trying to figure out exactly how the human body works. On the way home, Bella wants to take another walk in the city, and being refused attacks the doctor, but he quickly calms her down with the help of chloroform. Having put the girl to bed, Max searches the doctor's office and finds papers about the experiment on Bella. Deciding that there is no point in hiding, Godwin tells everything. One day he found the body of a pregnant woman on the riverbank. Taking a chance, he transplanted the brain of a still-living child into the mother's body and reanimated this creature. That's why Bella is acting like a child. The next day Bella finally discovers the delights of puberty and even tries to comfort the maid in this way, but Max explains that it is immoral. A little later, Godwin and Max discuss the incident and the doctor suggests that Max take Bella as his wife. Max is surprised, as he thought the doctor had kept Bella for himself, but Godwin reveals that his reproductive system has also suffered from his father's experiments and his feelings for Bella are rather paternal. Max proposes to Bella and she, excited by the promise of touching each other after marriage, accepts. To draw up the paperwork, Godwin invites a lawyer named Duncan Wedderburn into the house. While the doctor reads the prenup, Duncan, under the guise of going to the bathroom, begins prowling around the house looking for the bride. Being an inveterate heartbreaker, Duncan quickly charms the naive girl. That same night, he sneaks onto Bella's balcony and proposes to meet on the roof. There he cleverly manipulates the girl, promising to free her from that house and take her on a trip. Bella immediately goes down to Godwin and informs him that she will soon run away. The doctor tries to talk the girl out of it, but she is adamant. When she is packing for the trip, Max enters the room and says that he will not let her go anywhere, but Bella calms him down with a handkerchief with chloroform. Soon Godwin appears and sews rainy day money into the hem of her dress, then kisses her on the forehead and lets her go. The story gets colorful again and moves to Lisbon. There, Bella and Duncan go to restaurants where Bella tastes gourmet delicacies for the first time in her life, but most of the time they engage in what she calls furious jumps. One day, when Duncan, tired from his furious jumping, has fallen asleep, Bella goes out into the city where she admires it with great delight. Having relieved her stomach from an overdose of pastries, she returns to the hotel. Meanwhile, concerned about Bella's disappearance, Duncan paces nervously around the room, and when she returns, he asks her not to go anywhere alone again. The couple goes to a restaurant to meet Duncan's clients. Bella embarrasses Duncan in every possible way, spitting out food and trying to punch a screaming child at a neighboring table. Duncan has to take the girl aside and explain how to behave. Back at the hotel, they are met in the lobby by a lady who calls the girl Victoria, but Bella says she's mistaken. The next day, the couple goes to a restaurant again, where Bella, hearing music for the first time, goes into a frenzied dance. Duncan joins her and the dance quickly turns into a fight because another man has winked at Bella. Back at the hotel, Duncan notices some man's signature on the girl's thighs and realizes that Bella has run away again. The man realizes that he can't contain her unbridled temper, so he comes up with a plan. In the morning he suggests playing a game in which Bella needs to hide in a trunk, but a few hours later she finds herself on a cruise ship, from which Bella can no longer run away. Meanwhile, in London, Godwin falls unconscious at one of the lectures. Waking up, he lies that he had to much alcohol last night and knowing that his time is running out he asks Max to find a body. Together with Max, they revive another girl named Felicity, but her development is much slower than Bella's. Still resentful of Duncan for kidnapping her, Bella no longer wants to do furious jumps and immerses herself in reading, gradually gaining new words and knowledge. She meets two passengers a straightforward woman named Martha and a hardened cynic named Harry. Bella tells them about Duncan and how she sometimes wants to throw him overboard but Their conversation is interrupted by Duncan himself who leads Bella away. He proposes marriage to the girl, but she reminds him that she is already engaged to Max. Bella spends more and more time with new acquaintances discussing complex philosophical issues, which clearly does not like Duncan. Unhappy that the girl is no longer that naive silly girl, he throws her books overboard, but realizing that it is useless, goes to the casino. At one point Duncan even tries to theatrically throw Martha overboard, but he is quickly stopped. Troubled by philosophical ideas, the girl heads to Harry's room, where she questions his thesis that all humans are just cruel animals. Harry does not argue with her, but instead only suggests a walk in Alexandria. There, from the balcony of a posh restaurant, he shows her a poor area, where people are starving to death. Having suffered the first psychological trauma of her life, Bella is about to jump down the stairs to these people, but the man stops her. When she returns to the ship, she sees a dead drunk Duncan, who has won a large sum of money at the casino. Bella quickly collects the money to give it to charity, but on the way out she is stopped by sailors who inform her that the ship is leaving. They promise to give the money to the poor, and the girl naively believes them. Back in the cabin, Bella reports that she has given all the money to the needy, which infuriates the man. Soon the captain arrives, who learns that they are penniless, and tells them to disembark at the nearest port. They are dropped off in Paris and Bella, unused to thinking about where the money comes from, volunteers to look for a hotel where they will be allowed to stay for free. The search leads her to a brothel where the elderly lady offers her to earn some coins and Bella agrees. After receiving the money and the disappointment that not all men are as skilled in bed as Duncan, she returns to him with a bag of eclairs. Upon learning how this pastries were earned, he becomes enraged and says it's the worst thing she could have ever done. Convinced that Duncan does not share her thirst for experimentation, the girl takes out her father's money to buy him a ticket home, but Duncan grabs the money and leaves. After some thought, Bella returns to the brothel with the firm intention to get a job there. She is happily accepted there and Bella begins her path of becoming a courtesan. In between serving monks and one-armed men, Bella visits the anatomical theater to study medicine. During one of these visits, she meets Duncan, who tearfully begs her to return, but the girl drives him away. Meanwhile, in London, Godwin asks Max to perform surgery on him. Max finds the doctor has an inoperable tumor and Godwin, realizing that his days are numbered, asks him to find Bella. The search leads him to Duncan, who after a short speech that Bella is the devil in the flesh, tells him about the girl's location. After receiving the letter Bella returns to London. She immediately asks Godwin how she got her C-section and where her baby is. Godwin admits what he did to her body and her baby that day. Hearing this leads Bella into an existential crisis, from which she is brought out by Max with a proposal to marry him. A few days later Godwin walks the girl down the aisle, but suddenly a man enters the church, who introduces himself as General Alfie and declares that Bella is his wife Victoria Blessington. He demands the girl to stop fooling around and return home and Bella, determined to find out about her past life, agrees. The strangeness begins on the drive up to the house, the General pulls out a gun, saying that the servants could start a riot at any moment. At dinner, the General reveals that they shared a love of cruelty, but Victoria hated the child she was carrying for him. Having learned that Bella worked as a prostitute, he notes that the girl has always had a huge libido, but he will soon take care of it. text: Colin, a painfully shy man, lives a life so quiet it almost feels invisible. He still lives with his parents in suburban London, works a dull job handing out parking tickets, and spends his evening singing in a barberh shop quartet. His routine is safe, predictable, and painfully small. Colin is the kind of person who avoids eye contact with strangers and apologizes even when he has done nothing wrong. But beneath all that timidity is someone who secretly longs for something bigger, something dangerous, something that makes him feel alive. That change arrives in the form of Rey. Rey is the complete opposite of Colin. Tall, confident, dressed head to toe in worn leather, Ry carries himself with the kind of quiet authority that immediately commands attention. When Colin first notices him at a pub, he cannot stop staring. Ray seems like someone from another world entirely, the kind of man who lives boldly while Colin watches from the sidelines. Then something unexpected happens. Ray slips Colin a small note. No conversation, no explanation, just a time and place written on a piece of paper. For someone as timid as Colin, the gesture feels electrifying. It is mysterious and terrifying at the same time. He debates whether to go. His mind keeps telling him it is ridiculous, that he should forget about it and return to his normal life. But curiosity wins. On Christmas Day, Colin nervously follows the instructions on the note and meets Ry in a quiet alleyway. The encounter that follows is awkward and intense, leaving Colin completely offbalance. Rey barely explains anything. He simply takes control of the situation with a confidence that Colin has never experienced before. And just as quickly as the moment begins, it ends. Ry tells Colin that he probably will not see him again. For Colin, the experience feels like a strange dream that vanished the moment he woke up. Days pass, then weeks. Colin cannot stop thinking about Rey. The memory of that brief encounter lingers in his mind, pulling him toward a life he never imagined for himself. Eventually, he gathers the courage to send Rey a message. But there is no reply. For a long time, nothing happens. And just when Colin begins to believe the whole thing is over, Rey finally responds. This time, the invitation is different. Rey asks Colin to come to his apartment. When Colin arrives, he quickly realizes that Rey lives by very specific rules. Their relationship will not be a typical romance. Ry explains that he prefers a strict, dominant, and submissive dynamic. He makes the rules. Colin follows them. At first, the arrangement shocks Colin. Ry expects him to cook, clean, run errands, and organize his apartment. Colin is even told that he will sleep on the floor beside Ray's bed instead of sharing it. But strangely, Colin does not walk away. In fact, something inside him begins to awaken. For the first time in his life, someone is paying attention to him. Even though Ray's world is intense and controlled, Colin feels a strange sense of belonging. The structure, the rules, the certainty of knowing exactly what Rey expects from him. All of it gives Colin a sense of purpose he never had before. Slowly, Colin begins to change. He shaves his head. He starts wearing leather. His timid posture begins to disappear. The quiet man who once hid in the background is starting to become someone new. His rules remain strict and sometimes emotionally distant. While Colin grows more attached to Rey, he begins to wonder whether Rey sees him as a partner or simply as someone who exists to serve him. That uncertainty slowly builds tension between them. Colin starts questioning parts of the relationship that once excited him. The dynamic that once felt thrilling now sometimes feels isolating. Because beneath the leather jackets, the motorcycles, and the strict rules, what Colin and Ray are really searching for is the same thing everyone wants. Connection, understanding, and the courage to be seen exactly as they are. The story of Pillion is not just about an unusual relationship. text: Last breath opens by introducing the role of a saturation diver whose primary job is to maintain underwater pipelines, a profession considered one of the most dangerous in the world. The scene then shifts to Chris Lemons, who is listening to a radio report about an approaching storm set to hit Aberdine, Scotland. Chris, a rookie but talented diver who works at BBby Offshore, informs his fianceé, Morag, that he will be away for a month, having been selected as a saturation diver. Morag is uneasy about his job, knowing the risks involved. To reassure her, Chris insists that he will be fine. At Aberdine Harbor, Chris boards the dive support vessel DSV and is greeted by his superior Craig and fellow diver Duncan, who mentions that they will have a new captain this time. As the crew prepares the ship to sail, Craig briefs them on their mission. He explains that they will be living in what he calls a tin can, a pressurized living chamber, for 28 days. They will be pressurized to 300 ft, about 90 m, where they will work on replacing a section of the gas pipeline. Once the job is complete, they will undergo a 4-day decompression process before returning to normal atmospheric pressure. Craig divides the crew into three teams. Chris, Duncan, and a seasoned diver named Dave are assigned to team A. Chris has heard of Dave's exceptional reputation, but has never worked with him personally. Dave, however, seems distant. Duncan, goodnatured as always, teases Dave for acting standoffish around Chris. Dave, always focused on work, questions Chris's track record. Duncan vouches for him, explaining that Chris worked as a deckhand for 3 years before getting a shot as a diver. Since then, he has completed five dives alongside Duncan. Later, as the team settles into their bunks, Dave notices Chris placing a photo of Morag beside his bed. Offering his advice, Dave tells Chris that once he's in the water, he needs to stay focused and not let thoughts of the outside world distract him. Duncan, however, reassures Chris, playfully, mentioning that Dave himself is a softy with two kids. With all teams accounted for, their chamber doors are sealed, and Craig initiates the gas pressurization process. Meanwhile, the boat heads toward the Huntington oil field. The crew monitors the operation and Craig turns off the gas compression. Over the radio, Craig reminds the team not to leave the chamber before decompression, warning that the gas saturating their bodies could cause severe injury. Duncan jokes that he says that every time. During a quiet meal, Duncan reveals that he was let go by Bby offshore. To lighten the mood, Dave jokes that their job will probably be fully automated in 10 years. Chris suggests Duncan should go into management like Craig, but Duncan says he isn't interested. He tells Dave honestly that he's a good diver and doesn't need him anymore. Early the next morning, Chris receives a video message from Morag detailing their wedding plans and telling him to have fun with Duncan. After giving the boat coordinates to the marine control, the captain is informed that the approaching storm may be stronger than expected. Craig reassures him that they are in the North Sea, far from the storm's impact zone. Once the dynamic positioning system, DPS, is confirmed active, allowing the ship to hold position without an anchor, the captain gives Craig the go-ahad to start the dive operation. Craig informs the team and they begin dawning their diving suits, complete with flares, a knife, and a compass for extra precautions. Before entering the diving bell, Dave tells Chris to be careful and follow his lead. Team A reaches the diving bell, which slowly descends to 300 ft. Upon arrival, Craig announces they have reached depth. Duncan connects Dave's helmet to an umbilical cord, which supplies his oxygen and communications, and secures it onto his head. Dave then dives into the water with Chris following shortly after. However, as Chris submerges, he becomes nervous and breathes heavily until Dave reassures him. Once the ship drops the power cable, the divers begin work. After connecting the cable, they activate the manifold and report back to Craig. Everything runs smoothly until Chris checks the gas readings inside the manifold and notices they are too high. As he works to fix it, the crew suddenly realizes the ship's thrusters have gone offline, meaning they have lost the ability to hold position. The tide gets choppy as wind blows heavily. Sensing something is wrong, Dave notices the ship is drifting and quickly orders Chris to move away from the manifold. On board, the DPS completely fails and the crew loses control of the boat. Craig orders Duncan to abort the mission and instructs him to give the divers as much umbilical slack as possible. As Dave and Chris climbs onto the manifold to get better visibility, they could not spot the bell, and Chris's umbilical snags on the manifold. With the ship tilting because of the wind and the power cable detaching, the seabed plunges into darkness. The team also finds out their ship is not drifting as Chris's cord is acting as an anchor which is attached to the structure. Dave tries to reach Chris but couldn't and Chris's oxygen supply is running low. Dave urgently tells him to switch to his backup oxygen. Duncan informs Craig that Chris is on bailout, meaning he has only 10 minutes of air left. Dave warns Chris that his umbilical will snap, pulling him away from the structure. He instructs Chris to get back to the manifold so he can find him again. Before Chris can respond, his cord snaps and he is dragged into the dark water. Back on the ship, Craig reports that they have lost visual on the divers. However, their ROV, remotely operated vehicle, captures video footage of Dave returning to the bell. Upon reaching safety, Dave reports that Chris is gone. His cord was severed. Meanwhile, Chris ignites a flare and tries calling Duncan and Craig over the comms, but receives no response. Remembering Dave's instructions, he realizes he must get back to the manifold. The captain is informed that the thrusters are working, but the DPS remains down. Despite concerns about manual control in rough tides, he and his first officer decide to navigate the ship manually to prevent drifting further from Chris's last known position. After much effort, they managed to turn the boat. The DPO officer reports that they are 630 ft away from the dive site. Meanwhile, Chris reaches the manifold and collapses onto it, thinking about Morag. The DPO officer suggests resetting the DPS, but the captain refuses since it would take hours. He insists they find another solution. Finally, the ROV locates the manifold and spots Chris lying on top of it, convulsing. Craig assumes the movements are involuntary spasms and that Chris is dead. The DPO officer informs the captain that he has found a workaround. Since the DPS operates through a startup CPU, he can rewire it to bypass the startup delay. However, it poses a risk. The captain tells him to go ahead with it. Meanwhile, Craig orders his colleague to retrieve Chris using the ROV, but he warns that it's too risky. Determined, Craig operates the ROV himself. After a tense struggle, he finally tethers Chris onto the ROV. But Craig discovers that Chris has clipped himself onto the structure, likely to avoid being swept away by the tide. Craig is impressed by Chris's quick thinking, but frustrated by the situation. Back in the dive bell, Duncan tells Dave that he and Chris first met during a rescue dive operation. He recalls how during that mission, they failed to recover one of the bodies from a sunken ship and were only able to return the victim's belongings. Duncan vows that this time he will not return just Chris's belongings to Morag. He will bring Chris back alive. The DPO officer successfully rewires the system, bringing the DPS back online. With the ship now stable, the crew prepares to retrieve Chris. Duncan is informed that Chris is still on the manifold. Dave dives back into the water, spotting Chris lying on top of the manifold. He retrieves him, but as he tries to climb back up, Chris's weight slows him down. After a strenuous effort, Dave manages to bring Chris back into the bell. Craig immediately begins mouth-to-mouth resuscitation, but Chris appears unresponsive and glassy. He has been without oxygen for over 30 minutes. Just as the crew loses hope, Chris suddenly gasps for air, stunning everyone. The entire crew erupts in celebration. Due to the ordeal, the captain decides to cut the rotation short, and the team heads home. On day one of decompression, Chris confides in Dave that while he was down there, he felt a strange sense of peace. However, he was overcome with sadness, feeling like he had let Morag down. He thanks Dave for saving his life. On day three, after bidding farewell to the team, Chris shares the incident with Morag, who is shaken by the near tragedy. He reassures her, promising that no matter what happens, he will always find his way back to her. And with that, the story ends. [Music]

text: Filmart "Well Go" Acquires U.S. Rights to Korean Crime-Thriller - ‘Yadang The Snitch’ - Starring Kang Ha-neul. Coming this spring, director Hwang Byeong-gug’s action-packed thriller follows a street-smart survivor caught in the crossfire between law enforcement and the criminal underworld. Well Go USA has secured the North American theatrical rights to Yadang (The Snitch) a gripping Korean crime thriller starring Squid Game’s Kang Ha-neul. The company acquired the film from leading Korean production house Plus M and plans to release it in North American theaters this spring. The deal was unveiled Tuesday at Hong Kong’s Filmart content market. Directed by Hwang Byeong-gug (Wedding Campaign, S.I.U.), Yadang (The Snitch) offers a fresh perspective on the drug-lord crime saga. The film also features Yoo Hai-jin (Exhuma) and Park Hae-joon (Twelve Twelve - The Day) alongside Kang. Kang takes on the role of Kang-su, a streetwise survivor who finds himself entangled in a perilous web of crime and corruption. Wrongfully imprisoned, he strikes a high-risk deal with ambitious prosecutor Ku Gwan-hee (played by Yoo Hai-jin) become an informant in exchange for his freedom. But as Kang-su delves deeper into the dangerous world of drug cartels, corrupt officials, and deadly conspiracies, he soon realizes he is merely a pawn in a much larger game - where trust is scarce, and betrayal comes at a steep cost. At a recent promotional event in Seoul, director Hwang revealed that he was inspired to create the film after reading a news article about underworld informants who regularly visit Korean prosecutors’ offices to trade information for personal benefits. He aimed to set his story apart from other Korean drug war films by focusing on the unique and morally ambiguous role of the informant. “They operate within the boundaries of the law, yet their actions remain questionable. They exist in a gray area,” Hwang explained in an interview with The Korea Times. “I thought it would make for a compelling film.” “We are excited to bring Yadang (The Snitch) to North American audiences,” said Doris Pfardrescher, president and CEO of Well Go USA. “This high-stakes thriller delivers relentless tension, unexpected twists, and gripping performances, keeping viewers on the edge of their seats. It’s a pulse-pounding story that lingers far beyond the screen.”

text: Nocturnal recaps here. Today I'm going to tell you about one of the most unique movies in years, a 2022 comedy in the style of black and white Charlie Chaplin movies, titled "Hundreds of Beavers". The perpetually drunk distiller loses everything at one point and declares war on the beavers. The movie begins by describing the life of a distiller named Jean Kayak. Bro is living his best life, creating apple brandy and drinking like an animal. But, one fateful day, beavers ruin his idyll by stealing one barrel of brandy while another crashes into his house and sets the farm on fire. A man wakes up in the middle of a snowy forest and discovers that there is nothing left of his past life. Remembering that he had once watched a couple of episodes of Man versus Wild, he builds a fire and unsuccessfully tries to get himself a rabbit. Suffering from hunger, the man spots two beavers and selflessly attacks them, but they quickly show who is the gangster of this forest. Not finding success in the hunt, Jean goes to the river where, after several unsuccessful attempts, he manages to catch a couple of fish, using his bloody finger as bait. While lying in the snow because of blood loss, he notices a fur trapper riding his Gachimuchi sled to a merchant's house and decides to go there too. Jean is the first to arrive and as he clumsily tries to pull off a fish frozen to his ass, he notices how beautiful the merchant's daughter is. At the same time, a fur trapper arrives with a large shipment of beavers, and the merchant once again tries to marry off his daughter to him, but the man, not wanting to lose his bells on his wedding night, refuses. The fur trapper leaves, and Jean finally exchanges his fish for a coin, for which he immediately buys an average-sized knife. With this knife, Jean creates a rope and sets a trap on the rabbit, but fails as they use an imbalanced fast travel system. Utilizing the man's main evolutionary advantage, Jean blocks all but one of the burrows near where the snare is set. The plan works, but on the spot, he discovers an ancient Roman-level backstabbing from a raccoon that ate his rabbit. After a few more failed attempts, Jean, having created more rope from his pants, sets a hanging trap, into which the raccoon himself falls. After getting into a fight with a forest bandit, he drags it to a merchant, and on the way, he notices an Indian, with whom he trades his knife for snowshoes. Arriving at the merchant's house, Jean takes the raccoon's carcass to his daughter, who skillfully skinned it and made him the best drip in the neighborhood. Satisfied with his new look, he is serenely walking through the woods when he falls into one of the fur trapper's pits. The Hunter pulls Jin out of the pit, treats his wounds, and teaches him the path of the fur trapper. While traveling along their trap route, wolves regularly visit their camp each night, taking one dog with each visit. A few nights later, they take the last dog and attack Jean, but the fur trapper enters the fray with them, cosplaying Aragorn fending off the Nazguls. The forces are not equal, so they are forced to hide on a tree, but the wolves catch the fur trapper, and he gives Jean his trap map with his last strength, just before the wolves take him away. After coming down from the tree in the morning, Jean buries his sensei and follows the trail of the wolves, who have taken all their prey to their cave. Not really trying to understand the fur trapper's map, Jean erases it so he can draw a new one. Returning to the merchant, Jean trades the dogs' cards for rope and informs him of the fur trapper's death. After further exploration of the area, Jean meets the Indian again and smokes a pipe of peace with him. The man notices hoof prints and asks about them, whereupon the Indian shows Jean his horse, aka the next Academy Award winner for Best Costume. After a short wander through the woods, Jean manages to get one beaver caught in his trap, but his actions do not go unnoticed by Chewrlog Holmes and Dr. Gnawson. The man exchanges the beaver for a smoking pipe, for which he immediately receives a tomahawk from an Indian, with the help of which he builds various traps for catching animals. Jean gradually improves his skills by obtaining beasts and trading them for items from the merchant and the Indian, for even more efficient elimination of forest critters, until he barters the merchant's last item, a musket. While the merchant is distracted, Jin sweet-talks his daughter and suggests she marry him, but the merchant intervenes in this conversation. Clearly unwilling to marry his only daughter to this drunkard, he says that he will only allow them to marry if Jean brings him hundreds of beavers. Jean is not discouraged, and like a true sigma male continues his frenzied farming of forest wildlife. He automatizes these processes, harvesting beavers by the dozens, but when Damlock Holmes and Dr. Barkson notice all this, they call their bros to beat the crap out of him. After getting the idea from an Indian, Jean gathers brushwood to smoke the wolves out of the cave, but the beavers follow him on his trail. When they catch up with him in the wolves' cave, they discover it is only bait. Hearing the noise, the wolves wake up, and a fight breaks out between them, while Jean blocks the exit with icicles, locking them in a small branch of Sodom and Gomorrah. Grinning from ear to ear, he returns to the merchant with a huge sack of beavers to propose to his daughter. Having lost the ability to see stereoscopically, due to the blood flowing from his head to his hormone gun, Jean fails to notice the obvious trap that causes him to lose all his beavers. Gathering all his willpower in his fist, he heads to the dam to reclaim what is rightfully his. Using the dumbest stealth mechanic in video games, Jean sneaks up on the dam and sneaks inside, through a pipe. There, like a ninja in the emperor's castle, he makes his way through the many guards until he accidentally stumbles upon a barrel of his favorite Apple Jack. Plagiarizing the very scene from Lord of the Rings in Mount Doom, the man manages to overcome his desires, and he decides to return his loot by all means. Losing his guard for a second, Jean is spotted by the watchmen, and they raise the alarm and set off in pursuit of the intruder. This time luck turns away from Jean, and he hits his balls hard, which allows the beavers to catch him. The man is taken to court, where the prosecutor presents all the evidence of Jean's atrocities collected by Lumber Holmes and Dr. Woodson. The attorney is clearly not Saul Goodman, so the defense line fails miserably, and the man is found guilty. Jean opens his eyes, tied to the table, as beavers attempt to turn him into a coat. Using his intelligence, on the level of Hawking and Einstein combined, Jean breaks free from the loops, and a fight ensues between them, which I sincerely consider one of the best fight scenes of recent years. Showing who's the daddy, Jean goes outside and discovers that his beavers are being prepared for a funeral. The man goes after them and along the way discovers that the beavers are preparing to launch a rocket into space, using his Apple Jack as fuel. When Jean gets into a fight with one of the beavers, the latter accidentally breaks the prop and the rocket goes into an uncontrolled flight, dooming the beavers to lose the space race with Otter Union. The dam is slowly collapsing, as is my psychological state while I'm watching this movie, and the beavers run after the bastard who ruined months of hard work. Jean manages to escape, and after quickly dealing with the funeral procession, he pulls the sack of beavers down the mountain, turning it into a snowball. The man follows him on a sled, as do the beavers, giving us a chase scene that is more talented than all the Fast and Furious movies put together. While Jean is riding a snow globe the movie's writers decide to switch to harder drugs and transform beavers into giant mecha. As the robot gradually approaches Jean, he accidentally steps on the Indian's horse. The thirst for revenge burns in the eyes of the native, and he lassoes the erratically flying rocket, directing it towards the beavers. The mecha shatters, allowing Jean to successfully make his way to the merchant. Tearing open the sack, the man bestows the merchant with hundreds of beavers and takes his well-deserved reward.

text: Attakus Lisa's preparation for the next life delves into the lives of Skinner, a troubled Iraq war veteran grappling with post-traumatic stress disorder, PTSD, and Zo Lelay, an undocumented immigrant from Central Asia. Their unexpected love story explores the profound impact they have on each other, highlighting the struggles faced by both war veterans and undocumented immigrants in the United States, as well as the complexities inherent in cross-cultural relationships. The novel, praised by both critics and readers, won multiple awards, including the 2015 Penn Falner Award for Fiction. Published in 2014 by Tyrant Books, Preparation for the Next Life, follows two characters who form a bond based on mutual support, Zule, originally from northern Afghanistan, finds herself in the harsh reality of life as an undocumented immigrant in New York City. After being imprisoned under the Patriot Act, she fears deportation and her dreams of a better life in America start to fade. Skinner, just back from his third tour in Iraq, is a young man haunted by severe PTSD. His struggles with anxiety, depression, and disturbing nightmares lead him to self-medicate with alcohol and VA prescribed medications. He rents a basement room from Mrs. Murphy where he meets Zo Lelay. Their connection is immediate and they soon begin a relationship. both promising to help each other with their struggles. Skinner vows to protect Zolay from deportation and she hopes to help him manage his mental health. However, as Skinner's PTSD worsens, their relationship becomes strained. Meanwhile, Mrs. Murphy's son, Jimmy, is released from prison after serving more than a decade. A violent white supremacist, Jimmy brings chaos into their lives, including disturbing acts of violence and his continued hatred toward the Chinese community. His presence exacerbates tensions as his brutal actions highlight the fragile and volatile nature of the characters lives. As their stories unfold, the novel portrays the deep challenges each character faces and the ways their lives intersect in a harsh and unforgiving world. Skinner's deteriorating mental health, combined with the rising threat posed by Jimmy, creates a volatile environment, making their fragile attempts at healing and connection all the more poignant. When Skinner learns that Zule is an undocumented immigrant, he vows to marry her so she can obtain a green card. However, her lack of proper identification complicates the process, putting her at risk of being deported back to China. Meanwhile, Zule continues to lose hours at her job to a young man with a bad attitude, but she can do nothing about it as she is not legally allowed to work in the United States. In her search for work, Zolay meets a Muslim man from a region near her hometown. He introduces her to his wife who takes her to a mosque, providing her with food and water. After the service, the moola advises Zolay that everything she does from this point forward should be in preparation for the next life. Tensions rise when Jimmy, Mrs. Murphy's son, returns from prison. Skinner and Jimmy clash immediately. Skinner becomes paranoid, believing Jimmy is sneaking into his room and stealing things, which exacerbates his PTSD symptoms, making it even harder for him to relax at home. Despite his mental health deteriorating, Skinner tries to stay strong. One day, Skinner leaves Zolay in his room to go to the gym, only to return and find his room ransacked and Zolay's belongings gone. He immediately confronts Jimmy and the two men clash violently. Mrs. Murphy calls the police and Skinner is arrested. He insists that Jimmy should be the one arrested, convinced that Jimmy killed Zolay. However, it is later revealed that Zolay is not dead. Jimmy had broken into Skinner's room and attempted to rape her, but Zule managed to escape. She fled the house, running as far as she could. After being released from police custody, Skinner returns to the Murphy's house and finds all his belongings discarded in the trash bin. Among them, he spots his gun and decides to confront Jimmy. When Jimmy denies any wrongdoing, Skinner, not believing him, shoots him in the head, killing him. Skinner then runs into a nearby alley, reflecting on the destruction of his life. Feeling hopeless, he takes his own life with a self-inflicted gunshot. Zolay eventually returns to the Murphy home, searching for Skinner. She finds her things in the trash and asks Jimmy's sister, Aaron, about Skinner's whereabouts. Aaron feains ignorance, but Zolay senses something is wrong. Taking their belongings, she leaves. Using the money Skinner left her, she starts a new life in Phoenix, Arizona. Though she is heartbroken by the events that transpired, Zolay remains grateful to Skinner for the opportunities and strength he gave her. Thank you for watching. text: Minions: The Rise of Gru is currently the most recent Illumination film, the studio who has brought us such classics as The Secret Life of Pets 2, Hop, and The Secret Life of Pets. This movie was supposed to release on July 3, 2020, but chose not to go direct-to-digital like most at the time and instead wait until the following year, and release on July 2, 2021. This did not happen either, and so the movie was released today (at the time of making this video), July 1, 2022. As one might expect, the movie has Minions in it. Some die-hard Despicable Me 3 fans might recognize Kevin, Bob, and Stuart (my personal favorite Minion), but only avid Minions: The Rise of Gru trailer watchers would recognize the new Minion. Otto. I do not like Otto. Otto adds nothing to the story and only seems to be there to allow for a few extra scenes to make the runtime longer. Despite being the namesake, the Minions sort of take a backseat in this movie and are overshadowed by the numerous human characters that receive the spotlight. The movie focuses on one Felonius Gru, and his quest for becoming the greatest supervillain, after being inspired by a team of supervillains that for some reason has committed dozens of crimes over a series of decades and still runs scot-free. One of the members of the aforementioned group, actually named the Vicious Six, was exiled after doing literally nothing (he helped steal an amulet that will become plot-relevant later). He is Gru’s favorite supervillain, and he wants to be like him which works out for him later in the movie. I am not going to spoil this movie because I do not really feel like it nor do I want to ruin the surprises that were not put in the hundreds of trailers that have been popping up over the past few weeks. The movie has some easter eggs for fans of the franchise, which either set up some elements in Despicable Me or are just neat nods such as some character introductions and references. The climax of the movie as well as its McGuffin relate to Chinese New Year which they reference a few times, but the settings as well as character outfits do not make it seem like February. That might be too big of a nitpick. Gru, and his favorite super villain, Wild Knuckles, sort of look alike, in my opinion, and I am not sure if this is intentional or not or if it was a scrapped plot idea that they just did not feel like changing the model. The song by the rapper, Yeat, Rich Minion, was not featured in the movie, bumping down its personal score in my opinion. I felt drained making this recap and review and feel even more so now so thank you for sticking around. Overall, I would say that this movie is just alright. I think that I have started to hate it more the more I have talked about it, thought about it and seen it, but that’s fine. I am not the right audience for it whatsoever and I think (based on my audience) that it was adored by the young Minion fans that do exist. My personal score for this movie would be around a six out of ten, which is a stepup from Sing 2, but a step down from Despicable Me 1 and 2. Thanks for watching and please like subscribe and stay tuned for the next Smellman426 recap and review.
title: Recap and Review – Minions: The Rise of Gru
