Like the time Kafka saved her or when Mina arrived as they fought the giant mushroom/crab Kaiju and also when Hoshina came to face Kaiju number 10. She reflected on this and realized that it was never her who took down the powerful monsters. It was always someone else. Suddenly, she called Narumi a pea-brain and seriously told him that what he said had been her plan from the start. Kikoru then released her full power and her released force reached 84%. Both Kikoru and Okanagi were shocked by the reading they obtained and Kikoru also caught Mina's attention. Hoshina was pleased to see how far Kikoru had come. After that, Narumi commented that they should start and this was where the real battle began. He announced that he would target monster number 11, Hoshina and number 10 would take on 12, Rin and Tachibana on 13, Mina on 14, and Kikoru on 15. Kikoru immediately raised her battle axe and said they were moving to subjugate those powerful monsters. They looked at each other and one might really ask here if it was evil in the form of a shadow or a mirror image of Kikoru. While observing Kaiju number 15, Kurusu commented that this monster not only recognized Kikoru but also resembled her. He was puzzled by what was happening and immediately notified everyone in the Kamigasaki area that as of now, he would assign command of that area to Kikoru and they would now execute the second special troop formation. Kikoru promptly explained that she would designate the immediate 500 m radius around her as an alert zone and she instructed the nearby platoons to focus their strength on taking down the after beasts there and not let them enter the alert zone. The troop members in the vicinity agreed and Kikoru clenched her axe. She thought that at this moment, no one else like Mina, Narumi, or Kafka would be there to help her. She took a deep breath and declared that everything now depended on her. She prepared to subjugate number 15 and number 15 seemed to like the sound of her catchphrase, so it mimicked her. In the blink of an eye, number 15 vanished from in front of Kikoru and suddenly targeted her face. Fortunately, Kikoru was able to dodge the incredibly fast attack, but she saw its strength when the impact hit the building next to her. Number 10 commented that he was somewhat surprised that Kikoru had managed to dodge the attack. Kikoru bolstered her courage and thought not to be swayed by 15's words and just attack. She tried to slice 15, but it managed to kick her axe, causing a powerful shockwave around their area. Kikoru stopped herself from being thrown back, and when she saw a chance, she unleashed a combo of her techniques like the first, second, and fourth forms, attacking swiftly. However, 15 easily dodged everything, and when she was about to use her fifth form, she was grazed by a kick on the cheek. This made Kikoru realize that she was afraid of making a mistake because she knew her life could be at stake. Nevertheless, she gathered her courage and declared that she had to keep going. She continued to attack, showcasing her strength, which amazed Kurusu and led him to comment that Kikoru's speed, power, and efficiency surpassed the level of a commander averages. Kage also remarked that for a first-year troop, Kikoru was the strongest they had seen, even more talented than Esau. Hikari and Narumi were in their first year, leading Kurusu to assert that without a doubt, in due time, Kikoru would become the core of the entire defense force. But his confidence in Kikoru quickly vanished when he saw 15 easily beating her. 15 managed to slam Kikoru to the ground with extraordinary strength, and the struggle on Kikoru's face to resist this powerful monster was evident. 15 tried to follow up with a face projectile attack, but fortunately, Kikoru's suit was able to propel her sideways, allowing her to dodge this monster's attack. 15 charged at her again, and while she was speaking about her shield being shattered, 15 delivered a powerful punch. She managed to deflect it with her axe, but the force of the attack still sent her flying back, embedding her into a building. Kikoru spat blood from the impact of hitting the building, and Kurusu informed the others that Kikoru's shield had been penetrated, and she had sustained critical damage to her ribs and left lung. After the smoke and rubble cleared, Kikoru was shown badly beaten, but still trying to stand up. 15 then commented that her efforts were useless and suddenly extended its left hand. It told her that if she used her small axe and weak attacks against it, she would never be able to wound her. 15 then created a giant axe from the rubble around, aiming it at Kikoru. Fear and anxiety were evident in the eyes of Kage and Kurusu, and they thought that there was no chance for Kikoru to defeat this very powerful monster. 15 sent the axe and other small rubble towards Kikoru, but using her suit again, Kikoru propelled herself to dodge. Kurusu was pleased to see her dodge, but his expression quickly changed when he saw 15 easily close the distance to Kikoru after her attack. 15 prepared to launch another face projectile, and unfortunately, it hit Kikoru solidly, driving her into the ground. An assistant in the control room reported that the circuitry in Kikoru's left arm was damaged, whereupon Kurusu said they would bypass it because they had another attack coming. Kurusu realized he needed to do something. After what happened to Esau, he couldn't just let his daughter die as well. Kikoru tried to fend off the numerous attacks from 15, causing damage to her armor on the right leg and left flank, and she now had rib and arm fractures and was bleeding from many parts of her body. The assistants tried to heal Kikoru using the suit, but it seemed too late. Kurusu was frustrated because they couldn't keep up with 15, and it seemed like Kikoru had no shield because her defenses were easily penetrated by the monster's attacks. Out of deep concern, Kurusu tried to talk to Kage that the situation was deteriorating and they needed to save Kikoru, but Kage insisted that Kikoru was key to their future, so they couldn't to lose her. He told Kurusu that they would do what was necessary and ordered them to lower the defense level of their headquarters by two and send back up to Kikoru. However, they were suddenly stopped by Kikoru herself, which surprised them. Kikoru explained that if they did that, number nine would just attack them immediately, so she would handle it herself and take down 15. Kurusu tried to argue that she wasn't okay, but Kikoru insisted that she was close. Kage and Kurusu were puzzled by what she meant, but it became clear when Kurusu saw her released force had reached 88%. Kikoru was very close to catching up. She was seeing her mother standing in front of her as she thought this. Kurusu didn't understand what she meant, but Kage quickly realized it and thought that maybe Kikoru was seeing the ghost of Hikari. While Kikoru was fighting, we return to a point in time where she told Narumi that she could see her mother's ghost. She explained that sometimes when she wears weapon number four, she sees it. Narumi pointed out that what Kikoru was seeing was a ghost, which surprised Kikoru. Narumi explained that it was a rare phenomenon that occurs when wearing a numbers weapon that someone else had used in the past, and Commander Akutsu of the Northern Division had previously reported a sighting. To this day, it is still unknown what causes it, but some believe it is the memory of the imminent monster used in the core of the suit. Kikoru then thought that the memories of number four of her mother were in that suit. It turns out that since Kikoru saw Hikari, she tried to chase her, but could never get close. All her mother's attacks were extremely fast, precise, and powerful. She tried to match her mother's strength while training with Narumi, and during the battle, we see that Kaiju number four appears to her, making her think that if her mother were watching, the monster would not look unimpressed. She knew there was a distance in strength between her and her mother, but she also knew that just a little more and she would be within reach. We return to the present as she battles 15, and we can see the difference in speed between her and her mother. However, as she continues to push herself, Kikoru manages to wound 15. 15 is surprised by this, and determination is evident in Kikoru's eyes. 15 becomes irritated and claims that Kikoru just got lucky and should not get excited too quickly. 15 throws a powerful punch, but to its surprise, Kikoru easily dodges it. The monster's face shows shock at this turn of events. Kikoru pushes herself further, declaring that she will surpass her mother, not someday, but now. As she said, we see that after always being one step behind her mother, she has finally managed to surpass her. Kikoru pointed out that ever since she was a child, she had been chasing after her mother. Before long, her axe solidly hit 15's body, and the force of Kikoru's attack was so strong that it severed 15's defensive hand. Kurusu and the others were pleased because Kikoru's attack had landed successfully. 15 was puzzled by what was happening and sensed that something had changed, leading him to wonder what had happened to Kikoru. Kikoru unleashed a flurry of attacks, and Kurusu saw her released force gradually increasing until it reached 93%. Kage was astonished by what he saw and commented to himself that Kikoru had reached Hikari's strength. Kage grimaced and said that he and Kurusu had claimed Kikoru was the strongest first-year troop member they had seen, but he now felt that was an understatement. Kurusu wanted Kikoru to push herself further, while Kage encouraged her to surpass her mother's power. Kikoru prepared to attack and raised her axe using the troop style axe technique, fifth form, twin swallow slash. She managed to slice 15's neck and body with extraordinary strength. Her released force rose to 94%, allowing her to surpass her mother's power. As 15's body flew through the air, Kikoru saw that its core was exposed, so she prepared to use her sixth form attack. However, she was startled to see 15 laughing despite being in such a situation. She wondered why it was laughing, and suddenly something pierced her back. 15 commented on what a strong little trooper Kikoru was. Soon, 15 used a strange attack that looked like webs he had used on civilians before, and several strands solidly hit Kikoru. Shock appeared on Kikoru's face, while 15 laughed as it transformed into its Kaiju form, uttering the words wired in. Suddenly, Kikoru found herself in a dark place, causing chaos in the control room as they saw in the readings that Kikoru's mental stability had gone haywire and ended up all over the place. It seemed her mental state had blacked out, and they couldn't reach her, and her released force was decreasing as they faced noise that was disrupting her neural synchronization with the suit. They tried to communicate with Kikoru, but it wasn't working. So, Kurusu soon realized that 15 was performing a mental attack on her. The strain on Kikoru's body was visible, and she couldn't explain what was happening to her. Suddenly, 15 praised her, causing her to look around and search for it. And it asked her why she was trying so hard. Her headache intensified after 15's question, making her wonder what 15 was doing to her. 15 asked again why she was so desperate to become stronger, to which she replied that it was to protect the country from monsters like 15. 15 claimed she was lying and asked why she wanted to protect that country, to which Kikoru said she wanted to protect the people important to her, whereupon 15 said she was still lying. If that was the case, 15 asked why Kikoru wanted to protect them. As Kikoru was saying that the answer was obvious, she found herself unable to express what she really wanted to say. 15 pressured her to be honest with herself, saying she knew the real reason she wanted to be strong. We returned to a past where she was happily receiving head pats from her parents, Hikari and Isao. There, she revealed the real reason she wanted to become strong. It was to make her parents proud of her. She wanted to hear from her mom and dad that she had done well. 15 was pleased with her revelation, said he was proud of her, and told her that she no longer needed to try so hard. 15 then suddenly suggested they stop because no matter how hard Kikoru tried, Hikari and Isao were no longer there to praise her. The impact of this profoundly painful situation was visible on Kikoru's face. Her parents were gone for good, and Kikoru cried out loud after that. While in the outside world, Kurusu and others tried to talk to her, but she did not respond. Kurusu suggested that they try to access Kikoru's neural circuit from the outside. He also commented that this was the might of an eminent class monster. He pointed out that even though the greatest trooper of their time had awakened her power, it was still not enough against an eminent monster. While watching the situation, Keiji thought to himself that 15 had precisely targeted Kikoru's mental state, her most vulnerable part. Soon, Keiji noticed something extremely precise. He immediately asked for updates on the status of each battle, and someone quickly reported from Taito that Narumi was fighting number 11. The scene showed an intense clash between two powerful beings, and just as a troop member was about to say that Narumi had the advantage, and they were about to defeat the monster there, Narumi slipped on 11's liquid, and when he lost his focus, the monster delivered a powerful attack to his side. 11 immediately prepared to launch another attack, and because Narumi's body was off balance, unfortunately, the monster's punch landed solidly, throwing him against the wall. The troop members there couldn't believe that number 11 had managed to hit their commander even though number nine hadn't been able to hit him in their last fight. 11 then commented that he now knew Narumi's tricks, and explained that Narumi could read his movements using the electric signals inside his body. However, the monster suggested that Narumi try to read the water, and flicked its finger, releasing numerous water balls towards Narumi. 11 immediately sent his water attack towards Narumi, and it appeared to hit the commander solidly, prompting Keiji to comment that his suspicions were correct. In the third unit, Okonagi reported on their situation in Chofu, which also seemed to be dire. It was shown that Hashina was struggling to keep up with Kaiju number 12, and after being struck, he was thrown back. The strength of the monster's attack was causing damage to the surrounding area, which irritated Hashina. He charged again after being thrown, exchanging blows with 12 at an extraordinary speed. Unfortunately, he kept getting hit in the body, which further irritated him. It turned out that his growing anger was because he felt he was being outclassed in a battle of blades, and it appeared that 12 has blades for arms. Okonagi noticed that this monster specialized in close-quarters combat. While watching the two fight, she commented that the monster seemed to be like Hashina. It was an expert at focusing on the target in front of it. It was almost as if 12 was created for the express purpose of taking down Hashina. Keiji agreed with her and said that her observation was accurate, explaining that humans have studied various potential threats such as animals, insects, bacteria, viruses, and monsters to develop effective countermeasures against them, and he pointed out that now, for the first time they were the ones being studied. He added that these monsters were engineered to take them all down. Elsewhere, with Rin and Tachibana, it was shown that Rin appeared to have no hope in their situation, and it seemed that other troop members with them there were dead, with Kaiju number 13 choking Tachibana. On the other hand, a troop member is having a flashback, thinking about how overwhelming Narumi truly is. From the first day they were together on the battlefield, he has been an entity far beyond her reach. Returning to the control room, they were receiving reports from various areas. Since their main forces could no longer move, they were gradually seeing an increase in damage. Keiji commented that the monsters were taking down their personnel one by one using Kaiju that targeted their weaknesses, and their pool of officers who could fight the identified class was very limited. Even if just one of their sites were breached, there was a high chance it would cause their forces to fall. While Rin stared at the monster, she thought that their efforts were futile because the offensive capabilities and mobility of Kaiju number 13 were far beyond theirs. This was truly a Kaiju unlike any they had fought before, and fighting this monster was a lost cause. Tachibana was severely beaten while being choked by 13, and the control room noticed he had fractures in his mandible and C2 vertebrae, and he wouldn't last much longer. Consequently, an assistant urgently ordered Rin to provide backup, which surprised her. Rin suddenly remembered the times when Narumi had appointed her as a platoon leader, and soon her courage returned. She immediately raised her Gatling gun, and her unleashed combat power reached 73%. She unleashed a barrage of attacks on the monster, causing 13 to release Tachibana. As Rin continued to deliver attacks, 13 suddenly appeared in front of her and prepared to punch. She was shocked by the monster's speed, and it managed to deliver a powerful punch that destroyed her weapon and threw her back. As she was thrown back, she thought to herself that she wanted to be stronger and become a captain. It turns out she was the one speaking earlier about how overwhelming Narumi was, and she wanted to be strong so that Narumi would notice her. She explained that Narumi was only interested in strength. She was always out of Narumi's view, just another officer out of many. During these times, she made it her goal to be noticed by Narumi one day, and because of that desire, she made efforts to become stronger, more attractive, and much more. So, that was the reason why she was so happy when Narumi called her by her first name and recognized her skills by appointing her as a platoon leader, challenging her to show the next level of her skills. Returning to the battle, Rin steeled herself and shouted that as a platoon leader of the first division, as part of Narumi's operation, and being in charge of the front lines, it was an honor. Rin stopped herself from being thrown further using her hand, and quickly charged at 13. She knew she had no chance of winning, but she was sure that Narumi did. While running, she grabbed a bomb and immediately threw it at 13. In such a situation, as a platoon leader, there was only one thing she could do, and that was to fight to the end. Ice shards appeared around 13 from the bomb thrown by Rin, and she unleashed a barrage of attacks on the monster. While attacking, she knew it wasn't enough to kill 13. So, if the monster wanted her life, it could take it. She thought she needed to buy even a little time and gather as much intel as possible to pass on to Narumi. However, despite fighting with all her strength, in a flash, 13 suddenly appeared behind her and slammed her to the ground, creating a hole in the bridge they were standing on. She tried not to let the thought that she didn't want to die overwhelm her because she was a platoon leader of the first division, and risking her life to protect their country was her duty, so she shouldn't let that thought prevail. However, when 13 stood in front of her, she couldn't help it and admitted she didn't want to die. 13 prepared to end her life, and while this was happening, she thought she didn't need a reward, and all she wanted was to become stronger and more attractive, and to chase after Narumi. Then, 13 delivered a punch with extraordinary force that shattered the ground. But when the monster looked at its fist, Rin seemed to have vanished from in front of it. When the monster looked behind, it saw a man carrying Rin while walking. The monster stared at him, and upon regaining consciousness, Rin asked why the man had done that. It It out that Kafka was the one who saved her, and he apologized to Rin because he knew he had assigned her to rear guard duties, but he was disobeying that order. Anger was clearly visible on Kafka's face as he stared at 13. Let's go back to 5 days before all these events where Kikoru tells Kafka not to help her no matter what happens. Kafka was puzzled and commented on how random this was, asking what she meant. Flustered, Kikoru reiterated that she meant exactly that and told him not to help her in their upcoming battle even if she was in danger. Kikoru pointed out that she was indeed grateful for being saved by Kafka in the past, but she was done being rescued. She seriously told him that no matter how strong her opponents were, she was confident she could defeat them on her own. She needed Kafka to believe in her and to focus on the enemy in front of him and to wipe the floor with their faces. Returning to the present where Kafka had just placed Rin to the side and faced 13. Rin instructed Kafka to retreat because they couldn't afford to lose him there. However, Kafka just smiled at her and thanked her for her concern, but reassured her not to worry because he would not be defeated. Kafka stared at 13 and declared that he would handle this monster himself. Determination was evident on Kafka's face and soon he transformed into his Kaiju form. The force of his transformation sent a powerful shockwave around the area even felt by 15, 11, and 12. The control room sensors also picked up his transformation and immediately reported detecting a Daikaiju in the Oizumi area, and Kurusu exclaimed that it was Kaiju number eight. One of the higher-ups was shocked and asked if they had given him permission to fight, to which Kurusu replied no. Kageyji thought to himself that their original plan was to preserve Kafka's strength for the fight against number nine, but given their current situation, it seemed they had no choice but to use Kafka now. As Kafka walked towards 13, he felt the immense powers of other Kaiju from various locations. He could sense where Hashina, Narumi, and Kikoru were. He called Kikoru and told her that he wouldn't be going to her and that he believed in her. As for himself, he would be the one to face 13. He stared at it and suddenly it smiled. 13 then stepped back slightly from him and started to run in place as if warming up. Rin and Kurusu were puzzled by what they saw and 13 gradually picked up speed with its legs seemingly growing larger as it did so. After that, 13 suddenly got ready to sprint and Kurusu recorded readings showing its resilience level increasing to 9.2. Rin was worried and quickly tried to direct Kafka, but due to 13's incredible speed, he couldn't finish his sentence and 13 quickly got in front of Kafka and prepared to punch. However, unexpectedly for the monster and Rin, Kafka easily blocked the extremely fast attack with one hand, stunning both of them. Kafka continued what he was about to say earlier and stated that for his part, he would focus on his enemy and wipe the floor with its face. Kafka clenched his fist and prepared to punch and soon delivered a powerful attack to the Kaiju's body, throwing it back. The impact was so strong that even 13's teeth were damaged, though they weren't the direct target, and it was flung onto the skyway. The bridge was pierced and 13 went through it. We see 13's destroyed body while 11, 12, and 15 noticed what happened to their companion, and 15 commented that Kaiju number eight was on a different level. It suggested that all the Kaiju should band together to take down Kafka. So it decided to end its fight there and join the other Kaiju. However, when it turned to look at Kikoru, it noticed something about her and it appeared that Kikoru had returned to the real world and overcome 15's mental attack. Kafka's words earlier had awakened Kikoru, restoring her courage. 15 was shocked and immediately tried to stop Kikoru again, but failed and Kikoru easily slashed it across the body. Furious, 15 couldn't understand why Kikoru was still able to move and launched a massive string attack, which hit Kikoru solidly, but it couldn't comprehend why its mind hack no longer affected her. Returning to Kikoru's mind, 15 saw the young Kikoru still crying, which puzzled it as to why things were happening differently outside. As Kikoru cried, she expressed her loneliness and her desire not to be alone, longing to see her mom and dad. text: The story begins with the Minions in search of their evil master in the early 20th century. James is a Minion who likes to come up with stories, but he is an outcast among the other Minions. The tribe stops on an island where they serve a giant Cyclops. This comes to an end when James makes a Lego-like stone painting that the Cyclops steps on, causing a chain reaction that injures him and makes him kick the Minions out. While the rest of the tribe is mad at James, he becomes best friends with Henry, who thinks James is hilarious, as well as Ed, a hearing-impaired Minion. They are led by Dick, a Minion that the others are not too fond of. The Minions then work for a wicked sorcerer. Despite his warnings, James and Henry tamper with his spellbook to summon a giant fluffy pink bunny creature. It turns out to be a vicious monster with laser eyes that destroys almost the entire castle and turns the sorcerer into dust. James and Henry send the creature back, but now they are once again without a master. The tribe continues traveling until they see what appears to be an outlaw bandit riding a horse with stolen loot. The Minions chase the bandit as he makes his escape with a helicopter. James and Henry hijack the train and derail it, which causes it to go out of control in the streets of Los Angeles. They bring the train to a halt before it is revealed the entire thing was part of a movie set. The director, Max, is furious with the Minions and orders them off his set. Max has to present his footage to his bosses and heads of the movie studio, Elwood and Frank Bright. Although nervous to show them the footage with the Minions, the Brights think adding them is a genius move. They order Max to include the Minions in the rest of the film. Max gathers them for a battle scene, and the Minions beat up the other actors during the shoot. The Minions soon take Hollywood by storm, starring in a string of blockbuster hits. However, things take a turn when films begin to incorporate sound. The Minions' language makes it hard for them to act with dialogue, so the Brights fire the Minions from the studio. Hoping to turn things around, James comes up with his idea for a monster movie with the Minions. He comes up with a pitch that he presents to Max, who likes the idea but says he cannot help, though he does express hope and encouragement towards James. Dick is not on board with the movie idea and takes the rest of the tribe with him to find their new leader, leaving James with only Henry and Ed as his help. The trio grab the spell book and summon a tiny Cthulhu-like monster named Goomi. He is thankful to the Minions for freeing him and learns about James' movie project. Goomi says that he can get authentic monsters for the project, and he instructs James, Henry, and Ed to take him to an island where these monsters are located. The other Minions come across an alien robot named Dort, who claims to be on a mission to enslave the Earth. Dick and the others join Dort at his apartment that he claims is a spaceship disguised as an apartment. While out with the Minions, Dort meets a suffragette named Debbie and begins a relationship with her with help from the Minions. Goomi and his three loyal Minion guides finally arrive at the shores of the mysterious uncharted island. Stepping onto the dense terrain, Goomi joyfully reunites with his ancient colossal monster allies, Phillips and Howard, two truly gargantuan and terrifying kaiju who have been hidden away from the world. With the massive creatures in tow, the small crew makes the long journey back to Hollywood, where an unsuspecting James is feverishly preparing his indie movie set, completely focused on his cinematic vision. However, a dark and sinister secret begins to unravel when Henry accidentally overhears Goomi whispering a horrific truth to Phillips and Howard. The entire indie movie project is nothing but a clever front. They actually intend to use the set to summon an apocalyptic ancient monster named Irene, who will ruthlessly consume everything in her path as the ultimate revenge against humanity for centuries of brutal imprisonment. Before a panicked Henry can run to warn the others, the colossal monsters spot him. Following a frantic, terrifying chase through the shadows, they easily catch the helpless minion and take him hostage. Completely unaware of the looming betrayal happening right behind his back, James is smoothly told by Goomy that they will summon Irene directly on camera to capture a spectacular, high-impact opening scene. Goomy suggests using a bound Henry as a dramatic sacrificial actor to make the sequence look completely authentic. James agrees, and as the cameras roll, the ritual succeeds beyond expectation. Irene, a monumental, horrifying orange blob writhing with hundreds of glaring, chaotic eyes, is violently unleashed upon the world. The monster immediately begins tearing the historic movie studio to literal pieces. In the absolute, screaming chaos that follows, Henry miraculously manages a daring escape from his bonds, fleeing into the debris with a desperate James and Ed pursuing him through the burning wreckage, trying their best to reunite. As the seemingly unstoppable Irene slithers out of the studio ruins and into the heart of the city, unleashing an absolute rampage on the streets, the separate faction of minions, alongside Debbie and Dort, witness the unfolding apocalypse firsthand. Acting quickly, Dort evacuates everyone into his disguised department, which completely shocks the group by proving to be a highly functional, heavily weaponized spaceship. Simultaneously on the ground, another brave and reckless faction of minions commandeers heavy tactical tanks and advanced weaponry left abandoned by the fleeing military. Unfortunately, their heavy artillery barely scratches the surface of the rapidly evolving creature. Just as all hope seems entirely lost, Dort and his new fleet of minion-piloted spacecraft tear through the sky, unleashing a massive barrage of concentrated cosmic lasers. The intense heat of the alien weaponry causes Irene's gelatinous shifting form to rapidly harden until she violently explodes into millions of completely harmless pieces. Seizing the chaotic moment of victory, James and Henry swiftly grab the spell book together, loudly chanting the ancient incantation that forcefully banishes Goomy, Phillips, and Howard straight back to their eternal cosmic prison. In the quiet aftermath of the massive crisis, the Minions are hailed worldwide as legendary global heroes. Because the dedicated Ed was secretly rolling the camera through the entirety of the real-life apocalypse, James suddenly finds himself with all the spectacular, high-budget footage he could ever need to complete his masterpiece with the enthusiastic help of his brothers. The highly anticipated film premieres to an ecstatic, packed crowd inside a grand theater, instantly becoming a historic global hit, and earning a proud James a prestigious Golden Banana Award, the ultimate honorary Oscar. Suddenly, the perspective completely shifts, breaking the illusion. A woman named Olivia finishes telling this incredible, sprawling tale to her audience. A grand twist is finally revealed to the viewer. The entire epic story was merely a highly creative movie crafted by the imaginations of James and Henry, and every single character involved, including the terrifying cosmic entity Goomy, was just a talented actor playing a fictional part on a Hollywood set. Yet, the magic doesn't end there. During the closing credits, the timeline shifts forward to the era after the Minions are formally adopted by the villainous Gru. Finding the forbidden spell book left lying around the house, the mischievous creatures decide to play around with its dangerous magic once again. They casually cast a strange spell on Gru's dog Kyle when he is just an innocent little puppy, fully explaining to the audience why the creature grew up to look so incredibly bizarre, spiky, and freaky. Not stopping there, they also used the dark magic to play hilarious, frustrating pranks on a stressed Dr. Nefario. And finally, they summoned the giant fluffy pink bunny monster one last time for little Agnes, who finds the massive, laser-eyed beast absolutely adorable as it happily sits on the floor and plays with her.

text: Some stories don't just unfold. They haunt you. And Reminders of Him is exactly that kind of story. A tale of love, loss, and second chances that will keep you guessing at every turn. Based on Colleen Hoover's best-selling 2022 novel, Reminders of Him takes us deep into the life of Kenna Rowan, played by the mesmerizing Mika Monroe, whose past is as dark as her desire to reclaim her future. Imagine this. You're released from prison. You've lost the love of your life, and your child has been taken from you. Every face you see is a reminder of what you've lost. Every place you go, every sound, every memory, a ghost of your past. But what happens next changes everything. Kenna Rowan was just 20 when tragedy struck. She and Scotty Landry, played in flashbacks by Rudy Pankow, were involved in a horrific car accident. Scotty dies. Kenna survives, but she is convicted of involuntary manslaughter. The guilt is crushing, but that's not all. While in prison, Kenna discovers she's pregnant. She gives birth to a daughter, Diem, but the baby is immediately placed in the care of Scotty's parents, Grace and Patrick, portrayed by Lauren Graham and Bradley Whitford. Seven years later, Kenna is finally free. She returns to her hometown, a place filled with ghosts of the past, and her only goal is simple, yet seemingly impossible, to reconnect with her daughter. But there's a problem. Grace and Patrick want nothing to do with her. They blame her for their son's death and view her as unworthy of ever meeting Diem. And standing firmly between them is Ledger Ward, Scotty's best friend and the man who has been raising Diem like his own. Played by Tyrique Withers, Ledger is magnetic, guarded, and deeply loyal. He won't let Kenna near her daughter, not without consequences. So, we begin our story in a small Wyoming town. Kenna is trying to navigate life outside prison. She's looking for a job, searching for stability, and clinging to hope. Yet, every step she takes is a reminder of what she's lost. But, Kenna is determined. She walks into stores and restaurants filling out applications with a criminal record staring back at her. She doesn't hide her past. She owns it. But, every rejection pushes her closer to desperation. And, that's when the story really starts to get tense because life doesn't give her anything for free. Kenna's path to her daughter isn't just blocked by a custody battle. It's blocked by a man who once loved her late boyfriend. Ledger Ward doesn't know her at first. She introduces herself as Nicole, and their first encounters are filled with tension, misunderstanding, and subtle sparks that neither of them expected. No one expected what happens next. Ledger, still grieving the loss of Scotty, has been living a quiet life. He runs a bar that was once a bookstore where Kenna and Scotty spent time together. Ledger is a man torn between loyalty to his late friend and the natural attraction he feels toward Kenna. And, Kenna? She's conflicted. She wants to fight for her daughter, but she's slowly falling for the one man standing in her way. The tension builds with every scene. Kenna works at a local grocery store earning enough to survive all while writing letters to Scotty, her late boyfriend. These letters aren't just confessions. They're raw, emotional glimpses into her guilt, grief, and longing. She relives that fateful night asking herself, "What if I had done something differently?" Meanwhile, Ledger begins to see her not just as Scotty's killer, but as a woman who has suffered, endured, and survived. Slowly, the walls between them begin to crumble. Small gestures, a shared laugh, a protective instinct, moments of vulnerability pull them closer together. But, every step forward is fraught with danger. One misstep and Kenna could lose DM forever. And just when you think you understand the story, the past returns in vivid flashbacks. Scenes of Kenna and Scotty together show the depth of their love, their imperfections, their humanity. But, rather than easing the tension, these memories make the present even more complicated. How can Kenna fall for Ledger when Scotty still occupies her heart? How can Ledger reconcile his growing feelings for her with the loyalty he feels to his best friend? No one expected the emotional complexity to hit this hard. Every glance, every conversation carries a weight that feels real, almost too real. And then comes the first major turning point. Kenna discovers the depth of Ledger's bond with DM. She sees him reading to her daughter, teaching her, protecting her, and she realizes just how high the stakes are. If she wants DM in her life, she has to win Ledger's trust first. And trust, as we know, is the hardest thing to rebuild after betrayal. Now, the story takes a darker, more suspenseful turn. Secrets about that fateful night slowly unravel. Kenna didn't simply abandon Scotty. The accident, it was far more complicated than anyone knew. She left to find help, but timing, confusion, and her own injuries conspired against her. Ledger, upon learning the truth from Kenna's heartfelt letters, begins to see the situation in a new light. The tension reaches its peak when Patrick, Scotty's father, discovers Ledger's growing connection with Kenna. Fury erupts. In a shocking scene, Patrick confronts Ledger physically and emotionally. It's a moment that feels almost unbearable, yet necessary. Ledger stands firm, not just for Kenna, but for the truth. He proves to the Landrys that Kenna never intended to harm Scotty, that she has always loved both him and their daughter. Meanwhile, Kenna's past and present collide in unexpected ways. Every attempt to bond with Diem is met with resistance. Every interaction with Grace and Patrick carries the weight of years of resentment. But then, small victories begin to appear. A glance, a smile, a moment of connection. Signs that maybe, just maybe, healing is possible. And just when the audience thinks they know how this story will end, the most suspenseful twist emerges. Kenna and Ledger's feelings are undeniable, but their love could destroy everything if the Landrys refuse to forgive. Will they allow a mother back into her child's life, or will pride and grief keep the walls up forever? At this point, the tension is palpable. Every scene crackles with emotion. Every word, every gesture could be the turning point. And as the film approaches its climax, we're left asking, who will survive the ghosts of the past, and who will finally get the second chance they deserve? And then, the resolution. In a heart-stopping finale, Ledger reads Kenna's letters aloud to Grace and Patrick, revealing the depth of her love and guilt. The Landrys finally understand the truth. Grace softens first, offering Kenna the very ring Scotty had planned to give her, a symbol of acceptance, forgiveness, and hope. Patrick, too, begins to heal, embracing Kenna in a way that carries both apology and gratitude. And finally, Kenna meets Diem. The moment is quiet, perfect, and filled with raw emotion. Diem immediately accepts her mother, and the years of separation melt away in a single, beautiful moment. Kenna's journey comes full circle. From a woman imprisoned by guilt and tragedy, she emerges stronger, resilient, and capable of love once again. And with Ledger by her side, the promise of a new future built on honesty, connection, and second chances becomes real. But there's more to the story than just romance. Reminders of Him is about grief, resilience, forgiveness, and the power of human connection. Every letter, every look, every risk Kenna takes is a reminder that life doesn't wait, and love can heal even the deepest wounds. In the end, this adaptation does what many others fail to do. It takes a familiar formula and fills it with heart, emotion, and suspense that keeps you invested from the first frame to the last. It's not just a love story, it's a journey of redemption. text: Hey, are you single? Give me a call if you want to meet somebody. Materialist Recap. Materialist is the story of Lucy, a pragmatic, ambitious woman living in New York City who has built a career as a successful matchmaker after a brief failed attempt at becoming an actress. Now in her 30s, Lucy has become the trusted face of Adore, a matchmaking agency that specializes in pairing up high achieving professionals. With nine successful marriages under her belt, her work has gained her a certain respect among clients and peers alike. Despite being brilliant at understanding others love lives, Lucy keeps her own heart closely guarded. She has a firm personal rule. She will only date men who are wealthy and successful. For her, romance without financial security isn't worth the risk. She describes herself as a voluntary celibate, not out of disinterest, but from a deep belief that love without money inevitably leads to struggle. The film unfolds like a modern diary of Lucy's life in New York, full of small wins, emotional letdowns, and the endless pressure of striving to make it. In a city where appearances often count more than authenticity, the story opens at a wedding, another one of Lucy's successful matchmaking achievements. Friends and colleagues gather to toast her skills. They share anecdotes about her uncanny ability to sense chemistry between people, like she's putting together complex puzzles only she can solve. Brief scenes of Lucy working with clients reinforce her reputation. She's direct, business-like, and hyper analytical. In her world, dating is less about sparks and more about stats. Everyone is both buyer and product, trying to prove their worth to be loved. A recurring question pulses through the film. Are we only the sum of our surface traits, or is there something deeper that makes someone lovable? After the wedding, Lucy chats with her friend and colleague about a new client, Sophie. Sophie is intelligent, kind, and self-aware. But at 39, she's consistently rejected by male clients who want younger, flashier women. Lucy does her best to keep Sophie hopeful, but the feedback is brutal. She's too old, not exciting enough. Watching Sophie get dismissed by men less compassionate and far less self-aware is heartbreaking, and underscores the harsh nature of this curated dating economy. At the same event, Lucy is introduced to Harry Castillo, the brother of the groom. He's confident, well-dressed, and most importantly, rich. a successful finance year who checks every box on Lucy's mental checklist. Their conversation is easy, flirtatious. For a moment, Lucy wonders if maybe she's found exactly what she's always claimed to want. But then, fate throws her a curveball. Jon, her ex-boyfriend, is working the wedding as a caterer. Their reunion is filled with complicated emotions. Once actors struggling side by side, Lucy and Jon ended their relationship not because the love faded, but because of the emotional wear and tear of constantly fighting over money and survival in the city. Their dynamic is tender and charged. They remember what it meant to love each other without a safety net and how painful it was to fail together. From here, Materialist builds a quiet but compelling love triangle. On one side is Harry, polished and wealthy. Everything Lucy told herself she wanted. On the other is Jon. Sincere, creative, but still struggling. Each man offers Lucy something different. Stability versus soul, predictability versus passion. Harry courts Lucy with the ease of someone used to getting what he wants. He takes her to elegant restaurants, showers her with compliments, and listens intently to her career aspirations. To his credit, he genuinely respects Lucy's intelligence and drive. Their relationship becomes public, and Lucy starts to glow with the confidence of someone who's made it. Around this time, she finally matches Sophie with Mark, a charismatic doctor. It feels like a victory, a sign that Lucy's formula works. But Lucy can't escape Jon entirely. They keep running into each other, and every time they talk, unresolved feelings bubble to the surface. Jon is honest about his lingering love for her, though embarrassed about his financial situation. For Lucy, their connection still feels real in a way that's messy, risky, and deeply human. The tension builds to a breaking point when Lucy and Harry attend one of Jon's theater performances. The play is emotionally raw and Lucy is visibly affected. After the show, Jon confronts her. Why is she with Harry? Is she really happy or just settling into a role she thinks she's supposed to play? Lucy pushes back, but the question lingers long after she walks away. Then the illusion of control starts to unravel. Sophie contacts Lucy in distress. Mark, the man Lucy matched her with, has assaulted her. everything she thought she was good at, reading people, making safe matches, suddenly feels false. Lucy is urged by her boss, Violet, to let the legal team handle things quietly. But Lucy refuses to ignore her conscience. She reaches out to Sophie directly, takes accountability, and supports her in filing a legal complaint. Meanwhile, Lucy is supposed to be leaving for a trip to Iceland with Harry, but something inside her has shifted. The promise of luxury now feels suffocating. She breaks things off with Harry in a mature, heartfelt conversation. He's disappointed but respects her choice. With no plan and nowhere to stay, Lucy takes a quiet trip upstate with Jon. Using money he earned from his recent show. Away from the city. Stripped of expectations, they rediscover each other. There's no performance here, just two people who once loved each other trying to figure out if they still can. At another wedding, this time as guests, Lucy kisses Jon. It's a beautiful moment, but one not without tension. Lucy is still torn. She admits she's afraid. Afraid of struggling again, of choosing love over survival. Jon listens. He tells her plainly, "I never stopped loving you and I think we still have a future." Then the final crisis hits. Sophie calls in a panic. Mark has returned and the police won't act fast enough. Lucy and Jon rush to help. When they arrive, Mark flees and Lucy helps Sophie file a restraining order. This moment becomes the true turning point. She finally redefineses what love and connection are really about. Not perfection, but responsibility. Not image, but care. As the film nears its end, Lucy faces another major decision. Violet offers her a promotion, a chance to run the New York office of Adore. It's the dream job. But Lucy hesitates. For the first time, she questions whether she even wants to be part of the matchmaking industry anymore. She doesn't give an answer. In the final scene, Lucy and Jon are sitting in Central Park. The world feels still. Jon proposes. Simple, sincere. No grand gestures, no audience. Lucy says yes, finally ready to step into something uncertain but true. During the credits, we see flashes of couples, both old and new, including Lucy and John, getting marriage licenses. Some smile with giddy excitement, others hold hands nervously. text: 1897 – A cargo ship named Demeter is heading from Romania to England. When it is found on the shores, it is derelict with no survivors on board. A lighthouse crew discovers the wreckage, and they recover a captain's log, which warns them of the danger on board that led to the crew's demise. Four weeks prior, the Demeter arrived at Varna, Bulgaria to load cargo for its London journey. Captain Elliot and his first mate Wochek are in search of crew members for the ship. They are approached by a doctor named Clemens, who had previously studied at Cambridge. However, Wochek turns him down in favor of three other men. Still, Clemens decides to follow them. As the men were loading cargo onto the ship, there was this one crate with a dragon symbol that freaked out one of them. He let it slip from his hands. The crate nearly crushes Elliot’s grandson Toby, but Clemens pulls him out of the way in time. The man leaves, fearing that the dragon symbol is a bad omen. Grateful for Clemens' heroism, Wochek let him board the ship, along with crew mates Abrams, Olgaren, Petrofsky, Larsen, and Joseph. Toby gives Clemens a tour of the boat, introducing him to the animals they've got on board, including his dog Huckleberry. Clemens dines with the crew, while they hear noises from the Cargo and he joins Toby to check it out. Clemens finds out one of the crates fell and busted open in the hold. He discovers a woman buried in dirt, barely alive. Clemens administers blood transfusions to keep her stable to fight against a seeming infection. Out in the Aegean Sea, Clemens and his mate Olgaren spot a strange figure on the deck through the fog. Meanwhile, Joseph finds out that something brutally attacked Huckleberry and the animals. Thinking it might be rabies, the captain orders the crew to toss the dead animals overboard. Petrofsky makes derogatory comments regarding Clemens and the woman, and when Clemens attempts to respond, Larsen holds a knife at him. Seeing the chaos unfold, Olgaren gives everyone a heads-up about some intense evil presence on the ship. Toby is really torn up about losing Huck, and it's weighing on him because Elliot trusted him to take care of the animals. Clemens steps in to offer some comfort. Later on, Toby lets Clemens know that the woman they found has been saying a few things. Turns out, her name is Anna. That night, Joseph lets Clemens know that all the rats have disappeared from the ship, which is pretty unusual. A ship without rats is kind of strange. Later that night, while the rest of the crew is asleep, Petrofsky is on deck keeping watch. He hears a knocking sound and decides to go check it out. Petrofsky then sees a creature crawling on deck. Before he can react, the creature lunges at him and slashes his throat with its claws, then feeds on his blood. Meanwhile, Clemens finds the hole on the cargo hold and Petrofsky’s knife on the deck. Seeing this he rings the bell to alert everyone. Next morning, the crew becomes wary when they notice Petrofsky's blood smeared across the deck. Wochek is fast to suspect Clemens, even though Clemens was the one who reported Petrofsky's death. Meanwhile Anna wakes up and explains to Clemens that she knows what is the cause of all this. In her village, she lived near a castle where the creature dwelled. He is none other than Dracula, to whom she was bound to by her village. He bit Anna and had sinister plans to use her as blood rations. Later that night, Olgaren and Larsen are on deck, keeping watch. Suddenly, the same creature strikes again. It goes for Larsen, slamming his face onto the deck before devouring him. Olgaren manages to climb up high to escape from the creature. By then, entire ship wakes up and searches for Olgaren and Larsen. Eventually, they come across Olgaren, knocked out cold, with a bite mark on his head. He's alive but seriously injured. Olgaren is strapped down to a bed to be tended to, but as night descends, he's turned into this blood-thirsty thing. Olgaren manages to break free from his restraints and goes after Toby wandering inside the ship. Toby hides inside the captain's quarters, locking himself in. The rest of the crew senses something's not right and goes down below deck. They manage to control Olgaren and attempt to break into the room, but Toby's still in danger as the creature is stalking him. That's when Anna steps in, grabbing a rifle to shoot the lock off the door. Sadly, by the time the door is opened, the creature has already attacked Toby, draining most of his blood. As Toby receives care, Olgaren is secured to the ship's mast. He insists he can hear every sound, the wind, the ocean, and the blood flowing through everyone's veins. With the sunrise, Olgaren starts to feel an intense burning sensation. Sunlight touches his skin, in excruciating pain, he erupts into flames. Wochek steps in, putting an end to his suffering by shooting him in the head. Abrams takes up the night watch duty on deck. However, Joseph catches him off guard, knocking him unconscious. He takes a lifeboat to get off the ship, desperate to escape from the creature. In the meantime, Clemens and Anna take it upon themselves to inspect the cargo holds in search of the devil. They come across the crate marked with a dragon, managing to open it up. Inside, they find a cane, but the creature itself is nowhere in sight—it's already out, hunting. Having the ability to fly, the devil locates Joseph and ends his life, resulting in the lifeboat returning to the Demeter empty but marked with bloodstains. Next morning, worried that Toby might face the same fate, the crew wraps him in a sheet, readying to cast his body into the sea. Elliot gets confused and thinks he sees Toby moving. He opens the sheet, and Toby turns into a vampire-like state. The sun's rays cause Toby to burn, and even Elliot ends up with burns upon touching him. In a heart-wrenching decision, they throw Toby into the ocean, where he meets his final end. Elliot is left in despair as he faces this heartbreaking loss. As the Demeter draws nearer to England, the crew becomes anxious about the consequences of bringing Dracula with them. They decide that their last stand will be against Dracula, and they plan to sink the ship along with him. Despite Wochek's hesitation—because he sees the ship as his home—the crew stands united. As night descends, the crew prepares for the inevitable encounter with Dracula. The vampire creature swoops down and takes out Abrams as the first victim. Wochek crashes through the deck and injures his leg. Despite his injury, he makes his way to the cargo hold, intending to create a hole in the ship to sink it. However, Dracula tracks him down and ends his life. Elliot decides to go down with the ship. Unfortunately, Dracula locates him and inflicts fatal injuries, leading to his demise. Clemens attempts to fight Dracula, but he gets thrown on the deck. Anna grabs a rifle and fires at Dracula, but it gets a hold off her. Clemens finds an opening and stabs Dracula using his axe. They make a break for it in a lifeboat, but Dracula grabs Clemens by the throat. Clemens stands strong and says he does not fear him. Shockingly, the vampire speaks, uttering the words "You will." Anna cuts down the mast to pin Dracula. She and Clemens make it off the Demeter as it crashes against the shores of England where the lighthouse crew finds it. Dracula, still formidable, pushes the mast away and flees. As morning breaks, Clemens notices Anna's gradual transformation into vampiric state. He suggests another transfusion, but she knows it's only temporary. With a heavy heart, she leaves him. The sunrise marks her final moments, leading to her demise. Clemens arrives in London, learning the Demeter crew is reported dead. He goes to a nearby pub to seek out the abbey where Dracula once lived. There, he hears the ship's knocking sound and discovers Dracula in disguise. Carrying his wolf cane, Dracula is now in London. Clemens follows Dracula outside and vows to not rest, until he sends the creature back to Hell for good.

text: The Nollywood film My Sunshine is an ambitious cultural crossover that attempts to fuse Nigerian storytelling with the stylistic elements of Korean dramas. Directed by Esbayu and produced by Bukumi Aikidan, the movie has garnered attention as the first ever Korean Nigerian cinematic collaboration. While the concept has been praised for its creativity and novelty, the execution has received mixed reviews. The film follows a simple, emotionally driven narrative infused with typical Kdrama tropes, themes of young love, personal growth, and familial expectations, all reimagined within a Nigerian context. However, critics argue that the story lacks depth and sometimes feels rushed or directionless, likely due to the challenge of compressing Kdrama storytelling, usually stretched over many episodes into a single hour runtime. The acting received mixed reactions at Inosa Idmoodia in particular was a standout for her portrayal of F bringing humor and authenticity to her role. Matilda Obasaki Mosia and Bimbo Adamoy also delivered solid performances while MMU impressed in a key emotional scene that added unexpected depth to his character. The Korean integration, while bold, is where the film faltered most. Despite the cast's efforts to learn Korean, many lines lacked fluency and the accents were quite noticeable. While this was expected to some degree, viewers felt it detracted from the authenticity of the cross-cultural narrative. The creative team acknowledged this issue, explaining that Korean lines were scaled back during production to accommodate the language barrier. On the technical front, My Sunshine is commendable. Its cinematography, particularly during emotionally charged scenes like Prom Night, and its sound design were well executed for a film primarily released via YouTube. These visual strengths helped elevate an otherwise uneven script. Reactions from viewers have been polarized. Some praised it for its novelty and cultural experimentation, while others were disappointed by the film's lack of narrative coherence and language delivery. Despite its flaws, My Sunshine has sparked important conversations about the potential for cross-cultural collaboration in African cinema and continues to gain attention internationally, especially among fans of both Mollywood and Kdramas. My Sunshine is a bold, heartwarming experiment that doesn't quite stick the landing. It's charming in parts with moments of emotional resonance and strong performances, but it struggles to fully capitalize on its groundbreaking premise due to execution issues. Still, it stands as a testament to Nollywood's evolving ambition and openness to global storytelling. My Sunshine, the first Korean Nigerian fusion film from Nollywood, which blends Kdrama aesthetics with Nigerian storytelling. Despite mixed reviews, the film explores love, friendship, cultural identity, and the clash of expectations in a vibrant cross-cultural high school setting. The story is centered around Yande, a bright but reserved Nigerian high school student played by Akinsola Esther, who becomes the emotional anchor of the narrative. Her life changes when a group of Korean exchange students joins her school. This move is part of an international partnership program meant to encourage cultural exchange. Among the new arrivals is Minjun, a charming and mysterious Korean student who becomes a focal point of both admiration and envy. text: The movie opens on the icy planet of Niflheim in the year 2054. Mickey 17 wakes up in a ditch, quickly realizing that both his communications and thermal systems are broken. As he assesses his situation, he spots a rescue ship nearby and calls out for help. A man named Timo approaches, seemingly ready to assist. However, just as Timo is about to intervene, he hesitates and tells Mickey that he will only take his flamethrower, not him, because the ship will simply print a new copy of Mickey if he dies. With that, Timo leaves. Left alone, Mickey notices eerie creatures watching him from the distance and comes to a chilling realization. He is about to die. The next day, Mickey's voice over explains the process behind his existence. Each time he dies, his body is reprinted and his consciousness, stored in a device called a brick, is implanted into the new version of himself. He describes how this technology violates every law on Earth, which is why it is only used in outer space, where expendables like him are created for high-risk missions. As part of this process, scientists conduct various experiments on him, exposing him to lethal levels of radiation outside the ship. When he inevitably dies, they simply print a new version of him. Mickey then recounts how he ended up in this situation. His troubles began when a friend convinced him to invest borrowed money into a failing company. Eventually, they were caught and brought before the ruthless Darius Blank, a psychopathic business tycoon. Desperate to escape, Mickey decided to leave Earth and applied for an expedition to help colonize an ice planet. Unaware of what being an expendable truly meant, he submitted his application and was accepted immediately. It was only afterward that an employee explained how the expendable program worked. She detailed the process of printing bodies and transferring memories. As part of the procedure, she took a sample of his body and uploaded his personal memories into a brick, sealing his fate as an expendable. Aboard the spaceship, the crew gathers for lunch when a man named Kenneth Marshall introduces himself. As Mickey meets the crew, he crosses paths with Nasha, one of the members. Marshall then informs everyone that food will be rationed for the duration of the journey until they reach the ice planet. He also announces a ban on any sexual activity during the trip. However, Mickey and Nasha disregard the rule and continue their relationship in secret. Throughout the journey, Mickey dies and is printed multiple times while he and Nasha frequently find themselves in trouble. One day, a girl named Kai approaches Mickey for a conversation, but Nasha, overcome with jealousy, interrupts by kissing him. Months pass and the crew finally arrives at the ice planet. As part of an initial test, Mickey is sent outside to analyze the atmosphere for any unknown viruses. The experiment reveals the presence of a lethal airborne pathogen and Mickey succumbs to the infection. Soon after, he is printed again. Mickey 13, 14, 15, and 16 are each used as test subjects in the mission to develop a cure. After numerous failed attempts and countless deaths, the team finally succeeds in creating a vaccine for the virus. As the crew begins exploring the ice planet, they come across an alien species in a deep trench. In their attempt to flee, one of the crew members is killed. Back on the ship, Marshall furiously reprimands Mickey insisting that as an expendable, he should have been the one to die instead. As punishment, Mickey is forced to work 14-hour shifts with his food rations cut in half until he retrieves a sample of the creatures they encountered. One day, while eating his meal at work, Mickey 17 suddenly loses his footing and falls into a trench. The scene mirrors the beginning of the movie, but this time, when he wakes up, he realizes he is still alive. To his shock, the alien species has spared him. Instead of attacking, they help him out of the trench before disappearing into the icy landscape. As he regains his bearings, Mickey spots a nearby vehicle and boards it. He changes his clothes, returns to his quarters, and prepares to rest only to discover that a new version of himself, Mickey 18, has already been printed under the assumption that he was dead. A chilling realization dawns on Mickey 17. The crew has broken protocol. Multiple versions of him should never exist at the same time. Before he can act, Mickey 18 suddenly strikes him with a dumbbell, knocking him unconscious. Meanwhile, in a past meeting on Earth, the R&D department behind the printing machine is questioned about whether there are safeguards to prevent the technology from being abused. Concerns arise over the potential dangers of uncontrolled replication. Mickey recounts the story of one of the masterminds behind the technology, a man named Manchova, a brilliant but deranged scientist. When the police raided Manchova's house, they discovered not one, but two identical versions of him. However, unbeknownst to them, a third Manchova was still at large, using the technology to commit murders. Eventually, all three versions of Manchova were captured, leading to the passage of a strict law. No duplicates were ever to exist at the same time. Back on the ship, Mickey 18 drags an unconscious Mickey 17 inside a trash can, preparing to dispose of him. However, Mickey 17 is already awake, silently analyzing the personalities of his past iterations. As Mickey 18 moves to dump him into the broiler, Mickey 17 suddenly springs into action, attempting to strike him with a dumbbell. Mickey 18 swiftly counters, overpowering him and forcing him closer to the edge of the broiler. Desperate, Mickey 17 tries to negotiate, but Mickey 18 refuses to listen. Just as he is about to finish the job, someone approaches, forcing Mickey 18 to quickly pull Mickey 17 away to avoid suspicion. Meanwhile, Teemo arrives and begins selling drugs to the crew. Mickey 18, noticing this, confronts Teemo and aggressively shoves him toward the broiler. Mickey 17 rushes to intervene, but is unable to stop him. As the tension escalates, Mickey 18 grabs a metal rod and attempts to force him into the broiler as well. Before he can succeed, Nasha and another crew member arrive just in time, breaking up the fight. Mickey 18 and Nasha leave together, heading to her quarters. As Mickey 17 prepares to follow them, a crew member informs him that he has been invited to a dinner party with Marshall. At the dinner, Mickey 17 finds himself unable to stop devouring the food after weeks of harsh rations. To his surprise, Marshall offers an apology for the way he has treated him. As the evening continues, Kai, another crew member, arrives and joins the gathering. During the dinner party, Marshall praises Kai for her exceptional intelligence, revealing his true intentions. He wants her to become a baby machine to ensure the survival of the colony. Disgusted, Kai immediately shuts him down and shifts the focus to honoring the fallen soldiers, asking everyone to join in prayer. As the crew bows their heads, Mickey 17 suddenly begins vomiting uncontrollably. Alarmed, Marshall calls for the scientists who explain that it's a side effect of a growth hormone they secretly administered to him. In an attempt to ease his suffering, they give him a painkiller, but it fails to work. The pain escalates and Mickey 17 starts screaming in agony. Frustrated, Marshall draws his gun preparing to put him down. Before he can pull the trigger, Kai intervenes, stopping him and escorting Mickey 17 back to her room. In her quarters, Kai offers Mickey 17 some tea she brought from Earth. As the two grow closer and are about to get intimate, Mickey suddenly thinks of Naysha and pulls away, deciding to return to his room. As he leaves, Naysha notices them together and bursts into laughter, playfully writing the numbers 17 and 18 on their respective bodies. Mickey 17 quickly realizes that Naysha and the others are high on drugs. As he and Naysha begin making out, Kai unexpectedly walks in and is horrified to see two Mickeys standing before her. She tries to rush out to report the anomaly, but Naysha stops her. Seizing the moment, Kai makes a bold proposition. She suggests that Naysha keep Mickey 18 while she takes Mickey 17 for herself. Enraged, Naysha, still under the influence, becomes aggressive. Meanwhile, Mickey 17 and Mickey 18 erupt into a heated argument. The confrontation spirals out of control when Mickey 18, blinded by rage, grabs a gun and storms off toward Marshall intent on killing him. At that moment, Marshall is delivering a speech about a mysterious rock formation when one of the crew members suddenly spots a creature moving within the rock. Chaos erupts as Mickey 18 aims his at Marshall, ready to pull the trigger. Before he can shoot, another crew member tackles him, causing further panic. As the crew scrambles to capture the alien creature, Marshall spots Mickey 17 and orders him to join the hunt. While the commotion unfolds, Mickey 18 seizes another opportunity to assassinate Marshall. But before he can act, Marshall finally notices the impossible. Just as the tension seems to settle, another creature suddenly emerges from the damaged rock and leaps onto Marshall. Panicked, he immediately gives the order to kill it, and the crew opens fire, gunning it down. With the crisis momentarily resolved, Marshall turns his attention back to the duplicates. Realizing the violation of protocol, he issues a stern command. Mickey 17 and Mickey 18 are to be arrested immediately. Locked away in the ship's jail, Mickey 17 and Nasha reflect on everything that has happened. They come to a startling realization. The native creatures were the ones who saved Mickey 17 from the trench. Their thoughts are interrupted when Timo arrives, revealing that he has been sent by Darius Blank with a brutal mission. He must record a video of Mickey's execution. However, before he can act, Mickey 18 and Nasha fight back, overpowering Timo and his accomplice. They manage to escape the prison, but their freedom is short-lived. Security quickly captures them, and they are sentenced to execution. As they are being escorted to their fate, they notice something alarming. A massive gathering of the native creatures surrounding the ship. One of the crew members points out that ever since the baby creature was captured, it has been crying non-stop. Meanwhile, inside the ship, Marshall's wife heartlessly amputates the creature's tail and prepares a soup from it. Marshall arrives and, in an effort to keep order, marks Mickey 18 to distinguish him from Mickey 17. Taking his control further, he deletes Mickey's memories from the brick, erasing vital parts of his past. Nasha steps forward, fiercely defending Mickey 18, arguing that he was the one who first spotted the second creature. But Marshall cuts her off, shifting focus to preparing for war. Nasha refuses to back down. She insists that the native creatures don't want war. They will only fight if provoked. One of the scientists proposes an alternative. They could try to communicate with the creatures using a translator. Marshall scoffs at the idea, dismissing it outright. But just then, the captive creature humiliates him in front of the crew, pushing his patience to the limit. Enraged, he lashes out, arguing with Nasha. She refuses to back down, shutting him down completely. Cornered and desperate to assert his dominance, Marshall makes a cruel decision. He orders the creature to be tied up and thrown into the boiler. As it plummets, Nasha reacts instinctively, catching it with her mouth in a last-ditch effort to save it. Meanwhile, one of the crew members discreetly begins recording the entire scene, capturing undeniable evidence of Marshall's brutality. Marshall, determined to wipe out the native creatures, orders his crew to deploy a highly poisonous gas to exterminate them. His wife, always one for cruelty, suggests turning it into a twisted game. Whoever brings back 100 creature tails survives, while the loser dies. Without hesitation, they shove Mickey 17 and Mickey 18 off the ramp and into the frozen wilderness. Before they leave, a sympathetic scientist discreetly hands Mickey 17 a prototype translator. As they venture deeper into the planet's terrain, they eventually arrive at the stronghold of the native creatures and come face-to-face with their leader. Using the translator, Mickey 17 thanks the leader for saving him earlier and urgently warns him that the humans plan to release deadly gas. The leader, however, has his own question. Why did they kill one of their own, a creature named Luco? Mickey 18, ever the cynic, asks what would happen if they killed more of the native children. The leader's response is chilling. If the humans take another young life, the creatures will ensure the complete extinction of every human on the planet. As he speaks, he emits a powerful high-frequency scream, one so intense it could kill humans instantly. Understanding the gravity of the situation, Mickey 17 signals that they need to bring the captured baby back to the natives. Meanwhile, back on the ship, Marshall's adviser argues that Marshall should be the one speaking with the native leader, not Mickey 17. Marshall, always eager to assert control, leaves to confront the situation, temporarily handing over command to his wife. At the negotiation site, the native leader delivers a firm ultimatum. One of the two Mickeys must die as a form of retribution. Back on the ship, Nasha, realizing time is running out, grabs Marshall's wife by the neck and demands that the baby be returned to its people. When she finally releases her, Marshall's wife retaliates, grabbing a knife and slashing the commander's hand. In the struggle, the rope holding the baby nearly slips loose, but Nasha manages to grab it just in time and escapes with the infant. As tensions escalate, both the native leader and Marshall prepare for war. Just before the battle erupts, Nasha arrives, presenting the baby as a peace offering. The leader, seeing his child returned, holds back his forces. Understanding that only one of the duplicates can be allowed to live, Mickey 18 willingly sacrifices himself. Six months later, at a meeting, Mickey 17 reflects on how much has changed. The war never happened, and peaceful communication between humans and the native creatures has begun. Despite the success, he is haunted by strange, vivid dreams. Visions of Marshall and his wife returning from the dead. As the meeting concludes, the crew gathers around Mickey 17, expressing their gratitude for everything he has done. Peace has been secured for now.
title: Mickey 17 Movie Recap.
