text: This is not just a mummy story. It's a curse that jumps from body to body. Once it enters your family, it won't stop until everything is destroyed. And escaping it? Almost impossible. So, the story of the film takes place in a city named Aswan in Egypt, where we see a family happily traveling in a car. In this family, there is a mother, father, two sons, and one daughter. The father and children are enjoying themselves a lot, but the mother looks completely serious and disturbed. When the whole family returns home, they discover that their pet bird is dead. After this, the woman and her husband go down into the cellar of their house, where it is revealed that there is a pyramid-like structure hidden there, completely black in color. It is unclear whether their house was built over an ancient buried pyramid, or whether this was only a miniature version of one. Whatever it was, the couple enters inside it and finds a black basalt sarcophagus. For those who do not know, a basalt sarcophagus is a stone coffin made from black basalt rock. Basalt is an extremely hard volcanic stone formed after lava cools down, which makes it very heavy and durable. In ancient times, such coffins were used to preserve the bodies of powerful or important people, so they would remain safe for centuries. The couple uses chains and pulleys to open the sarcophagus, and inside lies a mummy. The woman nervously asks her husband if the mummy is alive. He says no, and both of them feel relieved. But suddenly, the mummy begins to move. Strange supernatural activity starts happening. Because of this, the chains used to open the coffin strike the husband's face and lift him into the air, killing him instantly. With this, the first scene ends. Now, the story shifts to Cairo, Egypt, where we meet another happy family. The husband's name is Charlie Cannon, who works as a TV investigator. His wife's name is Larissa, and she is currently pregnant. Larissa already has two children named Katie and Sebastian. We also see that Charlie and Katie often communicate through Morse code. One day, Larissa goes out for work while Charlie stays home to look after the children. Katie goes outside to play in the garden. Near the garden fence, an unknown woman begins talking to Katie. We realize that this is the same woman from the first scene, and she introduces herself as a magician. The magician and Katie begin chatting, and the woman entertains Katie with small magic tricks. She then gives Katie a chocolate to eat. From their conversation, we learn that Katie already knows the magician's daughter, Lala. In fact, this woman has been in contact with Katie for several days. Lala is Katie's good friend, and this magician is Lala's mother. After some time, the magician tells Katie that today she has brought a special fruit for her, sweeter than chocolate. Saying this, she hands Katie an apple. The moment Katie takes the apple, an insect crawls out of it and enters her mouth, making Katie choke badly. Inside the house, Charlie discovers many wrappers of the same chocolate hidden inside a cupboard. Seeing this, he suspects that some stranger has been secretly giving chocolates to Katie. Charlie immediately rushes outside to check the garden and notices that the fence is slightly broken and Katie is missing. Charlie starts searching everywhere and soon spots a woman running away with a child. He chases her, but suddenly a violent desert storm strikes the city, preventing him from catching the woman. After this, the scene shifts to the police station, where Charlie and Larissa report their missing daughter. The senior detective suspects that Charlie and Larissa themselves are responsible for Katie's disappearance, which makes Charlie furious. We also meet another detective named Dalia Jacky, who does not agree with her senior officer. In short, Charlie and Larissa receive little help from the police, and they fail to find Katie. Now, the story moves forward by eight years. Charlie and Larissa are still together, but they have never been able to forget Katie. In fact, she has still never been found. Their son, Sebastian, has grown up, and Larissa now has another daughter named Maddie. The family now lives in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Along with them lives Larissa's mother, Carmen, who is a devoted Catholic. Next, we are shown a random scene near the Aswan desert, where a man is fixing the chain of his bicycle. In the background, a small plane suddenly crashes. The man reaches the crash site and finds both pilots dead. There, he also discovers a basalt sarcophagus. The authorities are informed, and two archaeologists bring the sarcophagus to their lab. When they open it, they find a child mummy inside. But the moment they remove some of its layers, the mummy suddenly comes alive. Yes, friends, it appears that a living child had been wrapped like a mummy and sealed inside the coffin. The child is in horrible condition. The wrappings removed from the body contain strange inscriptions that no one can understand yet. The most shocking truth is that this child is none other than Katie, who disappeared eight years ago. Charlie receives a call from the American Embassy informing him that his daughter has been found after eight years, though she is in critical condition. Charlie and Larissa become overjoyed and immediately go to meet her. The doctors warn them that Katie does not appear normal. She is severely malnourished and trapped in deep trauma, to the point that she does not even speak. She is so unstable that even in a catatonic state, she harms herself, which is why she is kept sedated most of the time. Finally, they meet Katie, who now looks like a living mummy. At this point, Charlie and Larissa decide to take Katie back home, so they can care for her and help her become healthy again. Meanwhile, Detective Dalia is now working on Katie's case and promises Charlie that this time she will definitely uncover what happened during those missing eight years. Soon, Charlie and Larissa bring Katie home and give her a separate room. Sebastian is shocked to see his sister again, while Maddie is excited because she has never met Katie before. Katie is placed on the bed, and Carmen begins praying for her. Suddenly, Katie's eyeballs roll toward Carmen, and without warning, Katie headbutts her grandmother so hard that she starts bleeding. Then, Katie lets out a terrifying scream, and her body twists in a horrifying, unnatural manner on the bed. That same night, Katie rises from her bed and begins running inside the hollow walls of the house like a possessed creature. The walls have trapdoors that allow movement inside them. Charlie and Larissa chase her and discover Katie eating a scorpion alive. They force her to vomit and then lock her back inside her room. >> [clears throat] >> After this shocking incident, Charlie receives photos from Dalia of the inscription parchments that had wrapped Katie inside the sarcophagus. Charlie begins studying them. He desperately wants to know what happened to Katie during those lost eight years and is willing to go to any extent. The next day, Larissa and Carmen are cleaning and grooming Katie. Larissa notices that Katie's toenails have grown extremely long. When she tries to trim one nail, the skin of Katie's foot peels off along with it. Underneath, it appears as if the same inscribed parchments are hidden inside her flesh. Katie reacts violently, forcing them to sedate her once again. This completely breaks Larissa, because she cannot bear seeing her daughter in such a state. At the same time, Charlie notices a strange, sticky substance in the house rug. When he goes to check on Katie, he finds Larissa deeply upset. She begins arguing with Charlie, saying that now that Katie has returned, instead of caring for her, Charlie is obsessed with discovering what happened in the past. Larissa says Charlie is still living in the past when he should focus on Katie in the present. We understand that Charlie has always been blamed for Katie's disappearance, but Charlie argues that Katie had been receiving chocolates for days, so Larissa could also have paid more attention. Basically, both husband and wife blame each other, but eventually they comfort one another, too. Afterward, Larissa cries and begs Katie to say something, but Katie only spits on her mother. Later, when Charlie lifts Katie's fallen wheelchair, he notices the same parchment piece stuck in its wheel. He takes it to his room and peels away several layers of inscriptions from it. Clearly, the writing belongs to an ancient language. >> [music] >> So, Charlie visits Albuquerque Community College to get help decoding it. There, he meets archaeology Professor Bixler, who agrees to assist him. Later, when Charlie tries speaking with Katie, she starts making strange clicking sounds with her teeth. At first, Charlie thinks it is random behavior, but then he realizes the pattern is actually Morse code. Charlie writes it down and discovers that Katie is repeating the name Lala. >> [music] >> Charlie informs Dalia, who suggests he investigate whether Katie knew someone named Lala eight years ago. Charlie searches through Katie's old belongings and finds a card from Lala Khalil. Attached to the card is the same chocolate wrapper used to lure Katie. Written on it are the words, "You are sweeter than this chocolate." Meanwhile, Maddie hears a voice coming from Katie's room. When she goes closer, Katie suddenly begins speaking in her normal voice, even though she usually remains silent. Katie tells Maddie that she wants to talk to her and know her. But suddenly, Katie says she wants to test Maddie. Maddie gets frightened and runs away, but Katie begins chanting in a demonic voice and lifts Maddie into the air. After some time, Maddie falls to the ground, and we understand that the evil force inside Katie has now infected Matty as well. Meanwhile, Dalia tracks the letter back to Oswan and discovers a strange nectarine farm in the desert, which seems highly suspicious. She links it to the plane crash site and decides to investigate alone. At the same time, Charlie meets Professor Bixler, who has partially translated the inscriptions. He reveals that the language is older than 3000 BC and belongs to an ancient ceremonial binding ritual. One word appears repeatedly, Nazmarian. The professor then plays a recording explaining that Nazmarian is a demon that lives among humans like a shadow. It destroys families, making fathers kill sons and mothers bury their children. It spreads like a disease by passing from one body to another. Around 2000 BC, its appearances supposedly stopped because it had been trapped through an ancient ritual. Charlie is horrified and begins to believe that this demon may now be inside Katie. Meanwhile, Dalia investigates the house from the opening scene and discovers evidence of rituals. She is attacked by the magician woman, but Dalia shoots her. She captures Lala, who reveals the horrifying truth. The cult transfers the demon from one host body to another through a ritual. Katie had been selected as the new host. The ritual involves wrapping a living person in inscribed bandages. As the bandages are removed, the demon grows stronger and stronger. Because the demon cannot be destroyed, it must be imprisoned inside a living host, preferably a child since children live longer. The plane crash interrupted the ritual process, leaving Katie exposed and partially freed. Afterwards, Carmen goes into Katie's room and starts praying for her. But things take a dark turn when Katie suddenly bites her grandmother's hand and jumps on her, starting to speak in a demonic way. Carmen tries to save her life and escape, but she cannot resist much because Katie locks the room in a supernatural way and then keeps teasing her grandmother without stopping. At one point, Katie starts laughing and uses Carmen's cross, wrapping it around her neck in a supernatural way and lifting her into the air, causing Carmen to start choking. Then she pushes her with such force that Carmen crashes through the window and falls down. At the same time, Charlie is returning home with his daughter Matty and son Sebastian, and Carmen's injured body falls directly onto their car. Not only that, but coyotes suddenly appear and start tearing apart Carmen's body, leaving everyone in complete shock while Matty watches everything and laughs. Larissa also breaks down after seeing her mother brutally becoming a victim of coyotes. In the next scene, we see Carmen's wake ceremony, but instead of normal mourning, extremely disturbing things happen. Matty pulls out all of her teeth and then wears Carmen's dentures, which is extremely creepy. At the same time, Katie starts manipulating her brother Sebastian and makes him feel guilty. Then Katie breaks the floor of her locked room and begins crawling on the ceiling below. And in front of everyone, she jumps into Carmen's coffin and starts biting her and licking her blood. This horrifying scene scares all the guests and they run away, but one of them becomes a victim of the possessed Matty while Larissa and Charlie are left completely shaken. After this, they tie Katie to a wheelchair, lock her room with multiple locks, and even place guards outside so she cannot escape. Meanwhile, Katie keeps making strange noises and even lifts her wheelchair into the air before slamming it hard onto the ground. Right after that, Dalia arrives at the house with a cassette that reveals the full truth. In the recording, the magician explains that their family is part of an ancient cult that controls a demon called Nazmarian. The method is extremely horrifying. A living host is wrapped in special inscribed bandages, and as these bandages are removed, the demon becomes more powerful. Since the demon cannot be destroyed, it is transferred from one host to another, and children are chosen because they can survive for longer periods. The video also shows the ritual itself, where a black demonic substance comes out of the previous host and enters Katie, allowing the demon to take control of her body. This truth is extremely heartbreaking for parents as they witness such brutality against their daughter. However, everything goes wrong when the plane carrying the sarcophagus crashes, leaving the ritual incomplete and ultimately setting both Katie, who has now become a living mummy, and the demon free. Back in the present, Katie manipulates Sebastian into removing the last remaining bandages from her body, fully unleashing the demon. Now Nazmarian is completely free. Chaos erupts throughout the house. Matty, Sebastian, and even the dead Carmen become possessed. Katie begins levitating. Storms rage around her and everyone starts attacking one another. Katie attacks Charlie and bites him. Carmen forces a scorpion into Dalia's mouth, but Dalia survives. Charlie realizes there is only one way to stop all of this. He must transfer the demon into himself. He grabs Katie and asks Dalia to recite the ritual words. Despite her injured throat, Dalia chants the words. And the demon leaves Katie's body and enters Charlie. Charlie sacrifices himself in order to save his daughter. After the transfer, Katie becomes normal once again. Later, Charlie is sealed inside a coffin-like structure covered in inscriptions so the demon can remain contained. Katie taps I love you in Morse code and Charlie taps the same reply back to her. Time passes and all the children recover. But the demon still remains trapped inside Charlie. In the final twist, Larissa and Dalia secretly transfer the demon from Charlie into the magician woman, who is still alive in prison. And with that, the film ends.

text: The night didn't end with shattered glass and spilled blood. It only began there. Because as Hank crouched low behind the counter of his small apartment, the deafening echo of the bullet still rattling in his ears. He felt his heart pounding with the rhythm he hadn't he felt since his days on the pitcher s mound. That same pressure of knowing the next move could decide the whole game. But this time the stakes weren't just a win or a loss. This time it was life or death. And he knew instinctively that whoever had pulled that trigger wasn't he some junkie on street or some unlucky burglar. These were professionals. Killers who didn't care about the broken man he had become. Killers who cared only about what was inside the duffel bag. Now sitting like a curse in the middle of his living room floor. And Hank trembling yet somehow steady in his decisions. Pulled the wounded man's so-called acquaintance across the room pressing an old rag against the gunshot wound in his side demanding answers. But all he got in return was a choking cough and the muttered words. They'll kill us both if you don't run. Words that sank into Hank's chest like another bullet. Because he realized then that he wasn't just caught in some stranger's trouble. He was already part of it whether he wanted to be or not. And as another round of gunfire sprayed across the room, tearing through the framed photographs of his once hopeful youth. Hank grabbed the bag and the bloodied man and stumbled toward the fire escape. The metallic groan of the ladder echoing as he descended into the alley below where the stench of garbage and the flicker of a faulty street light gave the night an even more sinister air. It was there in that grimy alleyway that hangers saw them the hunters to men in dark suits with faces carved from stone and eyes that glow with the kind of calm cruelty that made his stomach twist. And though their footsteps were slow, deliberate, almost casual, Hank could feel the storm of violence that followed them like predators circling prey to wheat to fight. And in that instant, Hank made a choice. Not the kind of man thinks through. Not the kind that makes sense in the morning light, but the kind that comes from the gut from fear and desperation. The kind that decides if you live another minute. And so he ran, dragging his injured companion along. The duffel bag slung over his shoulder like an anchor pulling him deeper into. Hell, his breath ragged, his muscles screaming, yet his mind racing faster than ever because with every corner he turned, every shadow he passed, he could feel the city closing. And on him, the skyscrapers looming like watchtowers, the alleys twisting like mazes designed to trap him. And somewhere in the distance, the hum of sirens blended with the pounding of his pulse. And still he ran, his thoughts flashing back to the life he had wasted, to the promise of a career cut short, to the nights he drowned in cheap whiskey instead of fighting for something better. And now, in this twisted irony, it was that same survival instinct he thought he had lost that kept him moving forward. Because though Hank Thompson was no hero, though he was no fighter by choice, in that moment, he became something else entirely a man who refused to die. Not without taking a piece of the world with him. And as he ducked into an abandoned subway tunnel, the screech of the rails echoing above. He felt the reality of a situation settle heavy on his shoulders. The bag wasn't he just money. It was leveraged power. The kind of power people kill for. The kind of power that drag nobies like him into wars they never asked for. And the hunters would never stop. Not tonight. Not ever. Cuz once you're marked in this city, there's no clean way out. There's only blood and betrayal. And Hank for the first time in years realized he wasn't afraid anymore. He was ready. text: Late in the 21st century, Earth’s food supply is running out. Crops are going extinct, and dust storms occur with alarming frequency. The government has done away with the military, and schools use standardized testing to determine whether a child will go down one of two paths: to college, or to work as farmers to fight food scarcity. Former pilot Cooper is one of many of these farmers, but he still has nightmares about his time as a pilot, especially the day he almost crashed on his jet. His wife died of a brain cyst that wasn’t found because MRI machines are no longer made, so now he has to take care of his children Murph and Tom with the help of their maternal grandfather Donald. Lately, Murph has been visited by what she calls a “ghost” in her bedroom. Books have been falling off her shelf and she believes the ghost is speaking to her. However, Cooper tells her that ghosts aren’t real and that she must use science to figure out what is actually happening. From then on, Murph writes down the position of the books that fall to figure out if it’s Morse code. One morning when Copper is taking the kids to school, they have to stop the truck when they get a flat tire. While they work on changing it, they're shocked to suddenly see a drone flying above them. Desperate to follow it, Cooper pushes the family back into the truck and drives with the tire still flat. They leave the road and cross the harvest field, where Cooper gives Tom the wheel so he can take out his computer and try to hack the drone. After a long chase, Tom is forced to stop the truck when they reach a high cliff edge, but fortunately, Cooper has managed to gain control of the drone and makes it come back. Then they proceed to pull the pieces apart so they can use them for repairs at home. One day, the family is enjoying a baseball game when suddenly sirens start wailing, and the public notices a huge sandstorm approaching. Everyone puts on their masks and goggles and drives through the sand doing their best not to run over the running citizens everywhere. When they make it home, they rush to close the window to Murph’s room, and Cooper’s shocked to notice the sand left behind some kind of code on the floor. Cooper spends many hours figuring it out and realizes it isn’t a ghost, it’s a strange gravitational anomaly. It’s not Morse either, it’s binary, and Cooper translates it to reveal a set of coordinates. Immediately Cooper takes his truck to visit those coordinates and tells Murph she can’t come, but she sneaks into the vehicle without him noticing. When night falls, they make it to an unknown area, and Cooper cuts down the gate blocking them. A flashlight suddenly turns on, and a voice threatens Cooper before tasing him. Seconds later, Cooper wakes up inside the building and is interrogated by TARS, a tactical robot. Then Doctor Amelia enters the room and Cooper recognizes her as the daughter of the famous scientist. Amelia leads Cooper to a conference room where Amelia's father Professor Brand and Murph are hanging out with some important men. After Cooper explains how they found the place, the group reveals they're NASA and opens a panel to show they're building a real rocketship. As he shows Cooper around the labs, Brand explains that he knows society doesn't support funding for space exploration anymore because of the famine, however, they've changed their work to find a solution to the food shortage. The blight disease kills the crops and consumes the oxygen on Earth, so Brand predicts that Murph's generation will be the last to survive. NASA doesn't plan to save the world, they want to leave it. Then Brand introduces Cooper to Project Endurance, whose mission is to find a habitable planet. Brand wants Cooper to be his pilot and when Cooper hesitates because of his family, Brand convinces him by pointing out that this is the only way to save them. Next Cooper gets briefed about the details of the mission. NASA has discovered a wormhole near Saturn that leads to another galaxy and thinks that some aliens placed the wormhole there to help humans. Ten years ago, NASA sent twelve astronauts to twelve planets, but only three of them have sent messages back. The new mission has two plans: Plan A is to use the entire facility as a spacecraft that will harness gravitational forces to propel itself and the surviving humans into space, although the process is still a theory. Cooper would be Plan B, which will send thousands of fertilized eggs to start a colony on the new planet. Brand promises that Plan A will be operational by the time Cooper returns. When Cooper returns home, Murph is upset to hear her father is leaving. Donald confronts Cooper about such a dangerous decision, but Cooper’s sure that the mission is humankind’s final hope. The next morning, Cooper talks to Murph, saying that he's only doing this for her and Tom. Murph is still angry and tries to change his mind, showing him that she deciphered the ghost’s message and it says “stay.” Cooper doesn't listen and as a goodbye gift, he gives her a watch, telling her that time in space is slower than on Earth and that they may be the same age when he returns. Sadly Murph throws it away in anger. Afterward, he says goodbye to the rest of the family and drives away, so by the time Murphm finally comes out, it’s too late. Moments later the rocket launches and Cooper leaves Earth with a crew formed by TARS, Amelia, Doyle, and Romilly. The trip isn’t very long and sometime later they make it safely to the Endurance space station, where they dock the spacecraft as carefully as possible. The crew enters the station and begins powering it everything up as they meet CASE, another robot. Soon the boosters are working and the station begins spinning to fly them away. Now the crew starts their two-year journey to Saturn, so they’ll be entering cryosleep. While getting ready, Amelia shares stories about the other three astronauts they may meet later: Mann, Miller, and Edmunds. Mann in particular is known for being an inspiration for others to join. Later Cooper asks TARS if Amelia has a relationship with Doctor Edmunds, but TARS is programmed not to disclose sensitive information. Before going to sleep, Cooper sends a video message back to Earth, but when Brand takes it to the family, Murph isn’t interested. Brand talks to Donald and offers to take Murph under his wing. Two years pass, and when Cooper wakes up, the first thing he does is watch the video message his family sent back. It only takes the crew a few hours to find the wormhole and they brace themselves to cross it, ready to reach a whole new different galaxy. The spacecraft shakes during the whole trip because of the crazy speed, and Amelia swears she sees a distortion that looks like an arm. She assumes it’s one of the aliens that put the wormhole there and reaches back, saying it’s the first handshake. Just a few moments later, the spacecraft stabilizes and flies calmly again. They discover there are three planets orbiting a wormhole known as Gargantua, the same three the previous astronauts visited. An hour on one of these planets equals seven years on Earth, and soon an argument ensues. Doyle wants to proceed with plan B and let everyone on Earth die, so Cooper proposes a middle ground: the spacecraft will travel to the opposite side of Gargantua so that their time won't get affected when they land. The crew agrees to this, and CASE comes along to the expedition on the ship while Romilly stays in the station waiting for their return. As the ship approaches the planet, it begins experiencing heavy turbulence. Cooper uses all his pilot skills to guide the ship carefully, pulling a special maneuver to land safely on the vast surface of the water. Cooper stays in the ship while Doyle and Amelia go exploring with CASE, discovering that the planet has 110% Earth gravity. As they walk around, CASE finds debris from Doctor Miller's beacon, so they try to find the rest of the wreckage, thinking they walking towards the mountains. However, Cooper realizes that the mountains are actually giant waves and one is coming after them. Amelia ignores it because she wants to find Miller’s data, but when she does, she falls as she tries to grab it. CASE transforms into a wheel and saves her, bringing her back to the ship. Doyle tries to rush back too, but when he's about to enter, the waves carry him away before flooding the interior of the ship. The crew gets tossed around inside as waves shake the ship all over the place. Eventually, the wave stops and although the ship floats calmly, it’s also heavily damaged. A furious Cooper snaps at Amelia for wasting their time, now they’ve lost Doyle and a whole decade back on Earth. Amelia says that Doctor Miller probably landed on the planet hours ago due to the time difference, explaining why the wreckage was somewhat intact. At that moment, another giant wave appears and is about to hit them again. Cooper immediately returns to the controls and concentrates on activating the ship, expertly flying around the wave to get them out of the planet safely. When they return to the station, they discover twenty-three years have passed for Romilly. He’s learned all he can from the black holes, but couldn't send his research to Earth. A sad and desperate Cooper rushes to the messages the station received and watches twenty-three years of videos of his son growing up and forming his own family. Tom is now an adult and he explains Donald died, so they buried him with their mom. He also says Murph has grown distant and he’s accepting Cooper isn’t coming back, so this is his last message. Afterward, there’s a video from adult Murph, who insults her dad for leaving and points out they’re now the same age. Back on Earth, Murph hangs up and goes back to work. It turns out Murph is now working with NASA too and she wants to finish Brand’s theory to help save the world. After staring at the board for a while, she realizes that they've been looking at the equation all wrong. Brand knows this, but he doesn’t explain why he won’t change it. In The Endurance, the crew discusses what planet to visit next. Amelia wants to go to Edmund’s, who stopped transmitting some time ago, but Cooper thinks Mann’s is a better choice because he’s still active. Before Romilly can vote, Cooper tells him about Amelia’s bias because she’s in a relationship with Edmund. Instead of denying it, Amelia says the idea of their love is more than enough of a reason for them to choose Edmund. Nobody is moved by her speech, and Mann’s planet wins the vote. Now Amelia’s angry with Cooper, saying that if Mann's planet isn't suitable, they'd have to either return or continue with Plan B on Edmund's planet, which would sacrifice the lives of billions on Earth. Back on Earth, Murph rushes to the hospital to visit Brand, who is dying. She promises she’ll carry on with his work, but Brand uses his last breath to make a confession: Project Endurance was never meant to return and the theory for plan A isn’t achievable. Before Murph can ask for more, Brand dies, and Murph has to be the one to send a message to Amelia. In the video, Murph accuses Amelia of knowing about her father's lies. Sometime later, the spacecraft safely lands on the next planet, where they can see snowy mountains and a whole base. They get inside and find a cryosleep pod, so they open it to wake up Doctor Mann. The poor doctor cries at seeing another person because he had lost all hope and his resources were almost gone. Once he’s calmed down, Mann shows the crew around the planet. They are currently at a peak where there is no breathable air, but the planet also has a lower surface where life is possible. The discussion of how to carry on their plan is interrupted by TARS, who has a message for Amelia. She plays the video for everyone to hear and Murph reveals all the lies, but Amelia swears she didn’t know anything. However Mann does know about it: he says that Brand solved the equation even before the astronauts left, but simply proving the theory isn't enough. They need information on what's inside the black hole to put it into practical use, but the laws of nature don't allow that. Mann supports Brand's actions, saying that sacrificing the lives of the billions on Earth is necessary to save the human race. Cooper refuses to accept this and plans to return to Earth. Back on Earth, Murph tells the truth to her colleague and boyfriend Getty, who thinks they should inform the public of this. Murph refuses because she still hasn't given up on Plan A, thinking that the ghost from her childhood had told her to work on this. In the station, Cooper gets ready to return, and Romilly offers an idea: they could throw TARS in the black hole so that he can collect information about what's inside. TARS gladly accepts this mission. Afterward, Mann prepares to construct the laboratory and habitat modules brought by the Endurance, and Cooper goes with him to scout out potential areas. While the duo walks around, Mann begins a weird conversation about survival instincts, and when they reach the edge of a cliff, Mann removes Cooper's transmission device and pushes him off. Cooper manages to hold onto some rocks, and when Mann comes down to kick him, Cooper grabs him and takes him down with him. Once they reach the ground, Mann explains he can’t let Cooper leave with the ship and confesses he faked the data so someone would come to rescue him, in truth the planet isn’t actually habitable. Back on Earth, Murph visits her old room to decipher the ghost messages while Getty checks on Tom's family, who is very sick. Getty scolds Tom for not leaving their home like everyone else is doing, and Tom punches Getty for it. When Murph wonders if Tom is waiting for his kid to die, Tom kicks them out. On their way out, Murph drives into the cornfields and starts dowsing the crops with fuel to then start a fire before leaving. Tom quickly sees the flames and comes to take care of them, giving Getty the chance to rescue the family and Murph to return to her room. Meanwhile, on the planet, Cooper and Mann get into a fight, but when Cooper overpowers him, Mann headbutts Cooper’s helmet to expose him to the toxic air. While Mann gets away, Cooper crawls to his communicator and asks Amelia for help. CASE and Amelia immediately fly back to rescue him, arriving right before Cooper suffocates. While Cooper tells Amelia the truth, Romilly begins modifying TARS. However, when he looks at the data in Mann’s own robot, he discovers the truth as well. At that moment Amelia contacts him through the radio, but suddenly, an explosion happens on the base. When Amelia and Cooper come back to the base, they only see the remaining disaster and TARS rushing out from the flames. They pick the robot up and learn that Romilly’s dead while Mann takes his own ship back to the station. Cooper tries to get in contact with him and make him see reason, but Mann ignores them. At that moment CASE informs the crew that the auto-docking procedure on board the station is disabled, so it’s almost impossible for Mann to board Endurance successfully. Cooper tries to warn Mann, but this time Mann turns off communications completely and attempts to dock manually anyway. After lots of hovering and shaking, the ship touches the hatch, yet Mann fails to align it. Ignoring the blaring alarms, Mann opens the hatch anyway, and the airlock immediately explodes, destroying part of the station and pushing it away. The crew watches the explosion with horror and notices debris is coming in their direction. Cooper immediately flies around the debris and approaches the station on purpose, saying he will dock even at this extreme speed. CASE says it’s impossible, but Cooper insists it’s necessary and pulls a crazy maneuver to put the ship under the docking area right before Endurance leaves the stratosphere of the planet. TARS opens up the hatch and Cooper carefully guides the ship, his amazing pilot skills managing to dock it at the station with perfect precision. Now the ship stops the station’s rotation and pushes it out of the stratosphere. The duo’s celebration is short-lived because CASE announces they’re headed to Gargantua, and the ship is quite damaged. A second generator is keeping up the system, but the navigations are destroyed, so they can’t return to Earth. Their only choice is to reach Edmund’s planet, so Cooper plants to use Gargantua as a giant slingshot to get them there. To do this they have to get rid of all the weight they can, including TARS. Amelia doesn’t like the idea, but TARS is fine with this since his only goal is to save humankind. Soon Endurance is in Gargantua’s orbit, shocking the crew with its bright light. The station reaches the maximum velocity and the engines push for pull power, then the ship starts moving toward the exit as TARS says his final goodbye and detaches from the ship. Next, CASE announces Cooper’s section shall be detached as well. Amelia can’t believe what she’s hearing, and Cooper explains that there aren’t enough resources for both of them, so this is his way to give humanity a last hope. Amelia cries as she sees Cooper sacrificing himself, his station unit falling into the black hole. Darkness surrounds Cooper’s ship for a few moments until suddenly, flashes of light start to appear, looking almost like droplets of rain. The ship then begins shaking and the exterior burns up as the gravitational pull puts too much pressure on it, causing Cooper to lose consciousness. The computer suddenly wakes him up, reminding him to eject his seat. Cooper is released from the ship and he floats around in the darkness, passing through a cold corridor full of flashing lights before landing into a seemingly endless corridor. Cooper manages to hold on to the walls to stop the fall, and as he looks around, he realizes that the wall is made up of books. When he looks on the other side, he discovers some sort of room, so he bangs on the shelves to make the books fall. This reveals a young Murph on the other side. Cooper desperately tries to talk to her, but she never hears him, so Cooper remembers the message she decoded and spells “stay” as a way to ask her to never leave this room until she understands everything. While Cooper sees himself saying goodbye to young Murph, he cries hopelessly because he sees his leaving as a mistake. In the present older Murph starts to pull out the books as well and finally understands the ghost had been her father all along. Now she has to wait for a new message from him. At that moment, TARS gets in contact with Cooper. The robot has survived with the data and explains this is the dimension created by the aliens that put the wormhole, here time is a physical plane. Cooper realizes that since gravity can travel through time, this corridor is connected to all the years in Murph’s life, and he can send a message to Murph. It was humans themselves who built this place in the future and sent him back so Murph could save the world. No other human can travel through these corridors properly, it has to be Cooper because Amelia had been right, and the power of his love for Murph is powerful enough to guide him. Ready to solve the entire issue, Cooper asks TARS for NASA’s coordinates in binary and sends it to his past self in the form of the sand, putting his hands against the storm. Then he goes to present Murph and uses the watch he left her to give her all the quantum data from the wormhole that TARS gathered using Morse code, now Plan A can be more than just a theory. Murph grabs the watch and notices the second's arm ticking in Morse code. Excited to see confirmation her dad is alive, she runs outside and hugs Tom just in time to stop another fight between him and Getty. Afterward, Murph returns to Brand’s office, and with the help of the watch, she finally figures out how to execute Plan A. She resets the equation and designs it from zero, then gleefully announces to everyone in the base that their future has been saved. Meanwhile, in the quantum corridor, TARS informs Cooper that their plan worked and the dimension is closing up. Suddenly Cooper gets consumed by the bright light, and as he floats away, he sees Amelia reaching out her hand to him before he passes out. text: The first Insidious film introduces the Lambert family, husband and wife Josh and Renai, and their children Dalton, Foster, and Cali. Shortly after moving into their new home, Dalton enters the attic where he encounters a mysterious entity that eventually puts him into a coma. Three months later, as Dalton has yet to wake up, the family begin to experience a series of horrific events, including strange noises in the night, bloody handprints appearing on walls, Dalton beginning to sleepwalk, and even Renai being attacked by a paranormal apparition. Thinking their house is haunted, the Lamberts move away, though the paranormal activity follows them to their new home. Josh’s mother, Lorraine arrives, warning of visions of a red-faced demon, and calls in the help of psychic Elise Rainier and her assistants, Specs and Tucker. Elise explains that while he thought he was dreaming, Dalton had actually gained the ability to astral project his consciousness into a purgatory dimension known as the Further. Dalton’s mind has been captured by evil spirits in the Further, who are seeking a way to use his body to re-enter the physical world. While Josh first dismisses these claims, he eventually discovers that he possesses the same abilities as Dalton, and had repressed memories of Elise helping him similarly escape the Further as a child. The group quickly determine that the only way to save Dalton is for Josh to astral project into the Further to rescue him. Inside the Further, Josh fights his way through various spirits, including the red-faced demon and the spirit of an old woman who had tried to possess him as a child, eventually rescuing Dalton and returning to the physical world. As the family celebrate Dalton’s rescue, Elise senses something amiss and discovers that the spirit of the old woman has possessed Josh’s body. Upon being caught, Josh murders Elise before returning to his family. In Insidious: Chapter 2, the Lamberts are under investigation for the murder of Elise. As the Lamberts move in with Lorraine, they once again begin to suffer from paranormal activity, while Josh is urged by a demonic voice to kill his family. When Lorraine realizes that Josh is possessed, she instructs Renai to take the kids and run. Meanwhile, Specs and Tucker begin looking more into Josh’s history, discovering in old video tapes from Elise’s time with him as a child that the adult Josh can miraculously be seen in the footage. Working with Elise’s former colleague, Carl, the trio discover that Josh had been attacked by a serial killer named Parker Crane as a child, who wore a black gown and was dubbed the Bride in Black. And so, it is in fact Parker Crane who is the Old Woman possessing Josh. Carl, Specs, and Tucker confront the possessed Josh in an attempt to free him from Parker’s control, leading to Josh attacking them and inadvertently sending Carl to the Further. There, Carl reunites with the dead Elise and the real Josh. In the real world, the possessed Josh begins attacking his family, prompting Dalton to enter the Further to help his father take back control of his body. Inside the Further, the group becomes unstuck in time, eventually discovering that Parker Crane was viciously abused by his mother, Michelle, who forced him to act like a girl and led him toward his violent tendencies. During a final confrontation with Michelle, Elise kills the spirit with the help of a young Parker, putting the Bride in Black’s soul to rest. With the spirit defeated, Dalton is able to lead his father out of the Further and fully reclaim his body. Carl then uses his abilities to help the Lamberts once again suppress their horrific memories and happily move on with their lives. Insidious Chapter 3 is set three years before Dalton’s possession and focuses on Elise’s return to the profession of demonology. Grieving the death of her husband and traumatized by her years of experiences with spirits and the Further, Elise has given up on her profession. When teenager Quinn Brenner seeks out Elise’s help in communicating with her recently deceased mother, Elise refuses. Quinn then becomes the target of a spirit known as “the Man Who Can’t Breathe”, leading her to be hit by a car and temporarily confined to a wheelchair. Quinn’s father, Sean, seeks out the help of internet demonologists Specs and Tucker, but quickly realizes that they are frauds. Carl encourages Elise to offer her assistance in saving Quinn, and upon meeting Specs and Tucker, she invites them to join her in her mission. Elise then enters the Further to battle the Man Who Can’t Breathe, but realizes that Quinn would need to defeat the spirit herself. Elise seeks out Quinn’s mother, Lily, in the Further to aid her daughter, leading her to successfully defeating the spirit. With Quinn saved, Elise bids farewell to the family and decides to officially return to demonology, with Specs and Tucker working as her new assistants. Elise Rainier’s story continues in Insidious: The Last Key. Elise, Specs, and Tucker are hired by a man named Ted Garza to investigate the paranormal anomalies at his house, which just so happens to be Elise’s childhood home. The home brings back traumatic memories for Elise, whose father was abusive and mother was killed by a demon. Elise had fled the house as a child to escape her father’s beatings, abandoning her brother, Christian. Elise, Specs, and Tucker eventually discover that Ted is actually holding a young woman prisoner inside his home and Specs is forced to kill him in self-defense. Christian then returns to his childhood home with his daughters, Melissa and Imogen, though he remains bitter at Elise for abandoning him decades prior. Melissa is attacked by the demon from Elise’s childhood, known as Key Face, which traps her in the Further. As Elise searches for a way to save Melissa, she discovers that her father, Gerald, had also kidnapped and locked up young women inside their home. Elise is then attacked by Key Face, once again pulling her into the Further. Fortunately, Imogen possesses the ability to astral project, and enters the Further to save Elise and Melissa. The women discover that Key Face had been possessing Gerald and Ted, forcing them to commit their heinous acts against women, feeding on the women’s fear and hatred for their abusers. As Key Face tries to goad Elise into enacting revenge against her father in the Further, Imogen encourages her not to let Key Face feed on her hatred. As Key Face attacks Elise, Gerald’s spirit sacrifices itself to save her. As Key Face continues to attack the Rainier family, the spirit of Elise’s mother, Audrey, arrives to help defeat the demon. While attempting to escape the Further, the women accidentally open a wrong door, which leads to the young Dalton Lambert. Searching for another exit, they accidentally leave the door open, inadvertently giving the spirits of the Further access to Dalton and setting up the events from the first Insidious film. Upon leaving the Further, Elise reunites with Christian, who finally forgives her for abandoning him. As the film comes to a close, Elise receives a phone call from Lorraine Lambert to help save the possessed Dalton, bringing the story full circle. The story continues nine years later in Insidious: The Red Door. Though his traumas from the Further have been repressed, Josh Lambert is now divorced from his wife, Renai, grieving the recent death of his mother, Lorraine, and struggling to connect with his son, Dalton, who is now a freshman in college. While at school, Dalton paints a picture of the Red Door used to enter the Further, and sees visions of a ghost of a former student. With no memories of his childhood experiences in the Further, Dalton and his new roommate, Chris, begin researching the strange paranormal activities surrounding him. This leads the pair discovering YouTube videos of Specs and Tucker explaining the concept of astral projection, and of Elise discussing the nature of the Further. While experimenting with his newly rediscovered ability to astral project, Dalton is confronted by the red faced demon that attempted to possess him as a child. This leads to Dalton slowly remembering more details of his past, including his possessed father, Josh, attempting to murder their entire family. Dalton’s journey into his own past eventually leads to him being pulled back into the Further and getting trapped inside the red faced demon’s lair. Meanwhile, Josh becomes haunted by the spirit of his late father, Ben. While researching his father, Josh discovers that he too had the ability to astral project, but believed this was all a part of a severe mental illness. As Josh reconnects with his ex-wife, Renai, she helps remind him of his murderous possession a decade prior that permanently fractured their once happy family. Upon discovering that Dalton is now in danger once again, Renai helps Josh return to the Further to save their son. As Josh helps Dalton escape, he chooses to sacrifice himself, staying behind to ensure the Red Door remains closed for good. Back in the real world, Dalton paints black over the red door painting, sealing the real door and containing the evil threats of the Further from escaping. And in the Further, Josh finally comes face to face with the spirit of his father, who helps guide him back to his body and return to the land of the living. In the end, Josh begins to reconcile with his family, allowing the Lamberts to finally and fully move on from a lifetime of trauma.

text: Welcome to Movie Recaps with Brian. Subscribe below for daily recaps. Today we're recapping THE RUNNING MAN, directed by Paul Michael Glaser. By 2017, the United States has descended into authoritarian rule following a worldwide economic collapse and critical shortages of food, fuel, and basic resources. The government maintains its grip on power through constant propaganda, censorship of unsanctioned art and music, and state-controlled television broadcasts. The most popular, and feared, program is The Running Man, a brutal game show where convicted criminals are promised freedom if they can survive as “runners” against heavily armed and theatrically themed assassins called “stalkers.” The show is presented as patriotic entertainment, but in truth, it is both a tool of distraction and intimidation, reinforcing state control while quenching the bloodlust of the population. Captain Ben Richards (played by Arnold Schwarzenegger), once a police officer, becomes a symbol of resistance without meaning to. During a food riot in Bakersfield, California, he refuses an order to open fire on unarmed civilians begging for supplies. His fellow officers slaughter the crowd, but Richards is framed as the instigator, branded the “Butcher of Bakersfield.” Arrested and disgraced, he is sent to a prison labor camp where he spends 18 brutal months enduring forced labor and surveillance. Seizing an opportunity during a violent prison uprising, Richards escapes with two resistance members, Harold Weiss (played by Marvin mcIntryre) and William Laughlin (played by Yaphet Kotto). While they urge him to join their underground movement, Richards is skeptical of political causes, he only wants to stay alive and perhaps clear his name. His search takes him to his brother’s apartment in Los Angeles, but his brother has been seized for “re-education,” and the apartment is now occupied by Amber Mendez (played by Maria Conchita Alonso), a musician and composer for the state-run network, ICS. Desperate, Richards forces Amber to help him forge documents to bypass airport security and escape the country. But Amber, believing state propaganda about the “Butcher of Bakersfield,” betrays him at the last minute by alerting security. Richards is swiftly recaptured, and Amber begins to realize she may have made a terrible mistake when she sees official broadcasts falsely attributing civilian deaths to Richards. Meanwhile, Damon Killian (played by Richard Dawson), the arrogant, ratings-obsessed host of The Running Man, sees Richards as the perfect contestant to revive the show’s declining popularity. Slick, narcissistic, and utterly ruthless, Killian manipulates Richards into participation by threatening Weiss and Laughlin’s lives. When the game begins, Killian betrays Richards anyway, sending all three men into the lethal game zone, a sprawling wasteland of abandoned Los Angeles carved into four hostile quadrants. The show begins with spectacle: Richards and his allies are fired into the zone via rocket sleds as audiences cheer from the safety of their homes. The first stalker unleashed is Subzero, a hockey-themed killer armed with a bladed stick and explosives. In a shocking reversal of the show’s tradition, Richards fights back and kills Subzero—making him the first runner ever to defeat a stalker. The audience is stunned, and whispers of sympathy for Richards begin to ripple. At ICS headquarters, Amber’s suspicion grows. She sneaks into restricted archives and uncovers unedited footage of Bakersfield, proving that Richards was framed and the massacre was committed by the government. Before she can act, she is caught and thrown into the game zone as punishment. As the game escalates, new stalkers are deployed: Buzzsaw, a sadistic biker wielding a chainsaw and Dynamo, a flamboyant opera-singing assassin who electrocutes victims with a suit of weaponized lights. Richards engages both. He kills Buzzsaw in a brutal struggle but suffers the loss of Laughlin, who is mortally wounded. Dynamo is incapacitated, but Richards pointedly spares his life, shocking viewers who have only ever seen bloodthirsty executions on the show. Meanwhile, Weiss discovers a satellite uplink hidden within the game zone, the key to overriding government broadcasts. Before Dynamo kills him, Weiss passes the access code to Amber, making her the only person who can complete the mission. Amber, while searching for safety, uncovers a horrifying secret: the mummified corpses of previous “winners” of The Running Man, proving that nobody ever truly earned freedom. Fueled by anger, she continues to aid Richards. Together they kill Fireball, a flamethrower-wielding stalker, further electrifying the audience and causing unrest among viewers who now cheer Richards’ defiance instead of the stalkers’ carnage. With the regime’s credibility cracking, Killian resorts to dirty tactics. He tries to coerce Captain Freedom (played by Jesse Ventura), a retired stalker and former fan-favorite, to face Richards. But Freedom, disgusted with Killian’s manipulative methods, refuses to participate unless it’s a fair fight. Instead, ICS fabricates digital footage showing Freedom killing Richards and Amber. This staged victory is broadcast nationwide, but the cracks in the illusion are becoming too obvious. Richards and Amber are rescued by the underground resistance, led by Mic, who recognizes the value of Weiss’s uplink codes. Together, they launch a final assault on the ICS broadcasting center. As chaos erupts on the studio floor, Dynamo ambushes Amber, but she cleverly activates the sprinkler system, short-circuiting his electrical suit and killing him. Richards storms the control room, where he confronts Killian before a live audience. Killian, arrogant until the end, offers Richards a job as a stalker, claiming they could become legends together. Richards rejects him, instead forcing him into a rocket sled and launching him into the game zone. With no safety controls, the sled crashes and explodes, killing Killian spectacularly, an ironic reversal of his own twisted showmanship. As resistance forces broadcast the unedited Bakersfield footage and the truth about the government’s lies across the airwaves, the population begins to rise up. The studio audience, once bloodthirsty spectators, cheer Richards as a hero. In the aftermath, Richards and Amber embrace amid the crumbling façade of state propaganda. The television signal goes dark, marking the symbolic collapse of the regime’s strongest weapon, its control of the narrative.

As they search through one of the cartons inside the vehicle, Loose discovers a book that Shiloh used to document her daring bucket list. The book contains all the dangerous adventures she had either planned to experience or had already accomplished. As Jax touches her sister's belongings, memories of the past begin flooding back. She remembers the time she and Shiloh went skydiving together and briefly gets lost in the memory. Afterward, Jax tells Loose that she can keep everything they found inside the car. She makes the offer because looking at Shiloh's belongings only makes her feel sad, especially since they remind her of the final memory she has of her sister, which wasn't exactly a pleasant one. Not long afterward, they head inside, where Loose pours Jax a shot to help her relax. She then suggests that perhaps the best way for Jax to finally get the closure she desperately needs is to complete Shiloh's bucket list. Loose explains that they don't have to do everything at once. They can simply take the challenges one after another until the entire list is completed. Curious, Loose checks through the book and discovers that the next challenge on Shiloh's list is a plank walk on Mount Qwan in Thailand. According to Shiloh's description, the walkway sits about 4,000 ft above sea level and eventually leads to a statue that the locals call the death Dragon. Legend has it that the statue eats away your fears if you are brave enough to make it all the way there. Luce immediately asks Jax to accompany her, but Jax refuses, insisting that she isn't nearly as fearless as her sister was. Luce, however, isn't willing to take no for an answer. She encourages Jax to at least keep the book and think about the challenge. She reminds her that if she doesn't confront her fears now, she may never get another opportunity to do so. That night, Jax opens a box containing some of Shiloh's old belongings. While going through everything, she comes across an old memory card filled with footage from adventures the sisters experienced when they were much younger. The discovery brings back even more memories of the bond she once shared with Shiloh. The following morning, as soon as Luce wakes up, she sends Jax a message encouraging her to face her fears. After thinking about everything for a while, Jax eventually gives in and agrees to go. The two women board a plane and eventually arrive in southern Bangkok, Thailand. Along the way, Jax begins having second thoughts when Luce reveals that Mount Quan has been closed to the general public because of serious safety concerns. Still, Jax pushes her doubts aside, determined to face the fear that has been holding her back. A short while later, Mount Quan comes into view and the sheer size of the mountain immediately becomes apparent. As they make their way toward it, the women record videos of their journey, documenting the beginning of their dangerous adventure. Eventually, they reach an area at the foot of the mountain where a party is taking place. They approach a bartender and ask how they can find a guide capable of taking them through the infamous Plank Wall. Unfortunately, the response isn't what they hoped for. The bartender explains that the trail has been shut down because earthquakes have made the route extremely dangerous. Unwilling to simply turn around and return home, they ask about another challenge from Shiloh's bucket list called Icarus on the Rocks. The bartender points them toward another person behind the counter who may be able to help. They approach the man and explain exactly what they're looking for, but his attitude is far from welcoming. One by one, the others leave until only a man named John remains. John eventually offers the women seats and listens to what they have to say. He makes it clear that what they're asking for isn't an ordinary hiking trip. They are essentially looking for someone willing to illegally guide them along what is considered the most dangerous trail in Thailand. John agrees to serve as their guide, but demands $5,000 for the job. Luce attempts to negotiate the price, but John explains the seriousness of the situation and the enormous risks involved. After hearing him out, she agrees to his price just as he's about to walk away. Later that night, they return to their accommodation and settle into their beds. Luce falls asleep almost immediately, but Jax struggles to rest. Her mind keeps returning to the last adventure she shared with Shilo, particularly the day they went skydiving together. The memories continue playing over and over in her mind. When morning finally arrives, Jax gets out of bed, gathers her belongings, and prepares herself for what lies ahead. This is the moment their real adventure begins. They meet John in the center of the city, where he supplies them with the necessary climbing equipment, and gives them a briefing on what they should and shouldn't do during the journey. Once they are properly equipped and prepared, the three of them set off toward Mount Quan. As they travel deeper into the area, Jax notices a disturbing sight, a vulture feeding on a dead body along the path. The sight is unsettling, but they choose not to dwell on it and continue moving deeper into the dangerous terrain. After what feels like an incredibly long journey, they finally reach the ladder that will take them approximately 4,000 ft upward to the beginning of the ancient plank walk. John explains that this is the route they must climb before they can even begin the actual plank walk. When Jax sees how high the ladder stretches, fear immediately takes over. She backs away and admits that she doesn't think she can go go with it. Luce refuses to let her quit, reminding her that she is doing this for Shilo and that completing the challenge would make her sister proud. Eventually, Jax gathers enough courage to continue. John then attaches the two women together using twin hooks so that they remain connected throughout the climb. Once everything is secured, John starts ascending first. After climbing for some time, Loose follows behind him. Jax watches the stairs beneath them shake as they climb higher and she becomes terrified. Every instinct inside her tells her to turn around and stop, but forces herself to ignore the fear and eventually begins climbing as well. At one point, one of the rails Jax is standing on suddenly breaks away beneath her. Fortunately, her safety hook is firmly attached to the chain, preventing her from falling to her death. She manages to hold on and continue the climb. Not long afterward, thick fog begins surrounding the entire area, making visibility extremely poor. John instructs Jax to unhook herself and he reaches down and physically pulls her upward with his hands. By this stage, they have finally reached approximately 4,000 ft above sea level, the starting point of the ancient plank walk. Before beginning the dangerous crossing, John connects Jax and Loose together with safety clips, hoping the extra connection will give them a better chance of surviving if anything goes wrong. With everything secured, the three of them finally step onto the ancient plank walkway on Mount Quan. They carefully make their way across the narrow and unstable structure. After some time, they reach a sharply curved section known as the Devil's Elbow. From that height, the scenery is breathtaking and for a brief moment they stop to admire the incredible view and record a video of themselves there. John soon insists that they put the camera away and focus on continuing the journey. They follow his instructions and proceed along the ancient walkway, believing they are finally making good progress. Unfortunately, their journey soon takes a terrifying turn. As they move forward, they discover that the chains fixed along the mountain walls, the same chains they have been using to steady themselves and clip their safety equipment into are missing for a significant stretch of the path. This leaves them with nothing to attach themselves to as they cross the exposed section. Despite the obvious danger, James tries to reassure them arguing that only a couple of chains are missing and insisting that they should simply keep moving forward anyway. Without wasting another second, Loose left the others behind and continued along the trail without using any safety ropes until she reached the point where the chains resumed. Watching her fearless move, Jax and John called her crazy but her bravery also inspired them to push forward. Jax suddenly phased out for a few minutes and nearly lost her balance but John quickly brought her back to her senses. He handed her a small oxygen tank to help steady her breathing then tossed a rope toward Loose for her to clip onto. With the rope secured, Jax successfully made her way across while John followed behind and retrieved the rope as he went. As night drew closer, heavy rain began pouring down causing tiny pieces of rock to break loose and fall around them. Despite the worsening weather, John insisted that they continue assuring them that they were almost at their destination. The intense downpour eventually triggered an earthquake forcing John to shout at the women to quickly move back so they wouldn't be struck by falling debris while he headed in the opposite direction. Moments later, the falling rocks destroyed part of the path creating a huge gap between John and the two women. Once they got back on their feet, they could no longer see John making Loose believe he had probably fallen to his death. She then convinced Jax that they should turn around promising that they would stick together and make the difficult journey back one step at a time. Eventually, they reached the point where the chains they had been using to secure themselves ended. Loose suggested they repeat what they had done earlier with her taking the lead while Jax followed behind. Holding each other's hands, they slowly began their return journey but this time the wooden planks were extremely slippery and dangerously loose. Jax slipped and nearly plunged off the structure, but Loose managed to keep herself steady and secure the rope onto the chains ahead. Jax crawled toward her, and once she reached her, wrapped her arms around Loose in a relieved hug. A few minutes later, they arrived at the Devil's Elbow, and Jax became excited after finally spotting the ladder that could lead them to safety. Unfortunately, another earthquake suddenly struck, destroying the path ahead and nearly dragging both women down because they were still attached to the chains. Realizing the ropes could pull them straight into the abyss, Loose quickly unhooked them, saving them from being dragged to their deaths. Another massive rockslide followed, wiping out nearly all the remaining planks, and leaving only the small section where they were standing intact. Desperate to get help, Jax used her phone to call the Thai police station, but they couldn't communicate because the officers didn't speak English. Loose then tried contacting their universal emergency line, but the connection went dead almost immediately. With nowhere else to turn, the two women remained stranded, crying as the rain continued beating down on them throughout the night. Eventually, the sun came up and morning arrived. Loose calculated that approximately 50 m of the planks on both sides had been destroyed, leaving them with no choice but to attempt climbing across the bare metal rails if they wanted to survive. Using the camera they had with them, they zoomed in toward the bar and noticed something that gave them a small sense of hope that someone might eventually spot them. They tried signaling with John's laser, but they couldn't tell whether anyone had actually seen it. Jax therefore suggested that they wait until nighttime and use the laser again, believing its beam would be much easier to notice in the darkness. By evening, while the women were sitting on the remaining planks, a voice suddenly came through the walkie-talkie attached to the bag hanging from one of the rails. To their enormous relief, it was John, proving that he had somehow survived. Hearing his voice, they immediately began figuring out a way to reach the bag so they could communicate with him properly. They loosened their ropes, connected them together, and repeatedly swung the rope toward the hanging bag, but every attempt failed. Eventually, Loose leaned herself over the edge while Jax firmly held onto her belt. After several tries, Loose finally managed to hook the bag with the rope. Unfortunately, the rope snapped during the attempt because the bag was too firmly stuck and refused to move. Meanwhile, down in the village at the club, their laser beam reached the pool board and eventually caught the bartender's attention. However, after noticing the beam repeatedly flashing around and disturbing him, he eventually closed the blinds. With nothing else to occupy her mind, Jax began watching old footage of herself and Shiloh recorded on the camera while Loose lay down on the plank and quickly fell asleep. As Jax continued watching the old videos, she suddenly noticed Loose in one of the recordings, but the woman in the footage had a completely different face from the person who had been accompanying her. When Loose eventually woke up, Jax confronted her about what she had discovered. It was then that Loose finally confessed the truth. She had been impersonating Loose because she had seen how much pain Jax was in and believed that the best way to help her heal emotionally was to take her on this dangerous journey. The revelation left Jax completely discombobulated. Loose tried explaining her reasons, but Jax was furious and refused to even look her in the face. A short while later, morning arrived again. Loose had had enough of waiting, so she decided to cross the exposed brackets herself and retrieve the radio. Jax desperately tried to stop her, but Loose insisted there was no other option. She handed Jax her luggage, took a deep breath, and bravely stepped onto the first rail. As she carefully moved forward, one of the rails suddenly began to give way beneath her, but she reacted quickly and swung her leg onto the next one. When she got close to the bag, the rail beneath her finally collapsed, but Loose managed to grab the rail behind her, preventing herself from falling with it. Although, the sharp metal badly pierced her hands. She somehow managed to get both legs onto another rail, but her hands soon slipped free, leaving her entire body supported only by her legs. Acting immediately, Jax threw a rope toward her. Loose caught it just in time and clipped it securely onto her belt before she fell. Little by little, Jax pulled Loose upward until, after struggling for a while, she finally managed to grab onto the plank. Jax then used all her strength to haul her completely back onto the platform. The moment she noticed the horrible injury on Loose's body, Jax ripped a piece from her jacket and wrapped it around the wound to stop the bleeding, while Loose screamed from the unbearable pain. During this painful moment, Loose finally opened up and told Jax that she had cancer and didn't have much time left because she had chosen to stop her treatment. What hurt her the most was that she never got the chance to send a message to her mother explaining that she had discontinued treatment and wanted to say her final goodbye. Jax refused to let her lose hope and assured her that they would both survive, promising that Loose could tell her mother everything herself once they got home. Meanwhile, Jax began thinking about a memory from her childhood, when she went skydiving with her sister Shiloh. While they were falling through the sky, Shiloh suddenly pretended to pass out, terrifying Jax so badly that she thought they were both going to die. They continued falling dangerously close to the ground before Shiloh finally pulled the parachute. Once they landed safely, Shiloh explained that she had only done it because she wanted Jax to overcome her fear. Jax, however, was furious and argued that Shiloh had no right to decide when she was ready to face her fears. Shiloh attempted to apologize, but Jax angrily told her that she wished she were dead. Moments later, Jax snapped out of the memory and found herself back in reality. She immediately tried to wake Loose, only to realize that Loose was already dead. Jax then suddenly woke up and discovered that the entire horrifying moment had been nothing more than a nightmare. The following morning, Luce woke up to find that Jax had already made up her mind. She was determined to retrieve the radio and find a way to get them both off the mountain. Before setting off, Jax asked Luce what her actual name was and she cheerfully revealed that her real name was Billie. Without wasting any more time, Jax began the nearly impossible journey toward the bag. Remembering how she used to jump from one stick to another as a child, she carefully moved across the structure using her hands to shift from one rail to the next. As she approached the bag, Jax realized the safety rope tied around her waist wasn't long enough to reach it. Refusing to turn around after coming this far, she abandoned the rope and took a deep breath before making a desperate leap toward the rail supporting the bag. She nearly lost her grip and fell, but managed to grab the bag, use it to pull herself upward, and secure her hands around the rail. After pushing herself onto the structure, she sat down, then slowly dragged the bag toward herself. Jax quickly grabbed the radio and contacted John, instantly bringing a fresh wave of excitement and hope to both women. She told John their exact location and he instructed them to stay where they were because he was coming to rescue them. A few minutes later, John appeared directly above them. He lowered a rope and first pulled Billie to safety before returning for Jax shortly afterward. The three eventually reached a much safer area on top of the mountain. John contacted the emergency services and was informed that a helicopter would be dispatched to pick them up. All they needed to do was make their way to the designated landing area and wait for the rescue. Not long afterward, they reached the dragon's eye, which marked the end of the deadly plank wall. By now, Jax had conquered the fear that had held her back for so long, so she decided to take on the final plank without attaching herself to a safety line. When she reached the dragon's eye, she became emotional and looked out, hoping that Shyla would finally be proud of how far she had come. Unfortunately, their ordeal wasn't over yet. They still had to cross one final bridge before reaching the area where the helicopter was expected to land. John went first. The bridge stretched roughly 40 ft and had no chains, rails, or other protection to prevent someone from falling. Despite the danger, John successfully reached the other side. Billie then followed behind him. Her crossing was even more dangerous because the plank had already become unstable while the wire supporting it was gradually coming loose. Somehow, she managed to make it across as well. Jax then began her own crossing, and hers proved to be the most terrifying of all. But against every possible obstacle, she eventually reached the other side. The group decided to take a short break before continuing, but when they checked the small oxygen tank, they discovered that it wasn't actually filled with oxygen. Instead, it contained fentanyl. John finally admitted that he had been using them as drug mules to transport narcotics. He claimed that he did this regularly and had never been caught. Jax and Billie were furious, and during their heated confrontation, Billie threw the drugs away. That immediately enraged John, who shoved her off the bridge, sending her plunging to her death. John then turned his attention toward Jax, intending to kill her as well because he feared she would report him and send him to prison. Jax threatened to throw away the second package of drugs if he came any closer. John then revealed the horrifying truth. There was no emergency rescue operation coming for them. The people bringing the helicopter were actually the ones expecting to receive the drugs, and anyone who failed to complete a delivery would lose a finger. Realizing Jax wasn't going to surrender the package, John charged at her and attempted to take it by force. The struggle quickly became violent as he tried to choke her using the bag of drugs. Jax fought back, grabbed a wooden stick, and stabbed him with it. John recovered and attacked her again, this time using his bare hands to choke her. Jaxs managed to fight back by biting down on his thumbs, severing them, before grabbing the drugs and crawling toward the opposite side of the bridge. When she reached the middle, Jaxs pretended to lose consciousness. John cautiously approached and reached for the drugs, believing she was no longer a threat. At the perfect moment, Jaxs clipped her hook onto the rail and shoved it with everything she had. The sudden force sent John tumbling from the bridge to his death, while Jaxs' safety rope prevented her from suffering the same fate. Jaxs struggled her way back onto the bridge and eventually completed the crossing. Just as she reached safety, she spotted the helicopter approaching in the distance. She immediately raised the package of drugs into the air, signaling to them so they would come and pick her up. Jaxs had finally survived the nightmare and returned to the city. She went straight back to the bartender who had originally connected them with John. The bartender then helped Billie send the long-awaited message to her mother. After that, Jaxs opened the book and began looking at the next quest that awaited her.
