ही उन लोगों ने खुद को प्रोटेक्ट करने का भी जिम्मा लिया हुआ है अपनी एनिमीज़ से। अब बात करें उनकी एनिमीज़ की तो उनके एनिमीज़ और कोई नहीं ओचीन नाम के क्रिएचर्स हैं जो अक्सर रात के वक्त अटैक करते हैं। जिस यंग बॉयज की जो किसी ना किसी तरीके से हादसे से जूझे हुए हैं। जिन्हें वो एज अ हेल्पिंग हैंड अपने साथ रख लेता है उन्हें खाना और फाइटिंग स्किल्स सिखाते हुए और उसकी ट्रेनिंग के ही जरिए उन सभी का भी इंटेंशन text: The story of Buddy in 1 minute. Buddy does fun activities with his friends Freddy, Wade, Oliver, and Josh every day. But one day everything changes. He tells Wade and the two of them decide to tell Nurse Nancy to ask Buddy what is really going on. The unicorn kills her and the kids all decide to board Charlie the train in order to reach Diamond City. Buddy kills Charlie and tries to punish Wade by stabbing him. Wade manages to burn half of Buddy's body, giving everyone a chance to hop over the fence and escape. Sadly, Wade doesn't make it in time and gets impaled by Buddy. A lady from the human world named Grace gets abducted by Buddy via a TV. Somehow reality itself forgets her existence and changes. She becomes the new nurse. Buddy goes to Grace for medical attention and tries to assault her. The kids make it to Diamond City only to find that it's not real. Buddy catches the kids and forces them to sing a song that heals them and teleports them back to the park. Freddy finds out that Grace is actually her mother and they have a final showdown with Buddy. Everyone dies except for Freddy. She kills Buddy and goes back to the human world.

text: Tony begins during the summer of nineteen seventy five and follows a young college student whose confidence is far bigger than his experience. Determined to chase a girl named Nancy to Cape Cod, Tony arrives with little more than ambition and an inflated opinion of himself. Since he needs both a job and a place to stay, he finds work at a local restaurant called the Flagship. There he meets the Brazilian born owner and head chef, known simply as Chef, along with the rest of the hardworking kitchen staff. Although Tony believes he already understands the world, the restaurant quickly exposes him to a completely different way of life. At first Tony struggles to fit in. His academic arrogance often clashes with the demanding reality of restaurant work, where confidence means very little without discipline and effort. Chef pushes him to work harder while the rest of the kitchen crew teaches him lessons that no classroom ever could. Every shift chips away at the superiority Tony carries with him, even if he refuses to admit it at first. As the summer continues, the kitchen slowly becomes more than just a workplace and starts shaping the person he is becoming. Nancy also plays an important role in Tony's journey. She is the reason he came to Cape Cod in the first place, but their relationship never follows the simple romantic path he imagined. Instead, being around her repeatedly forces Tony to confront his own immaturity. His selfish decisions and impulsive behavior create distance between them, making it clear that growing closer to Nancy depends less on grand gestures and more on becoming a better person. Although the story is inspired by Anthony Bourdain's memoir Kitchen Confidential, the film reshapes many real events into a single coming of age narrative. Rather than recreating three separate summers, the story combines them into one season. Nancy is a fictionalized version of the young woman Bourdain briefly mentioned in his memoir, while Chef is a composite character inspired by Bigfoot, one of the influential chefs Bourdain later worked for after entering culinary school. The Flagship restaurant also blends elements from more than one location described in the memoir, allowing the film to focus on Tony's emotional growth instead of strict historical accuracy. As the summer progresses, Tony slowly changes through the daily routine of kitchen life. The long hours, constant pressure, and teamwork teach him responsibility in ways his education never could. Instead of trying to prove he is smarter than everyone else, he gradually begins listening to the people around him. Even so, old habits remain difficult to overcome, and his selfish instincts continue creating problems for both himself and those closest to him. Everything reaches a turning point after an accident destroys the Flagship. The loss devastates everyone connected to the restaurant, especially Chef, whose livelihood is suddenly placed in jeopardy. Feeling responsible for what happened, Tony becomes vulnerable to the influence of his co worker Sal. Together they organize a beach cookout that appears to be a charity fundraiser to help Chef rebuild. Secretly, however, they plan to keep the money for themselves and disappear. As the fundraiser unfolds, Tony watches members of the community come together to support Chef with genuine kindness. Instead of suspicion or anger, he witnesses people giving their time and money simply because they want to help. During the event Chef unexpectedly greets Tony with warmth rather than resentment. That simple moment forces Tony to confront the person he has been throughout the summer. Faced with a choice between selfishness and responsibility, Tony abandons the plan he made with Sal. Rather than stealing the money, he ensures every donation goes toward helping Chef. It is the first truly selfless decision he has made in the story. More importantly, the choice marks the moment he finally breaks away from both Sal's cynical outlook and the selfish behavior that has defined much of his young life. Tony's decision also begins repairing the relationships he damaged. Nancy sees that his actions now match the person he has been trying to become instead of the arrogant student who first arrived in Cape Cod. Chef's respect is earned once again, not through words or excuses, but through a meaningful act that places someone else's needs before his own. The ending also completes the larger theme that runs throughout the film. At the beginning Tony believes intelligence alone makes him exceptional. He talks confidently about changing literature and outsmarting professors despite having very little experience outside the classroom. Working inside the restaurant teaches him that confidence without humility has little value. Every mistake he makes forces him to recognize how much he still has to learn. After returning home, Tony cooks a meal for his family. Even his normally critical mother notices that something about him has changed. The transformation is not presented as dramatic or miraculous. Instead, it feels like the first genuine step toward adulthood. The young man who once relied on arrogance and performance has begun developing honesty, responsibility, and empathy. The ending also points toward Tony's future. Inspired by everything he experienced during that unforgettable summer, he decides to apply to culinary school. At the same time he begins using the name Anthony, symbolizing a new chapter in his life. It is a quiet but meaningful decision that reflects the person he is slowly becoming. The ending is powerful because it avoids turning Tony into a completely different person overnight. Instead, it shows that real growth comes from accepting mistakes and choosing to do better when the opportunity finally arrives. By keeping the fundraiser money where it belongs, rebuilding trust with Chef, repairing his relationship with Nancy, and committing himself to cooking, Tony leaves behind the entitled college student who arrived at the Flagship and takes the first authentic steps toward becoming the Anthony Bourdain the world would eventually come to know.

text: In Nazi-occupied Poland, in 1944, young Erik Lehnsherr is separated from his parents upon entrance into the Auschwitz concentration camp. While he attempts to reach them, he causes a set of metal gates to bend toward him. This is the result of a mutant ability to create magnetic fields and control metal, but he is knocked out by the guards. In the not-too-distant future, U.S. Senator Robert Kelly attempts to pass a "Mutant Registration Act" in Congress, which would force mutants to reveal their identities and abilities. Erik, now going by the name "Magneto", and his telepathic colleague Professor Charles Xavier, are both present. Xavier sees Erik in attendance and is concerned with how he will respond to the Registration Act. In Mississippi, 17-year-old Marie accidentally puts her boyfriend into a coma after she kisses him, because her mutant ability absorbs the power and life force of others. She runs away from home and adopts the name Rogue. In Alberta, she meets Logan, also known as "Wolverine", a mutant who possesses superhuman healing abilities and metal "claws" that protrude from between his knuckles. They are attacked on the road by Sabretooth, one of Magneto's minions, but two of Xavier's students – Cyclops and Storm – arrive and save them. Wolverine and Rogue are brought to Xavier's mansion and school for mutants in Westchester County, New York. Xavier tells Logan that Magneto appears to have taken an interest in him and asks him to stay while Xavier's mutants, the X-Men, investigate the matter. Rogue enrolls in the school. Senator Kelly is abducted by two more of Magneto's minions, Toad and Mystique, and brought to their hideout on the uncharted island of Genosha. Magneto uses Kelly as a test subject for a machine powered by his magnetic abilities that generates a field of radiation, which induces mutations in normal humans. Kelly later escapes by taking advantage of his newfound mutation. Rogue visits Wolverine during the night while he is having a nightmare. Startled, he accidentally stabs her, but she is able to absorb his healing ability to recover. This is observed by fellow students who arrived to help. She is later convinced by Mystique, who disguises herself as Rogue's crush Bobby Drake, that Xavier is angry with her and she should leave the school. Xavier uses his mutant-locating machine Cerebro to find Rogue at a train station, and the X-Men go to retrieve her. Meanwhile, Mystique enters Cerebro and sabotages it. Having left ahead of Storm and Cyclops, Wolverine finds Rogue on a train and convinces her to return to the school. Before they can leave, Magneto arrives, knocks out Wolverine and subdues Rogue, revealing it was Rogue who he wants rather than Wolverine. Although Xavier attempts to stop Magneto by mentally controlling Sabretooth, he is forced to release his hold on Sabretooth when Magneto threatens the police who have converged on the train station, allowing Magneto's Brotherhood to escape with Rogue. Kelly arrives at Xavier's school, and Xavier reads his mind to learn about Magneto's machine. Realizing the strain of powering it nearly killed Magneto, the group deduces he intends to transfer his powers to Rogue and use her to power it at the cost of her life. Kelly's body rejects his mutation, and his body dissolves into liquid. Xavier attempts to locate Rogue using Cerebro, but Mystique's sabotage incapacitates him, and he falls into a coma. Fellow telekinetic and telepath Jean Grey fixes Cerebro and uses it, learning that Magneto plans to place his mutation-inducing machine on Liberty Island and use it to "mutate" the world leaders meeting at a summit on nearby Ellis Island. The X-Men scale the Statue of Liberty, battling and overpowering the Brotherhood while Magneto transfers his powers to Rogue and activates the mutating machine. As Wolverine confronts and distracts Magneto, Cyclops blasts him away, allowing Wolverine to destroy the machine. He transfers his powers to Rogue and his healing abilities rejuvenate her, while incapacitating himself. Professor Xavier and Wolverine recover from their comas. The group also learns that Mystique escaped the island battle and is impersonating Senator Kelly, despite being seriously injured by Wolverine. Xavier gives Wolverine a lead to his past at an abandoned military installation in Canada. Magneto is imprisoned in a complex constructed of plastic and is visited by Xavier, and Magneto warns him he intends to escape one day and continue the fight.

Later, back at home, Cathy is crying over her broken toys when her father Ernshaw arrives and makes jokes about her mother like how her hands were very large and she had a mustache and that Cathy would turn out the same way. Cathy begins to cry and Ernshaw tells Nelly to toughen Cathy up saying he is going to Ram a place where he has business. After that, Cathy goes to Mrs. Burton's place where she overhears Burton and Zilla talking about how her father has given shelter to a new boy who is hiding somewhere upstairs. She goes upstairs to find him. Meanwhile, Burton and Zilla ask Ernshaw about the boy, who he was, and what he was doing there. Ernshaw explains that the boy's father was going to abandon him on the streets, and he brought him home, saying the boy could stay as long as he wished. Cathy finds the boy hiding under the bed, frightened, and brings him to her father. Cathy gives him the name of her deceased brother, Heathcliffe, and says she likes him very much. Nelly is jealous of him, and Zilla rubs salt in his wounds by calling him a bastard and taunting that he will never be a lady. Cathy is teaching Heathcliffe to read, but gets very angry at him and leaves. Heathcliffe walks away, but Cathy apologizes to him. However, Heathcliffe tells her to leave, but Cathy says something that makes it clear she will never be far from him. After that, the two spend time together walking, talking, and one day while roaming, they get caught in the rain and arrive home late. Ernshaw is very angry because Kathy had come late on his birthday and had forgotten it. In the middle of his anger, Heathcliffe takes the blame for their late arrival upon himself and is shivering. Ernshaw, furious, punishes Heathcliffe with a whip. After this, Cathy comes to see him and is very sad. Heathcliffe tells her not to be sad for him and that he is always ready to take beatings for her. With this, several years pass. Cathy tells Heathcliffe that new neighbors have arrived, the Lintons, who are very wealthy. A week passes and Cathy is restless that they haven't come to meet her and she is very irritable. Heathcliffe, after listening to her complaints, hangs her from a tree and walks away. In revenge, Cathy breaks eggs on his bed. The next day, Ernshaw is going to meet a solicitor. At that time, Cathy learns that her father had punished Heathcliffe two days ago, and she is very angry. That night, she tells Heathcliffe that the meeting with the solicitor did not go well and they have lost everything. Kathy is very cold and they have no firewood left. So Heathcliffe breaks a chair to light a fire for her. The next day while walking, Kathy spots the Linton's house and walks close to it where she secretly listens to Isabella and Edgar Linton's conversation from over the wall. Isabella spots her and thinks she is a ghost. But Cathy falls down while climbing and Edgar helps her. Edgar sends a letter to Ernshaw saying that Cathy is in his care because she had sprained her ankle. Ernshaw is very happy hearing this, thinking something could happen between Cathy and Edgar. But hearing this, Heathcliffe is very worried and waits for her return. 6 weeks later, Cathy comes back well-dressed and looking very refined. And everyone is happy to see her looking so good. But Heathcliffe does not go to meet her. So Cathy meets him herself. He is angry with her and tells her he is no longer the child who always play with her and asks her to leave. That same night, Cathy cannot sleep because of his words and goes near Heathcliffe's room where from above she sees Joseph and her maid being sexually intimate. At that moment, Heathcliffe covers her eyes from behind. Cathy is shocked seeing all this and walks away. The next morning, she cannot meet Heathcliffe for breakfast and going far away from there, she pleasures herself alone. Heathcliffe is looking for her and finds her pleasuring herself. Kathy is very embarrassed, but Heathcliffe confesses his love for her and pulls her close and is about to kiss her, but Cathy refuses and walks away. Outside, her father is creating a scene due to his illness while Nelly tells Cathy that Edgar has come downstairs to meet her. Cathy tells him she is not in a condition to talk, but Edgar requests her to listen to him. Cathy then tells Nelly that Edgar wants to marry her and she has said yes, but she is crying and says she already loves Heathcliffe. Nelly tells her to be quiet and forget Heathcliffe. Just then, Nelly notices Heathcliffe coming. And as Heathcliffe hears their conversation, Cathy deliberately plays a game with Nelly, saying she loves Edgar and is going to marry him. But in the middle of this, Cathy says that if she marries Heathcliffe, she would become a beggar. Heathcliffe, hearing this, leaves in anger. But Cathy wanted to use the marriage money to free Heathcliffe from her father's power. However, Heathcliffe rides away on a horse in anger away from Cathy. The next day, Cathy learns from Joseph that he has left, but she waits for him because she believed he would never leave her. But a year passes, and Cathy finally agrees to marry Edgar, goes to his house in her wedding dress, and the two kiss, beginning a new chapter of their lives. Isabella is very happy about Cathy's arrival and has ordered many clothes for her. Edgar has decorated her room according to her taste. With this weeks and months pass and Cathy tries to live like them, dressing like them, adopting their lifestyle, their manners. But from inside, Cathy feels hollow as if she is only alive in Heathcliff's memories. She does not love Edgar. Many years pass, and she asks Nelly what is going on. But Nelly tells her she has a home, warm clothes, and food, and that is what is right. At Christmas, Cathy returns home and learns that Zilla has left Joseph and her father is in very bad condition, living alone because he has no money for a maid. He scolds Cathy and also says that she could help her poor father a little, but Cathy refuses because she knows he will waste the money on gambling. As he taunts her for not visiting in so many years, she goes to him in anger with money. But seeing her father take it, she breaks down and returns to Edgar, who comforts her. A few days later, Cathy gives Edgar the news that he is going to become a father. After he leaves, just as Cathy sits on the bed, she hears the sound of eggs cracking and understands it was done by Heathcliffe and goes outside to find him. Finally, she spots Heathcliffe who has changed a great deal and she embraces him tightly. She sees he has become wealthy now and she introduces him to Isabella and Edgar and is very excited about his story. But Heathcliffe refuses to tell them and informs them that he is now their neighbor because he has bought Weathering Heights. Meanwhile, Isabella starts liking Heathcliffe, but Cathy speaks very badly of him and says he will not like her, which makes Isabella very angry and she breaks Cathy's dolls. Just as Heathcliffe and Cathy are talking, Heathcliffe learns from Cathy that Isabella likes him and to make Cathy jealous, he says he will date or even kiss Isabella. Cathy tries to stop him, to which Heathcliffe tells her she has a husband. Cathy says that since he came back, she has been talking to him nicely and now this argument is because of you. Heathcliffe reminds her that she had rejected his love and says there can be no reconciliation between the two of them. That night, Cathy tells Edgar that from now on, Heathcliffe will not be invited, which makes Isabella very angry. On the other side, Ernshaw is happy about Heathcliff's arrival because he thought he would get money from him. But he insults him by saying he will always be Cathy's pet animal. A few days later, Cathy gets the news that her father has passed away and she rushes to him and starts crying. After that, she is returning in the rain when Heathcliffe follows her to save her from the cold. The two take shelter somewhere and there Cathy asks him why he left. Heathcliffe tells her the truth that he had heard her say marrying him would degrade her, but Cathy tells him he hadn't heard the whole conversation and that she loved him. Heathcliffe says she herself had pushed them apart. No one else did, but he has come back and the two kiss. Heathcliffe says he will not stop loving her for any reason. They then go to Ern Shaw's funeral where Nelly sees Heathcliffe and Cathy holding hands. The two are now secretly spending time together, becoming intimate, and Cathy is cheating on her husband with Heathcliffe. She starts going to meet Heathcliffe secretly every day. But one day, Nelly asks her whether Heathcliffe knows about her baby. Days pass like this, and when the two are talking, Cathy says she wishes she could go back in time and not have said what she said that day. Heathcliffe tells her that Nelly had seen them. Hearing this, Cathy tells Nelly to find a new employer because she had found out that Nelly had deliberately not told her about it. But before leaving, Nelly goes to Edgar where Edra tells Cathy to stop meeting Heathcliffe and walks away. Heathcliffe waits for her, but Cathy cannot come because of Edgar. Suddenly, someone knocks on the window and Cathy goes outside on the pretext of a bird and Edgar senses something is different. Outside, Heathcliffe had come to meet her and starts kissing her. Cathy asks him to leave because her husband is there. Just as Edgar asks her to come inside for the sake of their baby because she will catch a cold. Heathcliffe learns she is pregnant. The next day, Cathy tells him the child is Edgar's, which she had confirmed before his arrival. But Heathcliffe tells her it doesn't matter to him and he wants to always be with her and starts becoming intimate with her. Cathy stops him and says the two of them have waited too long and they need to stop and she leaves. Heathcliffe then goes to Isabella's room and starts seducing her, telling her he will be rough and cruel with her and will marry her, but only to make Cathy jealous and asks if she agrees to all this. But Isabella, blinded by love, accepts all his conditions. And the next day, the two go to court and get married. Hearing this, Cathy is devastated and remains very sad. Meanwhile, Isabella writes a letter to Nelly saying Heathcliffe is a monster, cruel, like a beast who is using her just to play games. Nelly, whom Edgar had forbidden to leave the house, is burning all of Heathcliff's incoming letters and manipulating Edgar so that he can keep Cathy under control and had locked her in her room. Heathcliffe is frustrated that Cathy's response is not coming and he tells Isabella to write one more letter to her. A few days later, Nelly comes to meet her and sees Isabella being kept like a dog by Heathcliffe. He is tormenting her and controlling her with his gestures. Nelly wants to take Isabella home, but Isabella herself says she is at home. Heathcliffe keeps making Isabella write letters, but Nelly burns them before they reach Cathy.

text: The movie opens with a happy couple, Paul and Iris, riding in a car and we see that Iris is blindfolded, which means that Paul has arranged a surprise for her. Here we get to know that he has booked a seat in the newly opened restaurant Skyview. She is over the moon when her blindfolds are removed and in excitement hugs her boyfriend, Paul. But once they take the lift to reach the top, they get to learn that the construction was completed 5 months prior to the expected time. This makes Iris uneasy as such swift construction often leads to compromise with safety. Nevertheless, they reach the top and as she looks down, she gets frightened as she has acrophobia. Paul realizes this and apologizes to her as he should have planned a different venue. Iris puts on a smile to cheer her boyfriend and they decide to have some drinks. But as Paul goes to fetch her some drinks, she feels dizzy and runs to the washroom. There, seeing her condition, a woman asks her about her pregnancy and although hesitant at first, she confesses that she is 2 weeks pregnant and is yet to tell her boyfriend. We also get to see that the woman is a singer in the venue and she has a child who is also present there. The woman encourages her and assures her that everything will be all right. Iris feels a little bit better and decides to join the dance floor with Paul. This is when death begins its play. A piece of decoration falls of a chandelier and causes a slight crack on the dance floor which is made of glass. No one notices it at first and keep dancing. Paul takes her to the top most spot in the place and we see that there is a little boy about to throw a coin from the top just for sport, but the security guard stops him in time. Paul kneels down and proposes to Iris with a ring and this is where she discloses her pregnancy to him and he is overjoyed. Needless to say, Iris accepts his proposal of marriage and Paul slips the ring into her finger and they celebrate this moment. Here, we see the boy throwing the coin and it slides inside a vent and the coin gets stuck in the blades of a fan inside the vent, thereby stopping its motion. This goes unnoticed by everybody. But this This where things begin to get weird. Iris suddenly stops dancing and we see a string of events like the fire from the kitchen, the sound of the glass cracking, the singing of the band, and the cocktails being prepared for the guests. The glass gives in and some of the guests who were dancing fall down immediately. This creates a panic and everyone tries to rush to safety. Paul is also seen hanging from a broken glass and he tries to grab it tightly. Iris tries to save her boyfriend but she fails to reach him in time and he falls to his death. The fire from the kitchen spreads onto a woman's clothes and she runs in panic thereby causing the fire to spread and eventually causing an explosion which kills a lot of the remaining people. The lift man calls everyone to escape using the stairs and people oblige but the stairs also collapse and a lot more people fall to their death making the situation even worse. Seeing no other option, the lift man calls everyone else inside the lift to escape the ordeal and seeing this people rush to the lift. due to the huge number of people trying to escape and eventually the pulleys break leading to the lift falling directly to the ground and killing everyone in it. Half of the tower collapses and Iris watches everyone die in front of her eyes. This is when her eyes fall on the little boy whom we saw earlier and he was asking for help. Iris tries to comfort him but seeing the other half of the tower collapsing, she takes his hand and jumps to grab a pillar in the nick of time. The tower top is completely destroyed and we see the duo hanging on a pillar. But as the camera zooms in, we see that they are only hanging due to Iris's engagement ring getting between two nails. The weight of two people is on a single ring finger and as she tries to hold on, her finger rips off under pressure and both of them fall to their death. The scene shifts to Stephanie who was sitting in her class and we see that the previous events were part of her daydream. She gets scolded by her teacher and her classmates give her awkward looks. Next, we get to learn that she has been dreaming of this incident for the past few months and it has been hampering her sleep and now she is determined to discover the roots of it. The fact that she knows that the woman in her dreams is her grandmother Iris makes the situation even more scary. To uncover the secrets of her recurring nightmares, she decides to search more about her grandmother. She goes to meet with her father Marty and her brother Charlie. This is where we learn that their mother Darlene had abandoned them in their childhood and their grandmother Iris was behind it. Finding no clues from her father, she decides to visit her maternal uncle and Charlie decides to go with her. She meets with her cousins, Bobby, Eric, Julia, and her uncle Howard and aunt Brenda. When asked about Iris, their demeanor changed and they looked shocked after hearing the name. Here it is revealed that Iris had abandoned Howard and Stephanie's mother Darlene when they were kids and hence had to face extreme hardships. Howard used to receive letters from Iris and she claimed that death will come for their children and the letters also contained the patterns in which death used to haunt its targets. To escape this scenario, Howard had changed his address and had severed all forms of con- tacts with his mother, Iris. Even after hearing this, Stephanie is adamant in knowing the reason behind her nightmares, but Howard denies any further information. But her aunt Brenda gives her the letters that Iris used to send and this gives her Iris's address. When Stephanie arrives at her address, she is spooked by the way the place looks. Guarded by huge metal doors and all kinds of defenses, she had prepared a fort to keep death away from her. Stephanie nears the cabin where her grandmother stays and upon opening the door, she meets her grandmother Iris for the first time in her life. The place looks completely uninhabitable with no modern technology or devices. It did not even have the necessities for life, but Iris still has been living in that place for the past 20 years. Stephanie explains her nightmares and Iris explains that the events that she saw was not a dream, but a reality that could have happened 20 years ago, but she averted it. Here in a flashback, we are shown that on the fateful day, Iris had stopped the boy from throwing the coin into the air vent and had interrupted the band from performing. Ceasing the microphone, she had appealed to everyone to evacuate the place as they were all going to die. At first, people thought that it was just a joke, but as soon as they realized that the glass beneath their feet was cracking, they panicked and evacuated immediately and the place was shut down, avoiding the accident. This is the reason that death had been killing all the people that were supposed to die that day and even their children as they were never supposed to be born. She adds that death has its own unique way of hunting and it is very hard to avoid it. This is why Iris had secluded herself from her family and kept herself safe in that cabin as death always follows the order and as long as she is safe, her children, Howard and Darlene will be safe and this means that her grandchildren, Eric, Bobby, Julia, Charlie and Stephanie will all be safe. Stephanie thinks that isolation from the rest of the world had turned her grandmother into a crazy person and she repents her decision of visiting her. Iris tries to stop her, but Stephanie steps out of her cabin. Seeing no other way to make her believe the facts about death, Iris steps out of her cabin after 20 years and tells Stephanie to see what happens and to believe her eyes. She hands Stephanie her book about death and then stands a few steps away from her. This is when the unthinkable happens. Out of the blue, a weather vane falls on a fire extinguisher and a metal object gets hurled towards her face, piercing it completely. Blood splashes all over Stephanie's face and she is left stunned by the incident. The family gathers during her funeral and Stephanie's mother, Darlene also arrives after a lot of years. She continues reading the book and tries to find the pattern of death. On the other hand, Bobby accidentally drops a beer bottle resulting in a glass shard getting mixed with the ice kept nearby. The family holds a party in their house and all of them enjoy like a happy family. But Stephanie feels uneasy and heads to their location as if she had got a premonition. She arrives and everything seems to be fine until the glass shard falls to the ground. Howard accidentally steps on it, and at the same time the garden rake falls on the switch of the lawn mower activating it. Right at this moment, Howard falls to the ground owing to the injury caused by the glass shard, and the lawn mower cuts through his face, tearing it into numerous pieces, killing him instantly. The entire family is left horrified by this incident, and Stephanie now firmly believes in the book written by her grandmother. She shares her learning with the entire family, describing that death will come for each of the family members in correct order as per their age, as they should have never been born if Iris had not cheated death in the Skyview incident. As per the order, first Eric will die, as he is the eldest of all siblings followed by Julia, Bobby, and then Darlene followed by Stephanie, and at last Charlie. But she is ridiculed by her own family, and no one believes her. As per the order, Eric is the next in Death's book. Hence, Stephanie and Charlie try to accompany him wherever he goes. But being arrogant, Eric makes fun of the two. Stephanie sees a man cleaning a garden, and beside him a group of children are playing football. She suspects that the dust will get into the eyes of one of the children, and he will kick the balls, and it may hit Eric. Eric does not pay heed to this premonition, and makes fun of Stephanie. Julia meets with him, and after chatting, takes her leave. Right then a garbage collection truck appears in the background, and Julia walks alongside it. But out of the blue, the man who was cleaning the garden falls to the ground, and dust goes into the eyes of the children, and one of them kicks the ball, which hits Julia, making her fall into a garbage bin. The truck collects the garbage bin and dumps Julia alongside all the garbage into its container. The lid of the container slowly closes and Stephanie, Charlie, and Eric give chase. Stephanie tries to climb the truck and rescue Julia, but she is too late. The lid closes, crushing Julia into pieces, and again Stephanie is confronted by this horrible game of death, which she sees in front of her eyes. Here it is revealed that Eric was adopted and thus he did not die and as per order, Julia was the victim of death. Now everyone believes Stephanie and Bobby pleads to her to save him. Stephanie dives deeper into Iris's book and here she discovers that there is a person named JB who knows a victim who escaped death. They decide to visit the Hope River Hospital to meet JB and inquire about the person who escaped death. Here we get to learn that JB was the same kid who we saw in the beginning of the movie in the Skyview restaurant. JB tells them that they only have two choices, either die or kill someone else and then his longevity will be transferred to the killer. Stephanie inquires about the survivor who cheated death. JB reveals that there was a person named Kimberly who died and her heartbeat flatlined and then her doctors brought her back to life. The family decided to try this out but he warns them that cheating death is very risky and as a last piece of advice, he requests them to live their lives to the fullest before death eventually takes them. Without informing anyone, Eric takes Bobby to an unknown room and plans to give him peanut butter cookies as he is extremely allergic to peanut butter. But while taking the food from the vending machine, it gets stuck and Eric forcibly brings the packet out but in the process, a spring ejects. They lock themselves in a dark room just opposite to the emergency room inside the hospital. The plan was to rush Bobby inside the emergency room after his heart stops beating so that doctors can resuscitate him immediately. Eric goes to fetch him a wheelchair but after the door closes, a file drops on a keyboard activating the MRI machine inside the room. Hence also activating the powerful magnet inside the machine. The machine starts powering up without their knowledge. Eric takes away Bobby's EpiPen and promises that he will bring him back from death and urges him to take the cookies. After taking the peanut butter cookies, Bobby's allergy kicks in and he gets seizures but Eric still believes that he can bring him back from the dead. On the other end, the rest of the family keeps searching for the duo, but as the hospital is too big, they are unable to locate them easily. Bobby starts having painful seizures and is close to death, but this is when the power in the MRI machine gets to an extreme point and starts attracting all the metal objects. All of Eric's metal piercings start getting sucked from inside his body and the wheelchair pushes him into the MRI machine, eventually killing him. Bobby successfully takes the EpiPen, but the spring from the vending machine that we saw earlier gets pulled towards the magnet and pierces through Bobby's head, killing him instantly. This is witnessed by a nurse who screams, help the rest of the family to locate the room, but to their dismay, they are too late as Bobby had taken his last breath. This shows us that those who get in the path of death also get punished, just like Eric. To keep her children safe, Darlene decides to isolate herself inside Iris's cabin as death always follows its order. They travel to the secluded place, but death was not willing to give up. Upon reaching the cabin, Stephanie's seatbelt gets stuck and she is unable to open it. She breaks through the gates of the cabin using her van and urges Charlie and Darlene to go inside the cabin, but sparks from a nearby light causes fire to erupt in the vicinity of the cabin and as soon as Charlie and Darlene went inside the cabin, the spark lighted a leaking gas pipe and the cabin exploded. Darlene tried hard and eventually freed Charlie who was trapped under rubble. She tries to comfort Charlie that she will try to remain alive as long as possible, but right at that moment, a post falls on her, killing her in front of her son. Charlie gets shocked by this incident, but he has no time to waste as the explosion had overturned the van and it got submerged in a nearby pond, drowning Stephanie. Without wasting more time, Charlie gets inside the van and cuts the seatbelt using a knife, but before he can free her, she runs out of breath. Just when all hope seems lost, Charlie applies CPR and brings her back to life. The siblings believe that as Stephanie was brought back from the dead, they have beaten death and hence rejoice in their victory. In the ending moments of the movie, we are shown that Charlie is waiting for his girlfriend Jenny to take her to prom and this is when the ominous coin from the beginning of the movie drops from the purse of a lady rolling down a few steps and stopping a railway track from shifting its position for an incoming train. Right at this moment, Jenny's father, who is also a doctor, arrives to meet with Charlie. This is when he informs the siblings that technically Stephanie's heart did not stop and that is why Charlie could bring her back using CPR. Hearing this, the siblings get frightened. But before they could do anything, a train arrives and due to the tracks not being aligned properly, gets derailed. The siblings try to outrun it. But unfortunately, the train was carrying tree logs which fell on them killing Stephanie and then her brother Charlie. This is how death completes its mission. Again another mask is left at the scene of the crime, as Detective Bailey arrives, shattered seeing his daughter be claimed by Ghostface. He makes a comment about losing both of his children, hint hint audience members, as he swears revenge on Ghostface. Gal shows up, mentioning she has new information that could help, leading them to the grand Ghostface shrine that is featured in the trailers, packed with loads of easter eggs and memorabilia from the previous 5 Scream movies. Gale adds this theater was listed under Jason and Greg’s names, the two dudes who were claimed by another Ghostface in the opening. They come up with a plan to trace Ghostface’s phone, because Kirby I guess can do this in under 15 seconds, which actually traces the phone to Gale’s apartment. Gale’s new boy toy is axed, as she puts up a good fight. Even pulling the ole’ *69 trick to auto call back Ghostface’s phone, but is ultimately stabbed with a large shard of glass. The final plan sees them luring Ghostface back to the shrine theater, blocking all of the exits, and giving him the business. However, the group is separated via the subway, and with it being Halloween night, there are a bevy of masked characters. Ethan and Mindy are the two separated, resulting in Mindy being stabbed by a rogue Ghostface. Ethan gets her help, but Mindy is out for the third act. Back at the theater, Sam taps into her supernatural ghost Billy powers, telling her to grab his knife for protection. But every bit of their plan falls apart, with Bailey calling Sam to let her know Kirby hasn’t worked for the FBI for two months, she can’t be trusted. Ghostface appears, starting the climactic chase sequence, as a video of Ritchie’s plays from the projector. Chad is caught off guard, stabbed multiple times by Ghostface. Then another Ghostface shows up, tag team, eiffel towering Chad, essentially turning him into Swiss cheese. Detective Bailey shows up, shooting Kirby in the shoulder, and reveals himself to be one of the Ghostface Killas. Along with his son Ethan “What?!” And daughter Quinn “What a twist!” Who didn’t die earlier, it was all staged. And all three were related to Ritchie, being his father and sibling, making this one big family affair revenge trip “I am speechless. I am without speech” Quinn had started all of the Sam rumors originally to ruin her reputation, as the second part of their plan was to frame Sam for all of the murders in Scream 5. Essentially assassinate her character and cancel her. It’s a big ole’ Scooby Doo chase scene, as the family goes up against Sam and Tara. Tara bests Ethan by stabbing him in the mouth, like hella brutal even twisting it, while Sam shoots Quinn in the head, easily taking them out. After falling from the balcony and passing out, Bailey regains composure, now being hunted by Sam wearing Billy Loomis’s Ghostface costume. Sam taunts him using the classic voice changer, until she attacks him on stage, stabbing him furiously like she did to Ritchie in Scream 5. The final blow to Bailey is a gruesome knife to the eye, that I did not…. See coming. Surprisingly all of the OG cast, Gale, Mindy, and Chad survive, which you just gotta, idk just suspend your disbelief, as the final scene sees Sam staring at Billy’s Ghostface mask, being called to the darkness. She instead tosses it aside, following Tara back into the city. Which totally sets up the mask to return in like a Jim Carrey The Mask scenario for a sequel. Now just don’t leave yet, because Scream 6 has a post credits scene babay! Yes, the first of the franchise, following the trend of every single movie needing a post credits scene now, but at least they are taking the piss out of things with this one. As the scene opens on Mindy Meeks from earlier in the movie talking about the franchise rules of the movie they are in now, saying “Not every movie needs to have a post credits scene.” As it turns to black and the movie ends. It’s something, but not really. At least the Radio Silence team is sticking with the times, and this is a clever joke in the grand meta scheme of things, but is totally on par with the lame Spider-man Homecoming post credits scene, where Cap basically pulls the same gimmick, tongue in cheek, poking fun at whoever is still watching. Now one of the biggest absences from Scream 6, was the scream queen who started it all, Sidney Prescott aka Neve Campbell. Unfortunately her character does not have any screen time, but is at least mentioned in passing a couple of times. According to the movie, the reason she doesn’t make the trip to the ole’ big apple is because due to the news of more Ghostface killings happening, she took her husband, Mark, Ohhh hai mark, and children into hiding until this Ghostface news blows over. So at least the film acknowledged her missing in action, even if it was a “Hey, turn to the screen, and tell the audience directly what is happening with this beloved character.” However outside of the movie sphere, a different reason exists for Campbell not appearing, and it was purely over contract and pay disputes. Back in June of 2022, Campbell announced she would be stepping back from the Scream franchise saying: "Sadly I won't be making the next 'Scream' film. As a woman I have had to work extremely hard in my career to establish my value, especially when it comes to 'Scream.' I felt the offer that was presented to me did not equate to the value I have brought to the franchise." This doesn’t mean she is done forever, she could pop up in a Scream 7 if her family is threatened, but to me it just felt like the script didn’t allow a place for her character. So yeah, sad to see, but also it makes sense. As for a potential Scream 7, at the time of editing this there has been no official word on a sequel. There have been some rumor articles claiming that shooting on Scream 7 is happening later this year, while also mentioning that the early reviews and tracking box office numbers obviously signal that there is a thirst for more Ghostface. Even with the Radio Silence crew chiming in on their eagerness to pick up the mask for another go. So IF, you know there will be, but IF there is a Scream 7, what is it going to entail? Well with Sam essentially being called to the Billy mask, like some sort of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde character, I can see Sam potentially falling to that darkness. Essentially a loose cannon, not knowing if she will turn on her friends, or even going out of her way to scratch the Ghostface itch. Maybe that's too easy of a guess, but you know damn well they are going international with a sequel soon. A completely different environment for Ghostface to play, hell even a Ghostface on a Place scenario “enough is enough” But I can see this also leaning into social media a bit more, potentially people trying to become social media famous by staging Ghostface attacks, and then it’s discovered that there have been 2 killers the whole time, no surprise there, BUT they aren’t connected and have been stepping on one another’s plans throughout the entire movie, like some goofy “Who’s on first” looney tunes sketch. Also I’m surprised an actual Stab movie, show, spin-off, or short hasn’t been experimented with. There could be a market of them basically parodying their own films. But as for Scream 6, it’s a bloody good time. Is it the best in the franchise? Probably not. Is it the worst? Far from. And I think the two things that Radio Silence really honed in on this time around was the brutalness of the kills and the tension of Ghostface. Like you feel and hear the heaviness of the knife gouges, especially when there’s multiple in a row. But man the tension of slowly going through a scene, knowing Ghostface is going to pop out at any moment, was timed perfectly. Not overstaying its welcome, and not being premature. Sure is it another predictable Scream movie? Pretty much, I mean there are only so many liberties you can take with the same formula. But I didn’t guess all of the killers, so still a couple of surprises. I think the biggest thing that didn’t work was the ending felt a bit rushed and anti-climatic. Like the motives they had made sense, but also were just like “Ehhh okay, yeah cool”. And the meta nature of things felt a bit too heavy handed, like show don't tell. Because there’s a lot of “Now I’m announcing this is meta because this happened before.” Be subtle baby. I’ll give ole Scream 6 a solid 7/10 Ghostface attacks. I had fun with this one, and it does exactly what I wanted a Scream movie to do. The cast really shined a bit more than in 5, and I’m intrigued to see more of where these new relationships take them. Anyway I’d love to hear your thoughts on Scream 6. Was the brutal and meta direction everything you hoped for, or was this just more of the same Ghostface just doing his Ghostface stuff? text: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime: The Movie – Scarlet Bond, often shortened to Tensura: The Movie – Scarlet Bond, was a 2022 Japanese animated film based on the light novel series That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime by Fuse. In this action-packed film, set after the events of the second season of the anime series, we follow the journey of Hiiro, a survivor of the Ogre Village, and Towa, the queen of a neighboring kingdom. Following their desertion from Clayman's army, an Ogre and his fellow mercenaries are attacked by Clayman's soldiers, whose leader Yamza severely injures the Ogre. He is found by the people of the Kingdom of Raja and is given the name "Hiiro" by its queen Towa to recover from his injuries. Ten days later, Hiiro escapes Raja to return to the Ogre Village, only to find it destroyed by the Orcs. Wanting vengeance against the Orcs, Hiiro returns to Raja four days later and swears loyalty to Towa. Rimuru, who recently defeated Clayman and has been recognized by other Demon Lords as one of their own, is informed by Souei of an attack toward Geld and his fellow Orcs. The Orcs are fighting against Hiiro and his two Raja subordinates, during which Geld learns that Hiiro seeks revenge against his race, so he drops his weapons and accepts his fate of being killed by him. However, Benimaru saves Geld and pacifies Hiiro, who actually is his childhood friend. Hiiro reunites with Benimaru, Shion, Shuna, Hakuro, Souei, and Kurobe, and reconciles with Geld after learning that the Orcs are no longer their enemies. During a feast hosted by Rimuru, Hiiro reveals that he had arrived at the Jura Tempest Federation as Raja's messenger to ask permission to cultivate a part of the Great Jura Forest to serve as a food source for the kingdom. He informs that Towa is suffering from Curse Poison, the effect of using the power of her tiara to purify a lake filled with toxins from the country's gold mines. Agreeing to help, Rimuru decides to visit the kingdom. Rimuru, Benimaru, Shion, Shuna, and Ranga arrive at Raja. After analyzing her condition, Rimuru gives Towa honey from Tempest to restore part of her health. At the lake, Rimuru reveals to Towa that the toxins are not from mines, as he then splits the lake into two to reveal a hidden structure with an old magic circle that produces the toxin and destroys it. These events have angered Lacua, the merchant behind the poisoning, and schemes to create another disaster to earn praise from the Primordial demon Violet. The lake is poisoned again, so Towa uses her tiara to purify it, resulting in her health deteriorating. A neighboring country takes advantage of her worsening condition to attack Raja and seize the gold that the kingdom mined. Having learned of the news about the encroaching enemy, Rimuru mobilizes his allies, while Diablo heads out to meet with Violet, who created the tiara and the magic circle at the lake. Hiiro is tricked by Lacua to ingest a Curse Orb, being told that it is for transferring Towa's soul to his healthy body, and is fed by him with memories of his village being destroyed to fuel his transformation. Rimuru chases after Lacua, while Benimaru fights Hiiro and Shuna protects Towa. Meanwhile, Diablo confronts Violet, who reveals that she had given the tiara to a previous queen of Raja as part of a game with Raja's royal line in which if the possessor is fully inflicted by the Curse Poison, then she can take over the body and be physically reborn. After failing to defeat him, Violet agrees to Diablo's terms of leaving Raja alone while also voiding the contract with Towa and her line. At Raja, Rimuru defeats Lacua, who blows himself up to destroy everything around him. However, the explosion is contained by Rimuru. Hiiro removes the orb from his body and destroy it. Raja's doctor, who is actually in allegiance with Lacua, is killed by Ranga. Towa uses the full power of the tiara to revive Hiiro from the Curse Orb, causing her body to be covered by the Curse Poison and vanish. However, Violet revives Towa after voiding the game as an apology for her subordinate's actions. While celebrating, Rimuru offers the kingdom's ministers help in rebuilding Raja in exchange for Tempest buying their iron ore. Rimuru returns to Tempest, finds it partially destroyed after Veldora and Milim played together, and punishes them before collapsing from exhaustion. And there you have it, complete recap of That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime: The Movie – Scarlet Bond. And if you enjoyed our recap, don't forget to hit that like button and subscribe for more anime content!

text: The story begins with a bat entering an old house. It transforms into Dracula and moves toward the child in the room. It looks like he is about to kill the baby, but we learn the truth later. The baby's mother is no longer alive. Dracula raises his daughter alone, and they share a wonderful bond. Her father even changes her diapers himself. Later, he teaches his daughter how to transform into a bat. After much practice, she finally succeeds. We soon see a man visiting Dracula... ...who is building a hotel for his daughter's birthday. Because he hates humans, he is very careful while building it... ...ensuring that no humans are ever allowed inside. He wants her to avoid humans and dislike them as much as he does. But despite his efforts, Mavis wants to see the world. Years pass, and the hotel is finally finished. It is now Mavis's 118th birthday. Dracula has invited monsters from all over the world. Mavis reminds her father of his promise to let her see the world. She insists that he must keep his word. Dracula agrees and lets her visit the human world... ...on the condition that she returns quickly. With so many guests arriving... ...it would be wrong for her to be late. Mavis is thrilled and flies to a nearby village. Dracula secretly follows her, but she doesn't know. She arrives in an empty town and calls out for the people. When they appear, the news of a vampire spreads... ...and the angry mob uses fire to drive her away. Mavis tries to be kind, but a man's head suddenly falls off. Dracula quickly fixes the head before his daughter notices anything. We learn that these are not humans, but monsters in disguise. This was all part of Dracula's secret plan... ...to make her fear humans and hate them as he does. Later, Dracula warns all the monsters to avoid humans. Suddenly, a human enters the hotel, and Dracula tries to kick him out. He worries that if the monsters see a human... ...they will lose trust in him as their leader. Dracula asks the boy how he found the place. The boy says he followed some "burning humans" to the hotel. He simply followed them until he arrived. It was actually Dracula's own mistake... ...because the fire led the human right to them. Now, a human has discovered their secret location. He had burned his servants to scare his daughter. The boy saw them while they were returning to the hotel. Dracula doesn't have time to worry about that now. More monsters are arriving at the hotel... ...and he is terrified that they will see the human. He decides to hide the boy from everyone. He takes him to a closet full of clothes. The boy, Jonathan, thinks they are just costumes. Dracula gets an idea to disguise Jonathan as a monster. He dresses him up and drags him out into the hotel. Jonathan thinks he has found a Halloween party. He believes everyone is just wearing great outfits. He accidentally touches a real skeleton... ...and the monsters begin to chase him. Jonathan soon realizes these are real monsters. He tries to escape while processing the shock. He falls onto a flying broomstick... ...and crashes right into Mavis. They look at each other and feel a connection. Dracula quickly pulls Jonathan away to hide him. Jonathan is now terrified of Dracula. He begs Dracula not to drink his blood. He promises to leave immediately. Dracula explains that he is a modern vampire. He doesn't drink human blood anymore. He says human blood is too fatty and unhealthy. Jonathan feels much better after hearing this. Dracula tries to sneak him out the back way. Mavis spots them again while in her bat form. Dracula is forced to bring Jonathan back inside. When Mavis asks who he is, Dracula tells a lie. He says Jonathan is a party planner hired for her birthday. He claims Jonathan was just about to leave. After Mavis leaves, they try a different exit. But they keep bumping into other monsters... ...who are practicing their dance moves. They all notice the boy with Dracula. They ask Dracula about his new friend. Jonathan tells them he is a cousin of Frankenstein. The real Frankenstein is confused by this. He says he doesn't recognize this relative. Jonathan quickly makes up another story... ...and the monsters eventually believe him. They ask him to help with the music for the party. The monsters were singing a very dull song. Jonathan takes over and sings something modern. He shows them how to really have a good time. Everyone loves his energy and his music. They insist that he stays for the big celebration. Dracula can no longer force him to leave. Jonathan teaches them about scooters and pool parties. The hotel chef's rat smells a human at the pool. Dracula panics and tries to hide Jonathan again. He successfully pulls him away from the crowd. Dracula tries to erase the boy's memories... ...so he forgets about the hotel and the monsters. But because Jonathan wears contact lenses, the magic fails. When Jonathan removes the lenses, Dracula is surprised. As he prepares to leave, Mavis finds him again. She takes him to the roof to show him the night sky. Jonathan shares stories of his travels around the world. Mavis feels sad because she has never seen these things. Jonathan helps her see the beauty of the sunrise. Meanwhile, the other monsters are enjoying the pool. Dracula lies and says Jonathan left because he hated them. Suddenly, Jonathan falls through the roof into Dracula's arms. Dracula is very frustrated. He makes Jonathan help with all the chores. But Jonathan isn't good at manual labor. Dracula uses his powers to set the tables quickly. Jonathan is impressed and hops onto a flying table. Dracula is annoyed at first, but then starts to have fun. He realizes that he actually likes Jonathan. Suddenly, Jonathan is kidnapped by the chef. The chef wants to cook him because he is a human. Dracula finds them and rescues Jonathan just in time. He freezes the chef so the secret stays safe. By now, Dracula truly considers Jonathan a friend. He allows him to stay until the party is over. Dracula takes Jonathan aside and tells him his life story. He explains why he fears and hates humans. He and his wife were very happy once. They lived in a castle where Mavis was born. But instead of being kind... ...angry humans attacked and burned their home. He saved Mavis, but he could not save his wife. Jonathan is deeply moved by this tragedy. The party begins, and Mavis looks beautiful in her dress. Jonathan’s planning makes the party a huge success. As Mavis and Jonathan grow closer, the chef appears. He reveals that Jonathan is actually a human. The monsters panic and run away in fear. They are angry that Dracula let a human inside. Mavis tells Jonathan she still likes him. Jonathan pretends to hate monsters to save Dracula's reputation. He acts like the "evil human" they all fear... ...and leaves the hotel to protect the monsters. Mavis is heartbroken and retreats to her room. Dracula realizes his daughter truly loves the boy. He admits he was wrong about all humans being evil. He tells the other monsters that he made a mistake. He explains that there are good people in the world. The monsters forgive him and want to help. They agree to help him find Jonathan. They realize Jonathan is already on his way home. The monsters bravely enter the human world to find him. They find a human Halloween festival... ...where everyone is dressed like a monster. The real monsters fit right in with the crowd. They are happy to see that humans actually admire them. The humans help the monsters clear a path through traffic. Dracula needs to reach the airport, but the sun is out. Vampires cannot survive in direct sunlight. The humans work together to shield Dracula from the sun. They use their capes to create a tunnel of shade... ...allowing Dracula to reach the airport safely. However, Jonathan’s plane has already taken off. Dracula flies after the plane, despite the sun. He tries to communicate with Jonathan through the window. When the boy can't hear him through the glass... ...Dracula hypnotizes the pilot to speak to him. He apologizes and asks Jonathan to return. He gives his blessing for Jonathan and Mavis to be together. The plane lands, and Dracula brings Jonathan back to the hotel. Mavis is overjoyed to see Jonathan again. They confess their love for each other. Jonathan explains why he had to lie earlier. The monsters and humans celebrate the couple together. The story ends with a grand celebration.
