text: Six days after Rose Cotter's death, police officer Joel, now cursed, confronts two criminals who had shot a mother and her child in Newark. One of them asks, "Who are you?" to which Joel responds that he has something for them but that they need to watch what he's about to do. He then pulls out a knife, stabs one of the criminals, and slits his throat. The other criminal shoots Joel, but Joel shoots him back in self-defense. Realizing his mistake, Joel rushes to the man, saying, "Don't die!" He removes his mask and tells the man that he can’t die because the curse won’t transfer if he dies. However, the man eventually dies. Frustrated, Joel stands up, muttering that now there’s no one for the curse to pass to, but suddenly, he hears a noise behind him and turns to see a boy there. Joel confronts him, asking who he is and what he’s doing there, to which the boy, Lewis, replies that he was just there to buy from them. Joel apologizes, saying, this wasn’t meant for you, and when Lewis asks what wasn’t meant for him, Joel only says he's sorry and leaves. However, as he steps outside, he encounters more criminals, forcing him to rush back inside. He manages to escape through a window as they shoot at him, but he’s run over and killed by an oncoming car. After the interview, Skye greets her fans, signing autographs and taking selfies. When she returns to her car, her mom Elizabeth praises her for being perfectly graceful, and her assistant Joshua excitedly informs her that she’s trending number two on Twitter. Next, we see Skye at rehearsals, when suddenly she feels a sharp pain in her back mid-move, prompting instructor Anton to stop everyone and ask if she’s okay. Skye insists she’s fine, and Anton calls for a break and some ice, but Skye resists, asking if they can just continue. Later, Skye pulls a box of pills from her bag, but a sudden knock on the door startles her, causing her to accidentally drop the pills down the washbasin drain. Elizabeth opens the door, asking if she’s okay and ready to go, to which Skye replies that she just needs another minute. Later, Skye meets with Lewis, who suddenly pulls her inside, and holding a sword to her throat, asks what she wants. Skye nervously replies that she just wants Vicodin, like last time, to help with the pain. Lewis says Skye Riley isn't just gonna suddenly show up here, to which she tells him he texted her to come over. Confused, he checks his phone, admitting he doesn’t remember sending that message. Skye tells him to back off, and he quickly apologizes, explaining he’s having the worst week. Skye asks what was with the sword? to which he says he is in the middle of some genuinely freaky stuff and asks does she believes in weird things? Skye decides to leave, but he requests her to stay, saying he is stoked to see her, and tells her to come in and be his guest. Skye says she just wants Vicodin for her back, to which he asks her to wait and he will be right back. While waiting, Skye notices drugs on the table, and then her attention shifts to the TV, where news reports show that Paul Hudson died in a car accident after Paul and Skye had left a private party while intoxicated. The report then shows her photos, which went viral two weeks after the accident, prompting Skye to turn off the TV. Now when Lewis doesn't emerge from his room for a long time, Skye starts heading toward his bedroom, but suddenly, Lewis bursts out, screaming, which frightens Skye. Lewis then grows terrified as he sees something behind her, and she asks what it is, to which Lewis screams, "Get away from him!" He then begins choking, prompting Skye to rush to check on him and ask if she should call an ambulance, but after a moment, Lewis suddenly calms down, and a creepy smile spreads across his face. Skye, terrified, falls back, and Lewis grabs a weight plate, and Skye watches in horror as he strikes himself in the face with it. Lewis lowers the plate, revealing his crushed face before collapsing and dying, leaving Skye in shock. Skye dials 911 on her phone, but realizing there are drugs on the table, she hesitates and ultimately decides not to make the call. Shocked by the incident, Skye returns home, and as she tries to sleep, she hears a noise that startles her. She gets up to check but finds no one there. However, as she scans the room, she is horrified to see Lewis standing there, who disappears the moment she turns on the light. The next day, Elizabeth tells Skye she looks exhausted and reminds her to stay on top of her sleep schedule. She asks if she has spoken to Gemma about coming on tour, but Skye replies that Gemma won’t want to hear from her. Elizabeth insists that Gemma is her best friend and would forgive her. Skye tells her to drop it, but Elizabeth argues that real friends are hard to find. Joshua offers to help with any personal tasks and Elizabeth says she needs to stay hydrated, but Skye tells her to stop. Darius then enters the room and says he has a small favor to ask of Skye. He explains that there is a fundraising dinner for Music Inspires Hope tomorrow night, a foundation supporting underprivileged youth. He mentions that Interscope Records has done a lot of work with the foundation, and he was hoping she would be willing to be a special presenter. He reassures her that her remarks are prewritten, and all she has to do is smile and read from the teleprompter. Next, During Skye's photoshoot, her expressions reveal that something is weighing on her mind. Despite the glamour of the moment, she seems increasingly worried, her focus drifting as she battles with whatever is troubling her. Later, Skye Googles, "Does vomit have DNA?" recalling she vomited after seeing Lewis's dead body at his house. Worried, she begins to write a text message to Gemma but hesitates and decides not to send it, and just then, she receives a text from an unknown number. She opens the message, which reads: "Were you at Lewis' apartment last night?" Skye feels a surge of fear as she reads the text, and just then, she hears a sound, but when she quickly turns around to check, she finds no one there. However, when she turns back, she is shocked to see something, and it’s revealed that Lewis is standing right behind her, but when she looks back again, no one is there. As she turns once more, Lewis is still behind her, and suddenly, he forces a smile onto her face, sending a wave of terror through her. Skye looks around, finding herself completely alone, unable to understand what is happening to her. Her team then comes there and Skye tells Elizabeth that she's not wearing the dress, and when she asks what's wrong with it, Tanya flashes a light on Skye, and she points out that the lighting will show right through it onstage. Elizabeth says she thinks Skye is overreacting a little, but Skye firmly insists, "I'm not wearing it." The next day, at an event, a fan named Alfredo tells Skye he can see her sadness and claims he can make her happy, making her uneasy. He compliments her skin before security intervenes, pulling him away. Skye goes backstage, where Elizabeth asks if she's okay and offers her a break, but Skye shakes her head, saying let's just get through this. Now when Skye comes out, a little girl with a creepy smile approaches her. Skye asks, "What's your name?" but the girl just keeps smiling and staring at her. Feeling uneasy, Skye signs the girl's shirt, and Jason asks, "How about a photo?" As they pose for the picture, the girl continues to stare at Skye, deepening her discomfort, and then she walks away. Later, Skye, puzzled over who could have sent the message, anxiously pulls at her hair, and after some thought, she calls Gemma, but it goes to voicemail. Skye leaves a message, saying she’s been thinking about her and wants to apologize for everything. She admits she misses her and asks if she will call her back. Soon after, Gemma calls back, and Skye admits feeling overwhelmed and hesitantly asks if she can come over, to which Gemma agrees, saying she’ll be there in 45 minutes. Skye drinks from her water bottle, puts it on the table, and then leaves, leaving the bottle behind. She then begins singing a song while playing the piano, but after a while, a sudden noise startles her, and when she gets up to investigate, she finds her water bottle shattered on the floor. Skye grabs a mop to clean up the broken glass, but to her shock, she discovers Alfredo’s T-shirt, the one she signed at the event, lying on the floor. Scared, as she moves forward, she finds Alfredo's shoes and clothes on the floor. The lights suddenly go out, and to Skye’s horror, she sees Alfredo standing naked in front of her, grinning eerily. As he suddenly lunges toward her, Skye bolts in fear but stumbles back when she spots Gemma at the door. Gemma, alarmed, asks what’s happening, but Skye urgently signals her to be quiet and grabs a nearby vase. Gemma asks if someone else is there, and cautiously follows Skye, but to Skye’s shock, Alfredo’s clothes have vanished, and, even more unsettling, her water bottle is now back on the table. Confused, Skye hugs Gemma and asks how she got here so quickly, to which Gemma says she called her about an hour ago. Skye drinks from her bottle, and when Gemma asks if she's thirsty, Skye explains that her therapist advised her to drink a glass of water whenever she feels overwhelmed by the urge to get drunk. They sit down, and Skye tells Gemma that Lewis from high school died in front of her yesterday. Gemma is shocked, and Skye explains that she went to his apartment to buy Vicodin for pain, stressing that she hasn't touched alcohol or coke in a year, but her back is still messed up. Gemma asks what happened to Lewis, and Skye explains that when she showed up, he was terrified of something. He started freaking out, screaming, and then grabbed a metal gym weight and smashed his own face in with it. Gemma is shocked, and Skye continues, saying she didn’t know what to do, so she just left him there. Gemma asks if anyone else knows about this, and Skye replies, "No," before asking if she should tell the police. Gemma advises against it, saying if anyone connects her to a drug dealer's death, the story will take over her life and ruin everything, and it's not her fault. Skye confesses she keeps seeing his face everywhere, to which Gemma says she can't imagine how scary that must have been. Next, Skye is badly injured in an accident, and to her horror, she sees Paul's dead body next to her, but suddenly, she wakes up from the nightmare, gasping for breath. As she lies back on the bed, she tells Gemma, "I'm so sorry about everything," to which Gemma calmly replies, "It's okay, I already forgave you." Skye says she feels like her brain is full of chaos and noise like she's trapped alone in darkness, wanting to quiet the noise but not knowing how. Gemma responds, "That's because you're a horrible person." Shocked, Skye asks, "What did you say?" and to her terror, Gemma wakes up with a creepy smile. Her face suddenly changes, causing Skye to fall off the bed, but she finds no one on the bed. Just then, Gemma arrives, and Skye notices it's morning and realizes she’s late. In a panic, she rushes out to drink water, and when Gemma asks if she can help, Skye asks, "Will you come on tour?" to which Gemma hesitates, saying, "I feel like this is something we should talk about first." At that moment, Elizabeth enters, and Skye apologizes to her before quickly rushing to her room. Next, we see Skye at the rehearsal, and everything is going smoothly until, suddenly, a face flashes in front of her, causing her to break a bone in her leg, and she screams in pain. Anton rushes over to check on her and asks, What's wrong? and to her shock, Skye realizes her leg is completely fine. She quickly gets up and claims that someone was out of place and knocked her over. However, Anton replies, "From where I was watching, I didn’t see anyone out of place. Frustrated, Skye heads backstage, where Joshua passes by her with a creepy smile on his face, and when she enters her room, she finds that someone has completely destroyed it. Skye pulls her hair in frustration, and as she tries to leave, Elizabeth arrives, and Skye asks Joshua what his problem is, to which he claims he has no idea what she’s talking about. Elizabeth takes Skye back to her room, where Skye tells her to believe that Joshua did it, to which she tries to calm her down, saying that Joshua has been with her the entire day. Elizabeth asks if Skye is being honest and if she’s using again? to which Skye denies it, offering to take a test, but admits she feels like she’s losing her mind and regrets agreeing to the tour. Elizabeth reassures her, promising to adjust the schedule to help her decompress but insists Skye pull herself together and attend Darius's foundation event, reminding her of her commitment to underprivileged youth. Later, backstage, Skye texts Gemma, asking what time she’ll be done with her tasks, and as she waits, she’s distracted by a fly buzzing around her. She texts Gemma to come over when she’s finished, but the fly continues to bother her. Then, Skye receives a message from an unknown number saying, "I know this is Skye Riley, the singer." The fly lands just above her lips, and in swatting it away, she accidentally smudges her lip color. She then heads to the stage, where the crowd cheers for her, and she thanks them warmly. She then begins reading from the teleprompter, but it suddenly stops, leaving her momentarily speechless, and after a brief pause, she says, hoping the audience is enjoying the party. When the teleprompter still doesn’t resume, she decides to speak off-script, talking about her past struggles with drugs. However, the guests respond poorly, and the atmosphere becomes tense. Noticing the audience’s reaction, Skye quickly apologizes and realizes the teleprompter is working again. She begins reading, introducing the next guest as *"a very special person who surely needs no introduction, Paul Hudson." The crowd, along with Skye, is shocked, and she asks aloud why it says that. Just then, she spots Paul in the audience, staring at her with a creepy smile as he begins walking toward her. Terrified, Skye tells him to stay away, insisting that Paul is dead and that he isn’t really Paul. She closes her eyes, whispering to herself to stay calm, and when she opens them, Paul has vanished. An older woman approaches to check on her, but Paul suddenly appears, startling Skye so badly that she accidentally pushes the woman, injuring her. Later, Skye stares at her phone, waiting for a reply from Gemma, but Instead, she receives a message from the unknown, saying, "You’re in serious danger, and I can help you." Skye texts back, *"Who is this?" to which the response comes quickly: *"You’re not imagining things, and Everything you’re seeing is real." Panicked, Skye gets up and steps outside, only to receive another text saying, "Lewis posted this four days ago." She plays the video, which shows Lewis recording inside his apartment. Pointing the camera at a dark corner, he asks, "Do you see it?" As he zooms in, he whispers, "It just stares at me, smiling." Suddenly, Lewis appears, startling Skye, but when she looks around, she realizes no one is there. Skye decides to meet with the person who’s been messaging her and asks how he knew Lewis, to which he explains he didn’t, and he’d only been trying to warn him. He tracked down his address and found his apartment door unlocked, only to discover that Lewis was already dead. He checked Lewis’s phone and saw she was the last person he’d texted. Skye asks what he was trying to warn Lewis about, and he replies, that Lewis didn’t kill himself, but he was systematically infected, possessed, and then murdered by some kind of metaphysical being. Skye asks what he’s talking about, to which he says you might call it a spirit or a demon, but he has no clue what it is. It disguises itself to look like smiling people, but only the person infected by it can see it. Skye calls it supernatural bullshit, but he counters that she’s already seen it, which is why she’s still sitting here. Skye admits to him that she feels like she’s losing her mind, to which he tells her that’s precisely what this thing does. It drives its host insane, feeding on their fears and traumas, and eventually forces them to kill themselves in front of a witness. This witness then becomes the new host, and that’s how she got it from Lewis. He explains that it’s a parasitic entity that has been passed from person to person in a chain stretching back through various hosts, including a cop in Jersey, a doctor, a patient, and further back. He’s documented all of this and offers to show her, and reveals that his brother was a host, eight people before her. He says his brother tried to warn him, but it was hard to believe him, because what he was saying sounded insane. Skye asks if he’s gone to the police, to which he scoffs, saying they wouldn’t be able to help. Skye asks if she’s just supposed to wait until this thing kills her, to which he tells her he wants her help to destroy it. She asks how? to which he explains the chain breaks if the host dies outside the entity’s control. Skye realizes this means she’d have to die before it kills her. He agrees, suggesting a safe way to stop her heart temporarily and then resuscitate her. Introducing himself as Morris, an ER nurse, he warns they’re running out of time as she’s been infected for three days. Suddenly, people at the bar recognize Skye, mock her over a viral video, and start filming, forcing her to leave. Skye returns home to pack her things, but just as she’s about to leave, she freezes in terror seeing the background dancers standing in her living room, their faces twisted into unsettling, eerie smiles. Panic setting in, Skye looks towards the door, but when she looks back, the dancers are even closer, their smiles growing more sinister. Mustering her courage, she suddenly runs to escape, and the dancers follow her, but she meets with an even more chilling sight, and Skye realizes she’s trapped, as the group behind her now blocks her way back. The next moment, they all suddenly appear directly in front of her and begin closing in slowly, step by step. Skye panics and bolts toward the door, but before she can reach it, they grab her, pick her up, and hurl her onto a table. She tries to get up and escape, but they slam her head against the piano and the impact leaves her dazed and disoriented. The group surrounds her and one of them yanks her hair, forcing her to scream in agony. Her cries echo in the room, but they’re cut short when a hand reaches toward her mouth and forces its way inside, impossibly far, and the scene abruptly cuts to black. Next, we see Skye and Paul returning from the party, both visibly intoxicated. Their conversation quickly escalates into an argument, with Paul angrily calling her a psycho. Enraged, Skye retaliates, but Paul mocks her, laughing at her frustration. The tension in the car reaches its peak as Paul’s taunts push Skye over the edge. In a fit of anger, she jerks the steering wheel, causing the car to veer off the road and crash violently. The screen fades to black before Skye suddenly awakens, Elizabeth is seated by her side, trying to soothe her, and she tells her that she had a mild concussion. Skye asks where she is, and Elizabeth explains that it's a private wellness clinic. She adds that she fainted, hit her head, and was found unconscious on her living room floor, and the doctor mentioned that she was severely sleep-deprived and dehydrated. Skye insists that's not what happened, but Elizabeth tells Joshua to inform the doctor that Skye is awake. After he leaves, Elizabeth reassures Skye they can cover it with makeup, and the team is working on a hairpiece. She clears Skye’s schedule for rest but withholds her phone. Skye insists something crazy is happening and she needs to leave. Elizabeth, however, reassures her that they’ll stay together until tomorrow, when they head to the venue for the preshow, to ensure she’s at 100% and ready to perform. Skye says she can’t do the show, but Elizabeth warns her that if she cancels, she’ll have to check herself into a recovery program. Skye protests, saying she doesn't understand, but Elizabeth firmly states there are no more second chances. If she cancels, this is it, because the media will tear her apart, and everything they’ve built will be over. Skye asks why that's all Elizabeth cares about, accusing her of treating her like a mere windup toy. Elizabeth, visibly angry, stands up and says she has given up everything for Skye. She’s sacrificed every fiber of her being to support her, yet Skye is too selfish to see it. Elizabeth reminds her of the hell she’s put everyone through, and yet they still stand by her, only for Skye to want to throw it all away. Skye says she wishes Elizabeth could feel what it's like to live inside her head, to which Elizabeth says she’s tasted what’s in her mind. She then walks to a mirror and smashes it with her hand. Terrified, Skye tries to pull the IV out of her arm, and meanwhile, Elizabeth approaches her with a shard of the broken mirror. As Skye struggles, The entity says look what she’s doing to her poor mother and then begins stabbing her neck. Skye finally manages to rip out the IV, but the entity controlling Elizabeth makes her stab her own eye. Skye tries to escape but suddenly stops, horrified to find herself holding the mirror shard, her gown soaked in blood. Turning around, she sees her mother lying fatally wounded on the floor. She slaps herself, whispering that it’s not real, but as she rushes to her mother’s side, she realizes in horror that the entity made her kill her own mother. Skye steps out and tries to slip away quietly without being noticed. However, Joshua spots her and notices the blood, asking, "Is that blood?" Skye quickly denies it, but Joshua, concerned, says they need to get the doctor immediately. Skye snaps, telling him to shut up, but by then, the clinic staff has already arrived. Panicked, Skye approaches the security guard, and seizes his gun. She points it at the crowd, warning everyone to stay back. Darius asks what she’s doing and urges her to think about the tour, but Skye flees. As Skye steps out of the clinic, she accidentally steps on a broken bottle, wincing in pain. Just then, Gemma approaches her, asking, "What are you doing here?" to which Skye asks if her car is nearby, and Gemma replies that her mom's driver brought her. Without wasting another moment, Skye points the gun at the driver, forcing him out, and they drive off, leaving the clinic behind. Gemma asks, "Where are we going?" but Skye texts Morris for help, and says she doesn’t know, just to keep driving. Morris replies with a location, and Skye tells Gemma they need to head to Staten Island. Gemma insists she needs a hospital, but Skye pulls the glass from her feet and tells Gemma to pull over. Gemma reminds her she asked to go to Staten Island, but Skye says all I’ve ever done is make your life hell, so just pull over and get away from me before I ruin your life too. Gemma refuses, declaring, “Ride or die,” and keeps driving. Skye says she needs to tell her something, but her phone rings before she can, and she freezes, shocked to see the call is from Gemma. Scared, she answers, and Gemma apologizes, explaining that it took her a few days to return the call after hearing Skye’s voicemail. Skye asks if she spent the night at her place, to which Gemma replies she hasn’t been there in over a year, and as Skye looks at Gemma, the entity says, Gemma hates you. Frustrated, Skye attempts to get out of the car, but the entity tells her that no one cares about her. Skye tries to convince herself it's not real, repeating to herself, "It's just in my head, and You’re not in control, I am." Closing her eyes, she keeps repeating, "I am in control," and when she opens her eyes, she finds herself driving and narrowly avoids an accident. She then visits Morris and hands him the gun, saying, "If your theory doesn’t work or if you see me change and start smiling, shoot me in the head." Morris brings her into a building, and as they enter a freezer, he warns her that the freezer latch is broken, so if the door closes all the way, it can't be opened from the inside. They begin the procedure, and Morris explains that the moment she flatlines, he will start a timer for eight minutes. Once the timer is up, he will inject a dose of adrenaline into her heart and begin CPR to resuscitate her. Skye apologizes about her brother and thanks him for helping her. Morris asks what made her change her mind, and she responds, "Every good thing in my life ends up broken because of me. I hurt everything and everyone I touch, so it doesn't matter what happens to me anymore, but I won't let this thing use me to hurt anyone else. Morris then places a thermometer in her mouth and instructs her not to move, saying he just has to get something. He then leaves the freezer, leaving her alone inside. Panicked, she pulls the thermometer out and looks around, whispering, "Don’t leave me alone here." After a while, blood drips onto her, and she hears someone crying, and to her horror, she sees the entity in her form, right above her, crying in pain. Skye is terrified by the sight, and after a moment, the entity falls onto her, but when Skye looks around, she realizes there’s no one else in the freezer. Suddenly, the entity grabs her hair and slams her against the wall, saying, "I’ve been waiting for you for such a long time." It then says, "I like wearing your skin," before throwing her aside. Skye turns around, and the entity taunts her, telling her she can't escape from it. She glances toward the door, but suddenly, the entity appears right beside her and climbs on top of her, saying, "You will never escape who you truly are on the inside." Desperate, Skye tries to reach the needle, but the entity says, "Look at me," and Skye is frozen, stunned by the sight. The entity then force open her mouth, and then opens its mouth, prompting Skye to close her eyes. Suddenly, Skye opens her eyes, biting off the entity's thumbs, causing it to scream in pain. Seizing the opportunity, Skye grabs the needle and injects herself, making the entity scream in frustration. As Skye begins to fade, the entity starts laughing at her, telling her, "This isn’t real," and when Skye looks at her hand, she finds there is no needle in her hand. The entity slowly gets up, and Skye desperately tries to escape, but the door slams shut automatically, and the entity says, You are not in control, I am." It then moves toward her, adds, "Break a leg out there," and shuts the door. After a while, gas begins filling the chamber, and as the gas thickens, Skye suddenly finds herself on a stage, the crowd cheering around her, and her mother, Joshua, and Darius are also there, watching as if nothing is wrong. Skye then sees the entity, now in her form, wearing a creepy smile. It tears her dress, exposing the scar on her skin, and then with its hands, it begins to rip open her stomach, letting the entity’s hands emerge. Skye watches in horror as the entity’s head slowly emerges from inside her, and as she screams in terror, she collapses to her knees. The entity, now face to face with her, approaches her, opens her mouth wide open with its hands, and tears her jaw apart. But in reality, Skye is writhing in agony on stage, trapped in the horror of her mind. After a while, she rises, and the crowd erupts in cheers once again, but when she turns toward them, with a smile on her face, the crowd falls eerily silent. Skye raises the microphone to her mouth, and in front of them all, she ends her own life by driving the microphone into her eye, and the crowd screams in terror as the screen cuts to black, and the movie ends.

In the heart of New York City lives Iris, a solitary writer whose ordered existence is thrown into disarray when her closest friend and mentor Walter takes his own life. The aftermath of this tragedy brings an unexpected companion into Iris's life. Apollo Walter's imposing great Dne. friend unfolds as a poignant journey through grief, offering a window into how unexpected connections can lead to healing and self-discovery. The film opens with Iris contemplating Walter's suicide, wondering if he ever considered what would happen to his dog. This question becomes central to her processing of grief. What will happen to the dog? We're introduced to Walter through flashbacks at a dinner party where he enthusiastically recounts finding Apollo magically appearing between two bridges, silhouetted against what he poetically calls the limpid sky. The scene establishes Walter as a charismatic writer and storyteller, surrounded by friends who both admire and gently mock his dramatic flare. After Walter's death, we see the aftermath at his memorial service. His widow, Barbara, speaks about how his students and colleagues meant almost as much to him as his writing. The memorial brings together various people from Walter's life, including his first wife, Elaine, and his daughter, Val. There's tension and awkwardness as these women navigate their relationships in Walter's absence. Elaine refers to herself and Iris as surviving divorced wives, noting with some bitterness that there can only be one widow. This gathering reveals the complicated web of relationships Walter left behind. Iris is also working on a book of Walter's correspondence alongside Val, who is revealed to be Walter's daughter. This professional commitment keeps Walter present in Iris's life, even as she struggles to process his absence. The book project becomes both a tether to Walter and a source of tension, particularly as Val reveals that Walter had concerns about Iris's slow pace of work. The heart of the story truly begins when Barbara asks Iris to take Apollo. Barbara claims this was Walter's contingency plan. That should anything happen to him, Apollo would go to Iris. She explains that the dog is miserable with her, waiting by the door day and night as if expecting Walter to return. Iris initially resists, pointing out that dogs aren't allowed in her building and that she's more of a cat person. Nevertheless, she reluctantly agrees to take Apollo temporarily. Apollo's arrival completely disrupts Iris's carefully maintained life. The great Dne takes over her bed, destroys her pillows, including pages of her manuscript, and refuses to eat. He's clearly grieving for Walter, just as Iris is. Their early days together are awkward and strained. Apollo whines at night, refuses to use the elevator, and generally behaves like a creature who has lost his north star. Iris, meanwhile, faces practical challenges like sneaking Apollo past her building superintendent and finding places where Apollo is welcome. As days pass, Iris and Apollo begin to form a tentative bond. She discovers that Apollo loves being read to, possibly because Walter used to read to him. This small connection creates a bridge between them. Val helps by reading to Apollo from Walter's writings, and gradually the dog begins to eat again and engage with his new reality. The relationship between Iris and Apollo is complicated by an eviction notice from her building management. Dogs aren't allowed, and despite Iris's attempts to find Apollo another home, including a trial stay with Tuesday, who knew Walter, she increasingly realizes she doesn't want to part with him. Apollo has become important to her, a living connection to Walter and a companion in grief. Through conversations with others who knew Walter, especially Elaine, Iris begins to process her complicated feelings about her friend. She learns that Elaine knew about her brief romantic history with Walter years ago, something Iris had kept private. This revelation opens a door for Iris to be more honest about her complex relationship with Walter. They had a brief affair when she was a student, which then evolved into a deep, decadesl long friendship that was central to both their lives. The film explores Iris's creative struggles as well. She hasn't written much since before taking on Walter's correspondence project. In a telling scene, she discovers Apollo has destroyed pages of her abandoned novel, Eastern Block, which Walter had also disliked. This destruction symbolizes how Apollo is forcing Iris to confront both her creative block and her unresolved feelings about Walter. In a pivotal sequence, Iris sees a therapist, Dr. Warren, ostensibly to get documentation that would allow her to keep Apollo as an emotional support animal. This session becomes a breakthrough moment as she finally expresses her anger about Walter's suicide. Not just sadness, but rage at the selfishness of his choice and how it affected everyone who loved him, including Apollo. During this therapy session, Iris imagines a conversation with Walter where she confronts him directly. She accuses him of selfishness and lack of consideration, particularly for leaving Apollo alone in the house with his body. Walter defensively responds, "In my defense, I was suicidal." Highlighting the impossible nature of judging someone's actions when they're in such despair. This imagined conversation allows Iris to express her anger and move toward acceptance. The therapy session also leads Iris to consider writing about her experience. Not just editing Walter's words, but creating something new from her own perspective. This marks a turning point in her creative life, suggesting a path forward through her grief. Through persistence and some legal maneuvering regarding emotional support animals, Iris manages to secure permission to keep Apollo in her apartment. The superintendent, Hector, delivers the good news, and their celebration marks a moment of relief and joy in a story otherwise weighted with grief. As Iris and Apollo settle into life together, she begins to wonder about his history before Walter. Who was he as a puppy? Where did he come from? These questions parallel her feelings about Walter, the desire to know everything about someone you love, including the parts of their life you weren't present for. This curiosity shows how fully she has embraced Apollo as her companion. The final act of the film reveals that Val has arranged for Iris and Apollo to move to her family's beach house, which is being sold but is available until the end of May. This gives them one more summer together, a gift of time and space away from the constraints of city life. At the beach, Apollo can wander freely, and Iris has room to write. She begins to work on a new project, suggesting her creative revival. In these closing scenes, Iris reflects on the unfairness of dogs short lifespans compared to humans. She wishes Apollo could live as long as she does, knowing their time together will be limited. When Apollo momentarily disappears on the beach, her panic reveals how important he has become to her. Finding him safe becomes a moment of pure joy and relief. The film ends with Iris and Apollo on the beach dancing to Manhattan, embracing their time together. However long it might be, this final scene embodies acceptance of loss, of unexpected joy, and of the unpredictable nature of love and connection. Through Apollo, Iris has found a way to process her grief for Walter and reconnect with her own creative voice. Apollo forces Iris out of her isolation, making her interact with neighbors, building management, dog parks, and veterinarians. He disrupts her carefully ordered existence, but brings a new kind of joy and connection to her life. The film delicately navigates the complicated feelings surrounding suicide. We see characters struggling with anger, guilt, and confusion about Walter's choice. There's no simple explanation offered, just as there rarely is in real life. Instead, the film focuses on how those left behind must find ways to continue living. Walter's absence is a void that can't be filled, but new connections can be formed around that void. Walter himself remains somewhat enigmatic, shown mainly through others memories and reactions. He was clearly charismatic and talented, but also selfish and complicated. His relationships with multiple women, including his wives and Iris, suggest a pattern of connection and disconnection. His daughter Val represents an attempt at reconciliation as he brought her into his professional life by having her work with Iris on his correspondence. His behavior validates the depth of animal emotions while also providing a mirror for Iris's own grieving process. Unlike humans, Apollo can't rationalize or contextualize his loss. He simply feels it and responds with pure emotion. This directness becomes a guide for Iris's own healing. The film also touches on the complex dynamics of literary legacy. Walter was concerned about how he would be remembered, hence the book of correspondence. Iris, as his editor and friend, bears the responsibility of shaping that legacy. Yet, as she processes her grief, she begins to consider creating her own narrative about Walter rather than simply curating his words. This shift represents her reclaiming her own voice as a writer and as someone who has her own story to tell about their relationship. Class and privilege subtly underpin the narrative. Walter and his social circle are successful writers and academics able to afford brownstones in Brooklyn and beach houses. Iris lives in a rent controlled apartment that was once her father's. The preservation of this apartment becomes crucial not just for emotional reasons but practical ones. She will never find another place she can afford. This economic reality adds stakes to her fight to keep Apollo beyond just emotional attachment. The film explores different types of love without necessarily labeling them. Iris insists she wasn't in love with Walter in a romantic sense. Yet, their connection was profound and central to both their lives. Her relationship with Apollo develops from reluctant caretaking to deep attachment. These bonds defy simple categorization, but represent the various ways humans connect with others, both human and animal. Particularly poignant is the parallel between Apollo and Iris's father. Both faced illness with dignity, fought to live, and loved those around them. This contrasts sharply with Walter's choice to end his life. Through caring for Apollo in his aging years, Iris perhaps finds a way to honor her father's memory while also processing her complicated feelings about Walter's suicide. The beach house represents a kind of grace, an unexpected gift of time and space. It allows Iris and Apollo to escape the constraints of city life and find a place where both can thrive. The open space matches Apollo's size and energy while giving Iris room to breathe and create. It's both a literal and figurative opening up after the confinement of grief. By the end of the film, Iris has moved from seeing Apollo as Walter's dog that she's temporarily caring for to her companion, her friend. This shift represents her acceptance of her new reality, one without Walter, but with new and meaningful connections. She no longer sees Apollo as a burden or a reminder of loss, but as a gift, a living being with whom she can share love and joy. The friend ultimately suggests that healing from loss doesn't mean forgetting or replacing what's been lost. Rather, it means finding new connections that acknowledge the void while creating space for joy. Apollo doesn't replace Walter in Iris's life, and nothing could. But he offers a different kind of companionship that helps her move forward. The film ends not with complete resolution, but with a moment of joy amidst ongoing grief. Iris and Apollo dancing on the beach acknowledges that life continues, that pleasure is still possible even as time remains limited. It's a celebration of the present moment, embracing what is rather than dwelling on what was lost or fearing what might come. Through its exploration of grief, companionship, and creativity, the friend offers a nuanced portrait of how we survive loss. It suggests that sometimes healing comes in unexpected forms like a massive bed hogging Great Dne who refuses to eat anything but refuses to leave your side. In Apollo's steadfast presence, Iris finds not just a companion, but a way forward, a reason to engage with the world again, and ultimately a reflection of her own capacity for loyalty, love, and resilience. As the credits roll on Iris and Apollo dancing on the beach, we're left with the understanding that grief is not something to be overcome, but rather integrated into a life that continues to unfold in surprising ways. Their dance celebrates not just survival, but the discovery of joy in the midst of loss. The unexpected friendship that grew between a solitary writer and her friend's beloved dog. And the healing power of connection both to others and to our own creative voices.

text: Hello, and welcome to the PlayWorms. Today we shall be looking at the movie FAST X. The film opens ten years earlier in Rio de Janeiro. Crime boss Hernan Reyes and his sociopathic son Dante are awaiting for Dom and his crew to go for them. Their Brazil heist goes off in the streets, with Dante pursuing them alongside his father. They make it to the bridge where Dom stayed behind to ensure Reyes’s demise while Dante was knocked off the bridge and into the water. Present day in Los Angeles, Dom is showing Little Brian how to drive before taking him back home for a barbecue, as Abuelita Toretto has flown in for the occasion. They return home to the rest of the family – Letty Mia, Tej, Roman, Ramsey, and Han.After Abuelita delivers a speech, everyone eats before discussing a planned heist in Rome that was supposedly commissioned by Little Nobody. At night, Dom tells Letty how Little Brian said he’s not afraid of anything, but he really is afraid of losing his family. Moments later, a beaten and bloodied Cipher shows up at the house. Dom and Letty hide Little Brian before confronting their nemesis. Cipher says that they have a bigger problem coming their way in the form of Dante. He earlier came into her facility after killing two guards and revealing that he has kidnapped the loved ones of Cipher’s henchmen, forcing them to shift loyalties so that he can go after Dom. He leaves after taking her hacking tech and having the remaining henchmen stay to kill her. Cipher fought her way out before going down an elevator shaft with one last goon before coming to the Toretto home. Dom and Letty contact Little Nobody, who has agents arrive immediately and bring Cipher into custody. They then learn that the Rome heist was a setup orchestrated by Dante, so they fly on out there. While on the streets, Tej, Roman, Ramsey, and Han move their cargo, which turns out to be a massive bomb. Dante then hacks into their trucks to make them veer into traffic before attempting to deliver the bomb to The Vatican. Dom, Letty, and Little Nobody intercepts the rest of the gang and get them underground while Dante attempts to blow them all up. The bomb ends up rolling all the way down the hills and streets while Letty tries to chase Dante, only for him to get away and her getting arrested. Dom catches up to the bomb and uses a crane to knock it away from the path of The Vatican, but the ensuing blast radius causes significant damage. The gang are all branded as terrorists and go into hiding while Dante gloats to Dom about tearing his family apart. At The Agency, new director Aimes meets with Tess, daughter of Mr. Nobody. Aimes has been tracking the Toretto gang’s history of street racing to global heisting, believing that Nobody was too easy on them. While Tess argues in their defense and how they have brought down some pretty serious criminals, Aimes manages to convince the rest of the Agency’s board to go after them. The media then brands the gang international terrorists, resulting in Roman bringing Tej, Ramsey and Han to London. Mia is taking care of Little Brian when a team of Agency mercs storms in. Mia tries to fight them off while Little Brian hides, only for them to be saved by Jakob, having been contacted by Dom. He throws a guy through the floor and bashes other villains all around. Jakob tells Mia to get somewhere safe with Brian and the kids while he takes Little Brian with him safely back to Dom. Tess finds Dom in Brazil and tells him who Dante is, letting Dom know why he’s going after him. He asks for help in exonerating them and for getting Letty out, as she has been taken to a secret Agency base. Tess meets with Letty and creates a plan to get her moved out of their and into another location by making it look like Letty is attacking her. Dom goes to a street racing event to meet with Diogo, along with a young woman named Isabel that Dom knows. Dante shows up and challenges Dom to a street race alongside Diogo and Isabel. During the race, Dante makes Dom choose which of the two will die, as he has set up bombs under their cars. Dom ends up trying to slow Isabel down, making Dante blow up Diogo on the track. Dante then tries to go for Isabel anyway, but Dom knocks the bomb off her car despite making her crash. Dom pulls her out of the wreck while Dante gets away. The other four end up meeting an old hacking buddy of Ramsey’s named Bowie. Ramsey recovers a file and learns that her surveillance system God’s Eye is being used by Dante to target people close to Dom. Dante ends up draining their funds, but Roman had some cash secured. The four are forced to find Deckard Shaw (Jason Statham), who thinks Han is there to fight him after his attempt to kill him, but their scuffle is interrupted by more Agency goons showing up. Shaw kills them and learns from Ramsey that his mother Magdalene is among the potential targets, so he heads off to protect his family. The rest of the gang finds a transport to get them to safety. Letty wakes up in an Agency facility alongside Cipher. She hacks the place to gas the guards and free them. While they try to escape, Letty instigates a fight, leading to them punching and kicking and throwing each other into equipment. After they come back to their senses, Letty attempts to get out without Cipher, only to find out that the facility is in Antarctica. Jakob bonds with Little Brian and tries to blend in with him to avoid suspicion. They board a plane where a flight attendant who is Jakob’s friend alerts him to the presence of three of Dante’s goons. He knocks them out and has the woman hide their bodies while he and Little Brian board a secret jet toward Brazil. Isabel wakes up in Dom’s apartment that he shared with Elena, who turns out to be Isabel’s older sister. She tells Dom that she always felt like Elena was the better sibling and wonders if the wrong sister died. Dom assures her that is not the case. With Isabel’s help, they find Elena’s old files on Dante and find a property of his tied to an abandoned police station. Dom visits the station and finds numerous videos and recordings of him and his family over the years. Dante calls and taunts Dom about making him suffer before he dies, staring outside the window at Isabel before Aimes shows up to arrest Dom. Dom is transported over the same bridge where the heist went down when the convoy taking him gets bombed by Dante. A faceoff occurs on the bridge when Tess and Aimes try to take Dante and his goons down, but Dante has a sniper on them that shoots them both out of commission before having it point at Isabel, whom Dante had kidnapped. Dom gets Isabel out of the way while Dante takes God’s Eye from Tess, letting Dom know that he can know find his son before getting away. Isabel takes Tess out to safety while Dom races to find Little Brian with help from Aimes. Dante tracks Jakob and Little Brian’s location, but Jakob comes prepared with a cannon-loaded vehicle that blows the goons up. Little Brian attempts to help by climbing out the back, but this gives Dante an opportunity to swipe the boy from the car. Jakob alerts Dom before he can reach his brother. Dom is dropped out of a jet in his car before two of Dante’s sniper’s choppers shoot his car with harpoons! But then Dom drives off the bridge and makes them collide and EXPLODE! Jakob then gives Dom a chance to flee by sacrificing himself, flipping his bomb-filled car onto the incoming goons and going out in a tragic but epic blaze of glory. Dom reaches Dante’s car and gets Little Brian to fly out and into Dom’s car. Dante then has two oil tankers attempt to run into Dom and Little Brian over a dam, so he does the only reasonable thing and drives the car down the dam while the tankers blow each other up, forcing Dom to hit the nitro hard so that they can outrun the ensuing fireball. Just when it looks like Dom and Little Brian are safe, a plane carrying the rest of Dom’s gang get hit by a missile ordered by none other than Aimes, who was working with Dante ever since the Rio heist. Dom watches as his friends crash into a mountain. Dante declares that Dom has had his suffering, now he can die. He then rigs the entire dam to blow in a matter of seconds. Dom can only look at his son with fear. Back in Antarctica, Letty and Cipher emerge from the facility and see a humongous submarine emerge from the ice, piloted by Gisele. Letty looks on in shock while Cipher appears to have planned for this all along. Midway through the credits, a team of cops swarm an abandoned Dante facility. One of the men finds a ringing phone and answers it, hearing Dante’s voice marking him as his next target, for he is the man that personally executed his father on that fateful day. The man, of course, is none other than Luke Hobbs (Dwayne Johnson). He simply tells Dante, “I ain’t hard to find…ya sum-BITCH!” before crushing the phone to dust. Well, here ends our today’s Recap. text: Hi guys, Cinematic Recapped here. Before we start, WARNING! Spoilers Ahead! Today, I`m gonna explain an American science fiction and thriller movie, called NOPE. The movie begins by featuring a 1998 sitcom called Gordy's home, in which Gordy, a chimpanzee who is the lead actor in the sitcom, attacks several of its human co-stars after being startled by the pop of a balloon. Flash forward to the present day in Agua Dulce, a ranch owner named Otis Haywood Sr. trains and handles horses for film and television productions. While Otis prepares for the day with his son Otis “OJ” Haywood Jr., several metal objects mysteriously fall from the sky. Unfortunately, a nickel pierces Otis' eye, causing him to die instantly. Because of that, OJ and his sister Emerald “Em" Haywood inherit the ranch. OJ also tries to keep the business afloat and maintain his father's legacy, while Em seeks fame and fortune in Hollywood. Six months after Otis’ death, OJ gets a job filming a commercial with a prominent cinematographer named Antlers Holst. To further reassure the crew, the Haywoods claim that the unnamed jockey in "Plate 626" from Eadweard Muybridge's Animal Locomotion series of photographs was their ancestor. However, the project does not go well after one of the Haywood horses, Lucky, reacts aggressively when the crew startles it, resulting in OJ being fired from the project. Later, the ranch's financial woes have forced OJ to sell some of his horses to Ricky “Jupe” Park, who operates a small Western theme park nearby called Jupiter’s Claim. In his office, Jupe admits that he was the child actor from the sitcom Gordy's Home who was somehow unharmed in the tragic incident by hiding under a table, even Gordy finally found Jupe and extended his hand for a fist bump, before being shot dead by authorities. However, Jupe is now exploiting his story of the Gordy's Home incident at Jupiter’s Claim for profit in an attempt to mask his unresolved trauma. He eventually offers to buy the Haywood’s ranch, which Em certainly encourages OJ to accept. At night, OJ notices one of his horses, Ghost, fleeing inexplicably due to an unknown presence. After failing to find it, he stops his vehicle in an open field and sees a UFO shaped like a flying saucer in the sky, which he then tells Em. Motivated by a desire for wealth and fame, the siblings decide to document evidence of the UFO's existence. They go to Fry's Electronics store, where the two meet the store’s employee Angel Torres and recruit him to set up the surveillance cameras on top of their house and elsewhere on the ranch. After setting up the surveillance cameras, they set up a decoy horse which Em stole from Jupiter’s Claim. Not long after, Jupe comes to their ranch and invites them to his new family live show on next Friday. That night, OJ investigates strange noises from the barn and encounters a short creature that looks like an alien. While he is documenting it, another creature startles him, so he knocks it down, and it turns out to be Jupe’s kids who tell him not to mess with Jupiter’s Claim. While OJ is chasing a runaway horse, the UFO suddenly flies above their ranch and shuts down the ranch surveillance camera. At the same time, Em sees a praying mantis landing on the surveillance camera above their house, blocking the view of the UFO. She then runs out of the house and sees the UFO near OJ, so she tells him to run. As he hides in the barn, OJ discovers that the UFO has been devouring their horses then spitting out inorganic matter, which caused their father's death. The following day, Angel suddenly comes back to their ranch and reviews the last night’s footage, revealing that a nearby cloud never moves. As a result, they deduce that it is the UFO's hiding place. Soon, Jupe introduces a live show in Jupiter's Claim and plans to use Lucky as bait to lure out the UFO, which he has been feeding the Haywoods' horses to for months, in front of a paying audience. Unluckily on that day, the UFO arrives earlier than they expected, and it immediately devours Jupe and the entire audience, leaving Jupiter's Claim abandoned. After a while, OJ also comes there, only to find Lucky in the field. He attempts to recall his horse, but the UFO suddenly attacks them. Having managed to survive the attack, OJ quickly returns home to inform Em of his discovery. Meanwhile, the UFO has arrived at the Haywoods’ home, where it expels a rain of blood and regurgitates the victims' belongings on the Haywood home after digesting its victims. On the other hand, OJ finds his car engine dead just as he is about to reach his house, so he can only wait for the UFO to leave. While waiting, he deduces that the UFO will not eat anything that does not look directly at it, and that it is not a ship at all, but a predatory territorial creature. He also believes that, like a horse, its behaviour can be understood and influenced in order to capture footage of it without being killed. Over dinner, OJ, Em, and Angel discuss how to capture the creature on camera because it always shuts down their technology, and they decide to hire Antlers for assistance. text: 1996’s Scream opens with the murder of high school student Casey Becker and her boyfriend Steve at the hands of the mysterious Ghostface killer. Fellow high school student Sidney Prescott is still struggling with the murder of her mother Maureen one year prior by her young lover Cotton Weary. As the media descend on the town of Woodsboro to cover the murders, Sidney is forced to confront her emotional trauma. Part of the media frenzy is reporter Gale Weathers, a cold and cutthroat reporter who will stop at nothing to get the best story. And trying to help save the town from a vicious killer is Dewey Riley, a kind-hearted and bumbling Deputy Sheriff. Sidney’s friend group includes boyfriend Billy Loomis, best friend Tatum Riley who was also the sister of Deputy Dewey, Tatum’s boyfriend Stu, and Randy Meeks, a nerdy fan of horror movies who is constantly referencing and acknowledging patterns and motives of famous movie killers. Sidney soon begins receiving calls from the killer, who stalks and taunts her throughout the film. Ghostface kills the high school’s Principal Himbry, then kills Tatum at a house party. Dewey is later stabbed and thought to be dead. Eventually, Billy Loomis reveals himself to be the killer, with his best friend Stu acting as his accomplice. They planned to kill Sidney and pin all of the other murders on her father. Billy also reveals that he had killed Sidney’s mother Maureen the year prior and framed Cotton, as Maureen was having an affair with Billy’s father, driving his mother away. Just as Billy is about to kill Sidney, Gale arrives to intervene. Sidney and Gale kill Stu and Billy and its revealed that Dewey survived his knife wounds, although they did leave him with permanent nerve damage and a limp. Scream 2 opens with the premiere of Stab, a film based on the book Gale Weathers wrote about the Woodsboro Massacre. At the premiere, Windsor College students Maureen and Phil are murdered by a Ghostface copycat killer. Sidney Prescott was now enrolled at Windsor College and trying to move on with her life, so these new murders send her life into complete disarray. Fellow classmates of Sidney at Windsor College include her high school friend Randy Meeks, new best friend Hallie, her new boyfriend Derek Feldman, and Derek’s best friend Mickey. Following the arrival of the copycat killer, Dewey Riley goes to Windsor College to ensure Sidney’s safety. Gale Weathers arrives with a flurry of other reporters to cover the ongoing case and constantly butts heads with a reporter named Debbie Salt, who was obsessed with both the original case and Gale Weathers’ coverage of it. Also arriving at the college was Cotton Weary, who, following his exoneration of Maureen Prescott’s murder, has become obsessed with the media attention and hopes to convince Sidney to sit down with him for a nationally televised interview with Diane Sawyer. Randy tries to help uncover the new killer, utilizing his knowledge of past horror films and their sequels, but he’s eventually stabbed to death by the new Ghostface. Also murdered are sorority girl Cici Cooper and Sidney’s best friend Hallie. As Gale and Dewey team up to try to solve the case, the cold-hearted Gale begins to soften up and even starts a relationship with Dewey. That love affair is quickly cut short when the pair are attacked by Ghostface and Dewey is brutally stabbed. As all of her friends are getting killed off around her, Sidney begins to suspect that once again it was her boyfriend behind the mask causing the massacre. But eventually Sidney discovers that her boyfriend Derek was truly innocent, as Mickey has Derek tied up and reveals himself to be the killer. Mickey kills Derek and confesses to Sidney his master plan, going on a murder spree and getting caught, only to blame violent movies like Stab for normalizing murder at his trial. And then Mickey reveals his accomplice, Reporter Debbie Salt, who was actually Billy Loomis’ mother who wanted revenge on Sidney for her son’s death. Mrs. Loomis then kills Mickey and attacks Sidney, but just as Mrs. Loomis has the upper hand, Cotton Weary arrives to save Sidney. Cotton shoots Mrs. Loomis in the neck, but to ensure she was truly dead, Sidney puts another bullet in Mrs. Loomis’ head. And so, the new copycat killers were dead and the police and paramedics were on the scene. Dewey is revealed to have survived his encounter with Ghostface and instead of reporting on the events, Gale decides to join Dewey in his ambulance. As reporters flood Sidney with questions, she directs them instead to Cotton, calling him the true hero of the story. And so, Cotton gets the attention he’d been craving and Sidney is allowed to finally step out of the spotlight. In Scream 3, Cotton Weary has achieved the fame he’s longed desired, hosting his own television series called 100% Cotton. When a new Ghostface killers demands information from him on the whereabouts of Sidney Prescott, Cotton refuses and is murdered alongside his girlfriend. Sidney Prescott is living a quieter life, changing her name and working as an on-call crisis counselor. As Sidney lives in seclusion, the new killer begins their murder spree, trying to draw her out of hiding. In Hollywood, Stab 3, the newest film in the franchise based on Sidney’s life, is currently in production. Detective Mark Kincaid calls on Gale Weathers to help him catch the new Ghostface killer, who starts to pick off the Stab 3 cast, starting with actress Sarah Darling. The main cast of Stab 3 includes Angelina Tyler as Sidney Prescott, Jennifer Jolie as Gale Weathers, Tom Prinze as Dewey Riley, and Tyson Fox as the film’s equivalent of Randy Meeks. Also working on the set of Stab 3 is Dewey Riley, serving as a technical advisor. He and Gale have broken up following Gale’s successful career, but the two still have feelings for each other. As Dewey, Gale and the Stab 3 cast convene at Jennifer’s house to discuss their predicament, the killer strikes, blowing up the house with Tom still in it. When Sidney arrives in Hollywood to help stop the new Ghostface killer, the team are visited by Randy Meeks’ sister Martha. She plays them a video that Randy had made before his death, warning them of how dangerous the killer in the final film of a trilogy could be. At a birthday party for Stab 3 director Roman Bridger’s birthday, the Ghostface killer strikes again, killing Angelina, Tyson, and Jennifer. The killer knocks out Detective Kincaid and ties up Dewey and Gale before revealing his true identity to Sidney. The killer was in fact Roman Bridger, who also happened to be the long lost half-brother of Sidney Prescott. Roman was born out of an affair Maureen had had when attempting to start a career as an actress. When Roman tried to reunite with Maureen four years ago, she rejected him. And so, a bitter Roman secretly filmed all of Maureen’s extramarital affairs, including the ones she had with Cotton Weary and Billy Loomis’ father. Roman then showed Billy those tapes and manipulated him into becoming the original Ghostface killer. And now Roman planned on pinning all of the Stab 3 cast murders on Sidney. The brother and sister engage in a fight, which Sidney ultimately wins, stabbing Roman three times before Dewey shoots him in the head. As the movie comes to a close, Dewey and Gale get engaged while Sidney finally feels at peace and that all of the murdering was over. And that brings us to Scream 4. It’s been 15 years since the original Woodsboro massacre, and a new Ghostface killer has arrived in town killing students at the high school. Sidney Prescott, back in her hometown on a press tour for her new book, is framed for the murders and is forced to stay in Woodsboro for the duration of the investigation. Meanwhile, Dewey Riley, now the sheriff of Woodsboro, and his team of deputies, including Judy Hicks, begin investigating the new murderer. Dewey’s wife Gale, against his objections, goes back into reporter mode to conduct her own investigation. The students at the high school being targeted by Ghostface include Sidney’s cousin Jill Roberts, Jill’s cheating ex-boyfriend Trevor Sheldon, her neighbor Olivia Morris, best friend Kirby Reed, and horror movie enthusiasts Charlie Walker and Robbie Mercer. Ghostface kills Olivia, and the high schoolers retreat to Kirby’s house to figure out their best options. Ghostface then kills Jill’s mother Kate before setting its sights on the other high schoolers. A drunken Robbie is killed first, and then Charlie reveals himself to be the killer before stabbing Kirby to death. As Sidney arrives at the house to save her cousin, Jill reveals herself to also be one of the Ghostface killers, with Charlie serving as her accomplice. Jill explains her jealousy about the fame Sidney received for being a survivor of the original Woodsboro massacre and wanted the same attention. She then kills Trevor to pin all of the murders on him, and betrays Charlie, stabbing him to death to leave herself as the sole survivor. Jill then stabs Sidney and cuts herself to look like she was attacked. Dewey and Hicks arrive to rescue Sidney and Jill, unaware that Jill was actually the killer. At the hospital, Jill discovers that Sidney survived the attack and goes to kill her. Dewey, Hicks, and Gale intervene just in time, and Sidney is forced to shoot her cousin in the head. And so, once again, Sidney, Dewey, and Gale defeat the Ghostface killer and attempt to move on with their lives.

text: In December 1970, Paul Hunham is a strict, hidebound classics professor at Barton Academy, the New England boarding school that he once attended on scholarship. His students and fellow teachers dislike him for his harsh grading and stern attitude. Hunham's headmaster, Woodrup, berates him when he costs the academy an important donor by failing his son in his class, prompting Princeton University to rescind his offer of admission. As punishment, Hunham is forced to supervise the "holdover" students left on campus for the holidays, including Angus Tully, whose mother abruptly cancelled a trip to Saint Kitts to honeymoon with his new stepfather. Also staying behind is cafeteria administrator Mary Lamb, who is grieving the loss of her son, a Barton alumnus killed serving in the Vietnam War. To their dismay, Hunham imposes studying and exercise on the holdovers' break. After six days, the wealthy father of one of them arrives by helicopter and agrees to take all the students on the family's ski trip. Angus, unable to reach his parents for permission, is left alone at Barton with Hunham and Mary. Hunham catches him trying to arrange a hotel room, leading to a chase around the school until Angus defiantly leaps into a pile of gym equipment, dislocating his arm. At the hospital, Angus lies to protect Hunham from blame. Hunham later flirts with deputy headmistress Lydia Crane after meeting her at a restaurant, and she invites the pair to her Christmas Eve Party. He then deters Angus from an argument with a disabled war veteran. On Christmas Eve, Angus, Hunham, Mary, and Barton's janitor, Danny, attend Lydia's party. While Angus flirts with Lydia's niece while finger-painting, Hunham is disappointed to discover Lydia has a significant other, and an inebriated Mary breaks down in the kitchen over her son's death. Hunham insists on leaving early, despite protests from Angus, who angrily blurts out that his father is dead, causing Mary to chastise Hunham for his insensitivity. Having reflected upon his behavior, Hunham puts together a small Christmas celebration, and with Mary's persuasion, grants Angus's wish for a "field trip" to Boston. Dropping Mary off in Roxbury to spend time with her pregnant sister, Angus and Hunham bond over various activities in Boston, including ice skating and a visit to the Museum of Fine Arts. They bump into one of Hunham's classmates from Harvard University, who has become a successful academic. When prompted, Hunham lies about his career, with Angus playing along. After incessant questioning, Hunham confesses to Angus that he was expelled from Harvard after assaulting a peer, the son of a legacy donor who framed him for plagiarism, which ruined his career prospects. Thanks to the charity of one of his former teachers, he was able to secure a teaching position at Barton. In the morning, Hunham discovers that he and Angus both suffer from depression after noticing that they take the same anti-depressant. When they go to see Little Big Man at the Orpheum Theatre, Angus sneaks away and Hunham catches him entering a taxi. Angus explains that his father is actually alive and confined at a nearby sanatorium. Hunham takes Angus to see his father, whose mental illness drove his family apart. Over dinner, he reassures an anxious Angus that he is not fated to be like his father. They join Mary and Danny to celebrate New Year's Eve, watching the Times Square Ball drop on TV and setting off an M-80 firework in the school kitchen. When school resumes in January 1971, Hunham is summoned to Woodrup's office, confronted by Angus's mother and stepfather. They tell him that Angus's visit to his father was unauthorized and that the snow globe Angus gave him, which he stole from Lydia's party, led his father to have a violent episode. The mother and stepfather plan to send Angus to military school, but Hunham stands up for Angus and takes the blame for the trip. He is fired, but Angus is allowed to stay at Barton; Hunham decides to finally pursue his lifelong dream of visiting the ruins of Carthage. Mary, who has come to better terms with the loss of her son, gives Hunham a notebook for the monograph he had long wanted to write. He and Angus share a heartfelt goodbye. Leaving the school, Hunham drinks the cognac he stole from the headmaster, before spitting some of it out toward the school and driving away.

text: Kiki, a 13-year-old trainee witch, lying idle in a field listening to her father's radio on one blustery day when she hears an announcement that the evening would be clear with a beautiful full moon. She rushes home to meet her mother, Kokiri, and informs her that she intends to leave home that evening rather than the following month as she had planned. As Kiki rushes to her room to pack, Kokiri tells her client Dora about the age-old tradition of 13-year-old witches leaving home for a year on the night of a full moon to pursue their skill through training. Jiji, her cat, asks why they can't wait until next month while Kiki packs her belongings. She's so excited and she tells him that if she meets a boy, she will have to stay and not leave. Okino, her father, arrives home and learns of Kiki's plans to leave that night, canceling their previously planned camping trip. He begins calling relatives to inform them that Kiki is leaving and soon after Kokiri dresses Kiki in her purple witch's uniform with a red bow on her head. She asks her father if she can take the radio with her and he does not refuse. That evening, Kiki's family and friends gather to bid her farewell. Her mother offers her a broom in order for her to never get lost. She leaves with her companion, Jiji, a talking black cat. While having difficulty flying at first, she takes off in the direction of the ocean to the south. Along the way, she meets a fortune-telling witch who warns her about the difficulties she may face when settling in a new town. Since she has completed her training, the fortune-teller witch is returning to her hometown. After meeting her, Kiki realizes that she, too, requires a special skill. While Kiki and Jiji are flying around looking for the town, it begins to rain, so Kiki lands inside a train full of hay and decides to sleep there. Kiki eventually flies to the port city of Corico on her broomstick. The citizens, on the other hand, appear unfazed by her arrival. While looking for a place to live, Kiki is pursued by Tombo Kopoli, a geeky boy obsessed with aviation who admires her flying ability. She goes to a hotel, but they refuse to let her in because she is under the age of 18. She is having difficulty finding a place to live. They walk down the street and stop near a bakery whose owner appears completely overwhelmed by the volume of customers. After assisting Osono in returning a pacifier to a baby, Osono invites her into her home to thank her. They talk over coffee and Osono learns that Kiki is currently homeless. Kiki gratefully accepts her offer to stay in a small apartment storage area. When Kiki enters her room, it is covered in flour. She cleans up the room and goes to bed. The following morning, in exchange for lodging, Kiki assists Osono, the sweet and heavily pregnant owner of Gütiokipanja, a local bakery. She admits that her only skill is flying, so they decide to start a witch delivery business, delivering goods by broomstick. She goes grocery shopping and is strapped for cash. She sees some girls dressed nicely and wonders if she'll be able to afford nice clothes. When Kiki returns home, one of Osono's regular customers, Maki, notices her and requests that she deliver a birthday gift for her nephew cat. Kiki gladly accepts, and before she leaves, Tombo notices her ascending into the air, wishing he could fly like her. Unfortunately, her first delivery is a disaster because she is caught in a strong gust of wind and loses the black cat toy she is supposed to deliver. The toy landed on a crow's nest. Kiki is attacked by crows who believe she is attempting to steal their eggs as she attempts to retrieve the toy. Jiji laments how far witches have fallen and how crows used to be their retainers. Kiki comes up with the idea of having Jiji pretend to be the toy cat until she can find the real one because he looks so similar. Jiji is under the watchful eye of the family dog, Jeff, while at the young boy's house. Meanwhile, Kiki discovers the toy cat in the cabin of Ursula, a young painter. When Ursula notices that the toy is ripped, she offers to repair it in exchange for Kiki cleaning her floor. Ursula returns the doll after it has been repaired, and Kiki rushes off to save Gigi. With Jeff's assistance, they are able to easily make the switch and return home. Kiki experiences a slump as demand for her delivery service decreases. Kiki reluctantly accepts a party invitation from Tombo and his aviation club friends. She arrives at her next delivery appointment, the home of an elderly lady who had been attempting to make a herring and pumpkin pot pie for her granddaughter's birthday. Kiki offers Madame and Barsa assistance with her wood-burning oven in order to make the treat and assists with housework while it bakes. Madame quickly recalls that her clock is a few minutes slow, alerting Kiki to the fact that she will be late for Tombo's party. She goes to deliver the pot pie for Madame's granddaughter, and it starts to rain heavily on the way. When Kiki arrives at the young girl's house, she is taken aback when the girl expresses her dislike for the pot pie and walks home in silence. Kiki becomes ill with a fever after being exhausted from the journey, soaking wet from the rain, and missing the party. When she recovers, Osono arranges for Kiki to see Tombo again by sending her a package addressed to him. Tombo shows off the new dirigible that arrived in town for repairs after Kiki apologizes for missing the party. He takes her for a test ride in the flying machine he's building out of a bicycle. Kiki grows fond of Tombo, but is put off by his petty friends who appear to look down on her. She walks home defeated, upset. Kiki becomes depressed and realizes she no longer understands Gigi, who has befriended a beautiful white cat who lives next door. Kiki realizes she can no longer understand him and that she is losing her flying ability and witch's powers, forcing her to halt her delivery business. Ursula from the bakery pays Kiki a surprise visit and determines that her crisis is a form of artist's block and offers her time away at her cabin to relax. Kiki notices Ursula working on her latest painting, which was inspired by her encounter with Kiki. Ursula sketches Kiki while explaining how she had been in a similar situation and tells Kiki, "When I was about your age, I decided to become an artist. I enjoyed drawing so much that I almost despised going to bed. Then one day, out of nowhere, I couldn't draw anything. I didn't like anything I drew. I realized that my art up to that point had been a carbon copy of someone else's, things I had seen somewhere. I decided I needed to find my own style. It's still challenging. But then there are the results. They appear to be slightly better than before." She claims that if Kiki can find a new purpose for herself, she will Kiki pays a visit to Barsa and Madam the following morning. She wanted to thank Kiki for her hard work when she was last at the house and present her with a cake. At the same time, the television announces the departure of the dirigible, the Spirit of Freedom. As the seahorse band and crowd bid the airship farewell, a sudden gale dislodges the moorings and blows the airship off course, leaving Tombo dangling from a rope beneath the airship. The airship crashes into the clock tower and hangs above the town plaza. Kiki then notices that Tombo dangling from one of the mooring lines of the drifting vessel. As the radio reports that the helium in the dirigible is unlikely to explode, Kiki grabs a push broom from a street sweeper and regains her flying power, flying towards Tombo. The airship becomes entangled in the town's clock tower and a building across the street. Tombo, on the other hand, is still in danger as he clings to the rope beneath the ship. Kiki flies as fast as she can and, after some difficulty keeping the broom in place, rescues Tombo as he slips and falls.
