text: So, I just watched Kokohu. How do you even say it? Kokohu? Kokoha? My apologies. I was intrigued by this movie because of its concept, especially after learning that it became one of the top grossing movie in Japan. It's even Japan's official submission to the Oscars. Since I don't know much about Japanese culture, I was really drawn in by the movie. It shows so many layers along with a rich history and traditions that I didn't even know existed. In this video, let's talk about the inspiration behind the movie from the perspective of director Sing Il Lee and explore the history of Onnagata. I was honestly surprised that despite Japan being so conservative, men dressed up as women for Kabuki performances. We will also look at the deeper meaning of the Kabuki plays featured in the movie. >> [music] >> The movie begins when the renowned Kabuki actor Hanjiro visits the Tachibana Yakuza group for a New Year's gathering. There, he sees Kikugoro, the gang leader's son, perform as an Onnagata and is deeply impressed. Tragedy strikes when a rival Yakuza group attacks during the gathering, killing Kikugoro's father in front of him. Kikugoro tries to get revenge, but fails. A year later, Hanjiro agrees to train him. Kikugoro begins studying alongside Hanjiro's biological son, Shinsuke. Both boys are talented, but Kikugoro is intensely dedicated to mastering the art, while Shinsuke is more carefree. They debut as a popular Onnagata duo, Tohen, and achieve major success. However, tension grows when Hanjiro chooses Kikugoro over Shinsuke to take over a a role. Feeling overshadowed, Shinsuke leaves the theater world. Although Kikuwo inherits the title, he does not gain full acceptance. After Hanjiro's death, the Kabuki world turns against him. His Yakuza past and born out of wedlock daughter became public and critics accuse him of stealing the family name. Shinsuke returns and quickly receives leading roles because of his bloodline. Resentment builds between the former brothers. Eventually, Kikuwo leaves Kabuki and performs in small venues. Mangiku later summons Kikuwo and offers him a chance of redemption. After reuniting with Shinsuke, they achieve renewed success. However, Shinsuke develops severe diabetes and loses both feet to gangrene. Before he can no longer perform, Shinsuke fulfills his dream of playing a play with Kikuwo by his side. The performance is physically painful but artistically successful. Soon after, Shinsuke dies. Shinsuke is honored after his death and Kikuwo is officially recognized as a living national treasure known as Kokukoho. >> [music] >> Inspiration. Director Lee Sang-il became interested in a famous onnagata named Utaemon Nakamura. People said he was the best onnagata after World War II and even called him a national treasure because he was so talented. His personal life and his acting life were almost the same. He really lived his art. Lee saw videos of him and that's what made him curious. The movie is also based on Shuichi Yoshida's best-selling novel with the same name, History of Onnagata. I'm not really familiar with Japanese culture. Honestly, the first time I even learned about geisha was from watching the movie Memoirs of Geisha. Because of that, I always thought Japan was very conservative. So, when I heard about men cross-dressing as women in traditional theater, I was actually kind of surprised. I was thinking, "Doesn't that go against their tradition?" So, how did onnagata even begin? Onnagata are male actors who play female roles in kabuki, a traditional Japanese theater that has been performed only by men for hundreds of years. In 1629, the Japanese government banned women from acting in kabuki. Officials believed that female performers were connected to prostitution and public disorder in theater districts. To control this, women were no longer allowed on stage. Because of that, adult men began playing women's roles. At first, this was simply a practical solution to the ban. But, over time, it became a respected tradition. Playing female roles developed into a special skill that actors trained for many years to master. It's important to understand that kabuki is not meant to look like real life. It's carefully designed and exaggerated. Movements are slow and controlled. Voices are trained in a special way. Costumes and makeup are bold and dramatic. Everything is designed to look artistic, not realistic. Onnagata are not trying to become women in real life. They are not copying everyday women. Instead, they perform an idealized version of feminine qualities, a carefully created image of grace, beauty, and elegance according to kabuki style. Deeper meaning. Looking back at the movie, the kabuki plays really shows us who the main characters are and what they're going through. Let's start with Barrier Gate. This is the play when young Kikuwo was performing when Hanjirou first noticed him. In the story, the gate stands for the challenges in life and love. Another important play in the movie is The Maiden of Doji Temple, which tells the story of a woman who, because of unrequited love, transformed into a vengeful serpent demon. In Koko Hall, this play works as a symbol for Kikuwo and Shinsuke's journey. The play's strict rules and precise movements also show how Kabuki works. It takes years of practice and respect for tradition to perform it correctly. The serpent demon represents the costs of ambition, hinting at the loneliness, rivalry, and pressure Kikuwo faces as he tries to be perfect. Finally, because this play is performed as a duo, it highlights the importance of teamwork. Kikuwo and Shinsuke must trust each other and work together to succeed, showing that mastery in Kabuki is not just about individual talent, but also collaboration. Overall, I respected this movie more than I actually enjoyed it. At 3 hours, it can feel a bit slow and it's not always entertaining in the usual way, but if you like history, art, or Kabuki, it's really worth watching. The detail in the performances, the costumes, makeup, and movements, it's outstanding. It is Alphaba who confronts the guards with decisive force, taking them down one by one. Noticing reinforcements approaching, she mounts her magical broom and disappears into the sky. News of her bold actions spreads quickly, stirring fear among the citizens who brace themselves for her next move. Alphaba lives in seclusion, hoping to show her true character and disprove the false claim spread by the Wizard of Oz. As she gazes at the sky, her thoughts drift to Glenda, who has become adored throughout Oz and is beloved by Prince Furro. Meanwhile, Madamorable meets with Glenda, warning her the unrest caused by Alphaba and insisting that only Glenda can restore peace. She presents Glinda with a new mode of transport, a floating bubble. Glinda, delighted, presses its controls repeatedly, frustrating Morble, who explains that the bubble's mechanical power will improve her airborne abilities and instructs her to let people believe the magic comes from her. Morble also hands her a wand and reminds her of their meeting at the opening ceremony. The wand sparks memories of Glenda's childhood. When she received a wand for her birthday and attempted magic, though a rainbow appeared and fooled the children, she knew it wasn't her magic and felt disheartened. Her mother reassured her that she was loved and that was all that truly mattered. Recalling this, Blinda travels to the ceremony in her bubble. The citizens admire her more than ever, and she announces the official opening of the yellow brick road. The people of Oz celebrate, believing they are finally free from the wizard's control, singing alongside Glenda. Morble announces that Fiero has been appointed captain of the Gale Force, tasked with capturing the wicked witch. Fiero is surprised to learn he is now engaged to Glenda. Rumors circulate that the wicked, which possesses an extra eye and a tainted soul that can only be destroyed by holy water. Angered, Fo expresses his desire to leave, but Glenda reminds him that all eyes are on them. He remarks that she secretly enjoys the admiration, insisting he must find Alphaba first. Glenda pleads with him to stay, and Fiero decides to remain, kissing her before leaving the ceremony. Feeling melancholy, Glenda sings about how people's happiness depends on their dreams coming true. As she greets the crowd, the wizard arrives, denouncing the lies told to the people, while Morble claims Alphaba intends to harm Glenda. The Gale Force, aided by a winged monkey, pursues Alphaba through the forest. However, she cleverly tricks the monkey and hides in the dense woods. The captain orders a retreat, believing Alphaba is gone. Alphaba watches from the trees, reflecting on her past with Glenda and Fier. Elsewhere, Nessarose is appointed as the new governor. She enacts an animal mobility law, which Munchkinland has yet to approve. Other governors wait for ratification while Bach urges her not to enforce it, but Nessarose refuses to listen. She acknowledges Boach's past support yet demands he leave immediately. As Boach prepares to board the train, guard stop him due to the new law requiring a permit, removing others as well. Alphaba wanders the forest, hearing chaos as animals flee Oz. Terrified of the winged monkeys, she tries to convince them to stay and join her cause. During this, she reunites with Gooseberry, who explains that they had no choice but to leave. Alphaba insists that outside Oz lies only emptiness. But Gooseberry declares that no one will find happiness until she dies. Alphaba expresses her deep connection to Oz, her promise to protect it, and urges the animals to fight alongside her. Suddenly, a lion reveals that she was responsible for giving the monkeys wings. Alphaba admits the truth, but says she was deceived and would never have done it knowingly. Feeling betrayed, the animals depart through a tunnel, watched by the winged monkeys. Meanwhile, Bach is furious with Nessarose for keeping him. Noticing a notice of Glenda's engagement and departs. Alphaba visits Nessarose, asking for her assistance, but Nessarose is upset over Alphaba's absence after their father's death. Alphaba explains that their father despised her and asks Nessarose to help as the new governor. Nessarose also seeks help to relive school memories. As the pages of a spell book turn, Alphaba casts a spell, causing Nessarose to float joyfully. Boach arrives shocked to see Alphaba, declaring he must tell Glenda his feelings before it's too late. Nessa Rose becomes angry. Obsessed with Bach, she misreads spells, causing his heart to shrink, and he collapses. Alphaba instructs Nessarose to leave while she searches for a reversal spell. Alphaba goes to Glenda, who is preparing for her wedding as the city readies itself. A crack in the glass draws Glenda's attention, revealing Alphaba outside. Glinda brings her in, and Alphaba insists on seeing the wizard. Glenda offers to mediate, but Alphaba vanishes. Alphaba confronts the wizard with Glenda trailing behind her. She demands that he admit to everyone that he possesses no true power and cannot read the grim. She confesses that she once admired him as a remarkable wizard of Oz, but now there's no turning back. The wizard argues that people would not believe her and would continue following him, admitting that being praised and adored felt intoxicating. He invites her to join him. Glenda adds that if Alphaba sided with them, no battle would be unwinable. Alphaba responds that she would only agree if they first prove themselves by ceasing to blame animals, returning them to Oz and freeing the monkeys. The wizard consents. He hands Alphaba a key and she unlocks the gate confining the monkeys. When Chis descends, Alphaba apologizes and assures them they are free. After the wizard departs, Chis reveals a secret door filled with thousands more monkeys. Meanwhile, Glenda proceeds toward her wedding. Alphaba enters a chamber teeming with caged animals. The wizard approaches, warning that some creatures cannot be trusted. Fiero senses something a miss as he recites his vows. Enraged, Alphaba releases all the animals. Glinda witnesses Fiero confronting the wizard and is shocked when he announces he is leaving with Alphaba. Misunderstanding, she assumes a romantic affair and tells them to go. Morble arrives amid the mayhem and Glenda suggests using Nessarose to lure Alphaba into a trap. Meanwhile, Fiero and Alphaba reach her home. Alphaba can hardly believe she is finally sharing the moment she has dreamed of with him. Fiero declares his love and how long he has waited for this moment. Glenda counters that Alphaba herself took what wasn't hers. Alphaba asserts that Fiero never loved Glinda and now belongs to her. Glenda slaps her and Alphaba retaliates. A fight breaks out only to be interrupted by arriving soldiers, revealing Glenda's trap. As the soldiers sees her, Fiero appears with the monkeys, threatening them to release Alphaba or he will harm Glenda. They comply and Fiero tells her to leave alone. She departs, followed by the monkeys while Fiero eventually surrenders and is captured. Alphaba and the monkeys head to the palace where she attempts a spell to rescue Fio but struggles to read it. As she sings, visions of youngness arose. Dr. Dillondont and Foh tied to a pole appear before her. Consumed by rage, she summons an army of monkeys and swears off doing good deeds. Infuriated by Fiero's fate, Morble suggests using the visiting girl, the lion, and Bach, while the wizard orders them to capture the witch alive or dead. They rally the town's people against Alphaba, claiming she turned a man into tin and tamed a lion. Glenda witnesses this and confronts Morble, demanding she stop and questioning the twister. Morble admits her role. Glenda relinquishes the crown, changes attire, and leaves on horseback. Glenda warns Alphaba of the approaching town's people. Alphaba explains that Fiero is gone, and she intends to surrender, asking Glenda to leave. She promises not to clear her own name, reasoning that the people need someone to label wicked. She entrusts Glenda with a spellbook, urging her to learn and enact change, affirming that Glenda was her only true friend. Glenda acknowledges that knowing Alphaba shaped her for the better. Alphaba seeks forgiveness, and the two embrace tightly. Glenda hides as Alphaba shares a final moment with her before parting. text: Hello, welcome to movie moments, Today I'll be narrating one of the best movies released in 2022 "The Woman King" You ready let's go In an African kingdom, live the people of Dahomey; a new king Ghezo young and brave, just ascended the throne. Dahomey's enemy the OYO empire has joined forces with the Mahi people to raid Dahomey and sell her people to European slavers. While the OYO empire has guns and horses the Dahomey has but an elite force of Female soldiers "the Agojie" [The King's Guard] led by general Nanisca to defend the land. And so the story begins.. The movie opens with soldiers from Mahi gathered around a bon fire, they suddenly hear strange noises but first dismiss it as birds then a group of warrior women rise from the fields and attacks them. The women slaughter the men and free the captives. The Miganon Nanisca as called by her people, sees a horse shoe and suspects the Oyo soldiers have something to do with the Mahi people. Next we're transported to the beautiful kingdom of Dahomey; a young girl Nawi and her friend are in the market place when a sound from afar sends them all running with excitement. The Agojie has returned with the captives. The people bow as they pass as it is forbidden to look upon them. Nanisca seems worried despite their victory; so she request's to see the king. Nawi gets home to a big shock, her parents have sold her off to an elderly man for marriage; the man asks a question, when she doesn't respond he gets violent with her which angers her to push him down. He flares up and leaves. Nawi's father is so angry, he drags his daughter to the palace and offers her to the king. Izogie, One of the Agojie takes her in; Nawi is in awe of the sight of women training. The Oyo soldiers visit Mahi where the Agojie raided; and their General Ade Oba is enraged. The king of Dahomey King Ghezo, makes his way to meet with his counsel. He greets his wives as he passes. Nanisca is there waiting on him as the King's Guard. One of the Wives Shante, is jealous at how Nanisca is able to approach boldly before the king in war clothes. The king's attendant immediately puts her in her place. In counsel, the king presents the horse shoe Nanisca found and decides not to pay tribute to the Oyo empire anymore; he seeks Emancipation for his people especially now the Oyo empire dine with their enemies. Migan a counsel member advises him against it as it might bring about war. He suggest they maintain the current tribute to keep the peace and prosperity. Naniasca believes the Agojie can defend Dahomey against the Oyo empire and what prospers them is the selling of their captives to the Europeans; but they cannot continue for what happens when they run out of captives? she thinks they should sell gold and palm oil instead. There are many oppositions on this but the king is willing to give audience to Nanisca if she can prove it's possible to produce oil. In the next scene, the new recruits are prepped on what is required of them and given a last chance to back out if they wish. While Some women leave; Nawi seems like she's found her place. While snooping around the place; Izogie tries to instill a bit fear in Nawi so she can respect her; she orders her to go bathe and she leaves. Nawi meets Nanisca in the bath and the two get talking; she reveals she's only 19 years but willing to be a soldier. Nanisca says obstinate daughters like her often fail when brought here. It's the first day of training; the girls are handed ropes.. Nawi mutters a rope is not a weapon, Nanisca hearing this gives Nawi her sword and asks her to chop a dummys head off; she tries and fails. obviously. Nanisca takes the sword and chops the head off then and tells her to get back to roping. Way to show her who's boss! At nightfall, Izogie tries talking some sense into Nawi. Training continues and Nawi finds it hard keeping up; the Agojie holds a little contest with the men to see who can resist pain more and the Agojie wins. Nawi and her new found friends Fumbe and Ode get mischievious during training which gets them sanctioned. Nawi takes the blame; Nanisca is rather intrigued at the trick but Nawi's sharp tongue angers her and she almost kicks her out of the Agojie. Igozie meets Nawi later and warns her yet again to be careful what she says or do especially to Nanisca; saying she may very well be the first woman king they've had in a thousand years. Amenza visits Nanisca to ease her mind after she just woke startled by a dream. She shares the disturbing dream she just had and Amenza tries to interpret with a little help. Later, Nanisca is passing by when she hears a noise; she checks it out and finds Nawi practicing in the dead of night. The next day, the Dahomey people gather in celebration when it's disrupted by Oyo soldiers. With them is General Oba who is no stranger to Nanisca and she looks shocked and very pissed; Oba however doesn't seem to remember her. they've come for the tribute to their empire. The Oyo soldiers complain the tribute is small and ask for 40 Agojie to make up for it or else the port will no longer be open to the Dahomey people for trade. Although the port belongs to Dahomey the king agrees to give him 20 Agojie to avoid problems. Oba leaves some of his men behind to feast on his behalf. Nanisca chooses the 20 Agojie and Nawi is one of them. Later she's found rattled by Amenza; seems like the general assaulted her way back and it scarred her deeply. At the port of Ouidah, a new merchant arrives from Brazil; he does not seem happy with the slavery; while looking around the place, the Agojie arrives. The general receives them thinking they brought what he asked; instead they offer the heads of the men the general left in Dahomey. They come bearing a message from the king; he is a great king and he bows to no one. After their display, they make a run for it but Nanisca stays and attacks the general; Nawi seeing this stays back to help. She manages to knock the general down and they both run away as Oyo soldiers pursue them. The whites did not interfere all through the fight. Nanisca and Nawi jump into the water where their sisters wait on them. Once they get to shore, Nanisca goes off on Nawi for not following the plan; you think she'd be grateful. She warns her never to act alone; the Agojie's always work together. Knowing Nawi she's not gonna be quiet so she tries to defend her actions but Izogie stops her. Amenza approaches Nanisca quietly and says she's the one who did not follow the plan but she says her plan was to take the general's head. Back at the palace; Shante tries to sweet talk Nanisca about they sharing same interest in the kingdom but she sees right through her crooked ways. Nanisca's plan of producing oil seems to be working as she takes the king through the production site. Nawi visits the waterfall to sharpen her sword; the new merchant in town was out in the kingdom when he stopped for a bath in the waterfall. Nawi takes his clothes and tells him to return to Ouidah naked like the slaves he trades. He explains he's one of them, a Dahomey, his father is white and mother a Dahomey. He was on his way there when he stopped for a bath. Nawi returns the man's cloth; he introduces himself as Malik. Nawi is fascinated about the chain on his neck; while checking it out, she's startled and runs away when Malik's partner approaches. They visit the palace and present king Ghezo with gifts. He welcomes them especially Malik when he hears he's part Dahomey. King Ghezo also asks they join him as the Agojie's in training take their final test. The challenge begins and Nawi is relentless; she makes it through the bush of thorns but goes back for her friend stuck in it. She still manages to meet up with the others and becomes the victor. The king and everyone is so impressed at her performance; Ghezo specially welcomes her to the King's guard [Agojie]. Izogie helps Nawi take out thorns from her body; she asks why she went back for Fumbe and she responds because she wants her friend to stay. Nanisca comes and joins them; while checking the scars on her body she notices a mark on Nawi's back. Nawi says it's been there since her father choose her from an orphanage.. Nanisca storms off immediately; Amenza follows her to inquire what happened. Apparently Nanisca had a child; she gave her to Amenza to do with as she pleases calling it a burden; Amenza gave the child to a missionary; she tells her to calm down, there's no way that child could be Nawi. The Merchant tries to reason with King Ghezo about his decision to stop slave trading; after Shante briefs him of the palm oil production. Meanwhile Malik goes around the palace. Nawi sees him and goes to have a word; Malik tells her to come see him after dark just outside the palace walls. That night the girls take their blood oath as full initiation into the Agojie. Seems like Izogie has grown fond of Nawi; she asks her about Malik saying she noticed he waved to her at the contest. Izogie tells her love makes one weak and she shouldn't give her power away. Later Nawi sneaks out to go see him; they just sit and talk then he informs her that general oba is plotting something big for Dahomey. Nawi rushes to tell Nanisca but before leaving she gives him a sacred stone and takes his sword to remember him by. Nawi rushes to Nanisca to tell her what she heard but she reprimands her for seeing a man and warns her not to think she's too special not to be kicked out of the Agojie. Nawi protests that she has done her best and proved she is the best; she's too careful and would never be captured. Nanisca says she was captured and raped every night by Oyo soldiers; she was lucky to make an escape with Amenza but she was with child. After giving birth she cut the child and put a shark tooth in her arm, before giving her away. Nawi says she can't be the child she speaks of; when the scar is opened up, she finds the shark tooth and the news shocks Nawi who walks away. The next day, the Agojie's sight Oyo soldiers marching towards them; with just two days before they get to Dahomey. Nanisca devises a plan; she intends to use Nawi's explosive trick during training. The women prep for battle and rather than wait for the Oyo soldiers; they take the war to them. In the early hours of the morning, while the enemy slept; like fireworks they lit up the camp of the enemy. The General charges with his men at the Dahomey in a heated battle. Both parties are relentless; Nawi works the ropes with her sword. When she wasn't watching, a soldier grabs her from behind and throws her down a ditch. As she rolls down, she hits her head and becomes unconscious; Nanisca is looking for Oba; Oba on the hand notices his men being slaughtered and calls for a retreat. Our girls totally dominated but not without a few losses. The Oyo soldiers take some injured Agojie with them as they retreat. On Oba's train Fumbe and Nawi are among the Agojie's that were taken. Nawi tells Fumbe to jump off the cart and save herself. Meanwhile she one other are taken to Ouidah where they intend to sell them to traders. Not long after, Izogie is brought in; her arm is broken and she's helpless. She says they must slit their throats as Nanisca advised rather than be slaves but Nawi is not one to give up on life. Fumbe makes it back and informs the others. The king sends for Nanisca and Amenza. He gathered his wives as well to inform them he has chosen Nanisca to be the woman king; Shante is not pleased by this news. Nanisca is honoured but seeks the king's permission to go seek out the captives but the king refuses. He says they sacrificed for the good of many and she is to stay and do her duty as bestowed on her. the next day, Nawi and her sisters are auctioned to the whites; the girls have made an escape plan which almost fails when Malik sees Nawi. Thankfully his little protest gives the girls the perfect distraction to make their move. The girls make a run for it but Nawi is captured by some men; Izogie goes back for her and gets shot. she teases Nawi one last time before giving up; Oba offers Nawi to Malik for a price. Nanisca has made a decision to go after her daughter; Amenza tries to stop her but she leaves anyway. The following day, she turns back and finds Amenza, Migan and a few Agojie's following her. Malik buys Nawi and locks her in a room to keep the whites from hurting her since she killed a white man while trying to escape. He gives her a key for whenever she wants to escape but also suggest she comes with him to England. The King learns that part of his counsel has gone off despite his orders; his wife Shante advises him not to call off the feast he prepared or else he will look weak; rather he should name another woman King. While the white men party at night; the Agojie sneaks into their camp. One of the prisoners inform them of Izogie's death and Nawi's Trade. Nanisca angered by the news, instructs they burn the place to the ground taking no prisoners. The Agojie's attack with no mercy; Malik rushes to Nawi and tells her to go with him but she insists on helping her sisters; he gives her a change of clothes and tells her he'll be waiting on the beach incase she changes her mind. Nanisca is on the look out for Oba.; Amenza fights like she's drunk on rage. Migan sets fire to the camps. Malik's friend tries to escape with a few slaves and Malik can't stand this so he releases the slaves and they beat his friend to death. Nanisca finds Oba and this time she's ruthless and finally kills Oba. While she takes in the Victory; a white man almost shoots her but Nawi shoots him instead. She fights off the other men and the Agojie hail their victory. As they march back, Malik still waits for Nawi at the beach; he spots her with her sisters and she nods at him and follows her sisters. Back in Dahomey, the feast has begun; Shante has adorned herself to take the honour that was meant for Nanisca; the Agojie returns and the people hail them as they always do; especially chanting Nanisca. Shante feels ridiculed by this. Nanisca surrenders her sword to the king and accepts to drop her command for disobeying the king's order. King Ghezo after giving a heartfelt speech to his people; bestows on Nanisca, the title of the Woman king to rule the land with him as per their ancient customs. The whole Kingdom celebrates as she takes her seat next to the king. Now it's time for mother and child to have that heart to heart conversation; Nawi seeing how much her existence has caused pain to her mother; leaves her mother with "I'm sorry"; Nanisca is also sorry for giving her away. In the next scene; Nawi asks her mother for a dance and the two make peace. I guess all is well that ends well. The end.. The world of horror cinema is about to get a chilling new addition and it's called Dust Bunny 2025. A film that already has fans buzzing with curiosity and fear. When a movie stars Mads Mickelson, you know you're in for something unsettling, powerful, and deeply emotional. Known for his intense performances in Hannibal and Another Round, Mickelson now dives into a twisted horror drama that combines grief, imagination, and the terror that hides beneath the surface of ordinary life. This isn't your average monster movie. Dust Bunny is shaping up to be a haunting psychological story that explores how children see darkness differently from adults and how pain can create creatures that feel disturbingly real. At the center of the film is an 8-year-old girl, a quiet and imaginative child who believes that a monster living under her bed is responsible for her mother's death. The concept might sound like a childhood nightmare, but the film turns that innocent idea into something far more sinister and emotional. When she confides in her neighbor, played by Mads Mikkelson, things begin to unravel in unexpected ways. What starts as a child's desperate cry for help becomes a psychological descent that blurs the line between reality and imagination. What makes Dust Bunny truly fascinating is the creative mind behind it, Brian Fuller, the visionary creator of Hannibal. Fuller is known for his ability to mix beauty with horror, turning blood and fear into something strangely poetic. After years away from the director's chair, Fuller returns with a film that feels deeply personal and visually stunning. His trademark style, rich colors, eerie symmetry, and emotionally complex characters is expected to dominate every frame. Fans of Hannibal already know how Fuller uses silence, design, and performance to build tension, and Dust Bunny looks ready to take that to the next level. The film doesn't rely on jump scares, or cheap tricks. Instead, it leans into atmosphere, character, and emotional suspense. Every moment feels deliberate. Every sound carefully placed to pull the audience deeper into the child's terrifying perspective. The way the story is told through her imagination and through Mikkelson's uncertain viewpoint creates a dual sense of reality. Are we seeing a real monster or just a projection of trauma and loss? That's the question that drives the film forward. And it's exactly the kind of psychological tension that makes Fuller's work unforgettable. The movie's visuals reportedly have a vintage, almost dreamlike quality, mixing 1,980s suburban aesthetics with dark fairy tale imagery. The production design brings out that feeling of something familiar turning strange, cozy bedrooms turning into shadows of fear and quiet streets hiding secrets behind closed doors. As for Mads Mickelson's role, his character is layered, mysterious, and deeply human. He's not just a bystander in the girl story. He becomes emotionally entangled, perhaps even haunted by his own memories. His presence brings a weight that only an actor of his caliber can deliver. Fuller uses this metaphor to explore how trauma manifests differently in children and adults. text: Marvel’s Black Widow is FINALLY coming to theaters and Disney Plus after a yearlong delay. If your memory is a little hazy about everything Black Widow got up to in the MCU before her death in End Game, or if you’re thinking “Wait, spoiler alert, she DIED?!” then boy do I have the video for you. Instead of going back and watching Scarlet Johanson’s NINE previous MCU appearances to prepare Black Widow, this video has got you covered. Here’s a full recap of Black Widow’s history throughout the MCU. Throughout the MCU we learn of Natasha Romanoff’s backstory that pre-dates her first appearances. She was born in Russia and at a young age was recruited by the KGB. She attended the Red Room Academy where she was educated and indoctrinated in spycraft, eventually leading to her becoming one of the world’s greatest assassins. She was forced to do a lot of pretty messed up stuff at far too young of an age, including murdering innocent people. Her past in the Red Room will haunt Natasha throughout her time in the MCU. Eventually, her skills as an assassin put her on SHIELD’s radar as a threat, so they send their agent Clint Barton, aka Hawkeye, to take her out. But Clint sees something worth saving in her, and helps her defect from Russia and join SHIELD. Which leads us to Natasha’s first official appearance in the MCU... Black Widow, aka Natasha Romanoff, is first introduced to the Marvel Cinematic Universe in Iron Man 2 as a new employee of Tony Stark at Stark Industries. In reality, this is all a cover, as she’s actually a SHIELD agent working with Nick Fury to assess whether or not Tony is worthy of joining the Avengers Initiative. Spoiler alert: Tony gets the gig! Natasha is given a greater focus in her next outing, the first Avengers movie. Working alongside SHIELD, Natasha is a key figure in assembling the Avengers team, personally recruiting Bruce Banner, and quite literally beating some sense into a brainwashed Hawkeye. This movie gives us a lot of backstory on Natasha. She earns Bruce’s trust by telling him about her time as a child spy and recounts with Clint their shared history as SHIELD agents, including an infamous operation that happened in Budapest. Might we get a glimpse of that Budapest mission in the Black Widow movie? After helping to assemble the Avengers and saving the world from an alien invasion, Natasha partners up with Steve Rogers, who you might know as Captain America. During Captain America: Winter Soldier, Natasha and Steve team-up with Sam Wilson, aka Falcon, to take down the mysterious Winter Soldier and the villainous organization HYDRA. Steve has history with the mysterious assassin, as the man is revealed to be his old friend Bucky Barnes, similarly frozen in time. Like Natasha, Bucky has been brainwashed by the enemy and is trained to follow orders upon the reading of a series of code words. Natasha has her own history with Bucky. In her early days as a SHIELD agent, she was assigned to protect a scientist, but the Winter Soldier managed to hunt them down, shooting Natasha in the stomach and killing the scientist. By the end Captain America: Winter Soldier, Natasha and Steve have saved the world from another major threat, put a serious damper on HYDRA’s plans and have brought Bucky Barnes closer to redemption. Next up for Natasha is Avengers: Age of Ultron. It’s here that Natasha’s budding relationship with Bruce Banner begins to come into play. As the Avengers are once again assembled to take on HYDRA, Natasha begins utilizing a lullaby to help bring Bruce back down from his Hulk state. While hiding out at Clint’s family home, it’s revealed that Clint’s wife is pregnant with a boy that they’ll name Nathaniel, after Natasha. Natasha sees the family life that Clint has and dreams of a similar one with Bruce. Bruce rejects the idea, as he’s dangerously violent and can’t have children. Natasha reveals that she also sees herself as a monster due to her Red Room training, and was sterilized to prevent what the Red Room considered “distractions.” Natasha and Bruce find comfort in one another and debate running away together, but superhero duty calls! The Avengers travel to Sokovia to battle the villainous Ultron. Although they defeat Ultron after an epic battle, A Hulk-ed out Bruce decides it would be better for the world if the Hulk wasn’t in it, so he flies off to an unknown location. With Bruce gone, Natasha decides to help Steve lead a new team of Avengers, which includes Falcon, War Machine, Wanda Maximoff, and Vision. And that brings us to Captain America: Civil War. Following the destruction of Sokovia in Age of Ultron, and an unfortunate event in Lagos at the start of Captain America: Civil War, the United Nations, represented by General Thaddeus Ross, wants the Avengers to sign the Sokovia Accords, which would force them to abide by stricter regulations and oversight. The decision over whether or not to sign the Sokovia Accords fractures the Avengers, with Tony Stark leading the charge in favor, and Steve Rogers leading those who opposed. Natasha ultimately sides with Tony, feeling that she should be held accountable for all of her past actions. Tensions come to a head in a spectacularly awesome way as Team Cap and Team Iron Man fight at an abandoned airport. During the fight, Black Widow lets Steve and a rehabilitated Bucky escape. The rest of Team Cap is captured and arrested, and Tony informs Natasha that the same would happen to her due to her letting Captain America escape. And so, Natasha Romanoff was now a fugitive. And now let’s briefly put in a pin in this Black Widow history lesson. Because this is apparently the period of time when the new Black Widow movie takes place. With Natasha on the run following her letting Steve Rogers escape, it seems that our favorite female assassin decides to return home to Russia for a family reunion. What happens while she’s there? Well, we’ve got to watch Black Widow to find that out. What we do know is that she’ll come back in touch with her sister, Yelena, and they’ll be battling the villainous Taskmaster. It remains to be seen what sort of ramifications or surprises are in store that could affect the entire MCU. But let’s get back to class, shall we... After the events of Civil War, Steve drops Bucky off in Wakanda to fully deprogram him. Natasha returns from her hopefully super exciting and entertaining trip to Russia to join Steve in rescuing his imprisoned team. While most decide to return home to their normal lives, Sam decides to join Natasha and Steve on the run. The trio are off running secret missions for SHIELD when they get a call from Bruce Banner asking for their help. You see, there’s this guy named Thanos who wants to assemble all of the infinity stones in order to wipe out half of the universe’s population. So Black Widow, Captain America, and Falcon return to join the Avengers in their fight. General Ross wants the team arrested, but is dismissed. The team is back together! And with that comes a brief, awkward reunion for Natasha and Bruce, who have bigger problems to worry about than their budding relationship. Since one of Thanos’ coveted infinity stones is embedded into Vison’s skull, the Avengers head to Wakanda for help in removing the stone. While there, a rehabilitated and deprogrammed Bucky rejoins the team as Thanos and his army make their attack. And that’s where our team of Avengers band together to fight off Thanos and defeat his massive army, saving the day! ...No, Thanos wins and collects all of the infinity stones, snapping his fingers and wiping out half of the entire universe. Natasha and the remaining Avengers manage to track down Thanos and make him pay for crimes, but it doesn’t change the fact that half of their friends are now dead, let alone half of the entire universe. 5 years pass and Natasha is forgiven of her crimes and takes over as leader of the Avengers. While most of the other Avengers are now disillusioned and scattered, Natasha has hope that things will get better. The Avengers changed her as a person. They gave her family. They gave her hope. Her character is finally coming to peace with her past and actually forgiving herself. And that hope isn’t misguided, because Scott Lang, aka Ant-Man, escapes the Quantum Realm with a plan to bring back everyone who died. A time heist. Natasha helps reassemble the Avengers, including a newly tatted up Clint, who’s been off the grid and exacting vigilante justice on those he deems deserve it, like the Yakuza. Clint’s entire family was wiped out by Thanos’ snap, but Natasha offers him a chance to bring them back. The plan? The Avengers will travel back in time to various points from MCU past to collect the stones before Thanos and use their power to bring everyone back to life. The team splits up to travel to various past times for various stones, and Natasha and Clint are tasked with traveling to Vormir to retrieve the Soul Stone. Unfortunately, the only way to retrieve the stone is via sacrifice. Both Natasha and Clint are willing to sacrifice themselves to save each other and half of humanity. They share an emotional goodbye, and both believe they should be the one to make the sacrifice. They begin fighting in an attempt to save the other and sacrifice themself. Ultimately, Natasha wins the fight, forcing Clint to let her go. Natasha falls to her death, giving her life to save her best friend and bring back the billions of lives lost due to Thanos’ snap. Due to her sacrifice, Clint receives the Soul Stone. The other Avengers retrieve their own stones, and with the infinity gauntlet they are able to bring back everyone who was lost. Due to Natasha’s selfless act, the entire universe was saved. Oh, and Tony Stark sacrificed himself too, but he’s the only one who gets a big emotional funeral. Sorry, Nat. You deserved better. And that’s the (current) entire history of Black Widow in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Let me know some of your favorite Black Widow moments in the comments below and feel free to share your theories about what happens with the Black Widow character moving forward in the MCU. As always, thanks for watching and I’ll see ya in the next one.

text: Who are [Musika] you? Kumusta kaibigan? Ang kwento nating itatampok ngayon ay ang maaksyong pelikulang Aking Man. Habang nakikipaglaban, makikita naman na magaling si Levon sa pagtatanggol sa kanyang sarili dahil si FBJ pala ang nagturo sa kanya. Ginamit niya ang isa sa mga kalaban bilang panangga bago itinutok ang baril sa kanila at binalaang hwag na silang bumalik pa. Maya-maya lumapit ang binatang trabahador para pasalamatan si Levon. Pagkatapos isang dalagang nagngangalang Jenny na miyembro ng pamilya Garcia ang nagtanong kay Levon kung paano niya nagawa iyon. Itinanggi naman ito ni Calbo S10-Eleev na wala siyang alam sa mga naganap. Pagkatapos ng mahabang araw sa trabaho, pinuntahan ni Levon ang kanyang anak na babae na si Maryet. Isang single father si Levon sa kanyang anak at nakatira ito kasama ang kanyang lolo na si Dr. Rot. Kinabukasan, nagpunta si Levon sa kanyang abogado at nakipag-usap dito. Malalaman na galit si Dr. Rot kay Levon dahil sa paniniwalang ito ang dahilan ng pagkamatay ng kanyang anak. Pero ipinaliwanag ni Levon na nagpakamatay ang kanyang asawa noong sila ay nasa serbisyo pa sa ibang bansa. Sinabi naman ng kanyang abogado na maraming pera ang kanyang biyanan at kaya nitong kumuha ng magagaling na abogado. At kahit magbayad pa ito ng $1,000 kada oras ay gagawin nito para lang maubos ang pera ni Levon at mapalayo ito sa kanyang anak. Iminongkah ng abogado ni Levon na makipag-areglo na lamang ngunit ipinakita ni Levon na may sarili siyang kakayahan. Sa ibang eksena, makikita si Jenny na pumunta sa isang club kasama ang kanyang mga kaibigan. The upcoming film Ha 2025 is shaping up to be one of the most talked about psychological dramas of the decade. It's not just another remake or reinterpretation. It's a reinvention of Henrik Ipsson's classic play Het Gabler transformed into a cinematic experience that promises to be raw, haunting, and emotionally electrifying. What makes this project even more captivating is that it's directed by Joe Wright, the visionary filmmaker behind Atonement, Pride and Prejudice, and Darkest Hour. Wright is known for his lush, emotionally charged storytelling and visual style. And in Hetta, he seems ready to dive deeper than ever into the complexities of power, repression, and self-destruction. At the center of this ambitious film is Tessa Thompson, taking on the title role of Ha. Known for her bold performances in films like Creed, Passing, and Thor, Love, and Thunder, Thompson brings a magnetic intensity to every role she plays. But Hetta might be her most daring transformation yet. She's stepping into the skin of a woman torn between the desire for control and the crushing weight of societal expectations. Early buzz from insiders who have glimpsed footage describes her performance as mesmerizingly cold yet heartbreakingly human. There's a sense that Thompson's Ha won't just be another adaptation. She'll redefine what this character means for a modern audience. Set in a time period that blurs the line between the historical and the contemporary, Ha 2025 reportedly takes bold creative liberties with its setting. Joe Wright's signature visual flare with grand architecture, textured lighting, and emotionally symbolic cinematography is expected to play a crucial role in expressing Ha's inner turmoil. Instead of relying solely on dialogue to show her suffocating world, Wright uses the environment itself as an emotional extension of her psyche. Every room, every costume, every flicker of light tells a part of Ha's story. The film's production has also drawn attention for its daring artistic choices. The costumes are said to merge Victorian silhouettes with modern tailoring, creating a timeless visual identity. The color palette leans toward muted tones of gray, gold, and dark burgundy, symbolizing both Ha's luxury and her emotional confinement. Behind the camera, cinematographer Sheamus Maccgarvey, who has worked with Wright on several previous projects, brings a painterly touch to every frame. His approach reportedly captures the contrast between Ha's outward poise and her private despair. It's not just about beautiful visuals. It's about making every frame a psychological portrait. The supporting cast adds even more depth to this layered story. Each character in Ha's orbit represents a different force shaping her life ambition, desire, judgment, or escape. While official plot details are kept tightly under wraps, the core essence remains faithful to Ipsson's original masterpiece, Ha is trapped in a marriage that fails to ignite her passion. surrounded by a world that refuses to let her live on her own terms. Reports from the set suggest that Ha 2025 explores these themes with a more intimate and cinematic approach than any previous adaptation. Joe Wright is known for his ability to translate emotional conflict into visual language. Think of the long tracking shots in Atonement or the painterly compositions of Anakaranina. With Ha, he seems determined to bring that same visual poetry to a story that lives in silence, tension, and repressed emotion. Some early behindthe-scenes whispers suggest that Wright employs long single take sequences that immerse viewers directly into Ha's emotional world, making us feel her anxiety, her boredom, and her slow descent into despair. Production for Hetta began quietly in late 2023 and wrapped up in mid 2024 with much of the filming taking place in the UK. The project has been kept remarkably secretive which only adds to the intrigue. What little is known about the filming process suggests a meticulous approach, every gesture, every glance, every pause carefully constructed to reveal something about Heta's psychological state. The release of the first trailer in early 2025 instantly set social media ab buzz. Even though it revealed very little of the plot, its haunting tone and breathtaking visuals left audiences stunned. The trailer opens with a slow zoom on Ha sitting motionless in a grand sunlet room. The light falling softly across her face as her expression remains unreadable. The voice over whispers fragments of dialogue hinting at the battle between desire and despair. As the music swells, the camera follows her through corridors that seem to close and around her, ending with a single unforgettable line. I want for once in my life to have power. That final whisper was enough to ignite discussions across film forums and fan communities. As the anticipation builds, Ha 2025 stands as a reminder that great cinema doesn't always come from loud spectacle or heavy visual effects. Sometimes it comes from the quiet storm inside a single character. Joe Wright's direction is said to lean deeply into this emotional undercurrent, focusing on how subtle gestures and expressions can communicate volumes. In interviews, those close to the production have hinted that Wright designed the film's pacing like a slow tightening coil. The tension builds gradually until it becomes almost unbearable. This approach captures the essence of Ipsson's original tragedy, but gives it the rhythm of modern psychological thrillers, keeping audiences on edge while still grounded in character-driven emotion. The chemistry between the cast members is another element that's reportedly extraordinary. Each actor seems to serve as both an ally and a mirror for Hera, reflecting the parts of herself she tries to hide. The character of her husband, Jorgen, is portrayed as loving yet naive, unable to grasp the complexity of his wife's dissatisfaction. Their relationship, presented in an atmosphere of quiet domesticity, slowly unravels as the story unfolds, revealing not just emotional distance, but a profound misalignment of dreams and purpose. Meanwhile, other characters from Ha's past re-enter her life, each reigniting the embers of what could have been lost love, unfulfilled ambition, and the haunting pull of freedom. What's fascinating about Ha 2025 is how it portrays these relationships not just as plot devices, but as reflections of larger social pressures. The world around Ha is built like a golden cage, luxurious but suffocating. Every conversation, every social gathering carries the unspoken rules of gender, class, and reputation. Joe Wright reportedly uses mirrors and reflections as recurring visual motifs throughout the film haft often framed between multiple reflections, suggesting the fragmentation of her identity. This symbolic imagery turns what could have been a simple period drama into an exploration of the human psyche itself. There's also a strong emphasis on sound design. Early reports from test screenings mentioned that the silence in the film is almost as important as the dialogue. The echo of footsteps, the rustling of fabric, and the creek of furniture all add layers of tension, giving the film an immersive quality. These choices make the viewer feel like they're inside his head, experiencing her world in heightened sensory detail. When the music finally swells, it's not just background. It feels like an emotional release, as if the film itself is exhaling after holding its breath. Tessa Thompson's interpretation of Ha is shaping up to be a performance unlike anything we've seen from her before. She's not playing Ha as a simple victim or manipulator. Instead, she walks the fine line between control and chaos. Her eyes carry the story one moment sharp and calculating, the next distant and lost. What makes her portrayal even more compelling is how she captures the contradictions of the character. Heda wants to be free, yet she clings to control. She despises conformity, but fears being judged. She's both fragile and ferocious, both commanding and deeply insecure. Thompson's acting reportedly reveals these layers with such precision that audiences are left questioning whether they sympathize with her or fear her and that moral ambiguity is exactly what makes the story so powerful. Behind the scenes, the production design team went to great lengths to ensure that every visual element reflects Ha's internal state. The interiors shift gradually throughout the film, at first elegant and spacious, then suddenly closing in as her emotional unraveling deepens. The lighting grows colder, the shadows longer. Wright is said to have used practical light sources like candles and window sunlight to create an organic texture that blurs the line between beauty and decay. These visual transitions allow the audience to feel heta's psychological descent not through exposition but through atmosphere. Its cinema is emotion pure, unspoken, yet impossible to ignore. One particularly striking aspect of the movie is its use of pacing. Instead of relying on quick cuts or heavy dialogue, Wright embraces stillness, long takes linger on Ha's face, capturing the small flickers of emotion that reveal her internal war. This patience and storytelling allows viewers to feel the suffocating passage of time that defines her life. In several sequences, the silence stretches until it becomes almost unbearable, forcing the audience to sit in heda's discomfort. When moments of confrontation finally arrive, they feel explosive, not because of action, but because of the emotional weight that's been quietly building. text: In a Boston suburb, British museum director Charlie Thompson approaches bookstore clerk Emma Harwood while she is reading at a cafe, pretending he has read her book. Emma seemingly ignores him and he apologizes for making her uncomfortable. Emma explains that she is deaf in one ear and had not heard him. It's a perfect opening, effortlessly charming, laced with low stakes embarrassment. Emma, played by Zenaia with a warmth that makes what comes later all the more devastating doesn't let Charlie off the hook easily. Instead, she offers him something quietly profound, a second chance. She asks him to start over to introduce himself properly as if the stumble never happened. Charlie obliges. They go on a date. Something real begins. Dot. This start over moment isn't just a cute narrative beat. It's a thematic contract the film will cash in brutally at the end. Remember it. The couple is now engaged, living in Boston, building a life together that looks from the outside essentially perfect. One night while strolling through the city, they witness their wedding DJ Pauline smoking heroin in a public park. The moment unsettles them and they turn to their wedding party, made of honor Rachel and best man Mike to discuss whether Pauline should be fired. Emma makes a point she clearly believes. Everyone has done something bad. No one is clean. And so, almost casually, the table begins confessing. The confessions escalate in a way that is equal parts darkly funny and genuinely disturbing. Mike admits he used his ex-girlfriend as a human shield during a dog attack in Mexico. Rachel confesses she once locked her mentally disabled neighbor inside an abandoned RV overnight. Charlie reveals he cyberbullied a classmate so relentlessly that the boy's entire family relocated to escape him. And then Emma speaks. Emma drops a shocking truth about her past. At 15, she planned to commit a school shooting. She explains that she had told Charlie she was born deaf, but she actually lost her hearing when she fired a gun too close to her ear while practicing in the forest. Emma is quick to contextualize. She abandoned the plan after a mass shooting hit close to home and shattered her community. The experience rather than leading her down a darker path galvanized her into gun control advocacy. She became in a very real sense someone who redirected genuine darkness into something meaningful. But the damage to the dinner table and to Charlie is done. Rachel reveals that her cousin Samantha was paralyzed in a shooting. What was already a tense confession becomes immediately viscerally personal. The room doesn't just hold Emma's past. It now holds someone else's wound. Emma's nightmares grow more frequent, filled with shooting imagery, while Charlie's paranoia intensifies, fed by gun- rellated items found at home and at his workplace. Meanwhile, Alana's Rachel, who was already the film's most combustible supporting character, withdraws from Emma entirely. Rachel declines the wedding invitation, though Charlie eventually convinces her to attend. It's a small victory that feels hollow. You can convince someone to show up. You can't convince them to forgive. And then, because Borgley apparently decided one catastrophic secret wasn't enough, the film detonates a second bomb. An awkward run-in with Misha leaves Charlie rattled. He frantically reassures her that she would love Emma. A line that casts a shadow over the couple's trust. Misha is not nothing. Misha is the other thing. Everything that has been quietly building, Emma's secret, Charlie's guilt, Rachel's grief, the social pressure of performing joy in front of an audience, ignites simultaneously. In the bathroom, Emma overhears Miesa discussing a school shooting with another guest and pulls her into the room to confront the situation. Misha, sensing trouble, blames Charlie by claiming he kissed her first, a revelation that shocks Emma. Emma was already navigating the fallout of her own past. Now she discovers her fiance has his own secret she didn't know about. Two people who were theoretically being fully honest with each other were both in different ways holding something back. Charlie makes a clumsy attempt to address the tension with a heartfelt speech about his love for Emma, apologizing for the affair with Misha and urging guests to stop the gossip. The scene erupts as Blake confronts and attacks Charlie, leaving Emma to navigate the fallout. Emma decides to leave rather than cast doubt on the marriage in front of everyone. After a troubling night, a bloodied and despondent Charlie returns to the pair's apartment in search of Emma. When he cannot find her, he heads to their favorite diner alone. Soon, Emma arrives and sits opposite him. They reintroduce themselves as if meeting for the first time and for a moment they share a hopeful smile before the weight of their recent history settles between them. Borgley refuses to tell you which it is. The hopeful smile appears and then crucially the film notes that the weight of their recent history settles between them. He doesn't give you a clean they're going to be okay. He gives you the hope and the gravity at the same time and he makes you sit with both. The film's deeper argument running underneath all of the dark comedy and social horror is about moral symmetry and the impossibility of a clean ledger. Every character at that confession dinner had done something genuinely terrible. Charlie's cyber bullying drove a child's family from their home. Rachel locked a disabled person overnight in an abandoned vehicle. Mike used a woman as a shield against an animal attack. Emma planned but never executed a school shooting. The film never ranks these actions by severity. It presents them with equivalent directness and watches the characters immediately begin ranking them anyway. Rachel, who committed her own act of profound cruelty, becomes the one most horrified by Emma's revelation. The hypocrisy is pointed. It's not subtle, but it's also not simple because Rachel's cousin was paralyzed in a shooting, and that wound is real regardless of the inconsistency. The final diner scene asks, "Can two people who have seen behind each other's narrative, who have glimpsed the unedited version, still choose each other, and is choosing each other again with full knowledge more meaningful than the original choice? Or is it just a more complicated form of the same selfdeception?" Borley doesn't answer. He gives you a smile, a shadow, and the credits.

His initial coping mechanism is isolation and stubborn self-reliance. He is reluctant to interact with his new neighbors who are also victims of the blaze. His mantra, which he shares with his aranged daughter, is we don't need to bother nobody. Reflecting his closed off nature. This is a man who is a ghost in his own life, forced to confront the fact that his legacy and livelihood have been turned into scorched earth and rubble. The journey of Dusty's emotional rebuilding begins with the arrival of his young daughter, Cali Rose, played by Lily Lator. Cali Rose is the vibrant, innocent force that slowly chips away at Dusty's guarded exterior. She is the first step toward reconnecting with his past and his humanity. The film also focuses on Dusty's reconnection with his ex-wife Ruby, played by the talented Megan Fe. Dusty and Ruby had grown distant over time. text: The movie starts with a man named Heller working on his broken plane. His wife, Sarah, comes over and asks him to come inside. Heller makes her a cup of coffee, and Sarah tells him she has to go to London for five days for work. Heller isn’t happy about it, but he walks her to the car and says goodbye. Then Heller drives to his job. He works as an analyst at a CIA office. At work, he talks to a coworker named The Bear. While they’re chatting, The Bear asks for help with his computer, and Heller says he’ll help. Turns out that Heller is a genius and has an IQ of 170. After that, Heller goes into his office and starts looking at some files. While he’s working, he gets a message from an online friend named Inqiline. The message has some secret information about the government. As Heller reads it, he notices something strange. Then Sarah calls him. He talks to her quickly, then goes back to looking at the file. When Heller opens the files, he finds out something shocking—his own government ordered drone strikes on friendly countries. He also discovers that Director Moore and a man named Caleb are behind the attacks. Heller quickly leaves the office. That night, Heller tries to call his wife Sarah, but she doesn’t answer. The next morning at work, Moore comes to Heller’s office and takes him to see Director O’Brien. She tells Heller that Sarah was killed in an attack. Moore shows him the news and explains what happened. Heartbroken, Heller goes home, unable to believe that Sarah is really gone. The next morning, Heller talks to Moore and Caleb about what happened and asks what they’re going to do. Moore tells him not to worry, and that everything will be handled. A few days later, Sarah’s body and her belongings arrive at the airport. At home, Heller goes through her things and starts crying. Over the next few days, Heller keeps looking into the attack. He studies everything and explains what he finds to Moore and Caleb. It turns out the attackers were a team of four people. During a fight with the security team, one of them killed a guard. This made the others panic, so they quickly took some hostages. They grabbed people from the airport waiting room—and one of them was Sarah. The person who took Sarah was named Mishka Blazhic, and another one was named Ellish. While trying to escape, they killed Sarah. Later, the attackers gave the name of a dealer called Frank. But when Heller tells Moore and Caleb, they don’t seem surprised. That’s when Heller realizes they already knew everything about the attack. When he asks them about it, Moore says their real goal is to destroy the entire organization. Then Moore tells Heller to go to a therapy session. During the session, Heller tells the therapist everything. He’s confused and upset that the government isn’t doing anything. That’s when he decides he has to stop these people himself. A few days later, Heller hides a bug on his ID card and sneaks into the office. He prints out secret files that show what Moore and Caleb have done. Then he goes to a bar and notices a CD machine that he thinks he can use. The next morning, Heller takes the printed papers and starts blackmailing Moore and Caleb. He tells them he has backup copies of the information, and if anything happens to him, the files will be sent to the media. He also says he wants to be the one to take down the people who killed Sarah—and asks to be trained for the mission. Moore realizes they’re in trouble, so he agrees and assigns a man named Henderson to train Heller. During training, Heller struggles—he can’t even hit a target with a gun. But he’s great at making explosive weapons, like it’s second nature. Henderson also makes fake passports for him. While training, Henderson tells him that even up close, Heller just can’t bring himself to shoot. Back at the CIA office, Caleb becomes suspicious. He starts checking Heller’s files and searches everywhere for the backup data—even Heller’s house—but finds nothing. Then they discover Heller has been going to a bar several times. Thinking the files might be there, they check the bar and find the CD machine. But when they open it, they realize Heller was bluffing—there’s nothing inside. Worried, they call Henderson and tell him to bring Heller back. But when Henderson goes to Heller’s room at the training center, he finds it empty. Heller has already left, taking the fake passports with him. Heller uses the fake passports and travels to London. There, he starts following a dealer named Gretchen Frank. He even sneaks into her house to look for clues. When Gretchen comes home, Heller tries to point a gun at her—but he can’t bring himself to shoot. So, he comes up with a different plan. While Gretchen is getting treatment at a hospital, Heller sneaks into her room and puts poison in her oxygen machine. But she wakes up, escapes the chamber, and even fights Heller before running out into the street. There, she’s hit by a car and dies. Heller takes her phone and quickly leaves the scene. Then he grabs his things and travels to France. One night at a bar, he notices someone is following him—it’s Henderson. Heller tries to run, but Henderson catches up. Heller creates a distraction and talks to Henderson. Henderson tells him that he can’t change the past. While they talk, Heller uses the distraction to escape. The next morning, Heller sends a message to his anonymous online friend asking for help. Then he flies to Istanbul and meets up with his friend Inquiline. Together, they go to her safe house and start tracking down the killers. Meanwhile, Director O’Brien starts to suspect that Moore is doing something shady behind her back. She asks him about it, but Moore denies everything and says he fully supports her. As he leaves, O’Brien realizes that Moore was the one who sent Henderson to train Heller, and she begins an investigation. Back at the safe house, Heller and Inquiline find out that one of the killers is in Madrid. Heller travels there. He finds out the killer likes to swim alone in a sky pool—it's a pool made of glass, high above the ground. Heller builds a device that can break the glass of the pool. The next day, Heller confronts the killer and asks for the name of the other person involved in Sarah’s death. But the killer refuses to talk. So, Heller activates the device. The glass shatters, and the killer falls with the water, dying on impact. Inquiline finds out that Henderson is following Heller and quickly warns him. Heller starts running, but just as Henderson is about to catch him, another CIA agent—sent by Director O’Brien—steps in and stops Henderson. The two agents get into a serious fight. In the end, other CIA agents arrive and shoot Henderson. Heller wants to help Henderson, but Inquiline stops him and tells him to keep going. Meanwhile, back at the CIA office, Director O’Brien asks Moore about Heller. Moore lies and says he doesn’t know anything, then leaves. Later, O’Brien checks the surveillance footage from Madrid. She sees something that makes her think Inquiline might be helping Heller. So, the CIA starts tracking Inquiline and finds out she’s in Istanbul. They then contact the embassy there. That night, while Heller and Inquiline are sleeping, CIA agents surround their safe house. They wake up and quickly run away. They jump into a car and try to escape. But during the chase, a bullet hits Inquiline, killing her instantly. Heller keeps driving, heartbroken. Before leaving, he kisses her goodbye. A few days later, Heller gets a message through Frank’s contact about an arms deal. He agrees to supply weapons. Then, he uploads his face into special software that can make other people look like him. He doesn’t know that the CIA now thinks he’s in Berlin because of this trick—and they send agents there. Meanwhile, Heller sets a trap for one of the killers. He uses a bomb that goes off if anyone moves away from it. When the killer gets caught, Heller questions him and finds out that their leader always stays on a ship. Heller takes the killer’s phone and leaves. As he walks away, the killer accidentally moves and is killed by the bomb. At the same time, the CIA realizes they were tracking the wrong person. They stop their search for Heller. Heller makes his way to a port near the Baltic Sea and starts watching some of the illegal deals happening around a big ship. While tracking the deals, he suddenly runs into The Bear, his old coworker, who is also on the run. They talk for a while, and Bear tells Heller he knows everything he’s done—and says he’s willing to help him no matter what. A few days later, Heller watches a deal from a distance. But the dealers spot him, knock him out, and take him to their boss, a man named Slater. That night, Heller is brought onto Slater’s ship to meet him. On the ship, Heller confronts Slater about the deals he made with Moore and Caleb. Slater tells Heller that he’s not a killer—he’s too afraid to pull the trigger. To prove it, Slater hands Heller a loaded gun and dares him to shoot. Heller points the gun at him but can’t do it. Then, something strange happens—the ship starts to turn on its own. Slater gets nervous and tries to take control, but Heller calmly tells him that he hacked the ship. Now, it’s sailing into Finnish waters. Heller also says he already contacted Interpol and the Finnish navy. Soon, Slater and his men are caught and arrested. In the end, Moore and Caleb are also arrested for everything they did. Heller finally gets justice for his wife and finds peace. At the very end, he meets Henderson again—who turns out to still be alive. Heller then takes one last flight in the small plane Sarah had gifted him, feeling close to her once more.

text: Sup yall? This week, we beastin through the darkness with "Les Miserables," by Victor Hugo. After 19 years of hard time in a French prison fo stealin bread to feed his fam, Jean Valjean all cashed out lookin fo help. Nobody in town showin him any love, til a righteous holy man named Myriel like, "come on in, padna!" But, when da police catch Valjean tryna boost Myriel's silverware, Myriel jus' let it slide and tell the fuzz he gave it to him as a gift. Myriel say, "look man, I just saved yo ass. You best stop all dat hood sh*t and become a better man, yo!" After one last dick move — jackin some coin from a lil kid — Valjean break down and decide he gotta put his bangin days behind him. He change his name to Monsieur Madeleine and move to a new town, where he start stackin mad cheddar. Before you know it, brutha becomes the Goddamn mayor! Meanwhile, this po girl, Fantine, be straight buggin — Number one, she desperate fo cash. And, number two — her man just left her with a love-child named Cosette, and there ain't no way she gonna get work if word gets out about her. So, this shysti dude named Thenardier say Cosette can hide with him and his fam, so long as Fantine throw em some ends erry month. Fantine lands a gig grindin at Madeleine's factory, but gets da axe as soon as errybody find out bout Cosette. And with the Thenardiers greedy, lyin asses hittin her up fo mo cash, sh*t so raw for Fantine that she gotta sell her hair, her teeth, and start turnin tricks on da streets. Plus, all this sh*t is literally killin her. Damn. One night, the local law-man, Javert, arrests Fantine, but, Madeleine step in, tells Javert to hop off, and start to give Fantine a lil TLC. When Javert figure out Madeline's real identity, Javert cuff him right in front of Fantine. Girl wigs out so hard, she up and dies. By the way, Valjean's real identity only hit da streets cuz he wanted to save somebody's life. Thankfully, ain't no cell can keep dat boy, Valjean, down. Dude swings back to town to save Cosette from dem hater Thenardiers, who been treatin her like sh*t fo years. Valjean drop some fat stacks, buys her off em, and chunks deuces to Paris. Things aight in Paris fo a lil while, but when Javert hear that Valjean back in town, Val and Cosette gotta pack their sh*t and lay low in a convent. Years later, a dude named Marius peep game at a dime and immediately falls balls-deep in love! And, what do you know? It's Cosette, all grown up. Lookin good, girl! Look what he said bout dis girl — "The woman whom he now saw was a noble, beautiful creature, with all the most bewitching feminine outlines at the precise moment when they are still combined with all the most charming graces of childhood — that pure and fleeting moment that can only be translated by these two words: sweet fifteen." Ugh! Marius try to holler at a girl, but Valjean moves they asses outta there before a brotha can get his mack on. Marius gets a tip about Cosette's new digs and they eventually meet and confess they love fo each other. 'Cept, Valjean ain't down wit that. And, with all da political unrest goin down in the streets, Valjean decides it's time fo them to roll out to England. Marius gets so tore up dat he ain't gonna be with his baby dip, that he decide he don't give a f**k no mo and gonna join da revolution. When Valjean figure out dat Cosette and Marius are in love fo real, he can't let loverboy get his ass murked, so he straps up and joins the fight, too. When da rebels find out that Javert a royalist snitch, they give Valjean the job of ghostin his ass. But, Valjean — bein a nice dude and all — just lets him walk away. Lata', Marius get pretty messed up and Valjean gotta carry his ass through some boo-boo sewers to get him help. Valjean runs in to Javert again, and Valjean finally like, "Aight, aight. You can arrest me. Just let me drop this dude off at his crib, and make one last stop at my pad." Javert oblige a brotha, but start losin his sh*t when he realize he compromising everything his life stood for, and straight ends it. Marius heals up and him and Cosette get hitched. S'all good, right? Nah. Not in this f**kin book. Valjean tells Marius about his crimin days, and Marius start givin Valjean the cold shoulder. Our boy gets da hint and stops droppin by. Dat little sh*t Marius got no idea it was Valjean that saved his ass in that sewer. With nothin left to live for, Valjean start wastin away, hops in bed, and doesn't ever leave. Lata', Marius conversatin wit Thenardier when brotha finally recognize dat da only reason he alive is cuz of Valjean. Plus, Valjean the only reason he wit Cosette now. Oh yeah — and Valjean left em mad bank. Feelin like a real assh*le, Marius and Cosette swing over to Valjean's spot and forgive him. Now, Valjean can die in peace. Man, this book is straight relentless — gnarly prisons, po girls turnin tricks, disease wastin everybody! V-hug gonna lay out da worst that life's got to offer, and he throws out his biggest beefs in the preface. "So long as there shall exist, by reason of law and custom, a social condemnation which, in the midst of civilization, artificially creates a hell on earth, and complicates with human fatality a destiny that is divine; so long as the three problems of the century — the degradation of man by the exploitation of his labor, the ruin of woman by starvation, and the atrophy of childhood by physical and spiritual night — are not solved; so long as, in certain regions, social asphyxia shall be possible; in other words, and from a still broader point of view, so long as ignorance and misery remain on earth, there should be a need for books such as this." So, three big things he buckin — rich people takin advantage of da workin man, women starving to death, and little kids drownin in a dark world dat ain't got no hope. In short, Hugo wagin war on a society that's f**kin over its peeps. In fact, that's one of Hugo's main jams in this big-ass book: Society got da power to completely wreck somebody — and not only their body, but their soul, too. Whether it da big house dat turn Valjean into a stone-cold gangster, or da poverty and shaming that make Fantine turn to a life of hookin — society burnin everybody. Like Valjean himself say, "The prison makes the convict. Make of this what you like. Before prison, I was a poor peasant, unintelligent, a sort of idiot; prison changed me. I was stupid, I became wicked; I was a log, I became a firebrand." And, lemme tell you a lil somethin, man — society didn't break no regular erryday thug. Valjean is hella swole, man — fo real. On page 90, it even say he got the got da strength of four men. He still ain't got nuttin on deez guns. Don't hate. But no matter how jacked Valjean be, he still ain't got da muscle to flex with a broken system. Hugo's book ain't all bad, though. For Javert's ice-cold justice, there's Myriel's mercy. For Thenardier's greed, we see Valjean's willingness to give away everything — even his life. And, fo all the darkness that society can drop on a brotha, there's also light. We got da power to lift each other up and redeem erry brotha and sista with love and kindness. Valjean and Cosette reppin this idea perfectly: "He loved, and he grew strong again. Alas, he was as frail as Cosette. He protected her, and she gave him strength. Thanks to him, she could walk upright in life; thanks to her, he could persist in virtue. He was this child's support, and she was his prop and staff." Valjean try to make this same point to a bunch of hoods while they gardening. "One day [Valjean] saw some peasants busily pulling out nettles; he looked at the heap of plants, uprooted, and already wilted, and said, '…If we took a little time, the nettle would be useful; we neglect it, and it becomes harmful. Then we kill it. Men are so like the nettle!' After a short silence, he added, 'My friends, remember this: There are no bad herbs, and no bad men; there are only bad cultivators." As all my well-read ballas know, my number one motto is "Don't Judge a Book by its cover." Y'all know I'm all about that. But, lemme leave you with my number two motto, which "Les Mis" perfectly reppin: Don't ever underestimate yo own power and how much of a difference you can make. If you let anger, hatred, and injustice keep you down, ain't no tellin what kinda harm you can do. But, if you let love and light guide the way, then the world's dark side can't touch you. You got da power to cultivate good in da world. Use it. Thanks for keepin it real with me, my well-read ballas. Sparky Sweets out! Peace!
