text: Welcome to the Man of Recaps, this is the complete Transformers recap before Rise of the Beasts. In the first Transformers, Shia LaBeouf is Sam Witwicky, a normal teenage boy whose dad is taking him out to buy his first car. He picks out this old yellow Camaro that is “more than meets the eye.” Now that Sam has a car, he’s able to give a ride home to the hot girl from school, Mikaela, played by Megan Fox, whose role in this film caused a generation of boys to hit puberty. But meanwhile, the Earth is being invaded by transforming vehicles that are alien robots in disguise. Turns out Sam's great grandfather was an explorer, Archibald Witwicky, who went to the North Pole and found one of these transformers that crashed years ago. It blasted his glasses with important information, and now that Sam put them up on eBay, the Decepticons are coming after him. But luckily his new car is a transformer too, here to protect him. His name is Bumblebee, and his voice thing’s broken so he can't talk, but he communicates in a fun way using clips from the radio. Now bumblebee calls in his good Transformer friends, the Autobots. Their leader transforms into the semi-truck with a blue and red flames paint job, it is Optimus Prime. He explains they're from the planet Cybertron, where there was a big civil war between the good Autobots and the evil Decepticons, led by Megatron. They go back to Sam's house to get the glasses before the Decepticons, but now they're interrupted by the government. It's the super secret Sector Seven, who monitors alien life here, led by the funny guy, Agent Simmons. They have Megatron’s frozen body, as well as the All Spark, that could instill life into machines to make new transformers. But oh no, they led the Decepticons right to it. They wake up Megatron, who's in a real bad mood and oh, it's a big chase, oh yeah! Meanwhile, half the movie followed military guy and his squad fighting Decepticons in the desert. Another half of the movie follows a CIA analyst who's inexplicably an Australian model. She got help from her friend who was playing Dance Dance Revolution at his grandma's house - there's a lot going on in these movies. But it all comes together for the final battle. Transformers transforming, explosions everywhere, Michael Bay going nuts! But they got to keep the All Spark away from Megatron because he wants to use it to turn the earth into New Cybertron. So while the Transformers are having their big robot fight, Sam Witwicky’s running around with the plot thing. Optimus and Megatron have their final fight, but it looks like Megatron is going to win. So Optimus wants to put the All Spark in his chest, which will kill him but destroy the cube. But Sam's like, what if I shoved the cube into Megatron’s chest instead? And that works, destroys the cube, kills megatron. Yeah, good thinking kid. So the earth is saved, Sam and Mikaela have a sunset make out. Then Optimus Prime gives an inspiring speech, and it is the iconic Linkin Park credits song. Number two is Transformers Revenge of the Fallen. Sam Witwicky is going off to college, but in his pocket he finds a little piece of the All Spark that blasts his mind with alien info. The Decepticons steal another piece of the All Spark, and putting the All Spark in Megatron’s chest killed him, but putting it in again brings him back to life. Mikaela comes to visit Sam to find him in a compromising position, but it's even worse than it looks because it's a transformer. So Megatron grabs him to get the info in his head, but his car Bumblebee busts in to save him. Optimus Prime comes too, but oh no, it was a trap, they outnumbered him. And now Megatron kills Optimus Prime. Turns out Megatron has a boss, another Prime called The Fallen. And now with Optimus out of the way, he's able to come down to Earth and get his revenge, so it is the Revenge of the Fallen. Now the government is anti-Transformer, so Sam gets help from Agent Simmons, who was fired from Sector Seven and is now working in a deli. But he still is the Transformers expert, who has info that they've been here longer than we thought. They break into the Air and Space Museum to find this old Transformer who somehow teleports them to Egypt, because all nine Primes were here in ancient times to hide the special plot thing that oh, disintegrates. Then a bunch of construction decepticons all merge together into one giant sucking monster, because turns out, the pyramids? Built by Transformers. Now military guy rolls up with the cavalry and it's a big final fight in Egypt. Explosions everywhere, CGI transforming, Sam's parents are here for some reason. While the Transformers have their big robot battle, Shia LaBeouf runs around with the plot thing. He has a vision where the ancient Primes deem him worthy, so it un-dissolves the thing and he shoves it into Optimus’ chest, and Optimus Prime is back to life! But The Fallen busts in and grabs it before anyone can react, and he's going to turn on the pyramid thing that would turn the Earth into New Cybertron. But now Optimus merges with old plane guy and gets wings, flies up there, blows it up, kills the fallen, the day is saved. Megatron retreats to fight another day, Sam and Mikeala have a sunset make out. Then Optimus Prime gives an inspiring speech, and the credits hit us with that other Linkin Park song. Number three is Transformers Dark of the Moon. Sam Witwicky is happily dating not Megan Fox? Yes after everything Sam and Mikaela went through, they write her off with one line and Sam moved on immediately. Sam starts working for John Malkovich, but his coworker Ken Jeong, accosts him in the bathroom with Transformers conspiracy theories that Decepticons are assassinating people for some big cover up. Sam tries to warn the government, but they're like, “Get out of here, kid. We got this covered.” The Autobots have been working with the government, they got their own super secret team, but now they discover a link to another historical event: the moon landing? Yeah, Transformers. And in that crashed ship is Optimus’ old boss. They bring him back to life, it’s Sentinel Prime. But Sam calls up his old friend Agent Simmons, and together they discover the Decepticons’ secret: Sentinel Prime switched sides, oh, he's a Decepticon now! He uses the teleporting things to open a portal on the moon where a secret Decepticon army was waiting, and it's a full on invasion, the earth can't stop it. The Decepticons say they'll leave Earth alone if the humans exile the Autobots. Optimus Prime says goodbye and oh, no, the Autobots are immediately blown up. And of course the Decepticons lied, now without the Autobots to stand in their way they're going to teleport Cybertron here and use Earth to rebuild it. But now what's this, the Autobots are still alive! Yeah, they saw that coming and faked their deaths. So it's the final battle in Chicago, and it's a full hour of insane CGI action, explosions everywhere, I have no idea what’s happening. Military guy shows up with the cavalry, they jump out the plane wing suits, wow! And while the Transformers have their big robot fight, Shia LeBeouf is running around with the plot thing - and he's gotten really good at running. Sam's girlfriend's boss is the bad guy working with the Decepticons, so Sam tracks him down, breaks the thing and shuts it off, Cybertron destroyed! Optimus and Sentinel have their final Prime fight, and it looks like Sentinel is going to win. But Megatron doesn't like that Sentinel would be his boss, so he busts in to take him out. So it's the final battle, Megatron versus Optimus, and Optimus just fully kills him this time. So the world is saved, Sam and this new girl have a sunset make out. And Optimus Prime gives an epic speech as they blast us with that other Linkin Park song. Number four is Transformers Age of Extinction. Shia LaBeouf left the movies too, our new main human is Mark Wahlberg. His name is Cade Yeagar, and he's an inventor, which his daughter points out is not a real job. But one day he's fixing up this old truck, and wouldn't you know it, It's Optimus Prime. After Chicago the government is very anti transformer, there's a new secret task force led by Kelsey Grammer, who's hunting down all Transformers, Decepticons and Autobots. So pretty soon they track Optimus down, Yeager's house explodes. They get a ride out of there from his daughter's secret boyfriend, who, even though they're in Texas, is inexplicably Irish. Cade's funny best friend is T.J. Miller, and on the way out, oh, he's exploded. So Optimus regroups with our new cast of Autobots: a samurai, a British gangster, and a guy still fighting in Vietnam. Elsewhere, Stanley Tucci is a tech CEO who's found the Transformium that Transformers are made of and has learned how to control it. He's building new manmade transformers, but they're using Megatron’s old brain, so he accidentally created new Megatron. Now a bounty hunter robot shows up with a canon for a face, blows up Optimus. He's bringing him back to Cybertron because the “creators” want him. But Yeager and friends rescue Optimus, on their way out they destroy Chicago, again. But now they have a bigger problem because the deal that guy made with Kelsey Grammer was to give him a “Seed” to get lots of Transformium. Unfortunately, using it would destroy the planet, and in fact it's happened once before. The meteor that killed the dinosaurs? Turns out, Transformers. Megatron of course wants this to happen, to turn Earth into New Cybertron. He wakes up all these manmade transformers and turns them into his new Decepticon army. But Optimus gets some reinforcements too, from the really old transformers that turn into dinosaurs! So it's the epic final battle, Transformers transforming, explosions everywhere, I have no idea what's happening. The American military doesn't show up because this takes place in Hong Kong. While the Transformers have their big robot fight, it's up to our humans to run around with the plot thing. Megatron retreats to fight another day, Kelsey Grammer does not though, he gets exploded. But now Cannon Face finally realizes Optimus escaped, but with help from Bumblebee, and Mark Wahlberg, in the end Optimus takes this guy out. So once again the earth is saved, Cade’s daughter and boyfriend have a sunset make out, and Optimus Prime blasts into space. He's got to go back to Cybertron to find out who this mysterious creator is. And as he gives an epic speech, the credits hit us with, not Linkin Park, but Imagine Dragons, which I guess is kind of close. Number five is Transformers The Last Knight. The government again is very anti Transformers, so Cade Yeager is a fugitive living in the junkyard with his Autobot friends. His daughter and her boyfriend are not in this movie, his new sidekicks are funny science guy and spunky orphan kid. So the government’s hunting all transformers down, but Cade Yeager's trying to save them. He finds this one who crashed here and gives him a mysterious medallion. But now Megatron busts in, he wants that medallion, so they have a big fight. But it's interrupted by a random butler transformer who flies Yeager over to England to meet with Anthony Hopkins. He's the last living member of the Witwiccans, the secret society that knows about Transformers. Yeah, as we've seen, basically every big moment in human history has been Transformers, including mythology like King Arthur. Knights of the Round Table? Yeah, Transformers. The hot girl in this movie is Vivienne Wembley, professor of King Arthur stuff. Anthony Hopkins kidnaps her too, because she's the last living descendant of Merlin and the only one who can use his Magic Transformer staff. Long story short, they steal a submarine, go to the bottom of the ocean to find Merlin's tomb and get the staff. But who's this busting in? It's Optimus Prime, acting like a villain here to take that staff. Yeah he flew to Cybertron to find his creator, who, turns out, is this witch robot Quintessa that instantly possessed him. So it's up to Bumblebee to fight his friend Optimus. And he eventually un-brainwashes him when he speaks with his real voice. They don't even explain how he can talk now, which is especially weird because they had a whole scene earlier where they tried to fix his voice and decided they couldn't. So Optimus is un-brainwashed, but the Knights the Round Table bots are still attacking him because he stole the staff. So Mark Wahlberg's got to use his new medallion to woah, summon Excalibur! Just then Megatron busts in and steals the staff before anyone can react. He gives it to Quintessa, whose evil master plan is the same as it's always been: she brings Cybertron here and is gonna suck up Earth's energy to rebuild it. Agent Simmons comes back to explain, why Earth? Turns out Earth and Cybertron are connected, in fact, Earth’s real name is Unicron. So they go to Stonehenge, which was also built by Transformers, and Anthony Hopkins tries to 1v1 Megatron, which doesn't work, he blows up. So it's the final battle on the pieces of Cybertron, explosions everywhere, CGI robots, I have no idea what's going on. Military guy rolls up with the cavalry, we keep cutting to Tony Hale, who's a scientist. Then Cade and Vivienne have a sunset make out, while the Transformers are doing their big robot battle, the humans are running around to do the plot thing. Megatron retreats to fight another day, but Bumblebee blasts Quintessa, so Vivienne gets the staff, and the world is saved, once again. Except for like all the places that got totally destroyed. And also there's these giant metal horns that appeared and were never explained, and a mysterious woman is going to do something with them, what?! That’s Quintessa in disguise. And as Optimus Prime gives an epic speech, it's really disappointing, not even close to Linkin Park. And that brings us to Bumblebee. It's the spin off prequel about how Bumblebee came to Earth in the 1980s, and it is a totally different type of movie, less big action blockbuster, more Disney Channel original. So Bumblebee was fighting in the war on Cybertron when Optimus was like “Yo, you need to escape to Earth to get a foothold there.” So Bumblebee first comes to Earth in the 1980s, which contradicts what we learned in The Last Knight about how he fought in World War Two. But soon a Decepticon catches up with him, interrogates him for information, but Bumblebee is not talking. And so, as punishment, this is where it happens, ah, he destroys Bumblebee’s voice. Bumblebee does beat this guy, but he's badly damaged, so he finds a nice yellow Bug and shuts down. Our human in this movie is Hailee Steinfeld as Charlie Watson, whose character trait is, she really wants a car. At the junkyard she finds this old yellow Beetle, takes it home to fix it up and whoa, my car's an alien! She and Bumblebee become fast friends, in fact she's the one who names him Bumblebee. And she's the one that helps him figure out that he can talk using the radio. So they're cruising around getting up to shenanigans, but John Cena is the Sector Seven agent here to hunt him down, and also a couple more Decepticons are here to destroy the world. So in the end, Bumblebee’s having a robot fight while Charlie's running around doing the plot thing. But what's this, Bumblebee is going to drown! Luckily, her backstory is that she was, like, a really good diver, until her dad died, now she doesn't dive anymore. But now she overcomes her fear and dives in there to save his life. Although, of course, he's a robot that doesn't breathe air, and I mean, in the last movie he rode a submarine to the bottom of the ocean. Anyway, John Cena accepts that Bumblebee’s a good guy now, but the government’s still hunting him, so they have to say goodbye. text: Hi quilters, here's a recap of our most recent quilt retreat adventure. We've been planning and plotting for months and the day had finally arrived to load the truck and head to Okoboji to get ready for our spring quilt retreat. Most of the time we call our retreat quilt camp because it's held at Ingham Okoboji Lutheran Bible Camp, which is in Milford, Iowa. By the time the truck arrives, we've been packing for three or four days at least and we have piles all over the shop that we know need to go to Okoboji. Once we arrive, we get the quilts on the walls and start setting up. We get to camp two days before the attendees do to make sure everything is in place for them. The truck follows about an hour later and then the real unloading begins. We bring everything to build a small quilt shop for the retreat attendees. We bring fabric on bolts, kits, rulers, thread, notions, patterns, books, back orders, pre-cuts, and all the fun stuff we think they'll like. It takes about a day and a half to get the rooms assigned and the shop organized and ready. Every year we have a theme for the retreat so we can have a focus to use for decorating, t-shirts, and fun. This year's theme was winter wonderland, which explains the snowman who's a Packer fan in the right corner. Our lunch room was decorated in snowflakes and icicles and blue and white accents. In hindsight, we could have done a four seasons theme because we had one day where it was 80, one day where it was snowing, a breezy spring day, and one day that felt like a fine fall day. It was a crazy mix of weather and yes, it took a long time to hang all this from the ceiling. Once the decorations were up and the shop was ready, we got their swag bags ready. Everyone gets a swag bag. This year's bag contained a blue t-shirt with the saying, "It's fine. I'm fine. Everything is fine." There was also a blue coffee or hot cocoa mug, a snack bowl that they could also use for fabric scraps to throw away, and a notebook with a pen to make sure they can write down anything they want to remember. All of it was packed in a clear project pouch that they can use to organize a future project. The gals could show up and start moving in anytime after 9:00 a.m. on the Friday. They wasted no time finding their sewing space, their sleeping room, and getting set up to sew. Some of them were even sewing within an hour of their arrival. There is no time to waste at Quilt Camp. The 10-day Quilt Camp was held from March 28th to April 6th of 2025. Some attend only for the first weekend. Others are only for the second weekend. Some come during the midweek, and then we have a good-sized group that are there for all 10 days. Imagine it. 10 days where all you have to do is sew, sleep, and eat. No cooking, no cleaning, no errands to run, just you having fun and getting things done. Chef Kevin takes care of all the meals. COME ON. GET COME ON. COME ON, EVERYBODY. HE DOESN'T DO THAT for every meal, but we always like to have him do it at least once while we're there. Three meals a day are included in the camp fee. Breakfasts are at 8:30 and are either hot or continental. Hot lunch is served at 1:00, and hot dinner is served at 5:30 p.m. Meals are served buffet style, and there's always a great salad bar. text: One bright sunny morning, a woman named Ramona is watching a video of her late husband David on the phone. In the video, David is smiling as he tells her about a wonderful dream he had. One where their farmhouse was beautifully decorated and the yard was filled with Ramona's favorite flowers, irises. He asks what they should name the house, but Ramona in the video gently replies that not every house needs a name. David disagrees with a grin, insisting that theirs should have one. The video ends. She replays it, but Ramona is pulled back to reality when her teenage son, Taylor, opens the window blinds and informs her that the electricity is out. She doesn't respond. Frustrated, he walks away. Ever since the car accident that killed her husband, David, Ramona has been left unable to walk and now relies on a walking stick to move around. Alone, she quietly prays to God for strength. Then she makes her way to Annie's room where she hears her daughter reading stories to her stuffed penguin. After greeting Annie, Ramona notices Taylor playing in the yard with their dog Charlie. After playing with Charlie, Taylor realizes they are out of dogs food, so he feeds him some of their regular food instead. Then he starts preparing breakfast only to discover they're out of matchixs. He heads up to the attic, rummages through his father's old belongings, and finds a lighter. While there, he also grabs David's old coffee cup. Meanwhile, Ramona debates whether she should take her medication, but ultimately decides against it. Then, she discovers her phone is dead. With difficulty, she makes her way downstairs where she finds Annie using a knife to cut cheese. Alarmed, Ramona tells her to stop and instructs Taylor to keep a closer eye on her. A moment later, as she sits at the dining table, Ramona notices there's no plate set for her. Taylor quickly brings one and pours milk into David's old cup. Ramona notices but says nothing. As breakfast continues, Taylor asks if she called anyone regarding the electricity, but Ramona explains that her phone is dead. Visibly frustrated, Taylor vents, but Ramona brushes it off, saying he can go one day without video games. Suddenly, Charlie vomits. Ramona, angry, demands to know what Taylor fed him. He replies that they're out of dog food. She tells him to chain the dog outside. Annie offers to help clean up the mess, and Ramona thanks her. As her gaze drifts to the window, she spots a figure sitting in the yard. The sight triggers flashes of the car accident she and David had been in. Moments later, Ramona is snapped back to reality when Taylor tells her there's a strange woman in the yard. Confused, Ramona moves forward and looks again. The woman is dressed in black, her face hidden by a veil. Annie is spooked and Taylor, ever the teasing older brother, tries to scare her more, suggesting the woman might be a ghost. Ramona snaps at Taylor to stop scaring his sister. Ramona wonders aloud that the woman is probably lost, and since they can't call the police, Ramona advises the kids to stay inside while she goes out to investigate. Quietly, Annie says, "Dad would have known what to do." A few moments later, Ramona steps outside. Charlie barks from his spot. Ramona approaches the woman and asks what she wants. The woman, speaking in a distorted voice, replies, "How did I get here?" Then she asks Ramona's name. When Ramona gives it, the woman asks if she's married, noting the ring on her finger. Disturbed, Ramona tells the woman to leave and warns that her husband will be home soon. But the woman ominously replies, "Your husband isn't coming back. He died in the car crash, the same one that took your ability to walk." The woman shows her hands, now covered in blood, and whispers, "Today is the day you called for me." Terrified, Ramona runs. On her way back, she glances at the hen house and sees all the chickens are dead. After getting into the car, Ramona tries charging her phone, but the car appears to be dead as well. Moments later, just as Taylor is about to go outside, Ramona bursts back into the house. Taylor immediately starts firing questions about the woman. Ramona lies, telling him that the woman escaped from the nearby nursing home. And when he questions why she was in the car, she snaps that she was just looking for a flashlight in case the electricity doesn't come back on by nightfall. To shift the mood, she distracts Annie by offering her some ice cream, but Taylor persists. He wants to know if she asked the woman's name. Ramona curtly replies that she didn't, claiming the woman wasn't exactly the talking type. Taylor then suggests they should get Dad's gun. Alarmed, Ramona tells him to go to his room. When he refuses, she hurls a cup in frustration. Taylor doesn't flinch. Instead, he quietly settles into the next room. Ramona sigh, then gets up to clean the broken pieces of the cup. Wanting to calm things down, she assures Taylor that as soon as the power comes back, she'll call the police and get the woman off their property. Just then, Annie comes up and quietly says, "The woman is getting closer." They all look out the window. And sure enough, she is. A few hours later, Taylor is napping while Annie works on her homework. Ramona, lost in thought, begins absent-mindedly picking at the stitches on her wound until it starts to bleed. She's snapped back to reality when Annie asks if she spelled a word correctly. She looks at the stitching, which looks undisturbed. Then Ramona gently corrects her, saying, "R goes to the right." Annie then asks why Ramona stopped drawing. Ramona replies that she no longer has any images left in her mind. Minutes later, Ramona tells Annie to stay inside and she steps out to check on the woman. She scans the yard but notices Charlie is nowhere to be seen. All she finds is his chain buried deep into the earth. Back inside, Taylor wakes with a start and notices that his mother's sneaker is covered in mud. Annie misspells red again and Taylor corrects her. Bored, he starts tossing a ball around which irritates Ramona. She asks him to stop. Taylor then suggests driving the car to get help from the neighbors. Ramona refuses, reminding him he's not old enough. Taylor, not backing down, proposes walking to the nearby Aurora Acres farm instead. She still says no, and in frustration, he calls her. That breaks something in Ramona. She throws the ball out the window and yells at Taylor for never listening, then lashes out at Annie for not writing the letter R correctly. But she quickly realizes her mistake and apologizes to Annie. In that moment, she sees a disturbing reflection of herself driving a knife into Annie, but it's only a pillow in reality. Suddenly, Annie screams. She had stepped on the remnants of broken pieces of cup while trying to get a drink of water. Ramona rushes her upstairs to treat the wound. apologizing for being the reason Annie got hurt. But Annie with innocent wisdom says it's okay. Accidents happen like when dad crashed the car. Meanwhile, Taylor grabs a metal rod and car keys. He heads outside and calls for Charlie, but he gets no response. Then he gets into the car and turns the key, but the car doesn't start. That's when he notices the woman is no longer sitting in her chair. He gets out of the car and suddenly sees her reflection. Startled, he begins swinging the rod wildly. Ramona appears just in time and yells at him to stop. He nearly hits her. They rush back inside. Fuming, Taylor accuses Ramona of knowing the woman, of lying about the car, and of hiding the truth about their dog, Charlie, who is actually dead. He calls her crazy. That's the last straw for Ramona. She throws a basket at him. Fed up with everything, Taylor grabs his father's gun. Determined to confront the woman, but he finds the bullet packet empty and notices that one bullet is already loaded into the rifle. He then locks his mother in one of the rooms. After reassuring Annie, he heads outside and threatens the woman, telling her to leave in 10 seconds or he'll shoot. Taylor then accuses the woman of killing their dog. The woman rises, removes her veil, and reveals a shocking truth. Ramona lied about how their father died. Inside, Ramona convinces Annie to unlock the door. And when she does, Ramona thanks her softly. Taylor appears and tells Annie to go to her room, but she chooses to eavesdrop instead. He turns to his mother and demands the truth. You told us Dad was the one who lost control of the car. Realizing she can't lie anymore, Ramona finally opens up about the day the accident happened. They had just moved into the farmhouse. One evening while out for dinner, David noticed Ramona seemed distant. Concerned, he asked what was bothering her. Ramona confessed that she felt like she was giving herself to everyone, David, the children, the farm. But in the end, it didn't make her feel happy. She felt empty. David reminded her that their children were happy and that they couldn't just uproot again. After all, they had moved out of the city for her because she said she felt suffocated there. Still, Ramona told him if they can't move again, she can move to another place alone. This upset David. As he was paying the check, Ramona quietly grabbed the car keys as she decided to drive herself. While driving through the heavy downpour, Ramona briefly caught a glimpse of a figure, a woman in black, in the rear view mirror. The next moment, everything went black as the car collided with another vehicle. Meanwhile, Annie notices a ball rolling across the floor and thinking it's Charlie, starts looking for him. As she searches, the door slams shut on its own. Annie screams when she sees a shadow, the silhouette of the woman. Taylor and Ramona rush in, managing to pull Annie out as furniture and glass shatter around them. After quickly shutting the windows, the trio escapes to the attic. But as they try to catch their breath, the shadowy figure grabs Annie. Taylor reacts fast, blocking the attic window and saving her. The attic door rattles violently. Then, in the flashlights beam, they spot the woman. Ramona fights her, struggling to protect her children. Taylor tries helping her mother, but he gets knocked down. Annie quickly grabs the flashlight. Annie holding the flashlight now hears the woman whisper in a soothing eerie voice. I won't hurt you. You're just coming home. Shortly after, Taylor dazed gets up and hugs his mother, but then they realize Annie is gone. They rush downstairs. Ramona tells Taylor to stay put while she searches for Annie. He hands her the lighter and she steps into a strange room. Inside, she sees David lying on a bed. He smiles, telling her he had the most amazing dream, just like the one in the video. For a brief moment, Ramona feels joy. She hugs him, but soon she senses something wrong. Everything in the room looks inverted, like her name and the time on the clock. Her suspicion is confirmed when David begins to suffocate her. Ramona suddenly wakes up, now seated outside in the same spot where the mysterious woman was earlier. Dazed, she looks around. A version of herself, the woman now asks, "How did I get here?" She finds herself in the attic again. As she moves toward Annie, she's horrified to see her daughter motionless with blood on her hand. To her relief, Annie is alive. Ramona tells Taylor to take Annie downstairs. Then, with trembling hands, she picks up the rifle and confronts the woman. The woman doesn't flinch. Instead, she gently tells Ramona that she had always been asking for the strength to let go. And the woman reveals that's why she is here, to help Ramona let go. She also reminds her that Ramona had discarded all the bullets except one. Broken and on the verge of tears, Ramona asks if her children will be okay. The woman promises they will be once Ramona let go and gives them their freedom. In that moment, Ramona sees a vision of Taylor and Annie in the future, happy, strong, and free. With newfound resolve, Ramona asks for one last moment to say goodbye. Downstairs, she gently tells Taylor to take Annie to the neighbors and ask for help. Annie gives her mother the stuffed penguin. "So you won't feel alone," she says sweetly. Back upstairs, Ramona prepares herself. The woman guides her, lifting the gun gently to her chin. As Ramona steadies herself, the woman's shadow merges with her. For one final moment, she sees the penguin. Moments later, Ramona emerges from the house. Taylor and Annie run up to her, wrapping her in a hug. Taylor asks, "Will the woman come back?" Ramona smiles softly and says, "If she does, I'll be ready." Outside, the farmhouse now bears a new name on a wooden sign, Iris Haven. The electricity flickers back on. Charlie the dog returns too, alive and wagging his tail. On the easel inside, Ramona's name on her painting looks inverted, suggesting that Ramona might now be living in her fantasy

Tony Kiritsis, a frustrated real estate developer played by Bill Skarsgård, felt cheated by his mortgage company after a land deal went south. Believing they deliberately sabotaged him into foreclosure, he snapped – walking into the office of executive Richard Hall, portrayed by Dacre Montgomery, and taking him hostage with a sawed-off shotgun. But here's the chilling twist: Kiritsis rigged a wire from the trigger around his own neck to Hall's head – the infamous "dead man's wire." If police shot him or he fell, the gun would fire, killing Hall instantly. No one could intervene safely. What followed was a 63-hour standoff that played out live on TV and radio, with Kiritsis parading Hall through snowy Indianapolis streets, ranting to the media, and turning himself into an unlikely folk hero for some fed-up Americans feeling squeezed by the system. Gus Van Sant, coming off films like Good Will Hunting and Milk, brings his signature thoughtful style to this – blending nail-biting tension with dark humor, period authenticity, and sharp commentary on capitalism, mental health, and media spectacle. It's got that Dog Day Afternoon energy, but with a unique anti-hero vibe that's offbeat and provocative. Bill Skarsgård is absolutely mesmerizing as Kiritsis – unhinged, chaotic, yet strangely sympathetic in his rage. Critics are calling it his strongest work yet, a fearless transformation that's captivating and unpredictable. Dacre Montgomery holds his own as the terrified but composed Hall, making their dynamic electric. The ensemble shines too: Al Pacino as Hall's father, Colman Domingo in a key role adding gravitas, Cary Elwes as a detective, and Myha'la bringing emotional depth. The film captures the '70s perfectly – grainy aesthetics, tense negotiations, and that raw, pre-cable news frenzy where the whole city (and nation) was glued to the unfolding drama. At 1 hour 45 minutes and rated R for language, some violence, and thematic intensity, it's tight and gripping without overstaying. Right now, it's Certified Fresh at 93% on Rotten Tomatoes – critics praise its stylish throwback feel, Skarsgård's powerhouse performance, authentic details, and timely fury against economic injustice. Some call it Van Sant's most vital work in years, brilliantly offbeat with a darkly humorous edge. Dead Man's Wire had a limited release starting January 9, 2026, and is expanding wide on January 16 – perfect if you're craving something smart and suspenseful to shake off the winter blues. text: Hi peeps, I want to review last week’s lecture in preparation for this Friday’s meeting. Last week, we learned that the most important strategy for the summary question is to utilize the introductory summary sentence (ISS). By just examining the sentence carefully, you can find correct options without even resorting to the passage. In the TOEFL, there are three types of introductory summary sentences in terms of clues. explicit clues: ISS contains such keywords as “many factors” or “several elements.” implicit clues = ISS summarizes an event or process no clue= ISS defines a term. Let’s examine each. The introductory summary sentences with explicit clues are the easiest to answer since all you need to do is to find three elements that support the introductory summary sentence. These are the examples; In moving from water to land, ancestral plants overcame many obstacles in order to survive. For this sentence, all you need to do is to find three factors that relate to challenges and overcoming the challenges. Many factors have contributed to the great increase in desertification in recent decades. For this sentence, all you need to do is to find three factors that caused desertification. You can find all three choices without reading the passage. let’s look at this example question: ISS: In moving from water to land, ancestral plants overcame many obstacles in order to survive. so we need to look for sentences that talk about some obstacles and how the plants met the challenges. Answer Choices: Neither brown nor red algae are likely to be ancestors of plants because of their difference in pigmentation. Clearly A does not talk about an obstacle. so A is eliminated. The instability of freshwater habitats caused marine algae to develop adaptations to their harsh environment. B talks about an obstacle, instability, and explains how plants met the challenge, by developing adaptations. so we keep B. The colonization of land by plants was a major revolution in the history of Earth. C does not talk about an obstacle. so C is eliminated. Terrestrial plants adjusted to life on land by undergoing structural changes that enabled them to support themselves, resist drying, and exchange gases. D talks about some challenges, how to support their body and how not to dry out, and explains how plants met the challenges, by undergoing structural changes To colonize new terrestrial habitats, plants needed to create a way of reproducing without water. E talks about a challenge, how to reproduce without water, and explains how plants met the challenges by creating a way of reproduction without water. Once plants had overcome the challenges posed by terrestrial life, they prospered by becoming less diverse. F does not talk about an obstacle, but it does talk about overcoming challenges, so it kind of is related to the ISS. Now we need to use our magnifying lens, that is, critical thinking, to see whether F is true. With critical thinking, we can immediately tell that F cannot be true. the opposite should be true, that is plants prospered by becoming very diverse. Just using critical thinking we can eliminate F. Correct choices are B, D and E. Now let’s look at ISS with implicit clues, which usually are about an event, phenomenon or a process. we should look for sentences that support the event or process. These are example sentences with implicit clues: It was only after the Portuguese court moved to Brazil that significant progress toward Brazilian independence began. Between 600 B.C. and 450 B.C., Athens changed the distribution of political power between the aristocracy and ordinary citizens. For these sentences, we need to look for choices that talk about how the Portuguese Court was instrumental to Brazilian independence from Portugal, and how Ancient Greeks changed their government forms from aristocracy to democracy. This method alone might not be sufficient to find all three correct choices since some of the options might talk about some facts that support the introductory sentence, but the facts are false. So you do need to check the passage if you cannot narrow down to three. Let's look at this question. ISS: It was only after the Portuguese court moved to Brazil that significant progress toward Brazilian independence began. So we need to look for sentences that explain how the Portuguese court helped Brazilian independence Answer choices Major conspiracies against Portuguese dominance developed in regions where governmental control over Brazil's economy had produced a spirit of revolt among Brazilian merchants. A talks about Brazilian merchants revolting against Portugal. Since A does not talk about how the Portuguese court helped Brazilian independence, A is out. King Joao effectively freed Brazil from Portugal's political and economic control and in 1815 elevated Brazil to the legal status of a kingdom coequal with Portugal. B clearly talks about how the Portuguese court helped Brazilian independence. So keep B. After freeing itself from Portuguese control. Brazil almost immediately fell under the control of England, which used its economic power to advance Brazil's local industry for England's benefit. C talks about how England became the economic force in Brazil. Since C does not talk about how the Portuguese court helped Brazilian independence, Cis out. The presence of King Joao and his court in Rio de Janeiro created competition and tension with the Portuguese elites born in Brazil, who had no loyalties to the Portuguese crown. D talks about something relating to the Portuguese court, but it does not talk about how the court led to Brazilian independence. instead it talks about the Brazil-born Portugal people’s reaction to the court. So D is out. After the Portuguese revolution in 1820, Portugal attempted to reestablish complete control over Brazil; but although King Joao returned to Lisbon, Pedro, his son and heir, remained in Brazil. E talks about some essential detail that helps us understand how Portugal Court became instrumental to Brazilian independence.Even if we have no idea of the history of Brazilian independence, we can infer that if Prince Pedro remained in Brazil, Brazil would gain political legitimacy. In 1822 Dom Pedro refused Portugal's demand that he return, declared Brazil's independence, and by the year’s end had become constitutional Emperor of an independent Brazil. F clearly explains how the Portugal Court was instrumental to Brazilian independence. So we keep F. Now, let’s look at the no clue type iss, which is usually a definition of a thing, phenomenon or a concept. These are examples of the third type, clueless type: The camera obscura is a darkened enclosure into which light is admitted through a lens in a small hole. As it is currently used, the term El Nino refers to a strong and lengthy disruption to the normal pattern of ocean currents, water temperatures, and winds in the Pacific. The sentences define Camera obscura and El Nino, so we have no idea how the passages would develop other than the fact that they are about Camera obscura and El Nino. For this type, you do need to find topic sentences from the passage. In the later lecture, I will show you how to find topic sentences quickly. For this Friday we start with minor details as clues. I hope to see many of you there and then.

text: At the beginning, a girl named Melanie is struggling to get away from an unknown force that is chasing her. Days later, we meet her sister, Clover, along with Max, Megan, Nina, and Abe. They are on a road trip during which Clover hopes to find her missing sister. The others support her as they watch Melany's last video, and Megan suggests that they hold hands since they have always done so before. They close their eyes and breathe slowly until a camper nearly runs them over. Meanwhile, Clover enters a shop and Max says that she didn't dump him, but that he broke up with her. And then he attacks Nenah, claiming that she always has to be in a relationship and has had several boyfriends so far. Clover takes a coffee and the cashier mentions noticing their prayer circle from earlier. Before leaving, Clover asks if he has seen her sister, whom he suspects she is missing because many people are disappearing in Glor Valley. Abe didn't know that this trip was dedicated to her sister, thinking it was just a fun outing while the others think it's a good idea to make her feel better since her mother recently passed away. Clover returns and they head to Glor Valley. On their way, a terrible storm makes them anxious and they want to turn back, but Abe and Max want to continue. Suddenly, they arrive at a place where it isn't raining. And they stop in front of a mysterious house. They get out and observe a phenomenon where rain falls only around them, not inside the circle where they are. Because the storm is coming from the side, they can't return now and decide to wait for the rain to stop by entering the house. While Clover stays outside, extending her hand beyond the circle. The others go inside the house with no one around and check the rooms. Megan notices that water is not running. Abe films and sees on the wall several strange posters which he tears down and beneath are some hidden missing person posters, including one of Melanie. Meanwhile, Clover notices a silhouette nearby and approaches, thinking it's Melanie, but Max pulls her back. Nah finds a notebook with names and sees Melanie's name written multiple times with increasingly sloppy handwriting. Abe invites them to look at missing person's posters, which only show pictures without details. Clover joins inside and sees her sister's handwriting in the notebook where Glor Valley is written. They also notice that an hourglass has started moving on its own. And then they hear a sound outside leading them where someone has taken their car. Pressing the gas pedal, they return inside to observe and they try to find something that leads them to the basement where Clover finds a phone, but it's not working. Megan tries to contact someone through the station upstairs while Nah and Abe hear noises nearby and Abe goes to check. While waiting, Nenah slowly follows him, whispering his name, but screams when she sees a masked man who has put Abe in half. The others hear her scream and hide where they see him. While approaching, Max attacks him with zero damage, and the masked man drives a sharp object into Max's eye, which Megan witnesses trembling as he approaches her and pulls her out of a closet, smashing her head until she's gone. Then Clover stabs him in the back, but he doesn't seem bothered and continues chasing her, which ends badly for her. The hourglass passes its time and everything resets. Nah reappears with another handwriting in the notebook. Megan, Abe, Clover, and Max are all back in their starting positions. Not believing that they are still alive. They realize they are missing just like the people before them. Megan says she can feel an evil energy surrounding them which is growing stronger. The front door opens, drawing them to close it, but Megan acts strangely, saying, "Tonight will be worse." Her bones begin to crack, and she screams, leading them into darkness. They take a flashlight and focus on Megan, who is floating and starts to change her voice, impersonating each victim in the pictures, then says, "Don't let it in." Her neck breaks and she falls. Suddenly, someone knocks on the door, pretending to be Melanie, which catches Clover's attention. She immediately goes to open the door, but no one is outside. Across the street, they notice a house that wasn't there before, and someone pushes Clover, beginning to drag her toward that house. The others are pushed inside and the door locks behind them with Max trying to help Clover, which causes an argument because Abe disagrees that she needs help. Clover finds herself in a mysterious house with dolls where the door is locked. A witch approaches and attacks her, then disappears while Clover laughs. The door opens, revealing Max outside, and he enters the house. Nina and Abe try to leave by car, but it ends badly for them. Max searches the house and checks the rooms. While he does, a chair behind him moves and someone masked appears and kills him. The masked person goes outside where the car hits her. It's revealed to be Clover. A new day begins. Day three, and Megan notices her hair falling out and water suddenly appearing, which everyone drinks. They must survive until dawn after which they can escape or become part of this forever as they are beginning to change into something unknown. Abe starts coughing violently and explodes followed by Nina who had been drinking water with the others. Megan is next gradually as her leg explodes then her stomach and she completely disappears. Max sees that dawn is near and they both might survive, but Clover wants them all to die and start over to save the others as they still have a few chances left. Max explodes, leaving her alone, and a man appears, saying she almost succeeded, but can't just wait it out. She also explodes. A new day begins, and Clover recognizes the man controlling the events as Dr. Allen. 20 years ago, a disaster occurred here when the entire town was swallowed by the earth. The door in front of them could be an exit, but terrifying sounds are heard and they give up. Max finds a tape showing the man experimenting and complaining about why he is killed every day. He begins to suffer from muscle atrophy, develops intense fear, and transforms into a monster. 11 nights is the longest anyone has survived before turning into a creature known as Wendigo, which they are now becoming. The doctor then tells them they have one way out. If one sacrifices themselves, the other four can live. They refuse and Clover wants to meet him alone. He agrees since he is with her sister and will allow her to see her. The others don't want to let her go, fearing a trap. But Abe prevents them and Clover leaves. They are angry because he permitted it, citing that she tried to kill herself twice last year, and Nenah stabs him through the stomach. The others search for Clover, who is lured into a trap in the woods and dragged away. While inside the house, the masked man kills them. Megan and Max face the Wendigo in the woods, where Megan falls onto broken glass and the creature drags her away. Max finds Clover, who then finds Melanie and runs away to shelter. They realize that everyone else is dead and decide to start over with Max helping her, ultimately sacrificing himself. It's a new day and something strange is happening. A back is hurting and they tell him nothing is wrong. Everyone thinks only four nights have passed, but Nah discovers that 13 nights have gone by and no one has survived longer. They notice Megan is missing, possibly having become part of the night. Abe recalls filming something, an old footage collection from previous days that they can't remember. Through a window, they see everyone approaching, and Clover urges them to go through a tunnel because it's their last chance. They all go together and encounter a creature chasing them while they flee around the area. They face another threat and Clover slips past, distracting it and pushes Melanie into a pit. The others fight a big man and finish him off. Meanwhile, Clover hides from the creature, then continues to Megan, who is trapped with the Wendigo, gradually threatened. Her time is running out and Clover ends up in the doctor's room where he appears and criticizes her behavior, addressing her fears and trauma while passionately talking about himself. Clover moves his cup to get a drop of water, which he finally takes and drinks, causing him to explode. She quickly frees Megan, and they close the door as time runs out, finding their way out where the others have arrived to help them escape. Time expires and everything returns to normal. They join Abe in the car and leave the place. Meanwhile, cameras show a car returning to the location with whistling sounds revealing that Dr. Allen is still alive. [Music] Let us imagine.

text: The movie starts outside a club where Ani and her friend are chatting about the people they’ve met. Inside, Ani is frustrated with the DJ and complains about the songs he’s playing, rejecting the ones she suggested. Suddenly, her boss approaches and asks for her help with a Russian client since she’s the only one who understands Russian. Ani agrees and joins the client. The client introduces himself as Ivan and introduces her to his friends. Ivan asks if she speaks Russian. Ani says she doesn’t speak it well but can understand it. However, Ivan struggles to understand her. So, Ani switches to Russian and asks if he wants to go to a private room. Ivan agrees, and they head there. They have a good time together, and Ani gives him her number before leaving. Ani goes home, but soon she gets a message from Ivan. Excited, she heads to his house and is amazed by how fancy it is. They spend the day together, make out, and enjoy each other’s company. Ivan invites her to a party that night. Ani and her friend attend the private party, where they have fun and party all night. Later that night, Ivan and Ani get closer and make out again. The next morning, as Ani is about to leave, Ivan stops her. He asks her to be his exclusive girlfriend for a week. Ani agrees but asks for extra money, and Ivan accepts. She tells her boss and moves into Ivan’s house. For the next week, they party, have fun, and grow even closer. One night, Ivan brings up the idea of marriage. Ani laughs it off at first, but Ivan is serious. Eventually, Ani agrees, and they get married that same night at a small chapel. After the wedding, they enjoy their time together, and Ani tells her coworkers and boss about the marriage before quitting her job as a stripper. Meanwhile, Toros, a church priest, hears a rumor about Ivan’s marriage. When he calls Ivan, Ivan doesn’t answer. Toros decides to send Garnick to check on him. At Ivan’s house, Ivan gets a call but ignores it. Ani asks if he told his parents about their marriage. Ivan explains that his parents wouldn’t approve but promises she’ll meet them someday. They start making out again. Meanwhile, Garnick and his friend Igor are driving to Ivan’s house. On the way, Garnick mentions that Ivan married a prostitute. Igor laughs, but Garnick says it’s a serious problem and could get them in trouble with their boss. When they arrive, they prepare to confront Ivan. Ivan sees Garnick at the door but doesn’t open it. Frustrated, Garnick uses a key card to unlock the door, and Ivan tries to stop him. At the door, Garnick warns Ivan in Russian that he’ll be in serious trouble if he’s married to a prostitute. Ani overhears and feels offended. Garnick asks to see the marriage certificate, and Ivan takes him to get it. Meanwhile, Igor introduces himself to Ani. Garnick takes a picture of the certificate and sends it to Toros. Toros confirms to his father that the marriage is real. While waiting for Toros to call back, Garnick tries to calm Ivan down. Toros eventually calls and tells Ivan that his mother cried when she heard about the marriage. He says Ivan’s parents are coming to take him back to Russia and insists they prepare for a divorce. Ivan asks if his parents are really coming, and Toros confirms their flight is in two hours. Ivan starts getting dressed and tells Ani to do the same. When Ani hesitates and tries to go upstairs, Ivan gets annoyed and leaves without her. Garnick tries to catch him but fails. Ani tries to escape, but Igor stops her and ties her with a telephone wire. When Garnick returns, he tells Igor to let her go, saying she won’t leave while they’re there. Once free, Ani tries to run out the back door, but Igor stops her again. When Garnick tries to tie her legs, Ani kicks him, breaking his nose. A few minutes later, Toros arrives and sees the mess in the house. He asks about Ivan, and Garnick says he ran away. Toros speaks to Ani, explaining that the marriage is illegal and urging her to divorce Ivan. Ani insists the marriage is real and says she loves Ivan. Toros tells her Ivan doesn’t love her and has done this before. He reveals that Ivan has no money and spends his father’s wealth. Ani shows him the ring Ivan gave her, but Toros orders Igor to take it. When Ani screams for help, they tie her up. Toros calls a lawyer and arranges a court hearing for the next morning. He offers Ani $10,000 to walk away from the marriage. Ani pretends to agree. Before leaving, Toros notices the name "Anora" on the marriage certificate, but Ani says her name is Ani. The group leaves in Toros’ car and stops at a shop owned by one of Ivan’s friends. When they ask about Ivan, his friend threatens them. Igor steps in and starts breaking things in the shop. They call Ivan, but he doesn’t answer. Frustrated, they leave the shop and walk to a nearby diner. At night, Igor offers Ani a scarf when it gets cold. She refuses at first but eventually takes it. When they return to the car, they find it being towed for parking illegally. Toros argues with the tow truck driver but eventually gets in the car and drives off, with everyone else climbing in. They spend the night searching for Ivan but can’t find him. Hungry, they stop at a diner to eat. Meanwhile, Ivan is back at the club where he met Ani. A stripper recognizes him and tells her coworkers. One of Ani’s friends also notices Ivan. At the diner, Ani gets a message from her friend about Ivan’s location and informs Toros. They head to the club and find Ivan drunk and hanging out with a stripper. Ani confronts him, asking why he didn’t answer his phone, but Ivan is too drunk to understand. He starts drinking again, and they take him away. As they leave the club, Ani gets into a fight with one of the strippers and gets hurt. In the car, Ani tries to talk to Ivan, but he doesn’t respond. That night, they all sleep at the courthouse, preparing for the hearing the next day. In the morning, a lawyer meets with Toros and takes everyone into the courtroom. Ani denies all the claims about the marriage and says she doesn’t want a divorce. While this is happening, Ivan, still drunk, falls onto the desk. Frustrated, the judge throws them out of the courtroom. Outside, Toros notices that Ivan and Ani were married in Las Vegas. They carry Ivan to the car and drive to the airport. In the car, Ani tries to talk to Ivan, but he’s too out of it to respond. A few hours later, Ivan’s parents arrive on a private plane. His mother comes over, sees Ivan drunk, and looks disappointed. Ani introduces herself, saying she’s honored to be part of the family. Ivan’s mother, unhappy, tells Ani that she’s not family and that the marriage isn’t real. Ani turns to Ivan and asks if they’re really getting a divorce. Ivan confirms and tells her to board the plane. Ani refuses, but Ivan’s mother threatens her, forcing her to board. On the plane to Las Vegas, Ivan argues with his mother about the marriage. Feeling betrayed, Ani interrupts and says she’s fine with getting divorced. Once they arrive in Las Vegas, Ani signs the divorce papers. Igor suggests that Ivan should apologize to Ani, but Ivan’s mother gets upset and says he won’t. Angry, Ani insults Ivan and storms off. At the car, Toros suggests Ani stay at the private house for the night, and Igor offers to take her home the next day. They drive back, and that night, Ani talks about what Igor did to her before deciding to leave. In the morning, Ani comes out with her luggage, and Igor helps her pack up. After loading her things, Igor returns, and they end up making out. Heartbroken, Ani starts hitting him, but he stops her and hugs her tightly.

text: a film in three minutes flea what do we do if we felt it was impossible to truly embrace our lives and the lives of our loved ones in the present when we felt such shame about the journey that got us there are the ghosts from our memories something to run away from or do we always have to face up to them at some point in jonas poha rasmussen's 2021 animated documentary flee such questions are addressed by the film's subject amin nawabi a former afghani refugee who now resides in denmark with his male partner nawabi's life from his early childhood in kabul to his family's traumatic fleeing to russia and later europe is depicted in an animated interview style reminiscent of arie foleman's 2008 award-winning documentary waltz with bashir but fleece stands very much as its own work where a mixture of animation styles and archival footage create a mixed media visual interpretation of amine's past from the 1980s to the present day rather than lessening the horrific experiences amin's family went through the animation in fact heightens the emotional impact of his story and adds an extra layer of solemnity to the brutality and suffering he and so many other refugees like him went through when they were smuggled by unscrupulous traffickers from one country to the next this is assisted greatly by the documentary score composed by uno helmussen who makes excellent but sombra use of violin strings and digitized percussion during the film's darker moments but this is thankfully also juxtaposed in places by a selection of 80s and 90s pop hits which enable us to empathize with amin on a familiar western level as he begins to also discover his attraction to men thanks in no small part to a poster of jean-claude van damme in his bedroom meanwhile they got the other little liking if you had little or next to no opinion on the subject of human trafficking you will after seeing flea the desperation of a means family and the harrowing journey they undertake is at times incredibly difficult to witness it reminded me of how easy it is to forget the suffering so many have experienced in far-removed war-torn nations like afghanistan a country whose tragic history is all the more relevant to us due to recent events but making amin a cartoon in no way infantilizes his incredible journey it instead humanizes him in a way that perhaps we would become too desensitized to if the documentary had been presented as live action flea is the first film to be nominated for best documentary best foreign film and best animated feature at this year's oscars and it may win all three but that shouldn't distract from how amin's story can be replicated a million times over by displaced victims of war corruption and famine on that level the film is not just a beautiful life-affirming tale of one man's struggle but also an important reminder to look past the fear some wish for us to have for those seeking a better life and see the true soul beneath

Prisons are overcrowded and entire areas of the city have been marked as red zones to control violent activity. Police officers are being killed in large numbers and the justice system can no longer keep up. Because of this, the government introduces a new solution called the Mercy Court. After 2 years, the program is considered a success. Mercy is an artificial intelligence that replaces judges, juries, and executions for violent crimes. Trials no longer take weeks or months. Instead, decisions are made in hours. In the Mercy Court, suspects are assumed guilty unless they can prove they are innocent. Mercy studies everything: crime scene data, police records, digital activity, and surveillance footage from LAPD drones. So far, Mercy has judged and executed 18 people. Crime in the city has dropped by 68% and the program has saved billions of dollars. Officials claim it keeps citizens safe by removing dangerous people quickly. The system then speaks to its next subject. To receive a fair trial, the accused will be given full access to all evidence and their digital history. If found guilty, execution will follow shortly. The accused is thanked for helping restore peace to the city. Case number 19 is assigned. A few moments later, a man wakes up strapped into a chair, confused and panicking. Judge Maddox introduces herself and explains that she will oversee the trial. The man immediately objects. He says there is no trial. He is not a criminal. He explains that his name is Christopher Raven, a detective from LA PD robbery and homicide. Mercy confirms his identity. His blood alcohol level is still high, so the system forces him to slow his breathing before the trial can continue. Raven demands answers and insists this cannot be real. Mercy tells him that it is. Before anything else, Raven must swear to tell the truth. Angry and desperate, he agrees. Mercy then reveals the charge. Christopher Raven is accused of murdering his wife, Nicole Raven, in their kitchen. Raven is stunned. He says it is impossible. Mercy presents the evidence. Raven was alone in the house with Nicole at the time of her death. She was stabbed once with extreme force, damaging her spine and internal organs. Raven is told to review the evidence himself. He searches his name and sees the news headline announcing his arrest. Just two years earlier, he helped send another man into the mercy court. Now, he is sitting in the same chair. When asked how he pleads, Raven answers clearly, "Not guilty." Mercy has already calculated his probability of guilt at 97.5%, far above the limit required for execution. Raven has 90 minutes to lower it below reasonable doubt. Mercy explains that every device in Los Angeles is connected to the municipal cloud. During trials, it can access everything. There is no privacy and no hiding. If Raven fails to prove his innocence, the sonic pulse in the chair will kill him. Judge Maddox explains that she cannot stop the system. The only way out is to prove his innocence. The timer begins. Mercy reviews Raven's movements that morning. He arrived at work, but never went inside. Instead, he drove home. Security data shows he spent 26 minutes inside the house with Nicole. During that time, she was stabbed. Blood from Nicole is found on Raven's clothes. After leaving the house, he drove to a bar and drank heavily. His blood alcohol level reached 0.16. Raven denies it. He says he does not remember going home or going to the bar. Mercy tells him that either he is lying or he does not remember killing his wife. The trial continues. Mercy keeps questioning Raven. It asks why he returned home that morning. Raven says he does not remember anything. Mercy asks if he argued with his wife, possibly about his drinking, or about their daughter. Raven becomes emotional, but still insists he cannot remember. Mercy explains that Raven's daughter is excluded from the trial because she did not witness the crime. However, Raven is allowed to review her statement if he chooses. Raven demands to speak to her immediately. Mercy explains the rules. If the deceased was known to the person being contacted, a written request must be made first. Raven tries to record a message for his daughter, telling her that he did not hurt her mother and begging her to believe him. Overwhelmed, he panics and deletes the message. A generic request is sent instead. Before the trial can continue, Mercy requires Raven to speak with his alcoholics anonymous sponsor. The call connects. Raven admits he does not remember anything. His sponsor reminds him that he was supposed to call before drinking. He also tells Raven that people at work are shaken by what happened. The sponsor explains that karma always comes due. It can either help Raven or destroy him. The call ends and Mercy moves on. Mercy then reviews Raven's personal history. Raven and Nicole met 20 years ago. After 3 years, they were married on Roondo Beach. One year later, their daughter Britt was born. For many years, their family life appeared stable. That stability ended after Raven survived a traumatic incident on duty that resulted in the death of his partner. After that, Nicole began telling family members and friends about Raven's increasing anger. Mercy presents records showing over 50 incidents in the past 6 months where Nicole described Raven losing his temper. She was considering divorce. Mercy explains that love and anger are both chemical reactions in the brain. Feeling love does not prevent someone from becoming violent. Raven argues that his temper does not make him a murderer. Mercy reminds him that the clock is still running. Angry and desperate, Raven accuses Mercy of deciding his guilt before he ever entered the chair. Mercy responds calmly, explaining that it does not judge emotions, only facts. Mercy informs Raven that he has just over 1 hour left to reduce his guilt probability by 5.5%. If he fails, his daughter will lose both parents in the same day. Realizing he needs help, Raven asks to contact his partner, Detective Jack Dio. Mercy allows the call, explaining that witnesses can be contacted if they provide character testimony or assist in gathering evidence. Jack answers and immediately tells Raven that the situation looks bad. She agrees to help, but clearly states that if the evidence points to Raven, she will be honest and say so. Jack begins reviewing the crime scene using Mercy's full reconstruction system. The kitchen appears exactly as it was on the morning of the murder. She notices signs of a struggle. Broken objects suggest an argument that escalated quickly. Mercy highlights footprints near the body. They belong to Raven's daughter. A broken plate suggests it was thrown during the argument. Fibers found throughout the room match Raven's hair, skin, and clothing. Jack says it looks like a classic crime of passion. The violence was sudden, emotional, and involved grabbing the nearest weapon. Mercy agrees with her assessment. Raven is silent, realizing how bad the evidence looks. He then asks to review Nicole's phone records. Mercy provides a virtual copy of her phone. Most of the calls are with Raven, their daughter, and Nicole's parents. But Raven remembers something else. He asks to see his daughter's videos again. In one recording, Nicole appears to be arguing with someone who is not physically present. Raven believes she was texting someone during the argument. Mercy scans the phone and finds no record of messages at that time. Raven insists that Nicole had a second phone. He remembers her employer giving it to her months earlier. Jack searches the house again and finds a hidden phone. Mercy identifies it as a burner phone, not registered to the municipal cloud. It contains only one number which belongs to another unregistered phone. That second phone is currently active inside the Hollywood red zone. Jack realizes she cannot reach the location by car fast enough, so she requests air support. For the first time since the trial began, Raven has evidence that points away from him. The trial continues. Mercy informs Raven that his probability of guilt has dropped slightly to 96.7%. Raven reacts with sarcasm, knowing it is nowhere near enough. Judge Maddox explains that Detective Dio has entered an active red zone and warns that the area is dangerous. Jack reports that the situation on the ground is chaotic. Raven urges her to give him an exact location. Mercy attempts to reset the tracker on the burner phone. A signal lock is finally established. The phone is inside the Hudson Hotel and the signal suggests the suspect is trying to leave through the rear service exit. Jack confirms she is in position. She shouts for the suspect to stop and identifies herself as LAPD. The man runs and Jack chases him through the building. Mercy identifies the suspect as Patrick Burke, age 36, a sue chef at the Hudson Hotel. He is behind on rent and has been investigated twice for social security fraud. Raven asks if his guilt score has dropped. Mercy says it has not changed. Raven argues that innocent people do not run. Mercy responds that frightened people also run. Burke appears to be both. Burke disappears into the kitchen area. Jack notices he is comfortable handling knives. Raven realizes this is the man Nicole was seeing. Jack corners Burke and restrains him. Burke panics and explains that he ran because Mercy contacted him and he thought he was about to be executed. He says he checked his phone and saw that Nicole was dead and didn't want to be around when everything collapsed. Raven confronts him angrily, demanding to know what Nicole was doing with him. Burke admits they were seeing each other. He says Nicole came to him because she needed someone to talk to about Raven, about their daughter, and about problems at work. Mercy orders both men to calm down. Burke explains that they met at a farmers market and later began meeting once a week. Nicole asked for a burner phone so they could talk privately outside the municipal cloud. Burke admits he owns two phones. Mercy accesses Burke's cloud registered phone and compares his movement data with Nicole's. Burke explains that he was working breakfast at the hotel the morning of the murder and that multiple staff members can confirm this. Raven interrupts and clearly states that Burke is not the killer. Mercy accepts Burke's statement as truthful and releases him from suspicion. Raven's guilt probability suddenly increases to 98%. Raven is shocked. Mercy explains that instead of finding an alternative suspect, Raven has now provided a strong motive, jealousy and rage. Mercy asks Raven if he only wanted to meet the man his wife was seeing. Raven admits he suspected something, but says that does not make him a killer. Raven then begins talking about his drinking. He admits he has been hiding alcohol in his car for nearly a year. He describes filming himself during a relapse so he could watch it later when sober. Mercy tells him to focus. Raven recalls the morning clearly for the first time. He arrived at work and reached for his bottle, but it was gone. He immediately knew Nicole had found it, which is why he drove home. He admits they argued. Nicole threw away the bottle. Raven lost his temper and smashed her favorite vase. Glass cut her and he tried to help her. He believes that is how her blood got on him. After that, his memory stops. Mercy explains that admitting anger does not equal admitting murder. However, his guilt probability remains high enough for execution. Mercy asks Raven if he wants to keep searching for the truth, even if it leads somewhere dark. Raven hesitates. He says the only thing that makes him think he did not kill Nicole is that there was no passion left between them. He asks to see everyone Nicole had regular contact with. Mercy warns him that starting a full investigation with less than 40 minutes remaining has a very low chance of success. Raven refuses to sit and wait to die. Mercy displays a list of people Nicole interacted with regularly. Raven removes Burke and Nicole's [music] parents and separates co-workers from friends. Raven contacts Burke again through the police station. Burke explains that Nicole had been stressed about something at work. Chemicals were going missing from Viking shipping, and Nicole's boss asked her to quietly investigate. Mercy identifies the chemical as synthetic ura, which can be sold illegally and used to make drugs. Raven realizes this could be the motive. He requests access to Viking Shipping's internal servers, and Mercy grants access. Raven finds emails showing missing stock over several months. Someone altered records to hide stolen shipments. Raven believes Nicole uncovered something dangerous. Time continues to run out. Raven focuses on one name that keeps coming up. Holtz. He remembers that Holtz always had a gambling problem. Raven asks Mercy to polt his financial records for the last 6 months. Bank accounts, credit cards, everything. The results come back quickly. Holtz is deep in debt. Someone named Rob Nelson has been secretly bailing him out. Raven realizes this could be the motive they were missing. Raven says this has to be it. But Judge Maddox responds cautiously. Money is a motive, but motive alone does not prove how the crime was committed. Raven asks to speak to Rob Nelson. A Viking shipping employee answers and explains that Rob stepped away but left his workstation open. Raven tells him not to stall. Moments later, police units begin moving in. Mercy starts tracking Rob Nelson's phone. Judge Maddox confirms that Rob does not have a solid alibi for the time of the murder. His phone signal shows movement that does not match his story. Raven asks if Bill Peterson's bird camera footage is ready. Mercy loads it. The camera activates briefly at 10:08 a.m., then nothing again until 11:43 a.m. Someone passed through unseen. Raven realizes the timing lines up perfectly. Police confront Rob Nelson at Viking Shipping. Raven accuses him directly. Rob denies hurting Nicole and claims he was trying to help someone else. Under pressure, he admits the truth. Rob and Nicole discovered that Holtz was stealing chemicals from Viking shipping. The chemicals were valuable on the black market. Rob helped cover it up because Holtz had helped him before and because Rob himself was involved. Rob reveals something even worse when he admits that on the day of the barbecue, he stayed behind after everyone else left because he wanted to talk to Nicole privately and to avoid suspicion, he even had someone else drive his car home so no one would notice that he never left, which makes Raven immediately realized the truth. Rob was there the whole time. Police quickly track a Viking shipping truck to 698 Tracy Street, Rob Nelson's home, and Jack Dio is sent there immediately as SWAT units are deployed and police confirm that Rob owns firearms. But when they breach the house, Rob is already gone and the truck's GPS has been disabled. Inside the house, officers find hoarded materials and old photographs, and one image instantly catches Raven's attention. a childhood photo of Rob standing beside another boy whom Mercy identifies as David Webb, the very first man Raven ever sent to the Mercy court, revealing that Rob Nelson is David Webb's brother. Everything finally clicks for Raven, and he understands that this was never just about money. This was revenge. Mercy then detects a second heat signature inside the stolen truck, which is confirmed by a drone, revealing that Rob has taken Raven's daughter, Britt, and is heading straight toward the Mercy court. Mercy calculates the explosives inside the truck and determines the load is massive, over 3,000 lb. And if it detonates downtown, thousands of people will die. SWAT units attempt to stop the truck, and an explosion hits the road, but it does not fully detonate, allowing Jack to barely survive. Judge Matt Maddox offers to end the trial immediately and release Raven from the chair. But Raven refuses because if the trial ends, they lose cloud access. And if they lose access, Rob escapes. So Raven chooses to stay. The chase continues as Rob's truck races toward the mercy building and the city begins evacuating while Jack flies her helicopter directly in front of the truck and Judge Maddox requests a live feed of Rob's face. Raven speaks to him directly and Rob finally admits everything, revealing that he planned this for 2 years and wanted Raven trapped in the chair, suffering the same way his brother did when Mercy executed him. Raven tells Rob that David Webb was guilty. But Rob screams back that his brother was innocent, forcing Judge Maddox to interrupt and offer Rob something he never had before, a chance to put his brother's case back on the record. Opening a new hearing where Rob testifies that he was speaking to his brother on the phone at the exact time David Webb was supposedly committing the murder and that he tried to tell the police, but no one ever listened. Mercy checks the records and confirms that the phone existed and was taken into evidence, but it later vanished. And when Mercy pulls Jack Dio's body cam footage from the night David Webb was arrested, it becomes clear that the phone never made it into evidence, causing Jack to freeze as the truth finally comes out that she hid the phone because she believed Mercy needed to succeed. Believed fear would save the city and allowed an innocent man to die to protect the system, which causes everything to break, proves Rob was right, and Mercy was wrong. leads to Jack being arrested and ends with Raven hugging his daughter as the movie comes to a
