text: In a bleak alternate version of 1970s America, governed by a strict dictatorship, an annual endurance event called the long walk takes place. Young contestants referred to as walkers are required to keep a minimum pace of 3 mph, 5 kmh with a penalty of death if they fall below the limit. Ray won a lottery which granted him access to participate in the contest. So his mom drove him to the starting point of the walk. On getting there, she was hesitant to let him go because his father was killed participating in the same competition. Cry was the first person Ry made friends with. And as they both got in, they got acquainted with the other 49 walkers. Not long after, the major arrived at the scene. The major instructed them to come out and receive their tags on hearing their name while the others remain still and not move a muscle. After everyone finished collecting their tags, the major then explained to them why this contest is being held in the first place. According to the major, the country has been struggling financially since after the war. So, the first long walk was carried out to reintegrate the value of work ethic as there's always a spike in production after the event of event each year. The major swore to make the country great again. Then he stated out the rules of the contest, which are walkers are to walk till there's only one person left. They're to maintain a speed of 3 mph, and they get a warning if they fall below the speed. They also get an additional warning if they can't make speed in 10 seconds. Three warnings and they get executed on the spot. The contest ends when there's only one walker remaining alive, for which they receive a grand cash prize, and also one wish allowing them to get whatever they want. After listing out the rules, the major commenced the contest by shooting his gun in the air. The walkers began their journey immediately with a major and his crew by their side to enforce the rules. On getting to mile 5, some of them started getting tired, so they drank their water to replenish their lost strength. After walking for a couple of hours, a walker named Curly suffered a cramp in his leg, which caused him to slow down, resulting in a warning. Few others started walking backwards so as to motivate Curly, "Get up and keep walking." Curley was fortunate to continue walking before the third warning. But he now needs to walk 3 hours without getting another warning as he has exhausted the initial three he was given. While they were going, Ray told the walkers with him that this long walk isn't voluntary as they think. Rather, the system had them back to a corner and then pointed the long walk is the only way out, so they basically don't have a choice. One of the walkers took down the names of everyone in their tags. And when asked why, he revealed he's writing a book about the long walk from an insider's point of view, and it's bound to make him rich. On spur of moment, Curley develops a Charlie horse in his leg on the way and was about to stop, but Ray and Cry helped him continue walking for the meantime. Curley soon gave up as he couldn't endure the pain no more, and he ended up being the first walker to be executed. The others went into instant shock as it now knew the gravity of the situation they were in. On getting to mile 17, Gr urged Ray not to think about the end of the walk, but the next moment, insisting that's the only thing that can make them go longer without getting tired. Few minutes later, another walker ranked number one fell down and started convulsing. Unlike the others, Barkovich made fun of him and after a while, number one became the second person to be eliminated. Barkovich urged the other walkers to be happy when anyone dies as it increases their survival odd, but none of them were having it. One of the walkers on Ray's team developed a Charlie horse, so the rest of the team had to slow down their speed a little to give their comrade time to revamp. Elsewhere in the line, Barkovich tried his best to get another walker named Rank annoyed. Rank fell for his trick and started attacking him, not knowing he was given a warning for each time he attacked. When he eventually exhausted his warning by attacking the third time, the soldiers at the back executed him on the spot. The entire group shunned Barkovich for eliminating rank on purpose. Even some of them threatened to kill him as revenge, but Barkovich was only slightly bothered by their threats. As the walk progresses, one of the walkers needed to take a [ __ ] so bad that he couldn't walk anymore. So, the soldiers shot him mercilessly after his third warning. On getting to mile 35, the major congratulated them on making it this far without getting killed. And by that time, the first night was already fast approaching. Ry had flashbacks of the good times he's had with his mom. But in reality, he had fallen asleep for hours, and the flashbacks were in his dream. Ray mistakenly tripped and fell, which resulted in him getting a second warning. It was at this moment he crashed out and cries for helping him, insisting everyone wants everyone here to die, so he should stop pretending. They soon got to a steep road that requires additional strength to climb, and a good number of them were eliminated on that very road because of the difficulty. Ray didn't allow the things happening around him to bother him. Rather, he maintained focus and kept on walking as fast as he could. Ry almost slacked off, but McFry came through for him with a helping hand. Mry helped Ray till he was able to catch his breath and maintain his pace. Ray asked about the other member of his crew only to find out from that they were all eliminated. It was finally the second day of the long walk, but the total number of walkers have drastically reduced to 18 out of 53. Number 49 leg got twisted on the way, so he couldn't carry on any longer, resulting in his immediate execution. Barkovich was indifferent as usual and as he got into a little altercation with Fries, he promised he'll craft out plans to make sure he ends up dead. The major once again congratulated them walkers for making it to 100 miles, encouraging them their grand cash prize awaits them at the finish line. One of the walkers attempted running away, but was shot dead on the spot before he could. It was raining heavily when night approached. Ray rested on Cry's shoulder just so he could get some sleep, but Mcry, on the other hand, never seemed to get tired. Number six took a slight break to take [ __ ] but he was fortunate enough to get back up and continue the walk before his final warning. Asked Ry if he thinks he'll win the walk, and it was at this moment Ry revealed why he needs to win. According to Ry, his dad was the kind of man who thought him all sorts of things, including things the government had banned. So, on a faithful day, some soldiers stormed into their house, dragged his father out, and took him to receive judgment from Major. The major, after recounting his crimes of teaching banned ideas, gave him an option of pledging his allegiance to the state, but he refused. So the major then shot him dead in front of his family. Ray confessed he has harbored hatred for the major ever since that day. And if he ends up winning the contest, he's going to request for a carbine and use it to assassinate the major as revenge. Levise tried his best to convince Ry otherwise, insisting that it's not as easy as he thinks it is to take another man's life. He further told him that is socked as he gets tired, he intends to stop and wait to die. On getting to mile 170, a large portion of the walkers started losing their [ __ ] One of them tried to fight a soldier but ended up crushed to paces by a tank. Another one of them took of his clothes and started walking in another direction which earned him his ticket to the afterlife. Olsen wasn't himself anymore as he started hallucinating. As night approached, Ray unearthed Olsson was in a very bad state. So, he got closer to ascertain what the problem was, but Olsson was already long gone and couldn't even hear anything Ray was saying. All of a sudden, Olsen headed back and attempted to attack a soldier who eventually shoots him in his leg and leave him to bleed out slowly as punishment. Baker rushed back immediately to help him. But seeing time was running out, Ray dragged him to keep walking so he won't get eliminated also. They made it to mile 209 on day four, but out of 53 people who started this walk, only six of them were remaining alive, namely Barkovich, Gity, Stebins, Baker, Bri, and Parker. Parker revealed to the rest of the crew that Olsen was married and was the only Walker who was married. So they made a promise amongst themselves that the winner would give some of the grand prize money to Olsen's widow. Barkovich figured everyone left him out of the conversation. So riddled with guilt over Rank's death, Barkovich pleaded with Ry to accept him into the group. After a while of begging, Ry finally accepted him into the group. But then Barkovich started losing his mind as he kept on seeing Rank's dead body anytime he closes his eyes. The others try to comfort him by letting him know they've all forgiven him. And just when they thought everything was okay now, Barkovich turned and faced them, then stabbed himself to death with a spoon. The soldiers finished him off just to make sure he stays dead. On getting to mile 260, the walkers were remaining just five and they decided to entertain themselves with some music while walking. They eventually made it to Freeport and it was that Ray saw his mom sobbing and happy her son still alive. Due to intense emotions, Ray attempted to head back and hug his mother, but McFry was there to stop him just before he got eliminated. It was such a sorrowful moment for all the walkers and it made their hatred for the government intensify. To make Ry stop complaining and keep walking, Fry told him the story of how he has been walking his whole life and how he's always had it rough. However, on making it to the fifth day, Stebins, who had fallen very ill, urged the others not to help each other anymore so as not to prolong things. On spur of moment, Baker started bleeding through his nose. So, following the new rule, they just agreed on no one opted to help him out. Outraged, Parker vented his anger on one of the soldiers by shooting him. Then, he turned the rifle towards himself and ended his own life tragically. The others kept on walking like nothing happened, convincing themselves it was for their own good. As the walk progresses, Baker's condition kept on getting worse, and he could barely walk by himself. Baker was bleeding so bad he figured he has developed internal hemorrhaging. Ry and cries broke the rule by lending him a helping hand, but Baker had already had enough. So he pleaded with him to stop helping him, insisting that he can't take it anymore. He then gave Ray his cross to give to his grandma, after which he forcefully took out their hands and started walking backwards. And it was at this moment the soldiers granted him his ticket to the afterlife. Steban's illness grows more severe and realizing victory is impossible in his state, he confides in Gity and McVree, the reason he entered the contest. He is the illegitimate son of the major and had planned to use his prize to compel recognition from his father. He tells the two it has been an honor walking alongside them. Then halts and accepts death, leaving Gity and McVese as the final competitors. The duo reaches a town where spectators gathered to witness the outcome. McVree deliberately sits down, but Gity lifts him back up, urging him to continue. McVe obeys, unaware that Gity has now ceased moving. The major executes Gity and names McVree the victor. When asked about his reward, Mcfre demands a guard's rifle and shoots the major before turning away and continuing down the road. The movie then came to an end. Kindly subscribe for more movie recap like this. Thanks for watching and goodbye.

In the aftermath of the Korean War, a young couple and a weward brother find themselves entangled in a web of secrets, desires, and hidden identities. On Swift Horses takes us on a journey through 1950s America, where social constraints force people to live double lives while searching for authentic connection in a world that demands conformity. Through gambling dens, racetracks, and quiet suburban homes, the characters navigate their way toward what they truly want, even when society tells them they shouldn't. The complete story of Onswift Horses. The story begins with a song, Mr. Blue, setting a melancholic tone as we meet our three central characters. Muriel and her husband, Lee, are starting fresh in California after Lee's return from the Korean War. Lee's younger brother, Julius, also a veteran, has joined them. During Christmas celebrations, amidst happiness and drinks, Lee proposes that the three of them build a life together in San Diego, California. Julius seems hesitant, but agrees, and Lee makes Julius promise to join them. The brothers share a deep bond. During their military service, Julius had saved Lee's life in Korea by climbing onto a burning truck to throw ammunition down to trapped soldiers. Lee carries immense gratitude and love for his brother, seeing him as a hero despite Julius's modest dismissal of his actions. When Lee proposes a new start in California, Muriel accepts Julius as part of their new life. Though she seems to sense something different about him. However, plans quickly change. Julius, instead of joining them in San Diego, sends Muriel a telegram saying he's pursuing unexpected opportunities in Las Vegas. He sets off to make his fortune in the gambling world, breaking his promise to his brother. Julius finds work as a security observer at a casino where his job is to watch for cheaters from behind two-way mirrors. He's good at this because, as he admits, he knows how people steal because I've stolen in the past. In Las Vegas, Julius meets Henry, a fellow casino employee with a distinctive scar. Their connection is immediate and electric. Henry introduces Julius to tricks of their trade, showing him how the casino uses marked cards to ensure they always win. As their relationship develops, Julius and Henry dream of hitting it big through gambling and possibly escaping to Mexico together. Meanwhile, back in San Diego, Muriel and Lee buy a small house in a developing suburb. Lee works hard and Muriel takes a job at a cafe, but Muriel harbors her own secrets. She begins visiting the racetrack, developing an uncanny talent for picking winning horses. Through her winnings, she accumulates money that she hides from Lee in a coffee can. When Lee mentions wanting to buy furniture for their new home, Muriel surprises him with $3,000 she's won gambling, money that helps them secure their suburban dream. Muriel feels disconnected from the traditional housewife role she's expected to play. She writes letters to Julius who rarely responds. In her letters, she describes how their neighborhood is rapidly developing with houses going up fast around them, making her feel increasingly confined. She admits to Julius that she can't picture him living there because you wouldn't be able to breathe. During this time, Muriel meets Sandra, a neighbor who plays Spanish music on a mandolin. Their relationship begins innocently with Sandra selling Muriel eggs, but soon develops into something deeper. Muriel is drawn to Sandra's independent spirit and different way of living. Through their relationship, Muriel discovers a part of herself she never knew existed. Back in Las Vegas, Julius and Henry's relationship deepens, though they must keep it secret in the homophobic 1950s society. After witnessing the brutal consequences faced by gay men who are discovered, seeing a man's photo in the newspaper after being arrested in a gay bar, Julius becomes increasingly fearful. Despite his growing feelings for Henry, Julius resists Henry's suggestion that they cheat at the casino where they work, knowing the dangerous consequences they would face if caught. The story takes a dramatic turn when Julius reluctantly joins Henry in cheating at cards. Their scheme is discovered and they're ambushed by casino enforcers. Henry disappears and Julius is beaten. Worried that Henry has been killed, Julius flees Las Vegas, leaving behind the gun Henry gave him. He carries guilt and grief, not knowing what happened to his lover. Julius unexpectedly returns to San Diego, showing up at Lee and Muriel's home with a horse trailer and a horse he won in a bet. His arrival disrupts their carefully constructed lives. Lee is overjoyed to see his brother. But Muriel harbors mixed feelings. She has been changed by her experiences with Sandra and gambling, feeling a kinship with Julius's rebellious spirit while resenting his abandonment. During his stay, Julius and Muriel share quiet moments where they recognize something kindered in each other. Julius tells stories about a girl from their hometown who juggled relationships with two men, one passionate but unstable, the other respectable but boring. He suggests that the girl chose the unreal life of respectability over true passion. This story serves as a mirror for Muriel's situation caught between her conventional marriage to Lee and her passionate connection with Sandra. In a moment of vulnerability, Muriel reveals to Julius that she knows about Henry. She shows Julius the gun Henry gave him, which she somehow acquired, saying she plans to return it to Henry. Julius is shocked by her knowledge of his secret life. Muriel asks Julius for money to help her find Henry, essentially blackmailing him with the knowledge of his homosexuality. Their confrontation is heated with Muriel calling Julius a coward and a liar. The next day, Julius leaves without saying goodbye, taking his horse with him. Muriel, determined to find Henry herself, travels to Tijana, Mexico, where she believes he might have gone. There she tries to navigate the dangerous gambling world, losing the money she brought. She meets a man who claims to know where Henry is, but robs her instead. During her time in Tijana, Muriel has a powerful realization about herself and her desires. She writes a letter to Sandra expressing her feelings, though it's unclear if she ever sends it. Meanwhile, Julius, after leaving San Diego, also searches for Henry. He visits a gay bar and asks about Henry, describing his distinctive scar. The film culminates with both Julius and Muriel on separate journeys of self-discovery. Julius writes a letter to Muriel on Christmas Eve, apologizing for stealing from her and getting things so wrong. He expresses hope that she's found happiness, remembering her, saying, "Everybody deserves a chance to be happy. The letter suggests that Julius has found some resolution in his life, though we don't learn if he ever reunites with Henry. In the final moments, we see Muriel alone, suggesting she has chosen her own path, separate from both Lee and Sandra. The film ends with the lingering question of whether any of the characters have found what they were truly seeking, authentic love, and the freedom to be themselves in a society that demanded conformity. Understanding the ending of Onswift Horses. The ending of Onswift Horses intentionally leaves many questions unanswered, reflecting the uncertain futures of its characters. Julius writes a letter to Muriel expressing remorse and offering closure. But we don't know if the letter was ever sent or received. Similarly, Muriel's journey to Tijana ends with her alone, having lost the money she brought to find Henry. What's clear is that both Muriel and Julius have undergone profound transformations. They've broken free from conventional expectations. Muriel from the role of the beautiful housewife and Julius from the pressure to hide his sexuality. Though they may not have found exactly what they were looking for, they both claimed the freedom to choose their own paths. The film leads us to wonder, did Julius ever reunite with Henry? Did Muriel return to Lee, pursue Sandra, or choose independence? These ambiguities are intentional, suggesting that in the rigid social landscape of 1950s America, the journey towards self-discovery was itself a form of victory, even when complete fulfillment remained elusive. The deeper meaning, horses, gambling, and freedom throughout on swift horses, gambling serves as a powerful metaphor for both Julius and Muriel. Gambling represents a rebellion against predetermined outcomes. In a society that dictated rigid life paths, especially for women and gay men, betting on horses or cards was a way to assert control over fate, to believe in the possibility of beating the odds. Horses, too, carry symbolic weight. Swift horses represent freedom, the possibility of escape from social constraints. When Julius arrives with a horse he won in a bet, it embodies his wild, untameable nature. The horse exists outside the suburban landscape Lee and Muriel have created, just as Julius and Muriel's true selves exist outside societal expectations. The film also explores how people create secret identities to survive. Julius lives a double life in Las Vegas, working as a casino security person while engaging in a forbidden gay relationship. Muriel maintains the facade of a contented housewife while visiting racetracks and falling in love with Sandra. These secret lives allow the characters to breathe in a society that would otherwise suffocate them. The character journeys. Lee's character represents the conventional American dream of the 1950s. A war veteran who wants nothing more than a home, a wife, and eventually children. He embodies the ideals promoted in postwar America. His love for Julius and Muriel is genuine, but he fails to truly see or understand them. His dream of having his brother and wife together in their suburban home is ultimately revealed as naive, failing to recognize the complex desires and identities of those he loves. Julius struggles with his sexuality in an era when being gay was not just socially unacceptable, but actively dangerous. His decision to go to Las Vegas instead of joining Lee and Muriel in San Diego is driven by a need to find a place where he might exist more freely. His relationship with Henry offers him a glimpse of authentic connection only to have it ripped away. Julius's journey is one of accepting his identity and learning to navigate a world hostile to his existence. Muriel's transformation is perhaps the most dramatic. Beginning as a traditional wife, she discovers unexpected talents and desires, her gambling success gives her financial independence, while her relationship with Sandra awakens her to romantic possibilities beyond her marriage. Unlike many women of her era, Muriel actively chooses her path rather than simply accepting what society prescribes for her. Her decision to search for Henry, ostensibly to return as gun, reflects her deeper quest to understand the kind of love Julius experienced, a love outside societal norms. Henry remains somewhat mysterious, known primarily through his relationship with Julius. His scar physically marks him as different, matching his willingness to live outside society's rules. He is both more daring than Julius, pushing him to cheat at the casino, and more fatalistic, understanding the precariousness of their situation as gay men in the 1950s. His disappearance drives much of the latter part of the film, though whether he was killed or simply fled remains unclear. Sandra, like Henry, offers an alternative to conventional life. Her Spanish music and independent spirit attract Muriel, showing her possibilities beyond suburban housewifey. Their relationship develops organically from neighbor interactions to deep intimacy, though it ultimately faces the same societal pressures that threaten Julius and Henry. America in the 1950s, the historical context. The film vividly depicts post Korean War America, a time of economic prosperity and rigid social norms. The rapidly developing suburbs where Lee and Muriel live represent the standardization of the American dream. Identical houses filled with identical families living identical lives. This conformity offered security but demanded the suppression of difference. For women like Muriel, options were severely limited. Expected to be content as housewives and mothers, women who desired careers, independence, or non-heterosexual relationships had to either conform or live secret lives. Muriel's gambling and relationship with Sandra are acts of rebellion against these constraints. For gay men like Julius and Henry, the situation was even more perilous. Homosexuality was criminalized with police raids on gay establishments common. The newspaper article about a man arrested in a gay bar who later committed suicide reflects the real dangers faced by LGBTQ plus individuals. Their need for secrecy wasn't just social, but a matter of survival. Gambling occupies an interesting position in this landscape. Though technically illegal in many forms, it flourished in places like Las Vegas, representing America's complicated relationship with vice, risk, and reward. For characters like Julius and Muriel, gambling offers not just the possibility of financial gain, but a space where conventional rules could be temporarily suspended. The power of unspoken connections. One of the film's most compelling aspects is the unspoken connection between Julius and Muriel. Though not romantically involved, they recognize in each other a similar struggle, the conflict between societal expectations and authentic desires. Their relationship is complex, moving from affection to betrayal to understanding. When Muriel reveals she knows about Henry and shows Julius the gun, their conversation lacks explicit mentions of homosexuality, reflecting the era's inability to directly address such topics. Yet beneath the surface, they achieve a profound recognition of each other's true nature. Their conflict isn't really about money or the gun, but about honesty and courage in the face of a conformist society. Similarly, the film handles the romantic relationships between Julius and Henry and Muriel and Sandra with restraint. Physical intimacy is shown, but the deeper emotional connections develop through small moments. Henry teaching Julius about marked cards, Sandra playing mandolin music that reminds Muriel of her mother. These quiet interactions carry as much weight as more dramatic scenes, showing how meaningful connections can form even in restrictive circumstances. The circular nature of escape and return on Swift Horses explores how escape often becomes circular with characters leaving only to find themselves drawn back to what they fled. Julius leaves San Diego for Las Vegas, then returns to San Diego only to leave again. Muriel mentally escapes her housewife role through gambling and her relationship with Sandra, but physically remains in the home she shares with Lee until her journey to Tijana. The film suggests that true escape requires more than physical distance. It demands acceptance of one's authentic self. Julius and Muriel both struggle with this acceptance, alternating between embracing and fleeing from their true desires. The circular motions of the narrative reflect their internal struggles, the difficulty of breaking free from societal expectations even when physically distant from them. This circularity also appears in the structure of relationships. Julius leaves Lee and Muriel partly to avoid the conventional life they represent, yet forms a domestic arrangement with Henry. Muriel resents her expected role as Lee's wife, but creates a different kind of intimate relationship with Sandra. These patterns suggest that the desire for connection is universal, though the forms it takes may vary widely. The final message at its heart on Swift Horses is about the courage to pursue authentic identity in a world demanding conformity. The film doesn't offer easy resolutions or Hollywood endings where everyone finds perfect happiness. Instead, it presents the struggle itself as meaningful, the willingness to risk security for truth, to pursue desire despite the dangers. The final letter Julius writes captures this sentiment perfectly. Everybody deserves a chance to be happy. This simple statement becomes radical in a context where happiness was narrowly defined and available only to those who fit prescribed roles. By claiming the right to define happiness for themselves, Julius and Muriel perform acts of quiet revolution. Their journeys remind us that freedom often comes at a cost, that loving authentically sometimes means losing security, and that the path to self-discovery rarely follows a straight line. Yet the film ultimately suggests that these sacrifices are worthwhile, that the pursuit of authentic life and love, however difficult, matters more than comfortable conformity. In the end, On Swift Horses doesn't tell us whether its characters found lasting happiness. Instead, it honors their courage in seeking it on their own terms, recognizing that in some contexts, the search itself is an act of profound bravery.

text: Escape Room Tournament of Champions is about to hit theaters. So, to prepare, I'm going to dive into the first Escape Room and recap everything that you need to know before seeing the sequel. And just like a real Escape Room, I'm going to be doing it on the clock. So, let's start that timer and let's get into everything you need to know about Escape Room 1 in 3 minutes or less. Escape Room follows a group of strangers who were invited to take part in an Escape Room with a $10,000 prize. If you don't know what an Escape Room is, they're usually these elaborately designed rooms that you have to solve all the puzzles in to escape in a certain amount of time. Now, usually in real life, if you fail to escape the room in that set amount of time, you aren't brutally murdered, you're just forced to take a picture of yourself holding a sign that says you're a loser. So, the strangers in this Escape Room are Zoey, a physics student, Ben, a stock boy at a grocery store, Amanda, an Iraq War veteran with PTSD, Jason, a day trader, Mike, a truck driver, and Danny, an Escape Room enthusiast. The six strangers arrive at an office building and soon find that the game has already started. The office turns into an oven, which they manage to escape. Next, the group finds themselves in a freezing cabin, which eventually leads them outside onto a frozen lake. Unfortunately for Danny, he falls through the ice and drowns. The next room is an upside-down billiards bar. The longer it takes for them to solve the room's puzzle, the more pieces of the floor begin to fall away, revealing a seemingly bottomless chasm. Amanda ends up plummeting to her death before they can all escape. In a hospital-themed room, Jason uses a defibrillator to shock Mike to death in order to solve that room's puzzle. Jason immediately gets his comeuppance in the next room when he and Ben fight over an antidote to a toxin they've been poisoned with. Ben kills Jason and manages to escape, as does Zoey, who manages to trick whoever's running these games into believing she's dead and spring a surprise attack. Ben, as the official winner, meets the game master who explains that each year the mysterious Minos Escape Rooms Corporation lures a group of strangers to play these games, which are designed by a mysterious puzzle maker, while rich viewers bet on the outcome. The strangers always have something in common, with this group all having previously survived tragic disasters. Zoe survived a plane crash, Ben survived a car accident, Amanda survived an IED blast, Jason survived a shipwreck, Mike survived a mine cave-in, and Danny survived when his family died of carbon monoxide poisoning. And now that this particular game was over, the game master tries to kill Ben. Luckily, Zoe's ruse worked and she shows up to save Ben and together they kill the game master. A freed Zoe and Ben try to alert the police about this crazy murderous game, but when the police investigate the building, it's been completely cleared out. Six months later, Zoe alerts Ben that all of the deaths from the escape room have been covered up as accidents. But, she thinks she's figured out where Minos Corporation is located and wants Ben to come with her to Manhattan to take them down. And so, the two hop on a plane to Manhattan, but little do they know that the plane they're getting on also happens to be part of Minos's evil plan. Suspicion turns into fear as he pulls out her knife. Linda flees into the jungle. A violent struggle follows. She tries to strangle him with shoelaces, but Bradley fights back, ripping out chunks of her hair. She cuts him. He goes for her eyes, but Linda refuses to stop. In a desperate move, she swallows Zuri's ring. Bradley is moments away from killing her when Linda stabs him with a fork. Bradley escapes to a location Linda once warned him about. There he discovers a hidden mansion on the island. Inside he drinks heavily, thinking he is finally safe until he hears Linda's voice. She is watching him through CCTV cameras. Panicked, Bradley begins smashing the cameras, but Linda continues speaking from the control room. She confesses everything. She reveals that she could have been rescued much earlier, but chose not to leave. After the island's caretaker disappeared, she found the mansion and lived comfortably in isolation, enjoying the power and control she never had before. She admits she stayed because she wanted this life and because she [music] wanted Bradley with her. Linda then admits she killed Zuri. When Bradley reaches her, Linda is waiting with a gun pointed at [music] him. Bradley breaks down, apologizing for everything he did to her. He claims he finally understands her and says the outside world no longer matters to him. He suggests [music] they stay on the island forever together. Linda appears to calm down. When Bradley tells her he loves her, she almost believes him. Then Linda notices something off. One of the bull statues in the room is missing a horn. In that instant, Bradley attacks. He tries to shoot her, but the gun is empty. Linda fights back and kills him with a golf club. Sometime later, Linda is living a completely different life. Her survival story has gone viral. She is wealthy, [music] respected, and successful, now writing a self-help book inspired by everything she endured. In the end, Linda doesn't just survive the island. She finally takes control of her life on her own terms.

text: Our series today is about a student who has been tormented by cruel bullies throughout his school years, forcing him to change schools frequently. But his life is about to take a turn when he moves to a mysterious new town. Do you think he will finally be able to stand up for himself? If you want to know what happens, let's dive into the summary together. Our story starts in a classroom where a teacher is disciplining three students for talking during his lecture. These three are notorious bullies in the class. The teacher is angry because their pronunciation is not standard enough, and he angrily beats them with a stick in front of their classmates until the stick breaks, making them look ridiculous. The other students can't help but laugh quietly at the site. Sure enough, this doesn't end well for them. As soon as the bell rings and the class ends, the three bullies who were disciplined head to the bathroom. They follow the students who laughed at them and proceed to give them a good lesson, beating up everyone who dared to chuckle. At that moment, our hero, a teenager named Taye, walks towards them. Everyone thinks he's there to protect the weak, but he's actually just there to use the restroom. The bullies, however, don't let him off the hook. They remember that he also laughed, or at least was fighting hard to hold it in, so they grab him and beat him up as well until he passes out. Taye collapses in despair, lying on the ground, not knowing when this painful life will ever end. We see through flashbacks that since childhood, he has always been the target of bullying. He gets beaten for the most illogical reasons imaginable. Once it was for an extra line in his notebook. Another time it was because the wind blew a girl's dress up and she assumed he saw something. He even got beaten just for breathing too loudly. Over time, his personality has become weaker and more timid. His girlfriend eventually left him because he was too weak. This constant torment earned him the nickname Bumonte, which means foolish. The next morning, when Tay wakes up, he finds his father packing all their belongings. His father explains that they have to run away overnight. It turns out his dad was reported for running an illegal dance hall and has massive debts and he could be imprisoned at any time. Taye is upset about the move and even starts crying. He complains sadly that he's been beaten so many times in his current school that he knows how each of his bullies picks a fight and has finally figured out their movement patterns. Now he's going to have to learn the habits of a whole new set of bullies all over again. On their way out of town, his father decides they should go live with his brother in the countryside. When they arrive at his uncle's house, his brother welcomes them warmly. His uncle has a daughter named Jyn, who is Ta's childhood friend. She is clearly happy that Toy will be living with them. A little later, their neighbor, who is a police officer, greets them. Tai's father panics, thinking the officer is there to arrest him, but his brother explains that he's just their neighbor. The next morning, Taye's mother wakes him up for his first day at the new school. He refuses to go, saying he doesn't want to get beaten again. But she is the bread winner of the family and insists he must continue his education. She then asks him to go to the store and buy some rice. As he's leaving, he sees Jyn outside washing her hair and looking very funny. He laughs at her and borrows her bike to go buy the rice. On his way back, he sees a video game arcade and can't resist going in to play for a bit. He fools the younger kids into thinking he's their age and shamelessly wins all their pocket money. The kids get annoyed with him and can't accept losing to such a coward. So, they try to get their money back by force. Terrified, Taye grabs his bike and runs away. Meanwhile, in another part of town, we meet a young man famous for his great strength and cruelty known as the White Tiger. His real name is Guyong. He is as fast and violent as a tiger and was expelled from the seven schools he attended, so even the teachers fear him. A group of delinquents approaches Guyong and challenges him. After his face gets injured in the fight, his fighting spirit burns even fiercer. He instantly knocks out all the guys, leaving them all barely conscious on the ground. After the fight, Gong, as usual, stands by the road to light a cigarette. At that exact moment, a fumigation and disinfectant truck passes by, spraying a thick cloud of white mist and smoke that completely blocks the view. Taye, still fleeing from the kids at the arcade, is riding his bike very fast through this smoke, unable to see anything. When he finally emerges from the fog, he sees Guyong standing right in his way. Taye frantically squeezes the brakes, but they are faulty. He thinks he can stop, but due to the momentum, he flies through the air and crashes headon into Guyong. The blow is so strong that the white tiger passes out and ends up in the hospital with a head injury. In the hospital, Taye learns that Guyong's name is very similar to his own name, Jang Bjong Tai. This fact is important because due to the severe injuries, Gyong is transferred to a larger hospital, which means Te will arrive at the new school first. By the time Tee leaves, he remembers the rice, which has been spilled and eaten by chickens. Upset, he goes back home and borrows some rice from Jyn to avoid getting in trouble with his mom. The next day, on the bus to the new school, Jyn overhears all the students talking about a new merciless bully transferring to their school named Gyong, nicknamed the White Tiger. because of his immense strength that everyone fears. They say he single-handedly fought off 17 guys with his bare hands. Of course, Jyn immediately thinks of her cousin Tay since their names sound almost identical. She laughs to herself, thinking that the weakling Tay couldn't hurt to fly and is afraid of his own shadow. That night, a terrified Tay is encouraged by his father to be braver. His dad has noticed he's scared of the new school and comes up with a brilliant idea. He asked the neighbor, the police officer, to take Tay to school so everyone will think he's some kind of important, tough guy. Then his dad tells him to provoke the whole class. He guesses about five or six boys will raise their hands to challenge him. At that point, Taye just has to pick the weakest looking one for a fight. Even if he loses, he'll still be ranked sixth or seventh in the school's hierarchy, and no one would dare bully him easily. The next day at school, Tay is convinced by his father's words and decides to pretend to be brave. He walks confidently up to the podium and loudly introduces himself. Everyone is skeptical that he is the white tiger because he looks weak, but at the same time he has the same name. Internally, Taye is about to wet himself from fear, but he follows his father's instructions to appear charismatic. To put the rumors to rest, he stands in front of the class and loudly challenges them, asking if anyone there thinks they can win against him. To his surprise, only one boy raises his hand, but his classmates quickly pull his hand down, fearing he might get killed. All the other students keep their heads down, unwilling to make eye contact. This confuses Taye as things are not going according to his plan at all. It turns out they all mistakenly believe he is the legendary white tiger. His powerful aura has stunned them. Taye, however, is deeply troubled, feeling like he's messed everything up. While he is in the restroom, a group of delinquents, the school's main bully gang, approaches him aggressively. Their leader is a guy named Hong. Tai feels a chill in his heart, realizing his dad's method is useless. Instinctively, he drops to his knees, waiting to be beaten. But the bullies mistake this for a martial artist gesture of respect and quickly kneel as well. Hong greets Taye warmly and even suggests throwing him a welcome party after school. Tai sigh and asks if the party will be behind the restroom. Everyone freezes for a moment and then Hong bursts into laughter, saying Tai is funny and giving him a friendly pat. Thanks to years of experience getting beaten, Taye instinctively covers his head. Hong quickly realizes he overstepped and apologizes. After school, the delinquents personally escort Taye to a restaurant and even let him sit in the boss's seat. Hong pours him a drink himself and formally introduces each of his friends. Taye feels uneasy, thinking they're planning to get him drunk and then beat him up, so he resigns himself to his fate and treats the meal as his last supper. After dinner, they take him to a bar to continue the celebration. Suddenly, a beautiful girl named Lee joins them. The legend about her is that she will only date the bravest boy in town. As soon as Taye sees her, he is instantly smitten. His new friends introduce her to him, calling him the White Tiger. It's then that Taye finally understands the mixup is due to their similar names, which is why they are treating him so well. He freezes on the spot, his jaw nearly dropping to the floor. He realizes he's probably heading for disaster, but he decides to keep quiet about his real identity to avoid being bullied and beaten again. Faced with the awkward situation, he forces himself to stay calm. The next day at school, his new friends treat him with even more respect. During a soccer game, the other players clear a path for him to score a goal just to see his strength. But a student named Kim, who is the weakest kid in the class, easily stops him and knocks him flying, making him lose the ball. One of the bullies, Sledgehammer, sees this and bursts into laughter, mockingly asking if he's a fake white tiger. The atmosphere instantly turns tense. Later in the classroom, Kim confronts Tay. He confesses that he saw Taye being beaten by some youths on the street a few days ago near the arcade. Because of this, he knows Tay is not the real White Tiger. Taye panics and immediately asks him to keep it a secret. Sledgehammer, who is nearby, grows increasingly suspicious of Taye's identity after seeing him fall during the soccer game. He decides to test him to be sure because the White Tiger is known for smoking with style. During a break, he corners Taye in the restroom and puts a cigarette in his mouth, telling him to smoke it if he's the real deal. Taye does as he's told, but immediately starts coughing and turns red in the face. Realizing he can't keep the secret anymore, he is about to confess the truth. Just then, Hong and the rest of the bullies suddenly arrive, adding more tension to the moment. Taye thinks he's going to die, but instead of hitting him, the bullies defend him from Sledgehammer. Worried that Sledgehammer might be in danger for disrespecting the White Tiger, Hong gives him the beating of his life. The bald guy threatens Sledgehammer not to get near the White Tiger again, or he will hit him again. It seems Taye has them hypnotized under a spell. Sledgehammer apologizes for his friend's behavior, leaving Taye relieved. But his peace doesn't last long. Back in class, Kim, his neighbor, tells him that since he knows Tay is not the White Tiger, Taye has to treat him well, or he'll tell everyone his secret. A moment later, Kim accidentally spills his drink on Sledgehammer. Sledgehammer retaliates with a punch that sends Kim against the wall. Then he grabs him by the neck, and before he can punch him again, Taye comes to his defense. Sledgehammer tells him not to get involved, but Tay, without backing down, proclaims that he is the white tiger of Asia and is not afraid. However, he soon gets nervous and starts to sweat. And Sledgehammer notices. For this reason, he challenges him to a fist fight after school to see who is stronger. Unexpectedly, Taye agrees without hesitation, as if he's already accepted his cruel fate. His sudden calmness, however, only makes Sledgehammer start to panic. When they go to a secluded spot in a barn, the moment of battle finally arrives. Neither side dares to make the first move, and they stand off for a full hour. The onlookers grow restless and start playing games to kill time. Suddenly, Sledgehammer lunges like a beast, slamming Tay to the ground and choking him hard. The scared protagonist tries to escape, but the guy stops him and throws him back onto a pile of straw. Without giving up, Taye tries to run home, but the guy trips him, making him fall and then grabs him by the neck. In a critical moment with a trick up his sleeve, Taye bites his arm, managing to break free. Next, Sledgehammer lifts him into the air to throw him to the ground. At that point, Taye, completely by accident, throws his elbow back and hits the guy in the head, knocking him out cold. His companions, who are busy beating up Kim and not paying attention, happen to look over and witness the final blow in amazement. They are now convinced he is the White Tiger. At this moment, Taye picks up the cigarette from the ground and takes a hard drag. This action perfectly matches the White Tiger's famous line, "Nothing tastes better than a bloody cigarette." But nobody notices that he chokes on it a second later. Even Taye himself is surprised he managed to land a punch. From that day on, no one dares to question Taye's identity. His friends help him move the body and surround him as he leaves, not to hit him, but to congratulate him and invite him out for dinner. Sledgehammer sincerely apologizes for ever doubting him. Taye seizes the chance to urge everyone to stop using violence, passionately telling them that while they might be tough at school, in the real world, they're at the bottom of the food chain. His speech leaves the crowd in awe. He then tells Sledgehammer to sit down and says that from now on, they're brothers. Just like that, he blows his last chance to tell the truth and instead slowly adapts to his unexpected new identity. They drink together until they are completely wasted. As they're leaving the restaurant, they see Lee arguing with her boyfriend because he gave her a fake wallet. She decides to break up with him, but her boyfriend won't let her leave. Her boyfriend is known as the pliers, one of the top three fighters at the rival technical high school. He and his gang are always bullying students from agricultural high. In the past, Hong would never dare get involved. But now, he pushes Tae forward, telling him to win back the pride of their school. One of the boys steps in, warning the pliers not to get near Lee anymore. In response, the pliers pulls out a weapon, trying to scare him, but the bald guy mentions that the famous white tiger of Asia is on their team. Instead of convincing him with fists, Taye tells him he is embarrassing the girl. He says that to be a good boyfriend, you have to understand her feelings and realize that when a girl's heart no longer wants you, you have to leave. The pliers responds that Lee belongs to him as if she were his toy. Taye then throws a punch that leaves his face red. When the pliers realizes he's facing the white tiger and is outnumbered, he gets scared and runs away. Before leaving, he threatens to make Taye pay for this. Lee feels butterflies in her stomach. She was impressed by Taye's bravery, but especially by his poetic words and his way of seeing love. No one had ever touched her heart like that before. Taye invites her to eat, and with his fiery eyes, he makes her fall more and more in love. In a romantic gesture, she removes a piece of food from his lip. He is thrilled to be with the girl he has a crush on. On his way home, Tay sees his cousin Jyn fighting with some girls in the street and beating them up effortlessly. He finds out she's nicknamed the Black Widow and watches her fight better than a thousand men. After they go home, he has to meet her after dinner for an important matter. When they meet, he reveals that he knows her nickname. He threatens to tell her family her secret if she doesn't tell the truth. Jyn gets angry and warns him not to even think about telling anyone in her family, especially her father, who thinks she's a sweet girl. She then kicks him, sending him flying. Taye assures her he won't say a word after that kick. He then asks her to teach him a powerful move that can defeat anyone. She teaches him how to use his elbow to break free from a hold. He is very happy to have learned a move and keeps practicing it. While this was happening, the real white tiger, Guang, awakens from his coma in the hospital. He has amnesia and tries to remember what happened and how he got there, which means Taye is now in danger. Meanwhile, the pliers ask Lee to get back together with him, but she rejects him, saying she now likes the white tiger. This infuriates him so much that he searches the entire school for the tiger to kill him. Just then, Taye enters the school with great confidence and is stopped by a school patrol officer for not wearing his uniform correctly. As punishment, he must do 200 push-ups. Just in time, his friends arrive and defend him, asking the officer how he dares to stop their leader, the White Tiger. Hearing this, the supervisor gets scared and lets him pass. Taye thinks to himself that being the White Tiger has great advantages. After this, the plier sneaks into the school seeking revenge. He looks through the classrooms, hitting students until they tell him where the white tiger is. He finds out Tay is in the practical class learning agriculture in the forest. When the plier sees him, Tay is terrified and tries to escape, but it's too late. The pliers yells that he won't let anyone take a leaf from him. But Taye, having zero interest in fighting, yells back, "Man, take her and get away from me. I don't even like her or want her." The pliers can't believe his luck and quickly leaves before Taye's friends can see him. In the chaos, he steps in a giant pile of poop that gets on his hand and he leaves defeated. When Taye rejoins his friends, they encourage him to go after the pliers and teach him a lesson to restore their school's honor. They inform him that the pliers has a friend named the triangle who carries a triangle-shaped weapon. They decide he must be dealt with. The next morning, Taye gathers his friends and half the school, and they march to the rival school to finish them off. Taye cleverly stays in the back, directing the action with a microphone, yelling, "Go, careful on your right. Hit him on your left." Fueled by high morale, they crush their enemies who are using mud as their only weapon. After his men have done the job, Tay acts like a superhero and asks for the triangle. The triangle hears him and comes out challenging him to a one-on-one fight. Taye is in a tight spot, but suddenly one of his friends hits the triangle and Tay goes to hit him after he has already been thoroughly beaten. And so his team manages to defeat them. But before they can leave, a police officer arrives. Everyone manages to escape, including Tay, who slips away hidden. So, the officer doesn't see his face. Afterwards, his friends go out to celebrate, even though he did absolutely nothing but talk. They continue their celebration at a restaurant, and Lee joins them. One of his friends tells him that girls like guys who know how to dance. Taye gets up on the dance floor while everyone watches, unsure of what he's going to do. Just when it seemed he was going to make a fool of himself, Taye begins to dance with a special fluidity, turning the dance floor into a magical place. He jumps and moves his hips as if he were recording the best Tik Tok of his life. Because of this, Lee smiles, feeling love grow in her heart. To leave them speechless, Taye performs his final move, moving his body with such ease that he defies gravity. After he finishes, Lee, completely euphoric, runs to him and confesses that he has impressed her. As they are walking home, she suddenly holds his arm as if she were his girlfriend. Taking a big step, she moves closer to his face, expecting a kiss, but he remains still. She then sweetly asks if he is free on the weekend for a date. He replies that he is busy studying, so she leaves furiously until he thinks better of it and says, "Of course, he has the weekend free." She hands him a photograph with her phone number written on the back and whispers that she wants to see him again. The protagonist, with his heart on fire, feels like he's on cloud nine. The next morning, Taye goes to school very happy, but he is shocked to see the real Guing, who has transferred to their school. They look very similar. Taye is very scared and keeps looking at him throughout the class, waiting for the moment when he tells the truth and his life is ruined. After class, they meet in the bathroom and Taye discovers that Guang doesn't actually remember anything. The blow to the head affected the memory parts of his brain. Then the school bullies go to bother Guangong since he is a new student, but Taye defends him. Guyong is annoyed by their treatment, and even though he doesn't remember anything, he easily hits one of them with surprising ease, throwing him through the air. The thugs are terrified and Taye realizes that even though Guyong has lost his memory, he is still terrifying. Afterwards, Taye decides to spy on Guyong and become his friend to see if he is lying about his amnesia. He follows him to a bakery and observes his behavior, learning that the bakery belongs to his family. He is relieved that Guangong doesn't remember him at all. Before he leaves, Gong goes to sit with him, happy to have made a friend from their new school. When his mother learns that Tay is her son's classmate, she gives him some treats from the bakery. Later, the two of them go out together and run into the pliers and the triangle, who want to beat up Taye to keep him away from Lee. As usual, Taye is a coward and unable to defend himself, but Gong gets very angry when he sees his mother's baked goods thrown on the ground. He carefully picks up each piece only to be humiliated by the pliers. Guang is forced to unleash his fighting skills, beating them all up until they get scared and run away. At the end of the day, they sit together and hang out, now real friends. The next day, Taye gets dressed up and takes out all the money he has saved to meet Lee. They go on a date and spend the whole day together. At the end of the day, Lee takes advantage of Taye and makes him treat her to a very expensive meal at a fancy restaurant. Of course, Taye is broke, but feels obligated to buy her the food she ordered. When the food arrives, he excuses himself to go to the bathroom and runs to his friends to tell them he's in a jam and needs money. His friends are just as broke as he is, so they can only think of one person, Gaong. They try to bully Guyong and take the money from him, but Guyong beats them all up. At that moment, the pliers and his friends go up to him and hit him on the head. Here, his lost memories flood back like a tide. He remembers everything that happened, including Taye hitting him with the bike. Meanwhile, Taye is enjoying his meal with Lee. After regaining his memory, Gong beats up the pliers and goes to Tay to give him the money he needs, throwing it on the table. He sees Lee and is immediately smitten. Before he leaves, he gives them the food. It's clear is hurt, his face covered in blood, but he leaves without revealing the secret. When Taye finishes his dinner, he walks Lee home, ecstatic to be dating someone like her. As he walks home happily, he sees Jyn fighting with street girls and their brother, who's come to beat Jyn up for hitting his sisters. Tai plays the hero and approaches them, acting very confident. When the brother learns that Tar is the white tiger, he takes his sisters and leaves. When Tai is alone with Jyn, she thinks he has a crush on her, but he denies it. She then kicks him, sending him to the ground. The next day, Tai goes to school and finds a notice about the election for class president. The students all agree to vote for Tai. Later, he meets Gyong, who asks him when he'll get his money back. Tai tells him he'll return it as soon as possible. During a science activity at a farm, his friend Kim asks him to deliver a love confession letter to Jyn. In return, Tai asks for money to pay back Young. Kim doesn't have any money, but suggests they work at the farm for a day. Tai gathers his friends and they work at the farm. When they finish, they sit together and divide the money they earned. When Jang J calls Lee to ask her out, Gong asks if he can come along, and Tay strangely agrees. At the cafe, Guyong starts complimenting Lee's beauty right in front of Tai, who says nothing. As they walk together later, Gong continues to flirt with Lee and tells Taye he has a crush on her. Finally, Taye objects, but only mildly. After Guyong leaves, Taye gives Lee the wallet she wanted as a gift. He goes home happy, but also annoyed by Guyong's behavior. The next day, Gong goes to Lee's school with products from his family's bakery and continues to flirt with her. After many attempts, Lee agrees to go out with him. He takes her to a mountain and Lee starts to fall for Gong. When he takes her home, Tay is waiting for her and sees her arrive with Gong, who then kisses her. Lee slaps him, but Taye has seen everything. After Lee leaves, Taye confronts Gyong and tries to intimidate him, but to no avail. He returns home devastated and cries over what happened. The next day at school, Gong tells his bully friends that he wants to beat up Tea because he's annoyed with him. While the students are gathered, Gong reveals his true identity. "The time has come to reveal the truth," he explains to everyone. "I am the real white tiger." He explains that he thought Taye was his friend, but Taye let his bully friends pick on him. The astonished students look at Tay, who forced by Gong, confesses that what he says is true. Gong then starts beating up T and makes him confess in front of everyone that he is a coward and that Gong is the real White Tiger while he is just a nobody. At this, his friends feel truly betrayed and chase him. They catch up to him and beat him severely. Afterwards, Gang tells them to go celebrate and forces Tay to come with them. They order a lot of food and make him pay for it, and he isn't even allowed to eat any of it. After they leave, the restaurant owner takes his name so Tay can pay the bill in installments. Gyong then makes Taye call Lee to meet them at a bar. When she arrives, Gung forces Taye to tell her he's not the White Tiger. Realizing she's been deceived, Lee gets furious and slaps Tai for lying to her. Before she leaves, Gong asks her to stay with him. He convinces her to be his girlfriend, and she immediately agrees. The next day, before Tay's mother goes to work, she sees the bruises on his face, but he pretends to be asleep until she leaves. He gets up, puts on his school uniform, and goes anywhere but school, knowing he'll be beaten. He thinks about the hellish life ahead of him and sees a picture of Lee crying. He then decides to go see her after school to find out if she ever loved him. Her response is that she is utterly disgusted by him. She throws the wallet he gave her at him. With no other choice, Taye goes to sell the wallet and heads to the station to leave town for good. But even that fails as he runs into the restaurant owner he owes money to, who forcibly takes the money from him, leaving him broke. He wanders off and runs into another group of youths who know he's the fake white tiger and they beat him up too. At the end of the day, his family scolds him for being absent from school. The next day at school, his bully friends catch him and inform him that he must collect a tax from the students in his class or he'll have to pay it out of his own pocket. One of the bullies tells him that if he beats one student and takes their money, the rest will be scared and pay up. Taye thinks about it and decides to beat up his friend Kim. As soon as the teacher leaves the classroom, he finds no one else to hit but Kim and starts beating him. But Kim defends himself and hits Taye back. When Kim sees that Tay can no longer defend himself, he leaves him alone. But Taye follows him and hits him with a chair, continuing the assault. Kim faints, but all Taye can think about is collecting the money. His classmates notice that Kim is bleeding heavily and needs to be taken to the hospital. A little later, a police officer is waiting to take Taye in because Kim's parents have filed a complaint against him. The only solution is for Taye's parents to go and apologize to Kim's parents so they will drop the charges. Indeed, they go to the hospital to apologize and give his mother a large sum of money to forgive him. While the parents are making peace, Tay and Kim talk and reconcile as well. From that day, Taye vows never to become a perpetrator again. But whenever injustice comes, he chooses silence and endurance only to suffer even harsher humiliation. One day, Guang orders Tay to carry a heavy chair to the school before morning. He meets Jyn, who tries to help him. She notices how tired and bruised Taye is and tries to make him understand that he is not forced to do this and can defend himself. But it seems Taye has grown to like being beaten. Jyn is not happy with the situation at all. She leaves him and goes to Gong, warning him about his treatment of Tay. Ging provokes her, so she is forced to hit him, giving him a bruised eye. The next day at school, the bullies see Guyong's bruised eye. Unfortunately, Taye makes the mistake of asking about it and gets beaten, too. Later, Sledgehammer brags that he's the one who reported Taye's dad for running the illegal dance hall. It's obvious this is Gong's revenge. Enraged, Taye confronts Sledgehammer, only to be defeated instantly. His father is arrested. He falls into deep regret, realizing he can't even protect his own family. His mom takes the blame on herself, crying that it's her uselessness that has dragged him down. Seeing her like this, Tae feels his heart shatter. In that moment, he decides to go to Jyn to have her teach him martial arts. He swears he will make those who humiliated him pay. She makes him train all night to strengthen his body. She tells him the problem is not the training. The problem is in his eyes which show that he is very kind. His eyes need to show anger. She takes him to people who do hard manual labor with heavy weights and fire to strengthen him. She tells him he will stay in this place for 20 days. Indeed, Taye begins to train, or rather to be tortured. He thinks about escaping, but he remembers his mother's words and goes back to training until the 20 days are over. He finds Jyn has returned. She notices a big difference in his body and his eyes, which are now full of anger. Then he goes to her to learn the moves he can use to fight. After these training sessions, Taye returns to school. When one of the bullies tries to take his food, Taye no longer allows anyone to mess with him and prevents him from taking it, even spitting on it. He has changed. One day, he sees a wrestling show on TV and notices that the wrestler is wearing a mask. He thinks this is a very good idea and goes to Jyn to tell her about the mask plan. text: Ek Tha Tiger. The story begins in 2009 with a RAW officer, Avinash Singh Rathore, known as Tiger. While in Iraq, he is forced to kill his colleague, Ravinder, for defecting to Pakistan's intelligence agency, the ISI. Frustrated that his missions always involve violence. Tiger's boss, Shenoy, sends him to Dublin on a routine mission to monitor Anwar Kidwai. Kidwai is an Indian scientist currently teaching at Trinity College, suspected of sharing innovative Indian anti-missile research with Pakistani scientists. Tiger's handler, Gopi, accompanies him on this mission. Tiger introduces himself as Manish Chandra, a non-fiction writer. He claims he is writing a book about Kidwai and other Indian academics. To get to Kidwai's house, Tiger befriends Zoya, Kidwai's caretaker and a British-Indian dance student at Trinity College. Over time, Tiger and Zoya fall in love. A few days later, a mysterious attacker assaults Tiger, leading him and Gopi to fear their identities will be exposed. One night, they go out on a date at 11:00 PM. There, Tiger shows Zoya the stars. She tells him that in 1991, when she was six, her father Nazarchand used to take her in a police jeep to show her the stars. One day, after spotting the attacker, Tiger chases him through Dublin. This leads to Tiger publicly preventing a train accident. Afterward, Tiger attends a college play, "My Son Pinocchio," sponsored by Kidwai and choreographed by Zoya. During the play, Gopi calls Tiger to inform him about some suspicious activity at Kidwai's house. There, Tiger discovers that Zoya is an ISI agent tasked with stealing the research from Kidwai's computer. Zoya refused to commit treason and declined to hand over the research. Just then, ISI agent Feroze attacked her. After dealing with him, Tiger takes the hard drive from Zoya and lets her go. Back in India, Tiger asks his boss Shenoy for leave and requests to be moved from field duty to a desk job. Bagga informs him about an intercepted Pakistani secret message left by Zoya for Tiger. It informs him that Zoya will be attending a United Nations meeting in Istanbul. Tiger and Zoya meet, and they decide to run away together. On the other hand, after Zoya misleads her agency, Tiger and Zoya travel to Havana. One night, Tiger and Zoya stop a robbery taking place. But this is all recorded on CCTV and their location is revealed to both agencies. Spotted at an amateur boxing match, the couple tries to escape while planning to dodge the police and leave Havana. But Zoya is arrested by the Cuban police and handed over to the ISI to be surrendered to Pakistan. Following this , Tiger meets Gopi and says that Zoya will cooperate with RAW in exchange for her escape. Tiger and Gopi lead a team to intercept the convoy of Zoya’s prisoner vehicle. But after Gopi’s help, Tiger betrays him and both escape Cuba in an aircraft they had spotted in a nearby field. Some time later, Tiger calls Shenoy and tells him that he and Zoya will return to their country when Pakistan and India no longer need the ISI and RAW, and a few days later, Tiger and Zoya are reported to have been spotted multiple times in Venice, Cape Town, Zurich, and London. Tiger Zinda Hai. 8 years have passed since the events of Ek Tha Tiger, and there is no trace of Tiger and Zoya. In a city in Syria, 40 nurses, including 25 Indians and 15 Pakistanis, have been taken hostage in their own hospital by Abu Usman, the leader of a terrorist organization, ISC. This is because he was injured in the firing by the Iraqi army. Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chairman Shenoy feels that only Tiger will succeed in saving the nurses, and that too within seven days, because the United States of America will conduct an airstrike on that hospital within seven days. To kill Abu Usman, who recently posted a video online beheading an American CIA operative while threatening America. Currently, Tiger and Zoya live in the Austrian countryside and have a son, Junior. Shenoy and his deputy Karan succeed in finding Tiger and request him to take on the mission. Although Tiger was initially hesitant. But after Zoya tells him to carry out the mission for his country, Tiger agrees. Tiger and three other RAW agents, Azaan, Namit, and Rakesh, depart for Syria. Shenoy tells Karan to keep an eye on Tiger. He feared that after living with an enemy agent for eight years, Tiger might have changed. Tiger and his team enter Iraq from the Turkish border via a convoy of oil tankers. Upon reaching Ikrit, the plan is to get jobs as illegal immigrants at a refinery there. Once inside, they will carry out a controlled explosion at the refinery and act as if they were burned. The ISC will have no choice but to take them to the hospital. They arrive at the refinery. Where they meet Firdaus, also known as Tohban. He supplies illegal immigrants to the refinery and does not trust Tiger and his group at all. Tiger meets his local contact in Ikrit to buy materials for the bomb. While there, he encounters a young boy who was an ISC suicide bomber. He defuses the boy's bomb and kills the ISC terrorists who were pursuing him. Meanwhile, Zoya arrives just in time and helps Tiger and the ISC boy escape the terrorists. Zoya learns about the Pakistani nurses taken hostage along with the Indians and joins Tiger, along with two other ISI agents, Abrar and Javed. Tiger and Zoya decide to unite to execute the mission. But Karan and Shenoy do not approve of this. The next step of the plan goes wrong when the security team discovers the team inside the refinery, and a guard is killed in the explosion. The owner of the refinery wants to hang Tiger and his team. But Firdaus intervenes and explains to Amir that it was an accident and asks him to spare their lives. Firdaus is taking them to the hospital. Just then, Zoya attacks and saves Tiger and his team. Firdaus reveals that he is also a RAW agent and promises to help Tiger and Zoya. Firdaus takes the men to the hospital. While Zoya goes to get the building plans of the hospital. At the hospital, Firdaus learns that since America bombed Mosul, the ISC and Usman have turned it into their biggest base. Security is very tight with 300 soldiers. Indian Intelligence believes Usman is planning something major inside the hospital. Shenoy convinces the Indian Prime Minister to deploy defense forces in the Gulf and Iraq to attack the ISC-held areas in Ikrit and Syria. Meanwhile, at the hospital, Usman is conscious and befriends the Indian nurse, Poorna. But when one of his companions tries to escape, he has her killed in front of everyone. On the other hand, Zoya has found the hospital building plans. Just then, Amir Bagdawi calls Zoya into his bedroom, where she kills him. After which, she kills many such terrorists, and the footage is captured on CCTV. Which Usman watches later. Usman orders Firdauz to find Zoya. Firdauz and Zoya together convince the local US garrison commander to attack a concrete outpost on the day of the raid. Meanwhile, inside the hospital, Tiger and Rakesh poison the food, making half the soldiers sick.
