text: Welcome to Donut recap ,In today s video. we will be going through the 2022 American computer-animated comedy titled. Minions The Rise of Gru . time to Explore. Let's get started. Turn On Subtitles and Spoilers Ahead! The film opens in 1976. A supervillain named Belle Bottom. runs through the city as the Anti-Villain League chases after her. as she has stolen a map. After taking the Anti-Villain League agents down. Belle makes it to her hideout at the Criminal Records music shop. There, she joins the rest of her team, the Vicious 6 Strong Hold . Nun-Chuck . Svengeance . Jean-Clawed and their founder Wild Knuckles . They look at the map and find that it contains the location to an artifact known as the Zodiac Stone, which turns the users into powerful animals during the Chinese New Year. The Vicious 6 fly to an island where the Stone is. Wild Knuckles enters the temple and locates the Zodiac Stone, but he is attacked by small metal guardians. He fights them off and flees the temple, only to find more guardians going after him. The rest of the 6 pull Knuckles up, but they grab the Stone from him and double-cross him, declaring that he is old and that the team needs to be run by fresh blood. They drop Knuckles into the ocean and fly off Elsewhere, young Gru is 11 years old and dreams of being a supervillain, which makes him unpopular with the other kids that think he s a weirdo. He gets picked up by Kevin. Bob and Stuart . They ride back to Gru s house, where he finds something for him in the mail. It is a message from Belle Bottom, as Gru had sent an application to join the Vicious 6 since he is their biggest fan, and Knuckles is his favorite villain . Belle invites Gru to show up for an audition at the Criminal Records shop. Gru is excited and thinks his time as a supervillain has come. He is seen just living with his unsupportive mother Marlena , as well as the rest of the Minions that he has employed as his henchmen. Gru announces the big news to the Minions, who all support their mini boss Wild Knuckles turns out to still be alive, as he is living at home with three of his own henchmen. He is still bitter at the Vicious 6 for kicking him out of his own team, and he finds out that they are holding auditions for a new member. The next day, Gru makes it to Criminal Records and meets a young Dr. Nefario , an aspiring mad scientist. He shows Gru one of his new inventions, a gun that shoots a sticky green hand to grab things. Nefario gives it to Gru and shows him the secret entrance to the Vicious 6 hideout. However, when he meets them, they dismiss him for being a kid, as Jean-Clawed. assumed he was a tiny man when they reviewed his application. As they send him away, another candidate shows up and tries to show off his flight suit, only to have his jetpack malfunction and make him fly like crazy. The Vicious 6 try to stop him, causing them to be distracted as Gru spots the Zodiac Stone behind them. He uses Nefario s gun and swipes the Stone, but the 6 catch him and begin to pursue. Gru rejoins the Minions and tosses the Stone to one Minion Otto,Gru rides away as the 6 chase him. He causes Strong Hold and Nun-Chuck to knock each other out, and when Belle and Svengeance latch onto Gru s bike, he uses the rocket to get them out of there. Meanwhile, Knuckles witnessed the whole thing and follows Gru in his van. When Gru. makes it back to his house, he and the other Minions wait for Otto. to come home. When he does, he presents Gru with a rock with googly eyes. Otto explains that he ended up going through a bunch of mishaps until he ended up at a birthday party and traded the birthday boy the Stone for the pet rock. Gru is furious at Otto. for his screw-up, and he promptly fires all the Minions. He heads off on his own to go find the Stone, but as he walks down the street, Knuckles henchmen grab him and throw him in their van, which Kevin watches. He goes to tell the other Minions that their mini boss has been kidnapped. Gru is brought to Wild Knuckles hideout. Gru is excited to meet his idol, but Knuckles is angry to find that Gru doesn t have the Stone. He contacts Gru s home to attempt to get a ransom from his mom, but Kevin answers the phone, and Knuckles tells him to deliver the Stone to San Francisco within two days time or they will kill Gru. Kevin. Stuart .Bob and Otto. head to the house of the kid that Otto gave the Stone to. The kid tells them that he gave it to his uncle , who is taking off on his motorcycle. Otto rides after him on a tricycle with the other three Minions find a bus for an ad to fly to San Francisco. They go to the airport and pose as pilots and a flight attendant to sneak onboard the next flight. Kevin and Stuart try to fly and end up touching all the buttons and creating a mess before they end up landing safely Knuckles puts Gru in a torture device that s a record player that will push him closer to spinning saw blades. He sends his henchmen to go out, and they find the Minions. They try to grab them, thinking they have the Stone, and they end up in Chinatown where an acupuncturist named Master Chow watches the henchmen beating on the Minions. Despite being a small old lady, Chow displays impressive kung fu skills and fights the henchmen off. The Minions ask Chow to teach them her skills, but she says she is retired from that life. However, when the trio flash their puppy eyes at her, she relents. Otto rides across many states on his trike to catch up to the Biker, but he loses sight of him. The Biker ends up spotting Otto and picks him up, taking him to San Francisco on his bike and giving him the Stone. The henchmen quit on Knuckles after their mishap. He frees Gru from the trap and makes him do chores. While cleaning his pool full of crocodiles, Knuckles falls in. Gru manages to pull him out and save him, and Knuckles is thankful. He brings Gru along on a heist. They go to the Bank of Evil, posing as grandfather and grandson. Knuckles pretends to have a heart attack so Gru can swipe the keys of Mr. Perkins Gru manages to steal the Mona Lisa, making Knuckles proud. Chow trains the Minions in martial arts, but they end up hurting themselves more than they do any learning. They quickly manage to step up their skills, but Chow says they only passed basic training. Unfortunately, the Minions have already fled and are on their way to save Gru. The Vicious 6 track down Gru s house and tear the roof off, interrogating Marlena and the other Minions as to his whereabouts. One of the Minions spills that Gru was taken by Knuckles. The 6 then head off to Knuckles house and also tear the top off, trashing the place and finding nothing. When Gru and Knuckles return, they find his home destroyed. He knows it was the 6 that did this, and he becomes upset that they would continue to try and hurt him after all this time. He tells Gru he is giving up and he just tells him to go home, despite Gru s protests. Downtown, a Chinese New Year Parade is going on. Otto ends up running into the crowd. Gru spots him from the trolley and runs after him. Otto shows Gru the Stone, and he expresses pride in Otto. Unfortunately, the Vicious 6 have caught up to them, and they capture Gru. Just as they are cornered by the Anti-Villain League, Belle grabs the Stone and utilizes its powers to turn her and the team into giant animal monsters. The three Minions overpower the 6, and Gru grabs the Stone, using it to turn them all into rats. The AVL shows up and takes them into custody. Knuckles is injured and is also arrested, though he tells Gru that he will see him again soon. Cut to a funeral, where it seems that Knuckles has died. Gru gives him a touching eulogy, only to find that Knuckles faked his death and is hiding. After the Minions give a Minion rendition of You Can t Always Get What You Want . Gru asks Dr. Nefario if he would like to officially work for him and build gadgets, but Nefario says he is giving up the villain business. The year 2025 is set to deliver one of the most uncompromising, brutally honest, and visceral portraits of a woman's descent into madness ever committed to film, Die My Love. This is not a horror movie in the traditional sense, but a psychological thriller that transforms the intimate space of a new marriage and motherhood into a claustrophobic emotional prison. The film is a collaboration of Absolute Titans directed by the brilliant singular voice of Lynn Ramsay, starring two of the biggest names in Hollywood, Jennifer Lawrence and Robert Patson, and executive produced by none other than Martin Scorsesei. Based on the celebrated 2012 novel of the same name by Ariana Harwitch, the story refuses to simplify or romanticize the trauma of mental illness. Instead, plunging the audience directly into the terrifying reality of psychosis and the fracturing of a passionate love. It is a film that has already generated massive critical buzz following its world premiere, confirming its status as one of the year's most significant and challenging cinematic events. The core of the movie's plot centers on Grace, played by Jennifer Lawrence, a writer, and her husband Jackson, played by Robert Patson, a musician. The couple, initially portrayed as passionately in love and intensely physical, decide to leave the chaos of New York City life behind and move into a remote, sprawling old house in the American West, reportedly around Montana. This house, which belonged to Jackson's deceased uncle, Harry, hinted to have died tragically by suicide, is meant to be their new beginning, a quiet space to raise their newborn son, who remains nameless for the majority of the film. However, the idyllic setting quickly becomes a gilded cage for Grace. She, an ambitious writer, finds her creativity utterly blocked by the relentless, monotonous reality of domesticity. She is isolated, without a support network, and battling the profound, unspeakable alienation that can accompany new motherhood. A darkness that Lynn Ramsay insists goes far beyond simple postpartum depression and into the realm of full-blown psychosis. The plot's escalating tension comes from Grace's gradual, terrifying unraveling. With Jackson leaving for work for the majority of the day, Grace is left alone in the vast empty house, grappling with cleaning, infant care, and her rapidly slipping sanity. The domestic space meant to be her sanctuary becomes a psychological torture chamber. The quiet moments are filled with sensory overload, the constant barking of a dog gifted by Jackson to lift her spirits, the persistent, maddening skip of a record player, and the suffocating silence of the rural isolation. Grace's distress manifests in erratic, primal, and often violently destructive urges. She lashes out at Jackson. She wanders off into the wilderness. She engages in terrifying acts of self harm, like bashing her head on a mirror. and she even crawls on all fours like an animal, a powerful, raw visual metaphor for her loss of control. The character dynamics are central to the film's heartbreaking power. Jackson is portrayed as a man utterly devoted to grace, but pathetically helpless and impotent in the face of her collapse. Robert Patson plays him as a figure of noble yet tragic commitment, watching the person he loves disappear before his eyes. Their on-screen chemistry is startling. shifting rapidly from moments of raw primal sexual connection to moments of pure rage and fear. Jackson's genuine attempts to help are repeatedly rebuffed or met with aggressive lashing out from Grace who cannot articulate her pain. The film is a devastating portrait of a marriage metaphorically going up in flames with Jackson's refusal to abandon his wife serving as the film's only source of heartbreaking grace. The psychological terror is further compounded by a brief ambiguous flirtation with a local neighbor, Carl, played by the excellent Lakey Stanfield, a relationship that may or may not be real, adding another layer of instability and surrealism to Grace's experience of the outside world. The supporting cast is packed with Hollywood legends, adding serious dramatic weight to the narrative. Spacic plays Pam, Jackson's mother, a character described as a weary widow who provides tired, often ineffective advice to her son, suggesting a generational legacy of mental health struggles that no one can quite remedy. Nick Noli plays Harry, Jackson's father, who was described as suffering from dementia, further isolating Jackson in his struggle with his wife. Lawrence recognizing the opportunity for a deeply challenging role immediately took the reigns as star and producer. She and her partner Justine Chiroi had only one director in mind the singular voice of Lynn Ramsay. Though Ramsay initially hesitated, describing the novel as surrealist and a difficult adaptation, she was won over by Lawrence's enthusiasm and a realization that the core of the story was a devastating, albeit broken, love story between Grace and Jackson. The resulting screenplay, co-written by Ramsay, Anda Walsh, and Alice Burch is lauded for taking the novel's fragmented internal monologue and turning it into a visually terrifying external reality. Ramsay's technical mastery is absolutely crucial to the film's unsettling atmosphere. She and cinematographer Sheamus Maccgarvey made specific deliberate aesthetic choices to heighten the sense of claustrophobia and psychological distress. Unlike many modern dramas which favor wide sweeping shots, Die My Love was largely shot using the Academy frame 1.33 one aspect ratio. This decision narrows the perspective, creating a visual portrait that restricts Grace's world, making the large house feel like a small, suffocating box, perfectly mirroring her inner imprisonment. The sound design is equally meticulous, with the film utilizing bizarre, intrusive noises, the constant, relentless barking of the dog, the maddening, repetitive record skip to convey Grace's sensory overload and fracturing mind, immersing the audience in her escalating psychosis. This technical commitment elevates the film beyond a simple narrative, making it a truly immersive, sometimes punishing emotional experience. The performance from Jennifer Lawrence's Grace has been universally hailed as a career peak, a ferocious tour divorce performance that is simultaneously raw, vulnerable, and terrifyingly feral. Lawrence was reportedly 5 months pregnant with her second child during the intensive 35day shoot, a fact that added a disturbing layer of method to her performance. As she herself was experiencing a difficult postpartum period while preparing for the role, she insisted on a completely naturalistic approach, refusing makeup or digital touch-ups on her body, embracing a lack of vanity that underscores the character's desperate emotional state. Director Ramsay intentionally broke the ice on the first day of shooting by tackling the difficult primal sex scenes between Grace and Jackson, quickly establishing the intense animalistic chemistry that defines their tumultuous relationship before the arrival of the baby crushes their abandon. The film made its highly anticipated world premiere in the main competition at the 78th Kin Film Festival on May 17, 2025, where it immediately became a major talking point and was nominated for the coveted Palm Door. text: The movie begins with a young woman named Ellen Hutter having a frightening dream. In her dream, she makes a pact with a powerful and evil demon named Nosferatu. After the pact, the demon, who is also a vampire, has an intimate encounter with her and then chokes her, completing the possession. Suddenly, Ellen wakes up and realizes it was all just a nightmare. Her husband, Thomas, notices her distress and hugs her, reassuring her that everything is fine. The story takes place in 1838, in Germany. Thomas, who is in a rush to meet his boss, Herr Knock, says goodbye to Ellen and heads to work. Ellen, still shaken by her dream, keeps thinking about it. At work, Thomas apologizes to Herr Knock for being late. Herr Knock congratulates him on his recent marriage and then offers him a business deal. He wants Thomas to sell a house in Wisburg to a strange and reclusive man named Count Orlock. Thomas agrees to the deal, hoping it will help him secure a promotion. Later that day, Thomas tells Ellen about the trip he must take to meet Count Orlock. Ellen becomes upset and warns him not to go. She shares a terrifying dream she had before their wedding, where she saw herself marrying death, surrounded by dead boys as guests. Despite her fear, Thomas reassures her that it was just a dream and insists he needs to go for the sake of their future. The next day, Thomas takes Ellen to stay with his wealthy friend, Friederick Harding, while he is away. He comforts her again, saying she has nothing to fear. That night, Ellen has another nightmare, where Nosferatu strengthens the pact she made with him. The following morning, before Thomas leaves, Ellen gives him her necklace. Unbeknownst to him, she had cut a piece of her hair and placed it inside the necklace, fulfilling one of Nosferatu’s requirements. After a long journey, Thomas arrives in Transylvania. The locals welcome him warmly at first, but their behavior soon turns strange, and they start laughing in an eerie way. The village chief scolds them for their actions but warns Thomas about associating with Count Orlock. Despite the warning, Thomas bribes the chief, convincing him to let him stay one night. That night, an old woman gives Thomas a cross, telling him he will need it. Later, Thomas witnesses the villagers performing a ritual, where they stab a corpse they claim is a vampire. Terrified by what he sees, Thomas goes to bed but decides to continue his journey the next morning. As Thomas travels to the castle, a mysterious carriage appears out of nowhere. Although no one is driving it, he bravely gets inside. The carriage takes him to Count Orlock’s mansion, with wolves running alongside it. Thomas finally arrives at Count Orlock’s castle, where he is greeted by the frightening and impatient Count. Orlock comments on how late Thomas is and insists they dine together to finalize the house purchase quickly. During the meal, Orlock offers Thomas some wine. When Thomas asks about the strange things he had heard from the villagers, Orlock dismisses them as mere superstitions. As Thomas eats, he accidentally cuts his thumb, causing it to bleed. Orlock, drawn to the scent of blood, begins acting strangely. Thomas senses something is very wrong, but it is too late—Orlock reveals his true nature and attacks him. Meanwhile, back home, Ellen tries to warn her friend Anna about a looming danger, but Anna dismisses her concerns, thinking Ellen is imagining things. Thomas, now unconscious, has a strange dream. During this time, Orlock forces him to sign a mysterious document written in a strange, occult language. Orlock also takes Thomas’s locket, which contains Ellen’s hair. Afterward, Orlock pays Thomas with gold coins as part of their deal. When Thomas wakes up, he asks to leave the castle, but Orlock refuses, insisting it is impossible for him to leave now. Thomas soon notices strange bite marks on his chest and realizes Orlock has fed on him. Desperate to escape, Thomas searches the castle but finds all the doors locked. Eventually, he discovers a dark staircase leading to the basement. There, he finds Orlock sleeping in a coffin. Thomas tries to kill him with an axe, but Orlock wakes up and stops him. Terrified, Thomas runs away. Orlock then uses Ellen’s hair to cast a spell. As he performs the ritual, Ellen begins to feel its effects from afar, becoming weak and unwell. Orlock uses his powers to compel Thomas to open a locked door, rendering him unable to resist. Orlock then attacks Thomas again, feeding on him ruthlessly. Afterward, Orlock performs a disturbing act of dominance, further asserting his control over Thomas. Back at Friederick’s house, Ellen’s condition worsens. She experiences seizures and strange symptoms, leading Friederick to call Dr. Wilhelm for help. As the doctor examines her, Ellen begins to moan as if she is in a trance. Dr. Wilhelm sedates her, but her condition continues to deteriorate. He eventually suggests transferring her to his mentor, Albin Eberhart von Franz, a scientist in Switzerland known for his expertise in the occult. Meanwhile, Thomas manages to escape the castle by jumping out of a window, but he falls into a river. A nun later finds him unconscious by the riverside and brings him to a nearby church. She prays for him, and eventually, Thomas regains consciousness. Back at Friederick’s house, Ellen’s seizures become more severe, and Dr. Wilhelm struggles to help her. He warns that the devil’s presence is near, adding to the growing tension. As Thomas recovers in the church, he realizes the danger isn’t over yet. The nuns urge Thomas to stay and recover, but he refuses, insisting he needs to return to Wisburg to protect his wife, Ellen. Meanwhile, Count Orlock begins his journey to Wisburg, carrying a crate filled with grave dirt and plague-infested rats. Dr. Wilhelm and Friederick arrive at Professor Albin’s home in Switzerland. Albin welcomes them warmly and listens as Wilhelm explains Ellen’s worsening condition. After examining her case, Albin discovers that Ellen is under the spell of Nosferatu, a demonic, plague-spreading vampire. Albin tries to treat Ellen and challenges the entity to speak. In response, Ellen becomes possessed, and Orlock speaks through her. She screams for help, losing control completely. Albin tells Friederick that Ellen is cursed by a demon, but Wilhelm dismisses it as delusion. Friederick believes Ellen’s symptoms are caused by anxiety over Thomas’s absence. Albin insists he needs to study the demon further and asks Anna to keep a close watch on Ellen, warning her to call if anything unusual happens. Thomas returned to Wisburg and told Ellen she had been right about her dreams. But soon after, he fainted. At the same time, guards told Friederick about a shipwreck. They showed him a strange ship that had brought the plague to Wisburg. This was Orlock’s ship. Orlock went to his new home and met his servant, Knock. Knock bowed to him, and Orlock promised to spread fear and despair across the land. The next day, rats from the ship spread the plague through Wisburg, causing many deaths. Ellen stayed by Thomas’s side as he became very sick. Anna visited Ellen and apologized for the trouble she had caused. Meanwhile, Dr. Wilhelm and Albin studied a body found on Orlock’s ship. They discovered that the rats were not normal—they were evil. Albin said they needed to find Knock right away, but Knock had already escaped. Orlock began chanting a spell to spread darkness and despair. Thomas had a vision of Orlock and woke up scared. Meanwhile, Anna went downstairs and was shocked to see Ellen acting strangely. Ellen begged Anna to stay the night with her, and Anna agreed. At Albin’s office, he shared his research about the vampire plague. That night, Ellen dreamed of Orlock. He tried to trick her, saying Thomas had traded her for gold and signed divorce papers. Ellen did not believe him. Angry, Orlock threatened to kill Thomas if Ellen disobeyed him. When Ellen woke up, Orlock’s power had already spread. His rats attacked Anna, leaving Ellen horrified. The plague spread quickly, and Wisburg was put under quarantine. Anna, now sick, showed signs of the plague. Ellen screamed in despair at the chaos. Friederick stayed with Ellen to comfort her but later suggested she and Thomas leave the city. He thought they might be spreading the disease. Ellen became upset and angry at his accusation. Meanwhile, Albin found a strange symbol in Knock’s office. It warned of Nosferatu’s arrival. Ellen and Thomas returned home. Thomas begged Ellen to leave the city with him, but she refused, saying it was too late. Ellen admitted she had summoned the demon when she was young and had been connected to him ever since. She accused Thomas of caring more about money than their safety. She reminded him of the document he signed for Orlock. They argued until Ellen started shaking and became possessed by Nosferatu. Thomas realized what was happening and tried to get help, but Ellen stopped him. While possessed, Ellen demanded Thomas make love to her. Afterward, she returned to normal but was confused and scared. That night, Orlock killed Friederick’s children to show his power. Heartbroken, Friederick finally believed Nosferatu was real. Albin came up with a plan to kill the vampire. He explained that Nosferatu could only die if a pure-hearted woman willingly gave her life. Ellen was the only one who could do this. Grieving his family, Friederick tried to summon Nosferatu using his wife’s body. But when the others arrived, they found Friederick had died from the plague. His body and his wife’s were burned to stop the disease from spreading further. The group decided to carry out their plan. Ellen lured Orlock to her room. Meanwhile, the others found a coffin they thought belonged to Orlock. Thomas opened it and stabbed the body inside, but it was Knock, not Orlock. They realized Orlock had tricked them. Thomas rushed back to save Ellen, while Albin destroyed the crypt. At her home, Ellen waited for Orlock in her wedding dress. She recited her vows as he did, fully giving herself to him. She let him feed on her, sharing a dark and terrible intimacy. By morning, Orlock grew weaker and realized Ellen’s sacrifice was destroying him. He turned into a lifeless corpse and died in agony. text: The movie opens with Maya Martin, a lawyer and single mother, getting her young son Noah ready for school. Maya has an important day ahead because she is working on a major murder case. Before leaving, she makes sure Noah has changed his insulin pod and checks his glucose level. Everything seems normal and Maya tells her son she loves him before leaving. Maya then receives a call from her colleague Ted, who tells her that the time for picking up their star witness has been changed to 10:15. Ted then brings up their conversation from the night before, revealing that they are romantically involved. Maya reminds him that he made it clear he doesn't want kids, while she already has Noah and doesn't want to change her life. Maya starts her run. A moment later she gets a panicked call from Laura, one of her clients. Laura says the police have taken her computer and other devices and she doesn't know what to do. Maya calmly tells her not to speak to the police without her and reminds her that defending yourself means controlling the story. A little later, Maya gets a call from Noah. She asks what he forgot this time, but a man answers instead and tells her that he has Noah. Maya panics and asks where her son is. The man tells her that Noah is with him at the Temple of Venus in the park. Maya rushes there and spots a boy she thinks is Noah, but it isn't him. She searches everywhere calling his name, but still can't find him. The man calls her again and gives her two rules if she wants Noah to stay alive. She can only speak to him and must do exactly what he says. Maya then hears piano music and asks if they are still at the park. The man tells her they are at home. Meanwhile, the man drags a suitcase with Noah trapped inside. He then tells Maya to go to the nearby swimming pond and look inside a red bin. There, Maya finds Noah's school bag containing packages with a gun inside. The man orders her to kill Radiant Tafa, the star witness against powerful crime boss Tommy Boyd. Boyd is on trial for the murders of two women and Tafa is being kept under heavy protection at the Excelsis Hotel before his court appearance. The man then reveals that he knows everything about Maya's work. He knows that she is one of the few people who can get close enough to Tafa. Maya refuses, telling him she cannot kill someone. But the man already knows exactly how to control her. He reveals that he has hacked Noah's insulin device and deliberately given him an extra dose of insulin, leaving Noah unconscious in a hypoglycemic coma. He tells Maya that Noah has roughly an hour before it becomes fatal. The only thing that can save him is a glucagon injection, which Maya normally carries with her. But she will only get the chance to save Noah after she kills Tafa. With no other choice, Maya types a message to Ted asking for a last-minute meeting with Tafa. But before she can send it, the man sends it himself. Then he orders Maya to run to the hotel, which is 5 miles away, so he can monitor her every move. As she runs through the streets, he keeps track of her location and heart rate. He then starts going through the photos on Maya's phone, looking into her past. He finds pictures from her childhood and sees that her father was once her coach when she was a young athlete. He reminds Maya of the lessons her father taught her about controlling her breathing and staying calm under pressure. Then he brings up her mother, who was sent to prison for killing Maya's father. The man suggests that Maya has spent her whole life running from what happened that night and questions whether becoming a lawyer was her way of standing up to violent men because of her past. Maya refuses to talk about it, but he keeps pushing, even suggesting that she may be more like her mother than she wants to admit. The man reminds Maya that she has only 53 minutes left. As she follows his instructions, she slows down in a crowded street and notices how familiar he is with the area. From the way he describes her surroundings, Maya realizes that he must be local. She also recognizes the gun he gave her as the exact same weapon Tommy Boyd used to kill those women. The man knows how crucial Taffy's testimony is to Maya's case because without him, Tommy Boyd could walk free. Maya tells him she knows he isn't at home because she heard the piano in the background. She also suspects he has an accomplice who left Noah's school bag in the bin. At that moment, Maya gets a call from Noah's school. Before she can answer, the man takes over and uses an AI generated version of her voice to convince them that Noah is fine. Maya then keeps running and looks at the phones in people's hands hoping to find a way someone without the man knowing. She takes a different route calling it a shortcut and soon reaches busy street. Maya tries to snatch a girl's phone but fails. A moment later, she grabs an old man's phone only to find it locked with a passcode so she throws it away. She then snatches another phone and runs but the girl's boyfriend chases after her. Some men nearby mistake him for the person chasing Maya and stop him. Maya uses the chance to keep running and tries to contact Ted but she suddenly bumps into a child and falls. The phone slips from her hand and falls into the water. The man asks what happened. Maya then realizes that he has already hacked Ted's phone so she has no way to contact him without the man knowing. The man tells Maya that her mother is a killer and then asks if Maya is one too. Maya snaps back saying her mother is not a killer. He keeps pressing Maya to tell him what happened that night. Suddenly, a car hits her and she loses consciousness. Maya wakes up inside an ambulance with the man still talking to her. He orders her to get out and keep running. Maya jumps from the moving ambulance. The man then announces that she has only 35 minutes left. Maya asks for more time because her condition is getting worse but he refuses. Maya then breaks his rules and gets onto the tube. She turns on noise cancellation on her headphones so the man cannot hear what is happening around her. Maya sees a woman enter her passcode before putting the phone away then steals it. The man notices that Maya's pace has suddenly increased so she starts walking toward the other end of the train to make her speed appear slower. Maya notices that everyone's eyes are glued to their phones, but she spots one man reading a book. She approaches him and quietly slips something to him before getting off the train. The man realizes she has stopped running and asks if she's on the train, but the connection cuts before Maya can respond. She then realizes her phone has been stolen. Before she can react, the train starts moving. Maya races toward the next station desperate to catch the train. She pushes through the crowd without slowing down and reaches the platform just as the train arrives. She quickly gets inside with everyone around her staring. Maya asks the boy to give her phone back, but he laughs and refuses to take her seriously. She pulls out the gun, causing panic among the passengers, and the boy finally hands the phone back. Maya then spots a police officer who notices the gun and moves toward her. She heads to the back of the train as the officer calls for the emergency brake. Maya manages to get off and onto the railway tracks. She repeatedly calls the man, but he doesn't answer. As she runs along the tracks, another train suddenly approaches and Maya narrowly gets out of its way. Maya then climbs off the tracks and notices that the police are already searching for her. She ducks into an alley and tries calling the man again, but the call doesn't connect. Two officers approach her and Maya lies about why she is there. She spots an opportunity, slips away, and runs with the police chasing her. She eventually reaches a church and breaks down while thinking about Noah. A priest approaches her and tries to calm her down, but Maya notices the police officers coming and quickly leaves. After leaving the church, Maya gets a call from an unknown number. She answers, but it turns out to be some scam call. She suddenly realizes that her phone has been hacked, which means the man can clearly hear everything she says. Maya begs him to give her one more chance. The man calls back and tells Maya that she broke the rules. Maya begs him, saying she can still do it, But he tells her she is useless to him now because the police are onto them. He says he will have to deal with the situation himself, but it will be messy and could kill not only Noah, but many other people. He then says he was wrong about Maya all along. Maya finally reveals that she was the one who killed her father. The man becomes interested and asks her to tell him more. Maya explains what happened that night. Her father was drunk and beating her mother, so Maya took her target pistol and shot him. Her mother took the blame for the killing and went to prison, while no one knew that Maya was actually responsible. After hearing Maya's confession, the man gives her another chance and 15 minutes to finish the job. Maya immediately starts running again, but the police are already closing in around her. The man keeps guiding her through the streets and directs her toward another bridge. Maya begs him to stop the drip that is keeping Noah unconscious, but he refuses. He believes fear is what makes people do things they never would otherwise. As Maya reaches the area near the bridge, police officers begin surrounding her. The man tells her where to go, helping her avoid being caught. Maya spots a nearby shop, quickly grabs a cap and a t-shirt, and runs off. She finds some water, drinks it, changes her clothes, and checks the time. Only 8 minutes remain. Maya reaches the next bridge, but a police officer spots her and starts approaching. The man tells her to blend into the crowd, but the officer recognizes her. Maya pulls out her gun and aims it at him as people around them start recording on their phones. She takes the officer's radio, but armed police units soon arrive and surround her. With nowhere left to run, Maya jumps from the bridge. The man watches the moment through a live stream and believes she has gone into the water, but Maya has actually landed on a boat below. She slowly regains consciousness, points the gun at the boatman, and explains that her son is in danger. She asks him to take her to London Bridge, and he agrees. After reaching the area near HMS Belfast, Maya jumps onto the jetty and runs toward the hotel, where the security team is already preparing to escort Tafa to court. Maya enters the hotel and hears piano music playing. She realizes the man is inside the same building. With 267 rooms, finding him would be nearly impossible, but she knows she has to reach Noah while the man still expects her to kill Tafa. An officer stops Maya and asks why she is there. She says she is meeting a client and is running late. After checking her name, he lets her pass. In the lift, Maya checks the gun as the man instructs her, then turns on her phone and places it in her armband so he can see everything through the camera. She reaches Tafa's suite and shoots him. The man watches through the camera and gives Maya the room number where Noah is being held. Maya quickly leaves Tafa's suite and heads for Noah's room. At the same time, the man triggers the fire alarm and leaves his room. The entire hotel begins to evacuate, creating chaos as everyone mixes together. Maya breaks the lock and finds Noah lying on the bed. She immediately gives him the medicine he needs, and after a tense moment, Noah finally wakes up. Maya hugs him, relieved to see him conscious again. DI Phillips approaches Maya and tells her that the entire building has been sealed off. He asks if Noah can identify the man who kidnapped him, but Maya says Noah cannot remember anything. Ted then arrives, and Maya sends Noah away with him. Maya tells the police that the man has another plan involving a bomb. Suddenly, she panics and mistakenly thinks the paramedic approaching Noah could be the killer, so she pushes him away. Noah soon needs to use the washroom, so Maya takes him there with a constable. As they enter, Noah suddenly notices someone and wets his pants. Maya immediately understands that this is the man who kidnapped him. The man then sees Tafa alive and realizes Maya never killed him. Maya had already planned for this. Earlier, while she was on the train, she slipped a message to the man reading a book who then passed it on to Ted. Maya had also secretly written another message in lipstick. The police had prepared everything in advance. The gun Maya used in the lift was loaded with blanks us while blood pouches had been placed on Tafa to make it look like she had shot him. Tafa was safe and the whole scene was part of their plan to catch the man. Maya then confronts the man and fires the blank rounds at him. He is impressed that she managed to trick him. But the gunshots alert the nearby police. They quickly arrive and arrest him. With the man caught, Tafa gives his testimony leading to Tommy Boyd's arrest and conviction. Maya and Noah are finally safe. Later, Maya receives another call from an unknown number and immediately throws the phone away.

text: A wrestling match is taking place in a packed arena. Among the spectators is Daniel Kelner, a cybersecurity specialist who works for an intelligence company called Wardex. Daniel then ushers Jane into the car while Noah gravely says that if he reveals the information in the files, it won't do the world any good. >> How was the interrogations? >> History doesn't have a reset key. After ending the call, Daniel wonders aloud where they can stay safe for the night. Jane tells him she knows the perfect place. At Wardex, Boyd informs Noah that the Department of Defense wants an update on the stolen files. Noah instructs him to tell them it was just a minor security breach and that recovery efforts are already underway. Boyd then reports that 12 agents have failed to show up for work today and all of their desks have been cleared out. Noah realizes it's a carefully coordinated operation. He says that if Daniel hasn't released the files yet, then someone else is pulling the strings. Noah then asks Boyd to call Hugo Wakefield. Meanwhile, Jane takes Daniel to Saint Clara Monastery where Sister Mora warmly welcomes her. As Mora treats Jane's injuries, the two reminisce about old times. Once she's finished, Mora approaches Daniel and firmly tells him she won't ask who he is, but to leave Jane out of whatever trouble he's brought with him. >> You're a nun? >> We've had sex. Then he asks her why she never told him. Jane explains that people tend to judge. She then asks Daniel what exactly he stole. Daniel replies that he stole the data he was paid to protect because people have a right to know the truth. Curious, Daniel asks why she no longer wanted to be a nun. Jane says she lost her calling. She then asks how long he's worked for Wardex. Daniel reveals that he was recruited 8 years ago, right after he was released from federal prison, where he served 19 months for cyber crimes. >> Even with your record? >> Because of my record. >> Daniel admits that until 3 months ago, he didn't know half of what he knows now. He says the truth that Wordex discovered doesn't belong to them any more than air or water does. It belongs to all 8 billion people on Earth. The story then shifts to Margaret, a weather reporter for KCXE. Her boyfriend Jackson is watching one of her weather segments on his laptop. >> I asked you not to watch those. >> It's great. >> Jackson reassures her that she's great, but jokingly points out that she got the forecast wrong because she predicted hail. Yet, it's perfectly clear outside. Margaret then asks if he watched her audition tape for the weekend news anchor position. Jackson admits he hasn't yet, so he starts the video but stops it halfway through, telling her it was good. Margaret thoughtfully says they need to move. Clearly frustrated, Jackson asks, "Again?" She explains that she wants to move to a bigger city with a larger media market. Jackson reminds her they already moved from Dallas to Kansas, but Margaret admits she never felt she belonged in Dallas. Jackson calmly tells her that he's built a successful music career in Kansas and argues that moving to a new city isn't the solution to every problem. Just then, a cardinal flies in through the window. Jackson asks if she's okay, but suddenly she begins speaking fluent Russian. Completely confused, Jackson asks how she knows Russian. Margaret switches back to English and insists that she never spoke Russian. Then she says she's late for work and quickly leaves. Margaret is singing along to a song while driving when a police officer pulls her over for speeding. Looking at him, Margaret calmly says he's having a bad day. She tells him his wife didn't mean to snap at him and is only sleep deprived from taking care of the baby. She then suggests he bring her the red velvet cupcakes she loves. Margaret reassures him that he doesn't regret having the baby and that he's nothing like his father. The officer is left speechless as Margaret drives away. At the news station, the reporters are covering the escalating global crisis, explaining that World War III appears to be imminent as Russia and the United States prepare to launch missiles if ordered. While civilians living near key military installations have already begun evacuating. Margaret arrives at the station where her boss, Clay, is clearly unhappy that she's late. Back at Wardex, Defense General Dobbs is furious about the stolen data and offers to deploy 12,000 FBI field agents to hunt Daniel down. Just then, one of the agents informs Noah that a viral clip of a local weather reporter from Kansas has begun circulating online. He then asks whether her voice matched the dialect samples in the files. >> Yes, and it matched. >> At a hospital, Margaret undergoes an MRI scan. After reviewing the results, the doctor tells her that everything appears normal. Margaret asks if she's certain, insisting that something is happening to her. The doctor asks whether she's been under a lot of stress, but Margaret shakes her head. >> Your father had Parkinson's? >> Are you saying that's what it is? >> No, no, not necessarily. >> Margaret tells her that her father was 47 years old when he died, and that she was only a teenager at the time. Looking outside, she asks if the men outside are watching them. The doctor replies that they're FBI agents who simply have a few questions for her. Quietly, Margaret says they aren't really FBI agents. The doctor then asks whether Margaret ever received counseling after the traumatic incident she experienced when she was 10 years old. Margaret glances at Jackson, assuming he must have told the doctor about it. She explains that she barely remembers what happened because she was only 10 at the time. The doctor presses further, asking whether she has nightmares related to the incident. Margaret says no, but Jackson admits that she has them all the time. They involve butterflies, a Hansel and Gretel-style house in the woods, and that she even sings children's songs in her sleep. Frustrated, Margaret asked Jackson why he would tell the doctor all of that. He shrugs. A moment later, Margaret suddenly says that they want someone named David Kelner dead. She quietly asked Jackson to pretend she needs help getting to the bathroom. Jackson asks what she's doing, but she insists they need to leave immediately. She then looks at him. >> Oh, you got to be kidding me. >> Meanwhile, Daniel and Jane arrive at the safe house. Once inside, Daniel notices a group of deer staring at him. Jane then asks him to explain what's going on. Daniel reveals that Wardex stands for waved reporting, development, and extraction. She asks who was with Nixon. Daniel replies that it was a popular TV star from the 1950s whom Nixon wanted to impress. Jane watches as medical technicians pull the sheets off several aliens. Daniel connects another drive, revealing footage of an alien named Inviwo 10 being subjected to a painful medical procedure without anesthesia while crying out in agony. Noah warns the technicians to be careful, reminding them that they had already lost another alien during the same procedure. He tells Jane that the remaining drives contain 79 more years worth of data. He also reveals that Wardex, along with the Department of Defense, has been reverse engineering alien technology since the early 1970s without any government funding. He explains that the technology they've developed is incredibly profitable, but in the wrong hands, it could become a devastating weapon. >> What are you going to do? >> Full disclosure. To the whole world. >> But she warns that people may begin to see the aliens as deities and abandon their faith in God. Daniel points out that she left the church. Jane replies that she didn't leave because she stopped believing in God, but because she could no longer say with certainty that God is truly divine. Even so, she says God is essential because he holds civilization together. She argues that with World War III already looming, exposing the truth now would only trigger panic and chaos. Ignoring her warning, Daniel says he's going to contact Hugo, picks up the bag, and leaves. At Wardex, Boyd retrieves the device from cold storage and warns Noah that only Hugo knows how to operate it, as he's the only person who has ever formed a relationship with an alien. Noah simply orders him to give the device. Using the device, Noah attempts to take control of Daniel's mind, but the attempt fails, leaving him in excruciating pain. Concerned, Boyd asks what happened. Noah says that he saw Daniel's face for only a split second before it felt as though all the air had been sucked out of his lungs. Boyd suggests that Daniel might be an experiencer, meaning someone who has had direct contact with an alien, which explains why he can't be mind controlled. Thinking quickly, Boyd decides to mind control Jane. Back with Margaret, they successfully escape the hospital. Just then, she receives a call from an unknown number. It's Hugo. >> I have been waiting a very long time to meet you, Miss Fairchild. >> Confused, she asks him who he is. Hugo simply replies, "A friend." Adding that she should already know who he is. Margaret says she has no idea who he is and admits that she's frightened out of her wits. >> Because you're just a passenger on your way somewhere. >> Hugo tells her to let them help her get there. He adds that they've known about her all along, but waited until they saw the news report before reaching out. Out of nowhere, Margaret asks Hugo who 8732626 is. Hugo calmly replies that she already knows. "Daniel Kelner." Margaret whispers. Hugo then tells her to trust her instincts and advises her to go in the direction she feels inclined to. Before ending the call, he instructs her to destroy the phone so no one else can track her. Margaret asks how he'll be able to find her afterward. Hugo simply replies that he has confidence she will find them. Margaret immediately throws the phone out of the car window. Jackson shouts that it cost $600, but she ignores him and tells him to run over the phone. Then, Margaret asks him to drive north. Confused, Jackson asks why. She says that's where Daniel is. Frustrated, Jackson asks if Daniel is someone from her past. >> I think I don't know what I'm doing here. I don't know who he is. I just know he's someplace north. >> Daniel contacts Hugo. Hugo tells him to watch the video he just sent. >> She's the one we've been waiting for. >> Her? >> Did you not hear her? >> Don't be afraid of what you don't know. That's all she had to say? >> But, Hugo explains that they couldn't understand it because it wasn't in English. Daniel laughs and tells him that it actually was English. Hugo then tells Daniel that he'll send a car the following morning to take him to Kansas City, where the woman is from, and instructs him to stay at a local motel for the night. >> There are two of you, Daniel. >> Meanwhile, Noah successfully places Jane under mind control. Noah suddenly appears before her. He casually greets her and asks her to take a seat before questioning her about her location. Jane tightly clutches the cross and says she doesn't know where she is. As Jane grips the cross even tighter, she manages to sever Noah's psychic connection with her. The agents notice that Noah's heart rate and sodium levels are rapidly rising. Concerned, they urge him to stop, but Noah simply reestablishes the connection. This time, he sternly asked Jane where she was the previous night. >> Monastery of Saint Claire of the Dawn. >> He then asked whether they passed any street signs. >> Sykesville. >> What else did you pass? >> A river. >> Using Jane's answers, the agents narrow down Daniel's location to a remote farmhouse. Noah immediately deploys a team of agents to capture them. He then asks Jane for a favor. If his agents don't get the chance to kill Daniel, she must do it herself because the world cannot handle the information Daniel is about to reveal. Jane breaks the connection once again, but Noah again takes control of her mind and mentally compels her to pick up the chopping knife. At the same time, Margaret senses that Daniel is in danger. She immediately asked Jackson for his phone. Jackson, annoyed, asks if she's going to throw his phone away, too. Ignoring the remark, Margaret calls Daniel. >> They found you. I don't know who you are and I don't know who they are, but they're going to kill you. They are going to kill you, Daniel. >> GIVE ME MY PHONE. DANIEL, GIVE ME MY PHONE. >> Daniel notices that Ward-X agents have surrounded the entire farmhouse. Thinking fast, he sneaks into one of the agents' vehicles and crashes it straight into the house. He quickly gets Jane into the car and speeds away. Several Ward-X vehicles immediately give chase. During the pursuit, Noah regains control of Jane's mind and compels her to stab Daniel with the chopping knife. Just as she's about to strike, one of the pursuing vehicles slams into the car, causing her to lose her grip and drop the knife. Jane drives the knife into her own hand. The intense pain breaks Noah's control. One of the agents picks up the device, but he suddenly loses consciousness. Another agent picks it up moments later, but this time nothing happens. Soon after, the agents open fire on Daniel and Jane. Jane apologizes for nearly stabbing him. Daniel reassures her, saying that he knew Noah was the one controlling her. Eventually, they reach a dead end. Daniel grabs Jane's arm and tells her to run, but she stops him. Instead, she places a rock on the accelerator, sending the empty car plunging into the water, making it appear as though they had driven off the edge and drowned. Sometime later, Margaret and Jackson stop at a gas station where panicked people are stocking up on supplies as fears of World War III continue to spread. Margaret says they need to find Daniel. Jackson argues that they should go back to the hospital instead. >> If I moved, you'd stay. >> What? >> Kansas City, you want me to move, you're going to stay. >> Claiming he needs to buy some water, Jackson heads into the store. Once inside, he calls the doctor and tells him that Margaret's condition is getting worse. He says he'll bring her back to the hospital as soon as possible. Minutes later, Jackson returns from the store only to discover that Margaret is gone. >> She said to say she loves you, but she's going east. >> That night, Daniel and Jane check into a motel. Daniel asks Hugo why he has to go to Kansas City, but Hugo remains silent. Daniel then admits that he's starting to remember strange things. Friendly, yet terrifying animals staring at him, leaving him unable to look away no matter how hard he tries. >> It wasn't your idea to recruit me, What it? Not just for this, but but to Wardex in the first place. >> No. >> He goes on to say that there are parts of his childhood he simply can't remember and that the missing memories frighten him. Hugo reassures him telling him not to worry because he'll be there for him along with someone else. He then instructs Daniel to go to KCXE news station the following morning. Fearing Noah might mind control Jane again, Daniel removes anything that could reveal their location. He then asks Jane to listen to the recording Hugo sent him. >> Do you understand what she's saying? >> I hear it it's gibberish. I can't understand it. >> But Daniel says he can understand it perfectly because it is mathematics, which his mind automatically translates into English. Then she asked Daniel to tie her up so she can't hurt him. Reluctantly, he agrees. At midnight, Noah mind controlled Jane and uses her to learn the motel's name. Not long afterward, Santiago arrives at the motel to pick them up. However, he stops when he sees several Wardex vehicles surrounding the motel and quickly drives away. >> We're burned. >> Daniel wakes Jane and tells her they've been found. He helps her escape through the bathroom window, hands her the device, and tells her to protect it at all costs. Jane begs him to come with her, but he tells her to go. Moments later, Wardex agents storm the room and capture Daniel. Jane escapes deep into the woods. After searching Daniel's bag, the agents realize the device is missing. They demand to know where it is, but Daniel simply smiles. Daniel is then taken to Blacksite military base. Noah gets straight to the point, first asking Daniel what he did with the device before asking him to reveal exactly what Hugo's operation is. Margaret finds Daniel's location. One of the agents stops her at the entrance. Margaret correctly states his name, Thomas, along with his ID number. The agent lets her pass. Inside the facility, Margaret comes face-to-face with Daniel. Using her new found ability, Margaret makes Noah see the person he desires most, his late wife, Jocelyn. Boyd tries to restrain Margaret, but Noah stops him and orders all the agents to stand down. Margaret grabs the bag with hard drives and tries to leave the base. Boyd orders the agents to stop them. However, Margaret uses her ability on several agents, causing them to let them pass without resistance. Surprised, Daniel asks how she knows all those people. Margaret simply replies, "I don't." Boyd grabs his gun and keys and sets off to kill them. As they drive away, Daniel asks Margaret where she's taking them. "Kansas City," she replies. When he asks why, she admits she doesn't know. Margaret then looks at him and says that he has been to jail before. Startled, he asks how she knows. She explains that whenever she looks at someone, she can suddenly see moments from their life and even feel the emotions they experienced. She tells Daniel that at that very moment, his injured shoulder is throbbing with pain, and that he's thinking about Jane. Margaret reveals that this strange ability only appeared the previous day after a bird flew through her window. Daniel asks, "A cardinal?" Surprised, Margaret asks how he knew. Daniel explains that when he was 20 and in college, he experienced something similar. >> Well, you were flunking out, basically. >> I was pretty smart. >> You were, but it was the partying. It was the partying and the drugs. I mean, ketamine, come on, dude. >> Can we stop? >> Sorry, I'm >> He clears his throat and continues. One day, while lying in bed, he felt as though someone was watching him. When he opened his eyes, he saw a cardinal perched on his window. From that moment on, everything changed. He suddenly began understanding complex patterns and entire arrays fully solved inside his mind. Margaret continues, saying that he hated it because his ability made him feel isolated until he met Jane. He smiles. >> Don't be afraid of what you don't know. >> That's what you said on TV. >> They said I was talking nonsense. >> I understood every word. >> Just then, Boyd catches up to them and repeatedly rams their vehicle toward a moving train. Their car becomes hooked onto the train. Daniel manages to climb out of the car and leaps onto the train's ladder as Boyd shoots at them. At the very last second, Margaret grabs Daniel's hand and the two barely manage to pull themselves aboard. Once inside the train, Margaret suddenly suffers a panic attack shouting that she can't feel her hands and that she's developing Parkinson's disease just like her father. Daniel eventually calms her down by placing her hands on the piano strings. She thanks him. Meanwhile, Hugo realizes that Noah is trying to get into his mind. He immediately tells his agents to leave the room. >> Kelner was an experience, wasn't it? >> Yes. >> And then Vivo 17 told you to recruit him. >> Yes. >> Noah argues that if Daniel is following the aliens' plan, then he is serving their interests, not humanity's. Hugo disagrees explaining that the aliens view empathy as an evolutionary advantage while humanity's inability to embrace it is driving civilization toward war and possible extinction. >> And is your bleeding heart why you helped to escape? >> Yes. >> Furious, Noah asks Hugo how he could lie to him for five years and when he lost his mind. Hugo calmly replies that it happened around the same time Noah lost his own mind when his wife died. >> died, you reduced everyone to need-to-know including me. And Vivo 17 is non-human but nearer to God Noah than you or I. You don't need to fear them. >> Noah insists that revealing the truth to the public would destroy the existing world order. Just then, two agents enter to report something urgent. Hugo quickly ushers them back outside, but Noah catches a glimpse of them. He immediately orders his team to pull up the files of the 12 employees who failed to report to work the previous day. Noah orders the agents to trace the last known locations of their phones and they do. At a local diner, Jane calls Maura and asks whether God only loves humans because Genesis describes them as his supreme creation. Mora gently corrects her, explaining that humanity is God's supreme creation on Earth. Jane then asks whether there could be other intelligent beings in the universe. Mora says she believes there probably are, reasoning that God would not create a universe so vast if it existed only for humans. Jane asks if it would frighten her if someone proved to her they weren't alone. Mora asks why it would. Jane asks Mora to see where KCXE is located, remembering it from the clip Daniel showed her. Curious, Daniel asks Margaret whether she remembers anything from her childhood. Margaret says she doesn't remember anything before the age of 10. Then, they notice a fox watching them. At that moment, Santiago arrives in a fire truck accompanied by several of Hugo's agents. They escort Daniel and Margaret to a hidden warehouse. Hugo greets Daniel, who hands him the bag containing the evidence. Hugo then asks Margaret whether she knows who he is. She says yes. Margaret then begins telling the names of every agent standing around her. Confused, she asks why her childhood home has been recreated inside the warehouse. Shaken, Margaret says she doesn't want to become anyone's religion. She slowly walks through the reconstructed house and enters her childhood bedroom. Looking at Hugo, she asks why he rebuilt it. >> To return you to your experience. >> Daniel asks Hugo what experience he means. Hugo replies that it's the one he shared with Margaret. He gently asks Margaret how much she remembers about that night. Margaret firmly says she doesn't want to remember. >> Everything that happened to you on the 23rd of February, 1996 is blocked. >> Hugo explains that only by unlocking those buried memories will she discover her true purpose and finally stop being a passenger. He tells her that what had remained dormant inside her only awakened the previous day. While Daniel's gift was activated 15 years ago, Hugo tells them that both of them were chosen by the aliens. He explains that the aliens gifted Daniel with an extraordinary understanding of mathematics so he could understand the aliens, while Margaret was gifted empathy so she could help them communicate with humanity. Hugo then hands them the device. He asks Margaret to look around the room and think back to when she was a 10-year-old girl asleep in her bed when something woke her up. Margaret continues saying that she sang her song. Then, a deer, a cardinal, a fox, and a raccoon approach young Margaret. Daniel instinctively shouts for young Margaret not to follow them, but Hugo calms him explaining that the aliens take the form of animals to appear non-threatening. Margaret remembers following the animals to a house, much like in Hansel and Gretel. Once inside, the animals shed their disguises and reveal their true alien forms. Young Margaret reassures a frightened Daniel that everything will be okay. Moments later, both children are imbued with extraordinary abilities. Outside, Wartex agents surround the warehouse. Boyd informs Noah that thermal imaging shows 43 heat signatures inside the building. >> They found us. >> Margaret asks Hugo to hand her the device. Using it, she cloaks the house and everyone in it. She quietly warns the group that the cloaking effect won't last long. She tells them they need to move slowly and carefully. At that moment, Noah hears a faint noise and orders his agents to investigate the area. The group manages to reach the truck and escapes. A short while later, they arrive at the KCXE news station. Inside, the reporter warns that World War III is escalating with the European Union closing its borders amid concerns over a possible incoming missile strike. Margaret spots Clay and uses her power to convince him to let her go live at the anchor desk to deliver a special news report. He nods. Daniel asks Clay how to reach the control room, and Clay points him in the right direction. Then, Margaret's co-worker mentions that she and her daughter have moved out of her husband's house and are now living with her sister. Margaret smiles. In the control room, Daniel begins copying the data from the hard drives to the station's broadcast system. Outside, Noah orders his two teams to locate the station's main power supply and backup generator. They destroy the main power source, plunging the building into darkness. Seconds later, the emergency backup generator automatically kicks in. At that very moment, Jane also arrives at the news station. Just as Margaret is about to begin the broadcast, Noah's team shuts down the backup generator. Noah walks into the station. Moments later, Jane rushes toward Margaret and hands her the device, urging her to tell the truth. Using the device, Margaret restores power to the station. Boyd asks Noah if he's not going to stop them, but Noah quietly sits down. Frustrated, Boyd storms off. Margaret begins the broadcast, dubbing it Disclosure Day. Footage dating back to the infamous 1947 Roswell incident reveals that aliens were recovered and secretly experimented on for decades. She says that Wardex, along with the Department of Defense, has suppressed the data and conducted inhumane experiments on the aliens. Back in the control room, Daniel instructs the station director to contact the New York control center so other networks can carry the live broadcast. Before long, the feed is picked up worldwide and the rest of the world tunes in. Hugo then brings in In Vivo 17. The alien speaks to Daniel in its own language, and Daniel translates the message for Margaret. >> Listen.

text: Whatever you expect from an Alex Garland movie, he always gives you something else."Civil War" is something else again. It premiered in the US hours before I published this and it's already divisive. I look forward to reading all of the arguments for and against, even though both early raves and pans seem to be operating under the reductive assumption that it's one of three things: (1) an alternative future history of a divided United States that's intended as a cautionary tale; (2) a technically proficient but empty-headed misery porn compendium that derives much of its power from images redolent of genocide and/or lynching, but ducks political specifics so as not to offend reactionaries; or (3) a visionary spectacular with ultra-violence that might or might not have something important to say but will definitely look and sound great on an expensive home entertainment system. As it turns out, "Civil War" is mainly something else: a thought experiment about journalistic ethics, set in a future United States, yet reminiscent of classic movies about Western journalists covering the collapse of foreign countries, such as "The Year of Living Dangerously," "Salvador," "Under Fire," and "Welcome to Sarajevo." How utterly bizarre, you might think. And in the abstract, it is bizarre. But "Civil War" is a furiously convincing and disturbing thing when you're watching it. It's a great movie that has its own life force. It's not like anything Garland has made. It's not like anything anyone has made, even though it contains echoes of dozens of other films (and novels) that appear to have fed the filmmaker's imagination. Specifically, and most originally, "Civil War" is a portrait of the mentality of pure reporters, the types of people who are less interested in explaining what things "mean" (in the manner of an editorial writer or "pundit") than in getting the scoop before the competition, by any means necessary. Whether the scoop takes the form of a written story, a TV news segment, or a still photo that wins a Pulitzer, the quest for the scoop is an end unto itself, and it's bound up with the massive dopamine hit that that comes from putting oneself in harm's way. The kinds of obsessive war correspondents who rarely come back to their own countries don't care about the real-world impact of the political realities encoded within the epic violence they chronicle, or else compartmentalize it to stay focused. The main characters of "Civil War" are four journalists. The film introduces them covering a clash in New York City between what appear to be police forces from the official government and violent members of the opposition (we have to infer a lot because Garland drops you right into the deep end, as Haskell Wexler did in "Medium Cool," about a news cameraman covering the 1968 protests in Chicago). Kirsten Dunst plays Lee, a legendary white female photojournalist in the mold of her namesake Lee Miller. She's partnered with a South American-born reporter named Joel (Wagner Moura). Both work for Reuters news agency and are fond of Sammy (veteran character actor Stephen McKinley Henderson), an older African-American journalist who writes for “what’s left of the New York Times,” as Joel puts it; he walks slowly on a cane, definitely a liability when covering protests and battles. The group gains a fourth member, Jessie (Cailee Spaeny, the title character of "Priscilla"), a kind of junior version of Lee who idolizes her. Jessie charms the hard-drinking, on-the-prowl Joel and ends up joining the trio as they drive to Washington, D.C. in hopes of interviewing the president (Nick Offerman) before he surrenders to the military forces of something called the WA, or Western Alliance. The WA consists of militias from California and Texas (with secondary support from Florida, which is apparently a different separatist group that shares the WA's values). The first full-length trailer for "Civil War" got picked apart as if it were the movie itself rather than an advertisement for it (a weird regular occurrence in "film discourse," such as it is). But the actual movie turns out to be more politically astute and plausible than early reactions said, even though it's likely that Garland's "you already know the story" approach (like the way the overall arc of the US occupation of Vietnam was depicted in "Full Metal Jacket") will seem to validate the gripes for the first hour. Yes, it's true, Texas votes Republican in national elections and California votes Democratic, but as of this writing, Northern California is increasingly controlled by libertarian-influenced tech billionaires, and much of central and eastern California leans Republican and loathes California Democrats so much that they've advocated "divid(ing) parts of coastal California, including the Bay Area, from California to become an independent country." The president is referred to as a fascist. I’m not sure how literally we’re supposed to take that because both Trump and Biden have been called that by people who don’t like them. But if you had to make a list of what "Civil War" is trying to do, "diagnosing what ails the United States of America" might not crack the Top 5. Yes, if you wanted to treat the movie so reductively, you could. But if you pay attention to what the movie is actually doing rather than cherry picking elements that validate whatever take you brought in with you, it won't be easy. I went into "Civil War" with arms folded, expecting to hate it, because so many contemporary films about US politics by foreign filmmakers seem to have cribbed their worldview from New York Times editorials and bad Tweets. It upended my preconceived notions. As far as "future shock" goes, Garland, an Englishman, isn't cynically avoiding specifics or talking out of his behind. He's burying the text under subtext, in the name of creating a compelling but credible experience, until said text explodes through the screen via Jesse Plemons, who has a cameo as a soldier who might or might not be a Western Front officer but is surely a parasite on the remnants of the body politic. This soft-voiced, smirky hellion interrogates the terrified group of journalists (which consists of two white women, a native-born Black man, and a South American emigre, plus an Asian-American and a Chinese immigrant who joined them on the road) with all the delicacy of Gene Hackman's racist white cop Popeye Doyle terrorizing Black people in "The French Connection" for kicks. A terse line of dialogue reveals that Lee became famous for taking a prize-winning photo of something called the "Antifa massacre" when Jessie was very young. "Antifa massacre" is initially tossed off in a way that makes you wonder if Garland is hoping progressives will assume it was anti-fascists who were murdered by reactionaries, but reactionaries will assume it was the reverse. Thanks to Plemons' demonic showstopper and the thunderous, ultimately chilling finale (set during the attempted coup in Washington) I think it's clear what happened. But your mileage will vary. Nevertheless, these characters aren't constantly exposition-ing to each other and explaining the world to the viewer because that's not what people would do in real life, whether they were trying to survive mass extinction in Gaza or Ukraine or endure a military dictatorship in Argentina or Myanmar. Indeed, one of the most fascinating (or if you don't like it, perplexing) aspects of "Civil War" is that it often plays like an artifact warped into our world from some future popular culture that has decided it's finally time for a "big statement" movie in the vein of "Apocalypse Now" or "Full Metal Jacket," but for people who remember an American Civil War and have enough perspective to consider buying a ticket to a blockbuster about it. Garland is known as mainly a science fiction storyteller. He wrote "28 Days Later," "Sunshine" and "Dredd," adapted "Never Let Me Go" from Kazuo Ishiguro's novel, and wrote and directed "Ex Machina" and "Annihilation," all of which had an intense and believable physicality on top of dealing in metaphors and visceral experiences. (He also did the gender essentialist horror flick "Men," which some people defend but that I consider his only failure.) "Civil War" isn't science fiction, exactly, nor could it be described mainly as "speculative fiction," although it falls under that umbrella. The world-building is masterful. But the world-building is not the movie. I appreciated it as a story about journalists whose own country is cratering but who keep chasing the story and are determined to catch it even if it kills them. Would they have embedded themselves with Hitler's army if they'd somehow survived behind enemy lines in Germany in the 1940s and been given the opportunity? I wouldn't rule it out. They will probably come across as unlikable, or at least off-putting, to most viewers—the New York Times and other supposedly "neutral" mainstream outlets have come under fire in recent years for seeming to give the rise of American fascism the "both sides" treatment, and when their reporters are called out, they often say that their only duty is to tell the story. Certain members of certain professions have that code. Other members disagree. Both factions are represented in "Civil War," but in a fictionalized context that asks "Is the storyteller's highest obligation to tell what happened or choose a side?" and then lets the audience fight over the answer. A case could be made that the title is not just about the civil war in the future US, but within contemporary journalism. I've purposefully avoided describing a lot of the story in this review because I want people to go in cold, as I did, and experience the movie as sort of picaresque narrative consisting of set pieces that test the characters morally and ethically as well as physically, from one day and one moment to the next. Suffice to say that the final section brings every thematic element together in a perfectly horrifying fashion and ends with a moment of self-actualization I don't think I'll ever be able to shake.

text: The first Sonic the Hedgehog film introduces the titular Sonic, a blue hedgehog with supersonic speed living on an alien planet. When a tribe of villainous echidnas arrive to try and steal his powers, Sonic’s guardian, Longclaw the Owl, gives Sonic a bag of magical rings that open portals to other planets. Sonic uses the rings to travel to Earth while Longclaw stays behind to battle the echidnas. Ten years later, Sonic is living in secret near the small town of Green Hills, Montana. Sonic feels lonely and fantasizes coming out from hiding and befriending the town’s sheriff, Tom Wachowski, and Tom’s wife, Maddie. Little does Sonic know that his fantasy life will soon be disrupted as Tom is accepting a position to join the San Francisco Police Department. In a state of depression, Sonic begins running in circles at high speeds, accidentally creating an electromagnetic pulse which causes a large-scale power outage. The United States Department of Defense sends the eccentric and villainous Dr. Robotnik, alongside his assistant, Agent Stone, to investigate. Sonic flees from his pursuers and finally crosses paths with Tom Wachowski. When Tom shoots Sonic with a tranquilizer dart, the hedgehog accidentally drops his bag of magic rings through a portal leading to the top of the Transamerica Pyramid, a giant skyscraper in San Francisco. Tom agrees to help Sonic retrieve the rings, and the two head off to San Francisco with Dr. Robotnik in hot pursuit. Along the way, Tom and Sonic begin to bond, and Tom helps Sonic cross many items off of his bucket list. Robotnik manages to recover one of Sonic’s quills and uses it to harness Sonic’s energy to power his robotic machines. Realizing the depths of Sonic’s powers, Robotnik’s mission to capture Sonic becomes personal as he wants all of the power for himself. In San Francisco, Tom and Maddie help Sonic recover his rings, all while being attacked by Robotnik and his army of robotic drones. Using the rings, Sonic is pursued by Robotnik through various locations all around the world, eventually leading them all back to Green Hills. Tom, Maddie, and the people of Green Hills, including Tom’s dim-witted deputy Wade Whipple, rally around Sonic. And when Tom tells Sonic that he is his friend, it gives Sonic enough energy to defeat Robotnik, kicking him through a portal into a mushroom planet. Following their victory, Tom and Maddie decide to stay in Green Hills and officially invite Sonic to move in with them. The US government rewards them by keeping Sonic’s existence a secret and also gives the Wachowski’s a gift card to their favorite restaurant, Olive Garden. Because when you’re here, you’re family. Meanwhile, Robotnik swears to enact his revenge on his hedgehog nemesis, while a super-powered fox named Tails arrives on Earth in search of Sonic.
