In Sonic 2, the titular hedgehog has spent the last eight months living happily with the Wachowskis, while also trying and failing to use his powers as a vigilante hero. After Tom and Maddie leave to attend Maddie’s sister Rachel's wedding in Hawaii, Sonic is attacked by Dr. Robotnik, who has escaped the mushroom planet thanks to the aid of an echidna warrior known as Knuckles. While Robotnik wants to harness Sonic’s power, Knuckles wants to learn the location of the Master Emerald, which grants its user unlimited power and can change the very fabric of reality itself. Sonic is rescued from the attack by the superpowered fox Tails, a massive fan of the hedgehog who aspires to be like him. Sonic and Tails team up to find and protect the Master Emerald, and seek refuge with the bumbling acting sheriff Wade Whipple. At Wade’s home, Sonic learns from a message from Longclaw the Owl the location of a compass that leads to the emerald, and so, Sonic and Tails use their rings to travel to Siberia to find it. Robotnik and Knuckles track the heroic duo, and Knuckles reveals that his tribe of echidnas, including his father, had attacked Longclaw to obtain the emerald’s location, but Longclaw had killed them all and burned down their village to keep the emerald’s power safe and unused. And so, Knuckles has sought revenge ever since. As Knuckles and Robotnik steal the compass, the overpowered Sonic and Tails are rescued by Tom, who helps them escape via a ring portal to Rachel’s wedding in Hawaii. Unfortunately, the Wachowskis discover that Rachel’s fiance, Randall, alongside most of their wedding guests, are all undercover agents from a task force known as GUN, whose mission is to protect the world from extraterrestrial threats. Believing Sonic and Tails to be threats to humanity, they capture the duo and arrest Tom as their accomplice. Maddie and Rachel then rescue their friends, though Rachel does reconcile with Randall when he swears his feelings for her were always real. As Robotnik and Knuckles follow the compass to an underwater temple, Sonic chooses to pursue them alone, worried that the mission would only put the young Tails in danger. As Sonic and Knuckles fight for control of the emerald, Robotnik betrays Knuckles and steals it for himself, destroying the temple as he flees. Sonic and Knuckles are forced to work together to survive and escape the temple, before being rescued by Tails. Robotnik travels back to Green Hills and reunites with his loyal assistant, Agent Stone, using his new emerald powers to create a giant Eggman Robot. Sonic, Tails, and Knuckles all return to Green Hills and battle Eggman together, but as they try to reclaim the Master Emerald, it shatters into seven shards. Sonic uses these pieces to transform himself into Super Sonic, using his new, enhanced powers to destroy Eggman, and seemingly kill Robotnik along with his creation. Following the battle, Knuckles restores the shards back into the Master Emerald and vows to protect it from evil, alongside his new allies Sonic and Tails. Together, the three friends are finally able to live in peace alongside the Wachowskis. In a post-credit scene, Agent Stone avoids arrest by posing as a GUN operative, where he learns that the agency has just discovered the location of the mysterious and highly classified Project Shadow. The story continues in the spin-off television series, Knuckles, which finds the titular echidna struggling to adapt from his warrior lifestyle to a simpler life in the suburbs. To find a new purpose in life, Knuckles chooses to take on the bumbling Deputy Wade Whipple as his apprentice. The pair travel together to Reno, Nevada for a bowling tournament, where Knuckles teaches Wade how to be a warrior, and Wade confides in Knuckles about his constant struggles over being abandoned by his father at a young age. As Knuckles and Wade bond, they are pursued by corrupt GUN agents Mason and Willoughby, who plot to capture Knuckles and sell him to a mysterious Buyer. The agents use an array of superweapons, powered by Knuckles’ quills. As Knuckles and Wade are forced to battle the villainous GUN agents, the chaos that ensues results in Wade being branded a fugitive, forcing he and Knuckles to hide out in Wade’s childhood home. There, Knuckles helps Wade reconcile with his mother and sister, Wendy and Wanda, and learns that the reason for Wade’s desire to compete in the bowling tournament is because his absent father, Pistol Pete, is a bowling champion who will also be competing. And so, as Wade helps Knuckles evade his GUN pursuers, Knuckles helps prepare Wade for the bowling tournament, teaching him to believe in his own inner strength. In Reno, Wade reunites and reconciles with his father, though Wade’s mother, Wendy, warns of Pete’s duplicitous nature. As Wade advances through the bowling tournament, he secures a spot in the final round against his very own father. Fearing his son will beat him in the bowling tournament, Pete rats out his own family to Mason and Willoughby, who hold Wendy and Wanda hostage to force Wade into betraying Knuckles. But Wade remains a loyal friend, helping Knuckles defeat the GUN agents and rescue his family. With the agents defeated, Wade returns to the tournament, where he defeats his father to win the first place trophy. Unfortunately, they are interrupted by the Buyer arriving in a giant robotic mech suit to fight Knuckles. The newly united Wade, Wanda, and Wendy work together to help Knuckles defeat the Buyer once and for all. The traitorous Pete tries to flee with the bowling trophy in the chaos, but is thwarted by Wanda and Wendy. And so, in the end, Knuckles celebrates his victory with the Whipple family, finally accepting Earth as his home and its people as worthy of his protection.

text: At the beginning of the movie, we see a group of friends who have come to the Catskills to celebrate Elise's birthday. While there, they also learn that Haley and Grant have recently broken up. After some time, they realize they have consumed all the beer, and it cannot be delivered to the mansion they rented. Paxton suggests that he is sure the place has booze locked up somewhere, and they all start searching the mansion for it. During this, they find a door with a "Keep Out" sign on it, which they ignore, and Lucas breaks the door to get in. They enter the basement but find no alcohol there. However, they discover that the basement is filled with creepy stuff, and Haley tells them that it is all old astrological equipment. Meanwhile, Paxton finds a box of strange tarot cards and shows them to the others. Elise asks Haley to do a reading for everyone, and she agrees but comments that the cards look hand-painted and she has never seen cards like these before. She explains that each zodiac sign is represented by a card in the Major Arcana, and by incorporating the planets into the reading, it becomes more accurate. Just before they start, a gust of wind blows, startling them all. Haley suggests they shouldn't proceed, explaining that it's an unspoken rule not to use someone else's deck. However, when Elise insists, saying it's her birthday, Haley reluctantly agrees to do it. She explains that there are 12 tarot cards placed in a circle representing the zodiac, with a very important 13th card in the center, which indicates the overall theme of the reading and can provide clarity to the other cards. Elise, being a Libra, often has her curiosity leading her into the unknown. She is climbing the ladder toward success, but the High Priestess reversed is a warning to perhaps slow down. Rushing could cause her to slip up and suffer a crushing blow. Next, she does Madeline's reading and tells her that when she senses danger, she tends to run, which makes sense because her zodiac symbol is two fish swimming away from each other. However, this month, she should fight that urge and try not to get hung up on things. Meanwhile, when Paxton goes to the washroom, he notices a figure standing outside, but it disappears when the lights suddenly turn on. Here, Haley tells Paige that as a Virgo, she always wants to find logic in things, but this month, that might be challenging. Paige may feel like she is being pulled in two directions because the Magician's bag of tricks is deceptive and will prevent her from seeing clearly. Paxton returns, and upon their request for Grant to have his card readings, he declines. Subsequently, Paxton opts for a card reading, during which Haley informs him that the reversed Fool card serves as a caution against acting impulsively. She advises him to remain close to those he trusts and warns him not to be startled if he feels confined or restricted. Next, she tells Lucas that as a Capricorn, he is a rule breaker, down-to-earth, and also sensitive. She mentions that she foresees a change in his financial situation and that love is in the air. However, the reversed Hermit card can indicate poor judgment and serves as a warning to be mindful of his direction. While he is someone who will go out of his way for love, he should remain focused, as the Hermit's light could lead him down the wrong path. Finally, Grant agrees to have his readings, and Haley tells him that as a Leo, he is generous, loyal, and a natural leader. However, Leos can also be headstrong, arrogant, and always feel the need to be right. Grant thinks she is making things up and starts to leave, but Haley stops him and explains that the Devil card represents his shadow side. He is walking a very dark path, and this month he will need to face his demons and make a sacrifice, or he risks losing someone important. Haley then draws cards to read her own horoscope, which reveals that love will be the death of her. The next day, the group returns to campus, where Elise is staying in her dorm alone because everyone else has gone to a frat party. While on the phone with Paige, she comes out of the bathroom and is startled to see a ladder leading to the attic. She calls out to check if anyone is upstairs, and when she gets no response, she closes the attic and goes into her room. After some time, Elise is startled by a sound and hears someone laughing outside. Thinking that some girls have returned, she goes out to check and is shocked to see the ladder again. A figure briefly appears behind her before disappearing. Elise thinks Natalie and Claire are trying to scare her because she can hear someone running and laughing in the attic. She climbs the stairs to check, but when she doesn't see anyone there, she becomes a little scared, and suddenly, some movement increases her fear further. The dorm lights start flickering, and she hears someone laughing from downstairs, but she can't see anyone. When she looks back up, the atmosphere in the attic has changed. She sees the High Priestess card in front of her, and as soon as she picks it up, an entity haunts her, causing her to fall. The entity pulls the stairs up, and when Elise tries to reach her phone, an unseen force drags her back. Terrified, as Elise attempts to flee, the entity bludgeons her to death with the ladder. The next day, all of Elise's friends are shocked and saddened by the news of her death, and since Paige is the most affected by this, Haley decides to stay with her for the night. Later, Paige suddenly wakes up from a nightmare, and when Haley tries to calm her down, Paige tells her that she keeps seeing Elise's face every time she closes her eyes and believes Elise would still be alive if she had been there. Haley explains that whatever was going to happen would have happened regardless. She shares that she grew up in an old house in Minnesota. Her dad left before she was born, so it was just her and her mom. Her mom got sick, and despite trying numerous treatments, nothing worked. That’s when she got into Tarot. She couldn’t stop death, and she doesn’t want Paige to blame herself for what happened to Elise. Meanwhile, the entity appears behind Lucas but disappears when he turns around to check. There, he steps on a newspaper that reads, "You die today," and is shocked to see his photo printed on it. As he tries to comprehend the situation, the horoscope that Haley had mentioned starts echoing around him, and before he can make sense of anything, the entity haunts him. In an attempt to save his life, Lucas boards a train and hides, but the entity haunts him again, leading to his death by a speeding train. The next day, the friends are shocked to learn about Lucas' death, and Paige suggests they stay together that night for safety. Haley observes that each death corresponds to the tarot readings, leading the group to suspect something is wrong with the deck, though Grant remains openly skeptical. Paxton suggests they need an expert or someone who understands what's going on, and when Haley searches about the dangers of horoscopes, they come across the name Alma Astron, an expert on the occult and tarot readings. They read an article and learn that a group of people in Mexico died after a reading. The group decides to visit Alma Astron, but she initially asks them to leave. Haley explains that their friends are dying because of their readings, and if they don't do something, they are going to die too. Hearing this, Alma opens the door. Haley explains that two of their friends have died exactly as their horoscopes predicted. Alma asks to see the deck, but Haley admits she doesn't have it because she doesn't own it. Alma asks Haley if the cards were in a wooden box with a zodiac wheel on it? Haley confirms and insists Alma explain what's happening. Alma explains that these cursed cards are responsible for several tarot reading group massacres, including an incident in London that she narrowly survived because she did everyone's readings but her own, and since then, she has been looking for those cards to destroy them. She then reveals that the cards belonged to an astrologer in the late 18th century who served a Hungarian Count, predicting the future for him. After a reading predicted the Count’s pregnant wife and child would die in childbirth, and this came true, the grief-stricken Count accused the astrologer of witchcraft and ordered his men to kill her daughter. Enraged with grief, the astrologer performed a reading on the Count and his close friends, dooming them to death, and then killed herself. She bound her soul to the cards, sealing their fate and hers. Not long after, the count and those closest to him died horrible deaths. She got her revenge but cursed the cards and inverted the zodiac, and now anyone who has their horoscope read using those cards will have to face the dark side of fate. She urges the group to destroy the deck, which is still at the mansion if they want a chance at survival. While driving to the mansion, their car breaks down for no apparent reason and stops on a bridge. They become worried because, according to Haley's reading for Madeline, technology will fail unexpectedly. Madeline freaks out, and soon after, she notices a hanged man being drawn on the window. Terrified, Madeline runs out of the car, and the others sense an entity circling their vehicle. They then see the entity rushing toward Madeline with a rope, and meanwhile, when Haley tries to stop Madeline, suddenly a noose falls around Madeline's neck, and before she can react, the entity pulls her up. Grant and other reaches there, only to see Madeline's lifeless body hanging there before the entity pulls her up once again. They all get terrified and run away from there and after going some distance Paxton decides to leave, stating that he's done with all of this. On his way back to the campus, Paxton gets startled when he hears someone laughing, but finds no one when he turns around. Scared, he tries to flee, but to his horror, he sees the reflection of the fool on the door, and his terror intensifies when he sees the fool standing in the distance, staring at him. Paxton, terrified, enters the elevator to escape the danger, but notices the ascending numbers, and he is boxed in, just as Haley had described in his horoscope. As the door opens, Paxton finds the fool standing right in front of him, and before he can react, the fool enters the elevator and attacks Paxton, ultimately killing him. On the other hand, Paige books the mansion, and they revisit it. From a website, she reads that some cursed objects need to be physically destroyed, while others have a connection that needs to be severed, and the best way to remove an ancient curse from an object is through destruction by incineration. Haley throws the cards and the box into the fireplace to destroy them, but they are shocked to see that the cards are not burning. They call Alma for help and explain that something resembling The Hanged Man has killed their friend. Alma reveals that the astrologer embodies the cards like a shapeshifter, bringing the final outcome card to life. Alma tells them they need to turn what the astrologer created against her by separating the astrologer's spirit from the cards. She attempts to communicate with the astrologer, and after a while, she successfully summons her. Haley notices that Alma is bleeding, and Alma tells her she can't move. The astrologer then rises and takes control of the cards, and Alma explains that the astrologer is reading her horoscope. The astrologer draws the Six of Swords, and soon after, Alma is dragged into the darkness. Terrified, the friends try to flee, but their horror intensifies when Alma's lifeless body falls in front of them. During their escape, Paige accidentally gets separated from Grant and Haley, but she hears Haley's voice coming from the basement, calling for help. As she enters the basement, the door slams shut behind her, and Haley's voice turns demonic. The light then begins flickering before the bulb explodes, and Paige then encounters The Magician, who traps her in a box and saws her in half. Upstairs, Grant and Haley discuss how to undo the curse. Haley suggests that if she reads the astrologer's horoscope, they might be able to turn the curse back on her. Grant is hesitant about the idea, but Haley insists, saying they are already as good as dead, so they have to try. Eventually, Haley lets go of her mother's grief and the astrologer's spirit. As a result, the spirit is consumed by the curse and is burnt alongside the deck. Haley and Grant reconcile over their survival and relationship and start to make their way home. On the way, they reunite with Paxton, who had survived his ordeal after his roommate, Todd, opened the elevator door at the last second, which made The Fool disappear.

text: Anemone 2025 arrives as one of the most intriguing ocean-based survival horror thrillers of recent years, blending science fiction, environmental caution, and human drama into one visually striking narrative. While the film itself doesn't belong to a direct franchise, it draws inspiration from the long tradition of aquatic horror movies like The Abyss, The Meg, and even earlier classics such as Jaws. In that sense, it feels like a spiritual continuation of the genre, where the ocean is not just a backdrop, but a living, breathing antagonist. The story builds on themes of humanity's arrogance in experimenting with nature, hinting at familiar lessons from past films while creating its own identity with a mysterious creature born out of both beauty and terror. The plot centers on a group of scientists and explorers who stumble upon an everbeforeseen species of sea anemone deep within uncharted waters. What begins as a groundbreaking discovery soon spirals into chaos when the organism reveals its terrifying ability to mutate and prey on anything in its path. The movie excels at building suspense using the ocean's vast emptiness and suffocating pressure tools of fear. The underwater cinematography is gorgeous with bioluminescent visuals that contrast sharply with moments of pure horror, making anemone stand out as both breathtaking and terrifying. The performances add emotional depth with characters wrestling not only with the physical danger of the creature, but also with moral dilemmas about science, greed, and survival. On the positive side, Anemone 2025 shines with its stunning visuals, creative creature design, and atmospheric tension that makes you feel as if you are submerged in the abyss with the characters. The pacing balances moments of silence and beauty with sudden shocks, keeping viewers constantly uneasy. The score is another strength, weaving eerie aquatic tones with intense crescendos during attack scenes. Unlike many monster films that rely heavily on jump scares, this one gives enough psychological buildup to make each confrontation feel earned and terrifying. It also delivers a cautionary message about human interference with ecosystems, making the film more meaningful than just a creature feature spectacle. However, the movie is not without flaws. Some viewers may find the story line predictable as it follows familiar beats of the discovery danger survival final stand structure seen in many similar films. A few character arcs feel underdeveloped and at times the dialogue leans on cliches rather than originality. While the creature itself is unique in concept, certain visual effects during fast-paced sequences lack polish, slightly pulling viewers out of the immersion. Additionally, those looking for fast action may find the slower buildup in the first act a little dragging. Though, this pacing does help the suspense. Despite these drawbacks, Anemone 2025 is a mustwatch for fans of survival horror, ocean thrillers, and monster-driven stories. It captures the timeless fascination, and fear of the deep sea, reminding us that the ocean remains one of Earth's last great mysteries, one that humans are not truly prepared to face. If you enjoyed films like The Meg, Underwater, or Sphere, this will give you the same thrills, but with a more haunting and artistic edge. The MMA world Kerr enters isn't yet polished. Rules are looser, events more brutal. There's less structure, less glam, but more raw danger. As Kerr wins tournament after tournament, the consequences catch up. Bodies and minds that hurt. Moments of triumph shadowed by lows. The film doesn't just build toward big fights and knockout moments. It builds towards something harder. Acceptance. Accepting that being the smashing machine means more than wins and glory. It means facing loss, facing weakness, and figuring out what remains when the fight is over. As The Smashing Machine releases October 3rd, 2025, directed by Benny Saft, audiences are getting more than a sports film. Set in a dusty offbeat corner of California, the upcoming film Honey Don't finds its footing in a blend of neon- noir mystery and dark comedy that promises to be as stylish as it is unconventional. Directed by Ethan Cohen and co-written with Trisha Cook, this movie marks the next entry in their series of off-center character-driven stories following their first entry, Drive Away Dolls. But while Driveaway Dolls was a zany roadtrip caper filled with quirky humor and queer protagonists, Honey Don't shifts the tone to something more biting and mysterious, albeit still tinged with the Cohen's signature taste for irony and character idiosyncrasies. This film brings together a stellar cast with Margaret Quali taking the lead. Supported by Aubrey Plaza and Chris Evans among others for a story that swirls around secrets, deception, and the uncomfortable truths that lie just beneath the surface of small town respectability. Margaret Quali stars as Honey Odonahue, a sardonic and sharp private investigator whose laid-back exterior hides a penetrating intelligence and a knack for finding herself in sticky situations. The story kicks off with Honey being hired to look into a mysterious death linked to a religious group with a strangely growing influence across parts of the state. What at first seems like a routine investigation soon becomes a complex spiral of revelations, strange symbols, and tangled motives. Cohen and Cook inject the film with a heavy dose of atmosphere. Honey's journey into the inner workings of this cult-like community forms the backbone of the plot, offering suspense, character development, and a fair share of off-beat humor. The writing is reportedly infused with dialogue that's both razor sharp and playfully absurd, typical of Ethan Cohen's work. Trisha Cook's influence ensures that the narrative remains grounded in authentic queer identity and layered relationships, especially as Honey's own emotional journey unfolds in tandem with the mystery she's trying to solve. Chris Evans, known for his charisma and traditional leading man roles, plays against hype here as Reverend Drew, the mysterious and magnetic leader of the local religious sect. His performance is said to walk the line between charm and menace, keeping both Honey and the audience unsure of where his loyalties really lie. His relationship with the community is complicated, and his interactions with Honey are charged with a kind of philosophical tension. He's not just a villain in the traditional sense, but a figure who genuinely believes in his mission, which makes him all the more unsettling. Meanwhile, Aubry Plaza portrays MG, a local sheriff's deputy whose relationship with Honey deepens as the investigation progresses. The dynamic between Quali and Plaza is one of the emotional centerpieces of the film, giving it a human depth that balances out the more heightened genre elements. Their chemistry is reportedly electric with both actresses playing off each other's dry wit and emotional vulnerability with ease. The tone of Honey Don't rides the line between a traditional detective noir and a more experimental character-driven narrative. The film leans into stylized visuals and dreamlike sequences to capture Honey's internal state and the oddities of the town she's navigating. Arigner, known for her work on films like The Power of the Dog, handles cinematography duties, creating a visual pallet that shifts between dusty realism and vivid expressionistic imagery. That contrast helps highlight the duality of the world Honey is investigating, one that looks normal on the surface, but is anything but underneath. Carter Burwell returns to score the film, adding another layer of atmosphere. His compositions blend haunting melodies with unconventional instrumentation to reflect the strange energy of the town and the inner lives of the characters. As the music subtly underscores scenes, it helps the audience feel the building sense of tension and surrealism. Unlike its predecessor, Honey Don't dives deeper into the psychological toll of investigation and obsession. Honey O'don is not your typical hard-boiled detective. She's messy, a bit directionless, and driven as much by a need to understand herself as she is by the desire to crack the case. This makes her journey more intimate. Even as the plot expands to include more players and twists, her personal demons occasionally interfere with her work, and her connection to MG brings an emotional vulnerability that complicates the story. Yet, that complexity is what gives the film its emotional weight. Trisha Cook's script ensures that Honey's queerness isn't a subplot or window dressing. It's integral to how she navigates the world, how she interprets the lies around her, and how she relates to the people she's trying to protect or expose. That authenticity resonates across the board, making the film feel not only unique, but necessary in a genre that often sidelines or oversimplifies queer characters. Billy Iikner and Charlie Day round out the supporting cast, providing comic relief that never feels out of place. Instead, their characters are woven seamlessly into the story, adding eccentricity and unpredictability. The town Honey is investigating feels like a character in itself, filled with bizarre personalities and contradictory impulses. That atmosphere, one of both menace and comedy, is part of what makes Honey Don't so intriguing. Every corner Honey turns leads to another half-truth, another character who might know more than they're letting on, and another step closer to a conclusion that's as tragic as it is inevitable. The film also uses symbolism and surreal sequences to reflect Honey's descent into confusion. The further she digs, the more she questions what's real about the case, about the town, and about herself. There's also a strong thematic throughine about control and freedom. The church led by Reverend Drew claims to offer spiritual liberation but imposes rigid structures on its followers. Honey, by contrast represents chaos and independence, but even she begins to feel the weight of expectation and trauma. The eye interactions between her and Drew become philosophical duels, raising questions about the nature of belief, the allure of power, and the cost of truth. These are big ideas, but Cohen and Cook never let them overshadow the characters. Instead, these themes are revealed through their choices, their failures, and the messiness of human connection. The script doesn't go for tidy resolutions or forced catharsis. It embraces ambiguity, allowing viewers to draw their own conclusions about the characters motivations in the world they inhabit. The title Honey Don't itself plays with irony. It's both a warning and a dare. an invitation to defy convention and face the consequences. That tension runs throughout the film. Every moment of humor is laced with anxiety and every moment of drama is undercut with absurdity. In many ways, this is the heart of the Cohen's collaborative work, creating stories that are as intellectually stimulating as they are emotionally resonant with characters who feel lived in and flawed. The production process itself reflects this balance with Cohen and Cook working closely together as writers and producers. Their creative vision remains tightly unified. That cohesion is evident in the storytelling, the visual style, and the tone. Their decision to make a trilogy of queer bee movies isn't just about subversion. It's about reclaiming genre for voices and stories that have historically been marginalized. Honey, don't represents an exciting evolution in that vision. It maintains the irreverence and wit that made Driveaway Dolls so entertaining, but it deepens the emotional stakes and sharpens the satire. It explores identity not as a novelty, but as a lens through which the entire world is filtered. And at the center of it all is Margaret Quali's Honey, scrappy, smart, and stumbling her way toward truth in a world that doesn't make it easy. With its release slated for August 2025 and a premiere at the Can Film Festival in the midnight screening section, anticipation is building. Early buzz suggests that this could be one of the standout indie films of the year, blending genre, style, and heart in ways that few films manage. If you're a fan of off-kilter mysteries, sharp dialogue, and characters that break the mold, Honey Don't will be one to watch. Watch.

The year 2025 is set to deliver one of the most visually stunning, intellectually sharp, and queer affirming films of the season with the A24 style fantasy drama 100 Nights of Hero. This is not a simple period romance. It's a bold tongue-in-cheek feminist fable that dissects gender, power, and desire, all set within a vibrant meta medieval world. Adapted from the acclaimed graphic novel by Isabelle Greenberg and directed by Julia Jackman, the film utilizes the framework of 1001 nights to tell a story where the ultimate weapon against male dominance is imagination itself. The film's extraordinary world is a medieval inspired fantasy realm created by the god Birdman played by Richard E. Grant. However, the world was originally envisioned as a gender coeval utopia by his daughter Kiddo, played by Safia Oakley Green, until Birdman in a patriarchal fit of rage spoiled it. This meta narrative layer, the idea that the world itself is a failed utopia is crucial to the film's commentary. In this place, women are forbidden from reading or writing, but crucially, they are allowed to tell stories. This specific rule elevates storytelling from mere entertainment to a subversive powerful act of defiance. At the heart of this fractured, beautiful world are two women whose fates are intertwined, Cherry and Hero. Cherry, played by Mah Monroe, is the shy, melancholy noble woman trapped in a loveless and abusive marriage. Her husband Jerome, played by Amir Elmasserie, is a neglectful and borish figure whose pettiness drives the film's cruel central conflict. Cherry is not only deeply unhappy, but is already secretly in love with her clever maid, Hero. Hero, played by the immensely talented Emma, is the sharp-witted maidservant whose loyalty and love for Cherry are the only true sources of emotional stability in Cher's life. The action is set in motion by Jerome's supreme pettiness. Having failed to impregnate Cherry, he is nettled by a claim from his dangerously seductive friend Manfred, played by Nicholas Gallatine, that he could easily win Cher's affection. Jerome takes the bait, placing a twisted wager. He will depart on business for 100 nights. And if Manfred can successfully seduce Cherry in that time, Jerome will hand over Cherry and the castle to him. This bet is the ultimate act of patriarchal objectification, treating Cherry as property to be won or lost. The core narrative then becomes a fierce battle of wills and wits fought entirely within the domestic space of the remote castle. Hero, driven by her protective love for Cherry and her sheer intelligence, steps up to take charge. Her plan is to distract the smug and tiresome Manford with a relentless series of superb, enthralling stories. Much like Shahara Zada, Hero must tell stories so captivating that they bewitch, bother, and bewilder Manfred, forcing him to forget his lustful urges and delay his seductive attempts until the 100 nights are passed. The casting of the lead trio is a deliberate statement. Emma, who portrays Hero and identifies as non-binary, brings a nuanced subversion to the main character, imbuing Hero with an unexpected strength and depth that defies the traditional subservient role. Nicholas Gallatin's Manfred is played as an exceptionally charming but utterly Machavelian man, a product of the patriarchal society he is bred in, making his character a symbol of the very system Hero is fighting against. The on-screen chemistry between Corin and Mah Monroe is hailed by critics as the film's true emotional powerhouse, confirming that the forbidden queer romance is the real story here. The second half of 100 Nights of Hero delves into the metatextual and erratic dimensions of hero storytelling. Hero stories are not just tales. They are acts of subversion that allow her to comment on the misogynistic world she lives in, subtly challenging Manford's worldview while simultaneously entertaining him. Director Julia Jackman masterfully weaves these stories into the main narrative, allowing the film to explore complex ideas about gender, sexuality, status, and power in a playful yet sharp way. This structural complexity is part of what makes the film a compelling piece of horror origami, as one critic described it. The film's most talked about element is how Hero uses her stories to express her love for Cherry. Unable to openly declare their love, Hero finds a way to communicate her desire and devotion through erratic roleplay within the stories she tells Manford. She demonstrates through vivid narratives what Cherry could expect from a truly amorous suitor, a suitor who loves her wholly, subverting Manford's predatory advances. This makes the film a powerful, tender exploration of forbidden love, using the cloak of fantasy to explore queer desire and intimacy, which critics have noted has a serious sacrificial streak beneath the playful costumes. The ensemble cast includes pop icon Charlie XCX in her feature film debut as Rosa and Felicity Jones in a fascinating dual role as the narrator and the moon. Felicity Jones's role as the narrator anchors the film's meta level of storytelling, often pausing the main action to comment on the narrative structure, which some critics noted occasionally dissipates the energy, but adds to the film's intellectual depth. The involvement of actors like Richard E. Grant as the creator god Birdman and Amir El Massie as the despicable Jerome adds considerable star power to the feminist fable. The film also features supporting roles from Verdata Setu, Mark Elavanag as Mises A and Josh Cowarie as Beak Brother Hugo. The technical production of the film is crucial to its fantasy feel with the cinematography by Zenia Patricia and the gorgeous costumes by designer Susie Coloulter receiving specific praise and a British independent film award nomination. The film was intentionally shot with a high level of theatricality and color, giving it a vibrant storybook quality that enhances the fantasy genre. The entire project was filmed quickly in autumn 2024, demonstrating the commitment of the cast, including Mike Monroe, who admired how Emma Corin and Nicholas Gallatine created an electric atmosphere on set. It later served as the closing night film of the 69thBFI London Film Festival in October 2025, solidifying its critical acclaim and buzz. Its early screenings led to nominations for best costume design and best production design at the British Independent Film Awards. The official trailer for 100 Nights of Hero, released in August 2025, expertly teased the film's high concept charm. It focused on the sumptuous visual world and the highstakes wager, showing Nicholas Gallatin's Manford confidently arriving at the remote castle. Crucially, the trailer gave significant screen time to Emma Corin's hero, showing her quick wit and her intense, protective gaze toward Mike Rose Cherry, making it clear that the love between the two women is the force driving the plot. 100 Nights of Hero is scheduled for a wide theatrical release in the United States on December 5, 2025. Having failed to impregnate Cherry, he is nettled by a claim from his dangerously seductive friend Manfred, played by Nicholas Gallatine, that he could easily win Cher's affection. Jerome takes the bait, placing a twisted wager. He will depart on business for 100 nights. And if Manfred can successfully seduce Cherry in that time, Jerome will hand over Cherry and the castle to him. This bet is the ultimate act of patriarchal objectification, treating Cherry as property to be won or lost. The core narrative then becomes a fierce battle of wills and wits fought entirely within the domestic space of the remote castle. Hero, driven by her protective love for Cherry and her sheer intelligence, steps up to take charge. Her plan is to distract the smug and tiresome Manford with a relentless series of superb, enthralling stories. Much like Shahara Zada, Hero must tell stories so captivating that they bewitch, bother, and bewilder Manfred, forcing him to forget his lustful urges and delay his seductive attempts until the 100 nights are passed. The casting of the lead trio is a deliberate statement. Emma Cororin, who portrays Hero and identifies as non-binary, brings a nuanced subversion to the main character, imbuing Hero with an unexpected strength and depth that defies the traditional subservient role. Nicholas Gallatin's Manfred is played as an exceptionally charming but utterly Machavelian man, a product of the patriarchal society he is bred in, making his character a symbol of the very system Hero is fighting against. The on-screen chemistry between Corin and Mah Monroe is hailed by critics as the film's true emotional powerhouse, confirming that the forbidden queer romance is the real story here. The second half of 100 Nights of Hero delves into the metatextual and erratic dimensions of hero storytelling. Hero stories are not just tales. They are acts of subversion that allow her to comment on the misogynistic world she lives in, subtly challenging Manford's worldview while simultaneously entertaining him. Director Julia Jackman masterfully weaves these stories into the main narrative, allowing the film to explore complex ideas about gender, sexuality, status, and power in a playful yet sharp way. This structural complexity is part of what makes the film a compelling piece of horror origami, as one critic described it. The film's most talked about element is how Hero uses her stories to express her love for Cherry. Unable to openly declare their love, Hero finds a way to communicate her desire and devotion through erratic roleplay within the stories she tells Manford. She demonstrates through vivid narratives what Cherry could expect from a truly amorous suitor, a suitor who loves her wholly, subverting Manford's predatory advances. This makes the film a powerful, tender exploration of forbidden love, using the cloak of fantasy to explore queer desire and intimacy, which critics have noted has a serious sacrificial streak beneath the playful costumes. The ensemble cast includes pop icon Charlie XCX in her feature film debut as Rosa and Felicity Jones in a fascinating dual role as the narrator and the moon. Felicity Jones's role as the narrator anchors the film's meta level of storytelling, often pausing the main action to comment on the narrative structure, which some critics noted occasionally dissipates the energy, but adds to the film's intellectual depth. The involvement of actors like Richard E. Grant as the creator god Birdman and Amir El Massie as the despicable Jerome adds considerable star power to the feminist fable. The film also features supporting roles from Verdata Setu, Mark Elavanag as Mises A and Josh Cowarie as Beak Brother Hugo. The technical production of the film is crucial to its fantasy feel with the cinematography by Zenia Patricia and the gorgeous costumes by designer Susie Coulter receiving specific praise and a British independent film award nomination. The film was intentionally shot with a high level of theatricality and color, giving it a vibrant storybook quality that enhances the fantasy genre. The entire project was filmed quickly in autumn 2024, demonstrating the commitment of the cast, including Mike Monroe, who admired how Emma Corin and Nicholas Gallatine created an electric atmosphere on set. The film began its successful festival journey with its world premiere in the Sedimenta International Delicica section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival on September 6th, 2025. It later served as the closing night film of the 69thBFI London Film Festival in October 2025, solidifying its critical acclaim and buzz. Its early screenings led to nominations for best costume design and best production design at the British Independent Film Awards. The official trailer for 100 Nights of Hero, released in August 2025, expertly teased the film's high concept charm. It focused on the sumptuous visual world and the highstakes wager, showing Nicholas Gallatin's Manford confidently arriving at the remote castle. Crucially, the trailer gave significant screen time to Emma Corin's hero, showing her quick wit and her intense, protective gaze toward Mike Rose Cherry, making it clear that the love between the two women is the force driving the plot. 100 Nights of Hero is scheduled for a wide theatrical release in the United States on December 5, 2025. Distributed by IFC Entertainment Group, the film is rated PG-13 for sexual material, some bloody images, and language, confirming its sophisticated blend of adult themes with a fairy tale aesthetic. Ultimately, this film is a powerful, witty, and beautiful queer fable that uses the power of storytelling to defy the confines of a patriarchal world, proving that true love is the one story that cannot be undone by any wager. The year 2025 is set to deliver one of the most visually stunning, intellectually sharp, and queer affirming films of the season with the A24 style fantasy drama 100 Nights of Hero. This is not a simple period romance. It's a bold tongue-in-cheek feminist fable that dissects gender, power, and desire, all set within a vibrant meta medieval world. Adapted from the acclaimed graphic novel by Isabelle Greenberg and directed by Julia Jackman, the film utilizes the framework of 1001 nights to tell a story where the ultimate weapon against male dominance is imagination itself. The film's extraordinary world is a medieval inspired fantasy realm created by the god Birdman played by Richard E. Grant. However, the world was originally envisioned as a gender coeval utopia by his daughter Kiddo, played by Safia Oakley Green, until Birdman in a patriarchal fit of rage spoiled it. This meta narrative layer, the idea that the world itself is a failed utopia is crucial to the film's commentary. In this place, women are forbidden from reading or writing, but crucially, they are allowed to tell stories. This specific rule elevates storytelling from mere entertainment to a subversive powerful act of defiance. At the heart of this fractured, beautiful world are two women whose fates are intertwined, Cherry and Hero. text: The movie kicks off with a search party in search for a couple who mysteriously went missing. Unknowingly to them, there was a weird-l looking hole at the other end of the forest into which some dogs had happened to fall with no way out. Suddenly, the dogs saw a cave nearby and drank from it. Back to the search party, a guy managed to find the dogs, but they were just staring at each other in a weird-l looking way. He took these dogs home, but still the dogs maintained the same posture from earlier. Just then, one of them started making strange human sounds. The man's son heard the dogs barking non-stop, so he called his dad's attention to the barn. When the young man got to the barn, what he saw there was traumatizing as the two dogs began to merge their body together. The scene then shift to a guy named Tim, looking through his family photos, and just then, his girlfriend named Millie arrived to inform him that everyone is waiting for them. Once Tim was done, he came out to join his guests outside, and it turns out to be a send-off party as Tim and Millie plan to move to the countryside and bid to take their relationship to the next phase of their lives. In a surprising twist, Millie proposed to Tim at the party. Tim tends to believe this was all a joke as he never saw this coming while he stood still. So, in big shame and embarrassment, Millie got back up since she got no response from her proposal. Although Tim replied yes afterwards, but it now looks more awkward. So, later that night, Tim apologized to her for embarrassing her earlier in front of everyone, stating he didn't do it on purpose. However, Millie seems to have doubts about the sincerity of their love. She is of the opinion that they should split now as it won't be difficult, but Tim convinced her they are still in love. Although when they tried to sleep, Millie made a statement about some weird people looking at them. So when Tim looked towards the door, he found a mysterious lady crying. Quickly, he woke up only to find out it was all a dream. He then took a walk outside only to find Millie making some arrangements. So while they were both unpacking their things in the new apartment, Tim began to perceive a weird smell coming from upstairs. So he walked toward it to check where the source of the smell was coming from. Just then, he realized that the smell was coming from the ceiling, so he climbed a chair to check what it was. Fortunately, it was just a group of rotten rats tied together. This became a problem for Tim when he discovered one of the rats is still mysteriously alive. Although he waved this off as he didn't think anything much about it. Later that day, Millie got to her new job where she teaches elementary English. Then and there she met Jaime who was her co-teer. He welcomed her into the school and they became friends instantly. Jaime was throbbed on why someone of such caliber would choose to work here. However, during the conversation between them, Millie discovered that her and Jaime are actually neighbors as he lives just opposite their apartment. In the evening, we discovered Tim is an aspiring musician, and he practices every night before going to bed. The next morning, the couple embarked on a hiking journey around their new home. They stopped halfway, seemingly because they seem to have taken the wrong way. As they were looking around, Tim cited a weird looking bell in the forest, which is placed strategically to lead people down route. They proceeded with their journey, and after a long walk deep into the forest, they decided to return home, but unfortunately, they seems to have gotten lost in the process. Tim tried to using his compass to find a way out, but this doesn't help out. So Tim suggests they kept on moving forward but just then he fell into a cave. Millie tried to pull him out as he hasn't fallen completely but this only made them fall into this cave together. Luckily for them they sustained no injuries. Millie tried calling for help but there was no signal. Suddenly they started to get some weird feelings that the place is crowded and they seem not to be alone. So they tried looking for a way out but to no avail. So they decided to camp there for the night. Citing a pool nearby, the couple started feeling extremely thirsty. So Tim gave Millie the last water they had left before then using his hands to drink from the strange pool inside the cave. After which he collected more with his water bottle and drank till his full. While the two converts, Tim seems to be bothered. So Millie asked what the problem was and he told her he couldn't stop thinking about the rotten rats because it brings up some bad memories from his childhood. He told her how he walked into his parents room when he was little only to find his mom in a bad state smiling weirdly at him and this was due to the fact that she couldn't handle the fact that her partner had passed away. So her brain just snapped as she couldn't process all. He also informed her that he still has nightmares of that day up till now. And that smell has since then have always haunted him. So after their long conversation, they both fell asleep. So while they were both asleep, a mysterious entity from the pool closed in on them. Luckily, Tim woke up as a result of this mysterious sounds. But suddenly, he start to breathe rapidly in fear. Once he looked up, he saw that the vine above him is following his exact breathing sequence while Millie struggled to breathe. Fortunately, it was just a nightmare. The couple then tried to stand up and in a plot twist their legs got conjoined together like it was bonded by a strong glue. Carefully they managed to separate themselves. Afterwards, they climbed their way out of the cave. Unknowingly to them, their skin got torn from the separation. They eventually find their way back home together. Just then, Millie asked Tim to help him massage her shoulder. But while he went on with it, he started yearning for her. This made him lose focus after not realizing that he was squeezing Millie. Tim apologized before then going for a shower. On the other hand, Millie drove into town to get some groceries. All of a sudden, Tim fell unconscious inside the bathroom. The further Millie drove away from him, he experienced mysterious episodes where he is overly drawn to her. Like every single move she makes affects him, just like they were one person in two separate bodies. He started shaking uncontrollably in the shower while his head cracked open the tiles. However, he eventually regained consciousness. Tim, who is now in serious fear, goes to visit a doctor who, in return diagnosed him of mental illness caused from being in an unfamiliar environment. During their conversation, the doctor informed him about a couple from earlier who got missing a few months back. Back at home, Tim begins to research about the couple who got missing, and just then, Millie walked in. The two went through their own profile and discuss how basic life is and how far they have come. Suddenly, Milliey's coworker, Jaime, shows up at their home to welcome them to the neighborhood. During dinner, they told Jaime of their horrific experience at the cave. Jaime told him that the cave was once a chapel for a new age church until it mysteriously collapsed years ago. He believed it was a result of the bad weather. Then Tim drew Millie closer and they started kissing afterwards, but their lips joined together in the process and Millie thought it was Tim who bit her. So he tried to explain to her regarding his strange feelings, but Millie shrugged them off. So as they were both sleeping, Millie turned on the lights to discover Tim choking on her hair, which was terrifying. Immediately Millie tried pulling her hairs out, but to no avail as it was only choking Tim more. So after much effort he was finally able to pull it out as they both stared at each other in fear. The next morning Tim prepared to go for his gig but Millie doesn't support this as she feel he need to rest after what happened last night. However, Tim wasn't willing to cancel. So Millie drove him to the train station and before he left she told him to take his time and he shouldn't bother coming back home tonight so he can spend time with his friends hoping he would help him out. So as she drove off, Tim started having the same episodes all from earlier again. As farther she drove, the more his hallucinations increase uncontrollably. Due to this occurrence, he missed the train he was supposed to board. Tim couldn't help staying too far away from Millie, so he forcefully dragged himself to the school where Millie teaches. Millie rushed out immediately and Hurly took him to a bathroom stall. There, Tim couldn't help himself, so he started getting passionate towards her. After they were done, their body got stuck together and they found it challenging to separate themselves. As they were at it, someone spotted them and ran off instantly so they wouldn't notice. Quickly, Millie forcefully separated herself from him, which hurt pretty badly. The kid who saw them earlier called Jaime<unk>s attention to the situation, but Jaime handled it perfectly well and sent the kid back to class. Millie and Tim got back home and immediately she furiously vented her anger towards Tim for getting her into such mess. This caused them to get into a heated argument which made Millie to walk out. She then went straight to Jaime and bid to apologize for what happened earlier. The two had a pretty good conversation and just then Millie opened up to him about her relationship problems with Tim. Jaime encourages her not to let go of her partner whom he referred to as her other half. Millie inquired if he was the only one living here, so he told her about his relationship with his seemingly deceased husband. Jaime went to bring a tape of his wedding and suddenly Millie saw Tim peeping at them from outside. Later that night, Millie appears to be floating and moving as much as Tim is moving until he opens the door and has to slap her awake. The two discuss about what happened and Tim tried explaining what has been happening to them ever since they left the cave. However, Millie thinks it is ridiculous. Tim suggested to go back to the cave to get answers, but instead of supporting him, Millie broke up with him instead. Just as she leaves, her blood on the table drew closer to him. That night, they decided to sleep separately from each other. So, a few minutes later, Tim woke up finding himself moving towards Milliey's room, and his body started contorting in an unnatural way. This force pulled them together, and once they touched each other, they felt a little relieved, but at the cause of their hands fusing, which was immensely painful. Millie reached for Tim's muscle relaxing pills in the drawer. So, quickly, they chewed as many as possible to stop their limbs from contorting. Once this was done, they tried pulling themselves out and just then they lost consciousness. The next morning, Tim woke up to see Millie tying him to a chair and their arms fused together. She gives him whiskey and then uses a buzz saw to cut the skin between their arms. After separating themselves, Millie decides to drive to the hospital, but unfortunately, she realized she left her keys at Jaime<unk>'s house, so she went to get it. While Tim went back into the cave to find answers. Back to Millie, she finds out that Jaime was nowhere to be found. So while walking around she sees a wedding video being played of two men one who looks sort of like Jaime. The men are seeing undergoing a ritual where they are fused together. There and then Jaime reveals himself as being a fusion of both men stating it is the beginning of something wonderful. Tim on the other hand discovers other people who are fused to the wall along with Carrie and Simon who have now fused into a freakish monstrosity. He grabs a knife and slashes their fingers off to get away from them. Meanwhile, Jimmy explained that being part of the cult literally brings people together to become whole, and he hopes for Tim and Millie to do the same thing. He then slashes Milliey's wrist, but she hit him in the face, causing him to split into separate people. Millie runs back to the house and meet Tim as he prepares to cut himself in order for them not to turn to whatever he saw earlier. Just then, the force drew them yet again. So, as they are pulled closer together, Tim mimics Milliey's from the beginning of the movie and finally acknowledges how much he really loves her. Millie shows her wrist wound and accepts her death in Tim's arms. Tim then carried her into the house where she later gained consciousness to find Tim who willingly fused his arm with hers to stop the bleeding. After a terrifying long process, the two then completely fused their body together. Later that evening, Milliey's parents arrive at the house for Sunday dinner. But when the door opens, they are approached by a well-looking person who resembles both Tim and Millie. The movie then came to an end. Kindly subscribe for more horror movie recap like this. text: Free Guy movie recap, spoiler alert. In the open-world game of Free City, a non-player character called Guy suddenly becomes self-aware and deviates from his original programming. Initially seen as a glitch or a hacker, Guy becomes a worldwide viral sensation as he performs heroic deeds and inspires other NPCs to live beyond what they were assigned to do. This is noticed by game developers Millie Rusk and her former partner Walter Keys (Mickey), who originally developed the code for the game that Free City became, but it was stolen by Keys' current boss, Antoine, who just wants to turn Free City into a generic cash-grab franchise. After rounding up all the other NPCs and inspiring them to migrate to the island, Antoine tries to have Guy and Millie's avatar, Molotov Girl, deleted from the game, but Keys helps them get closer to the island. Antoine sends a bigger and dumber copy of Guy called Dude to beat him up, but Guy manages to get Dude on his side. Mouser developed their own game with the NPCs from Free City still saved, and Millie part ways with Guy so she can focus on her work, and she also later starts a relationship with Keys. Guy enjoys a new world

text: Grace wakes up in a strange bed with a robot above him that tells him he might be in an induced coma. He attempts to crawl out as the robot pulls him back, but he manages to release himself and screams where he is. He finds a ladder and sees that there are also a bunch of other people lying unconscious. He gets to an upper chamber and figures out it's a spaceship and he is in space. He gets back and recognizes some things, but is still confused about how he is here. He finds himself in a virtual reality room. He asks for the captain and the system responds that the captain is dead. He tries to tell the system to go back to Earth, but she responds that the time for that is 11 years. He gathers some information and figures it out for himself to be the truth. He then gradually begins to remember his past. In the news, there are some concerns about the sun dying. He has been a school teacher and is in a classroom. One student asks him about the dots in space that are said to be eating the sun. He tells them that two years ago a telescope enthusiast named Irena Petrova discovered a streak of infrared light from the sun to Venus, which is now known as the Petrova line carrying the dots. Grace relieves them saying it's only eating the sun in very tiny bits. They're still concerned since the Earth might slowly die within 15 to 20 years. He tells them not to worry for the scientists will figure something out. Back at the spaceship, Grace trims his beard and tries to clean up the place. He finds an album and remembers some of the other astronauts. He tries to figure out more of himself and passes the days. Back at the school office, a woman comes in. She introduces herself as Eva and says she is from the Petrova line research. She brings out a thesis written by Grace long ago about the inessentiality of water for probable alien forms. He soon gets up and attempts to leave because he was fired for that thesis. She follows him and says they need to do research on the space dots called astrophages. Her security member Carl also comes out to escort him and he eventually reaches the research center. He is put in a suit as a bunch of other people are outside. He checks out the astrophage and begins to test. He spent a lot of time trying to delve in, but he can't look into them. Everyone is exhausted. However, the attempts continue and he finds out it's a cell. Everyone is excited, but the cell soon dies. He then tries to figure out what they're made of and it turns out they're made of oxygen, hydrogen, and carbon. Outside, Grace sits a bit disappointed as his theory is pretty wrong. Eva comes up and confirms that the astrophages consume the sun's energy. She asks what its connection to Venus is and Grace doesn't know. She leaves saying they have over 300 more biologists to answer that. Grace follows her and says he would like to help further. She leaves him three astrophages for research. Grace continues his work as Carl keeps an eye on him. He says they need to get some things and they go out to buy them. They get back and figure they need an environment of carbon and heat where the astrophage can reproduce. They get on that and eventually he creates a box in a darkened room leading to the reproduction of an astrophage. They immediately take the news to Eva who is on a navy ship. She takes him to a room full of researchers where Grace hesitates. They clap for him and he begins to explain how he has done it. One of them asks how long it would take to make 2 million kilograms of astrophage. He doesn't understand why they need them. Eva then gets up saying she has assigned him as the head of project Hail Mary and Grace continues to be confused. Apparently, sun is not the only star that is dying, but all the neighboring stars as well except one called Tau Ceti 11.9 light years away. They have decided to build a ship to go there and find out why. They had the problem of powering the ship, but reproduction of 2 million kilograms of astrophages would fix it. They won't have enough fuel to get back. The astronauts will return the findings to Earth on the probe and they will die in space. This is their only hope contrary to watching the planet die. On the ship Grace checks out the deceased astronauts and gives them memorials saying he will do his best to complete the mission. He gradually let go of the bodies. He later chills in the virtual reality when suddenly a countdown begins and the gravity is gone. An ejector comes out of the ship and he is able to get hold of the monitor capturing the outside through a camera. Tau Ceti is nearby. It also has a Petrova line, but it's not dimming. He then notices that the Petrova line is stopped by some kind of object. The system suddenly says blip detected. Grace sees outside that there is a huge strange ship-like object. He is able to control the ship and get out of its way. However, the alien ship comes above him as well. He keeps getting out of its way and the ship follows. Once he stops, it throws something at Grace's ship. He settles down fearing an explosion, but it knocks and turns back. Then another is thrown moving rather slower. Grace tells the system to catch it and she recommends that he go on a space walk. He wears the suit somehow and gets out of the ship. He struggles to control himself and stumbles constantly as the object continues to move towards the ship. He somehow finds a balance and starts running towards it finally grabbing it. He takes it in and inside he finds something strange like a bunch of antennas. He understands it's from an alien form, but can't make heads or tails of it. He tries to do some research attempting to give it an energy source and eventually another similar object is thrown at a ship. There is something different inside this time. Then he sees a bunch of long poles from the alien ship connecting with his. The ships connect with a mysterious glass barrier. He opens the bay door and sees that a tunnel has formed all around. He walks into it and stumbles across a block. He taps on it and soon something scares him terribly. He recollects himself and sees a rock arm tapping on the glass. It shows him a human-shaped replica along with a model of his ship. It tries to tell him to go back to his ship and Grace returns. The tunnel disconnects and the ship begins to move, but only to reconnect to a different bay door. Grace gathers some instruments and depressurizes the ship. He walks out and finds the glass barrier. This time the alien shows up in its full form. It crawls like a spider and touches the glass door scaring Grace. He scares him back, but soon realizes the thing is only imitating him. Whatever he does, the alien does it as well including copying his laugh. Grace then checks out his body to look for a face, but doesn't find any. It attempts to communicate with Grace by pointing at the thing thrown at its ship earlier. He brings it to it and the alien tries to tell him something. After several attempts, Grace realizes it is asking him to take his helmet off. Grace won't do it and is about to return, but realizes the thing in his hand is indicating an oxygen model. The rock nods. He finds the courage to remove the helmet and realizes he can breathe perfectly. Grace then returns to the ship and inspects the other object previously thrown at him. He realizes it's the Petrova line. He returns to the rock and says they are here for the same reason. He tries to communicate with it by bringing in different objects to teach him numbers, but it doesn't understand much and only sees him at a surface level. He realizes the problem, tells him his name, and names him Rocky. He goes back and returns putting clothing over the numbers so that they can be seen. He shows him signs and Grace teaches him thumbs up, but he copies it as thumbs down. Rocky then brings in an object. It keeps on turning and Grace realizes it's their clock. Grace then brings in a computer with a microphone and uses an alien communication software to understand him. He shows him the astrophage and Rocky communicates calling it bad. He further says he is alone for there were 23 of them and all of them died. He asks about his ship and the story is the same. Rocky says they will save the stars together. They do a fist bump on this. Together, they try to make a plan and Grace tells him a bit about himself as Rocky asks what he is doing there. To stop reading the texts all the time, Grace assigns him a voiceover. Together, they pass through a bunch of them and choose one. He answers that he doesn't remember what he is doing in the space. Grace then decides to go to sleep, but Rocky tells him he must see him because he is afraid he will die as his crew died while he wasn't awake. Grace then lies under him feeling a bit absurd, but he goes to sleep. Back in the time, Grace was being introduced to the three astronauts assigned for the mission. They talk about how they have the option to end themselves once the mission is over and how they would prefer doing it. They are brought to show a demonstration of how the astrophage works to fuel the engine. In the spaceship, Grace remembers some fraction of those memories. The ship detects movement and he sees that Rocky has come out to the ship. He runs through the whole ship as Grace tries to stop him. He continues complaining about the mess. Grace calms him down and tries to teach him about boundaries, but he soon runs in search of his bedroom. Grace later records his journal about his new unwanted roommate. How he keeps on bothering him and his absurd way of eating. He whispers in the journal, but says Rocky can hear everything and see through walls. He whispers in a very low tone, but Rocky hears it all. Together, they build upon a plan. They're going to orbit through the planet where Astrophage breeds, collect a sample, and figure out why it's not eating Tau Ceti. Grace arranges the ship for the journey, and the system responds that it will take 11 days. They embark on their journey. In the meantime, Grace introduces Rocky to Earth through the virtual reality room, from nature to entertainment. He then asks Rocky what he misses most about home. He replies to his mate. Grace asks what their name is, and he respond with a very long sound wave. Grace says it's beautiful. Rocky asks if he has any mates. He responds that he used to be the one who left, saying his head is not in the real world, and she was right, Grace states. Grace then asks him how long he has been together with his partner, and Rocky responds 186.3 years. Grace remembers a time at the navy port, along with the scientists and the astronauts. He goes out to meet with Eva and chats with her a bit, saying how happy people are being despite knowing they're going to die. He asks if she thinks they would pull this off, and she only says it's God willing. Grace returns to the party, and everyone continues having fun when Eva enters and takes the microphone, and begins singing Sign of the Times, grabbing everyone's attention. In the present, Grace and Rocky have reached the planet. Since they are the first to discover it, Grace says they can name it. Rocky says it should be named medium rough texture circle planet. Grace responds that it's better to be a bit personal name, and imagines a name for Rocky's partner, and says it should be Adrian. Rocky approves of it. Grace returns with a sample and compares it with the Earth Astrophage. He says it's not leaving the planet for some reason. He inspects it further and finds a sign of life. It's not just Astrophage, but living bacteria. They are shocked by this revelation, which concludes that there is life on Adrian. Rocky soon begins to freak out, saying those living organisms on Adrian are making the Astrophage die, like a predator. If they can bring that predator home, they can save their stars as well. They need the microbacterial predator from the clouds of Adrian, but the ship isn't capable of reaching the planet. Rocky says he can create infinite chains, and they can reach that. But they both know that Grace is not a professional pilot, and Rocky trains him for it. In between, he reveals his plan of sending it back on a probe. Rocky is confused as to why he wouldn't be returning home with it. Grace says they don't have enough fuel to return, and he has a couple of years of food, and eventually he will die. Rocky says no, he must go home. Grace says he has made peace with it, but Rocky doesn't like it. He says he can give him 2 million kilograms of Astrophage, but he would go back home 6 years slower. He could not save his crew, and he can't let the same happen again. Grace sobs up, telling the truth that he did not make peace. He thanks him for it, hugging him, but he gets scared. However, he learns to hug back. Back in the time, Grace and Eva are together, chatting, about to launch the rocket. However, soon a catastrophe occurs. In the space, the rocket slowly approaches the surface of the planet. He drives the satellite, and there's a slight turbulence. When they are in position, they drop the collector with the chain. The collector collects the bacteria, and Grace goes out to take it back when he notices the satellite is slightly on fire. They pull the collector back, and Grace grasps a hold of it. The ship soon shows altitude warning. Grace then sees that the ship has been lowered from the cloud level. Soon, an object knocks Grace down, and the collector hangs low. A warning shows about excessive exterior temperature. Grace decides to take it, but Rocky says they can try again. It's not worth risking life. Grace doesn't believe there will be another time and goes for it. He grabs it and hangs by the chain. He cuts it off, swings by his hand, and throws in the collector. He gets back in and takes the pilot seat. He turns on the engine, and the satellite moves. The whole pressure warning continues. They somehow reach out of the atmosphere, but the fuel tank has a hole in it. He manages to eject the fuel tank, but knocks his head, making him unconscious. Rocky breaks out from his shell and saves him. He pulls him out and puts on an oxygen mask over him. However, he himself begins to waste away. Back in the past, the explosion killed one of the astronauts. They now have to have an immediate replacement, and Grace doesn't understand who, but everyone is looking at him. He says he is not an astronaut, but Eva replies that she doesn't need an astronaut, rather someone expert in Astrophage who is mission ready. He explains he cannot do this at all, but everyone says he can. He is afraid she is plainly asking him to give up his life, and she says yes, adding she has 3 hours to make a decision. Grace wakes up in the spaceship, but doesn't find Rocky anywhere. He follows the trails of carbon and finds him slowly dying. Later, Grace records a journal, saying he doesn't know what to do anymore. His work is done. Rocky left a message for him. Grace extracts the bacteria and compiles a successful test of how it kills the Astrophage. He continues the journal, complaining to Rocky that he gave up before reaching his planet and giving up on their plan. He falls asleep and wakes up to Rocky tapping beside him. He has come back into his shell. Grace wakes up and excited hugs him immediately. He brings him into the room where he collected all the bacteria. They decide to celebrate it, enjoying themselves in the VR room. He gives Rocky a sponge Earth toy. He now wants to check out his ship. They go on as Grace wears the glass suits. He enters, and it's all around is transparent rays that he cannot make heads or tails of. Back in the past, Grace reached Eva's office and told her that he can't do it. He doesn't have the bravery to do it. Eva tries to make him understand the consequences, but he has made up his mind and is about to leave. However, she is not going to let him go. A doctor comes in. She says he will be remembered as a hero. Grace tries to make a run, but he is surrounded. He still runs outside, but is soon grabbed and made unconscious. Grace now remembers everything on the spaceship. He is about to return home and says goodbye to Rocky. Rocky responds with a sign of their farewell. He returns and cuts off the connector. The spaceship disconnects and moves away as they show their thumbs up to one another. The system tells it will take 4 years to reach Earth. He dreams of all the past moments and wakes up to a warning saying contempt detected. He goes to check it and sees there is a leak as the bacteria have eaten away the zenonites, which are used to build the ship itself. He realizes it will also cause the death of Rocky. It will be one long, slow, and painful death. He makes the calculation and sees he has two options. One, he can go home, or he can save Rocky. He makes a decision. He packs up all his findings and, along with his journals, sends them away. He then journeys towards Rocky's ship, and once he finds it, he reaches for it. There is a huge glass barrier now, and he desperately bangs on it. Eventually, Rocky shows up and they hug. Back on Earth, their findings have reached, and Eva checks out his journals, and has also received a small gift. Their mission has taken place. Later, Grace wakes up to an alarm.
