text: This is Rummy’s Corner. Big George Foreman had one of the most extraordinary careers during the long rich history of professional boxing. Foreman won Olympic Gold in 1968, he was a two-time world heavyweight champion, and the most amazing thing about Foreman is that his two championship reigns were separated by more than 20 years. Indeed, the span between his two championship reigns included a complete 10 year absence from the ring, resulting in two clearly defined chapters during the damn fine long and illustrious career of Big George. After winning the Gold Medal, Foreman turned pro in June 1969 when he defeated Don Waldhelm on the undercard of Frazier-Quarry 1. As Foreman developed his craft and worked his way up while gaining valuable experience, he was viewed as a crude but strong powerhouse puncher who was a little rough around the edges. Foreman fought a total of 13 times in 1969, winning 12 of those 13 fights by knockout. Big George went on to win another dozen bouts the following year, including some notable victories against highly ranked contenders where he beat Gregorio Peralta by 10 round unanimous decision, and he also stopped George Chuvalo in round 3. Foreman additionally scored another notable stoppage win that year against Boone Kirkman. Over the next two years in 1971 and 72, Foreman won 12 more fights as he continued working his way up the rankings. By the time Foreman got the opportunity to challenge for the world heavyweight championship, he was still very much a bit of an unknown quantity. But he had worked his way up to become the #1 ranked contender by both the WBA and WBC, and he had compiled a perfect undefeated record of 37-0 with an impressive 34 out of those 37 wins coming by way of knockout. At that time Smokin’ Joe Frazier was the undisputed world heavyweight champion, and he was on a roll following his career-defining victory against Muhammad Ali in the Fight of the Century, which had taken place in March 1971. Following that win, Frazier had another pair of title defenses, but the greater expectation was that we would eventually get a big time championship rematch between Frazier and Ali. Indeed, the two camps were in negotiations for such, but those talks fell apart over financial differences, so instead of having the highly anticipated lucrative rematch against Ali, Smokin’ Joe instead opted to take on his mandatory - Big George Foreman. The champion Frazier was the favorite going in. The date was January 22nd, 1973, and Frazier vs Foreman was seen by many as nothing more than a prelude to the rematch between Frazier and Ali, but Big George had other plans. In an absolutely brutal display of devastating power, Foreman dropped the iron-willed Frazier early and often. Smokin’ Joe bravely battled on rising to his feet each and every time he was dropped, but the bludgeoning power of Big George was simply too much. After being dropped for the 6th time, referee Arthur Mercante had seen enough, and the fight was over. It was a 2nd round technical knockout, and 24 year old George Foreman had just become the undisputed world heavyweight champion, and he did so in dramatic style. Foreman successfully defended his world championship in September ‘73 when he battered and stopped the #9 ranked contender Jose Roman in round 1. Then in March 1974, Foreman made another defense against the highly regarded Ken Norton. Once again, Foreman’s devastating power was on full display, and he proceeded to knock Norton down three times in the 2nd round, simply overwhelming Kenny with brute force. It was a 2nd round technical knockout, and it was the 2nd title defense for Foreman. At this point in time Foreman was universally viewed as an invincible Heavyweight King, head and shoulders above the rest. A big part of that perception stemmed from the fact that Foreman had just destroyed two elite heavyweights, both of whom were famous for their victories and competitive fights against former champion Muhammad Ali. By late 1974, Ali was officially 1-1 against Frazier, with Ali winning the rematch that did eventually happen after Frazier had lost the championship against Big George; and Ali was likewise officially 1-1 against Norton, where Ali had avenged his previous loss in the lead-up to Foreman vs Norton. The devastating nature of Foreman’s championship wins led few to give anyone a chance against him, including former champion Muhammad Ali. The general consensus was that Ali was the past, and Foreman represented the present, the future, and beyond. But on October 30th, 1974, in the fight known as The Rumble in the Jungle, Foreman defended the crown against Muhammad Ali, and on this night it was a masterful performance from the former champion. Foreman’s pursuit was relentless, but he was having difficulty getting leverage on his punches. Ali was twisting, and turning, and blocking, and dodging, and he was also utilizing the ropes to great advantage. All of this served to lessen the sting of Foreman’s onslaught, where Big George was looking to land hard shots anywhere and everywhere he could. And all the while, despite being very defensively attentive, Ali was fighting effectively off the ropes, where his superior hand speed was giving Foreman all kinds of fits. Ali was picking and choosing his spots very wisely, and his awkward offbeat rhythm seemed to leave George confused and uncertain. Slowly but surely, with each passing round, Ali was effectively wearing Big George down, both physically and mentally. Things ultimately came to an end in round 8 when Ali unloaded with a series of sharp shots that sent Foreman staggering down. Referee Zach Clayton counted him out and the fight was over. Muhammad Ali had become the new world heavyweight champion, making him a 2-time champion, and Foreman’s aura of invincibility had vanished in a flash, and a great deal of his confidence along with it. Following the loss, Foreman was out of action for over a year before attempting to rebuild his career and work his way back into title contention. Foreman’s comeback bout in January 1976 got off to a very rocky start when he was pitted against Ron Lyle in an epic heavyweight showdown for the ages! In an absolutely wild and savage encounter, Lyle and Foreman beat the holy hell out of each other. It was a brutal war that saw Lyle and Foreman consistently landing hard clubbing shots in an action packed slugfest. Lyle dropped Foreman in round 4, and in the very same round, Foreman rallied back to drop Lyle. But the high drama fireworks persisted, and this time Lyle rallied back to drop Foreman for the second time in the round. In the following round, there were more dramatic shifts in the action, but Foreman was absolutely relentless and he ultimately quite literally beat Lyle down to win the fight in round 5. Any questions about Foreman’s heart and mettle following the Ali loss were put to rest, as Big George exhibited a damn fine display of courage to emerge victorious in this one. Later that year Foreman had a rematch against Smokin’ Joe, and despite Frazier putting forth greater resistance this time around, Foreman’s bludgeoning power once again proved too much for Joe. Foreman dropped Frazier in round 5 with a nifty barrage that was punctuated by a mean sharp left. True to form, Frazier bravely beat the count, but cool as an assassin, Big George moved in for the finish and he had Frazier down again. Joe again beat the count, but his corner had seen enough, and this fight was over. Foreman would win a few more fights over the next several months, including victories against Scott LeDoux (La-DO!), and also against undefeated heavyweight prospect John Dino Denis. But in March 77, Foreman suffered another loss at the hands of the talented Jimmy Young. The slippery Young proved mighty frustrating for Big George, as Young utilized numerous tactics to help neutralize the devastating power of Foreman. Big George began to fatigue over the second half of the contest, and Young managed to drop Foreman in round 12 en route to winning a 12 round unanimous decision. The loss came as a shock to many, and this effectively destroyed any hope of ever seeing a rematch between Big George and Muhammad Ali. In the aftermath, it had seemed that this was the end of the road for Big George Foreman. While he never officially retired, he had moved on from professional boxing, where he actually went on to become an ordained minister. His fight against Young happened when George was still only 28 years old, which is extremely young as far as heavyweight boxing careers go. With each passing year out of action, it would become apparent that Foreman’s boxing career was indeed over. But like a Phoenix rising from the ashes, Big George did return to boxing, 10 years later in 1987, a couple of months after he had turned 38 years old. Initially not many people were taking Foreman’s comeback very seriously. But Foreman remained dedicated and he was very active, just like when he began his professional career 18 years earlier. George was fighting frequently, and all the while he began trimming off the weight and getting into better fighting shape. Big George continued exhibiting his trademark power and he continued winning. Foreman had won 5 fights in 1987, he won another 9 fights in 1988, and he won 5 more fights in 1989. Foreman was piling up victories, and despite being older and slower, there was greater wisdom and discipline to his approach. In January 1990 Big George squared off against former heavyweight title challenger, Gentleman Gerry Cooney. This was easily the biggest event to date in his comeback, with a lot of fans utterly fascinated by the intriguing match up. The fight did not last long, however. Foreman scored a devastating 2nd round knockout against Cooney. Several months later, Big George scored another impressive knockout victory when he stopped WBA Top 10 ranked contender Adilson Rodriguez. And all of a sudden, people were beginning to take George’s comeback far more seriously, and not without good reason. By April 1991, Foreman had been on the comeback trail for just over 4 years, where he went a perfect 24-0 winning 23 of those 24 bouts by knockout, which ultimately afforded Foreman the opportunity to challenge the undisputed world heavyweight champion, Evander ‘Real Deal’ Holyfield. Not many people were giving George a real chance in this one, but his celebrity status along with the potential to make history had many fans intrigued for this championship showdown. This one was largely a tactical affair with some explosive moments scattered throughout. Foreman was having some spots of success, and he even managed to rock Holyfield a couple of times along the way. But despite having some difficulty, for the most part, Holyfield outboxed and out hustled his older challenger throughout the majority of the contest. Foreman was displaying great durability and championship heart, but it wasn’t enough. At the end of 12 rounds of action, Holyfield was awarded a unanimous decision victory. Despite losing, Foreman had put forth a brave and praiseworthy effort, which earned him respect and admiration from boxing fans. It was an inspirational effort from Big George. Even though George returned to action in December 91, his days as a serious contender were seemingly over. In April 92 Foreman faced Alex Stewart, whom he dropped twice in round 2, but Big George was unable to finish him off. Foreman went on to win a 10 round majority decision, but he ate a lot of shots in this one and many felt it was time for him to finally hang’em up for good. But he didn’t hang’em up, and after winning a fight against Pierre Coetzer (Coat-zer) in January 93, Foreman continued trying to rebuild, and he squared off against Tommy ‘The Duke’ Morrison in June 93. This one was for the vacant WBO strap, which was not viewed as a major world title at that time. Morrison proved to be an extremely tricky customer for Big George. Morrison utilized good movement, and he was effectively able to stick and move while steering himself out of harm’s way. Morrison won a 12 round unanimous decision to capture the WBO belt, and at this point - there was no doubt about it. Big George was finished at the top level. Following that fight, Big George was out of action for almost a full year, and then in April 94 Michael Moorer scored the upset when he won a 12 round majority decision against Evender Holyfield to win the unified WBA/IBF heavyweight championship. With the victory Moorer had also earned a valid claim to the lineal heavyweight crown. This paved the way to another shot at the title for 45 year old Foreman, who challenged the undefeated 26 year old world heavyweight champion. By the time the fight ultimately took place on November 5th, 1994, Foreman had been out of action for just shy of 17 months! The fact that Foreman had failed at the top level against Holyfield, and then later against Morrison led very few to give Foreman a chance against the undefeated champion. Early on Double M utilized his superior speed and athleticism to his advantage, and Moorer was able to outbox Foreman with quickness and movement. Foreman was having some spots of success here and there, but by and large the champion was controlling the action and dictating the terms of the fight. Foreman was having a lot of difficulty finding his range, and the champion’s slippery slick tactics were appearing to be too much for Old George to contend with. But in round 10, Foreman started finding the mark with his right hand. And then it happened. By George it happened! Foreman belted Moorer with a one-two punctuated by a booming right hand that dropped champion hard. Moorer was down, and he would not be beating the count. The fight was over, and at 45 years old,George Foreman had just become the oldest boxer to ever win the world heavyweight title - a record that still stands to this day. Against all odds, Big George Foreman had just become the new unified WBA/IBF and lineal world heavyweight champion. This historic win would start a chain reaction of events that would soon lead to a state of disarray in the heavyweight landscape. Foreman was stripped of the WBA belt in March 95. In April 95 Foreman defended the IBF belt when he won a controversial 12 round majority decision against Axel Schulz. Foreman then vacated the IBF belt two months later in June. Technically speaking, although Foreman no longer held claim to any of the major championship belts at that time, he still held a rightful claim to the lineal heavyweight crown. In November 96 Foreman won a 12 round unanimous decision against undefeated Crawford Grimsley, and then in April 1997, Foreman won a 12 round split decision against Lou Savarese. Then seemingly out of nowhere, Foreman was granted a feasible path to a showdown against WBC heavyweight champion Lennox Lewis, provided he first won an elimination bout. This paved the way for a showdown between Big George and Shannon ‘The Cannon' Briggs in November 1997. Foreman put forth a tremendous effort in this one. Indeed, Foreman looked as good as he had looked in years, effectively applying pressure and working behind the jab, and he progressively started landing more power shots which began taking a toll on Shannon ‘The Cannon’. Foreman finished the fight strong, but at the end of 12 rounds of action, Briggs was awarded a controversial majority decision, where most observers believed Foreman had done enough to win. But the judges saw it differently, and this wound up being the final fight during the long and illustrious career of Big George Foreman. Despite the controversy, Foreman was gracious in defeat and he officially retired shortly after. Foreman did however sign on for one final fight after this, and that one was scheduled for January 1999, when Foreman was slated to face Larry Holmes, The Easton Assassin. Holmes was the man who dominated the heavyweight landscape for the large bulk of Foreman’s 10 year absence between 1977 and 1987, and this was a fight that maybe could have happened in the mid to late 70s, or even during the early-mid 90s. It looked like it was finally going to happen, the one that got away, but unfortunately the entire event fell apart when the money failed to materialize, and the promoter was unable to pay the remaining purse promised to Foreman. When you look back at the two chapters in the amazing career of Big George, you have two almost totally opposite guys, both in terms of personality, and also in terms of style. The young Foreman was known as a brutal destroyer, with an almost mean bad guy demeanor, and the style fit the personality. Foreman was a feared power puncher, who threw his punches with authority where he was always looking to hurt and overwhelm his foes with sheer force and power. Young George was a complete and total powerhouse, and his mighty offensive arsenal blended well with his frightening bad-ass attitude. But then older George was almost the complete opposite. He was a merry and jolly beloved Grandfather figure, who ate cheeseburgers and sold fancy new age grills, while always guaranteeing us all that we were not gonna pay a lot for that muffler. Foreman had become a bona fide and well respected superstar celebrity, and this new persona was in stark contrast to the lean, mean, wrecking machine who wreaked havoc on the heavyweight landscape during the early and mid 1970s. In the same way George’s personality had evolved with time, so too did his fighting style. Instead of primarily relying on brute force and strength, Foreman relied more on pacing himself, where he had a certain cleverness to his approach, boxing at a more measured tempo, and looking to set traps for delivering his still devastating power in a more effective manner. But one thing that was always constant was a powerful stiff jab, and heavy-handed pop in both hands, along with an underrated boxing IQ that was predicated on a tremendous understanding of range and distance and finding ways to discover favorable angles where he can unload his ferocious power in terrifying fashion. Big George Foreman was truly one of a kind, and the historic significance of him becoming the oldest world heavyweight champion during the long rich history of professional boxing - an impressive landmark record that still stands to this day, even in an age where athletes are competing longer and having greater success at an advanced age - this accomplishment from Big George cannot be understated. Before 45 year old Foreman made boxing history - and really, he was only a couple of months shy of turning 46 - but before that, the oldest man to win the heavyweight crown was Jersey Joe Walcott, back when he stopped Ezzard Charles in their famous 3rd bout in 1951, and Jersey Joe was 37 years old when he set the mark that would later be broken by Foreman. But one big difference here is that Jersey Joe was still an active highly regarded contender going into that one. On the other hand, Foreman was largely viewed as being completely washed up, coming off a one-sided loss and 17 months of inactivity when he made history. That’s a fact that often gets lost and overlooked when trying to fully comprehend exactly how amazing a feat this was. And even when we look beyond the historical implications, and the incredible record that has now stood strong for nearly 30 years - Foreman’s impact as an inspirational figure, where he became the living personification of the idea that age is just a number - Big George Foreman truly is one of a kind. Big George was one of the most extraordinary boxers during the long rich history of professional boxing, but above and beyond that, he was an extraordinary human being who entertained and inspired millions of people through his words and his actions and his contagious unwavering heart and determination. His career achievements speak for themselves, and Big George Foreman has forever left his mark in boxing history. What a damn fine career! Thank you very much for watching everyone, I hope you enjoyed, and have a wonderful night. This is Rummy’s Corner.

text: The guy who created He-Man passed away a couple weeks ago at the age of 91. His name was Roger Sweet, and before you go see the new Masters of the Universe movie, here's the whole 45-year story from then to now. Let's begin. 1976, Mattel turns down Star Wars. George Lucas pitched the toy rights to every major toy company. Mattel's CEO looks at the deal, says no way. Kenner toy company says yes, becomes the biggest toy company in America. Mattel panics. They had Barbie, they had Hot Wheels, but no action figures for boys. They told designer Roger Sweet to come up with anything. Roger Sweet grabbed an action figure from Big Jim, added a huge amount of clay so the figure was massive. Mark Taylor, the goat, his sketches iconic. He had a character in a sketchbook called Torak that he drew in 1979, and he also had a Castle Grayskull image from 1975. Then Roger picked the name He-Man, and he also suggested the twist action waist. Now comes the generational toy line. It's February 1982. Mattel shows the toy line at the toy fair. Castle Grayskull, He-Man, Skeletor. Whose concept art? He was named D-Man. Can you imagine? He-Man and D-Man? I don't think so. Skeletor, great name. The toys went wild, instant success. Then a company called Filmation made the cartoon. By 1984, it was on over 150 stations, 30 countries, 130 episodes in 2 years. John Erwin voices He-Man, Alan Oppenheimer voices Skeletor. And the music co-composed by Haim Saban and Shuki Levy. 3 years later, 125 million toys. Castle Grayskull, Snake Mountain, Battle Cat, Panthor. Ah, so many. They reused all the body parts. That way they keep costs down and they ramp up toy production. At this point, it's such a success Mattel branches out into She-Ra, Princesses of Power. Roger Sweet designs her too, He-Man's sister, 93 episodes, huge toy line. By 1985, Masters of the Universe was the third largest toy line. The fall, 1987. They make a live-action film of He-Man. It doesn't do well. The toys started declining as well. Why was the fall so bad? So Transformers and G.I. Joe start taking over the toy aisle, and all the original fans that started to age out of the toys. In 1989, Mattel ended the toy line. 1990, Mattel tried one more time. The New Adventures of He-Man didn't stick, gone by 1992. Then it went dormant. Nine years of silence. In 2000, Mattel releases a commemorative series re-release. It worked. In 2002, full revival on Cartoon Network. The toys were sculpted by Four Horsemen Studios, Masters of the Universe 200X. 2008 to 2016, Masters of the Universe Classics. 2020, Masters of the Universe Origins launches. In 2021, Kevin Smith makes Masters of the Universe for Netflix. November 2022, gets inducted into the National Toy Hall of Fame. And now, 2026, Travis Knight directs the new live-action movie. Nicholas Galitzine as He-Man, Jared Leto as Skeletor. Whether you're a vintage toy collector like me or really into the modern toys, knowing the history of where this all started helps just add that texture. And as He-Man always said, "By the power of Grey Skull, I have the power." What a line.

text: Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore is about to hit theaters, so if you need a quick refresher on the story so far, don’t worry, this video has you covered. This is a recap of everything you need to know from Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them and Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald. Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them serves as a prequel and spin-off story of the Harry Potter franchise. The story starts with British wizard and magizoologist Newt Scamander arriving in New York City. When one of his creatures, a Niffler, escapes from his magical suitcase, Newt is forced to chase it through the city, bumping into human No-Maj, or non-magical person, Jacob Kowalski. Jacob is a witness to Newt using magic and the two accidentally swap suitcases. Newt is arrested by Tina Goldstein, a demoted Auror, basically the magic police, for using magic in front of a No-Maj. But when Newt’s suitcase is investigated and found to only include Jacob’s baking supplies he is released. And speaking of released, Jacob opens Newt’s suitcase and accidentally releases three magical creatures into the city. Newt, Jacob, Tina, and Tina’s mind-reading sister Queenie then team-up to track down the beasts and return them to their home in Newt’s magical suitcase. As the team works together to recapture the beasts, Jacob and Queenie develop romantic feelings for each other, despite a relationship between a witch and a No-Maj being forbidden. When US Senator Henry Shaw, Jr. is killed by an Obscurus, the team is arrested by Seraphina Picquery, President of the Magical Congress of the United States of America, as she believes the Obscurus was one of Newt’s escaped creatures. An Obscurus is a dark parasite which develops inside magically gifted children when their abilities are suppressed, and usually kills the host by the age of ten. After being arrested, Newt is accused by the Director of Magical Security Percival Graves of working with the infamous dark wizard Gellert Grindelwald. Graves sentences Newt and Tina to death, but Jacob and Queenie help them escape. Graves visits the orphan Credence Barebone after having a vision that he was connected somehow to the Obscurus. Credence lived with his adoptive mother, Mary Lou Barebone, who was staunchly anti-witchcraft and forced Credence to suppress his magical abilities. Graves promises to teach Credence how to use his magic in exchange for his help. When Mary Lou confronts Credence about magic, Credence’s Obscurus kills Mary Lou and her eldest adopted daughter, Chastity. Graves mistakenly assumes that Credence’s younger adopted sister Modesty was responsible and takes an interest in her abilities, dismissing Credence. This angers Credence, who reveals that he was the host of the Obscurus and had survived into adulthood due to the intensity of his magic. Credence then goes on a rampage throughout the city, exposing magic to the non-magical world. Tina had a history with Credence, having previously tried to protect him from the abusive Mary Lou, and being demoted after using magic to do so. As Newt and Tina try to calm Credence down and stop his destruction of the city, Graves tries to convince him to join his side. Seraphina and a team of Aurors then arrive, attacking Credence and his Obscurus, seemingly killing them both, although Newt does notice a wisp of the creature fleeing the scene. Graves then reveals his master plan was to use the Obscurus to reveal magic to the No-Maj world, tired of wizards having to live in hiding. Newt helps to apprehend Graves and reveals him to be Gellert Grindelwald in disguise. Fearing that Credence’s attack had exposed magic to the city, Newt tasks his Thunderbird to disperse an obliviate potion across the city, which would erase the memories of recent events from every No-Maj in the area. As the potion falls like rain, Queenie kisses Jacob goodbye as he loses all memory of her. The story continues in Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald. Grindelwald has escaped custody and was now amassing an army of loyal followers. Months later in London, Newt Scamander is asked by his old Hogwarts professor Albus Dumbledore to find Credence Barebone, who had resurfaced in Paris. Dumbledore believed Credence to be Corvus Lestrange V, the long-lost half-brother of Newt’s childhood love Leta Lestrange. Also searching for Credence is Newt’s Auror brother Theseus, alongside his fiance Leta. And Tina teams up with a wizard named Yusuf Kama who also has his own motives for finding Credence. Before leaving on his mission, Newt is visited by his old friends Queenie and Jacob. Jacob has restored his memory of the magical events in New York City and was now engaged to Queenie. Newt discovers that Queenie had put a love enchantment on Jacob and lifts the enchantment. Despite his love for her, Jacob refuses to marry Queenie out of fear for the consequences she would face for marrying a No-Maj. Heartbroken, Queenie goes off to find Tina, while Jacob joins Newt on his mission to find Credence. In Paris, Credence has teamed up with Nagini, a Maledictus who was cursed to transform into a snake, to uncover the truth about his birth parents. Before they can get vital information from the half-elf servant who had brought Credence to America for adoption, Grimmson, a loyal follower of Grindelwald, murders the half-elf. Queenie fails to find Tina and is instead brought to Grindelwald. Wanting to harness her abilities, Grindelwald manipulates Queenie into joining him, explaining that in his vision for the future, magical laws wouldn’t prevent her and Jacob from marrying. Eventually, all of the parties searching for Credence converge, bringing together Newt, Jacob, Tina, Yusuf, Theseus, and Leta. Yusuf finally explains his motives for hunting down Credence. When Yusuf was a child, Corvus Lestrange became infatuated with his mother and cursed and abducted her. Yusuf and his father later learned that she eventually died giving birth to Corvus’ daughter, Leta Lestrange. On his deathbed, Yusuf’s father makes Yusuf take an Unbreakable Vow to kill the person Corvus loved the most. Corvus never loved Leta, but did love the infant son he eventually fathered, which he named Corvus Lestrange V. Fearing for his infant son’s safety, Corvus sent Leta and baby Corvus on a ship to America. So now, believing Credence to be Corvus, Yusuf was on a mission to kill him. Leta then explains that on the journey to America, she couldn’t stand her infant brother’s constant crying and switched him with another baby. When the ship sank, the real Corvus died, and the swapped baby, Credence, took his place. The group’s search for Credence eventually leads them to a rally for Grindelwald’s followers. Grindelwald shows his followers a vision of World War II and details his anger that magic laws prohibited wizards from preventing such tragedies. Theseus leads a team of Aurors to surround the rally and apprehend Grindelwald. Grindelwald conjures a ring of fire, which kills many of the Aurors. Loyal followers of Grindelwald, like Credence and Queenie, are able to safely cross the fire to join him. Leta sacrifices herself to allow the others to escape. As Grindelwald and his followers flee, the fire begins to spread throughout the city. Newt and the other wizards then unite to extinguish the flames. Newt returns to Hogwarts, now fully onboard in the fight against Grindelwald. He presents Dumbledore with a vial of blood he had taken from Grindelwald, revealed to be a blood pact former lovers Dumbledore and Grindelwald had made that prevented them from dueling each other. As the film comes to a close, Grindelwald presents Credence with a wand and finally reveals to the orphan his true identity. He was Aurelius Dumbledore, Albus’ long-lost brother.

text: At Maybrook Elementary School, third grade teacher Justine Gandandy expects a normal Wednesday morning. But when she steps into her classroom, the rows of desks are empty, except for one. Out of 18 children, only one is there. Alex Lily. What detectives uncover is far more unsettling. Ring cameras from the missing children's homes reveal a pattern. In the early hours of Wednesday morning at exactly 2:17 a.m., each child wakes, runs out of the house in a straight line with arms outstretched, and vanishes into the night. As part of the investigation, Alex is questioned, but he insists he knows nothing. His teacher, Justine, just as shaken, has no explanation either. A month passes. To prevent further disruption to the students education, the school decides to reopen. On the eve of reopening, Principal Marcus organizes a counseling session for missing parents and teachers. From here onward, the story is told through six chapters, each from a different character's point of view. Justine sits quietly as a counselor addresses the audience. Tension erupts when one of the missing children's parents, Archer, interrupts, demanding that the authorities should stop wasting time and arrest the suspects sitting among them. All eyes turn toward Justine. Determined to prove her innocence, Justine steps onto the stage. She apologizes for what has happened recently and insists she wants answers as much as anyone. The crowd shouts her down, calling her a liar. Marcus attempts to diffuse the situation, but the room spirals into chaos, and the meeting is cut short. Humiliated and shaken, Justine drives to a liquor store to drink away her frustration. Shortly after, she receives a call from an unknown number. A voice warns her to watch her back. Back at home, she locks the door securely. Later, Justine prepares a drink when the doorbell rings. She peers outside. No one is there. Moments later, a loud knock rattles the house. Armed with a taser, she steps out and discovers her car vandalized in the driveway. The next morning, Marcus advises Justine to take a few days off and attend therapy. She refuses, insisting that work is the only thing keeping her grounded, but Marcus reminds her that the parents are still emotional and that it would be better if she stays away from the school for a while. Then Justine asks about Alex. Marcus assures her he is doing well in Mrs. Belt's class. She pushes to speak with him, but Marcus grows firm, warning that Alex has already endured enough and that Justine often crosses professional boundaries. She half- jokingly asks him to arrest her for consoling a crying child or giving a ride to a student who missed the bus. Marcus reminds her she is a teacher, not a parent. And though he understands her care for the students, he makes it clear she cannot contact Alex. Frustrated, Justine returns to her car. Later, she files a police report for the vandalism and the threatening calls. Across the street, she spots her ex Paul and waves at him. Later that night, Justine and Paul meet at a bar. Justine admits she's surprised he agreed to see her. Paul smiles and thanks her for reaching out, saying he had been thinking of calling to check on her after the news about the students disappearance. Justine gets defensive, insisting she can handle herself. She then signals the bartender to get Paul a drink. He ends up ordering a Coke. Paul gently asks Justine how she's holding up. She admits that people are calling her a witch and that someone even vandalized her car. Upon hearing this, Paul encourages her to take a deep breath and asks her not to get trapped in her own thoughts. He points out to her that people aren't thinking about her nearly as much as she imagines, but Justine disagrees. Changing the subject, Justine asks if his wife Donna knows he is here. Paul admits she doesn't and adds quietly that they're having problems lately. Justine smiles and urges him to get a drink, and he does. That night, they end up at Justine's house and sleep together. The next morning, she drives Paul to the spot where he left his car. On the way, she casually asks about his work. Paul, not in the mood to talk, brushes her off with a flat, "Whatever, fine." His indifference sparks Justine's anger, and she snaps that he isn't taking the missing children case seriously. Paul reminds her that he isn't a detective. When they arrive, he steps out. He tells her it was good to see her and walks away. After school, Justine follows Alex to his house. She rings the bell, then knocks, but no one answers. The windows are strangely covered with newspapers. Looking for another way, she opens a side gate and slips into the small backyard. From there, she peers through a gap in the window. Inside, two figures sit rigidly on the couch, completely motionless. Alarmed, she calls Marcus to report what she has seen. He reacts with frustration, reminding her he explicitly told her to stay away. Minutes later, he ends the call. Later, while buying drinks at the liquor store, Justine is confronted by Donna, who is discovered that Paul cheated on her with Justine. Donna accuses Justine of getting Paul drunk. Their argument grows heated until the clerk steps in to break it up. That night, Justine dreams that she is walking through Maybrook Elementary. In her classroom, every child is asleep at their desks. Alex looks up at her, his eyes wide and unblinking. She jolts awake, heart racing. As she settles back into bed, she notices a woman on the ceiling above her. Terrified, she screams, but when she looks again, the woman is gone. The next day, Justine approaches Alex. Are you okay? She asks. I'm okay, he replies. When Justine presses further, Alex suddenly yells, "Don't follow me." and storms off. Justine returns to Alex's house and knocks, but there is no response. She waits outside in her car. Hours pass until she sees Alex's mother quietly slip inside. Nightfalls and Justine dozes off. Suddenly, the front door bursts open. Alex's mother steps out, scissors in hand, her expression vacant. Without a word, she snips a lock of Justine's hair before retreating back into the house. Now, the story shifts to Archer's perspective. Archer, whose son Matthew went missing, is obsessed with finding out what happened to him. Each night, he replays the Ring camera footage from the night Matthew disappeared, studying it for any hidden detail. Archer also runs his own construction company. One day, his employee points out that they painted a door the wrong color, red instead of forest green. Archer admits he ordered it wrong, and he hauls the red paint can into his car and tells the worker to order the correct one. Later, Archer meets with Ed, the police chief, seeking an update on the case. Ed insists the detectives are working tirelessly, but Archer cuts him off, accusing him of protecting the real suspect, Justine. I looked into her past, he says. She was arrested for DUI 2 years ago and dismissed from a previous job for inappropriate behavior. Ed chimes in that was with a faculty member. Then Ed adds, "No one forced the children to leave." The footage shows they walked out of their homes on their own. That night during the counseling session at the school, Archer accuses Justine. After the meeting, he secretly follows Justine home and vandalizes her car. Then he goes back to his house and watches the footage again before falling asleep. Hours later, he jolts awake. 217 glowing on his alarm clock. Heading downstairs, he sees Matthew run outside. Archer chases after him in desperation, but somehow finds himself back in front of his own house, watching as Matthew slips inside. In the sky above, a glowing gun-shaped light shines with the numbers 217 etched into it. Archer rushes into his son's room, whispering, "Where are you?" He breaks down in tears, confessing he loves Matthew, though he never said it aloud. Suddenly, a woman with a terrifying smile appears in Matthew's place, and Archer wakes with a start. Archer spreads a map of Mabbrook on his table. Using a ruler, he draws a straight line from his house, mimicking the way Matthew ran that night. He then visits the home of another missing child, Bailey. After introducing himself to Bayleyy's mother, he asks to see their Ring camera footage. She refuses. Archer waits until her husband arrives. He makes the same request, and this time Archer is granted access. Reviewing the video, he confirms the same strange pattern, the children running in a straight line with Matthews and Bailey's homes at opposite ends of town. He draws a line between them. It intersects the map at a central point, but the spot reveals nothing familiar. Driving aimlessly to clear his head, Archer spots Justine's car pulling into a gas station and decides to follow. Confronting her, he demands answers. Justine snaps back, telling him to leave her alone, that she has nothing to say. Before the confrontation escalates, Marcus runs towards her and tackles her to the ground and pins her. Archer tries to help, but Marcus shoves him aside. Justine stumbles into the store. The point of view now shifts to Paul. Paul is on the phone with his wife, Donna, who is away on a business trip. She tells him she'll be home in 3 days and that they can start trying for a baby soon. Before hanging up, she asks if he's still attending AA meetings. Paul lies, saying he doesn't have time because of too much work, and ends the call. Then Paul greets Ed, who is also Donna's father, before heading out on patrol. Later, in a narrow alleyway, Paul spots a teenager acting suspiciously. He calls out, but the boy bolts. Paul gives chase first in his cruiser, then on foot, eventually catching and handcuffing him. The boy insists it was his house and that he lost his key, but Paul doesn't buy it. "What's your name?" Paul asks. "James," the boy replies. Paul searches James and asks whether he has any sharp objects on him. James says no, but Paul pricks his hand on a used needle hidden in the boy's pocket. Panic floods him at the sight of blood. He punches James, then scrambles to his car to clean the wound. Only then does he notice the dash cam has been recording the entire encounter. He returns to James trying to smooth things over. I shouldn't have hit you. You lied. I overreacted. We're both wrong here. He warns James never to return to this part of town and tells him that if he sees him anywhere next time, he'll put him in jail. Back at the station, Paul learns that Ed has already heard about his rough handling of James. Ed reassures him that as long as James doesn't file a complaint, the incriminating footage will remain untouched. Not long after, Paul receives a message from his ex, Justine. Against his better judgment, he meets her at the bar. They sleep together. The next morning, after Justine drops him off, Paul drives home only to find Donna there back earlier than expected. She immediately notices his disheveled state. It doesn't take her long to piece things together and discover his betrayal. At the station, Ed's sharp stare says more than words. Outside, Paul spots James loitering nearby. He yells after him, frustration boiling over, then decides to follow him, this time disconnecting his dash cam. The perspective shifts to James. James is a homeless, drugaddicted teenager. He survives by stealing and pawning whatever he can for a few dollars. On the day Paul cuffed him, James had been trying to break into a locked house. Now wandering through town in the pouring rain, James stumbles upon a large house, which turns out to be Alex's. He notices newspapers taped over the windows, but he shrugs it off and climbs inside through a window. Inside, the house is pitch black. James gropes around, stuffing valuables into a pillowcase. Passing through the living room, he mutters an apology when he sees Alex's parents seated on the couch, motionless, catatonic. They don't react, so he keeps going. Curiosity pulls him toward a door leading to the basement. There, in the dim light, he finds several children standing frozen. Panic surges through him. He tries to flee, but behind him, Alex's parents rise suddenly and give chase. James barely manages to scramble out of the house alive. Shaken, he heads to a pawn shop, sells off what he grabbed, and only then he notices a missing children flyer taped to the wall. Heart pounding, James calls the police and claims he knows where the missing children are. They tell him to come into the station. Outside the station, James notices Paul and he bolts into the forest. In the distance, he sees a strange woman waving at him. Spooked, he hides in his tent, clutching a used needle like a weapon. When Paul opens the tent flap, James mistakes him for the woman and stabs his face. Paul draws his gun in fury, but James begs for his life, claiming he knows where the missing children are. He guides Paul back to Alex's house. James watches nervously as Paul rings the bell. To his shock, someone actually opens the door. Nightfalls, but Paul doesn't come out. Then at last, the door caks open. Paul emerges, furious, dragging James inside with him. The perspective shifts again, this time to Marcus. Marcus is out shopping with his husband, Terry, when he gets a call from Justine. She explains her unease about Alex's house, especially the newspapers covering the windows, and asks Marcus to conduct a welfare check. To reassure her, he agrees to contact Alex's parents and arrange a meeting at the school. The next day, Marcus waits in his office for Alex's parents. A woman in excessive makeup enters and introduces herself as Glattis, Alex's aunt. Marcus apologizes, explaining he needs to speak directly to Alex's legal guardian. Glattis interrupts, saying they're unwell, which is why she has moved in to take care of them. Marcus explains that a welfare concern was filed and insists he needs to speak with Alex's parents directly. Glattis asks evenly, "Who made the complaint?" Marcus hesitates, then answers that it was anonymous. He warns that if he can't speak to Alex's parents by Monday morning, he will have to call the authorities. The next day, Marcus is enjoying a quiet breakfast with his partner when a knock sounds at the door. It's Glattus. She apologizes for disturbing him on a Saturday and explains that she missed her bus, asking if she could rest for a while. Marcus doesn't understand why she would come to his house, but Terry, always polite, welcomes her in. Inside, Glattis asks for a bowl of water. Then she asks Marcus if he has contacted the authorities about Alex. When he replies no, he notices Glattis tying his ribbon to a stick. Without warning, she presses the sharp edge of the stick into her own palm. Terry panics, rushing to hand her a rag for her wound, but Glattus suddenly snips a lock of his hair. She ties his hair to the stick and rings a bell and snaps the stick in half. Instantly, Marcus' body jerks. His movements no longer his own. He turns on Terry, killing him in a violent trance. When it is over, Glattus dips the stick into the bowl of water, which brings Marcus under control. From her bag, she takes another lock of hair. Justine's. She ties it to the stick and snaps it. Marcus runs toward Justine and after shoving Archer off, he enters the store and chases after her, but Archer intervenes, wrestling Marcus down long enough for Justine to escape. She dashes outside, jumps into her car, and speeds away. Archer follows them in his car, but an oncoming car strikes Marcus, killing him on the spot. Later, after a hospital check, Archer finds Justine waiting for him outside. She thanks him, shaken but relieved. Justine wonders aloud that she has never seen anything like Marcus' behavior before, but Archer says he has. He shows her his findings. The children, including Matthew and Bailey, all ran in the exact same posture in straight lines as if they were weaponized, programmed to attack like Marcus. Archer points out the intersection, saying this is the line that Matthew and Bailey ran, but he admits he doesn't know what it means. Justine looks closer and realizes the spot is the home of Alex Lily. Now the perspective shifts to Alex. Alex is a bright boy, but he often gets bullied by his classmates. text: Happy Holidays! It's me Chelsea! I know the holidays can be busy you guys and that's why I'm here to take a little bit off your plate by giving you quick recaps of some classic holiday movies, in case you don't have time to watch them. You're too busy wrapping presents, and I respect that. So here's The Grinch. So the Who's in Whoville are like singing and decorating and having a blast and then this furry green dude named The Grinch is watching them from up on this hill... Like a real fuckin' creeper. And he has a dog and a heart condition and he hates Christmas because it's too noisy with all the weird shit the Who's have going on, like Jing-Tinglers and Floo-Flooers and Justin Beibers. So The Grinch decides to dress up like Santa and steal Christmas because he's so mean that there's even a song about it and how no one will touch him even with a thirty nine and a half foot pole. Which, is the half foot really necessary? Like we get it. He's disgusting. So The Grinch drives his sleigh down the hill basically vertically and his dog is, A, wearing reindeer antlers, which is cute. And B getting run over by the sleigh all the time and you just feel so bad for this dog. Like is there no ASPCA in Whoville? Jesus So The Grinch breaks into the Who house and he's slithering around on the ground like a psychopath and he wakes up Cindy Lou Who. Which, then he makes up some lie to get out of it then she buys it because she's just a dumb kid you guys. And then he goes back up the hill vertically again, which is strange. And he balances the sleigh on top and it's very precarious and the dog is hanging over the edge and it's like will nobody help this dog?! Then he hears the Who's singing and he's like "What the actual fuck?!" "I fucking stole Christmas and these assholes are still singing!" But then his heart grows so big it breaks the thing, and it gives him inhuman strength and he rides the sleigh down the hill to give Christmas back! Even the roast beast! I don't even know what that is! But it sounds delicious! I'd put it in my mouth. And then Cindy Lou gives the roast beast to the dog and it's like finally somebody helped the dog! Merry Holidays There you have it, The Grinch So now, when you're nephew asks you to hang out with him, you can tell him this quick recap instead of spending actual quality time with him. You're welcome!

text: a film in 3 minutes Paris Texas the American West a tragic Wilderness of boundless fantasy and harsh reality its deserts are an escape a place to forget who you once were free from the Conformity of modernity but no matter how far you travel Fate has a nasty habit of making other plans just like it does for one man his family and the woman he left behind in the Vim vendor 1984 road trip Masterpiece Paris Texas a beautiful journey of redemption with a Bittersweet yet life affirming final message on love commitment and understanding that I challenge you not to feel moved by opening in the Wilds of West Texas the story follows Travis Henderson a mute traveler suffering from Amnesia who after losing Consciousness from exhaustion is cared for by an unscrupulous local doctor after finding a note with a phone number belonging to Travis's brother Walt Walt reunites with Travis and takes him back home with him to Los Angeles reintroducing him to his 88-year-old son Hunter who has little memory of him however a mystery still lingers over what happened to Travis's wife Jane eventually taking him and his son on a road trip that will change their lives forever a co-production between France and West Germany and directed by new German Cinema Pioneer V vendors Paris Texas depicts an America as seen through a uniquely European lens the Epic sense of scale the Stark anonymity of the Monstrous cities the neon soaked motels the uniformity of the Endless highways all the architectural facets of this Larger than Life land are photographed almost fantastically making the mundane and humdrum to American eyes appear elevated into something of a worldly a Dusty downtrodden Americana free of its glossy veneer and optimism but optimism is found in the heartfelt focus on family in in the story penned by one of America's most treasured playwrights whose protagonist Travis is not some mythical heroic figure of the wild west but an ordinary unassuming man brought to life thanks to the stoically contemplative performance from Harry Dean Stanton with the role being the actor's favorite out of over 100 credits at the time the many moments he shares with his son played by Hunter Carson who incidentally gives one of the greatest performances I have ever seen from a child actor are simply impossible not to smile at for their simple sincere charm but smiles will be mixed with tears during the film's touching third act a stunning emotional climax that seals Paris Texas's Legacy as one of the greatest examples of art housee Cinema ever made remaking the west from a land of empty bitterness to one of hopeful renewal where a brighter future is possible if only one is bold enough to face their past

text: Hi Everyone, Meta Anime here. Hope you are doing well. Today I am going to tell the story of a film called Wolf Children. It was released in 2012 and is another film that was written and directed by Satoko Okudera and Mamoru Hosoda. They were famous for their previous work: The Girl Who Leapt Through Time and Summer Wars. The story of this film is told by Yuki, a werewolf child. She told the life story of her mother, Hana who married a wolfman and raised their two children alone after he died. They move to the countryside and the children have adventures in the woods and at school. Before we go, this video contains spoilers. So please take this warning for those that haven't watched this movie yet. Without further ado, here's the recap of Wolf Children!! The film opens with Hana, a university student in Tokyo studying with the help of a scholarship. One day, Hana saw a man in her class that is so different from the other students. He always sat alone bringing only a notebook and never submit his attendance card after class. She approached him trying to get him an attendance card But he refused and said that he is not a student there then left. On his way out, she saw him help a kid that fell while playing, and made her happy. Time goes by and they got closer each day as Hana kept helping him in the class by lending her textbook and letting him enter the library. One night at a park, he showed Hana that he is a werewolf. He is the descendant of the Japanese wolf that went extinct a hundred years ago. And he is the last being that inherited a blood mix of humans and wolves. Hana accepts him no matter his circumstance because she is already in love with him. They then live together in a house just like a couple. While her husband works as a driver, Hana continues her study at the university. These are the happiest moments for them. One day, Hana got pregnant with their first child. While pregnant, her husband went hunting a lot to get Hana nutritious and delicious food. Because she is afraid that her child's identity as a werewolf would be exposed, she did not to go the hospital for her child's birth. Their first child was born in a form of a normal human girl and was named Yuki. Years went by and she got pregnant with her second child. Their second child is a boy named Ame because he was born in the rain. Life seemed perfect for a while. But one afternoon, her husband never got home. Worried, she went outside to look for her husband in the middle of the rain. She found her dead husband's body in the form of a wolf in a river. He seemed to be trying to hunt food for his family but failed. Now she had to be a single parent and raise her children alone. What she had feared became truth as her children are also werewolves just like their father. They transform into werewolves depending on their emotions. She is having a hard time, especially because her first child is so hyperactive while her second child is timid and weak. The problem came when one day Yuki got sick. She is uncertain whether to take her to a human or animal hospital. She then just called the two of them and consult through a phone. Luckily Yuki got better in the end. Because Yuki and Ame cried and howl a lot at night, the neighbors complained a lot to them. The neighbors also called the children's consultation center as they are worried that she is abusing her children. Since Yuki and Ame never got any immunization or medical check-up, Hana got more suspected by the children's consultation center. Hana then decided to move to rural areas and bought a house that is far away from any neighbors. This would allow Yuki and Ame freely play around their house. Hana then renovated her new house alone while her children play around the house. Her children are really happy with their new house because they are free to play around and explore their wolf side. Hana always taught her children not to show their wolf side to the villagers and always be nice to everyone. As their savings from her husband had already run out, Hana decided to learn agriculture by reading books about growing plants. But her endeavors to plant them always failed. With the help of a grumpy but nice old man named Nirasaki, Hana eventually learns to grow the plants properly. Due to her hard work, the plants she grew turned out to be good when harvested. To express her gratitude, Hana shared her crops with the villagers. But the villagers also gave Hana their crops in return which made Hana overwhelmed because her fridge can't fit all of them. The kind villagers then gave Hana a bigger fridge to fill them. Apparently, Nirasaki is the one who asked the villagers to help Hana which made Hana very grateful to him. This made Hana closer to the villagers. But this also made Hana more worried that people would find out about her children. During the winter, the three of them were playing around with the snow. On the way home, Ame got separated. He saw a bird eating a fish at a river. Unknowingly, Ame tried to hunt the bird but fell into the river. Yuki who saw that called her mother and jumped into the river to save Ame. Luckily, she managed to save him. After this incident, Ame who was previously rejecting his wolf side has now embraced that side of him as he is now sure that he is destined to be a wolf. Time goes by and Yuki is now old enough to go to school. Even though, Hana was hesitant at first but allowed her to go to school in the end. Hana made Yuki promise to hide her wolf side from other people no matter what. At school, Yuki was different from the other girls. She is more wild and like things that are different from the other girls like snakes and bones while other girls would like flowers and jewelry. Yuki then decided to be more graceful and girly so that she could get close to the other girls. Since Yuki went to school, Hana tries to get a job as an assistant for nature observers despite the low salary. Hana took Ame with her to work a lot. This gives Ame more enthusiasm for nature. He also feels more comfortable there because there is a wolf there. Time flies and Ame also go to school now. At school, he can't adapt well and got targeted by school bullies because of his quiet attitude. Because of that, Ame spent more of his time in the mountains. One day, Yuki got a new transfer student named Sohei. Souhei said that Yuki has a smell of furry animals around her. This made Yuki uncomfortable and worried that her identity will be exposed. She had no confidence to be close to her friends anymore. As Yuki always avoids Souhei, he got more curious and keeps bothering Yuki for answers. This made Yuki upset and accidentally attacked Souhei making his ear bleed. At school, Hana asked Yuki to apologize but was ignored. Souhei's parents then got mad at Hana. But Souhei said that it was not Yuki that attacked him but a wolf that he saw before passing out. This made Hana even more worried. Due to the incident, Yuki refused to go to school for days and locked herself at home. This made Souhei feel guilty. He visited Yuki's house every day and give her food or letter so that she would go back to school. Yuki then decided to go back to school and the two of them became friends. Hana's attention then turns to Ame that no longer wants to go to school. He prefers to spend his time in the mountain. At first, Hana let Ame go to the mountain alone to learn from someone he called his teacher. But Hana got curious and asked Ame to take her to meet his teacher. Unexpectedly, his teacher is a fox. Ame learned so many things about the mountain, especially how to survive in the wild from his teacher. Ame felt that this is his world. As time goes by, Yuki and Ame grew to be teenagers. The difference between the two of them got bigger. One night, Ame asked Yuki to go to the mountain together because that's where they belonged. But Yuki refused because she wants to live like a normal human. She even asked Ame to go back to school but refused. Because of their opinion difference, they got engaged in a fight and injured each other. Hana tried to stop them but in vain. Ame revealed his red eye indicating he is becoming a wild wolf day by day. One day, Ame found his teacher injured by a falling tree and might die soon. He told his mother that he must replace his teacher as the leader there at the mountain. Hana did not allow him to go back to the mountain anymore because she still consider him a child. Despite Hana's refusal to let him go, Ame still seemed determined to go. In the afternoon, a huge storm hit the village. Hana was about to go to school to pick Yuki up but he saw Ame go out of the house. She then pursued Ame despite the storm but lost him in the end. She went up the mountains to find him but ended up slipping and falling unconscious because of injuries. Meanwhile, at school, Yuki and Souhei are the only ones left. At that moment Souhei told Yuki about how his parent did not care about him and that he wanted to live alone. Seeing Souhei telling her about him, Yuki decided to tell him about her secret as well. But Souhei was not shocked as he already knew about it from the beginning. He promised her to keep it a secret. Yuki felt relieved and smiled happily. The scene shifts to Hana having a dream where she met her husband in a flower garden. He praised her for raising their children well. He also told her to let Ame go as the two of their children have found their path. Ame was seen carrying his injured mother down the mountains to somewhere safe. Right before he left, Hana woke up and told him not to go as she hasn't done much for him. Ame who has completely turned into his wolf form looked back looking worried. But still decided to go to the mountains in the end. At the peak, Ame howled as loud as he can. Upon hearing his howl, Hana realized that Ame has found his path and smiled. She finally let go of her child. The next year, Yuki left the house to study in a high school dorm. We can see the picture of her mother sending her off with a smile. Several years later, Hana still lives happily in her house while hearing Ame's howls from her house. She continues to look at the picture of her dead husband while smiling. So that concludes the recap of Wolf Children. What do you guys think? This film beautifully tells us a great story about motherhood. It shows the tough side of a mother who selflessly accepts her life for the sake of her children. She never gives up on her children no matter how hard the situation is especially with her unique situation and the fact that she had to raise them alone. This film made us realize to appreciate and respect our parents more especially those that were raised by a single parent. Other than the story, the film also gave us beautiful visuals which made it even more enjoyable. Please tell us what you think through the comment section. If you like this content, please leave us a like and share them with your friends. Thank you for watching, and till we see you again!

अपने गुरु के आश्रम में पहुंच जाते हैं और रफ़्तार को उसी गाड़ी के जरिए वह नीचे खाई में गिरा देते हैं पर कुछ टाइम बाद रफ्तार खाई से ऊपर पहाड़ पर आ जाता है जहां पर उनका आश्रम होता है और वहां पर अवतार बेहोश हो जाता है उसके गुरु उसको उठा कर अंदर कमरे में ले करके आते हैं फिल्म जुनून को देखते हैं जो कि अपने बॉस के पास गई होती है और वो कहती है कि हमारे पास में अभी बनारस तरह जो कि सिवा नाम के लड़के ने The modern horror landscape is being redefined by filmmakers who understand that true terror lies not in jump scares, but in psychological unraveling and atmosphere. For 2025, the director at the forefront of this movement is Osgood Perkins, and his latest venture, Keeper, is poised to be one of the most unsettling and talked about psychological horror films of the year. This is a story that takes the seemingly idyllic trope of a romantic cabin getaway and twists it into a claustrophobic nightmare using a familiar setting to explore the terrifying unknown of the person sleeping next to you. The film promises a dark, surreal trip where the past and the present of a secluded cabin merge, forcing one woman to confront not just a malevolent spirit, but the fragility of her entire relationship. The core premise of Keeper centers on a couple, Liz and Malcolm, who retreat to a secluded cabin in the wilderness to celebrate their anniversary weekend. Liz, the wife, is played by the Emmy-winning Tatiana Masslin, and Malcolm, the husband, is played by Ross Sutherland. They are initially portrayed as a couple deeply in love, using the romantic phrase keeper to describe each other a sweet notion that the film immediately sets up to be twisted into something sinister. The cabin itself is an isolated, almost censient character in the film, steeped in a horrifying, unspoken history. Their romantic getaway is shattered when Malcolm abruptly cuts their trip short and returns to the city, leaving Liz completely alone and isolated in the remote location. The plot kicks into high gear once Liz is left by herself. Her isolation is immediately disturbed by the presence of a malevolent, unspeakable evil entity that begins to approach her. This entity is tied directly to the cabin's dark, haunting past and starts to unveil the property's chilling secrets. The narrative shifts from a relationship drama to a visceral psychological thriller as the boundaries between reality and nightmare quickly dissolve. Liz begins to experience paranormal activity and psychological attacks. Forced to confront the idea that the cabin is not merely haunted, but is actively trying to break her mind. As her emotional world unravels, the film uses the supernatural presence to expose her own buried fears and the unsettling truths of her past. A major theme of the film, heavily hinted at in early marketing, is the duality of the title and the inherent horror of heterosexuality and disgusting maleness. A complex thematic concern that Tatiana Masslini and Osgood Perkins have openly discussed. The term keeper, initially a loving term, takes on a chilling double meaning. One theory strongly suggested by the marketing is that Malcolm has a killer secret. Perhaps using the cabin as a place to collect or keep the souls of his victims or deliver them to the evil entity. text: Welcome to our analysis and critique of the award-winning Greek film Dogtooth. Dogtooth is a 2009 Greek drama directed by Yorgos Lanthimos. The movie delves deep into the themes of control, manipulation, and isolation. The story revolves around a husband and wife who keep their three adult children confined to their isolated country estate, ignorant of the outside world. The father strictly controls every aspect of their lives, feeding them bizarre lies about the dangers that exist beyond the fence surrounding their property. He convinces them that they will be ready to leave the house once they lose a dog tooth, a twisted milestone of adulthood in their skewed reality. The children's only connection to the outside world is Christina, a woman brought by the father to satisfy the son's sexual urges. As she introduces the eldest daughter to some external influences, cracks begin to form in the fabricated reality, leading to inevitable consequences. Dogtooth stands out for its unique premise and unsettling portrayal of extreme parental control and manipulation. Lanthimos crafts a world that is disturbing yet intriguing, prompting viewers to reflect on societal norms and the nature of influence. The film employs a static, cold, and deliberate visual style matching the sterile and controlled environment the children live in. This contributes greatly to the film's eerie atmosphere. The actors give convincing performances, making the audience buy into the strange reality in which the characters exist. Their robotic behavior combined with moments of genuine emotion paints a picture of individuals deeply affected by their confined upbringing. One of the most talked about elements of Dogtooth is its ambiguity. The film does not explain why the parents chose to raise their children this way or delve deep into their motivations. This can be seen as a strength, allowing for various interpretations, but it might also be a point of frustration for some viewers looking for clear answers. The film contains scenes that are deeply unsettling, bordering on the perverse. While these scenes drive home the impact of the children's manipulated reality, they might be too intense for some viewers. At a deeper level, Dogtooth can be interpreted as a commentary on societal control, indoctrination, and the dangers of extreme sheltering. It challenges viewers to question the information they receive and the confines of their own upbringing. In conclusion, Dogtooth is a provocative and bold film that won't be to everyone's taste. It's a deep dive into a nightmarish scenario of control and isolation, showcasing Lanthimos's talent for pushing boundaries and challenging audiences. And just in case we haven't piqued your curiosity enough, here is the trailer of the film. And as always, thank you for taking this journey with us. We'll see you next time.

ဒါ့အပြင်မော့အနေနဲ့အပြင်မှာစွမ်းအားတွေကိုအန္တရာယ်ဖြစ်အောင်သုံးပါလို့ရခန်းကိုကတိပေးထားရတာမော့ပေါက်ကံမှုဖြစ်ဖို့နှစ်ဆယ့်နှစ်ရာခိုင်နှုန်းလိုသေးပြီးအိမ်မှာညစာစတော့အစွမ်းကိုမထိန်းနိုင်ဘဲဇွန်းကြီးကကွေးသွားရပါတယ်မစ်စုဆိုတဲ့ညီတစ်ယောက်ရှိပြီးတော့သူကတော့ကျောင်းမှာစတော့ပါတယ်ဒါပေမဲ့မော့နဲ့ညီအစ်ကိုယ်စိတ်ရှိသူဖြစ်ပါတယ်ဟင်းကပ်မွေးကြိုင်မြို့စားလယ်တန်းကျောင်းမှာမော့ကတက်နေတာဖြစ်ပြီးဆုမိဆိုတဲ့စော်လေးကိုလည်းကြွေနေတာပါမော့ဟာစာသင်ခန်းထဲမှာအိပ်နေလို့စာမေးခံရရင်လည်းစာမရပါဘူးဒါ့ကြောင့်တခြားသူတွေကလှောင်သလိုဘောလုံးကန်တော့လည်းအနည်းတမ်းပဲ [တေးဂီတ] မော့ကဒီလှိုင်ခေါင်းကနေကြီးမားတဲ့မကောင်းဆိုးဝါးအငွေ့သက်ကိုရနေပါတယ်တဲ့။အထဲကိုရောက်တော့ရေဂန်ကအသေးစားကောင်လေးတွေကိုမင်းနှိမ်နေလိုက်ဆိုလို့မော့ကပါဝါရီနဲ့ပစ်ကာသရဲအသေးစားတွေကိုစတင်ပစ်ခတ်ပါတယ်။ရေဂန်ကသူဟာမော့ထက်အစွမ်းကြီးသလိုပြောနေပေမယ့်အခုထိသာမန်လူထပ်ထူးခြားတာဘာမှမတွေ့ရသေးဘဲမော့ကိုဟိတ်ဟန်နဲ့ခိုင်းနေရာပဲတွေ့နေရပါတယ်။ရေကန်ကသရဲခေါင်းဆောင်အောင်တွေ့ပေမဲ့သူကတော့နဘန်းသမားကဘယ်လိုလုပ်ပြီးဒီမှာလာလေ့ကျင့်နေတာလဲလို့ထင်နေပါတယ်။ဆိုင်ကယ်သမားတွေအုပ်စုလိုက်စီးနင်းလာကြရင်ရှေ့ဆုံးကခေါင်းဆောင်ကငပြောသီးတက်နင်းမိရင်ဆိုင်ကယ်ကမှောက်သွားပါတယ်။ [တေးဂီတ] ဖိုရှော့သုံးပြီးမကောင်းဆိုးဝါးကိုဖြတ်လိုက်တာပါဒင်ပယ်နဲ့အတူရုံးခန်းကိုရောက်လာတော့ငယ်ငယ်ထဲကသူသိပုံတွေသူ့ရဲ့ဆန္ဒမူနာဖြစ်တဲ့အကြောင်းတွေကိုမဲဆက်တစ်ကိုပြောပြခဲ့ပါတယ်လမ်းတွေမှာလည်းမော့ပျက်ပုံကိုဆွဲပြီးအလိုရှိလို့ဆက်သွယ်ပါဆိုပြီးဖုန်းနံပါတ်ပါတဲ့စာရွက်တွေကိုကပ်ထားပါတယ်အဲ့ဒါကတော့သူတို့ရဲ့ဘာသာရေးခေါင်းဆောင်အဖြစ်မော့ကိုတင်မြှောက်ချင်နေတာပါ ပါ။ရွတ်စုကမဇ္ဇာတောကိုပြောပြေမယ့်သူ့အစ်ကိုကလူတွေရှေ့မှာအစမ်းမသုံးတာလည်းကြာပြီ။ဒါ့ကြောင့်သတင်းမှထည့်ရေးတာမျိုးတခြားသူတွေကိုသိစေမယ့်အရာမျိုးခွင့်မပြုဘူးလို့ပြောကာထွက်သွားခဲ့ပါတယ်။ရွတ်ဆုကသူလည်းမောဟညီဖြစ်တာကြောင့်တစ်နည်းမှာတော့သူ့ကိုယ်လုံးစိတ်ဆွမ်းအားရမယ်လို့ထင်နေခဲ့ပါတယ်။သံဃာတို့အဖွဲ့ကတော့ဒဏ်ရာတစ်ပါးနဲ့အနက်ရောင်ဖန်တီကအကြောင်းကိုတိုက်ဖို့ဆိုပြီးခန္ဓာကိုယ်ဖွံ့ဖြိုးရေးအသင်းကလူတွေကိုစက္ကူလာခေါ်ပါတယ်။ဒါပေမဲ့မူဆာရီကတော့သူတို့မှဆယ်တွေဆော့နေရတာကတိုက်ခိုက်ဖို့အတွက်မဟုတ်ဘူးဆိုပြီးမလိုက်ပါဘူး။အဲဒီနောက်တံခါးကဗလမရှိသေးတဲ့မုန့်ကိုတွေ့ပြီးအကြံရခဲ့ဘူး [တေးဂီတ] အဲ့ဒီနောက်တံခါးကဗလမရှိသေးတဲ့မော့ကိုတွေ့ပြီးအကြံရခဲ့ပါတယ်။မော့ရဲ့အဝတ်အိုထဲမှာပန်းခြံကိုလာဖို့စော်လေးကစာထားခဲ့သလိုမျိုးရေးထားခဲ့ပါတယ်။ဗနီကကျောင်းကသူတွေကိုကျောင်းကလက်စားချေဖို့လာမယ်ဆိုပြီးပန်းခြံကိုချိန်းထားလိုက်ပါတယ်။ခန္ဓာကိုယ်ဖွံ့ဖြိုးရေးအသင်းစီကိုတော့မော့ကိုတခြားကျောင်းကပြန်ပေးဆွဲပြီးလိုက်ရှင်းရမယ့်ပုံစံမျိုးစာသုံးဆောင်ပို့ထားခဲ့ပါတယ်။တစ်ကွက်ထဲကိုမော့ကွက်ဝင်သွားတာကြောင့်အနက်ရောက်ဖဏီကကျောင်းကသူတွေရဲ့ထိုင်ခုံမှာကြိုးနဲ့တုတ်ဖမ်းတာခံလိုက်ရပါပြီ။မူဆာတွေဦးဆောင်တဲ့ခန္ဓာကိုယ်ဖွံ့ဖြိုးရေးသိမ်းကသူတွေကရွှေရုပ်ဖွဲ့ကကောင်လေးတွေကိုမုကိုလာ [တေးဂီတ] မူဆာဦးဆောင်နဲ့ခန္ဓာကိုယ်ဖွံဖြိုးရေးသိမ်းကသူတွေကရွှေရုပ်ပွဲကကောင်လေးတွေကိုမော့ကိုလာခဲ့ကြတာဆိုတော့ကအခုမဟုတ်ဘဲဆရာကြီးလို့တစ်ဖက်ကထင်သွားကြပါပြီ။လုပ်နဲ့ရိုက်တော့လည်းမူဆာရီတို့ကလက်တစ်ဖက်ရမ်းတာနဲ့လူသုံးယောက်လောက်ကိုလွှတ်သွားတာပါ။အကုန်မှောက်ကုန်ပြီအဲဒီအချိန်တစ်ဖက်ကျောင်းကလူမိုက်တုခေါင်းဆောင်တယ်တည်ထုကရောက်လာပါတယ်။မင်းခေါင်းဆောင်မလုပ်နဲ့တော့ဆိုပြီးသူ့လူသူပြန်ဆော်လိုက်ပြီးတဲ့နောက်မူဆာအိမ်နဲ့ထပ်ရောက်လာတဲ့တံငါးကိုပါတယ်ကတည့်လွှတ်လိုက်ပါတယ်။မာစင်မရှိတဲ့တာကဘာကြောင့်ဒီလောက်သံမာနေရတာလဲ။သံဃာ့ကိုပါစိတ်ဆောင်ရုံပြီးတဲရုကတိုက်တာကြောင့်လူတွေကို သံဃာ့ကိုပါစိတ်ဆိုပြီးတဲရုကတိုက်တာကြောင့်လူတွေကိုခင်ဗျားရဲ့စိတ်ဆိုသုံးပင်မတိုက်သင့်ဘူးဆိုကာမော်ကရောက်လာပါတယ်သူ့ကိုတုတ်ထားတဲ့ကြိုးကိုပါစိတ်ဆိုင်ရနဲ့ဖြေပြလိုက်တာကြောင့်တဲကလည်းအတော်လေးအံအားသင့်သွားပါတယ်ဒီမှာတွေအပိုင်းလေးပြီးဆုံးပါတယ်ချင်နေပါတယ်စိတ်ဆွမ်းအားမြတ်မျိုးနဲ့တိုက်နေပေမယ့်မော့ကကုခံရုံကလွယ်ပြီးဘာမှပြန်မလုပ်ပါဘူးမော့ကိုအဆက်မပြတ်ကိုင်ပေါက်နေခဲ့ပြီးဒင်ပယ်ကစိတ်မရှိတော့ဘဲတဲတို့ကိုကျန်ရှိနေသေးတဲ့မကောင်းဆိုးဝါးဝိန်းစွမ်းကနေတိုက်ခိုက် [တေးဂီတ]
