ကိုနှောင်ဘူးလို့ထင်သွားကြပြီးအရင်ကလည်းလူမိုက်တော့ဖြစ်နိုင်ခြည်ရာပိုများနေတာပေါ့။လောကထဲမှာဖွင့်လှည့်ထားမိခဲ့တဲ့သံဃာရဲ့အလွယ်ရေးထဲမှာလည်းပုလွေတွေလည်းတွေ့ရပြီးသူကဒါတွေကိုရပ်နေခဲ့တဲ့ပုံစံမျိုးကာမွန်တော်တို့ကပြောဆိုနေကြပါတယ်။အကုန်လုံးကသံဃာဘက်မှာမရှိကြတော့ပေမယ့်ငယ်ငယ်တုန်းကတော့ကြီးလှရင်နင့်ကိုလက်ထပ်မယ်ပြောခဲ့တဲ့မာရီကိုသူ့ဘက်မှာရှိပေးမယ်ထင်ခဲ့ပါတယ်။ဒါပေမယ့်မာရီကိုကလည်းရွာစရာကြီးလို့ပြောချလိုက်တာကြောင့်စကားလုံးတွေကတံငါးရင်တည့်တစ်မှန်ပါပြီ။သံဃာကလူမိုက်ပင်မယ့်နှစ်လောက်ကျောင်းမှန်တက်အောင်ကြိုးစားခဲ့တဲ့သူပါ။အခုတော့အတန်းမတက်ချင်တော့တာကြောင့် အခုတော့အတန်းမတတ်ချင်တော့ကြောင့်ဒီဆန်ချိန်လေးကလည်းပျက်ပြတ်သွားခဲ့ပါပြီ။တစ်ဖက်ကရေစုကလည်းကိုကွေးနေတာအတော်ကြာတဲ့အထိကိုမကွေးရသေးပါဘူး။ဒါကြောင့်ကိုလွှတ်ပြီးငါဘာတွေလုပ်နေမိပါလေ။ကျွန်တော့်မှာအစွမ်းမရှိဘူးလို့ကံကြီးကိုပြောပြီးအိမ်ပြန်မှုပြင်ပါတယ်။အိမ်ပြန်သွားပါဇွန်းကတွန်းလိမ်နေခဲ့မယ်ကံကြီးကတွေ့ခဲ့ရပါတယ်။အိမ်ရှေ့ရောက်လာတော့လည်းစိတ်ဆွဲရဲရှေ့နေသာတွေ့နိုင်တဲ့ဒင်ဘယ်ကိုရစ်စုကမြင်လိုက်ရပါတယ်။ဒီမှာတင်အပိုဒ်တစ်ခြောက်ကပြီးဆုံးပါတယ်။ဒင်ဘယ်ကတဲတို့ဖောက်ခွဲလိုက်တာအမှုန့်ဖြစ်သွားပြီးအဲ့ဒီအမှုန့်လေးတွေ ဒင်ပယ်ကတဲတို့ဖောက်ခွဲလိုက်တာအမှုန့်ဖြစ်သွားပြီးအဲ့ဒီအမှုန့်လေးတွေကနေပြန်စုစည်းခဲ့ရတာပါအရင်ကတက်တော့အားပို့နည်းသွားပါပြီအဆင့်တဲ့ဝိညာဉ်တွေကမော့ပျက်အိမ်နဲ့ဝင်ရတာကြောင့်အခုခြံရှေ့မှာဖြစ်နေရတာပါဒူးနဲ့တက်ပြီးဖျက်ဆီးပေမယ့်သူ့အကိုရဲ့ဆရာဆိုတာအကြောင်းရပ်သွားပါတယ်ကကွေးကြည့်အများကြီးကိုကွေးနိုင်သွားပါပြီဒင်ပယ်ကသူနဲ့ပူးပေါင်းရင်အကိုပစ်သူမောထက်တောင်ကျော်နိုင်တယ်လို့မတ်လုံးပေးပြီးစည်းရုံးလာပါတယ်ရာမာရဲ့လွယ်အိတ်ထဲမှာစော်တွေရဲ့အားကစားသတ်စုံကိုကြပြီးယူထားတယ်လို့ကောင်မူနှင့်စုကတွေ့ရှိထားပါတယ် ဒါကလည်းကြောက်ချတဲ့ပုံစံမျိုးပါပဲ။တကယ်တော့ရစ်စုမှာစိတ်စွမ်းအားရှိပေမယ့်ဒစ်ပယ်ကထိန်းချုပ်ပေးပြီးမှအဆင်ပြေပြေသုံးလို့ရတာမျိုးပါ။အဲ့ဒါကိုရစုကသူ့စွမ်းအားကိုကောင်းကောင်းထိန်းချုပ်တတ်သွားရင်မင်းကိုဖျောက်ပစ်လိုက်ရမလားလို့ဒင်ပယ်ကိုတောင်ခြိမ်းခြောက်ပြောနေတာပါ။ဒယ်ဦးကခေါင်းပေါ်မှာဆံပင်ထူကြီးကေသစ်နဲ့ ဇေဘယ်ကတော့ဒီကောင်စိတ်ပါပြောင်းလဲလာတာပဲလို့တွေးနေမိပါတယ်။ပြန်ကြည့်စီကိုရစ်စုကတစ်ခေါက်ပြန်သွားပြီးစွန်းကိုစိမ်းဆွမ်းအားနဲ့ကွေးပြလိုက်ပါတယ်။အပြန်မှာသူ့ကိုအနိုင်ကျင့်နေကြသူတွေလာနိုင်ခြင်းတော့စိတ်ဆွမ်းအားသုံးမီးအကုန်လုံးကိုမှောက်အောင်လုပ်ပစ်လိုက်တာပါ။တဲရုကခေါင်းပေါ်မှာဆံပင်ထူကြီးကအသစ်နဲ့ရောက်လာပါတယ်။ကူလည်းအရင်ကမြောက်ကျမြောက်ကျဖြစ်ခဲ့တယ်။မဖြစ်တာကောင်းမယ်ဆိုပြီးစုကိုလက်ဆွဲနှုတ်ဆက်ပါတယ်။တဲရုလည်းစိတ်စွမ်းရမ်းရှင်မယ်ဆိုတော့ရစ်စုကပညာစမ်းချင်နေပေမယ့်တဲအစွမ်းကအရမ်းကြီးလွန်းလို့လေတွေလည်းတိုက်လာစုလည်းမခံနိုင်အောင်ဖြစ်လာရပါတယ်။ဒွက် ဂျင်ပယ်ကိုယ်တိုင်သူ့ကိုသွားမတိုက်ဖို့ပြောလာတာပါ။အဲ့ဒီနောက်ထွက်လာခဲ့ကြပြီးရွတ်ဆုကတော့ရဲ့စွမ်းအားကြီးပေါ်ပုံကိုအားကျနေရပါတယ်။အကြံဖန်လူကရန်သမားသန်းတန်တဲ့ရှေးဟောင်းပန်းအုန်းကြီးကိုမော့ဘ်ကိုခေါ်ပြီးမော့အနားကိုကပ်ပါးချိန်ပန်းအုန်းကိုမသိမသာတိုက်ချတယ်။မော့ကစိပ်စွဲအပ်နဲ့ထိပ်မှီခုံမော့ပြန်တင်တော့လက်ကိုတိုက်ပြီးပန်းအိုးအောက်ခြေကိုအံ့အောင်လုပ်လိုက်ပါတယ်။တန်ဖိုးတန်းလျော့ခိုင်းတော့မော့ဘ်လည်းသူ့ဆရာရေဂန်ကိုဖုန်းဆက်ခွာလိုက်ရပါပြီ။ရေဂန်ကဒီဘဲတွေလိမ်ညာကောင်တွေမှန်းသိပြီးမော့ဘ်ကိုစိမ်းစွမ်းအားသုံးပြီးခိုင်းလိုက်ပါတယ်။ပြခန်းမီးသီးကမှန်တယ်။ရှေးဟောင်းအိုးတွေကကွဲ ရှေးဟောင်းအိုးတွေကကွဲကုန်ပြီးပန်းချီကားတွေလည်းအလိုလိုလဲကျလာမှဖိုးတန်တွေနှစ်ယောက်လည်းတော်တော်လေးကိုလန့်သွားကြတာပါ။ဘဲနှစ်ကျောင်းကလူမိုက်ခေါင်းဆောင်ကျောင်းကိုရောက်လာပြီးအဖြူရောင်ဒီအဆိပ်လိုလူသိများကြတဲ့ကိုထုတ်ပေးလို့ပြောပါတယ်။ဒါပေမဲ့မော့မှန်းမသိကြဘဲအဖြူအောင်တည်အစိတ်ဆိုတဲ့နာမည်ကိုပဲသိကြတာပါ။ကျောင်းသားကောင်စီခေါင်းဆောင်ကာမတို့နဲ့ရစ်စုကကျောင်းရှေ့ထွက်ကြည့်ပြီးကိုစိတ်အားနဲ့ရှင်းပစ်လိုက်ပါပြီ။ကာမတို့ကအပြန်လှမ်းမှာတို့ကျောင်းကလူမိုက်အဖွဲ့တွေကသူ့ကောင်ထိလို့မင်းကအဖြူရောင်တည်ဆိပ်ပဲဆိုပြီးဝိုင်းဆော်သွားကြပါတယ်။ဒါတွေလည်းမကသေးဘဲအဖြူရောင်တည်စိတ်ကိုတွယ်ချင်နေကြတဲ့တခြား [တေးဂီတ] ဒါတင်မကသေးဘဲအောင်ဒီစိတ်ကိုတွယ်ချင်နေကြတဲ့တခြားကျောင်းကလူမိုက်တွေကတစ်ဖွဲ့ပြီးတစ်ဖွဲ့ရောက်လာကြတာကြောင့်ကောင်မူတို့လည်းထွက်ကြည့်ပြီးနေရပါတယ်ရေစုကသူကအဖြူရောင်တည်ဆိပ်ပဲဆိုပြီးလူမိုက်တွေကိုအစွမ်းတွေပြနေပါတယ်ဒါကိုတဲရွေးကတွေ့သွားပြီးမော့ကိုပြောပြရမယ်ဆိုကာထွက်သွားပါတယ်ကျောင်းသားလူမိုက်တွေကိုရစ်စုကစိတ်နဲ့တစ်ယောက်ကိုတစ်ယောက်ပူးပြီးကိုင်ရိုင်းပါတယ်အဲ့အချိန်မော့ကရောက်လာပြီးရစ်စုမင်းဒီမှာဘာလုပ်နေတာလဲလို့မေးလိုက်တာပါဒီမှာတင်အပိုင်းခုနစ်ကပြီးဆုံးပါတယ်တိုမီကမော့ကိုခေါ်ပြီးစိတ်ဆွမ်းအားရှင်တွေကိုလိုက်ရှာနေပြပါတယ်အဲ့နောက်တဲခေါ်လို့ လုပ်လိုက်သွားရာကနေသူ့နာမည်သုံးပြီးဖြစ်နေတဲ့စားလေးတန်ချောင်းကသူတွေ့လိုက်ရတယ်အဲ့ဒါကတော့တခြားသူမဟုတ်ဘဲသူ့ညီစုပါပဲရစ်စုကအစမ်းသုံးပြတော့မော့ကပြန်ဖိုင်းမယ်တင်ပေမယ့်မော့ကဂကုန်ယူပါတယ်မင်းဒါကိုမရလို့ငယ်ငယ်တုန်းကငိုခဲ့တာလေလို့ပြောခဲ့တယ်ရွတ်စုကတော့ငယ်ငယ်ကအစ်ကိုစိတ်စွမ်းအားသုံးနိုင်တာကိုအားကျခဲ့တာကြောင့်မဟုတ်ဘဲတကယ်ကကြောက်နေခဲ့တာလို့ပြောလာပါပြီတခြားကြီးကိုယ်တွေလိုရန်ဖြစ်ခဲ့တာကိုအကို့ရဲ့အစွမ်းကိုမကွယ်နိုင်လို့ပဲဒါကြောင့်အကို့သဘောအတိုင်းအကုန်လုပ်ခဲ့ရတာအခုတော့ဒါတွေကအတိတ်ဖြစ်သွားပြီဒင်ပယ်ကတော့မော်ဘ်ရှုံးမကိုမလိုလား လို့ပြောပြီးကိုယ်တည်းကနေထွက်ပြေးသွားပြီးဒါကိုမော့ကိုလည်းရေခနဲတွေ့လိုက်ရပါတယ်ဒါပေမယ့်မော့ကတော့လည်းကျနေတဲ့သူတွေကိုကျွန်တော့်ညီလေးလုပ်တာကိုခွင့်လွှတ်ပေးကြပါအခုကစပြီးသူနဲ့ရင်းနှီးနှီးနေပေးကြပါလို့ပြောပေမယ့်ဟိုလူတွေကတော့ဒီလောက်နဲ့ခွင့်မလွှနိုင်ဘူးဆိုပြီးမော့ကိုဒူးထောက်ခိုင်းပါတယ်မော့ကလည်းဒူးထောက်လိုက်ပြီးဒီမြင်ကွင်းကိုတိုက်ခေါင်မိုးပေါ်ကနေအင်္ကျီခရမ်းရောင်တဲ့လူကကြည့်နေပါတယ်သူကတော့ကိုရိုမာလို့ခေါ်ပါတယ်ကိုရိုမာကရူစကီဆီကိုဖုန်းဆက်ပြီးရူစကီကတော့ကမ်းကြီးတို့ကိုစမ်းသပ်ခံကာစောင့်နေကိုဒါနဲ့မေလမ်းနေရာလုပ်ထားတဲ့အဖြစ်ကလေးတွေကိုလည်းကြိုးနဲ့တုတ် လုပ်ဖမ်းထားပါတယ်။ဒါကိုလည်းစိတ်စောရပ်နဲ့ယူပြီးတစ်အိမ်ထဲကိုထည့်လိုက်ပါတယ်။ရစ်စုကိုအခုတစ်လောနာမည်ကြီးတွေရဲ့အဖီရောင်တည်အစိတ်ဆိုပြီးဖမ်းခိုင်းပါတယ်။ကိုရာမှာအောက်ကိုဆင်းချာပြီးရွေးဆုရဲ့မျက်နှာကိုဆုပ်ပျက်သတ်နေအောင်လုပ်လိုက်တာပါ။လူမိုက်တွေကိုလည်းသန်မာဇာနဲ့ပဲအေးအေးဆေးဆေးတိုက်ခိုက်နေသလိုလာတားရဲ့မော့ကိုလည်းနံရံကိုထိအောင်ကိုယ်ရုံမှာကထုတ်လွှတ်ပစ်လိုက်ပါတယ်။တခြားလူမိုက်တွေကိုလည်းတူထွက်ခိုင်းပြီးမထောက်ရင်သတ်မယ်ဆိုတာကြောင့်ကိုရာမှာကိုအားလုံးကဝိုင်းပြီးတူးထောက်ကြရတယ်။အဲဒီအချိန်မောကစွမ်းအားပါးပါးလေးသုံးပြီးကိုစတင်တိုက်ခိုက်ပါတယ်။ကိုရာမှာကလည်းမှဆွမ်းအားရှိရာသိသွားခဲ့ပြီးခရုပတ်စမ်းတိုက်ကွက်ကိုသုံးပါတယ်။ ကိုယ်တော်မာကလည်းမော့ဆွမ်းအားရှိရာသိသွားခဲ့ပြီးခရုပတ်စမ်းတိုက်ကွက်ကိုသုံးပါတယ်။မော့ကိုဆက်တိုက်ထိုးနေပြီးကလည်းအရမ်းကာဒေါသထွက်ပါ၏။ဒါ့ကြောင့်မော့ပေါက်ကွဲမှုက၁၀ရာခိုင်နှုန်းဖြစ်သွားပြီးကိုယ်တော်မရဲ့ပါးစပ်ကိုကိုင်ကာတိုက်နဲ့ဝန်ဆောက်ပစ်ပါတယ်။ကိုယ်တောင်မကအပြင်းထန်ပြန်ခံနေရပြီးလူမိုက်တွေကမော့ကိုအားပေးနေကြတယ်။မော့ကိုအဖေတည်ဆိပ်ဆိုတာလည်းသိသွားကြပါပြီ။ကိုရောင်မှာကမော့ကိုမနိုင်နိုင်ဘူးဆိုတာသိသွားပြီးရုကိုခေါ်ကာအမြန်ထွက်ပြေးပါတယ်။လူမိုက်တွေကိုကိုယ်ရာမှာကသူ့မျက်နှာမြင်သွားပြီဆိုပြီးနှုတ်ပေးဖို့ပြင်နေတာအခုထွက်ပြေးသွားတော့သူတို့အသက်ကနေကင်းမည်ဆိုပြီးမဝိုင်းဖက်ကာကြီးကျူးနေကြတယ်။ [တေးဂီတ] လူမိုက်တွေကိုကိုယ်ကိုရာမှာကသူ့မျက်နှာမြင်သွားပြီဆိုပြီးနှုတ်ပေးဖို့ပြင်နေတာအခုထွက်ပြေးသွားတော့သူတို့အသက်ကနေကင်းမည်ဆိုပြီးမဝိုင်းဖက်ကာကြီးကျူးနေကြပါတယ်မောကမတ်တပ်ကြီးသတိလင့်နေတာပါတဲထူးကရောက်လာပြီးမင်းတို့အိမ်နားကဖယ်နေသူတို့ကသာမန်လူမဟုတ်ဘူးလို့လာပြောပါတယ်မုန့်ကိုပြုစုပေးထားပြီးကအကျိုးအကြောင်းအားလုံးကိုတဲကိုရှင်းပြခဲ့ပါတယ်ကိုလက်သည်းအဖွဲ့ကလိုက်ရှာနေရတစ်နှစ်ကျော်ရှိပြီးသူတို့ကစိတ်စွမ်းအားရှင်အရောက်ရာလောင်းထဲကိုဖွဲ့စည်းထားတာစိတ်စွမ်းအားရှင်အဖွဲ့တွေအများကြီးရှိပေမယ့်အောင်မြင်တာကလက်သည်းဖွဲ့ပဲရှိမယ်သူတို့က [တေးဂီတ] ကကလေးစေဆန်ရှင်တွေကိုခေါ်ပြီးအတိတ်မင်းအောင်လုပ်တယ်။စစ်သားဖြစ်မွေးထားတယ်။ဓာတ်ခွဲခဲဆီဒင်ဘယ်ကခေါ်သွားတော့သိပ္ပံပညာရှင်လေးကမသေသေးဘဲသတိလစ်နေတာပါ။ဒါနဲ့ကမ်းကြီးကိုရေလောင်းပြီးနို့တော့မော့နဲ့ရစ်ဆူမှားပြီးခေါ်လာရတယ်ဆိုတာကိုကမ်းကြီးကသိသွားပါတယ်။ကလေးတွေဖမ်းသွားတဲ့အတွက်ကမ်းကြီးကတကယ်ကိုစိတ်မကောင်းဖြစ်နေရှာပါတယ်။မင်းတို့ကဘယ်သူတွေလဲမေးတော့တဲရိုးကမော့ကိုလေထဲမြှောက်ပြီးကိုယ့်ဘာသာစိတ်ဆိုးရှင်ဖြစ်ကြောင်းမိတ်ဆက်လိုက်ပါတယ်။မြို့ပြင်ကခြံဝင်းကြီးတစ်ခုဆီကလေးတွေနဲ့စုတို့ကိုခေါ်သွားကြပါတယ်။တောထဲမှာစမ်းသပ်ခံအန်ကြည်ကြီးကရှိနေပါတယ်။ဒီမှာတင်အပိုင်းရှစ်က ဒီမှာတင်အပိုင်းရှစ်ကပြီးဆုံးထားပါစခန်းထဲဝင်လာကြတော့ကိုမကသူမဖမ်းနိုင်ခဲ့တဲ့အစတီရတာနဲ့ကိုပြောပြလိုက်ပါတယ်ကော့ကိုဖမ်းဖို့ကားနဲ့ထွက်လာခဲ့ပြီးတုကလည်းလက်သည်းအဖွဲ့ကိုရက်ဆိုင်ဖို့သူလည်းကူညီမယ်လို့မော့ကိုပြနေပါတယ်ပြောနေဦးမှပဲကရောက်လာကြပြီးကိုယ်ရောင်မှာနဲ့ရာစုကီi ကတော့အခုချိန်အနေနဲ့နှိပ်စက်ခံနေရလောက်ပြီးပဲထင်နေပါတယ်တကယ်ကရေဘုန်းထဲမှာတွင်းကြီးခေါင်းနှစ်ခံရပြီးနှိပ်စက်ခံနေရသူကတော့ terရက်တာပဲဖြစ်နေခဲ့တာပါလက်သည်းအဖွဲ့ဝင်တိုင်းအမှိုက်ရိုးရှိပြီးခေါင်းဆောင်နဲ့တိုက်လို့ လို့အမာရိုးရကြတာဖြစ်ပါတယ်။အဲ့နောက်သူတို့ကိုပေးချင်ရာရာထူးပေးလိုက်ကြပါတယ်။စခန်းတည်နေရာအဖွဲ့ဝင်နာမည်အစွမ်းဆောက်တာတွေကိုမော့ဒို့ကမေးမြန်းနေရာဖြစ်ပြီးတစ်ဖက်ကလက်တည်းအဖွဲ့အစည်းအဝေးမှာလည်း၁၁ယောက်မှာခုနှစ်ယောက်ပဲရောက်သေးလို့ပါစီးဖွားစီးတွေဖြစ်နေကြတာပါ။ဒါလိုမျိုးအပြင်ထက်သွားတဲ့သူတွေကိုဖြုတ်စေချင်တဲ့သူတွေပါနေပါတယ်။ခေါင်းဆောင်ကတော့အီရှိကိုယ်တို့ဖြစ်ပြီးခန်းထဲမှာလည်းသူ့ကလက်သည်းအဖွဲ့ဝင်ဝင်ဖို့စည်းရုံးခံနေရပါတယ်။ရစ်စုကသူတို့ကဘာစမ်းမှမရှိဘူးပြောတော့ထိုးခံရပြီးသူတို့ကိုဦးဆောင်စည်းရုံးနေသူကတော့မူတိုပါပဲ။မူတိုကကိုကကိုင်တိုကိုခေါ်သွားတယ်။ [တေးဂီတ] ကကိုင်တိုကိုခေါ်သွားပြီးအတိတ်မေ့အောင်လုပ်တော့မယ်ထင်ခဲ့ကြတယ်တကယ်ကမူတိုကကိုင်တို့ကိုဓားနဲ့ထိုးသတ်လိုက်ပါတယ်ဒါကိုမြင်ပြီးလွယ်အခြားကလေးတွေကတုန်လှုပ်ကုန်ပါပြီမော့ဘ်တဲနဲ့တို့ဟာစိတ်ဆွမ်းအားနဲ့မထားတဲ့ကားပြန်ကြီးကိုစီပြီးတော့စခန်းနားကိုရောက်လာကြပါတယ်အနာရောက်တော့ကားကိုပစ်ချလိုက်တာလေအေးတွေပါထားပွင့်ကုန်ပါတယ်ကမီတာအရှေ့အထိကိုသုံးလိုက်တဲ့လေကြာပူးကိုထုတ်ပြီးသတ်ပင်တွေမာမော့တို့ကိုတိုက်ခိုက်ပါတယ်မော့ကသပင်နတ်ပင်နဲ့တာဝါဒကိုညှပ်ပစ်လိုက်တာကြောင့်ငြိမ်သွားပါပြီဘဏ်ကြီးနဲ့ကိုင်တို့တွင်တို့ ညီကိုဟာအရမ်းဝေးနေရင်တောင်စိတ်ဆက်သွယ်လို့ရပြီးခုနကတောင်စိတ်နဲ့စကားပြောနေတယ်လို့ထိုင်ချီကဆိုလာပါတယ်။ခုနသူတို့ကိုပြတဲ့ကင်တိုရဲ့အလောင်းဟာစိတ်ကိုထင်အောင်အထင်မှာဖြစ်အောင်လုပ်ထားတာဖြစ်ကောင်းဖြစ်နိုင်ပါတယ်။မူတိုကဒီအဖွဲ့ရဲ့မှတ်ဉာဏ်ကိုဖျောက်တဲ့သူဖြစ်ရမယ်။အစောက်သုံးရုပ်ကလည်းစုတို့ထွက်ပြေးဖို့လုပ်နေတာသိပေမဲ့မလုပ်နိုင်အောင်ထင်မိအေးအေးဆေးဆေးနေကြတာပါ။ကလေးတွေထဲကတစ်ယောက်က resစ်ဆုအမြဲသင့်နေကြအပူပေးပြီးသောခလောက်ထဲထည့်ကာသောကလည်းပွင့်သွားပါတယ်။အစောင့်တွေရောက်လာတော့စီစီတီမမြင်နိုင်တဲ့ဘက်ကိုကခေါ်သွားပြီးသူ့အစွမ်းသုံးကအစောင့်တွေကိုမှောက်စေခဲ့ပါတယ်။ စီတီမမြင်နိုင်တဲ့ဆီများခေါ်ပြီးတိုက်ခိုက်ရတာကအစွမ်းကနည်းနည်းပဲရှိတယ်လို့သိစေချင်တာကြောင့်ပါအဲ့ဒီအစွမ်းကိုလည်းအစွမ်းပြားဖို့ရူကစိတ်ထဲကနေအမြန်တောင်းပန်ပြီးသုံးလိုက်ရတာပါကီရဲ့ခန့်မှန်းစွမ်းကိုသုံးပြီးကိုင်တို့ဘယ်မှာရှိလဲခန့်မှန်းကြမှာပါပြီးရင်တော့သွားခဲ့ကြမယ်စစ်ခန်းရှေ့မှာတော့အဆောက်နှစ်ယောက်ကိုတဲထူးကမကြာသေးခင်ကာမှမြင်ဖူးထားတဲ့လေကြာဖို့အစွမ်းကိုသုံးပြီးတော့ဆွဲခေါ်လိုက်ပါတယ်အစောင့်တွေကသာမန်လူတွေပဲဖြစ်တာမို့လို့လန့်နေတဲ့အချိန်မှာဒင်ဘယ်ကဝင်ပူးလိုက်ပါပြီကျန်တဲ့အချိန်ဆိုရင်ဝင်ပူးလို့အဆင်မပြေပါဘူးစိတ်ဆွမ်းအားရွှင်တွေကိုတော့ အစနည်းနေတာကြောင့်ဝင်ပူးလို့မရသေးပါဘူး။ကိုရိုရိုစာကီရဲ့ခန့်မှန်းစွမ်းနဲ့ကိုင်တိုးကိုရှာနိုင်ကြပြီးမောတို့ကလည်း CCTV ကိုဖျက်ဆီးတွေ့တဲ့သူတွေကိုစိတ်စွမ်းအားနဲ့ပဲအမှောက်သိပ်ပြီးဝင်လာပါတယ်။ကလေးတွေကိုထားတာမြေအုပ်ခန်းမှာလို့သိလာရပြီးစီစီတီဘီကြည့်နေတဲ့အခန်းမှာတော့ကျူးကျော်သူတွေရှိနေပြီဆိုတာသိလိုက်ရပါတယ်။ချင်တယ်ပြောနေတာကြောင့်ခေါင်းဆောင်အီရှီဂိုရိုကတစ်ယောက်တည်းကိုတော့နှစ်ခါရှုံးလာလို့မရဘူးလို့ပြောပြီးလွှတ်ပေးလိုက်ပါတယ်။တကယ်သွားချောင့်မောလောရဲ့သာတို့ကိုရာမကလှုပ်တောင်မရဘဲနေရန်တွေကိုဇာတ်တိုက်ကာပေါက်ခံလိုက်ရပါတယ်။ဒီမှာတင်အပိုင်းကိုယ့်ဟာ ဒီမှာတင်အပိုင်းကိုကုန်တာပါတယ်သူ့လက်အုပ်ကသားပေါက်တွေကိုကျူးကျော်သူတွေကိုရှင်းပြမယ်ပြောနေပါတယ်ဒါပေမယ့်သူတို့နေတာနဲ့မော့ဘ်တို့တုတ်ကိုမရှင်းနိုင်မှာလည်းသိနေပြီးသားပါကိုကိုက်တို့ကိုဖမ်းထားတဲ့အခန်းဆီမော့ဘ်တို့တုတ်ကခိုးဝင်လာပြီးကယ်ဖို့လုပ်ခဲ့ပါတယ်အစောင့်ကမြင်သွားမယ်အဆောင်ထဲကအရပ်သောက်နေတဲ့ဂင်ဆိုတဲ့သူကအေးအေးဆေးဆေးသွားခိုင်းခဲ့ပါတယ်ဘာလို့ဆိုဂင်ကသာမန်လက်အုပ်ခံအစောင့်အနယ်နဲ့မော့လို့ဆွမ်းရွက်ရှင်တွေကအစားဘယ်လောက်ကွာချာလဲသိနားလည်လို့ပါပဲလက်သည်းပွဲကကမ္ဘာကိုအုပ်စွန်းနိုင်တဲ့အခါလက်အောက်ခံတွေကဆုလမျှော်လင့်ထားပါတယ် စွမ်းအားနဲ့ကလေးတွေကပေါင်းတိုက်တော့အနည်းငယ်ထိရောက်သလိုရှိပေမယ့်ဒီဘယ်စွမ်းအားကိုမကျော်နိုင်တာတော့သေချာပါတယ်အဲ့နောက်နာကျင်မှုကိုခံစားစေပြီးစွမ်းအားပွင့်အောင်လုပ်ပေးတဲ့အခန်းတွေထဲကိုရောက်သွားခဲ့တာပါမယ်ဆိုတဲ့လက်သည်းဖွင့်ဝန်တစ်ယောက်လည်းရောက်လာခဲ့ပြီးတစ်ဖက်မှာအချုပ်ခန်းထဲကကလေးတွေကိုမတွေ့တော့တေးရုကအစောင့်တစ်ယောက်ကိုရပ်နေပါတယ်ကျမ်းပြမှာလည်းတဲရုလက်ချက်နဲ့မှောက်ကုန်တဲ့လူတွေအများကြီးကိုတွေ့ရမှာပါမီးအစွမ်းနဲ့မာကာဝါကတဲကိုမီးတွေလုပ်ရင်းနဲ့လာရောက်တက်ခိုက်ခဲ့ပြီးတဲကအကာအကဝယ်ဖန်နဲ့ကာပါတယ်ဒါပေမယ့်တဲရုကမီးတွေကိုတန်ပြန်သွားစေခဲ့တာကြောင့်မာဝါပဲမီးပြန်ကောင် သွားပါတယ်။ဒါပေမဲ့အလေးဝင်တိုက်တာကြောင့်တဲရုကမှောက်သွားပါပြီ။မူကိုင်ရဲ့စေခိုင်းလို့ရတဲ့အရုပ်တွေဟာကျူးကျော်သူမော့ကိုရှာတွေ့သွားပါတယ်။ရုစုကအစွမ်းမရှိတဲ့ပါပွားလက်အုပ်ခံကလေးတစ်သားတွေကိုနှစ်ယောက်စီပူးရိုက်ပေးတဲ့နောက်ခြေစောင့်တာနဲ့အုတ်ရံကိုကွဲရက်သွားစေတဲ့ရှိုဆိုတဲ့သူကရောက်လာပါတယ်။သူကလည်းကလေးပါပဲ။မုန့်ကမူကိုင်ရဲ့သေတသတ်ရုပ်တွေအားလုံးကိုစိတ်စွမ်းအားနဲ့ပျက်စီးလိုက်တာကြောင့်မူကိုင်းကတော့ငိုသွားပါပြီ။စုချီi ကမူကိုင်းငိုသွားလို့မုန့်ကိုတိုက်ခိုက်ခဲ့ပြီးသူကသာမန်သိုင်းဂတ်တွေနဲ့ချတာပါ။ဆုကတခြားသူတွေနဲ့မတူတာကခန္ဓာကိုယ်တစ်ခုလုံးကကီကို စုချီကတခြားသူတွေနဲ့မတူတာကခန္ဓာကိုယ်တစ်ခုလုံးကကီကိုဒူးနဲ့လက်သီးမှာစုပြီးအားနိုင်ပါတယ်အမေကြမ်းထက်ပိုကြံပြီးချနေပေမယ့်မောကတောင်ငိုနေပါတယ်အကြောင်းကတော့သူ့ဆရာရေကန်ပြောတာကမိန်းမတွေကိုရိုက်တဲ့သူတွေကဆိုးဝါးတဲ့သူတွေဒါကြောင့်အခုလည်းကိုမတိုက်ချင်တာကြောင့်ဖြစ်ပါတယ်ဒါပေမဲ့စုချီi text: In this movie, we are shown such a world where both humans and dinosaurs live. Many years ago, when there was a destruction in the world, most of the dinosaurs were killed. But those who survived started living underground. They could not come to the outside world and their population kept increasing below. But a few years ago, a huge explosion took place. Due to which a huge path opened up, and dinosaurs started coming to the outside world through it. But the air and water here were not appropriate for them. Due to which many more dinosaurs were killed. But there were still some places where dinosaurs were living and those were sea areas and islands where the air and water were suitable for them to live. Due to this, that place became dangerous and humans stopped going there. But there were a few selected companies at that time that were allowed to go there so that they could do research on dinosaurs and people could get more information about these monstrous creatures. Now we see the scene of 2010. Where a company named InGen had built a laboratory on one of these islands. Where many geneticists and scientists are conducting research on dinosaurs. They were actually working on mutation of dinosaurs. It means, to change the dinosaurs and make them stronger and dangerous, these people were collecting the blood of all the dinosaurs and changing their DNA so that they could mutate all the dinosaurs. This InGen company has already mutated many dinosaurs in its laboratory. All of them were kept inside big containers, and now the dinosaur they were mutating was T. rex. But due to the mistake of one of their workers, the machine malfunctions. Due to which their mutation work stops in the middle. Due to which T. rex which was sleeping earlier wakes up. It gets free and starts wreaking havoc in the entire laboratory and also eats many people mercilessly. Seeing this T. rex, we understood that it had mutated to a great extent because it was appearing very big in size, very dangerous and fierce. Seeing this, all the scientists and geneticists get scared, and they run away from there leaving their laboratory and mutation work in between. After which no one came back to this laboratory and now 17 years passed in the story, and we are shown the time of 2027 directly after the year 2010. In this present time, we see a man whose name is Martin. Martin used to work in a very big pharmaceutical company named Parker which makes medicines for every deadly disease. At this time also, a very dangerous heart disease is going on in the whole world which is affecting every second person and Parker Company finds out from its research that in the coming time this disease will increase so much that one out of every five people will definitely suffer from it. text: Alright so Creed III is punching its way into theaters, with Adonis returning for the main event, going toe to toe with a ghost from his past, the Kang Gang… Wait, that's actually.. Uhhh Nevermind. But yeah these Creed flicks have really landed for me, and this third ramps things up even more. So in this video we’re going to be breaking this thing down for y’all, what the ending means for Creed, where the heck was Rocky, potential spin-offs, and of course our reaction and review for this haymaker flying, Hadouken style movie. All sorts of heavy spoilers in this heavyweight match up, so a huge thank you for clicking this, I’m your feather-weight host Jared. Put up your dukes and let’s get into Creed III. Alright so Creed III picks up years after the events of Creed II, with Adonis now comfortably living the retired life career-wise, and being more of a family man. He hasn’t boxed in the ring for roughly 3 years, taking a page from Rocky 3, instead focusing on training the best up and coming boxers in his gym, and setting up the biggest of prize fights. However as these things go, a ghost from his past appears at his doorstep stirring up old forgotten memories. Damian "Dame" Anderson, played by Jonathan Majors, is that ghost. Back in the day, both lived in a boys home together, with Damian being an up and comer in the amatuer boxing leagues. But after a night of the two hanging out, Adonis assaults an old boy's home guardian that abused them, Damian pulls a gun, with Adonis running away, resulting in Damian taking the heat and going to prison for 18 years. Now all of this past coming back to haunt them/underdog revenge story leads the pair to face off against one another in a huge prize fight at Dodger stadium. But not before Adonis gives Damian a second chance, training at his gym for free, becoming a sparring partner with Creed’s prized Felix Chavez, the reigning heavyweight champ of the world. However all of this was a part of Dame’s plan, orchestrating an assault on Viktor Drago, who was supposed to fight Chavez, taking his place in the event due to urgent scheduling, beating him mercilessly in the ring, and becoming the heavyweight champ basically overnight. Classic nepotism. Creed knows he must make right for his wrongs, so he retires from retirement, jumping back in the ring, publicly challenging Dame for the title. Now the whole story, especially the ending, deals with past trauma, regrets, grudges, fractured relationships, living in the past, needing to overcome those barriers, and forgiveness. Creed is dealing with the haunting memory of that night long ago, Damian essentially using him, and his mother who hid letters Damian had written Creed all those years ago. Very The Notebookish. But one of the most emotional scenes is Creeds mother passing due to a stroke, but even she goes as far as to forgive Apollo and Adonis in her last moments, which drives Creed to do the same. As for Damian, he is dealing with the fact his life and dream was robbed from him, and even though he doesn’t know Creed never received his letters, he holds that against him in their final bout with one another. This final climatic 12 round boxing match is different from your stereotypical boxing matches, because Jordan uses some of his anime influences here to showcase how, yes this is a fight amongst two behemoths, but also each is fighting their own internal problems and struggles. A moment where prison bars are on a side of the ring is the struggle Damian endured, while visualizing it for Creed. The same goes for Creed, when punching Damian, he visualizes him as a pillow, which was something tied to the boy's home where he was abused as a child. So it’s really interesting the way Jordan was able to frame this final fight as several different things, allowing it to become personal for each character. Creed essentially gets a second, third, ninth wind thinking of his mother, knocking out Damian with less than a minute left in the 12th round. Creed goes on to become the reigning heavyweight champ once again, and the peak of boxing. So not too surprising for this underdog type story. But the ending honestly feels like the deleted scene from Creed II where Creed talks with Viktor in the locker room. Of course this time it is Creed and Damian in these positions, with the two finally forgiving one another for everything they had gone through. It’s a much-earned final scene for the pair, calm and emotional, and sets up Damian as someone who could make a return in the franchise. Now does Creed III feature any sort of post credits scene tease towards what's next for the champ? Like does Street Fighter’s Blanka jump out, electrify Creed, and break apart his car? Ehhh no, not exactly. But at the Hollywood Premiere of Creed III, Michael B Jordan did hint at potentially more Creed movies or even spin-offs saying, “Building the Creed universe is something that I’m really excited about.” So it’s no surprise B Jordan wants Creed to be what Rocky was. So I could see Creed 4 having him back in the limelight, his stock higher than ever, but with a bigger target on his back. Even going international with the scope of things and the anime influences of the villains and fight choreography. Maybe not as far as the street fights of Rocky V and Tommy Gunn, but you see where I’m coming from. And with the mention of a bigger Creed universe, this all ties in with the reports of a Drago movie in the works. Reported exclusively by TheWrap, screenwriter Robert Lawton had been tapped to write Drago, focusing on the Drago family, both Ivan and Viktor. No further details have been revealed, so I could see this picking up on the character current day in terms of the Creed franchise, but peppering in flashbacks to show some of his origins and struggles, without fully diving into another stereotypical Hollywood origin story. I’m curious if you’d want to see this Rocky and Creed franchise blow out, and get weird with all of these different boxers. If so, drop your best anime/video game-esque character for Creed to face off against in the comments. Mine would be Ethelbert P. Shackleton III fighting only in the Old English boxing style BRILLIANT! Now one of the biggest felt absences from the film was good ole’s Rocky. Ehhh Rocky, where you at? Stallone is nowhere to be seen. His name is mentioned in passing a couple of times, while some scenes feel like they needed his essence. However the story never fully gives the audiences an explanation of where he’s at, his status, really anything. Well it's a bit of a messy behind the scenes reason why the creator of this character and franchise isn’t here. Quick story time, but back when Stallone was trying to get Rocky off of the ground, he ended up selling the ownership rights to producer Irwin Winkler, because at the time Stallone only had $100 to his name, and basically had to. Now fast forward almost 5 decades, Stallone still has zero ownership of the character or franchise, and was a bit caught off guard when he heard news of the Drago spin-off, calling Winkler a "parasite" who is "picking clean the bones of another wonderful character I created." In a recent interview with Sirius XM, Stallone shared that he's had a "rough emotional ride" in choosing to cut ties with the franchise he created, but that he refuses to support any new Creed movies as long as producer Irwin Winkler is still involved. So who knows, maybe if and/or when Creed 4 comes around, Rocky will make his long awaited return up those Philadelphia Museum of Art stairs with everyone cheering. But yeah I had a solid time with Creed III. Sure, is it predictable, with the story beats jumping to exactly what and where you thought they were going? Yeah kinda, but I don't think this needed a deep introspective look on the character. Though it does crack into some great symbolism and subtext of past trauma, regrets, grudges, fractured relationships, and living in the past in the final fight between Creed and Dame. With the final fight being something totally new, fantastical, leaning into the anime influences Jordan wanted to showcase here. And honestly that worked for me. It feels like it has its own style and identity thanks to Michael B Jordan’s directorial debut vision, but is a bit more than just another boxing movie. It has a sprinkle of a revenge thriller, mirroring elements of 2015’s The Gift, with Jonathan Majors absolutely nailing the dramatic scenes, and being a complete monster in the physical scenes. My scorecard at the end of 12 rounds would be a 7/10 for Creed III. It’s got the stuff Rocky and Creed fans are looking for, and there’s enough evolution in the fight choreography to make it feel fresh. Like some really cool slow down, analyzing and targeting body parts that feels video game-esque. But I thought there were some really obvious pacing issues between acts 2 and 3, hoping for more bombastic boxing, and honestly Rocky was definitely missed in the emotional scenes after Creed’s mother passed away. Rocky didn’t need a huge roll, but he was missed. Also you know in Creed 6 or whatever, his daughter is going to carry on the mantle. It’s right there, let me know I was right in like 12 years. Anyway I’d love to hear your thoughts on Creed III. Was this another solid addition into the Rocky/Creed world, and what did you think of B Jordan’s directorial debut? Noreen then turns to look at the car and keeps staring at Chris. Seeing all this, Sarah feels weird and leaves with Chris for their home. In this house, Chris spots a spider and this makes Chris nervous. Sarah catches the spider in a jar and goes outside to release it. But here Chris asks Sarah why they both left Chris's father behind. Chris gets angry and says that if his father were here, he would have killed the spider. And saying this, Chris kills the spider with his shoe. Chris then runs toward the forest and Sarah follows him. In the forest, Sarah finds a large hole in the ground and she peers inside it. Just then she turns around and finds Chris there. That same night at a dinner party, a friend of Sarah's tells her that Noreen's son James and she used to study together in their childhood. Sarah's friend says that one day Noreen barged into their class and was later forcibly removed. After which , the police also came to the school. James was later expelled from school, and a few months later, he was murdered because Noreen had run her car over him . Anyway, that night, Sarah was sleeping and she heard some noises. She comes out of her room and sees that the front door is open, and Sarah starts thinking that Chris has left the house. Sarah goes into the forest to look for Chris, but she doesn't find him there, and after that, she comes home and calls the police. But in the middle of the call, when Sarah turns around, she sees Chris standing there. The next day , Sarah goes to the doctor and is given medication for anxiety. So, when Sarah brings Chris home from school, she finds Noreen standing on the way, and this time, Sarah also meets Noreen's husband, Des. Yes friends, someone had brutally beaten Noreen to death, and her head was buried in the ground. Later, Sarah attends Noreen's funeral and sees that there were mirrors all over Noreen's house, and they were covered with black cloths. Des then explains to Sarah that Noreen believed her son James was an imposter, and Noreen could tell this by looking at James's reflection. This belief of Noreen's had become a habit that she had become obsessed with. Sarah asks what happened to James? And Des says that James died after being hit by a car. But that car wasn't Noreen's, it was actually Des's. This confuses and shocks Sarah because her friend had said that James died because of Noreen's car. Anyway, meanwhile, Sarah and Chris's relationship also starts falling apart, and Sarah notices that Chris has started behaving a bit strangely. For instance, Chris didn't like spaghetti at all. But suddenly, he was eating this dish with great relish. One day while jogging, Sarah finds Chris's toy soldier in the woods and asks him why he went there despite her forbidding it. Chris gets extremely angry and pushes the dinner table toward Sarah. Now this scene was very weird because the table was heavy and a small child like Chris couldn't push it so easily. That same night, Sarah hears strange noises after her bath, and when she goes near Chris's room, she sees him catching spiders and eating them. Not only that, friends, Chris's body was twisted in a strange way, which scared Sarah. The next day, Sarah takes Chris to the doctor, and the doctor says that Chris is perfectly normal. But Sarah had started feeling that Chris was not himself. The next day, Sarah and Chris are having breakfast. Chris starts touching Sarah's face. But then Chris starts touching the scar on Sarah's head and begins to pry it open. In the next scene, we see Sarah suddenly wake up in bed and realize it was just a nightmare. That same day, Sarah goes to Chris's school function, and during his performance, she notices that Chris is suddenly focusing on her while saying his lines, and his voice sounds very strange. Sarah runs out of the room, and later, one of Chris's teachers brings him to her. Sarah starts doubting even more if Chris was real. And that is why she hides a camera in Chris's room. The next morning, when Sarah watches those videos, she becomes even more convinced that Chris is not her real son. Sarah takes her camera to Des's house and shows him the videos too. But Des didn't want to see any of this because it reminded him of Noreen and James, and he angrily throws Sarah's camera away. Sarah asks Des one last time if he doesn't believe her, but Des doesn't give a clear answer. Sarah returns home and starts testing Chris, and when Chris is watching TV, she asks him to play their favorite game. In this game, Sarah used to count to three, and then she and Chris would make funny faces. But this time, even after counting to three, Chris keeps looking at Sarah blankly. Sarah then says that whoever he is, he is not Chris. And then Chris starts picking Sarah up and slamming her all around the kitchen. This makes it clear that he isn't really Chris, but some supernatural entity. Yes, friends, Sarah falls unconscious from her injuries. But when she wakes up, she finds herself on the ground outside her house. She sees that this entity, which looked like Chris, is digging a hole in the ground. After this, the entity drags Sarah away and buries her head in the ground. From this scene, we realize that Norine was also killed by this entity, as Norine's head was found buried the same way. And yes, the entity killed Norine because she realized by looking at him that he wasn't the real Chris. Anyways, after burying Sarah in the ground, the entity itself passes out because Sarah had drugged it. Meanwhile, Sarah pulls herself out of the ground and drags the entity into her basement. Here, Sarah sees the entity's reflection in her car's broken mirror and sees a demonic entity in the reflection. The entity starts waking up and attacks Sarah again. Sarah somehow frees herself and locks the entity in the basement before running away. Sarah now goes to that large hole in the woods and climbs inside. Through this hole, Sarah reaches an underground tunnel where she finds the real Chris, who was still alive. Sarah takes Chris and heads out of the tunnel. But she sees that there are many monsters in the tunnel chasing them. Sarah also finds quite a few skeletons in this tunnel. And when Sarah and Chris reach the end of the tunnel, a monster grabs Sarah's hand. Sarah starts hitting it with her flashlight. But in no time, that monster starts looking exactly like Sarah. Sarah and Chris somehow manage to exit the tunnel and go home to get the car keys. Sarah sets the house where the entity was locked up on fire and leaves with Chris. In my opinion, the answer to this is no. Which means, the one Sarah was taking a picture of at the end of the movie was indeed Chris. So why did his face look blurred? That is because Chris was riding his bike and was in motion when Sarah was taking his picture. That is why his face appeared blurred. This scene actually shows that Sarah has become so paranoid from that incident that she was always suspicious, which is why she had put up many mirrors in the house. Sarah already had anxiety and was in an abusive relationship, which had traumatized her, and she was also experiencing hallucinations throughout the movie. So it seems this was all Sarah's psychological distress, and she had started behaving exactly like Noreen, who, if you remember, also used to keep mirrors in her house. Now the second question, who exactly was that entity? We find the answer to this in Irish folklore. Actually, that entity was a changeling, and such entities usually feed on children. In this movie too, this changeling takes Chris's place to live his life and leaves Chris in that tunnel to die. We saw many skeletons in that tunnel, and this shows that these changelings have been in that place for a long time and have been feeding on children. Perhaps the same thing happened with Noreen's son, James. These changelings live underground, and the monsters Sarah saw in that tunnel were also all changelings. Another theme of this movie is that it depicts the relationship between a mother and her child. Often when children grow up, their parents notice how they start to change. material for a tv miniseries and yes they try to include it all what happens is none of the angles gets fully covered this is a hit and run biography that winds up sounding like life's little instruction book zachary levi who plays warner doesn't get time to process what all of the changes mean anna paquin as his wife is short-changed too first she's a woman who doesn't want to marry him want to know the outcome a film called being kurt warner might have been much more inspirational than american underdog that could have drilled down and got into the essence of a man who accomplished text: Hello everyone, and today we are going to summarize a popular poem by Nissim Ezekiel titled "The Visitor.""The Visitor" was published in his 1965 poetry collection titled*The Exact Name *. This poem is basically about the myth which says that if you hear cawing sounds at your house in the morning. If a crow sits and caws, it means that perhaps a guest is about to arrive. A visitor is about to come. So now, let's begin with the first stanza. In the first stanza, a crow sits on the poet's window, the room's window, and caws three times. Hearing which, the poet looks at it. Now, because this crow has cawed three times, there is a possibility that perhaps a visitor, perhaps a guest, is coming. The way the crow is looking at the poet, the way it is staring, is striking. It looks quite ominous. It is sitting in a stiff posture. The poet compares its entire posture, and the way its neck is positioned, to a nagging woman. That is to say, a pestering woman; the room is filled with the crow's cawing sounds. In the second stanza, the poet says that when he received this message that a visitor is coming. Meaning, before the crow made this sound, the poet was sleepwalking. Sleepwalking meant he was lost in his thoughts, and in those thoughts, he was thinking about the world's well-being. He was wearing minimal clothes, wandering the world in them, and thinking about the good of others. As soon as the crow cawed three times, he came out of his thoughts and now he has become worried. Why has he become worried? Because a visitor is about to arrive, and the poet does not know who the visitor is. So, he is thinking about how he will receive the visitor who is coming. And how will he deal with them? If a visitor comes whose views do not match his own, how will he talk to them? How will he deal with them? In the third stanza, he waits for the visitor all day long. While waiting, several thoughts come to his mind about who the guest might be. Then he wonders if an angel is coming in human disguise and he won't be able to recognize him, or perhaps Satan might arrive. What if some evil like Satan arrives in some unknown form, in an unfamiliar shape, so the writer doesn't recognize him? Then what will happen is that the writer's character will be tested. The evil, let's say Satan, will try to tempt him. And if he gets tempted, then what will happen? And if all this happens, his sleep will be lost. It will be ruined, which he doesn't want. In the fourth stanza, when the visitor arrives and leaves. After that, the poet says that the person he had imagined the visitor to be, no such person came as he had expected. The visitor who came arrived empty-handed, just to pass some time, to kill his time, with good intentions, just to pass time, to talk, to have light conversations—that was his intention. Even the visitor talked about such unimportant things, nothing significant, that there was more substance in the cigar or the smoke of the cigarette they were smoking than in his words. Now in the fifth stanza, the poet says that the visitor was a very normal visitor. It was a routine visitor; there was nothing like what was expected. So the poet says that he had completely failed to guess what the visitor would be like. His assumptions had turned out to be completely wrong. The poet further says that miracles only happen within a human being. They do not happen in the outside world. We can only see normal, ordinary things. Like the patterns on the carpet, human sexual urges, and the changing seasons. We are only able to see these ordinary changes. So, this is where the poem ends. So, here is where this poem ends. Alexander reaches him and apologizes for calling him by his real name, but he doesn't mind. He has brought in some drawings of Fernando along with a letter. He knows that his paternal grandparents were not even adults when they had his father. Marcelo's mother was enslaved in the house. Now he can barely remember him. He then takes a drive and they go out. की 1952 के इवेंट्स के कर साल बाद जहां पर हम एक चर्च को देखते हैं जहां एक बच्चा जैक होता है जो की रेगुलरली चर्च जय करता था और फादर के केमोन में हाथ बताता यहां पर यह फादर काफी जरूरी थे और किसी खास मकसद से यहां पर थे गैराज के मांस के बाद वो अपना कम खत्म कर रहा होता है और यहां पर वाइन को नीचे रखना जा रहा होता है की तभी उसे किसी की हलचल का एहसास होता है जिसको वो चेक करता है तो उसे कॉफी भयानक आवाज सुने देती है अब वो फादर को बुलाने जाता है और तभी फादर वहां पर आते हैं और जब वो दोनों चेक करते हैं तो वहां पर उन्हें होली वाटर बहुत ही तेजी से उबलता हुआ दिखाई देता है जो आप बनकर उड़ जाता है और इस के पीछे ही हम किसी शैडो को देख पाते हैं जहां पर बहुत ही खौफनाक मंदिर हमको दिखता है और इसको हम अच्छे से जानते हैं यह कोई और नहीं बल्कि नॉन यानी की डिमांड बालक होता है और ये फादर को बड़ी ब्राह्मी से हवा में उड़ता है और उनको जिंदा जलाकर खत्म कर देता है और यहां पर अब सोच रहे होंगे की रैंडम वेलॉग ऐसे ही सबको मार रही है लेकिन यहां पर ऐसा बिल्कुल नहीं था वेलवेट का एक बहुत ही खतरनाक मकसद है डेमों वॉक का यहां पर एक बहुत ही भयानक मकसद था इसके पीछे हरि इसी के साथ में उसे चर्च के टॉप फ्लोर पर हम नान को देखते हैं और नीचे एक व्यक्ति अपना बैग लेकर वहां से बाहर आता हुआ नजर आता है यानी की ये आदमी और बेल यहां पर जुड़े हुए थे एब्सन यहां से शिफ्ट होता है और हमें दिखाए जाता है सिस्टर आयरन को जो की अब किसी चर्च में रहती है और जैसा की मैंने बताया की नान के इवेंट्स के बाद कहानी 4 साल आगे जा चुकी है और यहां पर किसी को सिस्टर आयरन के बड़े में ज्यादा नहीं पता की उन्होंने आखरी मूवी में बालक से लड़ाई कारी थी बल्कि सब यही जानते हैं की वो जो कोई भी सिस्टर थी वो कहानी दूर चली गई थी या फिर पागल हो गई थी फिर यहां पर अच्छी इसी लाइफ को बीता रही होती है और गॉड की शरण में होती है तभी यहां पर हमें एक नई लड़की देवरा दिखाई जाति है जिसका इंटरेस्ट यहां पर नान बने में और गॉड की तरफ काफी कम होता है अब वो दोनों बात करती है जहां पर डेब्रा अपने बड़े में बताती है की उसके फादर ने उसे यहां पर भेज दिया क्योंकि उसके भाई देश सेवा के लिए गए हैं तो फादर ने उसको गॉड की सेवा के लिए भेज दिया है इस पर ये दोनों थोड़ा सा मजाक करती हैं सिस्टर आयरन अपने बड़े में बताती है की उसके फादर ने उसको यहां भेजो था और वो उसे उतना खास पसंद नहीं करते थे एवं वो उसकी मदर को भी पसंद नहीं करते थे और उसे अपनी मां के बड़े में ज्यादा कुछ याद नहीं है बस छोटी-मोटी झलकियां याद है और इन झलकियां में हम उसके मां को भी देख पाते हैं और नापसंद करने का रीजन यही था की यहां पर जो इनको बिजनेस वगैरा आते हैं वह सब को झूठ लगता थे खैर यहां पर अब चर्च में आखरी मूवी के हाथों के बड़े में चर्चा हो रही थी लेकिन किसी को यह नहीं पता था की वह नान खुद सिस्टर आयरन थी इन फैक्ट वह खुद इन चीजों से दूर रहना चाहती थी क्योंकि भले ही वह इविल को हारने में कामयाब हो गई लेकिन हम जानते हैं की हर इंसान के अंदर डर होता है जो की उसके अंदर घर कर चुका था फिर तभी यहां पर मूवी का सीन थोड़ा सा शिफ्ट होकर फ्रांस के अंदर बोर्डिंग स्कूल की तरफ जाता है जहां पर आखिरी मूवी का फ्रैंची या फिर मॉरिस कम कर रहा था और स्कूल को मैडम लॉरेन को चलाया करती थी और नेचर वाइस वो काफी एग्रेसिव होती है मॉरिस के साथ में जिसके पीछे एक रीजन है अल में उनका बेटा एक यही पर चप्पल के अंदर मारा गया था जिसकी वजह से चप्पल के अंदर जान पर प्रतिबंध लगा हुआ था घर यहां पर सूफी नाम की एक मासूम सी लड़की भी पड़ती है जिसकी मदर किड वहीं पर पड़ता हैं और मोरी सोफी का बहुत अच्छा दोस्त है और उसकी किट से भी अच्छी खासी बॉन्डिंग थी वो उसकी काफी केयर भी करता है और सबसे बड़ी बात की यहां पर तीन-चार ऐसी लड़कियां हैं जो की सोफी को बल्ली करती रहती है जींस अक्सर मॉरीशस को बचता है वो उसको उसका बॉयफ्रेंड का कर चढ़ते हैं और सबसे बड़ी बात ये होती है की यहां पर हम क्लीयरली देख पाते हैं की मोदी के साथ में कुछ ना कुछ गड़बड़ है और हम जानते हैं की वो क्या गड़बड़ है उसके अंदर नानी की बालक थी जिसकी बाद में अगली सीन के अंदर में एक लड़की को यहां पर देखते हैं जो की कुछ समाज डिलीवरी करने के लिए यहां पर आई है और उसको अजीब हालात में मालिश मिलता है यहां पर अल में कॉकरोच इसको का रहा था और कॉकरोच को साफ करने के लिए इसी बोर्ड स्कूल की मैडम ने उसको बोला था जिसके पीछे रीजन यह होता है की यहां पर जो बोली लड़कियां थी ना उन्होंने यहां पर मैडम के रूम के अंदर कॉकरोचेस दाल दिए थे कहर मॉरिस के अंदर से अचानक से ही बालक बाहर आकर उसे लड़की को खत्म कर देती है और अब तक आपको समझ में ए गया होगा की शुरुआत में जो आदमी वहां पर सूटकेस लेकर निकाला था जिसने की फादर को जलाकर मार दिया था वो कोई और नहीं बल्कि यहां पर मोहनी सी था जिसके अंदर ना थी यानी की बालक और विलक यहां पर ऐसे ही किसी को नहीं मार रही बल्कि इसके पीछे बहुत ही सॉलिड रीजंस हैं खैर दूसरी तरफ हम देखते हैं की सिस्टर आयरन को यहां पर नाइटमेयर्स आते हैं मॉरिस के जो की उसे मत मांग रहा होता है लेकिन तभी उसे बालक दारा देती है क्योंकि यहां पर वो इन सब चीजों से जुड़ी हुई थी इसके बाद में वो काफी परेशान रहने लगती है अब सीन वापस से बोर्डिंग स्कूल की तरफ जाता है जहां पर वो बोली लड़कियां एक दिन सूफी को परेशान करती हैं और उसको इस एबंडेंट एप्पल के अंदर लेकर जाति है जहां पर वो उसको एक गेम खेलने के लिए बोलती हैं की उन्हें विंडो पर बने हुए गोट की आपको देखना होगा जिसके अंदर डेमों की आई दिखाई देती है और अगर उसने नजर हटाई तो दे माना कर उसे खत्म कर देगा और अब वो इस को देखने लगती है लेकिन वो लड़कियां उसको अकेला छोड़कर वहां से निकाल जाति है तभी वहां पर अचानक से ही हलचल शुरू हो जाति है और पैरानॉर्मल चीज भी वहां पर होने लगी थी और विलग उसे हंड करती है जिससे डर कर वहां से भागने लगती है लेकिन तभी मोरी सागर उसको बच्चा लेट है और अब तक किट भी वहां पर ए गई थी जो की उसे अपने साथ ले जाति है और फिर से सीन यहां पर आयरन की तरफ शिफ्ट होता है जिसको रेवरों बुलेट हैं और उसे कहते हैं की अलग-अलग जगह पर प्रीस्ट और नंद की जान जा रही है और रिसेंटली फ्रांस के चर्च के अंदर एक प्रीस्ट को जलाकर मार दिया गया यानी की वही शुरुआत वाला सीन और ये कम इस डेमों वेल का है जो की मारा नहीं है और खत्म नहीं हुआ वो वापस ए चुका है इसको पहले भी एक बार सिस्टर आयरन ऑलरेडी हर चुकी है तो दोबारा उसे इस कैसे को इन्वेस्टिगेट करना होगा लेकिन यहां पर सिस्टर आयरन इसके लिए माना करने लगती है उसका यह कहना था की उसके साथ में फादर बग भी थे जो की काफी अच्छी पोजीशन पर है तो उन्हें उनसे बात करनी चाहिए लेकिन रेगुलर यहां पर यह कहते हैं की उनकी हैजा से मौत हो चुकी है और ये कम सिस्टर आयरन को करना हुआ क्योंकि यहां पर दुनिया की और इंसानियत की बात थी जिसके चलते सिस्टर आयरन अपने डर पर काबू पाती है और यहां पर जल मिलती है इसकी इसको इन्वेस्टिगेट करने के लिए क्योंकि यहां पर रेवरेंट का यह मानना था की यह मौतें ऐसे ही नहीं हो रही है यहां पर जो साड़ी की साड़ी जेड हैं वो रोमानिया से जुड़ी हैं लेकिन यहां पर वो बालक क्यों ए चुका है तो इसका रीजन सिस्टर आयरन ही पता लगा शक्ति है अब आयरन फ्रांस की इस चर्च के लिए निकाल जाति है जहां पर फादर को जलाकर रख किया गया था और यहां पर उसका साथ देने के लिए सिस्टर डबरा चुपके से ट्रेन के अंदर चढ़कर उसके साथ निकाल जाति है जी पर आयरन उसको समझती है की यह ठीक नहीं होगा और पता चलने पर उसको निकाल दिया जाएगा लेकिन डबरा उसे अपनी मां की फोटो दिखाकर बोलती है की वह भी जल कारी मेरी गई थी और वो उनको ही अपना गॉड मानती थी और तब से उसका पेट टूट चुका है और उसे कोई भी मिरेकल नजर नहीं आया और वो नहीं मानती की वाइन को छूकर प्रेयर्स करने से वो जीसस क्राइस्ट के खून में बादल सकता है इस पर ध्यान दें और फेथ से बड़ी कोई भी चीज नहीं है और फेथ के चलते ही बड़े-बड़े मिरेकल्स होते हैं जो की उसने खुद देखें हैं और मेरे ख्याल से यहां पर इस मिरेकल को देखने आई थी खैर इसी बीच बस को अपनी मदर की भी कहानी सुनती है की उसने उससे झूठ कहा था उसे अपनी इसे याद है जो की गॉड में बहुत मानती थी और उनको गॉड की साइड मिली हुई थी लेकिन उसके हसबैंड उसको पागल समझते थे और फिर उसके पिता ने उसकी मां को मेंटल हॉस्पिटल में भेज दिया था हमेशा के लिए इसके बाद से वो उनको नहीं देख पी का रहा वो दोनों फ्रांस पहुंच जाते हैं और इन्वेस्टिगेशन शुरू होती है और आयरन को यहां पर आते ही जैक की विधानसभा आने लगता हैं यानी की चर्च के अंदर आते ही और जैक ने यहां पर उसे एक ऋषि फिक्स भी पकड़ा था की अब यहां पर वो थोड़ी बहुत छान में करती है और नान की विजंस उसको बार-बार हांट करते रहते हैं अब तभी उसे खेलते हुआ जैक मिल जाता है लेकिन वो उसे कुछ खास text: The story begins as a supply truck crawls through Ardennes fog. Inside the cab, a first sergeant rides beside his driver, Evans. Evans blames the roads for every slide and skid. Evans corrects him and keeps his hands on the wheel. Their orders are simple, get the resupply to Schönberg. Evans hopes the war might end by Christmas. The sergeant snaps that the Germans just broke the front line. The sergeant tells everyone to freeze. Armored vehicles roll up on the truck. The Germans open fire without a word of warning. He holsters a Luger and walks the bodies. His column is 10 hours late, so he wants the truck stripped. The stolen truck drives away leaving silence. One wounded American still breathes beside the wheel. A colonel asks whether he is speaking to Mrs. Caldwell. He gives his name as John Castle. Her name and address came to him from Galvan Industries. He says he has come about her pension plan. Her lawyer has told her not to talk to anyone from Galvan. Then she reads the patch on his shoulder. He served with the 324th Engineers, 99th Division. That means the Battle of the Bulge. Her own son was there, too, with the T. Castle asks whether that is coffee he can smell. She cannot believe the company gave her whereabouts away. He admits it took persuasion and a little sweet talk. Galvan has spent years refusing to pay what she is owed. She has threatened them for years without the money to sue. She asks whether he is some kind of army lawyer. He says only that Galvan holds her in high regard. He does not need her file to know that. He knows it firsthand, and that is why he is here. He lights a cigarette from old habit. His company is camped in snow at Krinkelt. Castle calls a soldier named Cash over to him. Cash argues that the company still needs him. A colonel arrives at the command tent. Colonel Neill asks for Charlie Company status. Neill spreads a map across the table. One road between Lanzerath and Elsenborn has to be closed. It lies about 5 miles from the camp. Neill wants it blocked that same morning. The counteroffensive is 3 days old and massive. Hitler is running the same plan that worked 4 years earlier. The Germans must be kept away from the fuel depots. Castle studies the road on the map. Then Neill names the unit coming down that road. Nobody in the division has fought anything like them. Given the chance, Neill says, "Take them out." A tattoo, hidden in the armpit, marks them. Castle promises to supervise the road block personally. Castle steps out to gather his men. Castle takes him personally to the field hospital. Battalion will move, so the company must find them by radio. Castle asks how much TNT is left. About 100 lb goes onto the truck. Murphy takes the wheel of the truck. Avanti carries the company radio they call Lassie. Top assigns Miller to the mines while he fuses them. Battalion [clears throat] answers Avanti's radio check loud and clear. Castle picks six trees to start the barrier. Murphy says the fuel pump has flooded again. Castle swears and makes the only choice left. They will walk in and carry what they can. Ramirez runs wire while Murphy unpacks the charges. A single shot cracks across the clearing. "Snipers!" someone shouts, and Murphy is down. It sounds like an MG 34 at 9:00. He picks Ramirez to go with him. Top is left to finish the barrier. The two men break cover and run. They crawl the ditch toward the gun. Castle counts two Germans on the position. He signals Ramirez to move on three. A grenade goes in and the gun stops firing. The blast throws earth over the sandbags. Castle calls the position clear. He sends Ramirez in to check the bodies. One German still breathes among the dead. Ramirez says he will oblige him. Ramirez screams a warning and Castle lunges back. The grenade detonates inside the position. Ramirez is killed where he stands. Shrapnel tears into Castle and knocks him flat. He crawls over and finds nothing to save. More engines are already coming up the road. Castle drags himself back through the position. Top, Miller and Aventi lie dead. The abatis stands and the road is closed. He takes the German sniper's rifle. He works the bolt and sights down it. A German patrol comes up the road. Castle fires and the nearest man drops. Then he goes back to his own dead. He opens their collars and takes the tags. Every tag goes into his hand. He limps back to the broken truck. German voices carry through the trees behind him. He begs the engine to turn over. It coughs once and stalls again. Battalion calls for him and gets no answer. He hauls himself into the cab. The truck moves a little, then dies. Only then does Castle answer the radio. He reports the mission accomplished. Five killed in action and he is the wounded one. The vehicle is hard broken he needs help. He passes his grid position over the net. Battalion says there is too much fire between them. The radio battery is his lifeline from here. So Castle shoulders the radio and starts walking. Snow, fog and empty road lie ahead. A wolf howls somewhere in the trees. Chickens scatter as he reaches a farmyard. A photograph of his wife lies on him. Her face is the last thing before sleep. He forces a barn door and collapses. He cuts his trouser open to reach it. Morning brings a shotgun into the doorway. A farmer stands over him shouting in French. Castle can only tell him he is American. Water is heated and the wound washed out. The farmer takes his weight and helps him. A young woman binds the wound tight. Castle grits his teeth and thanks them. A small child watches from behind the table. A shell lands and the child flinches. He tells her quietly that it is frightening. He packs the radio to move on. A finger comes down and says, "Here." Then vehicles pull up outside the house. He calls battalion again and hears nothing. The child runs to her mother. Now he knows exactly where he is. SS troops break in through the door. Castle drops through a hatch below. An SS officer wants to know where the fuel depot is. She raises her hands and refuses again. The child calls out for her mother. She says no one last time. The officer shoots her where she stands. Gunfire tears through the house above the cellar. Castle grabs the screaming child. Then he comes up shooting. He takes a Luger off a dead German. He kills the men between him and outside. Bullets ricochet off the stones. The only cover is a German tank. He climbs in through the hatch. Then a shell strikes the tank. He sees Rebecca holding their baby son. The memory fades into ringing. He comes round deaf and boxed in. He [clears throat] swears he will not die inside a German machine. The hatch will not move. He asks God for help and shoves again. He thanks whoever was listening. A dog watches from the bank above. Ahead of him stands the ruined farmhouse. He goes back down for the child. She is still alive where he left her. He asks whether she is all right. He tells her the Americans are coming. They will help her when they get here. He puts his own pistol into her hands. He apologizes for not coming out faster. Keep it for protection, he tells her. He leaves her there and walks out. Now only the Luger is left to him. He crosses open country as armor moves. He radios a new position and asks for advice. Battalion tells him the Germans are everywhere. They still cannot reach him. He is told to hold the same vector and keep going. 17 km still lie ahead. He walks into a field of American dead. He lies among the bodies and stops moving. A German patrol walks the line of dead. One stops astride from his face. Castle knifes him without a sound. A vehicle passes, he stays still. He checks his compass and moves north. An abandoned house offers a roof and stove. Footsteps come straight for the kitchen. The two men collide and go down. Castle kills him with his hands. More Germans arrive and settle into the house. He lights a rag and cups the flame. Castle works around the outer wall. One of them shaves at a mirror inside. He throws the fire through the wall. He walks away past what burned. A German tank sits abandoned by a barn. He climbs over it and keeps north. A loose white horse stands in the snow. It lets him pass and grazes on. Then he recognizes a truck in the road. It is the truck from the first morning. Propped against its wheel is a wounded sergeant. He settles on the name Pierce. Castle uses the name Pierce from then on. The truck runs, Pierce says, "but it is stuck." Castle promises to get it unstuck. Pierce asks for water and drinks it slowly. He tells Castle to use the winch. Castle digs the wheels out. He keeps Pierce talking so he will not slip away. Pierce is from Bridgeport and thinks Castle would like it. A shell lands on the truck. The blast throws Castle into the snow. He crawls back and finds Pierce dead. The barrage drives him down again. He drags himself away through mud. A white horse crosses the shellfire. He screams to be taken home. He says his son's name out loud. The word is Hunter. Night falls. Small fires burn in wreckage. A chain rattles somewhere in the dark. A voice calls the dog off. Castle answers with his rank and his unit. The other man calls himself Sergeant Bellingham. Bellingham gets an arm under him and lifts. He offers to carry the radio for him. He sees the shrapnel and says it looks bad. He claims he cannot remember what happened. He helps Castle sit down under the wreck. Castle explains he must reach the 99th Division command. He is carrying a package for the commander. Bellingham supplies the name, General Lawer. He says he only has contact with battalion. "A priority frequency," he says, "is above his pay grade. He is currying reports on the Third Army instead." Bellingham warns him that he is bleeding out. Bellingham notices the Luger and calls it a fine trophy. He has been hunting one since he arrived. He asks to take a look at the radio himself. The company radio operator named it Lassie. Lassie is receiving again. Castle wants to focus on getting out alive. He has sealed position maps and nothing else. He calls on the net and no one answers. The Germans, Bellingham says, love to fight at night. They cannot wait to die for the fatherland. Castle says it is because they have little to live for. Bellingham argues the Germans were given an economy. He mentions the Olympics they were given, too. Every country, he says, has its undesirables. He calls Hitler a monster in the same breath. Underestimating them, he says, is the real danger. Then battalion calls Derek 06 over the working radio. Castle guesses they are south of Hittenburg. Castle gives them Bellingham's name and errand. He asks them for the sergeant's onward position. Bellingham says he is from Milwaukee. He is not a baseball man at all. Football is his game and one fixture is a holiday. He calls it the Naval Army game. He drove tanks in Africa before someone reported him. Now, he says, he blows up bridges instead. A letter ended his own romance two weeks into basic. He asks Castle the same question back. Castle shows a photograph instead. There is one child, a son called Hunter. Bellingham says he will be seeing the boy soon. Castle says that is the plan. His wife already lost her brother at Midway. So, getting back matters more than anything. The night quietens and Castle thinks. He asks who Bellingham takes in the Naval Army game. Bellingham simply asks what he means. Battalion tells them to write a code group down. Castle copies them and asks for the men to hurry. Battalion wishes Captain Castle Godspeed and signs off. Castle holds the paper out to him. He says it is the position of headquarters. Bellingham stares at the letters. Bellingham falls back on his pay grade again. It is an SOI encoding, Castle says. Signal operating instructions, which any courier would know. But you would not know that, he says. Castle raises the Luger and holds it. Bellingham asks him to put the weapon down. Castle tells him to shut up. Nobody taught him how to light a Lucky properly. Americans burn the brand off, so the glow leaves no trace. Castle warns him to think of it next time. "Not a sympathizer," Castle answers, "a Nazi." Bellingham swears again that he is American. "Then show me," Castle tells him. He checks the Luger and finds two rounds left. Shots chip the stone above him. The dog whimpers somewhere out in the dark. Castle waits for the muzzle flash. He fires once from behind the rock. Bellingham groans and stops shooting. The radio calls him one more time. A Christmas song drifts across the same frequency. Headlights come up the road. He wakes in a moving vehicle asking where the radio is. The radio is right there beside him. A general comes to his bedside and tells him to relax. He introduces himself as General Lauer. Lauer says Castle has really been through it. The Abatis stopped the column in its tracks. It bought the division precious hours. Castle says he barely remembers the last position. The Germans shelled it to open a path to Elsenborn. Lauer tells him he is being put in for the Silver Star. Castle asks what happened to the man beside him. "He was SS posing as an American," Lauer says. "He is dead, and Castle killed him." The SS were hunting the general's own location. Castle was right to shoot the man. Lauer asks how he knew. "He said some wrong things," Castle answers. "And he never burned the brand off his cigarettes." Lauer calls that sin number one. "Three cheers," he says, "for poor German training." Castle says every one of his men dead. Lauer answers that he already knows and is sorry. Keeping his men safe was his job and he failed. Lauer tells him that is not the job at all. Soldiers die in war, he says. The job is to keep everyone's mothers alive. The job is to keep all our children alive. Castle types with the dog tags in hand. The first letter goes to Murphy's mother. He turns the tags over as he writes. Outside, trucks load for the next move. Cash finds him sitting in the cold. Cash says he did not fare as well as the captain. He has heard the men died well. Cash tells him at least he came through it. Cash is going to a hospital in Paris and then home. Cash asks whether the captain finally gets home, too. They talk about more snow coming. It will not make the fight any easier. Both sides, Cash says, and gets up to go. He hands something back and Castle tells him to keep it. Finally, the story returns to the living room. Mrs. Caldwell repeats the phrase "Naval Army game." "Very unlucky," he answers. "But lucky enough to make it through. But without that radio, there was nothing. Unit 5204, line four, station seven, batch 52, issued in November 1943. The check is for $9,000. She has been trying to settle for years. Nothing ever came of it." He claims he simply told them to do the right thing. She calls that a load of horse shit. So, he admits the rest of it. He buys every radio the army orders nationwide. He told Galvin he could find another supplier. "80 years from now," he says, "the battle will be known." He wonders whether anyone will understand it. She takes down her own son's photograph. Castle walks out into a snowy street. At home, he tells his son they will play tomorrow. He asks the boy who loves him. Hunter answers, "Dad." Castle sends him off to bed one last time. He turns off the light and stands there.

Years later, Gabbie and Travis, a mother and son duo from New York, settle down into the mysterious Gracey Manor with the intention of setting it up as a B&B, not knowing what strange spectres dwell within. Ben is visited by the priest and exorcist Father Kent, who requests Ben to photograph the ghosts of Gracey Manor. Despite his initial doubts, Ben soon finds himself being pursued by the ghost of a Mariner that forces him to return to the mansion. Ben discovers that Gabbie, Travis, and Kent have all experienced hauntings that sent them back to the mansion. So he and Kent decide to call on Harriet, who is known to have genuine supernatural abilities, then take blueprints of the mansion from Prof. Bruce Davis, who specializes in haunted house history. In the end, they uncover a secret séance room. Harriet manages to make contact with the spirit of Gracey, who writes a message telling them to speak with Madame Leota, the renowned medium. But before they can carry on, a mysterious being drives Harriet from the house. Bruce soon arrives, and he too becomes the target of an eerie haunting. The gang remains at the mansion while searching for Leota's spirit. Ben ventures into the attic, where he encounters a spectral bride, and discovers a locked trunk. After further inspection, they uncover a crystal ball containing Leota. Leota shares that William Gracey acquired the large house and asked her to contact the soul of his deceased wife, Eleanor, each night for an entire year. As a result, hundreds of ghosts were unleashed into the mansion. Unfortunately, a malevolent presence convinced Gracey to take his own life, leaving Leota forever entrapped in her crystal ball. Harriet attempts to astral project in order to gain more knowledge, but instead sends Ben out of his body. During his out-of-body experience, Ben comes across Gracey and the malevolent Hatbox Ghost. The following morning, Bruce accompanies Ben to a sketch artist to have the image of the Hatbox Ghost put down on paper. Alistair Crump was a wealthy heir who had experienced abuse from his father after his mother passed away, resulting in him being thrown out of the house. As an adult, he took his revenge on his old social peers for ostracizing him by murdering them. His own servants eventually beheaded him in a revolt. Ben, Kent, and Travis manage to escape Crump Mansion as the ghost of Crump locks it down. They later find Crump Manor has become a historical site. The Mariner, who followed them, informs them that Crump will only escape if someone volunteers to take their own life and become the mansion's one-thousandth spirit. Travis uncovers Crump's hat, a necessary item to denounce Crump back to the underworld. Upon arriving at the Gracey residence, Ben and Kent manage to free Gabbie, Harriet, and Bruce, but before they can use the hat, Crump incinerates it. In the meantime, Gabbie reveals to Ben that Travis' father has passed away. Crump intends to manipulate Travis' sorrow to persuade him to become his last ghost. Ben encounters Travis and succeeds in convincing him to release his father as they and Gabbie challenge Crump in the cemetery. Kent manages to persuade the ghosts to abandon Crump and team up with them, and Bruce hands over a bit of the hat to Harriet who casts Leota's spell to send Crump away. Crump attempts to convince Ben to give up his life willingly in order to reunite with Alyssa, but Ben reveals that he has already accepted her loss. He then delivers a swift kick to Crump's face, sending him back to the underworld. Afterwards, several of the ghosts decide to remain at the mansion, now in peaceful unison with Gabbie and Travis. Ben returns to his teaching job and on his way out of his apartment, he pets the cat that has been lounging around his door, discovering its special name is 'Tater Tot' - a tribute to his wife's passion for the snack. On Halloween, the gang get together a the manor to celebrate with the friendly spirits. Harriet feels sure about her psychic gifts once more, Kent takes charge as Pastor, Travis is selected for the student council, and Bruce keeps the friendships he made.

text: You ever try reading Nabokov's Lolita… not in New York, not in London, not even in a quiet café in some bohemian suburb… but in Tehran, under a regime that thinks books are more dangerous than bombs? Now, imagine doing that not alone, but with seven other women—all of you dodging the eyes of a moral police force that believes a bare strand of hair can cause social collapse. That’s not just reading. That’s revolution with a hardback. This story begins in the aftermath of the Iranian Revolution—when the Shah was overthrown and the Islamic Republic settled in like a strict uncle who moved into the house and started rewriting the rules. Azar Nafisi, our narrator, is an academic, a teacher of English literature, and, above all, a lover of books. But in revolutionary Iran, loving books—especially Western ones—is a rebellious act. The government doesn’t take kindly to people enjoying Nabokov, Austen, Fitzgerald, or Henry James. No, they want books that chant the party line, or better yet—no books at all. That way, there’s nothing to contradict the slogans on the street. So what does Nafisi do? She gathers seven of her most committed female students and starts a secret book club. No banners. No hashtags. Just books, tea, and defiance. They meet every Thursday morning in Azar's home. It’s a quiet rebellion. Each woman removes her veil as she steps in. Outside, they are invisible, shapeless figures wrapped in black. Inside, they are themselves again—lively, opinionated, curious. Each page they turn is a step away from the world outside and into something freer. And what do they read first? Lolita. Yes, that Lolita. The one where a middle-aged man manipulates and abuses a young girl. Not exactly bedtime reading, especially not in Tehran. But Azar isn’t reading it for shock value. She’s reading it because she sees something bigger in it. In Lolita, the central character—Dolores Haze—has no voice. Everything is filtered through the man who controls her. In a way, Dolores becomes a symbol for the people of Iran—trapped, spoken for, reshaped by those in power. Just like how Humbert Humbert rewrote Lolita’s story to suit his narrative, the Iranian regime was rewriting people's lives, desires, and identities. One of the most enlightening moments was when Nafisi explored a single word: poshlust—a term from Nabokov referring to empty, fake beauty or false ideals. It resonated with them so deeply because their entire society felt poshlust—full of empty righteousness and moral facades. But Lolita is just the beginning. Over the course of the story, Azar and her students read works by Jane Austen, Henry James, F. Scott Fitzgerald, and more. Each book serves as a mirror to their lives. The Great Gatsby leads to a discussion on dreams and the illusion of freedom. Daisy Miller helps them explore gender and morality. Jane Austen gets more applause than any mullah ever will in that living room. These women don’t just read books—they inhabit them. They use fiction to understand their reality, to reflect on their identities, to question the regime and even themselves. They discuss romance, power, betrayal, and choice. And with every conversation, they chip away at the walls built around them. But outside that small bubble of tea and literature, the country is changing—and not for the better. After the revolution, civil liberties don’t just shrink—they get guillotined. Women are forced to wear the veil. Universities are purged of professors who don’t toe the line. Literature is censored. Dissidents vanish. Friends and family leave. The Iran Azar knew becomes unrecognizable. But she doesn’t leave immediately. For years, she tries to work within the system. She teaches literature in classrooms filled with suspicion. She faces down authorities who want her to teach ideology instead of ideas. She watches students disappear or grow silent. And slowly, painfully, she realizes that she can no longer function in this suffocating atmosphere. Eventually, in 1997, Azar Nafisi makes the decision to leave Iran. But before that, before the departure, before the heartbreak, she captures these years—these moments of stolen freedom—in the form of this memoir. The book is Reading Lolita in Tehran: A Memoir in Books by Azar Nafisi. Published in 2003, this book is not just a memoir. It’s a love letter to literature. It's a protest song in the key of Austen. And it’s a subtle, intellectual rebellion wrapped in a velvet cover. Reading this book felt like sitting in Azar Nafisi’s living room. You’re there with her and the students—laughing, debating, trying to understand why The Great Gatsby hits harder when you know freedom isn’t promised. What struck me most was the parallel storytelling—how Nafisi uses other books to explain her own life. It's brilliant. One word—like Nabokov’s “poshlust”—can reverberate across cultures, continents, and decades. This isn’t just a memoir about Iran. It’s a memoir about books. About how they outlive dictators and survive censorship. About how reading is, in many ways, an act of resistance. But the book isn’t perfect. And it’s important to say that. The structure can be disorienting. Nafisi jumps back and forth in time with such abandon, you’d think she was trying to shake you off. Chronology is more a suggestion than a rule. Events blur together. Characters fade in and out like background noise. You get the sense that the story is being told to herself more than to us. And in a way, that’s what memoirs are. Also, like most dissident memoirs, America is the quiet hero in the background. It’s the symbol of freedom, progress, rationality. Meanwhile, China and Russia appear only to remind us what not to become. Even the Gulf War gets barely a mention—as if the global context didn’t matter. But Nafisi isn’t writing history. She’s writing memory. And memories are deeply subjective. Another point worth noting: Nafisi briefly mentions that under the Shah—the secular regime—religious people were also oppressed. Veils were banned. Women who insisted on wearing them were jailed. It’s a powerful irony: both extremes—the theocratic and the secular—took away choice. One forced the veil on. The other forced it off. Somewhere in between is the space where people just want to choose for themselves. This idea of choice—the right to live your life, dress how you want, read what you want—is the soul of this book. It’s not really about Lolita, or Gatsby, or Daisy Miller. It’s about agency. About finding freedom in small places—in pages, in conversations, in quiet Thursday mornings. Azar Nafisi paints a tragic portrait of a country that lost itself. A revolution that spiraled out of control. She shows how intellectuals fled, how even faithful Muslims lost the meaning of hijab when it became law instead of love. She shows how once a revolution becomes a tool for power, it eats its own children. But she also shows how, even in the darkest times, people resist. With literature. Here are a few themes that stood out: The Power of Literature – Books don’t just entertain. They help us make sense of our reality. In a society that punishes independent thought, reading becomes a form of protest. Freedom vs. Control – From forced veils to banned books, both the secular and religious governments tried to control how people lived. Nafisi’s memoir shows how such control robs individuals of their humanity. Gender and Oppression – The memoir focuses on women, but not just as victims. Nafisi and her students are thinkers, critics, dreamers. Their discussions show the strength of women in the face of institutional erasure. Revolutions and Disillusionment – Every revolution starts with hope. But when different interest groups hijack that hope, it leads to chaos. Nafisi’s Iran is a cautionary tale about revolutions without brakes. Azar Nafisi was born in Iran in 1955. She earned her doctorate in English and American literature at the University of Oklahoma and returned to Iran, where she taught at several universities. After the revolution, her refusal to conform to the ideological pressures of the Islamic Republic eventually forced her to resign. She left Iran in 1997 and now lives in the United States, where she continues to write and speak about the importance of literature, freedom, and education—especially for women. Her other books include Things I’ve Been Silent About and The Republic of Imagination—both of which expand on the themes of literature and personal freedom. Reading Lolita in Tehran isn’t an easy book. But it’s an important one. It asks uncomfortable questions and offers no neat answers. It’s fragmented, like memory. Biased, like memoir. But moving, intelligent, and quietly powerful. If you're a fan of memoirs, especially those that blend politics, culture, and literature—this one's for you. But if you’re new to memoirs, maybe start somewhere else. Come back to this one when you’re ready to read between the lines. And when you do—bring tea. And maybe a copy of The Great Gatsby. You can use it to grab yourself a copy and keep the adventure going. And if you're in the mood for more great reads, don't go just yet. text: Many people are probably going to say that Challengers is one of the best films of the year. I am not one of those people. As someone who's a fan of Luca Guadagnino and Zendaya, I walked in this film and thought it was going to be amazing. Trailers made it seem really fun and enjoyable, and the end result is just not that. The centralized love triangle on display never feels fleshed out. The characters feel sterile and there's no chemistry between them. Zendaya is half-decent as the lead, but the other two characters really struggle to keep up with their momentum. The use of flashbacks is also really distracting here and convoluted. Nothing feels particularly full of substance here, and it's a very confusing amalgamation of ideas, really struggling to get airtime all at once. Ending is easily the best part of this, by far. And the script and direction are fantastic along with the cinematography, but at the end of the day, it's a pretty pretentious and tedious film that thinks it's way smarter and saying more than it actually is. That's why I'm giving Challengers a 65 out of 100. Challengers releases in theaters everywhere this Friday, April 26th.

text: In an alternate reality version of New York City, an unusual law bans premarital sex throughout the year, except for a single night when all restrictions are lifted. That one evening erupts into a city-wide spectacle of parties, impulsive flings, and relentless social pressure, transforming what should be a celebration into the least romantic night imaginable for anyone searching for genuine love. While most singles embrace the chaos as an opportunity for meaningless hookups, Owen and Ally are different. Both long for a real emotional connection in a world obsessed with instant gratifi cation. Owen enters the night heartbroken after planning to propose to his long-time girlfriend, only to be abandoned when she chooses a spontaneous encounter with someone else. Across the city, Ally, an optimistic singer who still believes in true love, suffers a similar disappointment when her best friend leaves her behind to chase a stranger. Lost in their own heartbreak, the two unexpectedly collide, sharing an undeniable spark during a brief chance meeting. But before either can act on it, a whirlwind of hilarious misunderstandings, unexpected detours, bizarre side adventures, and missed opportunities continually pushes them in opposite directions. As the city descends further into its outrageous annual celebration, filled with extravagant parties, dating apps, eccentric personalities, and the absurdities of modern romance, the pair repeatedly come close to finding one another, only to be separated again. By the time dawn arrives, they realize that the authentic connection they had been searching for all night may have been standing right in front of them from the very beginning. When fate finally brings them together again, they choose not to rush into a relationship. Instead, they decide to spend time building a genuine friendship and truly getting to know each other. One year later, when the city's infamous night returns, they reunite, not as lonely strangers swept up in the frenzy, but as two people who have patiently nurtured something real and are finally ready for the opportunity they chose to wait for.
