text: Kenna, in a cab, is heading somewhere. She stops in the middle of the road and heads to a memorial sign for someone named Scotty. She breaks it out and takes it, telling Scotty she is out for good behavior. She is stealing this because he hated memorials and now she does so, too. She reaches an apartment called Paradise. She pays for the first month's rent and the manager says she also has to take a kitten. She helplessly takes it and heads to her room. She says she will have to take a job for she is here to see someone. Meanwhile, a guy named Ledger is playing with a little girl named Diem. Her grandmother, Grace, soon calls her up. She takes Diem and Ledger drives off. He sees someone has stolen Scotty's memorial. He heads to the bar he manages and meets with his employees, Roman and Mary. He tells Roman that someone stole Scotty's memorial. He wonders who would do such a thing. Kenna is on a job hunt. She is going from one store to another to find work, but none of them are hiring. She goes to a diner where she is finally needed. She is given an application. She stops at the question if she has ever been convicted of a crime. She ticks yes and the woman says they can't hire someone with a record. She suggests the supermarket Dollar Den where they're always looking. She heads to the Dollar Den and remembers Scotty, where she first met him. She was a cashier. He approached him to ask her out. She says they have a policy that employees can't date customers. He takes his products away and returns them saying he will never buy from here again. He approaches with his proposal again and she criticizes the color of his truck. He says it's his best friends and she eventually agrees to go out. She doesn't enter the Dollar Den and heads to a bar. It's Scotty's place. She only asks for coffee. He says it's a bar but agrees to make one for her anyway. She brings out some notebooks and gets busy with them. He brings her the coffee. He asks for a review. She takes a sip and gives it three stars, smiling and telling about the mistakes. He asks her about the notebooks. She instantly takes them back into the bag and asks if they are hiring, but they are not. Ledger attends to some other customers and she leaves. He sees she has left a couple of notebooks on the stool. On her way back, she remembers them and returns to the bar. He says it's in the back, gives them to her, promising he hasn't read it. He walks her back and before she leaves, he asks for her number. She says she doesn't have a phone. Someone calls Ledger from the other room. Hearing his name, her smile vanishes and she leaves the spot immediately. She heads to her room and writes in her journal addressing Scotty. She met his friend today. He didn't recognize her because they had never met and she would keep her distance. She remembers the time of his birthday. She wanted to go out and have fun even though his mom didn't want them, but they headed out anyway and the police arrived at night saying they had an accident and he did not make it. Kenna was held accountable. She pleaded guilty to vehicular manslaughter and was sentenced to 7 years. The next morning, Ledger is to pick up Diem for ball game. Diem asks Ledger about her mother. She says Grace told her that her mother can't meet her until she gets a bigger car. Outside, he tells Grace that she will keep asking about her mom until she knows. Kenna heads to a supermarket, but this time as well she is denied for her record. She heads to the washroom frustrated. A worker named Amy is also inside crying because she smashed someone's car but doesn't have insurance. She asks what her trauma is and Kenna replies that she can't get a job because she just got out of prison. Amy says she wins. She then tells her that she can manage to get her a shift as a bagger by talking to manager. Soon, a girl named Diana walks in. She recognizes Kenna because they live in the same apartment. Later, Kenna heads to Grace's place. Ledger is inside when he notices her coming out of the car. He heads out asking how she knows he lives here. She says she is not here for him and just then he realizes who she is. He instantly pulls her away from the house and takes her into his home. He reminds her she has no right to her daughter anymore. He gets out to prepare the car to take her away. She takes the chance to run out, but he chases her and stops her. Grace comes out, but he stops her and takes her back to her apartment. She curses him and walks off. She heads into the room and dreams of the time of giving birth in prison and her daughter being taken away from her. She wakes up as Diana heads into her room. She asks why she doesn't have any furniture. Kenna says she just moved in. Diana opens the fridge and asks if she can take the cheese. She says yes and requests that she leave. Diana gets to pet the cat and asks why she is poor. Kenna says she just got out of prison and Diana responds that her father is also in prison. She then asks why she is so sad and Kenna tells her about her daughter. Diana says she has some sparkles and would like to light them with her. Kenna remembers a time in prison. A woman helps her with her breast milk and tells her that she is never going to recover from her child being taken away from her. So, she has to make a decision right here whether she wants to die in her sadness or live in it. She says she will live in it. Ledger heads to the couple and they are frustrated that she is out already. Patrick says he will call the lawyer. Back at work, Ledger tells Roman that Kenna is back. He only saw her mugshot once, but she looked different. Roman says she is not exactly a stone-cold murderer, but he reminds him that she left him to die. Roman says he has been through terrible things and he wouldn't judge her without knowing her well and neither should he. Kenna is enjoying the sparkles with Diana. Ledger pulls up there. She angrily heads to his car, gets in and asks what he is doing here. He says he wanted to see if she was okay. She says he is worried that she will end her life and he will feel guilty for the rest of his life. Diana comes in asking who he is. She says he is the one who is not letting her see her daughter. She calls him a jerk and they leave. The next morning, the couple continues to worry thinking that she might snatch Diem away. Ledger says she probably won't do such a thing, which offends them saying he doesn't know what she is capable of. He says maybe they can try meeting her up to see what she has to say, but Patrick denies it saying it has already been very hard. Diem calls up Grace and Patrick gets busy fixing Scotty's playhouse. Ledger says this is where Scotty had his first kiss. He then remembers a time being with him high, chatting and chilling. Kenna is working at the market when Ledger heads there to shop. When she is about to bill, he heads to her counter. Amy asks her to assist him and she takes the things to his truck. She asks him if her daughter looks like her. He says yes and she asks who she is like. He doesn't answer that. Diana comes and calls him a jerk again and she can't help but laugh. Later, on her way back, it begins to rain and she heads to Ledger's bar. He offers a ride home, but she says she will wait out. She says the music is miserable and no wonder no one comes here. She also says all music is miserable. Ledger drops Kenna off. He asks her if she went to the bar to lead her way to Diem. However, she says she did not know him. She recognized her name and left right then. At his work, Ledger chats with Diem on the phone. She says they are going grocery shopping, but before he can ask the shop name, she hangs up. He instantly goes out and calls Grace but can't connect. Ledger drives fast and reaches there in time. He rushes to her to stop. Kenna sees it from inside and runs after them, but they have already left. She is furious at Ledger. Amy comes out asking if everything is okay. She says she can take the day off. Kenna thanks her and heads out. Ledger follows her by car asking her to get in. She doesn't listen and sits by a field. He joins her. She says other moms in prison told her that she would have two days with her child before they would be taken away. However, her daughter was 6 weeks early. Her lungs were not fully developed yet and she had to be taken to the hospital immediately. Kenna had to endure those 2 days alone. She thought Grace and Patrick would let her be a part of her life, but she was stupid to believe that. Ledger shows her a video of her daughter. She watches it in awe and smiles seeing how happy she seems with Ledger. Later, in the evening, they had some food. Kenna asks him if he hates her. He responds the first day he met her at the bar, he found her intriguing, but when he got to know who she was, she thought she was the worst person in the world. However, only later he felt like she was the saddest girl in the world. Back in the car, Ledger tells her that after her sentencing, everyone said that she looked so unremorseful. She says she was broken losing the only thing she had. Ledger drops her off. Kenna says she is trying her best to stand on her feet so Patrick and Grace see she is fit to meet her daughter. He asks her what if the day never comes. She says she will at least live in hope of it, although she can barely pay her rent now. He says she can come work for him. They need help on the back and she can work 2 days a week. She happily agrees. The next morning, Kenna, a little happier, gets out to work. Grace is there keeping an eye on her. She heads to the bar and Roman explains her work. She is given the work to tidy up Ledger's office. Mary comes to see her and sits to chat. She asks Mary about Leah, a name she sees on some files. Mary says she was Ledger's ex-fiancée. They broke up a year ago, especially because of his niece, to whom he is devoted for some reason. He struggled to leave the town. Later, Ledger returns to see that Kenna has done good work cleaning up the whole back room. He thanks her and asks if she needs a ride home. The others tease her about how her job comes with perks. On their way, Kenna asks if her daughter asks about her. He says that she is told that she can't meet her until she has a bigger car. She asks more about her and this time he says a bit about her personality. She tells him sorry about Leah. He assumes Mary revealed that, but she responds that he heard of her from from He then says she knows a lot about him and he needs to know more of her as well. He asks what she writes in her notebooks. She says she writes letters to Scotty. He asks if she wrote about the night and she did. He turns on the music but she tells him to stop since all music is miserable. Returning to her place, Diana introduces her mother to Kenna who invites her to the Mother's Day party. She further requests her bringing in some chairs for they are always short of them. She asks for some seats for Roman the next day at work and he shows her. When Ledger is taking her back and seeing her using her phone, he asks for her number again. She denies and he says that as her boss, he needs to contact his employees. She gives it to him and he sends her a playlist of happy songs saying not all songs are miserable. He helps her move the chairs into her room. He sees she sleeps on the couch and he brings in his camping gear. While he places it on the floor, he sees the stolen cross. He gets angry seeing it but she says Scotty hated memorials and she did him a favor. She says he doesn't have to trust her and tells him he can go now. Ledger doesn't let her open the door and eventually they begin to kiss. However, she stops him saying it will only make things worse. Ledger agrees and leaves. The next morning at work, someone approaches Kenna, gives her a file and says she has been served. Ledger is hanging around the park with DM and Grace when he receives a text from Kenna saying she has just received a restraining order. He picks her up on the way and she is frustrated that if she is seen near DM, she will be arrested. They decide to get some food. There he talks about the house he has been building for four years. He asks if she would like to go see it and she decides to do so. They drive to the place and she is impressed seeing the spot. She asks when he plans to move in but he can't answer that. She understands it's because of his breakup with Leah. She tells him he can rent it because she prefers seeing him closer to DM. It comforts her. He says he wants to do right by her since she doesn't have a dad. She understands but also says he can't live Scotty's life for him by neglecting his own. Back at work, while working on the back, Ledger sees Patrick and Grace walking in. They say they needed a night out. Kenna sees them. Patrick says DM left her backpack in his truck and goes to take it. Ledger follows him saying he can do it himself but he goes on anyway in the rain and takes it. Luckily, Kenna has already left. Back at the apartment, there's a knock on her door. It's Ledger come to say thanks. She says he could just say it in text. He smiles. She asks why he is here and then he kisses her and they eventually make love. In the morning, he sees her writing her journal. He requests that she read it. She writes to Scotty that she just had sex with his best friend. He might not have wanted to hear it but wherever he is, she knows he would like her to be happy. Ledger goes to see Grace and gives her flowers wishing her a happy Mother's Day. DM asks what Mother's Day is and upon knowing, she says she would want to give her mother flowers too. He assures her that her mother will get flowers. Kenna is at the celebration when Ledger comes in with a bouquet. They travel to his place. As they lie together, he asks her to tell him what happened on the night of the accident. She decides to read it to him from her journal. They were by a lake and took drugs. They went to swim, made love and spent the time till evening. On their way back, while she was driving and they were singing, she lost control and the car flipped over eventually falling upside down. She was conscious but Scotty was not. She managed to get out of the car and tried to wake him up. She did not feel any pulse from him. She screamed in agony and went to the road for help. No car stopped for her. She was eventually found by the police and taken in for questioning. They asked if she knew he was still alive when she fled the scene. She burst in anger and was arrested. She didn't know his hand was crushed and thus lost the pulse. However, if she knew she was pregnant, she would have never pled guilty. She thought she had nothing to live for anymore. He tells her sorry for losing him and Kenna says nobody ever said that to her. Just then, Patrick walks in to check on him for Grace did not hear from him. He is stunned to see her and leaves the place immediately. Ledger follows him and reaches his place. He tries to explain that they have had the wrong idea of her all along. He asks if he is sleeping with her. Ledger continues trying to explain but he punches him and heads into the house asking him to leave them alone. Later, when Kenna is at her house, Ledger goes to see her. She sees his wound and gets worried that they won't let him see DM anymore. He is not sure about it. Kenna decides to leave immediately. She doesn't want to change things for DM. It's better if things return to how they were. He hugs her requesting her to not go. She doesn't listen and tells him to apologize to them and return to DM's life. He holds her and says he will make sure her daughter knows how amazing a person she is. Then he decides to leave. While on his way, he steals her journal and gets out. He heads straight to Patrick's place. Grace can see him from the window. She opens the door and tells him to leave. He says it won't take long adding that he gave his last five years to the little girl and they owe it to him. He gives them the journal asking them to read the letter he bookmarked leaving the rest for privacy. He wants them to read the letter for the sake of Scotty because he loved her. He then leaves. At night, when Patrick is asleep, Grace is awake with the notebook beside her. The next morning, Kenna is packing up deciding if she should take the kitten with her when knocks are heard on the door. She is shocked to find Grace there with her notebook. She lets her in and Grace gives her the notebook. She stumbles and speaks that above all, she believes Scotty would have loved for his daughter to meet her mother. She can't promise anything further and leaves. Eventually one morning, she heads to the house. Ledger is there. She is invited for lunch. They head in together and she sees her daughter playing in the yard. They head to her. DM shows Kenna her pet turtle. Ledger leaves and she heads into her playhouse as Grace watches it from a window. Kenna tells her that she used to know her dad. She was his girlfriend. DM asks her why she is so sad. Kenna says it's because she is so happy to see her. DM wonders why and then Kenna reveals to her that she is her mom. DM is curious and wonders if she got a bigger car now. Kenna says she is still working on it. She then engages in play with her. Kenna comes back in and seeing Grace in the kitchen, she asks if she can help her with anything. Grace eventually begins to sob as Kenna approaches her and hugs her. At the lunch table, DM moves to Kenna's lap from Ledger's as the grandparents watch it in peace. Outside, Patrick goes to Ledger and says he has known him since his childhood and never once has he given him a reason to doubt him. So if he tells him that Kenna is worthy of DM, he trusts him. Later, Ledger drives Kenna and DM to the place of Scotty's memorial. Together, they put it back in and eventually embark on their way back. text: What's happenin mah well read ballas? This week we gettin red tape up in that ASS with The Trial by Franz Kafka. Banker-man Joseph K. just turned 30 and now he chillin at the crib waitin' fo some grub. S'all good til- KNOCK KNOCK. "Man dat BETTER be my foo-." "Huh? Who this suit rollin up on my spot?" Da top dawg inspector start runnin his mouth bout how K is in some deep shit, but he STILL don't say why! Da hell? K walks for now, but this mess sho' as hell ain't over. Not even close. Later, word come from the law dat K gotta bust ass to court without tellin him what time, or the room number where all this goin down'. Later, K-baby on the grind when he hear somethin funky- "Aw hell no.. people best not be gettin freaky in MY bank- Uhhh..what da hell is goin on?". Apparently the suits who arrested K gettin whooped on cuz K ratted on them in court fo' tryna' boost his swag. K feel mad guilty, and wanna put a stop to this mess, but da whippin man aint backin' down fo' nothing. Brutha gotta do what he gotta do. Then K's uncle drop in and be all like "You takin this case seriously boy? Yo ass is on the LINE!" So K's uncle introduces him to a lawyer named Huld and his BANGIN' nurse Leni. Mmm-mmm-MMM YEAH! But Huld is completely f*ckin useless. Brutha ain't got a clue why K got the law up his ass and there ain't nuthin he can do. And if dat aint cray 'nuff, the Chief Clerk of da court was just chillin in the shadows this whole damn time just diddlin himself o' somethin. As time go by, K keep hittin up his lawyer, but this shyster never do jack sh*t! Now K buggin so hard bout da case that a customer roll up at work and be like: "Psst bruh. You should talk to my homey Titorelli. He work up at the court so he know what's what." So K hit up Titorelli, who all like "Real talk. You're basically fucked. They ain't never gonna call you innocent so you might as well just bend over." Now K thinkin' he gotta shake his punk-ass lawyer. So he swang over to the office where this raggedy dude named Block be chillin. Apparently, Block was ballin' as a businessman back in the day, but since the law came down on his ass like they doin to K, he spent all his cheddar on legal defense and now he all cashed out on the struggle. When K try to break it off with Huld, da lawyer like "Not so fast, bruh. You walk away, and you ain't gonna be nuthin but a dog like Block." Then the bank tell K he gotta show one of their big dawg clients round town. Dude say he wanna peep game at the cathedral, but when he a no show, K just check spot himself. Befo' he but to leave, da priest holler and tell him he work for da court too. He try to explain K's bunk-ass sitiation with a fable, but it don't mean a damn thing to K. A year go by since all this craziness first went down. On da night before K's 31st birthday, two suits arrive at his crib. This time, though, K ain't trippin bout it. Matta' fact, K take the lead and they head to a quarry where K put his head a boulder. Then one of the suits shank him right in the heart and TWIST. K's last words befo' he take that long dirt nap: "Like a dog!" Man this trap Joey-K livin' in sho one crooked-ass place. Brutha ain't got no rights, no voice, and no options- da law got his nuts in a vice and there ain't nuthin he can do bout it. But da scurriest thang Kafka preachin is dat it don't take a hardass thug puttin a glock to yo dome in order to take away yo dignity n' freedom. Naw blood, up in this hood homies are broken down by a slow, orderly system dat's designed to keep people in check even though it frontin' like it all righteous. Like check this- Even though K never do any time behind bars, it ain't cuz things all good. Truth is, they don't need to throw K in the slammer since erry-day in this society is like livin' in the pen anyway - "You have misunderstood me. You are under arrest, certainly, but that not need hinder you from going about your business. Nor will you be prevented from leading your ordinary life." Yuh, the man all the way up K's ass for this whole damn book. But just cuz they the law sho as hell don't mean they preachin justice. Matta fact, the "law" could be da most un-just thang you eva' seen- but when you got people follow it blindly, and enforce it just cuz "it's their job"- da fact dat it ain't just don't even matta'. Da law s'posed to protect yo' rights. But up in here, it's nuthin' mo' than a weapon to keep you scurred and in yo place. "Our officials... never go hunting for crime in the populace, but, as the Law decrees, are drawn toward the guilty and must then send out us warders. That is the Law. How could there be a mistake in that?" It's like K-money livin' a totalitarian nightmare. Matta' fact, Kafka style-game makin this whole novel feel like a tripped out dream. Fo example, when K up in court, he try chunk deuce outta there, but the magistrate just pop up in front of the door like he teleporting or something. Da hell? Or when he meeting with his lawyer, da Chief Clerk just appear in da corner of da room like he been creepin in da shadows this whole time. What the hell is he doin over there? Thang is tho, a few years after Kafka was runnin the lit game, this shit wasn't a dream no mo'. It ended up coming true. This whole society sound like some kinda totalitarian prophecy- all da fear and isolation deez whack-ass places used were hella-similar to Joseph K's society- straight down to the threadz the po-lice wore. And da most fucked up thing bout it ain't da way they can break yo bones, but da way they can break you spirit. And that's exactly the point. Evil ain't gotta be some moustache twirling playa doin gangsta shit. Sometimes da gnarliest evil is a boring-ass bureaucracy that wears yo ass down day by day with bullshit rights and corrupt systems dat make yo life such a living hell dat you don't even know what you fightin fo' no mo. A society like dat can dehumanize you so much dat you just wanna be takin out back and put down. BAM- like a dog. Yo thanks for kickin it with yo boy. Catch y'all next time. Peace!

text: In the heart of a highly secret intelligence network, a new operation is being prepared. This is not an ordinary mission. It is built to stop global threats before they even begin. Everything is planned in silence with no public record, no backup, and no room for failure. Jason Statham's character is brought in as the key asset for this mission. He is known as someone who gets the job done, no matter how dangerous it is. At first, everything looks under control. The team is skilled, the technology is advanced, and the target is clear. The mission is to stop a powerful hidden force that has been moving in the shadows, controlling events across different countries. But what no one knows is that the danger is not just outside. It is already inside the system. As the operation begins, small signs of trouble start to appear. Data goes missing. Orders are changed at the last second. Communication lines are blocked without reason. It looks like simple technical issues, but slowly it becomes clear that someone within the team is controlling the flow of information. Trust begins to break down even before the real action starts. Jason Statham's character starts to notice that something feels wrong. He has been in many missions before, but this time the pattern is different. The enemy is not reacting like a normal target. It feels like they already know every move before it happens. That creates tension inside the team. Some members believe it is just bad luck, while others begin to suspect a deeper betrayal. As the mission moves forward, the stakes rise quickly. A key exchange point is attacked unexpectedly. The team suffers heavy loss, and the operation is forced into emergency mode. At this moment, everything changes. What was once a controlled mission turns into chaos. The system that was supposed to guide them is now working against them. Jason Statham is then given a direct order to continue the mission alone. But the strange part is, the order does not come from the usual command channel. It comes from an unknown source inside the network. This is where the real danger begins to show itself. Someone powerful has taken control of the mission from behind the scenes. Now, the situation is no longer about completing the objective. It becomes about survival. Jason Statham's character realizes that he is being pushed into a setup. Every step forward is more dangerous than the last. The team he trusted is no longer fully in control, and the mission he believed in is slowly turning into something far more deadly. And just when everything seems confusing enough, a final message appears on his system screen. A single word, mutiny. This is the moment everything begins to fall apart. After the message mutiny appears on the screen, everything starts to feel different. The mission is no longer just a secret operation. It now feels like a controlled trap where every move has already been planned by someone else. This is where the story of Mutiny 2026 begins to take a darker shape, moving from a simple mission into a global level crisis that no one can fully understand. In this new world, intelligence agencies are no longer fully trusted. Different governments are secretly connected through hidden systems, sharing data that controls military actions, surveillance networks, and black operations. But inside this system, something has gone wrong. A hidden force has started to take control of information, slowly turning allies against each other. The film builds a world similar to modern spy thrillers like Dead Reckoning, where technology is not just a tool, but a weapon. Every system can be hacked, every mission can be changed in real time, and every agent can be replaced or framed without warning. In this kind of environment, truth becomes harder to find, and survival depends on instincts more than orders. Jason Statham's character is placed right in the middle of this collapsing system. He is not just fighting enemies in the field, but also fighting a broken network that no longer follows human control. The mission that was supposed to protect the world has now become the biggest threat to it. The idea of mutiny becomes more clear here. It is not just about soldiers rebelling against leaders. It is about the system itself turning against its own creators. The intelligence network has split from the inside. Some parts still try to follow orders, while others have already been taken over by unknown intelligence forces operating in the shadows. As the story expands, the scale becomes global. Secret operations are failing in multiple countries at the same time. Agents are disappearing without trace. Entire missions are being erased from the system as if they never existed. This creates fear inside the organization because no one knows who is controlling the destruction. At the same time, rumors begin spreading about a classified program known only as Dead Reckoning. It is believed to be a final protocol designed to reset global intelligence systems in case of total failure. But no one knows who activated it or why it is already in motion. This is where tension builds even further. If Dead Reckoning is real, then the world is already heading toward a controlled collapse. And Jason Statham's character may be the only one standing between order and total system failure. But the biggest question remains unanswered. Is he trying to stop the mutiny, or is he already part of it without even knowing? As the system keeps breaking down, all attention slowly shifts to one man caught in the center of it all. Jason Statham's character is no longer just an agent following orders. He has now become a target, a suspect, and possibly the only person who still has a chance to stop everything from collapsing completely. What makes him different in Mutiny 2026 is not just his strength or combat skills, but his experience with missions that others would never survive. He has worked in the darkest parts of intelligence operations, where truth is hidden and survival depends on fast decisions. But even for him, this situation is different. There are no clear enemies, no clear allies, and no clear mission anymore. After the system goes into full alert mode, he starts receiving conflicting messages. One command tells him to continue the operation. Another tells him to abort immediately. But both messages seem to come from trusted sources. This creates confusion, and for the first time, he cannot rely on the system he has trusted his entire career. Inside his team, trust begins to disappear completely. Some agents believe he is the reason everything is falling apart. Others think he is the only one who can fix it. But no one has full information anymore. Every conversation feels dangerous, and every decision could lead to another betrayal. Jason Statham's character begins to act alone, not because he wants to, but because he has no choice. The system that once guided him is now unpredictable. Every location he goes to is already compromised. Every safe house is already known. It feels like someone is always one step ahead, watching his every move. As he moves deeper into the truth, he starts discovering hidden files buried inside the intelligence network. These files reveal something shocking. Parts of the mission were changed before it even began. This means the betrayal was not random. It was planned from the very beginning, long before the team was even assembled. This discovery changes everything. Now, it is not just about stopping an enemy. It is about uncovering who inside the system designed the mutiny itself. But the deeper he goes, the more dangerous it becomes. Every step forward increases the risk of being erased completely, both physically and digitally. At the same time, he is forced to confront a painful reality. The people he once trusted may not be innocent. Some may already be controlled, manipulated, or turned against him without even realizing it. In this world, loyalty can be rewritten, and memory itself can be altered. But even in this chaos, one thing remains constant. Jason Statham's character refuses to give up. Even when the system is against him, even when the world is collapsing around him, he keeps moving forward. Because deep down, he knows the truth is still out there, hidden somewhere inside the word that changed everything. As Jason Statham's character moves deeper into the hidden truth, the situation reaches its most dangerous point. Every step now feels like walking into a trap. The system is no longer just broken. It is fully controlled by an unknown force that is rewriting every rule in real time. What once was a mission has now turned into a full global level crisis with no clear way back. At this stage, the real enemy begins to take shape. It is not just one person or one country. It is a hidden network operating inside the intelligence world made up of rogue agents, corrupted leaders, and advanced digital control systems. This force does not fight in a normal way. It controls information, changes identities, and turns allies into enemies without warning. It is always present, but never visible. Jason Statham finally discovers the truth behind the word mutiny. It was not just a warning. It was a signal. A signal that the intelligence system had already split into two parts. The original command structure and a hidden takeover program running in the background. The mission he was sent on was never meant to succeed. It was designed to activate this split. Now everything becomes clear, but also more dangerous. The same system that gave him orders is now hunting him. His identity is flagged. His movements are tracked. Every location he visits is automatically exposed. There is no safe place left in the world of intelligence. Even silence feels like surveillance. The villain behind all this remains hidden for most of the story, working through layers of control. This person does not need to appear in front of enemies. Instead, they control everything from behind screens using global networks to manipulate events. Their goal is simple, but terrifying. Complete control over all intelligence systems across the world. As the final act builds, Jason Statham is forced into a last mission not assigned by command, but chosen by himself. He realizes the only way to stop the mutiny is to go directly to the core system where it all began. But reaching it means going through the most heavily protected zones where every step could be his last. The final sequence becomes a race against time. The system is preparing a global shutdown protocol known as dead reckoning, designed to erase corrupted intelligence networks completely. But if activated fully, it could also destroy millions of innocent lives connected to those systems. In the middle of this chaos, betrayal hits hardest. Someone from his past, someone he trusted deeply, is revealed to be part of the hidden network. This twist changes everything. It proves that the mutiny was not just external, it was personal from the very beginning. Now Jason Statham stands at the final point where everything will end. One decision will decide the fate of the entire system. Stop the mutiny and risk global collapse, or let it continue and lose control forever. And as the countdown begins, one final question remains hanging in the air. Can one man stop a system built to betray him, or is he already too late?

text: At the start of the movie, Gwen arrives at the all tucked in motel in the dead of night, ready to begin her new job as the night shift manager. As she steps inside, she rings the front desk bell, but no one answers. The eerie silence makes her uneasy, and as she glances around, her eyes lock onto a yogi hanging on the wall. Something about it seems off, but before she can dwell on it, she decides to explore the motel. While wandering through the dimly lit hallway, she notices something strange. Room 18's door is wide open. Cautiously, she steps inside, but the room appears empty. Then, out of nowhere, she bumps into Teddy Miles, the motel manager, who had just finished cleaning. Teddy seems friendly and straightforward, giving Gwen a rundown of the place. It's good, it's bad, and the things she should keep an eye on. He mentions that the job pays in cash, and as they talk, the yogi suddenly crashes to the floor. Teddy shrugs it off, explaining that he inherited the motel from his grandfather and is planning a remodel if his loan gets approved. He continues the tour, leading her to the supply room, which holds all the motel's essentials, but then he gives her a warning. The door can only be opened from the outside. To prevent getting trapped, he props it open with a brick. Outside, Gwen notices the motel's abandoned pool surrounded by caution tape. Teddy explains that a sinkhole opened up last summer and while he reported it to the county, the response was slow. They're finally supposed to fix it this weekend. Normally, Teddy works double shifts. But tonight, he has a date, meaning Gwen will be alone. When she asks about security, he reassures her nothing bad has ever happened here. But if she ever feels unsafe, she can lock herself in the parlor and call him. With that, Teddy leaves for the night. And just as his car disappears down the road, Gwen feels a chill. From the corner of her eyes, she spots a shadowy figure watching her. A wave of unease washes over her. Shaking it off, she checks the key holder and realizes room six is occupied. A guest named Ms. Marsh is staying for one night. Deciding to check on her, Gwen knocks on the door. When Ms. Marsh opens it, Gwen's stomach drops. Her fingernails are filthy, caked with blood and dirt. Trying to ignore the uneasy feeling, Gwen goes about her duties. As she's cleaning, she notices a black car creeping past the motel. The driver is watching her. Her skin prickles, but she forces herself to move on. Later, while stripping the sheets in room 8, she stumbles upon something odd. She doesn't linger on it, just tosses the dirty bedding into the wash and moves on. Stepping outside, she sees a woman entering the lobby. Assuming it's a guest, she follows. But when she steps inside, the lobby is empty. Brushing it off, she orders food. Soon after, the reception phone rings. She answers. Silence. The line goes dead. A second later, it rings again. This time, she checks the caller ID and freezes. The call is coming from room 13. Gwen's heart pounds. She knows that room is empty. Picking up the phone, she hears a faint ghostly laughter. Fear tightens around her chest, but she grabs a knife for protection and heads to room 13. The door caks open and she steps inside, empty. The phone is there, but there's no sign it was used. Just as she turns to leave, the phone rings again. She looks at the caller ID. The call is now coming from the reception desk. Her breath catches. She knows there's no one there. Then a ghostly figure lunges at her. Gwen screams and stumbles backward, her heart hammering in terror, only to collide with Alice, the girl from cabin 6. Alice just wants a replacement hairdryer. In the storage room, while searching for the dryer, Alice casually asks what Gwen saw in room 13. Gwen brushes it off, blaming exhaustion. Maybe she's imagining things. Just as she finds the dryer, Alice accidentally knocks over the brick. The door slams shut. The light flickers. Alice starts to panic. She's terrified of the dark. Suddenly, rats scurry across the floor. They both jump, their fear rising. Then a knock. The door caks open, revealing the food delivery guy. Gwen exhales in relief. As they sit and eat, Alice opens up about her past. Her mother is controlling, harsh. After a huge fight, she ran away from home. But as she talks, Gwen can't shake the feeling that something is very, very wrong with this motel. Feeling sympathetic, Gwen gently suggests that Alice's mother might be out there looking for her. But Alice shrugs it off, saying her mom once grounded her for a month over something ridiculous, so she doubts she even cares. Gwen relates to her struggles, admitting that her own mother was just as strict and difficult at times. But despite everything, she still loved her. Her mother has since passed away and she firmly believes that family matters no matter what. She warns Alice that the world can be dangerous, especially for someone trying to make it on their own. Wanting to lighten the mood, Gwen heads to the vending machine to grab two Cokes. But as she waits, her stomach knots. The same black car from earlier is back. It slows down near the motel before creeping past her. A chill runs down her spine. Something isn't right. She hurries back to the lobby, locking the door behind her. Just as she tries to calm herself, Alice suddenly touches her shoulder, and Gwen jumps, dropping the Cokes. Alice notices her shaken expression and realizes something is seriously bothering her. Sensing Gwen needs space, Alice simply thanks her for the food and heads back to her room. As Gwen bends down to clean up the mess, a loud thud echoes through the lobby. She freezes. Turning her head slowly, she sees that the Yogi statue has fallen again. Before she can process it, she hears the rumble of a car pulling into the parking lot. Her instincts kick in. She grabs a knife and cautiously approaches the reception desk. The door swings open and inwok Warner and Birdie, a lively, flirtatious couple. They want to rent a room for just an hour. Laughing, they explain they ditched a boring art gallery and now want to salvage their night with some fun, but Gwen shakes her head. Motel policy doesn't allow hourly stays. Annoyed, Warner insults the motel, clearly frustrated. After some grumbling, he finally agrees to a full night booking, and Gwen reluctantly hands them the key to room 2. Later, while making her rounds, strange noises coming from room 2 catch Gwen's attention. Curious, she peaks through the window shutters and her eyes widen in shock. Inside, Birdie is whipping Warner. Before she can react, Birdie's head snaps toward the window. Gwen ducks, her heart pounding, then quickly flees, hiding behind their car before she's caught, trying to shake off what she just saw. Gwen heads to the abandoned pool area. Her eyes drift toward the sinkhole, still left unrepaired. Something about it draws her in. As she steps closer, she grips the metal pool ladder for support. But suddenly, it gives way. Gwen loses her balance and plummets into the sinkhole. Her body slamming against the jagged earth. Pain shoots through her leg. And then she hears it. A ghostly girl begins to emerge from the darkness. Her pale figure creeping toward Gwen. Her breath hitches. The girl's face is distorted. Her hollow eyes locked onto Gwen. Gwen screams. scrambling to escape. Just then, Alice rushes in, pulling her to safety. Gasping for air, Gwyn stares at her in shock, trying to process what just happened. As Alice treats her wounds, she finally comes clean. She already knew the motel was haunted. In fact, that was one of the reasons she came. She had heard stories about this place and wanted to see if the rumors were true. Before Gwen can respond, her eyes catch movement. Warner and Birdie are leaving the motel. Something about them feels off. But before she can dwell on it, she turns to Alice. It's time to tell her the truth. Taking a deep breath, Gwen reveals a dark secret from her past. Years ago, when she was Alice's age, a man named Walton Gray broke into her house and murdered her mother and sisters. Gwen was the only one who survived. The police caught Walton and locked him in a mental institution, but 2 days ago, he escaped. And what terrified Gwen the most? She found her mother's necklace, the one she thought was lost the night of the massacre, sitting in her mailbox. Walton sent it to her. Realizing he was coming for her, she panicked and fled town. But now she knows he followed her. She's already seen him twice today. And if he's here, Alice isn't safe either. Gwen warns her to lock her door and stay inside. As she turns to leave, she sees something that makes her blood run cold. A little girl is standing in the lobby. Gwen calls out to her. No response. She looks around. The girl is gone. Confused, Gwen checks the security cameras and sees the girl standing outside. But when she looks out the window, there's no one there. Turning back to the screen, she finds the girl has disappeared. Then suddenly, she bumps into something. Her breath catches. It's the girl, but something is wrong. The girl isn't human. She's a ghost. Fear grips Gwen as she stumbles back, rushing into a room and locking the door behind her. Her hands tremble as she dials Teddy, demanding to know why he never told her the motel was haunted. She frantically recounts everything she has seen, but Teddy insists the place isn't haunted, claiming he has never experienced anything unusual. Gwen doesn't believe him. Angry and terrified, she makes up her mind. This will be her last night here. Then the front desk bell rings. Still shaken, she takes a deep breath and steps out to assist the guest. But as soon as she sees who it is, she freezes. It's him. The man who has been following her all day. Keeping her composure, she books him a room for the night, handing over the key to room 8. As they walk outside, unease creeps over her. She notices the black car parked nearby, the same one from earlier. Inside the room, Gwen pretends to fetch a clean towel. As the man is distracted, she quietly sneaks behind him, gripping a pair of scissors. In one swift motion, she attacks. Blood spills, but instead of collapsing, the man groans in shock. Gwen stares. Something is wrong. He isn't reacting like a killer would because he isn't one. His real name is Raymond Bailey. He isn't some murderer chasing her. He's her doctor. Everything around her starts to blur as Raymond explains the truth. She has been under his care at Ashford Psychiatric Facility for the last 12 years. She escaped two nights ago. There was never a Walton Gray. He was nothing but a story she created. Gwen's body tenses, her mind struggling to process the words. But then the final blow hits. Her family's murder. She wasn't the victim. She was the one who killed them. The corpses she thought she had seen earlier flash in front of her eyes again. But now she sees them for what they really are, hallucinations. The motel was never haunted. Everything was in her head. And then realization turns to rage. Before Raymond can react, she drives the scissors into his throat, his body drops, blood pooling at her feet. Outside, an Ashford hospital van pulls up. Two men step out. They've come to take her back, but Gwen isn't going anywhere. A cold smile creeps across her face as she lures them inside. And then one by one, she kills them, too. Hearing the commotion, Alice hesitates before stepping out of her room to investigate. What she finds sends a chill down her spine. Three lifeless bodies sprawled on the floor. And standing over them is Gwen clutching a bloodstained pair of scissors. Alice's breath catches. Gwen lifts her head, locking eyes with her. Alice bolts. She rushes back to her room, slamming the door shut and locking it. Her hands shake as she backs away. Then suddenly, the power goes out. The room plunges into darkness. And in the silence, Alice hears it. The sound of Gwen trying to unlock the door. Heart pounding. She stumbles into the bathroom, fumbling for her phone, but the screen stays black. The battery is dead. Then crash. The door bursts open. Alice doesn't think. She scrambles to the bathroom window and climbs out. The moment her feet hit the ground, she sprints toward the lobby, grabbing a knife for protection. Her eyes dart around in desperation. Gwen's car keys. She snatches them and rushes outside. Just as she reaches the car, Gwen appears. An axe swings toward her. Alice barely dodges in time, the blade slicing through the air just inches away. Without hesitation, she plunges the knife into Gwen's side. Gwen gasps, staggering back as Alice takes her chance and flees. Reaching the hospital van, she yanks the door handle. Locked. The keys are missing. Panic surges through her veins. She has no choice. She has to go back. She dashes toward room 8, desperately searching for the keys. But before she can escape, Gwen is there. The axe swings down. Alice gasps, collapsing. Gwen stands over her, eyes empty, and then without hesitation, she finishes her off. Moments later, Teddy arrives at the motel. Something feels off. As he steps inside, he notices the door to room 8 is wide open. Inside, everything is eerily clean. No signs of struggle, no bodies except for a faint blood stain on the bed. A chill creeps down his spine. He steps back, calling out for Gwen as he makes his way toward the pool area. Then suddenly, she emerges from the water. Dripping wet, she watches him. Confused, Teddy hesitates. He asks what she was doing down there. Gwen tilts her head. A slow smile spreads across her face. "Come closer," she whispers. "I'll show you." One year later, a college student named Cole is driving to Ashford for school. It's a long 7-hour journey, and as night falls, he decides to stop at a small roadside motel. All tucked in, the place looks different, freshly painted, a brand new neon sign, a fully built pool. When Cole arrives, he's greeted warmly by the motel's owner, Gwen. She welcomes him in, chatting casually as she hands him the key to room 8. As they talk, she mentions the pool, reminiscing about how the hole in the ground used to be so big it could fit five people. Then the truth settles in. That's exactly what it did. Beneath that pristine pool, the bodies remain. As Cole walks to his room, Gwen suddenly sees them. The ghosts of her family, the ones she murdered, Alice, Teddy. They stare at her, their eyes hollow, unblinking. But she doesn't fear them. Not anymore. And then, as if on Q, the Yogi statue on the wall falls once again. With that, the movie ends. So, what do you think? Did you see that twist coming? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

text: The Black Phone 2 was set to hit theaters on October 17th, but if you're struggling to remember what happened in the first film, we're here to help. Instead of a play-by-play of the entire film, here's a slimmed down version of the plot. This is the only recap you need before The Black Phone 2. 2021's The Black Phone is one part supernatural thriller, one part grim coming of age story with a killer performance from Ethan Hawk, who plays our villain. Set in 1978 Denver, the film follows 13-year-old Finny Blake, a shy kid navigating bullies and an abusive home life. But things get much worse when he's abducted by a local serial killer known only as the Grabber, a maskwearing psycho who locks him in a soundproof basement with nothing but a disconnected black rotary phone on the wall. That phone, it turns out, can ring, and when it does, it connects Finny with the ghosts of the Grabbers's previous victims, all kids who didn't make it out alive. Each call gives Finny more clues. How and where to dig a hole, where to find a hidden cord, even how to use the rotary phone as a weapon. While his sister Gwen experiences psychic dreams that guide the police to the neighborhood, Finny puts every trick the ghost taught him to use and builds a trap. When the grabber finally comes for him, Finny traps him in the hole and uses the black phone's cord as a literal noose. In a brutal finale, Finny kills the grabber and escapes. The ghosts finally find peace and Finny finds his voice. The small town and Finny are finally safe from the monster that haunted their town. You might think that's the end of the story, but the Black Phone 2 takes the supernatural horror even further. As Finn, now 17, struggles with life after his captivity, his sister begins receiving calls in her dreams from the Black Phone and sees disturbing visions of three boys being stalked at a winter camp known as Alpine Lake. It's revealed that the Grabber is somehow still roaming the earth, presumably as an undead phantom, seeking revenge on Finny. But that's about all we know for now until the Blackbone 2 hits theaters on October 17th.

text: Hi guys, Cinematic Recapped here. Before we start, WARNING! Spoilers Ahead! Today, I`m gonna explain a European drama and satirical black-comedy movie, called Triangle of Sadness. The movie starts with a young man named Carl, who is trying his luck at modeling. Because he had once been a magazine advertisement model, the judges immediately accept him as their model. Carl’s girlfriend, Yaya, is also a model and influencer. After having dinner at a restaurant, Carl waits for her to pay the bill because Yaya promised to pay for today’s food. For some reason, Yaya does not want to pay at first, even though she earns more than Carl. When Yaya wants to pay, her credit card cannot be used, so Carl ends up paying for the food. On their way home, Carl explains that he just wants Yaya to be a responsible person. However, his reason is still not enough, and the two start bickering about money and even gender roles. A few moments later, Yaya comes to Carl’s room and apologizes to him, regretting what she did just now. A few days later, they are invited on a luxury cruise aboard a superyacht in exchange for promoting it on social media. The chief of staff, Paula, orders the crew members to fulfil the guests' absurd requests in hopes of earning generous tips. While Carl and Yaya are sunbathing on the rear deck, a crew member suddenly takes off his shirt in front of them, which teases Yaya a bit. Seeing this, Carl looks jealous and decides to report the crew to Paula. At that moment, he also plans to propose to Yaya by giving her a diamond ring. Afterwards, Paula tries to call the yacht’s captain for a safety drill, but the captain says he is not feeling well. Among the wealthy guests are the Russian oligarch Dimitry and his wife Vera, who own a fertilizer business for agriculture; the elderly couple Clementine and Winston, who have made their fortune manufacturing grenades; and Therese, who is only capable of speaking a single sentence in German following a stroke. After lunch, Carl is surprised to see that the crew he reported earlier have been fired. At night, a lonely tech millionaire named Jarmo seems to be looking for friends, but he only sees Yaya and Vera there. With the excuse that his girlfriend couldn't come, he asks Yaya to take a photo of him. After that, Yaya and Vera unexpectedly try to cheer him up by taking a group photo. Because of their generosity, Jarmo wants to repay their kindness by buying them luxury watches. Furthermore, Yaya dances in front of Jarmo, which makes Carl jealous for the second time, but she eventually manages to mend their relationship later. The next morning, Vera asks all the crew members to swim in the pool. At first, Paula disagrees with it, considering the crew have to prepare captain's dinner for later, but after hearing some inputs from her assistant Darius, she finally allows them to swim. Therefore, all the working crew members are heading towards the deck, while Darius tries to tell the captain about it. The yacht’s captain, Thomas, finally comes out from his cabin and tries to cover up that he had been spending his time drunk. Shortly after that, the entire crew members jump into the sea one by one to please Vera. Soon, Paula gets Thomas to sober up and attend the captain's dinner. At the same time, the yacht passes through a storm, which causes several of the guests to become violently seasick, and panic finally breaks out. Meanwhile, Thomas and Dimitry are having a conversation about socialism and capitalism. Not only that, they also play games until both of them get very drunk. The drunken Dimitry comes to the captain’s cabin and declares an emergency call that the ship is sinking, which obviously makes things worse. Not long after that, Thomas also joins him, and they continue the argument over the intercom. Several guests are injured as the storm continues to toss the ship, and the power eventually goes out. The following morning, pirates appear out of nowhere and decide to attack the yacht. They quickly kill Clementine and Winston with one of their own grenades and end up capsizing the yacht. Fortunately, a small group of survivors consisting of Carl, Yaya, Dimitry, Therese, Paula, and Jarmo manage to escape to an uninhabited island. However, there is an unknown man named Nelson who also joins the group. He claims to be a ship mechanic, but Dimitry suspects him of being one of the pirates. Having never been to the wilderness, the wealthy guests are frightened by the sounds of animals in the night, one of them even lighting their last flare out of panic. The next day, the group finds a lifeboat washed ashore. Apparently, a toilet manager named Abigail has been staying inside with a lot of supplies since the accident. Paula quickly orders her to open the hatch and has her distribute the supplies to the others. Abigail, the only one with any survival skills, manages to catch an octopus to eat later that night. As Abigail gets more food than the others, Paula confronts her and reminds her to serve the guests. Surprisingly, Abigail quickly sheds her lowly crew member status and usurps command. After that, Abigail, Paula, and Yaya sleep in the lifeboat, while the others sleep outside keeping the bonfire alive. Dimitry even offers his luxury watches to Abigail in exchange for sleeping in the lifeboat, but his efforts are in vain. On the other hand, Carl and Nelson find a pack of pretzel sticks inside Abigail’s bag and decides to eat them. The following day, Dimitry is sad to find his wife dead. Abigail eventually discovers that her pack of pretzel sticks was being eaten by Carl and Nelson, so she punishes the two by not getting any food for them. Because of this, they can only watch the others eat at night. During dinner, Abigail keeps her eyes on Carl and ends up inviting him to sleep with her in the lifeboat. Yaya grows jealous, but Carl promises her not to have any sexual relations with Abigail. When morning arrives, Carl steals pretzel sticks before leaving the lifeboat and then gives them to Yaya. Long story short, the survivors bond and come to terms with their new situation. At one time, Jarmo successfully hunts a donkey, though he could not bear to kill it. As the group celebrates his success, Yaya spots Carl’s hand under Abigail’s jacket, which makes her suspect that Carl is having an affair. In the middle of a stormy night, it is revealed that Abigail has coerced Carl into a sexual relationship in exchange for him getting special privileges and food. At that point, Carl also considers leaving Yaya for Abigail. The next morning, Nelson finally admits to Dimitry that he was a pirate. Yaya comes to the lifeboat and borrows a backpack because she decides to hike to the other side of the island. Hearing this, Abigail volunteers to go with her despite Carl's concerns. After a long journey, they finally discover an elevator and realize that they have been stranded near a luxury resort. Yaya is very happy to find the elevator, but Abigail seems reluctant to enter. After asking for a moment to relieve herself, Abigail prepares to attack Yaya with a rock, but hesitates when the oblivious Yaya offers Abigail work as her assistant. In the meantime, Therese encounters a beach vendor, but unfortunately, she is unable to communicate her situation. The movie ends with Carl seen running frantically through the forest. text: As many of you know, I had the privilege of watching Wes Anderson's new film Asteroid City at the Cannes Film Festival a few months ago. With the film now beginning to come out more widely, I thought I'd share my thoughts on the film. Asteroid City is a comedy/drama that follows the story of a recently widowed father and his children. The father takes his children on a road trip to desert town Asteroid City for a junior stargazers convention for his son. While there, they meet the other visitors of the convention and the local people of the town and in true Wes Anderson fashion get into some quirky and existential hijinks. Admittedly I've recently fallen out of love with Wes Anderson's movies and style. Most people say that you can't be neutral to his work, that you either love it or hate it, but these days I feel quite neutral. With his recent films, in particular 2021's The French Dispatch, I felt saturated and overwhelmed by what has become the quintessential Wes Anderson style. The meticulous colour, symmetry and visual gags coupled with the lengthy deadpan dialogue can feel hollow and insincere. It feels like we're now a world away from the movies of Rushmore and The Darjeeling Limited, two of my favourite Wes Anderson films and now are moving into a all Sizzle no stake territory. Taking all of that into consideration I wasn't expecting much from Asteroid City but I did enjoy this film. Of course Asteroid City has all the hallmarks of his style with all the visual characteristics and motifs you come to expect from one of his films, but this time the look and feel was much easier to digest and I think the desert setting helped influence a more paired back style and feeling to the film. The cast for Asteroid City is stacked. Each actor has their moment to shine and they do it well. Even Jeff Goldblum in his tiny moment was a hoot. I was most impressed by Jason Schwartzman and Scarlett Johansson who have the most to work with in the story. The dialogue and the story felt much more genuine and reflective this time around, there were some great scenes towards the end of the film that were quite impactful and felt very honest. I wish that there were more of these scenes instead of the eccentric mingling you get for the majority of the film, because it was in those scenes where I felt like we were actually coming close to understanding and connecting with the messages of the film. Without saying too much the film explores themes of isolation and grief but is restrained for most of the film. Wes Anderson's films are not the type to be melodramatic or gritty, so I wouldn't expect that from his work, but I think the film loses out in a way because these films are being held back by the typical gimmicks. Asteroid City is nowhere near perfect but it is Wes Anderson's best film in many years. It's funny, playful, well-acted and of course gorgeous but the real gold is in those small moments where all pretence is dropped. Even though award season is far away I can see potential nominations for production design. I look forward to seeing and hearing what others think of this film and if you've seen it please let me know your thoughts. As always thank you for listening in and please stay tuned for more reviews of the films that I saw at Cannes.
title: Asteroid City review | Cannes 2023 recap

text: The trailer for “Abigail” tells you almost everything you need to know about the movie, a wacky high-concept horror thriller about a group of kidnappers who bite off more than they can chew when they unwittingly abduct a child-sized vampire ballerina. The vamp, played with some relish by Alisha Weir, only really comes alive when she’s leering at or stalking her prey. Genre fans will also spot some familiar faces among the movie’s ensemble cast, all of whom do their best with this tic-y, schtick-y material. They curse (enough to seem like they’re overcompensating for some things); they run (around each other, mostly); they get picked off one by one. You already know what you’re in for if you’ve come to “Abigail” to watch a body count caper featuring plummy character actor performances from That Guys like Kevin Durand and Dan Stevens. Most of their co-stars keep up in less attractive roles, including Melissa Barrera’s thinly drawn anti-heroine team leader. There’s also plenty of viscous-looking blood splatter and some modestly good-looking vampire makeup—the fangs, in particular. Some action scenes are well-choreographed, but generally over-edited and shot just ahead of whatever’s moving on-screen. The rest of this 90-minute genre exercise is unfailingly conventional, though that’s also a big part of its ostensible appeal. I can’t really get or stay mad at “Abigail” for essentially delivering what its marketing promises. Sure, the movie’s creators, led by co-helmers Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett (better known as “Radio Silence,” directors of “Ready or Not” and the 2022 “Scream” reboot), could have delivered more, even though disenchanted viewers can’t exactly claim false advertising. The setup is strictly by the numbers and the characters are all stock types. A team of bickering misfits kidnaps the title character (Weir). They follow her home with a comically oversized gizmo stuck to the bottom of her chauffeur’s car. Then they bring the 12-year-old-looking girl to a secluded mansion, where they’re reminded of their mission’s stakes. Shady but well-dressed ring-leader Lambert (Giancarlo Esposito) gives us and them the rundown: no real names, no cell phones, nothing personal—it’s 24 hours of baby-sitting a pre-teen who really likes to plié and step-toe her way through “Swan Lake” rehearsals. Simple is as simple does. We learn very little about everyone, thanks in no small part to a scene where Lambert nicknames the characters after members of the Rat Pack. Durand’s character, a jolly-but-dim muscle-bro named Peter, tries to find the sense in being nicknamed after rats. Later, he gets that it’s a disposable pop culture reference and promptly moves on. Peter’s the most sympathetic character in “Abigail,” partly because he’s constantly straining against the limits of what his character can know and do. He’s joined by a call sheet of tropes, including Abigail’s minder, the empathetic and observant Joey (Melissa Barrera); their irritating and wasted driver Dean (the late “Euphoria” star Angus Cloud); and the strong-silent ex-soldier Rickles (William Catlett). Eventually, the team has to worry not only about Abigail, but a few predictable liabilities, like their bratty and easily bored electronics hacker Sammy (Kathryn Newton) and their foul-mouthed, inexplicably accented ex-cop backup leader Frank (Stevens). None of these party game-light character traits really matter once Abigail gets loose from her handcuffs. The house that Abigail’s prey stay in has more personality, but it’s basically the house from “Clue” with some extra goth-y touch-ups. Maybe that’s all you need to enjoy watching a game cast check off every box as they struggle to figure out how to stop a “real” vampire. Nothing worth writing home about comes to mind. It’s hard to get too excited watching so many talented actors try and barely succeed in making you want to care about their characters, especially since that isn’t the same thing as making you care. More could have been done with less tedious dialogue, as what's here is designed mostly just to hold the hands of viewers as the plot skips from beat to beat. More could have also been done with Joey, who, at one point, stuffs a loaded gun into her tight jeans’ waistband. I do and I don’t believe it. “Abigail” may find its audience given a lucky combination of good timing and wishful thinking. It’s not badly made, just uninspired and played out. If you like B-movies made with a budget and are specifically looking for an undemanding time, “Abigail” might be for you. “Abigail” might also disappoint you, especially if you’re hoping for more than what’s advertised.

मुश्किल से सड़क तक पहुंचा तो रात हो चुकी थी रानी की हालत भी गैर हो रही थी पर अब वह पुलिस ऑफिसर के पास महफूज हाथों में था आगे मंजर बदलता है समर सीजन होता है और ज्यादातर लोग वेकेशंस पर आए होते हैं अब हम 1997 का बना हुआ घर देखते हैं नो नाम का लड़का कुछ टाइप कर रहा था अपनी मदर के बुलाने पर वह नीचे आता है और साइकिल लेकर चला जाता है तभी वहां हेल बसन नाम की लेडी आती है वो नोआ की मदर के साथ बहुत बातें करती है नोआ अपनी लिखी गई स्टोरी केविन को दिखाने के लिए जाता है पर वह इसमें इंटरेस्टेड नहीं होता नो के फ्रेंड का मैच होता है वह मैच जीत जाता है और खुशी खुशी अपने फ्रेंड्स के साथ जा रहा होता है सब फ्रेंड्स को रास्ते में शरारत सूझी और वह एक बोले आदमी के घर में चले गए यह इसके घर की बैक साइड थी सब बच्चे इसके स्टोर में चले गए और चीजों को चेक करने लगे बुरा आदमी कोई चीज लेने के लिए वहां आया तो बच्चों ने डर कर खुद को छुपा लिया पर इस आदमी ने उन बच्चों को देख लिया तो वह सब वहां से भागे पर नो का बैग अंदर ही रह गया था वह बैग लेना चाहता था पर उसके फ्रेंड ने कहा कि अभी तो यहां से चुलू बाद में देख लेंगे तो मजबूर ना इसको वहां से भागना ही पड़ता है और वह अपने फ्रेंड को लेकर घर आ जाता है इसके फ्रेंड के पास टिकेट्स थी नोए इनको देखकर बहुत खुश होता है जैसे ये इसके लिए कोई खजाना हो इसका फ्रेंड उसे कहता है मुझे यकीन है कि एक दिन तुम बहुत अच्छी स्टोरी लिखने में कामयाब हो जाओगे नोआ का फ्रेंड रात के वक्त एक लड़की के साथ स्विमिंग करने के लिए जाता है विच दौर से खड़ी होकर उन्हें देख रही होती है और उन्हें कहती है कि तुम लोग इस वक्त यहां क्या कर रहे हो और वह भी पानी में कूद जाती है पहले वह लड़की को पानी के अंदर ले जाती है लड़की अपनी जान बचाकर बाहर आती है तो वो लड़ को पानी के अंदर खेंच लेती है और अपने साथ ही ले जाती है अगले दिन नोआ घर से बाहर आता है तो इसका बैग बाहर ही पड़ा था वह बैग उठाता है इसमें एक बुक पड़ी थी इसके बाद वह अपने फ्रेंड के घर जाता है इसकी मामने पुलिस को रात में पेश आने वाले सारे वाक के बारे में बता दिया था इसके फ्रेंड को भी बचा लिया गया था पर जब नो इसके पास गया तो वह तो गुमस बैठा था नो ने इसके साथ बात की पर वह इसकी किसी भी बात का जवाब नहीं दे रहा था फिर वो इस लड़की के पास गया जो उसके फ्रेंड के साथ थी इसने नोआ को विच के बारे में बता दिया था इसके बाद नोआ इस बूढ़े आदमी का शुक्रिया अदा करने के लिए आया जिसने इसका बैग इसको वापस किया था नोआ के घर में एक बूढ़ लेडी रहती थी उसे शक होने लगा कि कहीं यही तो विच नहीं है बेन के बारे में न्यूज में भी दिखाया जा रहा था जीन नाम के बोले आदमी ने जब यह न्यूज़ देखी तो वो नोआ के साथ बेन के पास आया बेन अभी तक इसी हालत में ही बैठा था जीन ने जब इससे बात की तो उसकी बात का जवाब देने लगा जीन उसकी बात सुनकर वहां से चला गया सब फैड्स इकट्ठे होकर विच के बारे में ही बात कर रहे थे कुछ फ्रेंड्स मिलकर जंगल में बोन फायर के लिए जाते हैं वहां पर लड़की एक लड़के को अपने साथ आने का इशारा करती है वह दोनों बाकी के लोगों से दूर चले जाते हैं फिर इस जगह पर जोरदार धमाका होता है और अगले दिन नो न्यूज में देखता है कि इसका फ्रेंड भी उन लोगों में शामिल होता है वो भी गुम समम ही हो जाता है जीम ने भी यह न्यूज देख तो वो नोआ को काल करता है और उसके साथ जंगल में चला जाता है वहां वह दोनों मिलकर सबूत इकट्ठे करने लगते हैं तलाश के दौरान उन्हें एक लंबी स्टिक वाला झाड़ो मिला और कपड़े का एक टुकड़ा भी जीन और नोआ के दो फ्रेंड्स के पास गए और उनसे अपनी मदद करने को कहा क्योंकि अब यह तीन फ्रेंड ही बाकी रह गए थे जो होश में थे वह चारों आपस में सारी बात डिस्कस करते हैं और सारा प्लान बनाते हैं कि उन्हें आगे क्या करना है नोआ दूरबीन से अपने सामने वाले घर में मौजूद बूरी लेडी पर नजर रख रहा था तो व भी इत्तेफाक से इसी की तरफ ही देख रही थी नोआ से देखकर डर जाता है पर वह हिम्मत नहीं हारना चाहता था बूरी लेडी सामने के घर में किसी काम से गई थी वरना तो वो नोआ के घर के ऊपर वाले हिस्से में रहती थी नोआ ने अपनी माम को सोते हुए देखा तो उनके पास से चाबी उठाकर ले गया और बूढ़ी लेडी के रूम में आ गया वहां उसको वही कपड़ा दिखाई दिया जिसका कुछ हिस्सा उसने जंगल में देखा था तभी डोर खिलने की आवाज आई बूढ़ लेडी अंदर आने वाली थी तो नो ने खुद को अलमारी में छुपा लिया बूढ़ लेडी अंदर आई इसने आसपास देखा और शाल लेकर वापस चली गई अब नोआ अपने फ्रेंड्स के साथ मिलकर इस बूढ़ी लेडी पर नजर रख रहा था बूढ़ लेडी अपना साइकिल लेकर निकली तो नोआ भी अपने फ्रेंड्स के साथ इसका पीछा कर रहा था इन लोगों ने मौका पाकर बूरी लेडी पर हमला कर दिया पर लेडी ने सबके सामने प्रूव किया कि वह विच नहीं है और नोया की इस हरकत की वजह से बूढ़ी लेडी ने वह घर छोड़ दिया नोआ की मदर उसे रोकती रह गई पर वो जा चुकी थी नोआ की मदर इससे नाराज हो गई नोआ ने उनसे मुफी मांगी और जीन के घर आ गया जीन और नोआ की बहुत दोस्ती हो चुकी थी क्योंकि इन दोनों की हबीज बहुत मलती थी पर अब इन दोनों ने इस विच के बारे में जानने का पक्का इरादा कर लिया था आगे हम एक बच्ची को मिलाने की कोशिश कर रहा था नोआ अपने यूजीन नाम के फ्रेंड को तलाश करने के लिए जंगल की तरफ आ जाता है और उसे आवाजें देता जा रहा होता है नोआ को अपना फ्रेंड तो मिल गया पर उनके सामने विच खड़ी थी इसलिए इन दोनों ने यहां से भाग जाने में ही आफियत समझी और भागकर जंगल से बाहर आ गए नोआ सीधा जीन के पास आया और इसे सारा वाकया बताया जीन ने नो को बताया कि इससे पहले भी बहुत से बच्च को विच अपने साथ ले जा चुकी है और text: The Odyssey explained in two minutes. Odysseus was the king of Ithaca, a Greek hero who fought for 10 years in the Trojan War. When the city of Troy finally fell, he prepared to sail home to his wife Penelope and [music] his son Telemachus. What followed was not a simple journey, but a long and dangerous wandering that lasted another 10 [music] years. At the beginning of his voyage, Odysseus angered the sea god Poseidon by blinding the Cyclops [music] Polyphemus, the god's own son. From that moment, Poseidon vowed to prevent the hero from ever reaching home. Storms [music] drove his ships far from Greece, and many of his companions were lost. On the island of the Lotus-Eaters, some of his men forgot their purpose and had to be [music] dragged back to the ships. Later, the enchantress Circe turned part of his crew into animals before Odysseus forced [music] her to restore them. Following her advice, he traveled to the edge of the world to seek guidance [music] from the spirit of the prophet Tiresias. After receiving warnings about the dangers ahead, [music] Odysseus faced the Sirens, whose songs lured sailors to their deaths, and he passed between the deadly sea monsters Scylla and Charybdis. Each trial reduced [music] his crew further until none remained. Eventually, he reached the island of Calypso, who kept him there for many [music] years, wishing to make him her immortal husband. According to the account, the gods finally took pity on him, and Zeus ordered Calypso to release [music] him. Odysseus built a raft and set sail once more, only to be shipwrecked again before finding refuge among the people of Phaeacia. They listened to his story and helped him return at last to Ithaca. At home, he found his palace overrun [music] by arrogant suitors who believed him dead and sought to marry Penelope. With the help of Athena and his son Telemachus, Odysseus disguised himself, tested their loyalty, and then revealed his identity. He defeated the suitors and reclaimed his household. Peace was restored to Ithaca, and the long [music] journey of Odysseus finally ended where it had begun. The tale closes with the gods establishing order once more, allowing the weary king to live out his days in the land [music] he had struggled so long to reach.
