text: Season one of The Flash opens with the Scientific and Technological Advanced Research Laboratories, or STAR Labs, creating a particle accelerator that would theoretically bring clean energy to Central City. Unfortunately, the accelerator explodes, causing a storm that gives super powers to every human caught in its wake. One of those new metahumans is forensic crime scene assistant Barry Allen, who wakes from a coma after nine months having gained superspeed. Barry is trained by STAR Labs’ team, including paraplegic founder Dr. Harrison Wells, and his assistants, Caitlin Snow and Cisco Ramon. After Cisco develops a suit for Barry that can withstand his high running speeds, the new superhero names himself the Flash. With a name, a suit, and a team supporting him, Barry vows to help STAR Labs capture all of the metahumans who were using their newfound powers for villainy. As Barry thwarts a series of metahuman villains as the Flash, he also has to juggle a complicated personal life. Barry was adopted and raised by Central City Police Detective Joe West, after Barry’s father, Henry, was convicted of murdering Barry’s mother, Nora. Barry had witnessed his mother’s murder as a small child, but no one had believed him that the death was caused by a fellow speedster wearing a yellow suit. Now with the powers of the Flash, Barry had a renewed hope in bringing his mother’s true killer to justice and exonerating his father. As Barry continues to work alongside his surrogate father Joe to catch his mother’s killer, dubbed the Reverse-Flash, Barry also harbors a secret life-long crush on Joe’s daughter, Iris. Iris, meanwhile, begins a romance with Joe’s detective partner, Eddie Thawne. Some of the many villains Barry must fight against in season one include Leonard Snart and Mick Rory, aka the freeze and heat ray toting duo of Captain Cold and Heat Wave. The weather controlling Weather Wizard, the rage inducing Rainbow Raider, a super-intelligent gorilla named Grodd, and even Caitlin Snow’s fiance, Ronnie Raymond. Ronnie was thought to have died in the particle accelerator explosion, but had actually physically merged with a physicist named Martin Stein, losing his memories and becoming the metahuman Firestorm. Caitlin and the members of Star Labs help Ronnie and Stein learn to separate their bodies and control their powers. Despite their brief romantic reunion, Ronnie is forced to leave Caitlin as he and Stein depart Central City to learn more about their powers. Barry also meets and befriends Oliver Queen, a fellow superhero from the neighboring Star City who goes by the alter-ego Green Arrow. Though having no metahuman powers, Oliver is a skilled fighter and leader who further teaches Barry how to be a superhero. As Joe helps Barry in investigating Nora Allen’s death, the detective eventually begins to suspect that Harrison Wells might actually be involved. It’s revealed that Wells is in fact a metahuman from the future named Eobard Thawne, a descendant of Iris’ boyfriend, Eddie. Eobard was the villainous Reverse-Flash, who used his speed powers to travel back in time to kill his arch-enemy, Barry Allen. When his plan failed, Eobard instead killed Barry’s mother, Nora. Unfortunately for Eobard, traveling back in time weakened his powers, stranding him in the past. Eobard then killed the real Dr. Harrison Wells and stole his identity, then set about to use STAR Labs to create the particle accelerator, cause the explosion that gives Barry his powers, and then steal those powers to have the energy required to return to his home in the future. After uncovering this revelation, Joe and Barry team up with Caitlin and Cisco to trap Thawne and bring him to justice. Firestorm and Oliver then return to Central City to help Barry defeat the villainous Thawne. Seemingly safe, Ronnie and Caitlin finally get married. Unfortunately, the imprisoned Thawne convinces Barry to help him create a wormhole that would allow Thawne to return to his home in the future, and Barry to travel to the past to save his mother. Barry accepts the offer, but while in the past, Barry realizes that he must allow his mother to die in order to become the superhero Flash in the future. Barry returns to the present and confronts Thawne, leading to a final fight between the Flash and Reverse-Flash. Reverse-Flash gets the upper hand, but before Thawne can kill Barry, Eddie shoots himself, meaning his descendant Eobard vanishes from existence. As the season comes to a close, the wormhole created by Barry and Thawne becomes unstable, turning into a singularity that could destroy all of Central City. In an effort to save the city, Barry runs into the singularity, leaving his fate unknown. In season two of The Flash, it’s revealed that Firestorm helps Barry destroy the singularity, but Ronnie is killed in the process. Six months later, a taped confession from the now dead Eobard Thawne is made public, which exonerates Henry Allen of his wife’s murder. Barry then begins being hunted by other metahumans, who all claim to be sent by a mysterious villain known as Zoom. A man named Jay Garrick arrives at STAR Labs, introducing himself as the Flash from a parallel Earth, known as Earth-2, pulled into this multiverse by the Singularity while fighting his greatest villain, the demonic speedster Zoom. The singularity has stripped Jay of his speedster powers, but the alternate reality Flash is still able to train Barry and teach him new powers and moves, including throwing bolts of lightning. During his time with Team Flash, Jay develops a romance with the grieving Caitlin. As Barry and the Star Labs team fight off Zoom’s army of metahumans from Earth-2, Joe forms a new metahuman task force for the Central City Police Department. Also joining the task force is police officer Patty Spivot, whom Barry begins a relationship with. The opening of the singularity causes many more ripple effects for the team at Star Labs. Cisco develops metahuman abilities of his own. Taking on the name Vibe, Cisco is able to locate other metahumans and even travel freely throughout the multiverse. The real Dr. Harrison Wells from Earth-2 arrives, explaining that he was responsible for the accidental creation of Zoom and the other metahumans from his timeline, and so he traveled to Earth-1 to right his wrongs and help Team Flash defeat the villains. Despite still reeling from the betrayal of the original Wells, Cisco grows close to this alternate version, nicknaming him Harry and forming a strong friendship. When Cisco discovers that Zoom has kidnapped Harry’s daughter, Jesse, the team travels to Earth-2 to save her. On Earth-2, Barry meets the alternate version of himself, who is married to Iris, and the team must face off against villainous versions of Cisco, Caitlin, and Ronnie, who go by the names Reverb, Killer Frost, and Deathstorm. Ultimately, the team are successful in rescuing Jesse, but upon their return to Earth-1, Zoom manages to pull Jay back to their homeworld, seemingly killing him. Meanwhile, Joe’s long estranged wife, Francine returns to town to inform Joe and Iris that she is dying of a terminal illness. Francine’s dying wish is to introduce Joe to his secret son, Wally West. Wally’s introduction to the West family starts off shaky, but he quickly becomes a valuable member of not only the West family, but of Team Flash. After discovering that Barry is secretly the Flash but never told her, Patty breaks up with Barry and leaves Central City for good. Meanwhile, Caitlin grows cold over the supposed death of another love, leading Cisco to fear that his friend will turn into her villainous Earth-2 counterpart, Killer Frost. The team eventually discover that not only is Jay Garrick alive and well, but that his real name is Hunter Zolomon, and he was in fact the villainous Zoom. Zolomon was a serial killer who gained superspeed from the particle accelerator explosion, but tried to increase his speed by taking a drug known as Velocity. As the drug started to kill him, Zolomon captured the real Jay Garrick of Earth-2 and imprisoned him to drain his powers and keep himself alive. When that wasn’t enough, Zolomon set his sights on Barry in Earth-1. Now, Zolomon captures Wally, trading his life for Barry’s speed. In order for Barry to regain his powers, Harry recreates the particle accelerator explosion. During the explosion, Wally and Jesse are also caught in the blast, though its effects on them are unknown. Zolomon then murders Henry Allen, provoking the newly repowered Barry to a race to determine which of them was truly faster. Barry, distraught and angered over his father’s death, agrees to the race despite the warnings of his team that the race was a trick to use Barry’s speed to destroy every other planet in the multiverse. Barry ultimately succeeds in beating Zolomon and thwarting his plans. Time wraiths, whose purpose are to keep order in the timeline and multiverse, capture Zolomon for his crimes. Barry rescues the real Jay Garrick, who turns out to be Earth-2’s doppelganger of Henry Allen. With the multiverse saved, Harry, Jesse, and Jay say goodbye to their new friends and return to Earth-2. Barry, still distraught over everything he has lost, travels back in time and stops Eobard Thawne from killing his mother. In season 3 of The Flash, after successfully saving his mother, Barry returns to his present with Eobard Thawne as his prisoner. Despite Henry and Nora still being alive, Barry realizes this new version of the future, which Thawne nicknames Flashpoint, is much worse for all of his family and friends. This prompts Barry to allow Thawne to return to the past and kill Nora, resetting the timeline. Thawne is then imprisoned in his future timeline, and things seem to finally start going well for Barry, who begins dating his childhood crush, Iris. A mysterious villain known as Alchemy begins creating metahumans that only existed in Flashpoint, giving them their memories from the alternate timeline and sending them to face off against the Flash. Meanwhile, Harry and Jesse return from Earth-2, with Jesse being revealed to have also gained superspeed from the particle accelerator explosion. As Barry trains Jesse in her new powers, Harry begins searching the various versions of Earth in the multiverse to find a new version of himself to join Team Flash and help in their fight against Alchemy. Ultimately, H.R. Wells of Earth-19 is selected as his replacement. After Jesse completes her training, she decides to stay on Earth-1 to pursue a relationship with Wally. After Harry returns to Earth-2, H.R. is discovered to be a fraud. Instead of being an actual, genius scientist, he was more of an “ideas” man, who had no actual scientific or technical skill. Despite this, team Flash allows the well-meaning H.R. to stay. Meanwhile, Wally begins having visions of Flashpoint where he also developed superspeed and was known as Kid Flash. Feeling jealous that he didn’t have powers in this timeline, Wally is persuaded to trust Alchemy, who gives him the speed powers he so desperately wants. Eventually, Barry discovers that Alchemy is actually his new CCPD partner, Julian Albert, who is being mind controlled by a villainous speed god known as Savitar. Savitar is seemingly impossible to defeat, being significantly faster and stronger than Barry. During a battle with Savitar, Barry is briefly thrown five months into the future where he witnesses the speed-god murdering Iris. In the present, Jay Garrick comforts Barry and assures him that the future can be changed. Barry and Iris get engaged, and all of Team Flash come together to devise a plan to change the future, save Iris’ life, and defeat Savitar. At first, Barry and Iris decide to keep the future death a secret from Joe, who has happily started a new romance with a district attorney named Cecile, but eventually Joe learns of his daughter’s supposed fate and joins the fight to save her. Meanwhile, Caitlin begins developing the cryokinetic powers that had turned her into the villainous Killer Frost on Earth-2. She finds comfort in a romantic relationship with Julian, who similarly struggles with being forced into a mind-controlled partnership with Savitar. As Caitlin’s powers grow more out of control, she eventually turns into Killer Frost and joins Savitar. After realizing that Savitar knew impossible details about members of Team Flash, Barry deduces that Savitar was in fact a future version of himself. Savitar confirms this, explaining that he is the result of a future timeloop. After Iris’ future death at the hands of Savitar, Barry runs fast enough to create a time remnant of himself to defeat Savitar. But because this time remnant wasn’t the real Barry, he is shunned by all of his family and friends. Feeling distraught over his abandonment and purposelessness, the time remnant sets about becoming a God, which would force people to love and worship him. After obtaining his god-like powers, Savitar needed to return to the past and kill Iris in order to ensure that Past Barry would create the time remnant and thus continue the loop and cause his existence. As the season comes to a close, it’s the day of Iris’ death. Barry and Savitar fight, but ultimately Savitar wins, defeating Barry and murdering Iris before escaping. As Barry mourns his love, he discovers that Iris was in fact a disguised H.R., who sacrificed himself to prove his worth to the team. Barry then continues his fight against Savitar, with Wally, Jay, and a remorseful Caitlin by his side. After Barry destroys Savitar’s armor, Iris kills the villain, defeating the speed-god once and for all. As the season fades to black, an energy storm appears in Central City due to the speed force needing a prisoner to pay for the various crimes against the timeline. In an attempt to atone for his creation of Flashpoint, Barry enters the prison, his ultimate fate unknown. In season four of The Flash, after six months of being trapped in the Speed Force, Cisco finally figures out a way to rescue Barry. Unfortunately, Barry’s exit from the Speed Force releases dark matter particles that grants metahuman abilities to twelve passengers on a city bus. A mysterious man named Clifford DeVoe, known as the Thinker, begins manipulating the new metahumans into doing his bidding in a plot to defeat the Flash. One of the new metahumans is Ralph Dibny, who gains the ability to stretch his body and morph his appearance. Ralph is a former corrupt CCPD cop that Barry had gotten fired for planting evidence. Now, Ralph is a private detective trying to better himself. Barry gives Ralph a second chance, leading him to join Team Flash and help them defeat the Thinker. Also helping Team Flash defeat the Thinker is Harry Wells, who returns from Earth-2 after an argument with Jesse. When Jesse breaks up with Wally, the Kid Flash departs Central City in an effort to find himself. Harry then forms a Council of Wells from the various Earths in the multiverse, who bring their genius minds together to formulate a plan to defeat the Thinker. As the team battles against the new metahumans and grows closer to thwarting the Thinker’s plans, there are many major life events to celebrate. Joe and Cecile find out they’re expecting a baby, and during the pregnancy, Cecile begins to develop telepathic abilities. Meanwhile, during an epic crossover with the heroes Green Arrow, Supergirl, and the Legends of Tomorrow, Barry and Iris finally get married. Eventually, the team discovers that Clifford DeVoe, aka the Thinker, is a man dying of ALS. He had been given genius level intellect after the particle accelerator explosion, dubbing himself the fastest mind in the world. Unfortunately, his ALS worsens, and DeVoe needs to stay connected to his specially designed chair to survive. The Thinker then transfers his consciousness into a metahuman named Dominic Lanse, gaining his ability to read minds in the process. The Thinker then stages his original body to frame Barry for his murder. Although Barry is sentenced to life in prison, Ralph is able to use his morphing powers to appear as the original DeVoe and clear Barry’s name. Meanwhile, the Thinker begins stealing the powers of the other bus metahumans, killing them in the process. This eventually leads him to Ralph, tragically killing him and stealing his powers, which allows him to morph into his original Clifford DeVoe body. The Thinker’s ultimate plan is to create an Enlightenment Machine, which would diminish the intelligence of everyone on Earth, and DeVoe could teach them all how to live better lives. Originally seeing his plan as benevolent and for the greater good, the Thinker is slowly corrupted by the horrors he must commit to achieve his vision. This prompts DeVoe’s wife, Marlize, to abandon him. Harry then tries to create a thinking cap device that would help him reach the Thinker’s intelligence level, but the dark matter used causes brain damage and an increasingly deteriorating intelligence. As the season comes to a close, DeVoe activates his Enlightenment Machine. With time running out, Cecile uses her newly developing powers to send Barry into DeVoe’s mind. While there, he finds and rescues Ralph, who returns to the real world and reclaims his body from DeVoe. DeVoe’s mind is still alive due to his chair, but his wife Marlize destroys the chair, killing DeVoe for good. After DeVoe’s Enlightenment Machine satellites are destroyed, the heroes celebrate their victory. Harry’s brain damage is stabilized and he returns home to Earth-2, no longer a genius, but ready to live a normal life. Cecile gives birth to her and Joe’s daughter, who they name Jenna. As the season fades to black, a new speedster from the future arrives, introducing herself as Nora, Barry and Iris’ daughter from the future. In season 5 of The Flash, Barry bonds with and trains his daughter, Nora, who warns that she has no memory of him in the future, as he disappears in a Crisis event in 2024. Meanwhile, a mysterious superpowered killer known as Cicada becomes hellbent on exterminating all metahumans from Central City. Cicada wields a meta-tech dagger that could detect metahumans and negate their powers. To help in their mission to unmask and defeat Cicada, Team Flash recruits the multiverse’s greatest detective, Harrison Sherloque Wells. While helping the team fight Cicada, Sherloque also becomes suspicious of Nora’s true motivations. And Sherloque is right to be suspicious, as it’s revealed that Nora is secretly working alongside Eobard Thawne, a time remnant from when Barry created Flashpoint. Team Flash eventually discovers that Cicada is a man named Orlin Dwyer. After his sister’s death in a metahuman attack, Orlin adopted his young niece, Grace. And after Grace is put into a coma and he is critically injured in the wake of DeVoe’s Enlightenment Machine destruction, Orlin becomes Cicada and vows to kill all metahumans as revenge. Caitlin and Cisco then start developing a metahuman cure, which Team Flash hopes to use on Cicada to stop his killing spree. When it’s discovered that the comatose Grace has developed metahuman powers of her own, Barry convinces Orlin to end his vendetta against metahumans and take the cure, in the hopes of proving its viability and using the cure on Grace. Before Cicada can be cured, he is abducted by a new Cicada, who reveals herself to be an adult version of Grace. When Orlin tries to convince Grace to end their cycle of violence, she murders him. Meanwhile, Caitlin tracks down her father, Thomas, to learn more about her burgeoning ice powers and her villainous alter-ego, Killer Frost. Thomas Snow had accidentally caused the metahuman powers in himself and his daughter after searching for a cure for ALS. Now, Thomas’ villainous alter-ego Icicle wants to kill the human versions of them both by using a machine known as a cryo-atomizer. Before Icicle can kill Thomas and Caitlin, Cicada II arrives and attacks them to steal the machine for herself. Thomas manages to take back control of his body and sacrifices himself to save Caitlin from Grace. With the cryo-atomizer, Grace plans to reverse the metahuman cure into a weapon that would kill all metahumans. Sherloque then discovers that Nora has been working alongside Eobard Thawne, and exposes her actions to the rest of Team Flash. Nora explains that in the future, with Barry missing, Iris had implanted a power-dampening chip in their daughter that would suppress her speed powers in an attempt to protect her. When Nora is attacked by a speedster known as Godspeed, who kills her best friend, Lia, the chip malfunctions, and Nora discovers her powers. Furious at Iris for keeping her powers a secret, Nora turns to the only speedster she knows of for help, an imprisoned Eobard Thawne. Thawne, wanting to change his legacy to one a bit more heroic before he is executed for his crimes, trains Nora to defeat Godspeed and then travel back in time to meet her father. Upon hearing this explanation in the present, Barry remains furious at his future daughter and banishes her back to her time. Thawne then teaches Nora how to use the Negative Speed Force to return to the past, where she teams back up with a remorseful and apologetic Barry and Iris to stop Grace once and for all. Although their original plan is to destroy Cicada’s dagger, Ralph and Sherloque realize that the dagger is dampening Thawne’s powers in the future, which keep him imprisoned. And so, it was Thawne’s plan all along to send Nora to the past to help destroy the dagger, which would ensure he regains his powers to escape execution. When Nora’s new plan to enter the young Grace’s mind and convince her to take the cure also fails, Barry is forced to destroy the dagger, creating a new timeline that releases Thawne from his imprisonment and erases the future Grace from existence. Also erased from existence is Nora, who gives an emotional goodbye to her parents. With the city and timeline saved once again, Sherloque returns to his Earth, Caitlin and her Frost persona agree to co-exist, Cisco uses the metahuman cure on himself, Joe is promoted to Captain of the CCPD, and the future Crisis event that causes the disappearance of Barry Allen is moved from 2024 to the end of the current year. In season 6 of The Flash, Barry learns from a multiversal being known as the Monitor that he must die in the upcoming Crisis event in order to prevent the destruction of the entire multiverse. As Barry and Iris come to terms with this inevitability, the rest of Team Flash are resolved to figure out a way to save both Barry and the multiverse. A new Wells then arrives on Earth-1, adventurer Harrison Nash Wells, looking for a rare substance known as eternium. Upon learning of the Flash’s impending death, Nash reveals he knows how to save Barry’s life, and thus begins tracking the mysterious Monitor. Meanwhile, a former colleague of Caitlin’s, Dr. Ramsey Rosso, begins searching for a cure for HLH, a rare medical condition that killed his mother and was currently killing him. After testing a possible cure made of dark matter on himself, Rosso develops metahuman abilities which allow him to turn people into zombie-like creatures which he can control. With his new powers, Rosso, now known as the villainous Bloodwork, begins trying to obtain more dark matter to not only finally cure his HLH, but to obtain more power and turn the entire city into his zombie slaves. During a fight with Team Flash, Bloodwork gets the upper hand on Ralph and begins draining his blood. When Barry saves Ralph’s life by giving him a blood transfusion, some of Rosso’s blood enters Barry’s bloodstream. With his metahuman powers, Rosso is able to infect Barry and learn all of his thoughts and memories, including his secret identity, and his impending death. Promising to give Barry enough power to survive the Crisis and save the multiverse, Rosso fully infects and corrupts Barry’s mind, drawing him to his villainous cause. As Bloodwork and the Flash attack STAR Labs to use the particle accelerator to spread Rosso’s blood throughout Central City, infecting all of its inhabitants, Barry’s mind manages to fight back against Rosso’s control. This helps Cisco and Iris devise a cure, releasing everyone, including Barry, from Bloodwork’s mind control. Furious that his plan failed, Rosso turns himself into a blood monster to enact revenge on Barry. Ultimately, the Flash prevails, defeating Bloodwork and imprisoning him. With Bloodwork defeated, the members of Team Flash come together to say their goodbyes as the Crisis event finally arrives. Nash finally finds the Monitor’s lair, where he hopes to learn from the being how to save Barry’s life. Instead, Nash discovers that he has actually been tricked by the villainous Anti-Monitor, the Monitor’s evil doppelganger. Mistakenly released from his prison, the Anti-Monitor releases powerful waves of anti-matter and an army of shadow demons that begin destroying countless parallel worlds in the multiverse. As the Crisis on Infinite Earths begins, the Monitor’s partner, Harbinger, forms a team of heroes to defeat the Anti-Monitor. The assembled heroes include the Flash, Green Arrow, White Canary, the Atom, Batwoman, and Superman. A version of the Flash from Earth-90 sacrifices himself during the battle to save the multiverse, thus fulfilling the prophecy. Unfortunately, Anti-Monitor still defeats the heroes, forcing them to retreat to the Vanishing Point outside of Time and Space as the entire multiverse is destroyed. In a final battle against the Anti-Monitor, the heroes defeat the villain. Nash helps create a bomb that shrinks the Anti-Monitor and banishes him to the microverse, while Oliver Queen sacrifices himself to restore the multiverse into a singular Earth, known as Earth-Prime. Only the heroes who saved the universe have memories of the Crisis and their formerly separate worlds, but they all agree to work together to protect this new world and to honor Oliver Queen’s memory. Following the Crisis, Team Flash attempts to move on in their new home world. The telepathic Cecile begins using her powers to legally represent wrongfully convicted metahumans. This leads her to helping a young metahuman named Allegra, who can control electromagnetic light. After being exonerated of her falsely accused crimes, Allegra joins Team Flash. Meanwhile, the various versions of Wells from throughout the multiverse all converge inside the mind of Nash. McCulloch Tech CEO Joseph Carver hires a team of metahuman assassins to thwart the investigation, and Iris is pulled into a mirror dimension where she finds Carver’s long lost wife, Eva McCulloch. Although Eva teams up with Iris to find a way out of the Mirror Dimension, she is secretly plotting a villainous plan of her own. Furious that her husband Carver has been turning her tech into weapons for the Black Hole terrorist group, Eva begins trapping humans in the Mirror Dimension and replacing them with Mirror versions that she can control. Eva creates mirror versions of Iris and Kamilla to infiltrate Team Flash, and a mirror version of CCPD Chief Singh to infiltrate the authorities. Eventually, Eva escapes the Mirror Dimension to enact her final revenge, leaving behind Iris to find and save Kamilla and Singh. In the real world, Eva convinces the Black Hole metahumans to betray Carver and align with her. As Team Flash grows closer to defeating Joseph Carver, Ralph meets and begins a relationship with a woman named Sue Dearborn, whose parents were being extorted by Black Hole. Sue then joins Team Flash in their fight against Eva’s metahuman and mirror army. In a final battle at McCulloch Tech, Barry and his allies fail at stopping Eva from murdering Carver and taking back full control of her company. Eva then frames Sue for Carver’s murder, forcing her and Ralph to go on the run. As the season comes to a close, Team Flash vow to find a way to rescue everyone that was still trapped in the Mirror Dimension. In season seven of The Flash, the Council of Wells figure out a way to create an Artificial Speed Force that would give Barry his powers back. Unfortunately, Nash has to sacrifice himself and all of the Wells in his head to power it. After Nash’s death, the original Earth-1 Harrison Wells is brought back to life, theorizing that the universe will always need a Wells. Barry regains his powers, but also gains speed thinking, allowing him to see every possible future outcome. This new power turns Barry cold and emotionless, prompting him to turn off the Artificial Speed Force and lose his powers again. Meanwhile, Eva discovers that she was in fact a mirror version of herself and that her real body had actually died in the particle accelerator explosion. This inspires her to form a new villainous plan, creating a mirror army to replace everyone in Central City. When Barry finally rescues Iris from the Mirror Dimension, she helps him revive the Speed Force with the power of love. Barry then convinces Eva to surrender, and she helps destroy her own mirror army and release all of her captives before returning to the Mirror Dimension. With Central City saved, Harrison Wells uses his new universe-given time powers to live in a time loop of the four years he spent with the love of his life, who had been murdered by Eobard Thawne. Godspeed had developed his speedster powers by taking the Velocity drug, but wanted his powers to be real and permanent, and so he unleashes an army of Godspeed clones on Central City in an effort to force Barry into giving him his power. text: So last night, I saw Ready or Not 2: Here I Come. And this was really fun. But I'm hearing a lot online that the movie can sometimes be hard to keep up with with all the new game rules, devil cult bylaws, character motivations, character deaths, and what Grace manages to pull off at the very end. So in this video, I just want to quickly go through the storyline of the film from beginning to end. And along the way, clear up any possible confusion about the game rules, council rules, the character deaths, the character motivations, and the entire ending. So let's get started. So, the first thing I want to do is very briefly give a little bit of background on the first film because I think it really helps to understand the setup in this second film. So in the first film, Grace marries Alex, who is a member of the Le Domas family. The Le Domases are part of a devil worshipping cult and have a deal with the devil, who is known in this film as Mr. Le Bail. And what the deal is is when someone marries into the family, they have to play one of several household games with the family. And the way they must choose this one game is by that new spouse drawing a card. However, the big catch is one of these games is deadly. If Grace draws the hide-and-seek card, which she sadly does, the game is she has to hide while the rest of the family tries to kill her. If she survives till dawn, every family member except Grace is punished by the devil Le Bail and their bodies all explode. But if they kill Grace by dawn, they're allowed to live on. But unfortunately for the Le Domas family, Grace manages to survive and therefore every remaining Le Domas family member at the end of that first movie blows up. So at the very end of that first movie on the steps of that property, the second movie picks right up from there. So starting the second movie all bloody, injured, and traumatized, Grace is taken to the hospital. And her sister Faith arrives as her emergency contact. All the while, we see a few individuals all over the world getting calls and texts about the death of the Le Domas family after Grace's hide-and-seek win. And soon enough, one of these people, specifically Bill Wilkinson, attacks Grace at the hospital. And right before he's about to deliver the final blow, his body just explodes, just like the Le Domases. And I'm going to hold off personally on explaining these opening scenes because I think it's better to wait until we get to the scene where all the families are in that one room at the manor. Because in that scene, everything gets tied together. So we also see this very rich and powerful old man named Chester, who can, for example, end a war in one quick phone call. And in his bed, his son and daughter pay him a visit. And what Chester tells them is the Le Domases have died after the hide-and-seek game with Grace. And therefore, his son and daughter need to kill him. So listening to their father, they suffocate him with a pillow. And again, if any of this seems confusing, the big explanation is coming within seconds. So in the next moment, Grace and Faith are caught at the hospital by a few mysterious people and are knocked out. And here is where many of the big questions get answered. So once Grace and Faith are woken, they're tied up and ball gagged in a room of this extravagant manor. And in the room is an attorney and four families, each with two to three members present. The unnamed attorney turns out to be the attorney for Le Bail, the devil himself. And he breaks down to the sisters and the movie audience as well why all of this is happening. So essentially, the family who Grace defeated in the first film, the Le Domases, are part of a much bigger organization. There are six different families that serve on a council for the devil Le Bail. And this council is basically a devil worshipping secret society that runs the world behind the scenes. These six families include the Le Domases, the Wands, the Al Caedas, the Rajins, the Wilkinsons, and the Danforths. And four out of those six families remain alive and are present at this meeting. Two of the families are dead. The Le Domases, of course, were blown up by Le Bail when they lost the hide-and-seek game in the first movie. And the Wilkinsons were blown up by Le Bail as well, as we saw in the beginning of this movie when Bill tried to kill Grace. And the reason why Le Bail blew up Bill and his whole family line is because Bill was breaking Le Bail's rules. He's not allowed to kill Grace yet. So as of now, we have these four remaining council families surrounding Grace and Faith. And the lawyer explains why the two sisters have been brought here. So basically, what the lawyer says is these four council families all have a seat on the council. But there's one seat that holds more power, the high seat. And currently, the Danforths own that seat. However, the big issue, and the reason for this whole movie really, is that there's a rule in Le Bail's bylaws where if any council family is defeated in a deadly hide-and-seek game, like the Le Domases were by Grace after her wedding, then the family with the high seat loses security of that seat and all council members will enter into a competition for that high seat. And the way they compete for the high seat is in another game of deadly hide-and-seek. It's pretty simple. Whoever kills Grace gets the high seat. But if Grace survives by dawn, Grace gets the high seat. And of course, as you would guess, Grace doesn't at all even want the high seat or any council seat for that matter. But sadly, she is forced to play and this time must also protect her sister along the way. So overall, this big meeting scene makes sense of the many mysterious things happening at the beginning of the film leading up to this scene. The council families were all thrilled because they get a shot at the high seat. Chester Danforth could end a war in one phone call because he had the high seat. And Chester as well demanded his son and daughter kill him so they now, as the highest in the family line, could be the ones to compete in retaining the family's position in the high seat. So after this meeting, the game officially starts. And because the Danforths are the most recent high seat holders, the game is hosted on their property and they actually get to compete with two hunters at once, unlike the other families who can only compete with one at one time. So as we see, all four families are on the chase. Ursula and Titus are shooting from a golf cart. Ignacio is sniping from a ledge. Viraj is swinging his blade. And Chen Xing is mysteriously holding back from afar. And we'll soon get into why. So soon enough, in the laundry room, the girls manage to burn Viraj to death in this industrial washing machine. And what happens when a competitor dies is the next family member in line takes their place. But Viraj's younger brother Madu is too scared to join. So he signs his title over to his wife Martina and therefore forces Martina to compete in his place. But once his wife enters the game, she just drives off, forfeiting her place in the game, but also taking all of Madu's fortune. So in a later scene, the girls escape into the bar. Chen Xing shows up and reveals a loophole. In this competition, if the one being chased agrees to marry into one of the council families, the whole competition ends and the two newlyweds take the high seat. So Chen Xing pitches that Grace marry her son Cheng Fu and therefore Grace and Faith's lives would be saved. But Grace refuses, claiming she wouldn't ever be part of such an organization. And when Ignacio suddenly appears with his gun in the midst of a three-way fight, Chen Xing's sword goes through the neck of Ignacio, killing him. And as part of the rules of the game, if a hunter kills another hunter, even by accident, they and their family die at the hands of Le Bail. Therefore, Chen Xing and Cheng Fu's bodies completely explode. So that leaves three more hunting families. And because Ignacio just died, his vengeful daughter Francesca, the ex-fiancée of Grace's ex-husband, subs in to hunt down Grace. And after a heated, emotional argument between the sisters, they split up. And Faith is quickly found by Titus to get brutally beaten out of his sadistic, wicked nature and many personal frustrations and insecurities. And when Ursula steps in, she convinces Titus to use Faith as bait for Grace to come to them. So after defeating Francesca in a vicious fight and hearing where Faith is, Grace comes prepared with a shotgun, finishing off Francesca, dodging the shots of her younger brother, and finally reaching Faith, Titus, and Ursula. Titus has Faith at gunpoint. But in order to save both her sister and herself, Grace offers to marry Titus, which as we learned from Chen Xing, ends the game. So in the final act of the film, Grace is getting ready for her wedding. And Ursula steps into the room for a quick word. And she basically tells Grace, Titus is bad news. He truly is, like I said before, twisted and sadistic. So she proposes that the two of them work together within their future together as a family to keep Titus in check as much as possible, essentially controlling him without him really knowing. But unbeknownst to Ursula, Titus was listening the whole time. And in retaliation, he breaks Ursula's neck, leaving her dead on the floor. But one very important thing he says to Grace in that moment is there are no rules in the cult about killing family members. That line will, of course, come back around very shortly. So the wedding begins. And after the two of them vow and kiss and sign their names, and Titus gets the high seat sigil ring, Grace suddenly grabs the blood pen and stabs Titus in the neck repeatedly. And just before he dies, Grace says, "There are no rules about killing family members." And Le Bail's attorney confirms this is true. And Grace is left with the sigil, the high seat, and the greatest level of power. And Grace receives confirmation from the lawyer that Grace can now do anything she wants. So, as you would guess, she forfeits her power and membership from the cult. And then the lawyer clarifies that the next person to have the ring on at dawn will take the high seat. But if no one is wearing it at dawn, Le Bail will not be happy. So, Grace just tosses the sigil ring in that goat corpse pit. And out of greed for that power, every cult member immediately dives right in, brutally wounding and killing one another, so much that when dawn strikes, no one ends up with the ring on their finger at all. And as the lawyer warned, Le Bail would not be happy. So, in classic Le Bail fashion, he explodes the body of every single person in that pit and in the cult, except for his lawyer. So, Grace, Faith, and the sacrificial goat all stare back at the aftermath, and in the blink of an eye, they get a nod of respect from Le Bail in fire and smoke, very similarly to the way Grace did at the end of the first film by the fireplace. So, in the end, the two sisters and their new goat walk out the gates of the Danforth property, and the film cuts to black. And just to be clear, I stuck around for any kind of post-credit or mid-credit scene, and there was nothing. So, yeah, I hope you enjoyed this quick little recap, and I hope it clears things up because the movie, while fun and funny, I can also admit is sometimes pretty complicated and tough to wrap your mind around in one viewing. text: Welcome to this chapterby chapter summary of Project Hail Mary by Andy Weir. Follow Ryland Grace, a lone astronaut who wakes up millions of miles from Earth with no memory and the survival of humanity resting on his shoulders. Thanks for listening. Let's begin. Chapter 1. In the near future, middle school science teacher and molecular biologist Dr. Ryland Grace wakes up in the dormatory of the Hail Mary interstellar spaceship. Experiencing total amnesia, Grace has no idea who or where he is and assumes he is in a high-tech hospital as he is connected to an IV, a catheter, and many sensors. Grace feels weak and groggy, but is otherwise in excellent physical condition and attempts to remove his IV. A computerized voice asks for his name, and robotic arms extend from the ceiling to reattach his IV and sedate him when he is unable to answer. Grace regains consciousness while being tended to by the robotic arms. He rolls off the bed to escape, ripping out his catheter in the process. A thin red line of blood causes a memory to flash through his mind. While eating at a San Francisco diner, Grace gets an email from an astronomy curiosities message board. Russian scientist Dr. Arena Petrova has discovered a faint but detectable line of infrared light emission stretching in an arc from the top of the sun to Venus. Grace explores the dormatory, dodging the robotic arms. He finds the desiccated corpses of a man and a woman in the other two beds, presumably long dead. Grace concludes that each of them was put into a coma and maintained by the robotic arms, but only he survived. Grace climbs to a hatch out of the dormatory, but falls from the ladder with exhaustion. The robotic arms catch him and return him to bed, where he falls asleep despite sensing a wrongness to how he fell. When Grace wakes up, the robotic arms bring him a tube of unexpectedly delicious food. Grace demands more, but the computer tells him that the food aotment for this meal has been met. Energized by the meal, Grace gets up and makes a toga with his bed sheet. The robotic arms allow him to climb through the hatch into a laboratory where the bolted down equipment reminds Grace that he is a scientist. Grace attempts to open another hatch and continue exploring, but the computer refuses to unlock it until he confirms his name, which he can't remember. He falls again and experiences the same sense of wrongness as before. Grace times how long it takes for a test tube to fall from the lab to the floor, remembering the formula for gravity easily. The test shows that gravity is 1.5 times stronger than it should be and Grace realizes that he is not on Earth. Chapter 2. A frightened Grace tries to think of other explanations for the heightened gravity. Grace makes a simple pendulum and uses physics to determine that he can't be on Earth, on another planet, or in a centrifuge because of how large the centrifuge would have to be and how fast it would have to spin to achieve 1.5gs. Wondering how he knows so much about space, Grace guesses that he works for NASA and has another memory flash. In the memory, Grace meets his friend Marissa, a government scientist, for dinner. Marissa is visibly upset and tells Grace that a Japanese solar probe has determined that the sun is getting exponentially dimmer at the same rate that the Prova line of infrared light emission is getting brighter. Although the probe caught the problem early, the Proval line is stealing energy from the sun. The dimming sun will cause a new ice age, crop failures, and mass starvation. The US president will announce the dilemma with other world leaders. The next day, back on the Hail Mary, Grace realizes that his mission is to solve the Prova problem and prevent the sun from dying. Grace sobs as he is flooded with memories of the other two crew members, now the corpses in the dormatory, and realizes that only he survived the suspended animation they were put in for the interstellar journey. The computer announces another meal time and Grace is again comforted by the food. Grace acclimates to the ship, requesting water from the computer and finding a zerog toilet that has been strangely modified for use in gravity. Attempting to remember something on purpose, Grace recalls a televised NASA live stream of Project Arklight funded jointly by the United States, the European Union, Russia, China, India, and Japan. Project Arklight was developed to determine the cause of the Prova problem by collecting samples and data from the Prova line near Venus. On TV, NASA scientists received the first data from the unmanned space probe Arkite. The images show black dots that look and move like microbes, suggesting that the Proval line may comprise an alien life form. Grace is pulled from this memory by the computer, warning him of an angular anomaly. But in order to find the control room and solve the problem, he has to remember his name to open the hatch out of the lab. Grace combs through the NASA live stream memory for clues and realizes that he is a junior high school science teacher from San Francisco. Chapter 3. Grace remembers a particular day teaching his science class. He's a popular teacher and his students enjoy his lightning round style quiz. After school, Eva Strat appears in his classroom. Formerly with the European Space Agency, Strat now leads the Prova Task Force, a secret international project to solve the Prova problem and save humanity. Strat has been granted absolute authority and total immunity by the United Nations. Strat informs Grace that he has been selected to evaluate the Provaline samples captured by the Arkite probe because of a paper he wrote when he was still a molecular biologist. The paper, an analysis of water-based assumptions and recalibration of expectations for evolutionary models, challenges the widely held Goldilock zone theory, which assumes that life is dependent on liquid water and can therefore exist only within a narrow temperature range. The controversial paper costs Grace his academic funding and he refuses the Prova task force assignment, claiming that he is happier now as a teacher. Later, FBI agents apprehend him at home and escort him to a secret laboratory. At the lab, Strat explains that the black dots seem to be a life form that is rapidly eating the sun, and so they can't be water-based, or else they would be destroyed by the sun's heat. Despite Grace's rejection from the field, he is still considered by other speculative extraterrestrial biology experts to be the most qualified to examine the samples. Strat leaves Grace to get to know his new lab and assignment. Having finally recalled his name, Grace unlocks the hatch to the Hail Mary's control room. The monitors show that the ship is traveling at a much higher velocity than expected, but Grace can't determine where he is headed. He recognizes the Hail Mary mission crest which includes the names of his crew mates Yao Lee Gier and Olesia Ilukina. Grace suppresses painful memories of his friends by trying to remember his first encounter with the Proval line samples instead. In his memory, Strat and an international military coalition watch from an observation room as Grace opens the sample capsule from the Arkite. The sample has been transported in a sealed container of non-reactive argon for safety. And the lab is also pumped full of argon, requiring Grace to wear a hazmat suit and an oxygen tank while working. Strat is impatient, but Grace determines very little at first. The black dots absorb X-rays, can't be vaporized, and are unaffected by temperature. By comparing the movement of the black dots to their infrared emissions, Grace hypothesizes that they consume energy and emit light as a method of propulsion. Grace concludes that the life form is an invasive species in Earth's solar system, consuming the sun exponentially as their population grows. Grace names the black dots astrophase from the Greek words for star eater. Back in the Hail Mary's control room, Grace realizes that the star on the monitor is rotating too quickly to be Earth's son and that he must be in another solar system. Chapter 4. Grace panics at the realization that he is in another solar system until he notices a monitor in the control room labeled Astroofage. Grace deduces that the Hail Mary is using Astrophase as fuel and recalls another memory from the secretrova task force lab. After days of unsuccessful experiments, Grace punctures an astrofage cell with a microscopic needle, killing it and destroying its light blocking properties. Grace tests the dead astrophase and discovers that it is mostly made up of water, but is able to survive by somehow maintaining a constant temperature of 96.41° C. Grace goes to the ship's supply room to find clothing, and the embroidered names on the crew uniforms help him to remember his crew mates personalities, the stern but reasonable Commander Yao and Alicia Ilukina, the mission's cheerful engineer. He gives Yao and Ilukina a space burial via the airlock in the control room. In flashback, Grace remembers his first day back, teaching after his secret experiments in the Prova task force lab. His students ask him to explain the Prova problem, which has become global news. Grace is astounded at how little his students parents have explained to them and compares the catastrophic potential of the astrofage infestation over the next 30 years to climate change. Grace panics as he imagines his students dying of hunger in a future that is far closer than they imagine it to be. He rushes back to the secret lab and demands to continue working with the remaining astroofage samples which are being divided among labs all over the world. Back on the Hail Mary, Grace discovers four beetle probes named John, Paul, George, and Ringo, which are designed to be sent back to Earth with findings from the mission. Grace discovers that he only has enough fuel for another 40 days, not nearly enough for the 4-year journey back to Earth, and that he is on a lethal one-way mission. Chapter 5. In Flashback, Grace recounts his own experiments on astrophase as scientists around the world race to learn about the extraterrestrial life form, which resembles single-sellled organisms on Earth. While trying to determine why they are attracted to Venus, Grace accidentally breeds more astrophase. He hypothesizes the entire astrophase life cycle. The astrophase gather energy from the sun, then use that energy to migrate to Venus, where the carbon dioxide rich atmosphere supports their asexual reproduction. And then the parent and daughter cells migrate back to the sun to repeat the cycle. Grace calls Strat to give her the news and she immediately has him escorted via several consecutive military helicopters and fighter jets to a Chinese aircraft carrier in the middle of the South China Sea. There, Strat has Grace report his findings to an international body of highlevel scientists and political operatives whom Strat has gathered for a mission called Project Hail Mary 89. Grace explains how he bred the astrophase and how astrophase could be bred on a large scale and enriched with energy. A Chinese scientist reports that her lab has reproduced Grace's results and Grace is hurried away to rest while the others continue the secret meeting. The next day, Grace meets with Strat, the Chinese scientist, Germany's Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Dmitri Karov, a Russian scientist. They explained that astrophase infestations have been found on all the stars close to Earth except for one. Tao Sadi Kulov has discovered that the astrophase store energy by converting it to mass and is designing an interstellar spaceship that uses astrophase as fuel to travel to Tao's SETI and learn why the star is not affected by astrophase. Grace is tasked with breeding enough astrophase for the journey and due to the dangerous amounts of energy that will be stored in them, more than an atomic bomb. All the work must take place on the aircraft carrier in the middle of the ocean. Chapter 6. Back in the present, Grace activates the Hail Mary's navigation system and learns that the journey will be complete in 5 days. Once the astrophase powered engine is turned off, Grace will be able to use the Prova scope to search for the signature infrared light emission of Astrophoge around Tai. Grace does the math and realizes that because of relativity, he has been traveling for 3 years while at least 13 years have passed on Earth. If Grace is able to successfully send the Beetle probes back, Earth will still have to survive a total of 26 years with a dimming sun. Grieving his crew mates and struggling with the psychological burden of bearing responsibility for the survival of the human race, Grace decides to familiarize himself as much as possible with the ship as a distraction. This powerful film portrays Amy's journey of recovery from alcoholism, exploring how unresolved childhood trauma can shape our adult behaviours. Amy's complex trauma, including emotional neglect, leads to issues like insecure attachment styles and rejection sensitivity, making it difficult for her to form stable relationships. Her addiction is a response to deep-seated pain, blunting her emotions and pushing her into self-sabotaging behaviours. Physically, trauma takes a toll on the body through substance abuse, and emotionally, it disconnects Amy from her true self. But "The Outrun" offers hope. It shows that reconnecting with nature, processing emotions, and addressing past trauma are key steps toward healing. Galactus accepts this offer, so Norin leaves Charla behind to fulfill his obligation and is transformed into a completely metallic man with a surfboard. In 2007, the Silver Surfer made his big screen debut in the film featuring his name. Rise of the Silver Surfer used CGI and the voice of Lawrence Fishburn to bring the surfer to life. But the famed monster actor Doug Jones wore a motion capture suit to help VFX artists make him move more naturally. Another world awaits. Let it be done quickly. The Silver Surfer appears in First Steps as well, but with an alternate universe twist. In the Fantastic Force reality, Charlabal was chosen to be the herald of Galactus over Norin Rad. It's not a totally unprecedented decision as Charla Bal becomes a surfer in the Earth X comic book universe, but it means that all bets are off as far as what to expect is concerned. Regardless of what happens, Ozark star Julia Garner is sure to give a memorable mocap performance. Pop quiz. Who's the most powerful member of Marvel's first family? Reed, Sue, Johnny, or Ben? Trick question. It's none of them. Franklin Richards, the son of Mr. Fantastic and the Invisible Woman, puts his parents, uncle, and godfather to shame. Some birds are more difficult than others, but Franklin's takes the cake. After a pregnant Sue falls sick, the men of the Fantastic 4 are forced to venture into the negative zone and acquire the cosmic control rod in order to keep mother and son alive. Franklin comes out okay, but the radiation that gave his parents their powers is passed down to him with dramatic effects. He's a mutant with extraordinary abilities that he doesn't quite know how to wield at first. If you're thinking that this sounds an awful lot like Jack Jack from The Incredibles, that's because Pixar's superhero family took major inspiration from Marvel's. In the comics Earth 616, Franklin has used his powers to subdue and control Galactus. But in the same universe in which Charlabal becomes Silver Surfer, Franklin actually becomes Galactus himself. After Reed kills the original Galactus, Franklin takes over in order to maintain cosmic balance. Franklin has never been portrayed in live action before as the earlier Fantastic 4 universes didn't last long enough to include him. In First Steps, he's played by, well, a baby, potentially multiple babies, considering typical child acting practices. Sue gives birth in space just in time for Galactus to show up and turn her parenting skills into a matter of life and death. You're going to be the best mom in the world and you are going to be the best dad. Just kidding. You are out of your death. We are going to be the best uncles ever. They say that in some movies the city itself is a character. So, let's take a look at the version of New York City that First Steps takes place in. The 1960s Fantastic 4 comics are set in a version of the Big Apple that's been shaped by the technology that geniuses like Reed Richards helped create. Rather than dragging the family into the present day, director Matt Shackman and his creative team decided to model their parallel universe after the original aesthetic. With a retro vibe and quirky gizmos abound, the setting of First Steps looks like Jack Kirby artwork that comes to life. Just like in the comics, the MCU Fantastic 4 are based in the Baxter building located in the heart of Manhattan. Once owned by the Leland Baxter Paper Company, it now serves as a headquarters for everything from scientific research to family dinner every Sunday. Several key pieces of technology used by the Fantastic 4 in the comics are present as well. Their vehicle, lovingly dubbed the Fantastic, is seen dodging traffic on the New York streets. And their robotic assistant, Herby, does an applauseworthy job cooking sauce. Okay. Okay. Is this guy good or what? Their retrofuturistic reality would be a great place to live if it wasn't marked for death. But hopefully the Fantastic 4 can do something about the big man touching down on their turf. This may be the Fantastic 4's first step into the MCU, but it definitely isn't their last. All four members are confirmed to appear in Avengers Doomsday in 2025, likely dragging them out of their home universe and into the continuity that they'd earlier managed to avoid. Spoiler alert for Thunderbolts or the new Avengers, whatever you want to call it. But that film's postredit scene shows a Fantastic 4 spaceship approaching Earth, likely after the events of First Steps take place. The Fantastic 4 will return, whether we like it or not. Of course, a team's break from fighting Dr. Doom was never going to last longer than one movie. As the name suggests, Victor von Doom is the main villain of Avengers Doomsday. And as the entire internet is aware, Robert Downey Jr. is playing him. In the comics, Reed and Victor are college rivals. But there's a good chance that Doomsday will change the nature of their relationship to something more multiversal. First Steps promises to be a fresh take on Marvel's original superhero team. Even though any sequels it gets won't be nearly as contained, it still promises plenty of exciting moments and a future for the Fantastic 4 that's full of possibilities. You'll just have to see it for yourself when it releases on July 25th. [Music]

text: Say your vows or when your Chuck Taylor All Stars and grab your crossbow. You can Google how to use it later. We're breaking down 2019 surprise horror hit Ready or Not. Obviously, major spoiler alert if you haven't seen the first movie. Ready or Not opens with a tracking shot of several board games. The tiles were all created for the film, but if you pay close attention, they actually give away the entire plot. What you need to know now though, is that the games are the basis for the Le Domas family or Dominion. >> Uh Dominion? We prefer Dominion. >> The Le Domas Dominion's vast wealth. They live in a giant mansion, which serves as a setting for both the current day story and this first scene flashback. Here we learn that the Le Domas's love a good game of hide and seek, especially on wedding nights. Brothers Daniel and Alex are running through the halls. They're scared. Are they being chased? We don't know. Daniel hides Alex in a wardrobe and turns around only to run directly into Charles, his Aunt Helene's new husband. Charles is begging him for help. He's been shot by an arrow. Daniel does what any young child would do in his position. >> HE'S IN HERE. >> AT that point, the rest of the Le Domas family converges into the scene wearing masks straight out of that one episode of The Twilight Zone. And while Helene pleads for them to stop, they shoot Charles with another arrow and drag him away. Here we meet Grace, our protagonist. It's her wedding day and she's clearly nervous, but she does give us some good exposition. >> His family is richer than God. And Dad definitely had drinking your alcoholic brother keep hitting on me. >> We learn that Grace and Alex have only been together for 18 months, much shorter than the family's expected three-year courtship. Grace is worried about being seen as a gold digger, but we know she's actually in it for love, which is bad news in this dominion. Alex clearly hates his family and Daniel, well, Daniel has his own opinions. >> It's not too late to flee, you know. You don't belong in this family. I mean that as a compliment. >> Daniel isn't the only one in favor of canceling the wedding. Alex tries to give Grace an out, but she's all the way in. >> I'm all the way in. >> At the wedding we're introduced to the rest of Alex's family, and they are just as awful as one would expect a board game Dominion richer than God to be. While Grace poses for photos, Alex and Daniel's father and current family patriarch Tony tells Daniel he thinks Alex could have done better. And we get another bit of important information that will come into play later on. >> You're just saying that because he's your favorite. >> Alex is the prodigal son returned after a 2-year absence, and his family really wants him to stay. They're also really concerned that Grace is not one of them. >> But she'll never be one of us. >> He's one of us. Is Grace? >> Also in attendance, Daniel's wife Charity. She's, according to Daniel, a gold-digging word that rhymes with bore. Aunt Helene is there, too, and as we'll discover, she's a little angry these days. Before the bells, Grace meets Becky, Tony's wife and Alex and Daniel's mother, who also wasn't thought to be good enough for the family. Not only does she have a very nice cigarette case, but she seems to like Grace and gives her some advice that will come in handy as the night wears on. >> Stand tall and >> And then there are maids number one, two, and three. They're not especially important here, but they are kind of terrifying. After the ceremony, Grace and Alex head back up to his former room, where Grace is hoping to consummate the marriage. Too bad for her, Aunt Helene exists. >> You'll have to hide better than that. >> Thanks for that foreshadowy entrance. We now know that there are secret doors throughout the house, which lead to a maze of servants' corridors. And we also find out that if Grace really wants to be a part of this family, she's going to have to participate in a wedding night ritual game. It could be any game. She doesn't have to win. She just has to play. Grace, assuming there's nothing more to this outside of just a general weirdness of having to play a random game at midnight instead of hooking up with her new husband, puts on her game face and heads to the music room. Downstairs, Tony tells Alex that he's sure Mr. Le Bail is with them today as they look on at an empty chair. Le Bail, by the way, can be read one of two ways, as an anagram for Belial, a demon often associated with the devil itself, or as a French word le bail, which means the lease or rental agreement. Tony wants to know how much Alex has told Grace about the family. And because we've seen just how sweet and loving Grace is, we already know the answer. >> Nothing. And I never will. >> Alex plans to leave with her the next day because, again, he hates his family. But you don't just leave the Le Domas dominion and Tony wants to be sure that Alex will be able to do what's necessary if Grace pulls that card. In the music room, beloved butler Stevens plays a butler's sonatina and we get a little backstory on Grace thanks to Becky. Grace was brought up in foster care. That's why family is such a big deal for her. While Alex would have been just fine living in sin forever, he knew how much it meant to Grace to be a part of a real permanent family. And Becky wants that for Grace, too. >> Finally, one of our children has brought home a good one. >> Becky also hopes that Grace will be able to convince Alex, the favorite child, to come back into the fold because as much as Alex hates his family, they kind of all hate each other more and it seems like the most hated family member is Daniel and Alex's fashionably late sister, Emily. >> Brown-haired niece, you continue to exist. >> And by extension, her husband, Fitch. No one likes that kids, Georgie and Gabe, either. Emily has a little bit of a drug problem, but Grace doesn't seem to mind, real family and all that. And in spite of Alex not feeling very well, maybe it's the creepy maids, the family moves into the study/game room, which, as Tony tells us, >> So this room is reserved for family members only. >> While the Le Domas says love a good board game, they also love their big game, as the obscenely wealthy do. So, while Grace is admiring the weapons and taxidermy on display, the rest of the family gather around their family members only table, and Tony gives us a family history lesson, in which he emphasizes both that the LeDomas says are big on tradition, and that >> You know, it's almost as if someone's watching over us. >> That someone is wealthy benefactor Mr. LeBail. Tony's great-grandfather, Victor, had been a merchant seaman, where he met Mr. LeBail on one of his excursions. Both of being lovers of games of chance, the two bonded over cards. But, Mr. LeBail had in his possession a mysterious box. >> Yo, WHAT'S IN THE BOX? >> If Victor could solve the puzzle of the box, Mr. LeBail would fund any endeavor of his. Victor, of course, does, and now anytime a new person joins a family, a blank playing card gets put in the box. >> And Mr. LeBail will tell us which game to play. >> Everyone is taking this really seriously, except for the other spouses. Charity says her game was chess. Fitch jokes that he got old maid. They're not thinking much about this tradition. And then there's Alex. Of course, because we wouldn't have a movie otherwise, Grace pulls a hide and seek card. Alex and Daniel both look like they're going to pass out. Becky looks genuinely sad, and Aunt Helene, she's just happy to be there. Before they get to playing, Alex tries to convince Grace to meet him in his room, but she says no. She's stoked to play. She even toasts to good old Mr. LeBail before the hiding and seeking begins. Tony breaks down the rules for Grace. It's pretty standard. She can hide anywhere in the house, they count to 100, and then they go and find her. She wins if she lasts the night. Grace asks about the security system, but don't worry. Remember, the LeDomas says are big on tradition, and traditionally, security systems were not in play. Neither were modern weapons, but we'll get to those. As Grace goes off to hide, Stevens puts the hide-and-seek song on the gramophone to really set the mood. >> Who wants to play a game? It's time for hide-and-seek. >> And the family gets armed with weapons from great-grandfather Victor's time, because tradition. Grace is a little tipsy, but feeling good, and she decides to hide in the literal most obvious spot, the dumbwaiter. While all of this is going on, maid number one reads Georgie and Gabe a bedtime story. It's actually a passage from Milton's Paradise Lost, the better to reign in hell than serve in heaven bit, spoken by Satan. Sweet, right? Alex wants no part of this whole hide-and-seek fiasco, so Becky suggests he just hang out while they go take care of the killing business, and then has Charity watch the door. They've apparently forgotten about those servants' corridors, but not Alex. He bails immediately. The family is out looking for Grace, not in the obvious dumbwaiter, and doing a little bonding. >> You know I've never liked you, right? >> Grace is bored by this point, so she decides to leave her hiding spot, but her dress gets caught. It's the first tear in this fabric metaphor. Because she can't get very far, Alex grabs her and pulls her into a bedroom. He's got some explaining to do, but Grace still thinks she's just playing a game. That is until maid number one, who'd fallen asleep mid-Milton, wakes up to find Georgie has disappeared. So, she sets out to track him down. Maybe not the smartest thing, letting unaccompanied minors wander a giant mansion while everyone else is heavily armed, but who are we to judge the rich? Maid number one checks the room Alex and Grace are hiding in, but she stops when she hears something break in the hallway. That something turns out to be a coat-out, trigger-happy Emily. >> Why'd you shoot her in the face, sweetheart? You're supposed to maim her. She needs to be alive for the ritual. >> Grace is freaking out. It's about time, but she has to keep quiet while Becky, Tony, and Aunt Helene work out disposing of the body. >> Slippery little pig. >> Why she was my favorite. >> Alex gets in go mode. He's standing Grace up, figuring out phones, trying to get her out of there. Grace, however, is a little shell-shocked, and the best explanation Alex can come up with is >> You pulled the one bad card. >> Not one to let a little thing like an accidental maid maiming get her down, Emily gives herself a pep talk before heading back out to do more maiming. In the corridors, Grace loses it. Alex finally tells her that his family thinks if she isn't killed, something very bad will happen to them. If you don't play, you die. He's not like that, though. He was just playing along so he could get her out, but he also kinds of blames her for the situation she's in. >> You brought me here. You didn't warn me. >> You wanted to get married. >> Regardless, he convinces Grace to head for the kitchen while he works on disabling the security system. He also gets her to change into a pair of Chuck Taylor All Stars, a much more appropriate choice of footwear for outrunning killer board game dominions, richer than God. Unfortunately, all of this arguing is overheard by Fitch, who stepped away from the hunt to heed nature's call and watch how-to crossbow videos. Fortunately, he doesn't seem to care. Grace makes her way toward the kitchen, but this dress is really not working for her. So, she does what anyone would do in her situation and tears the bottom off for better mobility. Because this house is enormous and the corridors are confusing, Grace doesn't know which door leads into the kitchen and accidentally takes the wrong one, but she runs into Daniel, Tony, Aunt Helene, and maid number one. Emily rounds the corner, sees what's happening, and does what SHE DOES BEST. >> JESUS! GOD DAMN IT, EMILY! >> GRACE TAKES THE OPPORTUNITY to escape and ends up in a billiards room, where she again has to hide and again runs into Daniel. But Daniel's not feeling especially meme-y at the moment. >> I just came to get a drink. >> He tells Grace that he has to call the others, but he does offer to give her a 10-second head start, which he makes one of the longest 10 seconds ever, and we, the audience, start to wonder if he isn't such a bad guy after all. Once the family is alerted, Charity finds a way into the room and tells Daniel how she really feels about him. >> You're pathetic. >> Daniel isn't worried about having let Grace get away, because he has faith in his soulless family. He's also come to realize just how much Charity fits in with that soullessness, but she's not about to go back to where she came from. >> I'd rather be dead than lose all of this. >> The family reconvenes to figure out what to do next. Emily, in her drug-fueled mania, has lost her gun, so Fitch offers her his crossbow. You can see where this is going. >> Mr. LaDomas, Mr. LaDomas, I just SAW HER RUN. >> OH MY GOD! >> WITH MAID NUMBER two down, but not quite out, Fitch takes Emily to find an edible so she can even out a little bit, and Charity asks if killing the help counts. Aunt Alena is sick of this line of questioning. She's also sick of these maids not actually dying when Emily shoots them, so she finishes off number two herself. >> OH, WHAT THE [ __ ] >> BECKY SUGGESTS TURNING THE SECURITY cameras back on, and Tony's all for it, because great-grandfather Victor would have used them if they were available back in his day. They still can't use modern weapons, though, because, again, tradition. But what about those Twilight Zone masks, you might be wondering? That was Tony's dad's idea. >> It's the '80s. >> Grace winds up back in the study/game room and grabs great-grandfather Victor's antique hunting rifle and ammo off the wall. Because if you have to survive a killer board game the minion richer than God, then you're going to have to even the playing field. Meanwhile, Alex makes it to the security room, but can't seem to figure out how power buttons work. And Grace finally gets to the kitchen, but she too runs into an issue. Well, a couple of issues. Steven just wants a little snack, because sacrificial cleanup works up an appetite. He's in good spirits though, and whistling his favorite tune, Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture. We get a couple of close calls here, while Grace works on loading the gun. And just when you think she may have figured out how to get out of the house, Steven drops some predictably bad news on her. >> The ammunition is display only. >> That's okay though, because there's always hot tea. Alex does figure out the security system, but getting it up and running tips off Tony and Daniel, who now have to take a detour from the hunt to stop him. But by the time they get there, Alex has taken an extinguisher to the controls. He wrestles Tony down, and then begs Daniel to help him get Grace out, which he agrees to do. Right before Tony knocks Alex out from behind. So Grace is back wandering the halls, and she decides that the best place to hide, again, is the dumbwaiter. Found Uncle Charles. She does get out, but it's not a good time. And she is not happy with Georgie. Charity's on a smoke break when Grace runs by. So, she takes a shot, but hits a bird instead. She just has to get through that fence, but this isn't one of those neighborhoods. >> You piece of [ __ ] little tiny liquor get it out of my >> So, Grace is back to running. At least some of them are. Daniel's ready to go, but Tony puts his foot down. The LaDomas says are not the first family to have made such a pact. Another family, the Van Horns, all died in a house fire after going back on their deal with Mr. LaBail. So, Becky sends Fitch and Charity, who's way more into this than she should be, to go wait for Stevens, but she won't let Emily go too, because she doesn't want to lose any more of the help. Emily and Daniel are relegated to clean up duty for the F-ups, which means taking the maids to the goat pit. And at this point, Grace is hiding in the woods. Alex is trying to saw his handcuffs through the bed frame, and Emily and Daniel are dealing with the maid situation. Daniel suggests they all deserve to die, but Emily thinks their kids deserve to live. Do they though? And Daniel finally seems to realize just how messed up his family is. Grace is still going, but she's caught by Stevens.
