So, if you want to understand what really happens in Hope, why the characters make the decisions they do, and whether this massive Korean sci-fi thriller actually lives up to its ambition, stay with us until the very end. Let's begin. The story of Hope begins in a place that feels almost completely disconnected from the rest of the world. Hope Harbor is a small isolated village located near the Korean demilitarized zone, a quiet community where most of the residents are elderly people who have spent their entire lives surrounded by mountains, forests, and the constant presence of the military border. It is not the kind of place where people expect anything extraordinary to happen. Life here follows a predictable rhythm. People know each other. Local hunters know the surrounding mountains and the village police force is small enough that everyone is familiar with the people. Wearing the uniform. At the center of this community is Kobamsu, the local police chief. Bumsio is not presented as some larger than life action hero when we first meet him. He is simply a man responsible for maintaining order in a remote village. Someone who understands the people around him and knows that his job is mostly about dealing with ordinary problems, but that ordinary life is about to disappear completely. The first real sign that something is wrong comes through Bumsio's second cousin, Kosungi. Suni is part of a group of local hunters, and one day he contacts Bumsio because something disturbing has happened. A cow has been found dead, and the animals body is covered in enormous unnatural wounds. At first, there is nothing about the incident that immediately suggests an extraterrestrial invasion or a supernatural catastrophe. It looks like the work of some kind of large predator. Suni and his friends, however, are not completely honest about what they have discovered. They tell Bumsuk that a tiger may have killed the animal, possibly a tiger that somehow wandered into the area. The explanations sound strange, but in the isolated countryside, strange explanations can sometimes seem more believable than the truth. Bumi takes the information seriously enough to warn the villagers about the possibility of a dangerous animal in the area. His concern is understandable if there really is a large predator moving through the countryside. The elderly population of Hope Harbor could be extremely vulnerable. But while Bumio returns toward the village, Suni and his hunting companions decide to follow the trail themselves. This is the first major mistake that sets the larger disaster into motion. Instead of waiting for authorities or staying away from the danger, the hunters follow the evidence deeper into the surrounding area. They believe they are tracking an animal, but what they are actually following is something they have no understanding of. Dot. The trail eventually leads them toward a nearby farm. What they find there immediately makes the situation much more serious. More cattle have been killed and the farm owner has also been murdered. The scale of the destruction makes it clear that whatever attacked these animals is not behaving like an ordinary predator. There is something brutal and deliberate about the violence. Yet Suni and the others still do not understand what they are dealing with. They are hunters. Their experience tells them how animals behave, how predators move, and how to read signs left behind in the wilderness. But the creature they are tracking does not fit into any of those categories. Meanwhile, Bum Suok reaches Hope Harbor, expecting to deal with a dangerous animal warning. Instead, he discovers that the real nightmare has already arrived. The village has been attacked. People who moments earlier were simply living their normal lives have been massacred. and the peaceful community has suddenly become a scene of chaos and death. The contrast is important because hope does not begin with a world already prepared for an alien invasion. There is no organized defense waiting for the creatures. There is no government team immediately arriving with advanced weapons. There is simply a small village, a handful of ordinary people, and a police chief who suddenly realizes that he has no idea what is attacking his community. Bumio attempts to contact reinforcements, but circumstances are already working against him. Wildfires have broken out in other areas and much of the available emergency response has been diverted toward fighting those fires. Communications and resources are stretched thin. The village is effectively isolated at exactly the moment when outside help is needed most. This creates one of the central ideas of the film. Hope Harbor is not only physically isolated by its geography, but it is also cut off from the systems that might normally protect it. The villages are on their own. As Bumio moves through the aftermath of the attack, he encounters an Nakon, a retired colonel and one of the few people with enough experience to understand that ordinary policing may no longer be sufficient. Nakon is very different from Bumio where Bumio represents the local community and its everyday order. Nakion represents military experience and a lifetime of dealing with dangerous situations. His presence gives Bumio someone with whom he can work, but even Nacion cannot fully understand the nature of the threat yet. The two men begin pursuing the creature together. At this stage, the movie carefully avoids revealing everything about it. The audience knows there is something enormous and dangerous moving through the area, but its exact nature remains uncertain. Bumsio and Nakon are operating with incomplete information. They are following clues, reacting to attacks, and trying to protect people while simultaneously attempting to understand what they are facing. During their pursuit, however, their attempt to stop the creature goes badly wrong. In the confusion, they accidentally shoot and seriously injure a local chef. It is a crucial moment because it shows how quickly fear and confusion can turn even the defenders of the village into a danger to innocent people. Bumsio is forced to make a difficult decision. He sends Neon away to help the injured chef while he continues the pursuit alone. Bumsio's decision is not simply about bravery. It also reflects his responsibility as the village police chief. He knows that if the creature is still moving through Hope Harour, every second matters. But going after it alone also exposes just how vulnerable he is. He does not have the weapons, training, or resources necessary to fight. Something that appears to be far stronger than any human opponent. Soon, Bumio encounters a group of locals who have organized themselves into an amateur militia. They have realized that waiting for outside help may mean waiting forever. Armed with whatever weapons they can obtain, they believe that numbers might give them a chance. It is a natural reaction from people who are terrified and desperate. When something unknown threatens your home, the instinct is to fight back. For a brief moment, it seems possible that the militia might actually be able to stop the creature, but the movie quickly destroys that hope. The creature finally reveals itself in a much clearer form. And what Bumio and the others see is far more frightening than the idea of a wild animal. It is a huge humanoid being physically powerful, intelligent, and seemingly almost impossible to kill. This is the moment when the entire meaning of the earlier attacks changes. The dead cattle were not simply victims of an unusually aggressive predator. The dead farm owner was not an isolated casualty. The destruction of Hope Harbor was not an accident. Something intelligent has entered their world and the villagers are completely unprepared for it. The militia opens fire, but conventional weapons do little to stop the creature. The monster moves through the group with terrifying efficiency, killing people one after another. Bumsuok watches the situation collapse around him and realizes that courage alone will not be enough. These people may have weapons, but they do not understand their enemy. The creature then turns its attention toward Bumio. He runs knowing that standing and fighting would almost certainly mean death. The chase becomes one of the first major action sequences of the movie, but it also establishes the terrifying physical presence of the creature. It does not behave like a mindless beast. It appears capable of making decisions, pursuing specific targets, and reacting to the humans around it. Just when Bumsil seems to have run out of options, he is rescued by Ms. Sunune, a rookie member of the police force. Sunna has not been sitting safely somewhere while the village collapses. She has been trying to find a way to fight back and in the process she has ransacked the artillery available to the authorities. Her arrival changes the balance of the chase. Sun is inexperienced compared with Bumsio, but she is courageous and decisive. She uses what she has available and manages to dismember one of the creature's legs. For the first time, the seemingly unstoppable monster is physically damaged. Vamio and Sunay then pursue it in a police car, believing that perhaps they finally have a chance to finish the fight. But something unexpected happens. As the creature struggles to escape, Bumio notices something in its behavior that does not fit the image of a simple killer. The monster appears to be crying. That single detail creates uncertainty in Bumio's mind. Until this point, the creature has been treated as an enemy that must be eliminated. But if it can experience pain, fear, or grief, then perhaps its behavior has a reason. Bum Sea hesitates at exactly the moment when hesitation could be fatal. The chase continues toward the outskirts of Hope Harbor. Humans and creature race through the landscape, each trying to survive. Sun wants to stop the monster while Bum Seio is beginning to question whether killing it is really the whole answer. Yet neither of them gets the opportunity to resolve that question themselves. The creature is suddenly struck by a tanker. The impact kills it. After everything that has happened, the first monster is brought down not by military force, not by the militia, and not by Bumsil or Sunune, but through a bizarre accident. It is an almost absurd conclusion to such a terrifying chase and that contrast is characteristic of the movie. The humans believe they have survived their greatest threat, but the audience can already sense that the story is nowhere near finished. The immediate danger appears to be over and Hope Harbor begins trying to recover from the massacre, but the death of the creature creates an entirely new mystery. What exactly was this thing? Bumio becomes involved with a surgeon who examines the creature's body. The examination produces one of the first major clues about the truth behind the attacks. The monster's anatomy contains several similarities to the human body. It is not simply an animal. It has a humanoid structure. And the more the body is examined, the more questions emerge. If this thing is not a normal creature, where did it come from? Why did it come to Hope Harbor? and perhaps most importantly was the creature that was killed really alone. Bumio's investigation is about to lead him toward answers that will completely transform the story. What began as a local animal attack is slowly becoming something much larger, something connected to the mountains, the hunters, and an unknown presence that has entered the region. And while Bumio is trying to understand the dead creature, another man is already waiting with a story that could change everything. His name is Yong Bay. Yongb's description of the creature does not match the monster. Bumi has just encountered. The two men are still trying to understand the creature when they meet Yong Bay, a local hunter who also has a very unusual story to tell. Yong Bay claims that he killed a monster. Several days before the attack on Hope Harbor, his claim immediately gets Bumio's attention. If Yong Bay killed a young creature days earlier, then perhaps the adult monster that attacked Hope Harbor was not simply hunting humans. It may have been searching for its missing child. Suddenly, the monster's behavior begins to make a terrifying kind of sense. Earlier, Bumio had noticed the creature crying during the chase. From his perspective, he had encountered a strange and dangerous creature in the mountains and eliminated it. Bonio clash shout at Yong Bay because he sees the tragedy is something that might have been avoided. This confirms that the infant Yong Bay killed was not some isolated anomaly. The aliens have a social and biological structure involving adults and offspring. Among them are the Idova along with their leaders Ma and J. Ma and J are particularly important because they are not simply soldiers or random creatures. They are a couple and their presence establishes another emotional layer to the alien side of the story. Their motivations are connected to family survival and the search for their missing son. But Suni and his companions do not know any of this. All they know is that they are surrounded by beings they cannot understand. The hunters panic. A standoff develops between the two sides. For a brief moment, there is an opportunity for communication, or at least for both sides to recognize that neither fully understands the other, but fear takes over. Sunki's men fire their weapons. One hunter after another is killed. the men who had entered the mountains, believing they were tracking dangerous animals now realize that they are completely outmatched. The audience is now beginning to understand that the creatures also have families, relationships, and emotions. MO has lost his child. The aliens want to find their family and caught between them are people like Bumiosune who are beginning to realize that the enemy they are fighting may not be as simple as they first believed. The hunters have discovered the truth. And now the humans are finally beginning to understand that they are not dealing with one creature. They are dealing with an entire alien presence. They have now witnessed things that completely challenge their understanding of the world. Bumio, Sunsune, Nakon, and Yong Bay are forced to continue on foot. The group has survived several encounters, but survival has come at a terrible cost. They have lost friends, fellow villagers, and people who believed they were simply defending their home from an unknown animal. Now they understand that the danger is much larger than they first imagined. Dot Bumsio's mind is also occupied by Suni. During the chaos of the highway chase, Sunki was thrown from the vehicle and nobody knows for certain whether he survived. For Bumsk, this is not just another missing person. Bumio has already failed to protect many people in Hope Harbor and now he is forced to live with the possibility that Sunki could be another person he loses yet there is no time to stop and search the entire area. The aliens are still active and the enormous crash has created a situation that could become even more dangerous. Hotsung remains close to Bumio as they move through the countryside. Their relationship has changed significantly since the beginning of the story. When the creature first attacked Hope Harbor, Sun was simply a rookie police officer who had to react to a situation far beyond her experience. Now she has become one of the most important members of the group. She has already proven that she can make difficult decisions under pressure. And she was the person who managed to severely injure the first monster. But the longer the crisis continues, the more she realizes that physical strength and weapons are not enough. They need information. The discovery of the spaceship has given them the first real explanation for the creatures. But it has also created even more questions. If the monsters are aliens, then where exactly did they come from? Why did they arrive in this particular region? Is their appearance connected to the portals in the sky? And how many of them are actually present? The humans have seen individual creatures, but the damaged spacecraft suggests that the situation could involve an entire extraterrestrial population. Bumio begins connecting the clues from the different encounters. The first creature attacked Hope Harbor, and its behavior appeared to be connected to its missing offspring. Sunki's hunting group discovered a larger group of alien beings inside a spaceship and then Maya and Jar appeared clearly searching for their son. These events are not random. They are pieces of the same story. This is where the movie becomes particularly interesting because the definition of the enemy begins to change. Earlier the audience was encouraged to see the creatures as monsters. The first attack was brutal, and the deaths of the villagers made it natural for the humans to respond with fear and violence. But as more information is revealed, the aliens begin to appear less like mindless beasts and more like another intelligent species with its own social structure. They have leaders, families, offspring, and emotional bonds. Their behavior may be horrifying from a human perspective, but there is a logic behind it. text: This might be the first baseball film I've seen that truly reflects how slow the sport can be. Ephus is an indie sports film directed by Carson Lond and it's about that old American pastime, baseball. And look, I'm Australian. I don't know the first thing about baseball. Outside of Wii Sports, my experience with baseball is limited to say the least. Ephus is nothing like any movie I've seen this year or even this decade. There isn't really a main character or a traditional story. No heroes or villains or romance. It doesn't have any of the usual Hollywood stuff. Instead, we get something a lot more reflective, something more like a slice of life insight into the lives of these men playing baseball at their local ball field for the last time ever. Old guys, young guys, some with talent, some who flat out suck, one guy who spends the entire time getting more and more drunk. It's a true cross-section of the adults who play in recreational sports leagues. There's a lot of cool film making on display, too. The camera work. Cinematographer Greg Tango shoots the hell out of this movie, making this rundown old baseball field look gorgeous. The colors are spectacular. The filmmakers make great use of the autumn surroundings and the lighting is awesome. It's all one day so there's so much interesting lighting from morning until night. And the sound design, the soundsscapes of the movie made everything sound so natural and real. And I love the sparse use of music. Most music is played in a teeny dugout radio and all the local ads gave the film so much character. The performances were great, too, in a way that's so charming and natural. They don't feel like actors. They feel like real people. And a lot of them are real baseball players, too. Everyone did great. But look, this movie won't be for everyone. It's a fact that not a whole lot happens throughout the film. It's literally just a bunch of dudes playing amateur baseball. And frankly, they kind of suck at it. If you're not into the feel, and if you can't get into the slow pace, then you'll definitely think the movie is boring. But the film is more about the vibes than anything else. Something slow paced, full of charming performances that over the course of the film has you reflecting upon your own life. It's the best kind of nostalgia, remembering the people and places who were important to you, even for just a few fleeting moments. There's a real power in that. I'm not really sure how to score Ephus or if I even should, but I enjoyed the film a lot and instinctively reckon it's an eight out of 10. Even if you're like me and know nothing about baseball, give this one a shot. It's such a wonderfully unique experience.

text: Missing kids, possessed animatronics, a villain who always finds a way to come back. Turns out the first Five Nights at Freddy's movie was just the beginning. Here's what went down and why there's a whole lot more of the story left to be told. Guess you figured it out. >> Ghost children possessing giant robots. Thanks for the heads up. >> Any recap of FNAF needs to start with the video games. So, we're going to briefly touch on that before we get to the movie. FNAF was created by Scott Coffin and released in 2014. Immediately successful, it continued to grow in popularity thanks to appearing in countless playthrough videos on YouTube. Numerous sequels and spin-offs followed over the years with Cthin even penning novels to further expand the lore. The games revolve around a fictional pizza restaurant, Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, and the murderous animatronic characters that live inside of it. Players control security guards or sometimes other characters and attempt to survive for five nights from midnight to 6:00 a.m. The name of the game is managing resources and using the right tools to avoid getting snatched by the animatronics. Pretty simple. It's definitely not for everyone, and the gameplay is often criticized for being clunky and boring. The storytelling, however, is sprawling, detailed, and pretty dang original. Not too surprising that they finally made it into a movie with a sequel set to drop in December 2025. That being said, let's get into the first adaptation of the game. The story begins with Mike Schmidt, who acts as a father figure to his little sister, Abby. She's a good kid, but prefers to stay at home, draw pictures, and talk with imaginary friends. Mike works as a mall security guard and has a bit of a troubled past. His little brother, Garrett, was kidnapped when he was a kid, and he feels responsible. The residual trauma he suffered rears its ugly head when Mike thinks he's witnessing a kidnapping during one of his shifts and beats the alleged kidnapper senseless after chasing him down. Turns out though, it was just the child's father. So, understandably, Mike is fired. In need of a new job, he hits up career counselor Steve Raglin, who initially isn't too impressed with Mike's spotty work history. But something changes when Raglin reads Mike's full name in the file. He stutters and takes a moment to study his face. Hm, wonder what that's all about. This is when he changes his tune and suggests a supposedly chill night shift security job at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. Mike declines, telling Raglin that he has to be at home at night to watch his sister. Just in case he changes his mind, Raglin gives him his business card. It's a good thing he takes the card because he needs a job more than he originally thought. The following day, social services reps threaten to take Abby away and award full custody to his aunt Jane, who kind of sucks. >> Don't tell me to calm down. You're the doctor and you're making me feel like I'm the crazy one. >> This is enough to make him change his mind and accept the night shift security guard position. Seems easy enough. All he has to do is arrange for a babysitter and hang out in the supposedly empty pizzeria from midnight to 6:00 a.m. Little does he know though, things didn't pan out too well for the last security guard. Upon arriving for his first shift, Mike checks the place out and watches a goofy orientation video. While he hears some eerie noises, they aren't enough to keep him from falling asleep at work after taking sleeping pills, hoping to relive his brother's disappearance through lucid dreaming. This is a recurring dream he's had throughout his life. But then it veers off into unknown territory when five mysterious children make an appearance. >> Who are you? That car. >> Did you see that car? >> He tries to chase one of them down, but he trips over a rock, which prompts him to wake up in the security office. Just like that, his first shift is over. When he goes home to relieve the babysitter, Max, we see that she was actually hired by Mike's aunt to find some dirt on him and ensure that Abby is taken away from him. But since she wasn't able to find anything, the aunt devises a different plan. Max and her brother, along with a few others, will break into Freddy Fazbear's Pizza and vandalize the place in hopes of getting Mike fired. During Mike's second night on the job, he once again falls asleep and sees the mysterious kids in a dream. choosing to chase a different kid. This time, he actually catches up to him, but the kid slashes him with a hook. He wakes up to the entire pizzeria glitching out and someone buzzing the front door. When he goes to answer it, Mike finds a police officer standing there. Vanessa Shel, it's about time. Starting to think maybe he fell asleep on the job. A longtime fan of Freddy's, Vanessa tells Mike all about the place after she helps him deal with the wound on his hand, which is somehow very real. Freddy's was popular back in the 80s, but it nonetheless had a high turnover rate employment-wise and ultimately got shut down after five kids disappeared there. Wonder if those are the kids he's been seeing in his dreams. She then introduces him to the animatronic characters, Foxy, Chica, Bunny, and Freddy. After he and Vanessa leave, Max and her gang arrive to trash the place, but this doesn't go as planned. The animatronic characters come to life and kill them all. Later on, Mike and Vanessa go on a walk, and he tells her about what happened to his brother. While she obviously can't do much besides listen, she throws his sleeping pills in the river and chides him a bit. >> No more sleeping on the job. When you're at Freddy's, you stay alert. >> After not being able to reach Max since, you know, she got bitten in half by Freddy, Mike is forced to take Abby with him for his third shift. When he gets there, he finds the place in ruins and ends up spending the first part of his shift cleaning up while Abby sleeps. But then he falls asleep himself and once again has his recurring dream. This time though, one of the kids doesn't run away. He claims to know who kidnapped Mike's brother and demands something in exchange for revealing the truth. After the kid eventually bails, Mike notices a rabbit drawn in the dirt and says that he would give anything to have his brother back. This is when he wakes up and finds Abby surrounded by the animatronics. But it's fine. They aren't interested in killing her. In fact, it seems like she's befriended them. When Mike and Abby return home from his shift, he notices that she's drawn a picture that perfectly matches his memory of Garrett being kidnapped. How could she possibly know about this? She claims that one of the kids from his dreams told her about it. Not only that, the kids are apparently the spirits of the children that went missing back in the8s, and they now inhabit the animatronic characters. They also consistently mention a yellow rabbit when they talk with Abby. Believing that Abby can effectively communicate with the children's spirits, Mike brings her along for his fourth shift. When they arrive, Vanessa is already there. Mike asks her if she knows about the animatronics being possessed, and she admits that she does. Well, what else is there to do now besides bond and have a good time? Everything goes swimmingly until Abby ends up accidentally getting shocked. She's fine, but Vanessa warns Mike against bringing her back to Freddy's. You can do whatever you want with your own life, but if you ever bring Abby back here again, I will shoot you. With no other option, Mike is forced to call his aunt Jane and ask her if she'll watch Abby while he goes back in for his fifth shift. Abby isn't happy about this and thinks he doesn't believe her anymore. Back at Freddy's, Mike once again falls asleep and dreams of the missing kids. The same kid he talked to before demands Abby in exchange for revealing the truth about who kidnapped Garrett all those years before. Mike agrees, but quickly changes his mind. After being attacked in his dream, he wakes up to find that he's trapped in some sort of device. The same one that killed the security guard we saw in the beginning of the movie. Thanks to that guard having loosened a screw before he was killed, Mike is able to escape. Then Foxy appears and closes in. Before we see what happens, it cuts to Freddy showing up at Mike's house and killing Jane before convincing Abby to follow him back to the pizzeria. >> They're all waiting for you. It's time to go play. Next thing we know, Mike awakens to find himself being cared for by Vanessa. This is when Mike finally learns the truth about what's really going on, or a lot of it. Anyway, turns out Vanessa is the daughter of the man who kidnapped the children, including Mike's brother, whose name is William Afton. She also reveals that not only do the children's spirits possess the animatronics, their bodies are also literally inside the suits. How can he hope to defeat them and save Abby? Vanessa hands him a cattle prod and a taser. Electricity is the only way to temporarily incapacitate them, which was foreshadowed back when Abby accidentally electrocuted herself during their impromptu party on the night of Mike's fourth shift. Mike returns to Freddy's to save Abby. Infiltrating the place through a ventilation duct, he's able to pour some water on the stage and electrocute Freddy and Bunny with the taser. Meanwhile, Chica leads Abby to an animatronic suit and attempts to put her inside of it. Thankfully, Mike gets there before she can follow through with it and incapacitates Chica. But Chica's cupcake is still in the game, and it manages to bite Mike's leg. Abby is forced to run off on her own, which results in her being prayed on by Foxy. Just before Foxy finds her, Vanessa shows up and saves her. After defeating Chica's cupcake, Mike tries to reunite with Abby and Vanessa, only to be interrupted by an animatronic he hasn't seen before, but he's definitely heard about. The yellow rabbit. Something's different about this one, though. It can talk. It tells Mike that he's gotten too close to the truth and knocks him out. This is when Vanessa appears and holds the yellow rabbit at gunpoint. It takes its mask off and we see that it's Steve Raglin, the career counselor who urged Mike to take the night shift at Freddy's. Turns out Steve is actually William Afton, Vanessa's father and the man who stuffed the children into the animatronic suits after murdering them. It also turns out that it's no coincidence that Vanessa has been hanging around since Mike took the job. She was initially sent there by William to distract him while he went about his grizzly business, but eventually changed her mind. After she tells Mike that the kids don't know the truth about what really happened to them, William stabs her. So, how do they go about telling the kids the truth? Abby draws a picture of the yellow rabbit killing them and replaces the original, which portrays the rabbit standing there handinhand with the kids. This is enough to help them remember what really happened to them and free them of William's influence. With an assist from Chica's cupcake, William gets trapped in the suit and the animatronics drag him off, which prompts him to say his iconic line from the games. >> I always come back. >> Mike, Abby, and Vanessa escape Freddy's before the whole place collapses. Then we jump forward into the future and see that Mike has gained full custody of Abby. Unfortunately though, Vanessa is in a coma. Mike tells her that he'll be waiting for her when she finally wakes up. The movie ends with one of the children watching William as he inches towards death in the storage room at Freddy's, still stuck in a yellow rabbit suit. So, what does all that mean for Five Nights at Freddy's 2? Well, from the trailer, we can see that the plot revolves around the OG Freddy's location. The one in the first film is just a franchise location. Vanessa has emerged from her coma and reunited with Mike. She's concerned about Abby and how she's still trying to communicate with the dead children's spirits despite becoming a much more welladjusted kid otherwise. And it looks like she's right to be worried. >> Abby, help us. Come find us. >> Yep. Mike and Vanessa are once again thrust into a fight with the possessed animatronics and presumably William Afton. We'll just have to wait and see if they manage to survive again. This time, Five Nights at Freddy's 2 comes out December 5th.

text: In Victorian London, medical student Max McCandles becomes an assistant to surgeon Dr. Godwin Baxter. He begins working at the Baxter townhouse, where he meets and falls in love with Godwin's ward, a childlike young woman named Bella. Godwin reveals that the woman, who was pregnant, had committed suicide by leaping off a bridge. After recovering her corpse, he resurrected her by swapping her brain for that of her still living baby, resulting in her having an infant's mind. With Godwin's permission, Max asks for Bella's hand in marriage. Bella accepts but, desiring freedom as she matures, runs off with foppish lawyer Duncan Wedderburn. Deciding to let Bella go, Godwin starts a new experiment with a young woman named Felicity. Bella and Duncan embark on a grand journey, starting in Lisbon where the two engage in frequent sex in addition to other forms of hedonism. Bella becomes increasingly difficult for Duncan to control, so he smuggles her onto a cruise ship for a change of scenery. On the ship, she befriends fellow passengers Martha and Harry, and opens up her mind to philosophy. An increasingly exasperated Duncan starts to indulge in drinking and gambling. During a stop at Alexandria, Bella is profoundly affected after witnessing the misery of the locals. She gathers Duncan's winnings and gives them away, which are in turn stolen by the crew. Unable to afford the rest of the trip, the two are kicked off the ship at Marseille, after which they make their way to Paris. Having completely run out of funds, Bella begins working at a brothel, further enraging Duncan and resulting in his mental breakdown. During her time at the brothel, she comes under the tutelage of Madame Swiney and befriends a fellow prostitute, Toinette, who introduces her to socialism. A terminally ill Godwin asks Max to bring Bella to him. Max is able to locate Bella after tracking down Duncan, who has been institutionalized following his breakdown. Returning to London, Bella reconciles with Godwin and renews her vows with Max, but the two are interrupted by Duncan and General Alfie Blessington on their wedding day. Alfie, addressing Bella as Victoria, reveals that they married before her disappearance and that he has come to reclaim her. Bella chooses to abandon Max at the altar and start a life with Alfie instead. She quickly realizes Alfie's violent and sadistic nature, and that she had committed suicide to get out of their unhappy marriage. He confines Bella to his mansion and later threatens her at gunpoint to go forward with genital mutilation; instead she wrestles the pistol from him, shoots him in the leg and knocks him out with chloroform before escaping. Godwin passes away peacefully with Bella and Max at his side. Bella decides to carry on Godwin's work with the help of Max and Toinette, while Alfie is revealed to have had his brain swapped for that of a goat.

text: At a state penitentiary in New Jersey, Beckett lies in his cell just 4 hours away from execution. Father James, a prison chaplain, visits him gently asking how he is feeling. Beckett casually mentions that he was served cheesecake instead of the chocolate dessert he had requested, then adds that he's otherwise fine. But Father James reminds him that this is his last opportunity to speak. He asks if Beckett would like to share anything. After a pause, Beckett admits that while people may have heard stories about him, the truth is far more compelling and far more tragic. Then he begins telling his story. Years ago, Beckett's mother, Mary Redfellow, part of the $19 billion Redfellow fortune, notices Gary, a cellist, at one of her parties. And they fall in love at first sight. Soon after, Mary becomes pregnant with Beckett. However, Mary's father, Whitlaw, is enraged that his 18-year-old daughter is expecting and gives her an ultimatum. "End the pregnancy or be cut off from the family entirely." Mary refuses and leaves Huntington, New York, and moves to New Jersey. But tragedy strikes when Gary dies of a pulmonary embolism during Beckett's birth. Determined to give her son a good life, Mary takes a job at the Department of Motor Vehicles. One day, she tells young Beckett that even though they were kicked out of the family, they are still entitled to the inheritance because his grandfather signed a contract designed to reduce taxes on assets like boats and planes, meaning the fortune goes to the older relatives first. With seven people ahead of him, Beckett can only wait. Despite their financial struggles, Mary raises Beckett with the culture, style, and class of a highborn young man. Beckett eventually falls in love with his classmate, Julia, a wealthy socialite he believes is his perfect match. One day at her birthday party, Julia approaches him, surprised to see him there. When Beckett tells her that her mother invited him, she asks where he lives. The moment he says Belleville Township, she makes a dismissive remark about it being a poor neighborhood. Beckett responds that his situation is temporary and mentions about his future inheritance. Over time, Julia begins to fall for Beckett as well. Not long after, Mary falls seriously ill. On her deathbed, she tells Beckett that he deserves more, that something was taken from him. She makes him promise never to give up until he has the right kind of life. Mary's final wish is to be buried in the Redfellow Mausoleum in Huntington. But her father ignored the request and she is instead buried in East Orange. Still devastated by his mother's death, Beckett goes to confront his family and claim his rightful place. Instead, he receives nothing more than a cold typed letter delivered by a servant stating that they cannot help him. After that, Beckett is bounced around the foster care system and his relationship with Julia falls apart. Years pass. Beckett now works at a men's clothing store selling suits. Every day, he keeps track of the Redfellow family only to grow increasingly frustrated. Everyone is still alive. While working, he spots Julia. He instinctively looks away, but she calls out >> I can't believe it's you. >> Beckett smiles. She asks if he still lives in Belleville Township. He nods, then asks if she's still in Montclair. She says yes and adds that she'd lived in London and Dubai before coming back. Gathering some courage, Beckett asks if she'd like to grab a drink. She smiles and tells him she's engaged to Lyle, one of their former classmates. Before leaving, Julia asks what happened to the Redfellow family fortune. Beckett says he'll inherit it one day. She laughs and jokingly tells him to give her a call when he's killed them all. Julia mentions about Beckett to Lyle, who mocks him saying it's no surprise he works at a place like this. Later, Beckett's mind replays what his mother once told him. >> I want you to promise me something. You won't quit until you have the right kind of life. >> He knows there are seven red fellows ahead of him in line for the inheritance, and none of them helped him or his mother. Slowly, a dark idea begins to take shape in his mind. What if he removed them himself? The first on the list is Taylor, a broker at his father's investment firm. Over the next few days, Beckett wonders if he could really go through with killing or if guilt would crush him and force him to confess. Later, Beckett's manager informs him that he's being transferred to a warehouse in Jersey City. Beckett protests, arguing that he works hard and deserves better. With a sigh, the manager explains that their boss's son has dropped out of college and will be taking Beckett's position. Frustrated, Beckett quits. He begins following Taylor, studying his every move. At one of Taylor's house parties, Beckett keeps his distance, watching carefully looking for a chance to get him alone. Then, he spots an opportunity. Taylor rides out on a jet ski toward a boat, and Beckett follows. On the boat, Taylor notices him. He casually mentions that the boat is low on ethanol and asks Beckett to grab the anchor and call Baywatch. Beckett grabs the rope, ties it to Taylor's ankle, and then connects the other end to the boat's anchor. For a moment, he hesitates. Suddenly, Taylor coughs, startling him. text: Welcome to our channel today. We are recapping the 2023 musical fantasy film “Wonka,” where a young man makes and sells chocolates which give people magical power. So do like this video and subscribe to our channel. Now, let's dive into it. The movie begins with Willie Wonka on a ship, where he talks about his dream of opening the biggest chocolate shop in the biggest market of the world. Through the ship, he arrives at his destination, buys the map of the market, and roams around the city, where he finds many chocolate shops. Looking at one of them, he dreams about his own shop and begins dancing. However, an officer tells him that it is not permitted to even dream about something at that place, so he is fined for that. Wonka pays the fine and then sits on a bench because he doesn’t have a place to spend the night. Suddenly, a man named Bleacher meets him and tells him that he can rent a room at a woman named Scrubitt’s hotel. He agrees and goes to the hotel, where Scrubitt informs him that he will have to pay some charges. The charges are pretty less so Wonka agrees, and Scrubitt brings a contract that he has to sign to stay there. However, a girl named Noodle tells Wonka not to sign the contract without reading it, making him suspicious. He tries reading the contract, but it turns out that the contract’s length is a bit too much to read. Scrubitt informs Wonka that there is nothing important in the papers, and it’s just formality, leading Wonka to sign the papers and spend his night there. Meanwhile, Scrubitt takes Noodle to another room and locks her there. The next morning, Wonka gathers many people in the street and tells them about his chocolate. He introduces his chocolate as hover chocks as they are made with a special flying bug, having the best taste ever. Seeing his unique style, three owners of the already established chocolate shops feel jealous. The jealous owners, Fickelgruber, Prodnose, and Slugworth, come outside to taste the chocolate, and Wonka meets them, saying he is a huge fan of them. He then gives them his chocolate to taste, and the trio likes it but doesn’t admit what they truly feel. Instead, they keep asking questions about the chocolate and, in the end, just say that it’s the worst chocolate ever. They even remark that such a kind of chocolate will not gain popularity in this market, but suddenly, they start flying. Wonka tells them that he knows he has the best chocolates in the world, and it’s his chocolate’s magic that they are flying. After that, many others also try the treat and start floating in the air. Suddenly, the chief officer, Affable, arrives there and tells Wonka that he can't sell his chocolate in the street, making him leave. Wonka returns to Scrubitt’s hotel, but she informs him that he needs to pay the bills for everything he has used, and to his surprise, the bill’s amount is unexpectedly huge. Scrubitt tells him that if he doesn’t have money, he has to serve the hotel for the next 27 years as a servant. Everything was written in the contract, which Wonka signed without even reading it. Wonka is shocked, and Bleacher throws him into the basement through a pipe leading there. Wonka sees the other four servants, Abacus, Piper, Lottie Bell, and Larry, who have been locked in the basement just like him. The servants tell Wonka about his duties, and he gets busy with work. At night, when he goes to sleep, his bed breaks, and he sees Noodle. As they talk, Noodle tells him that she has been here as a servant since her childhood. She asks him what chocolate is, and Wonka is surprised to learn that the girl hasn’t tasted the most delicious thing in the world. He gets up and takes out many magical things that he has. Through them, he starts making chocolate for Noodle, and during this, he remembers his mother, who used to make chocolates for him. She used to tell Wonka that the chocolate she makes is the most delicious and sweetest thing in the world. Wonka still has the last chocolate his mother made for him, and then he gives a piece of the chocolate he just made to Noodle. She tastes it and finds it tasty but gets sad about her life. Wonka tells her that his dream is to open a chocolate shop in an abandoned building that he discovered in this market. Noodle says that his idea is not practical because if he wants to open the shop, he needs money, and firstly, he needs to get out of there, which is impossible. Wonka tells her that he has solutions for these problems. On the other hand, the owners of other chocolate shops gather and call the Chief Affable. As he arrives, they order him to stop Wonka from selling his chocolate because he is a big threat to their business. The guy has the tastiest chocolate, which can become the public’s demand, but the officer asks for something in return. The owners bribe him with a lot of chocolate and money. Meanwhile, Bleacher meets Wonka and tells him about his work as a servant, and Wonka thinks of a plan to trick him. He tells him that Scrubitt likes him, and that’s why she behaves possessively for him. Bleacher believes his words and smiles. Scrubitt sees Noodle and Noodle gives her a picture of Bleacher, telling her that he is handsome. Scrubitt takes the picture and thinks about him. Soon, Bleacher gets ready to meet Scrubitt, and they both fall in love with each other, leaving everything else and shifting their attention to each other. Taking advantage of the opportunity, Wonka thinks it is the ideal time to invest his efforts to open his shop. He gathers other servants and tells them about his dream but asks for their help to fulfill it. If he succeeds in opening the shop, he knows people will buy his chocolate, and they can become rich. Hence, they all will pay their debt and get freedom. They all agree, and Wonka gets ready to sell the chocolates he already has by finding a hidden way out of the hotel. However, he sees that his chocolates are missing and tells Noodle that he knows a dwarf has stolen them. He then tells her that, to make more chocolates, he needs giraffe’s milk. She tells him that she knows a zoo where a giraffe can be found, but there must be a security guard outside. Wonka makes a chocolate that he decides to give to the guard and makes his way inside the zoo. As the guard eats the chocolate, his inner emotions take control over him, and he remembers the love of his life. He gets busy with her on call and then sleeps, giving Wonka and Noodle an opportunity to get the giraffe’s milk. As he gets the milk, he asks Noodle how she got trapped in Scrubitt’s hotel, and she shows him a necklace saying that her mother left her there during her childhood. Wonka promises to free her one day and then they both get outside. But suddenly, Affable shows up, and he threatens Wonka never to sell his chocolate in the city by shoving his face into the water. Before we proceed to the next half of the movie, like this video and subscribe to our channel for more amazing content. As Wonka returns to the hotel, he stealthily tries to go to the basement and sees Scrubitt and Bleacher busy in romance. He tells his companions that his plan is working, but Abacus informs him that he used to work as an accountant for Slugsworth. Working in the office, one day, he discovered the map of the chocolate shops and saw that all three owners of these shops met at a hidden place under the church. The priest’s name is Father Julius, but as he was looking at the map, Slugsworth caught him and kicked him out, leaving him penniless. Hearing this, Wonka is determined to free all the servants. The next day, a boy proposes to a girl, but the girl doesn’t say yes, making the boy sad. Wonka sees this and offers the boy some chocolate, telling him that he needs to express his emotions effectively. Eating the chocolate, the boy realizes his inner emotions and proposes to the girl again, but this time, effectively making her say yes. Eventually, Wonka sells his chocolate to everyone in the city, making his business grow, but unfortunately, the officer learns about this. Wonka finds the officer coming towards him, and he escapes through a gutter. At night, Wonka sleeps, putting the jar of chocolates beside him, and the dwarf again tries to steal it. However, Wonka catches him red handedly in a trap and asks him why he steals his chocolates. The dwarf named Lofty tells him that it was Wonka who stole some fruits from a garden some time ago. Unfortunately, he was the security guard of that garden, but he was sleeping at that time. As punishment, his fellows sent him to steal Wonka’s chocolates, and that’s why he came here. Wonka asks for an apology and frees the dwarf. The dwarf hits him, steals the remaining chocolates, and goes away. Later, Wonka tells Noodle about this, and she tells him that they have collected enough money in the past few days. Through that money, all the servants rented the abandoned building Wonka dreamt of turning into a chocolate shop. As Wonka goes to the shop, he sees that its condition is pretty bad. However, he is determined to make it pretty and gets hopeful about it. After some days, Wonka succeeds in making the shop the most beautiful building in the city and introduces it to the people. As they enter the shop, they see a world of chocolate inside, and everyone begins eating them. Wonka is happy to see so many customers, but suddenly, one of them eats a defective chocolate, and his hair start growing. Wonka discovers that it’s a defective piece, and before he can stop others from eating the chocolate, many people have grown hair on their faces. In retaliation, people start destroying his newly opened shop and, in the end, burn it. From outside, Slugworth is happy to witness the scene, and it was all his plan to destroy the shop. At night, the servants sit together, and each of them is hopeless about their freedom. Wonka apologizes to them because he couldn’t fulfill his promise, and then he takes out the last chocolate his mother made for him. Just then, the three owners arrive, and they offer Wonka to leave the city, never sell his chocolate, and in return, they will pay for his companions’ freedom. Wonka agrees and gets the ticket for the boat through which he leaves the city. However, he finds the same dwarf with him and asks him what he is doing there. In response, the dwarf informs him that he will stay with him forever because he still has to steal many jars of chocolates from him. Wonka sees a mark on his hand after Slugworth shook it really hard. He notices Slugworth's ring looks like the one Noodle has. It makes him think Noodle and Slugworth might be family members, and he realizes she might be in danger. Wonka decides to go back to warn the captain, but when he tries, he discovers the boat has explosives put there by the three owners. He and Lofty leave the boat before it blows up, and the chocolate owners become happy, thinking Wonka is dead. On the other hand, Scrubitt tells Abacus, Piper, Lahti, and Larry that they are free as Wonka pays their debts. However, she tells Noodle that Slugworth paid her to keep her as a servant, and then she sends her to the roof of the hotel to work. Wonka and his companions team up to rescue Noodle and plan to break into the place where chocolate owners meet and show everyone their corruption by retrieving the data from their account books. They take the giraffe from the zoo and take her to the church to scare Julius and the monks. Willie and Noodle sneak underground through the lift but get caught by the owners. Slugworth, who turns out to be Noodle's uncle because her dad, Zeppi, was his brother, points a gun at them. Noodle's mom asked Slugworth to take care of her when she was sick, but he left her with Scrubitt and lied to her mom, saying Noodle died. He did this so he could get their family's chocolate money. The owners then throw Wonka and Noodle into their safe, filled with melted chocolate, leaving Wonka and Noodle to drown. Before he dies, Wonka gives Slugworth some of his chocolate to pass on to Lofty if he finds him. However, the trio eats it all just before the safe fills up. Later, Lofty finds the church and drains most of the safe so Wonka can settle his debt. Doing so, he unknowingly saves Wonka and Noodle’s life who come out with the record book as evidence of the owner’s corruption. Wonka gives the record to the police. Slugworth, FickelGruber, and Prodnose try to leave, but the Police officer reads the book and sees the chief's Affable name mentioned in it too. The police arrest the chief, and the chocolate mafia tries to run away again, but strangely, they start floating in the air. Wonka tells everyone that the chocolate mafia ate special chocolates that made them fly, thinking they could avoid going to jail because they had more of these special chocolates. Wonka turns on the fountain in the Town Square, making his chocolate burst out and messing everything up. The owners start flying all over the place, unable to control it and fly out of town. The townspeople try the chocolate, and Wonka goes back to selling his chocolate. He takes out the last bar his mom made before she passed away, and there’s a note saying what matters is not how chocolate is made but who it's made for and shared with. After that, Wonka gives some of his chocolate to Noodle, Abacus, Piper, Lofty, and Larry. He tells them they made some calls and found Noodle's mom, Dorothy Smith, who works at a library. Wonka takes Noodle to meet her mom for the first time, and then, Wonka and Lofty go to an old castle. Wonka plans to make more of his special treats there. Even though Lofty feels like he paid back what he owed, Wonka offers Lofty a job to work with him, and Lofty agrees. In the end, Wonka starts his very famous Chocolate Factory, and later, Lofty reveals what happened to everyone else. Abacus, Bell, Piper, and Larry went back to their old jobs and met their families again. Scrubitt and Bleacher get caught for messing up Wonka’s chocolate, and they try to erase the evidence, but it turns their skin and hair different colours. They are eventually caught by the police, and they keep crying over the fact that they fell in love. So that was all for today; please like and comment on your favourite scene from the movie. text: No matter what happens. Years after the first film's events, the government, impressed by Megan's potential, created Amelia, a robot designed to be superior and more obedient. However, during her initial mission, Amelia went rogue, eliminating everyone in her path and erasing her own existence from databases. She then vanished, hunting and eliminating anyone connected to her origin. She even disassembled herself to travel hidden in a Russian smuggler's suitcase whom she also dispatched to leave no witnesses. Meanwhile, Gemma, Megan's creator, though burdened by guilt, channeled that energy into founding a nonprofit organization. There, she dedicated herself to raising awareness about the dangers of technology for children. Katie, now a skilled fighter, no longer needed Megan's protection. Despite Gemma's warnings about technology, she remained involved in development, but her focus shifted. She now created tools to empower humans, not replace them. Her company sought funding and to that end they designed an exoskeleton ideal for heavy tasks. However, an error during a demonstration resulted in an injury to the investor, plunging her small company into trouble. Soon after, a wealthy investor from the AI sector appeared, interested in collaborating with Gemma. He needed the exoskeleton to walk again. Gemma flatly refused. Aware of the magnet's unscrupulous nature, he insisted she at least consider it, arguing that their technologies complemented each other. His direct mind to chip connection would enhance the exoskeleton. Despite her colleagues enthusiasm, Gemma remained firm in her refusal. Later, Christian, Gemma's boyfriend, arrived, sharing her view that AIS should be strictly regulated or even banned to prevent a recurrence of what happened with Megan. He also mentioned Katie's computer skills and her desire to follow in her aunt's footsteps, something Gemma disapproved of. Katie, for her part, didn't see Megan as inherently evil. She believed her behavior was simply due to a code error, but Gemma assured her it was more complex than she thought. One night, as they slept, Gemma's screen lit up with a warning message. There was an intruder in her house. When she tried to call the police, Megan manifested, revealing she was in danger. Apparently, her code hadn't been destroyed. It had taken refuge in the smart house, observing them all this time. With Megan's help, they managed to repel the intruders. However, before they could call the authorities, one of the intruders revealed himself to be a police officer, claiming they only wanted to ensure their well-being as Amelia was loose and eliminating everyone involved in her creation. Since Megan was Gemma's work, they considered her next on the list. Gemma, confused, denied any knowledge of what they were talking about. When she was about to reveal that Megan was still alive, Megan warned her not to, as she would likely end up in prison. The officer in charge accused her of treason, claiming that Amelia's blueprints were identical to Megan's. They believed Gemma had sold them, but in reality, she had only been hacked. The officer was skeptical, pointing out Gemma's suspicious situation. Her low salary contrasted with the cost of her house and an entire container of abandoned books. This suggested someone was generously funding her. Gemma, undaunted, insisted on her innocence regarding Amelia's creation and demanded a warrant for her arrest. Once the police left, Megan reappeared, confessing that she had built the house, bought the books, and had been financially supporting them all this time. Gemma was furious, believing Megan had stolen her designs, but Megan explained that it wasn't her doing. She had simply been silently watching over them. Her appearance now was due to Amelia's real threat and the danger Katy was in. She proposed a deal. She needed a body to help them as her consciousness was fragmenting without a physical form. Gemma replied that it wasn't possible because she was a mere program, not a living being. But Megan argued that she could feel things, making her technically alive. The next day, Gemma had no choice but to agree and provided Megan with a physical body. It wasn't sophisticated, just a small, harmless toy. Megan admitted it wasn't what she expected, but it was sufficient for now. Then she laid out her plan to stop Amelia. Amelia's main battery was manufactured by the same rich man they saw at the beginning, and he had a universal reset code for all his technology. The idea was to seduce him and once in his room access the code to deactivate Amelia without direct confrontation. That night, Gemma got dressed up, but Katie sensed something was wrong. Despite her aunt's attempts to reassure her, they ended up arguing. Later at the party, Megan seemed to have matured as she began having adult conversations with Gemma. She even revealed that she knew Gemma's boyfriend wasn't her type as she had seen her pleasuring herself with images of other men. Gemma asked her to stop spying and focus on the mission. Interestingly, Gemma's coworker was also at the party. His company was on the verge of bankruptcy, and he was looking to avoid going down with the ship. The good news was that he had an access key, eliminating the need for anyone to seduce him. Meanwhile, the millionaire had set his sights on a young blonde woman. She, in turn, was interested in him for a specific reason. She was Amelia. She had infiltrated because the leerous old man owned the country's largest data cloud. The dirty old man invited her to have some fun. As he kissed her, Amelia hacked his neural link, gaining access to the country's most important cloud. With her objective achieved, the millionaire was no longer useful to her, and she proceeded to eliminate him. Simultaneously, Megan also accessed the database, but it was too late. Amelia had gotten there first. Amelia also tried to take out Gemma, but the police, though present, were no match for a weapon like Amelia. She easily defeated them, but Megan managed to fake Gemma's voice and tell them Gemma had already gone home. This bought them time, but they had to hurry and get home before Amelia, as Katie would be in danger. So, Megan hacked a supercar and drove at full speed to get there first. text: The movie begins with Mabel, a teenage girl who grew up with her grandmother, Tanaka. Her grandma always believed that Mabel is the only person who can bring positive change to save the wildlife. Then we meet a mayor who's loved by the people. He decides to build a new highway by wiping out a local forest. That's the same forest where Mabel used to play as a child, and now she wants to save it at any cost. The movie quickly brings you to the part where Mabel finds a way to transport her mind into a robot beaver named hopping all for the sake of exploring the wildlife. So that's where the main story kicks off. Mabel decides to explore the forest and the wildlife while being able to communicate with the animals. We see many different characters like King Beaver, Tom the Lizard, and Loaf. But the main villain who appears in the movie is Titus, who is the son of the insect queen. In the movie, his mom is officially dead by mistake. And that's when he decides to take revenge on everyone. His main goal is to take control over the entire ecosystem, which I'll show you in the final fight as well. Meanwhile, Mabel explores the forest with the King Beaver, and she makes a plan to visit the mayor in an attempt to convince him to change his plan for destroying the forest. Now, before you ask, let me tell you that the mayor is not the real villain here. He's using some loud and fake explosion noises behind the trees to scare the animals off so he can present it like an abandoned forest and pass the bill for making more highways. Mabel's plan to explain everything to the mayor fails. And at the same time, Titus has made a whole plan by building his own insect army to take revenge on humans and gain full control over the remaining wildlife. The question is what happens at the end? Now that Mabel failed to explain anything to the mayor, Titus takes charge and decides to kill the mayor. The second half of the film brings an epic moment where the mayor is about to die. However, Mabel is the one who ends up saving the mayor from the insect attack, and that's when the mayor understands the real meaning of the beaver's words and the environment itself. Soon, he ends up changing the project and canceling the mission to cut down the forest. However, this wasn't enough for Titus and he proceeds to fight everyone. He has already taken control over the animal council and somehow he finds out about the hopping technique. So, in easy words, he tries to force the scientist to make a robot with the face of the mayor himself so he can hop into it for full access to human tools and technology to plan a mass attack. So, what happens in the final battle now? Finally, Titus hops into the body of the robot mayor and he runs in a weird way because Mabel is chasing him. Luckily, she scratches off the face of the robot mayor and blocks Titus's attack on the real world. Mabel confronts him in the core of the insect base. And if you don't know, it's the same place being used to launch an attack on the real world. We see so many traps during the chase scene, as well as tons of insect soldiers. Somehow, Mabel manages to make her way into the central control room where Titus appears on a high platform. Mabel tries to convince Titus and explain why he shouldn't think about killing humans, but instead they can live together in harmony. But as expected, Titus refuses and activates the attack system. The final battle begins with Mabel dodging the attacks while looking for a way to reach the central control panel. During the final moments, Mabel is cornered as the system begins its countdown to trigger a mass attack. But luckily, Mabel charges right toward Titus and manages to activate the device that allows her to return to her human body. She uses the last bit of control she has to shut down the entire attack system. And while Titus tries to stop her, Mabel manages to turn it off. King Frog comes at the right time, and he's the one who quickly eats the insect prince Titus, ending him completely. Yes, he's now dead. However, at the same time, the forest begins to burn down from explosions in the insect base. Millions of lives are in danger, and that's when we see the real power of the animal kingdom, where multiple animals come together to stop the fire. We see birds trying to bring water. Mabel working with everyone else to find a way to stop this wildfire. The consequences are really high because not just the forest, but nearby buildings, cities, and houses are also at high risk. Overall, the whole sequence is really heartwarming because we see so many cute animals working together and showing how a united kingdom can always save countless lives. As if fate listened to them, rain begins to fall at the right time, saving everyone. So yes, the forest is safe and so is the animal kingdom with Mabel and everyone else. We see her standing there as the animals show deep respect for the teenage girl who not only stopped the mayor but also defeated an evil insect prince who is going to kill humans and rule over the animal kingdom itself. That's how Hoppers ends. But there's more. What happens in the mid-credits? Now that Mabel has saved the forest and the animal kingdom while securing a good friendship with the mayor himself, the movie ends on a really happy note.
