Krypto joyfully jumps on him, although Superman is no longer able to move, and with barely any strength, begs his faithful companion to take him back home. It's then that we see that Superman's suit once again sports the classic red underwear integrated into its design. Just as Superman requested, Krypto guides him back home. Thus, the icy surface cracks and the Fortress of Solitude emerges imposingly with its characteristic ice castle and the iconic letter S on the door. Immediately, Superman's robots come to his aid. Although Superman thanks them, the robots respond that they are completely devoid of consciousness and were designed only to serve. So his thanks are meaningless to them. To reassure him while he recovers, the robots project a message from his biological parents. In the recording, they explain that they sent him from Krypton to Earth to save him and express that they love him more than heaven and earth combined, placing all their hope in him. However, the transmission is abruptly interrupted as only half of the message remains intact. The other half was lost or damaged during the journey to Earth. The robots report that Superman has 14 broken bones as well as damage to his kidney, liver, and bladder. They consider it essential to expose him to an intense dose of solar radiation to fully restore him. Therefore, they bring him directly into sunlight to speed his recovery. At the same time, we meet Angela Espa, a human meta tracking Superman in Antarctic. although she informs her team that she has been unable to locate him so far. Meanwhile, in the Fortress of Solitude, Superman tells his robots that he wants to return to combat. However, the robots warn him that he has barely reached 85% recovery. Despite this, Superman ignores the warnings and prepares to resume the fight. In parallel, we see Luther, who is also Angela's boss, directing his team with the goal of defeating Superman using every resource at his disposal. It is then that Baravia's hammer appears, delivering a violent blow to Superman, leaving him defenseless on the ground. It seems as if he knows Superman's every maneuver in advance. At that critical moment, a civilian named Malik Ali, who had once offered Superman food, approaches and helps him up. However, Lex Luthther quickly identifies the civilian. For her part, Angela follows Superman's tracks to the Fortress of Solitude and manages to spot him, although she barely catches a glimpse of him before he disappears. Luther, in turn, manages to observe him from his office thanks to the installed cameras. Baravia's hammer sentences Superman, proclaiming that this will be his last battle. Seeing Superman lying on the ground, the crowd begins to mock him. Meanwhile, we discover that Baravia's hammer arrives at the Luther Corporation facilities, revealing itself to be a powerful robot known as Ultra Man, who had only been posing as Baravia's hammer to deceive the public. Finally, Luther explains that Ultra Man has spent decades meticulously studying Superman's every move, giving him a definitive advantage to attack him relentlessly. Later, we see Clark Kent arriving at his job as a journalist. He receives a call from his parents who greet him warmly and tell him they just wanted to congratulate him and remind him that they think about him a lot, asking him not to forget them. However, Clark briefly says goodbye and continues with his day. At that moment, Lois Lane appears, mocking Clark a bit with his usual mischievousness. Meanwhile, the news reports that the president of Borava, Basil, has publicly declared that there are no ties between his country and the individual known as the hammer of Borava. For his part, Clark comments that he has had the opportunity to interview Superman on multiple occasions. At the same time, the news shows how public opinion towards Superman has turned negative since his appearance. At the Luther Corp facilities, Lex Luthther gathers several representatives of the elite to present what he describes as the most powerful force on the planet, Ultra Man, as well as a group of raptors, powerful beings designed to neutralize any extraterrestrial threat. Luther attempts to persuade businessmen and influential figures to invest in his metahumans, arguing that Superman represents a potential threat. However, the representatives point out that Superman has prevented a war and is also popular among the population. Despite this, Luther insists that Superman is dangerous and must be stopped, though he admits he lacks conclusive evidence to prove he poses a real danger. For this reason, the representatives refuse to take drastic measures. Meanwhile, Lois and Clark decide to go on a date as they haven't had one in the past three months. During their meeting, they discuss recent events related to the Boravian Hammer. Superman expresses his desire for Lois to interview him, to which she agrees. Are you serious? Yes. Will you let me interview you as Superman? Of course. The recording begins and Lois asks him about the criticism he's received lately, noting that even the secretary of defense has announced he will investigate him for his actions on Borava. Superman explains that he intervened in Jarjer and had a conversation with the president of Borava, although he cannot reveal details because it is private information. This angers Lois, who approaches him for not simply declaring in an interview that there are things he can't share, as that leaves a bad impression on the public. Clark replies to Lois that he acted the way he did because he's convinced the Boravian government has ignoble intentions. Roy asks if he at least requested permission to enter Boravian airspace, but Superman admits he didn't, arguing that he acted solely as his own representative and in accordance with what he believes is right. He adds that he made that decision because many lives were at risk and he firmly believed he had to intervene. Lois comments that she has received countless criticisms on social media as a result of the situation. However, Superman clarifies that he doesn't have time to pay attention to social media. He then opens up emotionally and tells Ly about his biological parents. He explains that he comes from Krypton, a planet that no longer exists, destroyed along with all its history, culture, and loved ones. He tells her that his parents sent him to Earth when he was just a child with the purpose of saving him and allowing him to serve humanity. Lois then confesses that much of the population suspects he's on Earth for disturbing or secret purposes, which deeply irritates Clark. Lois, visibly frustrated, admits that she sensed the conversation wouldn't go well and acknowledges that romantic relationships aren't exactly his strong suit. At this, Clark decides to leave quietly, leaving Lois alone and thoughtful. Meanwhile, Luther and his team have arrived in Antarctic, where they discover Superman's ice castle. Upon arrival, Luther manages to activate it and completely invade the facility. Although Angela doesn't know how he managed to do so, as the castle should only be opened with Superman's DNA. Luther, accompanied by his superhumans, destroys all the robots that stand in his way. Angela contributes significantly, and just as they have eliminated all their adversaries, Krypto appears. However, they only cover his face and dismiss him without further involvement. In reality, Luther has traveled there with a single purpose, to find evidence that could incriminate Superman. Meanwhile, Otis, a member of Luther Corporation, has arrived in Metropolis carrying a box containing something intended to release something dangerous. He aims to distract Superman while they extract crucial information from his castle. For her part, Angela dedicates herself to recovering the rest of the damaged message from Superman's parents and after arduous efforts, manages to fully restore it. Back in Metropolis, Otus frees the little monster, and Superman immediately arrives to help rescue a puppy who is about to be crushed by the creature, which grows enormously. While this is happening, Lois watches the events through the news. That's when the Justice Gang, consisting of Hawk Girl, Green Lantern, and Mr. terrific bursts in. Together, they manage to defeat the monster. And just as the enormous creature is about to collapse and crush the crowd, Superman intervenes to ensure everyone can escape unharmed. Finally, the news reports that fortunately, there were no casualties. However, after this heroic act, no one applauds. The news has spread that Superman is actually a threat. According to reports, the message sent by his parents was analyzed by 28 of the world's most prestigious linguists who confirmed its translation. In it, his parents expressed that they love him more than heaven and earth and reveal that his beloved home will cease to exist forever. However, they assure him that hope lies in Superman, as after traveling the universe, they concluded that Earth is the best place for him. Its inhabitants, however, are simple, confused, and possess weak minds. Therefore, as the last son of Krypton, he must eliminate all those unable to serve him. Furthermore, their genes and legacy are in his hands, and he must honor them by ruling without mercy. Faced with this revelation, Luther appears before the public and proclaims that Superman is subjugating humanity, paving the way for his descendants to conquer Earth, something he will never allow. Consequently, Superman wanders the streets deeply saddened while being subjected to insults and recriminations from the people. Finally, Superman takes refuge in a room. There, Green Lantern comes to confront him, convinced after hearing his parent message that Superman is a threat. However, Superman assures him that he never heard the entire message as the second half was damaged during transit. At that moment, Mr. Terrific intervenes and clarifies that the forensic department wouldn't have certified the messages authenticity if there was any doubt, so the content couldn't be fake. At this point, Superman decides to return immediately to the ice castle, convinced that this is the only place they could have obtained the original recording. Meanwhile, representatives from various nations meet for an urgent summit to discuss whether Superman really poses a danger to the planet. On the news, the president of Borava appears, declaring that Superman only intervened in his invasion of Jarjer with the purpose of subjugating his people and keeping him as slaves. He further states that Boravian women are more attractive and that for this reason Superman wants to integrate them into his personal harum. After concluding his interview, the president retires to his office and passes through a secret portal that leads him to Luther. Upon meeting, the president is exaltant, convinced that they have managed to take Superman out of the game thanks to the supposedly fake message Luther fabricated. However, Luther clarifies that the message is authentic and explains that destroying Superman was extremely easy. partly due to his own parents. When Superman arrives at his castle and finds it completely devastated, he encounters one of his robots named for who confesses that he did everything in his power to protect him but failed to fulfill his mission. He then logs off in Superman's arms, leaving him visibly shaken. Shortly after, Superman realizes that Krypto has disappeared. Determined, he heads to Luther Corp to demand that Luther reveal the whereabouts of Krypto. However, Luther claims to have no idea what he is talking about. While the two argue, Luther partner Eve is secretly recording them and broadcasting the conversation live. During the broadcast, an agitated Superman is seen yelling at Luther, which creates a media scandal. Simultaneously, the news broadcasts images of Peacemaker, who takes advantage of the situation to speak in derogatory terms about Superman. After this episode, Superman, deeply dejected, arrives at Lois apartment. She surprised tells him that she just found out he has a dog and tenderly offers him a cup of hot chocolate. Superman then reveals that the ship he was sent on was damaged during the journey and that he had only managed to listen to the first half of his parents' recording. Lois understanding tells him that she believes in him, although she points out that one of his greatest flaws is blindly trusting everyone and assuming that all human beings are kind, which is far from the truth. Clark, somewhat confused, asks what he means by he realizes their relationship wasn't working out and confesses that he's considering turning himself in, as perhaps that way they'll lead him to his beloved Krypto. A bewildered Lois asks him why he's so interested in a mere dog, to which Superman replies that he was entrusted with its care and is determined to fulfill his responsibility. Lois, unable to help herself, hugs him. Superman whispers that he loves her and they say goodbye. The next day, Superman voluntarily surrenders to Luther soldiers who brutally subdue him and force him to the ground without mercy. Stunned, Superman is captured and with a hint of irony mentions that no one has read him his rights. However, Colonel Flag coldly explains that the court has ruled that as an alien, Superman has no rights under human law. He is then put on a ship and taken to a secret Luther base located in the middle of the desert. Once there, a squad of raptors escorts him to a dimensional portal that leads to a pocket universe created by Luther through a small rift between the two worlds. Luther accesses this universe through multiple portals scattered across the planet. They eventually arrive at a hidden prison where Luther holds various individual whom Borava has ordered imprisoned. Among the prisoners are troublemakers and even Luther's former lovers. He has even imprisoned a woman whose only crime was writing a spiteful blog after her breakup with him. Superman is then confined in a cell alongside Rex, a shape- shifter capable of altering his body's makeup at will. Luther orders Rex to transform one of his hands into kryptonite, the only substance capable of weakening Superman. Rex, with no alternative, complies with the order as Luther holds his son captive in a cell within the same prison. Meanwhile, Lois is at the newspaper office investigating the reasons why Luther Corp is interfering in Boravia's affairs. During his search, he uncovers alarming information. Luther Corp had sold weapons to Borava at ridiculously low prices. At that moment, his partner Jimmy appears and reveals that thanks to a contact, he has learned that Superman is trapped in a pocket universe. Inside that pocket universe, Luther appears before Superman and reveals that they have crypto in their possession. He assures him that the dog will remain locked up, will be exhaustively studied, and will eventually be permanently put to sleep, but not before undergoing a painful process. Furthermore, Luther informs Superman that he will never leave that place either, as it is his private correctional facility. Luther also confesses that if it were up to him, he would have already ended his life, but the governments insist on interrogating him before making any decisions. Meanwhile, Jimmy meets with Eve, Luther's partner, and secretly Jimmy's informant. He questions her about Luther's true plans, but Eve claims not to know for sure. However, she promises to find out more details if Jimmy agrees to go on a date with her. Before leaving, Eve distraughtly confesses that Luther tortured a dog the day before and that she's not finished with him because he boasts about having all his exes locked up in his private correctional facility. Meanwhile, a weakened Superman proposes to Rex that removing the kryptonite could help him rescue his son, the little shape shifter. However, Rex reacts furiously and instead of helping him, brings the kryptonite even closer to Superman, causing him unbearable pain. At the same time, Lois rejoins the Justice gang, determined to find and rescue Superman. Mr. Terrific manages to track Superman's location, having previously planted nanot trackers in his blood. He explains to the team that Superman is at a deactivated military base, and although the signal is lost at that point, it confirms that he is in a pocket universe. However, Green Lantern and Hawk Girl are reluctant to participate in the rescue, stating that they do not wish to fight to save Superman. Lois, visibly upset, bids them farewell, sarcastically, telling Green Lantern that his haircut does not suit him. As she prepares to leave, Mr. Terrific follows her and assures her that he will accompany her on her mission. Meanwhile, Basil and Luther take Malik Ali, a civilian who had previously helped Superman by feeding him and helping him get up when he was injured, to the prison. Luther plans to use him to blackmail Superman and force him to answer all the questions they intend to ask him. In his agony, Superman begs Luther not to hurt Malik. However, when they begin to question him about possible accompllices, Superman insists that he does not work with no one else. The capttors don't believe him and without hesitation, they shoot Malik in the head. Meanwhile, Mr. Terrific and Ly finally arrive at the secret base where Superman is being held prisoner. Determined to rescue him, Mr. Terrific senses signs of Superman's presence and without hesitation begins to confront all who stand in his way, protecting Lois with an energy field. Once he has defeated his opponents, the two continue their journey and reach a tent that houses access to a pocket universe. There, Mr. Terrific explains to Lois how dangerous it is to create a pocket universe, as it could trigger the formation of a black hole and fracture space every time someone enters or leaves it. Mr. terrific then confesses that he is only helping her because it will upset Green Lantern. Wasting no time, he begins to decipher the code needed to open the portal to that universe. For his part, Rex is deeply dejected for not having managed to save the civilian who died before his very eyes. Stealing himself, he asks Superman if he's capable of reaching his son and rescuing him. Superman nods determinately, and then Rex decides to disintegrate the kryptonite he was holding in his hand to stop injuring and weakening him. When Superman manages to partially recover, Rex questions him about why he continues to look so weakened. Then, when Superman explains that his poor condition is due to the lack of sunlight, he needs to absorb the radiation of the yellow sun to regenerate his strength since that's where his powers come from. Meanwhile, Mr. Terrific and Lois finally managed to decipher the code that allows them to enter the pocket universe and cross the portal. Once inside, they encounter a river of antiprotons that prevents them from continuing. If they ventured to cross it, they would be vaporized in a matter of seconds and would never make it back to Superman alive. Meanwhile, in the cell where Superman is being held captive, Rex explains that although he cannot create a true sun, he is capable of generating something similar by combining various substances produced by his own body. Once the mixture is complete, it produces a flash so intense that it allows Superman to gradually regain his strength. When Superman is fully recovered, he immediately flies to the cell where Rex's son is being held and frees him, reuniting the baby with his father. However, Rex asks Superman to take his son with him as he cannot carry him when he shapeshifts. Together, they then set out to find Krypto. But just as they are about to escape, they are surprised and pulled into the river of antiprotons. Krypto bravely intervenes to help. At the most critical moment, Superman is about to be sucked into a black hole and desperately calls out to Krypto. Rex also rushes to their aid and thanks to his help and Superman's tip off, they manage to get to safety. Mr. Terrific, manages to find them and helps them escape. Managing to escape just before the portal closes permanently. After their escape, Superman and Lois reunite. Superman, although weak, tells Lois that there are still more people who need to be rescued. Mr. Terrific offers her his ship so she can travel safely. Meanwhile, Eve contacts Jimmy and reveals that he has all the information needed to destroy Luther. However, before proceeding, he demands that Jimmy promise that they will go out together on Saturday, just the two of them. However, Luther suddenly appears, takes Eve away, and although she manages to send the information, it turns out that what was transmitted were only provocative photographs of herself. Meanwhile, Lois accompanies Superman to visit Clark's parents. Later, Jimmy contacts Lois to inform her about the situation and sends her the photos. To everyone's surprise, at the bottom of those selfies lies crucial data belonging to Luther, which turns out to be of great relevance. Meanwhile, Luther prepares to reopen the portal to the pocket universe. Despite the fact that doing so could cause a three-dimensional rift. However, the possibility of such a catastrophe doesn't concern him, and he actually causes the rift to form, demonstrating why a pocket universe should never be created. The next day, Superman's father tells him that Lois is a good girl and that he's also noticed that he's different. Superman feels bad because his parents sent him to kill. But Jonathan Kent tells him that parents don't decide what their children want to do. It's their decisions and actions that make them the man they are and that he couldn't be more proud of him today. They hug each other. On the other hand, Green Lantern watches the news about the war in Borava. Superman also sees this and learns that the children of Borava are asking for his help. So he plans to go there. But Terrific informs Superman about the rift. So he must go as it could destroy the entire Earth. Later, Jimmy and Lois tell Perry, the head of the news communications department that Luther is doing all this to get half of Jar Hampamper seated to him since Luther wants to make himself king. He's even colluding with the president of Borava, Basil, who created the rift to distract Superman and prevent him from intervening in the war. Mr. Terrific is unable to stop the rift. And neither is the Luther Corp team because Luther refuses to do so. So, they take the ship out of their building. Mr. Terrific claims there's a code to close the rift, which is located at Luther Corporation. But Superman must first find Krypto, whom he had taken for a walk so he wouldn't kill his parents' cows. Ultraman then arrives and takes Superman to a football stadium where they also fight with the metahuman Angela. Luther asks Angela to fill Superman's lungs with air and she does so before Luther watches. When Superman is literally on the verge of death, Basil is sent to start the war. Superman is infested with nayites and Luther orders Angela to finish inserting them completely. Superman flies to the highest point, even leaving the planet. And when he can no longer go any further, they fall at maximum speed, something Angela may not survive due to the force of the impact. However, when they land, Superman is still alive and manages to expel the naites. Luther sends the raptors as they discover that Angela is still alive, although she is about to die, and that Ultraman has also survived. It is then that Ultraman's mask falls off and Superman learns that he was cloned. Luther searched the rubble of his battles and found a hair to clone, allowing him to open his ice castle because it possesses his DNA. However, the clone proved imperfect as it is clumsier than him, easier to control, although stronger. Thus, Luther orders Ultram Man to hit him with all his might. Elsewhere, we see a child praying for Superman to arrive and free them from the war. Superman assures Luther that no matter what he does, he will not win and that his plans in Boravia will fail as he has called some friends. It turns out that he sent Justice Gone who is helping to stop the war also with the support of Rex and his baby. Meanwhile, Perry says they can publish the whole truth since Jimmy and Lois already know everything Luther has done. Luther started the war solely to have an excuse to kill Superman. Luther wants to kill him because according to him, Superman is destroying them all and he's also jealous, something he even admits. Superman smiles as he's being defeated, stating that mind overcomes strength and calls Krypto. When he's freed from his clone, he sends Krypto to collect the spheres, which were actually the surveillance cameras Luther had installed. Just then, the raptors arrive and Superman prepares to fight them. After defeating them, the clone reappears to continue beating him. However, Superman attacks him with greater force and sends him into a black hole. He then heads off with Mr. Terrific to close the rift and they arrive at Luther Corp. Superman declares that he is as human as anyone, that he knows how to love and also feels fear that every day when he wakes up, he puts one foot in front of the other and moves on and that he makes mistakes many times because that's what being human is all about. He expresses his hope that Luther will one day come to understand him. Luther, however, replies that he doesn't care because the governments have given him permission to kill him. But Krypto intervenes and begins to brutally beat Luther. He and the other co-workers were watching and see how the rift is closed thanks to Mr. Terrific who obtained the code. On the news, everything is revealed about Luther, his secret collaboration with Basil and the Boravian government. Now everyone knows that Luther is a traitor. It is revealed that the entire world had turned against Superman. But now everyone recognizes that they owe him an apology because Superman is and always will be the hero they always believed in. Luther has fallen. The war has been averted and the people are happy. Rex joins the justice gang after helping to save the war. Luther is arrested and everyone he had held prisoner, including his former partners, is released. Eve meets with Jimmy and then Lois meets with Superman. She goes to interview him in a secluded location, although she really only does so to kiss him. And finally, Lois tells him that she loves him, too. Afterwards, Superman returns to his ice castle where his robots have repaired everything and are self-repairing. He names his fourth robot, who will now be called Gary. Later, his cousin Supergirl arrives, who is actually the owner of Crypto and enjoys partying on other planets since their metabolism prevents them from getting drunk on planets with yellow suns. Therefore, his cousin prefers to travel to worlds with red suns. Now, Superman is getting ready to rest while he watches a message from his human parents, reviewing all their memories. and he feels happy. Thus concludes this story. But there are two post-redit scenes. In the first, we see Superman contemplating Earth with crypto. In the second, we see Superman talking with Mr. Terrific about the state of Metropolis after the great threat that almost destroyed everything. And now this story ends. Until next time.

text: With Nha 2 on the horizon, let's take a look back at the story and get a 10-minute refresher on Nha 1. For thousands of years, the spiritual energy of heaven and earth condensed into a single powerful pearl known as the primordial pearl. Absorbing the essence of the sun and moon, it grew immensely powerful. Master Yuan Tian ordered his disciples Taian and Shinong Bao to retrieve it. However, the pearls power was overwhelming. Left with no choice, Yuan Sher Tanzun personally intervened and refined it, splitting it into two parts, the spirit pearl and the demon pill. The demon pills soul was indestructible, so he cast a heavenly curse upon it, ensuring that in 3 years, a divine thunderbolt would descend and destroy it. After Yuan Sher Tian Xun<unk>s passing, it was decided that if the Spirit Pearls reincarnation, Nha, could grow into a great warrior, he would aid Kinghao in overthrowing the Shang dynasty, and Taian would earn his place among the 12 Golden Immortals. Shin Gong Bao, envious and bitter, believed that he was the one who truly deserved this honor. Using his puppet magic, he controlled the guards and servants, launched an ambush, and managed to seize both the spirit pearl and the demon pill. In a swift move, he secretly placed the demon pill into a stone altar inscribed with dowist runes. Thus, our protagonist, the demon child Neha, was born. From the moment he entered the world, he exhibited an unruly and fiery nature. Sensing disaster, Taiishan quickly used his master's treasure, the universe ring, to restrain Nha's wild power. Thanks to his parents' protection, Nha survived. Meanwhile, Shen Gong Bao ventured into the undersea prison and infused the spirit pearl into a dragon egg. The old dragon king, upholding his end of the deal, allowed his newborn son, Ao Bing, to become Shinonga<unk>s disciple. With the spirit pearls power, my son will gain boundless abilities and might even ascend to godhood, he declared. General Lee Jing and his wife, rulers of Chinteng Pass, were beloved by their people for their constant battles against demons and monsters. However, their busy duties left them little time for Nha. In the blink of an eye, Nha had already reached his first birthday. One day he lay on a wall staring at the scenery, unusually quiet for such a mischievous child. Lady Lee, having finished her official duties, tried to cheer him up by playing shuttlecock with him. She knew she had been too busy to spend time with him, but she didn't expect Nha's immense strength to send her and the armored guards flying into the walls. Soon after, a scout reported that a monstrous eel was terrorizing a fishing village. Lady Lee wished to stay and play with Nha, but was duty bound to protect the people. Before leaving, she sternly instructed the guards to keep Nha from sneaking out again. However, as soon as she left, the clever and restless Nha tricked the guards with a rock and slipped away into town. His arrival through the once orderly streets into utter chaos. Determined to give Nha a joyful childhood in his last two years, his parents asked Taan to take him as a disciple, teaching him virtue and Kuns mystical arts. Nha, naturally gifted, mastered transformation magic in just one day. Taian marveled, "My goodness, you learn that in a day." Nha grinned. I just figured it out while practicing. Taian sighed. Hey, can you share your secret? Nha smirked. Teach me more spells and I'll tell you. Taian laughed. All right, deal. Armed with his new abilities, Nha chased a sea demon, the water Yiksha, who fled toward the ocean. Thinking he could escape, the Yiksha leapt into the sea, only to be met with a frozen surface. I've sealed a mile of the ocean in ice. You're not getting away, Nha declared. At that moment, Nha encountered Ao Bing. The two became fast friends, spending their free time playing shuttlecock by the sea. Though it was just a simple toy, they enjoyed it immensely, delighted by their newfound companionship. Opening up to Nha, Ao Bing revealed the truth about his people. In ancient times, dragons ruled the world, commanding immense power. But after submitting to the heavens, we fought countless battles before finally earning the title of Dragon King. If we leave the sea, the monsters we suppress will break free. The Dragon King's title is nothing more than a prison sentence, keeping us trapped beneath the waves forever. As creatures born from demons, dragons were never truly trusted by the heavens. The spirit pearl was their one chance. If Ao Bing could prove himself in the upcoming battle of the gods, he might ascend, earning the right to free his people. In preparation, the dragons forged their strongest scales into an indestructible armor, the myriad spirit armor, and gave it to Ao Bing. He understood that his people's fate rested entirely on his shoulders. 10 days later, Nha's birthday banquet arrived. To celebrate, Taiishan gifted him the fire tipped spear, the universe scarf, and even his most prized mount. This mount adapts to its rider's nature. For you, it's the windfire wheels. Haha. Then why was it a pig when you had it? Nha teased. Unbeknownst to Nha, Shan Gong Bao revealed his true origins before the banquet. Devastated, Nha misunderstood his parents and Taan, believing they had locked him inside the mystical painting to trap him forever. Enraged, he activated the universe ring, transforming into his demonic form in front of everyone, ready to unleash destruction. Though Ao Bing bore the burden of his people's future, he still had a kind heart. Unable to watch Nha's family perish, he risked exposing himself to save them. Dark storm clouds swirled in the sky. A terrifying electric dragon crackling within. A massive thunderbolt struck Nha, nearly reducing him to nothing. At that moment, Il Bing leaped into the thunderstorm, attempting to shield Nha. However, as reincarnations of the demon pill and spirit pearl, their fusion triggered the primordial pearls ability to absorb all energy. The falling thunderballs were partially absorbed, but the relentless celestial lightning continued to ravage them. On the brink of death, Taian, witnessing their struggle, made a desperate move. He used his master's legendary seven-colored lotus to aid them. In the aftermath, Taishan explained, "The seven-colored lotus is a divine artifact. It cannot preserve their bodies, but it can keep their souls intact. As long as their souls survive, there is still hope.

text: Eden unfolds in 1929, a dangerous yet hopeful era as Germany's social foundations crumbled. Dr. Friedrich Ritter, Jude Law, a philosophical idealist, and his wife Doris Stra, Vanessa Kirby, who suffers from multiple sclerosis, reject their civilization's perceived moral decay and escape to Floriana Island in the Gopagos. His goal is to compose a radical manifesto while Dora believes meditation will heal her condition. Their solitude soon fractures when the pragmatic Whitmer family, Hines, Daniel Burl, his wife Margaret, Sydney Sweeney, and their ill son Harry arrive seeking physical and ideological refuge. Though they bring little survival experience, the Whitmers work earnestly to build a new life. While Ritter and Dora remain wary of outsiders, complications escalate with the arrival of Eloise boss Kada Vagner Werehorn, Anna de Armis, a self-styled baroness dripping with privilege, flanked by two devoted companions and grand plans for a lavish hotel on the island. Her dramatic entrance and dismissive attitude ignite jealousy and suspicion among the settlers as they struggle with the brutal climate, dangerous wildlife, and lack of resources. Interpersonal tensions spiral. Ritter's idealism clashes with Eloise's narcissism and the Whitmer's practicality, revealing the undercurrent of power dynamics, betrayal, and human fragility. Nature may be harsh, but it is human psychology that ultimately threatens the fragile equilibrium on Floriana. As alliances shift and deception takes root, the island becomes a crucible, exposing each character's inner demons, prompting desperation, moral erosion, and in some cases, mortal consequences. Filmed in Queensland under intense conditions, the cast found themselves bonding deeply, a sharp contrast to the psychological fractures on screen. Directed and co-written by Ron Howard with a screenplay by Noah Pink, Eden premiered at Tiff in September 2024 and will be released in US theaters on August 22nd, 2025. With haunting cinematography by Matias Hernel in a powerful score from Hans Simmer, the film earned mixed positive early reviews. text: Eden even shows Margaret while pregnant being attacked by wild dogs. But did that actually happen in real life? Let's talk about Eden because this movie really caught my attention. It says it's inspired by real events. But the whole time I was watching it, I could not help asking myself, did this really happen in real life? Take the Baroness for example. In the film, Anna de Armas plays her as this manipulative, almost evil figure who tries to control everything. But was she really like that in real life or did the movie turned her into a villain for the drama? And then there's Frederick. Did he actually killed the Baroness or is that just part of the legend? And what about the Witmerst? Their story raises so many questions. In this episode, we're uncovering the Galapagus affair based on the movie Eden. Digging into what's true, what's exaggerated, and what still remains a mystery. Because the deeper I go into the real history, the stranger and more fascinating it becomes. [Music] In 1929, a man named Dr. Frederick Ritter and his wife Doris Stron left their home in Germany because they did not like the way people were living back then. They moved to a far away island called Floriana in the Galapagus Islands. Frederick wanted to write a big book about his ideas while Dora practiced meditation to help with her illness. They believed the world kept making the same mistake, fighting wars and bad leaders. They thought they're the only people who could fix things and build a better life. At first, they were happy to be alone on the island, but the peace did not last for long. In the movie, Dora is shown as Frederick Ritter's wife. So, they are presented as a couple. Is that the truth? It's a fiction. In real life, Dora was not Frederick Ritter's wife. She was actually his mistress, and she left Berlin, abandoning her husband, to follow her lover, Dr. Ritter, to a remote and completely disorded island, Floriana, in the Galapagus. Together they hoped to escape the world and built an entirely new life far away from civilization. Richard himself was no stranger to success. He was a respected doctor in Berlin with a thriving practice and comfortable life. Yet, he made a shocking choice. He left his career and his wife behind to pursue a lifelong dream of renouncing society and living entirely off the grid with Dora. It's also true that Dora had multiple sclerosis and Frederick helped looked after her using his own ideas about healthy eating and natural living to treat her. Another wild detail from the movie Eden is a scene where the baroness invites everyone to the dining table and we see that Jude Law's character Dr. Ritter is wearing a stainless steel dentures. Is that true? It's a fact. It's not just a movie prop. It's based on a true story. Before heading off to their isolated life on Floriana Island, Frederick and Dora both had their teeth removed back in Germany. Why? Well, Richtor being a doctor believed that pulling out his teeth would somehow strengthen his gums and help him survive a raw primitive lifestyle. Dora, who suffered from multiple sclerosis, went through it, too. But here's where it gets really intense. Once they were on the island, Dora's remaining teeth started rotting from the lack of proper care. And without dental tools, Ritter had to use, get this, gardening tools to remove her decaying teeth. Yeah, you heard that right. This strange dental routine gave rise to a legend of them being the toothless couple of the Galapagus. Their unusual lifestyle did not stay a secret either, passing ships noticed, and European newspapers even reported on them, turning them into something of a bizarre island legend. The Whitmers. Hines and Margaret Whitmer arrived on the Floriana Island with their young son, Harry, who was sick with tuberculosis. Their doctor had recommended sending Harry to a sanitarium, but the family simply could not afford it. They dug a makeshift well to collect spring water, worked tirelessly to build the front yard farm, and eventually moved out of the mosquitoinfested cave into a stone house they completed in just a few months. In the movie, did Dr. Witter actually tell the Whitmers to live in the caves? Is that real? It's a fiction. In Eden, there is a scene where Dr. Frederick Ritter directs the Whitmer's family to a remote cave on the Floriana Islands. However, it is important to note that this specific interaction is a dramatic interpretation created for the film and is not directly supported by historical facts. The movie draws inspirations from real events involving European settlers in the Florana Islands. While both groups face isolation and harsh conditions, historical accounts do not provide detailed records of Dr. Witter instructing the Whitmers to reside in a cave. The Baroness and her lovers. text: The movie opens in 1982 at a bar where we meet Hank Thompson, a former basketball player now working as a bartender. After his shift, his girlfriend Ivonne, a paramedic, drops by and playfully urges him to take advantage of her poor judgment. The two leave for Hank's apartment where they share a passionate kiss. On their way to the bedroom, they run into Hank's neighbor, Russ, who is preparing to leave for London to visit his father. Russ asks Hank to look after his cat while he's away. At first, Hank refuses, but when Ivonne mentions that she likes cats, he reluctantly agrees. The couple then retreat to the bedroom and share an intimate moment while the cat watches them with an unsettling stare. The next day, Ivonne leaves for her job as a paramedic while Hank stays home to make breakfast. As he searches for cat food, two Russian mobsters, Pavl and Alexe, suddenly burst into the apartment. They demand to know Russ's whereabouts, but Hank insists he isn't home. Suspicious, the men search Hank's room and discover his cat, assuming Hank is lying. When they press him again about Russ, Hank snaps back that it's none of their business. Enraged, the mobsters beat him savagely, striking his side until he collapses. The assault leaves him gravely injured, and they leave him bleeding on the floor. Hank eventually loses consciousness. When he wakes, he finds himself in a hospital bed with Ivonne at his side. Confused, he checks his body and realizes he has undergone surgery. Ivonne gently explains that his kidney was damaged and had to perform surgery. Hank discharged from the hospital and Ivonne informs that during his recovery period, he must avoid salt and alcohol. Ivonne takes Hank back to the apartment before heading off to work. Left alone, Hank gathers all the bottles of alcohol and dumps them down the toilet. Later, while taking out the trash, he spots one of the mobsters who attacked him standing inside a nearby pizza shop. Panicked, Hank hurries back upstairs only to find the other man furiously pounding on Russ's door. Hank slips out to the balcony and hides, secretly watching as the mobsters break into Russ's apartment and begin searching the place as there is something important hidden inside. But when one of them notices him, Hank quickly climbs back through his own window and calls the New York police. After the Russian mobsters leave, Detective Roman arrives at Hank's apartment to question him. Hank explains that three men tried to break into Russ's place, but insists he knows nothing about them. Roman reveals that Russ is actually a drug dealer with ties to the notorious Hidic brothers, Leipa and Schmully Ducker, likely the reason the mobsters showed up. Before leaving, she warns Hank to call her immediately if he sees them in again. Later, while cleaning the bathroom, Hank notices the cat's litter box. Inside, he discovers something unusual. One of the droppings is actually hiding a key. Just as he makes the discovery, the mobsters return and begin forcing their way through the door. Hank quickly calls Detective Roman, telling her not only about the break-in, but also about the key he has found. Hank heads to Paul's bar and starts drinking heavily despite the doctor's orders. He gets so drunk that Ivonne comes to take him home, but his slurred, foolish remarks push her away, and she leaves in frustration. Stumbling back to his apartment building, Hank vomits, strips off his clothes outside, and collapses on the floor, passing out. In his sleep, he dreams of his past. Once a star high school baseball prospect, Hank's promising career ended in tragedy after a drunken car crash killed his best friend, Dale, and left Hank with a devastating knee injury. The next morning, Hank wakes up to find the Russian mobsters back in his apartment, this time accompanied by their Puerto Rican associate, Colorado. Colorado demands to know what Russ gave him before leaving for London. Hank insists Russ gave him nothing, but he found the key hidden in the cat's litter box. When pressed about it, Hank realizes he can't remember what he did with the key during his drunken haze the night before. Furious, the mobsters begin beating him. Just as Colorado raises his gun to finish the job, a knock suddenly echoes at the door. The knock at the door turns out to be their neighbor, Dwayne. Hank tries to shoe him away, but when Dwayne keeps knocking, one of the mobsters opens the door. Startled, Dwayne bolts down the hall. Colorado then warns Hank not to involve the police and hands him his number, instructing him to call when he finds the key. Determined, Hank leaves the cat with Ivonne, and sets out to track down the missing key. He phones Paul, the bar owner, to ask about it. But before he can get answers, the Ducker brothers men show up and chase him through the streets. Hank barely manages to slip away and quickly calls Colorado, promising he's on his way to search for the key and return it once he finds it. But Colorado, growing impatient, coldly mentions his girlfriend, Ivonne's name. Realizing she's now in danger, Hank races back to her apartment only to find her lying dead, a bullet wound to the head. Heartbroken, Hank calls Detective Roman, insisting that Ivonne had nothing to do with the Russian mob. Roman coldly reminds him that his defiance angered them and Yvon's death was their way of sending a message. She also explains that the key likely holds enormous value, possibly opening a locker stuffed with cash, its exact location known only to Russ. Hank admits that he gave the key to his boss Paul at the bar, asking him to hide it before getting drunk and forgetting about it. As they talk, the mobsters suddenly arrive, led by Colorado, and Hank is stunned to learn that Roman is secretly working with them. They force Hank into a car and park outside Paul's bar, waiting for him to appear. Hank asks Colorado who killed his girlfriend, but Colorado says he did not kill his girlfriend. After a long wait with no sign of Paul, they shove Hank inside to retrieve the key himself. Hank confronts Paul, demanding it back, but Paul insists Hank never gave him a key. Suspicious, the mobsters storm in with Roman, who presses Paul for answers. When Paul continues to deny having the key, they execute one of his men on the spot and turn their gun on Paul, demanding he hand it over. As Colorado prepares to execute Paul, Detective Roman suddenly turns her gun on him and shoots him dead. Paul then admits the key is in his safe and moves to retrieve it. But instead of unlocking the safe, he grabs a hidden shotgun and opens fire on the mobsters. They scatter, and when Paul steps outside to finish them off, they gun him down. Roman turns to Hank, demanding that he open the safe and hand over the key, but Hank hesitates. Something clicks in his mind. Instead of obeying, he slips out through a side exit and escapes the bar unnoticed. Back at his apartment, Hank rummages through the garbage, searching desperately. There, he encounters a homeless man asleep and wearing Hank's old pants from the night he blacked out. Hank urges him to check the pockets. The man digs inside, pulls out the missing key, and hands it over. Hank rushes back into his apartment when suddenly there's a knock at the door. Grabbing a baseball bat, he cautiously unlocks it, strikes, only to find Russ standing there. Stunned, Hank demands answers, pressing him to reveal what the key opens and where the money is. Russ urges Hank to come with him. And once they're in the car, he begins to explain everything. He admits that after selling drugs for the Ducker brothers in Colorado's nightclubs, Detective Roman caught wind of his operation. To keep her quiet, Russ was forced to cut her in since she owed a massive debt to the Russians boss. The key, Russ reveals, unlock storage containing just over $4 million money he was supposed to split among all the parties on the day he left for London. Hank and Russ arrive at the storage facility and unlock the unit, revealing stacks of cash. Suddenly, Russ pulls a gun on Hank. He explains that the mobsters believe he ran off with the money and are hunting him down. Desperate to save himself, Russ plans to take the cash and flee the country. Before he can act, Hank knocks him out cold. Hank then calls Roman, demanding she meet him at the location and to bring his cat. He loads Russ into the car and drives to the rendevu. When they arrive, Hank offers Roman both Russ and the key in exchange for the cat, but the deal spirals out of control. In a panic, Russ grabs Pavle's gun and shoots Alexe dead before escaping with Hank and the cat. On the run, Russ finally reveals the truth. It wasn't Colorado who killed Ivonne, it was Roman. The two flee into a crowd at Shea Stadium, then slip onto the subway, but Russ, gravely concussed and bleeding, collapses from his injuries and dies there. Hank is left alone, cradling the cat. He boards a bus bound for Coney Island. Hank arrives at Coney Island and falls asleep on the beach. The next morning, he's jolted awake by a call from Roman. She has framed him for the string of murders and now threatens his mother's life, demanding that he bring the key to the Russians supper club. Shaken, Hank immediately calls his mother, assuring her that the news reports are lies. He urges her to leave the house at once and take shelter at a friend's place. Desperate, Hank contacts the Ducker brothers and strikes a deal. If they kill Roman, they can keep the money. The brothers accept. Hank surreners himself to them and is zip tied to the steering wheel of their car while the heavily armed brothers prepare to storm the club. Inside the supper club, the Ducker brothers unleash chaos, mowing down Roman's henchmen and guests. Roman manages to slip away, fleeing outside where Hank spots her. Desperate, he burns through his restraints with the car's cigarette lighter and gives chase. Before he can reach her, Pavle intercepts him. Hank overpowers him in a brutal fight, then corners Roman. She fights back fiercely, knocking him to the ground, but Hank manages to stab her in the leg and wrestle a gun into his hands. Just as he's about to pull the trigger, the Duckers appear and finish her off with a hail of bullets. Hank then reveals the key hidden in a bandage wrapped around the cat's leg. Impressed, the Ducker brothers decide to spare his life and even cut him in on his share of the money. They order him to drive them home. Behind the wheel, Hank notices something strange. He's the only one wearing a seat belt. Seizing the moment, he rams the car into a pillar at full speed, killing both brothers instantly. Sometime later, Hank assumes Russ's identity to flee the country with the cat and half of the fortune. At the airport, he presents Russ's passport and is waved through by security. Before boarding, he calls his mother, assuring her that he's safe and telling her to return home. Hank arrives in Tulum, Mexico, ready to begin a new life. Meanwhile, back at his mother's house, she receives a parcel from him. Inside is the rest of the money left for her. In this way, movie ends here. Thanks for watching.
