As she found all this unbelievable, the man beside her handed her the whistle and told her she must use it to summon the children instead of calling their names. After saying this, he prepared to control Maria in the same way. But Maria firmly refused to agree as she felt it was humiliating to people. As the renowned Navy captain trap, he had never been defied like this. But he did not get angry. Instead, after mocking Maria, he simply walked towards the exit. However, he was stopped by the whistle again. Immediately, Maria teased, saying, "I still don't know how to call you." Since it was the first time the strict father had left, after he left, the children unconsciously relaxed. Maria dared to act this way because she was originally a nun in a convent who loved to run to the mountains to sing loudly by herself. This often made her late miss prayers, causing the other nuns to have mixed feelings about her love of freedom, and even the Abbis didn't know what to do with her. Coincidentally, the Abbis heard that the captain needed a family tutor, so she sent Maria here. However, what Maria never expected was that not only was the captain cold and ruthless, but the children were not as obedient as they seemed. They were extremely resistant to tutors, having already driven away one teacher. Some teachers were so scared they fled within 5 minutes. Initially, Maria didn't realize the seriousness of the situation until a toad was slipped into her pocket. However, the maid told her she was lucky because the previous teacher's welcome gift was a snake. She thought the test was over. Unexpectedly during dinner, Maria sat down on the chair with the pine cone again. And as she cried out in pain, the children immediately showed triumphant smiles. Then they hoped this new teacher would voluntarily resign to their father so he would have to spend more time personally guiding and accompanying them. However, Maria not only didn't plan to give up, but she also sincerely thanked them for their steadfastness. Perhaps because they had never felt such acceptance, the fifth child suddenly cried with guilt. And soon after, the other children also began to shed tears. When the confused colonel asked what was going on, Maria simply said that the children were overwhelmed with happiness. Just as the dinner atmosphere was tense, the butler delivered a telegram. The baroness invited the colonel to Vienna. Upon learning their father was leaving again, the children showed sadness and discontent. Only the eldest daughter, unnoticed, slipped outside like an excited fawn. It turned out she had secretly fallen in love with the boy who delivered the telegram. But due to their vastly different social statuses, it was difficult for them to be openly together, so they could only occasionally meet secretly at night like this. Like all couples in love, they seemed to have endless sweet nothings to share. But neither wanted to overstep boundaries as they both respected each other greatly. Suddenly, with thunder and lightning, it began to rain, so they had to hide in the glass pavilion to continue their whispered promises. Meanwhile, the maid delivered new fabric to Maria's room, reminding her to quickly make some new clothes. because the colonel couldn't stand the ugly outfit she wore, which even the poor wouldn't want. Additionally, the maid told Maria not to sing at home, not even to laugh out loud. Since the mistress passed away, the colonel had become very stern and was much stricter with the children. Moreover, to avoid any emotional reminders, he strictly prohibited anything that would remind him of his wife. In fact, to completely forget his late wife, he intended to marry the Baroness, who had also lost her partner. This invitation to Vienna was to discuss the marriage arrangements. Maria felt deep sympathy for the seven children, but she also believed that God had sent her here to help them better accept their new mother and rediscover the warmth of family. So, she began to pray devoutly. Just then, the eldest daughter, who had just returned from a date, suddenly climbed over the balcony and broke in. But upon seeing Maria, she worried about being reported by her. So, she asked Maria to help keep it a secret. Little did she know, Maria was already lenient with the children, and seeing her drenched from the rain only triggered a silent sympathy within her. Not only did she promise not to betray her, but she also considerly took out clean clothes for her to change into in the bathroom, ensuring that no one else would notice anything a miss. People's hearts are made of flesh and especially for children who have lost their mother. Even a little affection can bring immense happiness. So, after feeling Maria's kindness, the eldest daughter genuinely accepted this new teacher. While she was changing clothes, the youngest daughter suddenly pushed the door open and rushed into Maria's arms. Not only that, but with a loud clap of thunder, the other three girls also rushed in fearfully, followed by the two boys who appeared with terrified faces. Looking at the six frightened children, Maria let them hide under her covers and told them that whenever she felt scared, she would think of beautiful things like water, fresh flowers, green meadows, a starry sky, and dew on rose petals. This would help ease the tension. With her guidance, the children soon forgot the thunder outside and were all immersed in imagining beautiful things. However, just as they were happily playing, the captain walked in with a stern face. Seeing her about to scold them, Maria quickly pointed the children away. Afterward, Maria pleaded with the captain to give her more fabric because she wanted to make clothes for the children to wear when they went out to play. As a result, she was flatly refused. Fortunately, Maria had another plan. She remembered the maid saying earlier that the curtains in the room would be replaced the next day. So, she permanently used the curtains to make new clothes for each of the seven children. After the captain left the house, she took the children to the countryside to play. The warm sunlight shown on every corner, and the breeze carried the scent of grass. They cheered and skipped along the riverside path, arriving at a green field full of white flowers. Knowing her mission was to help the children get along with their new mother, whom they hadn't met yet, Maria, who loved singing, decided to teach the children to sing during their picnic on the grass. Once they learned, they could use their singing to welcome the baroness. However, the children said that because their father didn't allow them to sing, they didn't understand music at all. So Maria had to start teaching them from the very basic seven notes. Fortunately, the children were very smart and before long they were able to combine the notes into beautiful melodies. Not long after the captain returned with the baroness. But just as the two were strolling by the picturesque lakeside, chatting about feelings and life, they suddenly noticed the children singing and rowing abode towards them. Seeing their father, the children excitedly stood up. Unexpectedly, in the next second, they all fell into the water due to losing their balance. Luckily, the lake was shallow and they climbed ashore without any danger. Watching the children still laughing and playing after falling into the water. The already angry captain became even more furious. But since the Baroness was present, she had to suppress her anger and ordered the children to go change their clothes. However, when Maria was about to leave, the captain suddenly called her back. Seeing this, the Baroness tactfully found an excuse to leave. Without any reservations, the captain vented all his dissatisfaction on Maria. He accused Maria of taking the children out to play and of dressing them in coarse clothes. But Maria retorted that the children didn't care about dressing well. They just wanted to be cared for and loved, especially wanting affection from you as their father. But you never paid attention to them. So they resorted to teasing the governness to get a little bit of your attention. Although every word was true, the captain, instead of reflecting on himself, decided to fire Maria. Just as Maria was too agrieved to speak, melodious singing suddenly came from the room. When the captain followed the music, he found that the children were singing to welcome the barness. This was the first time since his wife's death that the room was filled with singing. All the beautiful memories instantly flooded the captain's mind. Unconsciously, as if under a spell, she joined the children's chorus. When her deep, resonant voice blended with the children's clear, bright singing. The children hugged her tightly. At this moment, Maria, who had been hiding behind the door, saw the youngest daughter present the barness with a bouquet of Adal vice. As Maria turned to leave, the captain immediately chased after her and sincerely apologized for his earlier words. I really don't understand my children as you said. I asked you to stay, and Maria gladly agreed. From then on, the big house was no longer filled with annoying whistles, but with laughter and increasingly rich music programs. That day, after Maria and the children finished performing a puppet show, a friend of the captain, who was thoroughly impressed, suggested that the children participate in the folk festival competition, saying they would surely become an instant hit. But the captain refused to agree as she believed the children should not be in the limelight. To ease the awkward atmosphere, Maria intended to sing another song, but the children told her to let the captain perform. Initially, the captain politely declined, but under Maria and the children's persistent urging, she picked up the guitar and sang Adelvvice, a song that praises the small, white, clean, and bright national flower of Austria. The song expresses the Austrian people's love and blessings for their homeland through the praise of the Adelvvice. As the moving song continued to linger in the air, the deeply touched children joined in harmony. The Baroness was attracted by the gentle side of the tough captain, but she didn't expect that the captain's gentle gaze was always directed at Maria in the corner. Sensing a crisis, she asked the captain to hold a ball for her so she could declare her sovereignty in front of everyone. The captain gladly accepted the proposal. Soon, the ball was held as scheduled, and social elites, aristocrats, and military figures all attended to honor the captain. After lengthy pleasantries, the dignitaries began to dance to the music. Since it was an Austrian folk dance, almost every Austrian was familiar with it and knew the dance steps. However, the children found it unfamiliar, so they asked Maria to show them. At that moment, the captain also stepped out, and seeing the awkward dance between the big and the small, she stepped forward to replace the child. At first, they were both just immersed in the dance. But as their bodies touched and their eyes met, they developed unusual feelings for each other. More awkwardly, this scene was witnessed by the Baroness. Maria, blushing to her neck, quickly found an excuse to escape awkwardly, but soon returned to the hall because she had to lead the children in a performance for the guests. After the performance was successfully completed and the children exited the stage, the captain's friends suddenly stopped Maria, who was about to leave, and invited her to stay for the dinner. Due to the warm invitation, Maria had no choice but to go upstairs and change into an appropriate dress for the occasion. Unexpectedly, the Baroness followed her. Through her observations over the past few days, the Baroness was certain that the captain had fallen for Maria, and Maria had developed feelings for the captain as well. To eliminate this rival, she exposed the feelings Maria dared not admit, leaving Maria utterly shocked. As a nun, she was not supposed to have romantic feelings. Previously, she could deceive herself. But now, being exposed in public, she had no choice but to leave. This was exactly the Baroness's intention. Thus, Maria changed back into her original clothes, left a letter, and quietly departed. The Baroness thought that without Maria's presence, she could completely win over the captain and the children's hearts. However, she didn't realize that in any relationship, the most important thing is to give your true heart, not to eliminate the competition. So, even though Maria had been gone for many days, she still hadn't gained the children's approval. Not only that, the children often mentioned Maria and even asked the captain several times if Maria would return. The captain said she would not return. From now on, you will no longer need a governness because I am going to marry the Baroness. From now on, this new mother will take care of you. Although they were unwilling to accept it, the children politely kissed the barness. Afterward, they went to the convent gate with sadness, hoping to see Maria one more time. But the nuns said Maria was in seclusion and not seeing any visitors at the moment. Helpless, the children left disappointed. Since returning to the convent, Maria had indeed locked herself in her room, completely losing her previous cheerfulness. The mother superior felt that this couldn't continue. So, she took the initiative to talk to Maria. After learning the whole story, the mother superior said that avoiding the problem was not a solution. If you're not sure whether you've truly fallen in love with the captain, then go back and continue to find the answer. Staying here without clarity is disrespectful to the convent and irresponsible to yourself. Because the convent does not accept those who are attached to the secular world, and you have the right to live the life you truly want. Meanwhile, back home, the children feeling down began to sing the song that always lifted their spirits. But the more they sang, the more they missed Maria because the song was filled with memories of her. However, just as they were becoming more and more despondent, Maria suddenly returned with her suitcase. It turned out she finally took the dean's advice and decided to seek the life her heart truly desired. However, this willingness was shattered when she heard that the captain was about to marry the barness. But she didn't leave immediately. Instead, she planned to settle the children first before making any decisions. In the evening, under the bright moonlight and the crisp sound of frogs, a confused Maria wandered alone at the door. Meanwhile, the captain stood on the balcony, gazing intently. Suddenly, the Baroness came out. Upon seeing Maria not far away, she immediately realized that she had already lost in this love triangle. Yet, unwilling to give up, she still wanted to fight for it. So, she relied on her strong financial power, hoping to win back the captain's heart. But the captain never wanted marriage to be a transaction. Moreover, in her view, money couldn't compare to true love. After all, she already possessed a measurable wealth. Hearing this, the Baroness was completely relieved. But to preserve her last bit of dignity, she was the first to propose a breakup. Actually, you're not suitable to be my marriage partner because I need someone to depend on. But you clearly don't need me, not even my money, so we might as well part ways here. Tomorrow, I will return to Vienna. I wish you and your beloved can be together." After saying this, she turned and left. Meanwhile, Maria, full of thoughts, was sitting on a bench shrouded in the night, lost in thought. until the captain cautiously approached and said, "I have already broken off the engagement with the Baroness because I can't marry one person while loving another." Although his words were very subtle, Maria immediately understood the meaning. However, before she could recover from her surprise, the captain tenderly kissed her forehead. At this moment, the bright moonlight poured down, capturing their love as an eternal silhouette. Not long after, they completed their wedding in the monastery, blessed by the nuns. However, their happy days had just begun when they were forced to face bad news. At that time on the eve of World War II, Austria was annexed by German forces. Nazi flags were hung everywhere. When the captain returned from his honeymoon and found his doorstep also occupied, he tore down and destroyed the flag without hesitation. Because in his heart, Austria was always an independent nation. Neither disappeared nor a Nazi appendage. However, not everyone felt the same way. Even when faced with a powerful Yabo, he still refused to yield. In contrast, more people willingly became traitors to survive or gain power. For example, the telegraph boy who once dated the eldest daughter has now become an emotionless war machine. When he handed the telegraph to the eldest daughter again, it was no longer with the gentle affection of before, but rather filled with coldness and detachment. Although there was no explicit breakup, the eldest daughter knew in her heart that the relationship had come to an end. After passing the telegraph to the colonel, she sought out Maria for a heart-to-he heart talk. Since it was her first love, she didn't know how to overcome the pain of heartbreak. Maria comforted her, saying that if she felt really bad, she could have a good cry. But after crying, she should forget everything and face the next day with a positive and optimistic attitude. You must understand your life is just beginning. Your understanding of the world and human nature is still being refreshed and reshaped. One day you will meet someone who truly understands and loves you. Then you will marry, have children, and live a happy and fulfilling life together. But just as the two were envisioning a bright future, the colonel suddenly came over and interrupted. It turned out that the telegraph explicitly required the colonel to take a position at a naval base in Germany. If she refused, her family would be torn apart. If she accepted, her beliefs would collapse. Clearly, either choice was a disaster for the colonel. Helpless, she could only flee with her family overnight. But unexpectedly, the butler had already betrayed them. So, before they could leave the house, the Nazis, who had been notified in advance, blocked the door. They thought they were doomed. But fortunately, the colonel had a sudden idea. He remembered that a friend had signed them up for a choir competition, and the performance was scheduled for that very night. Initially, when he first heard the news, the colonel was adamant about not participating. Little did he know, this event he disliked would become his lifeline. Thus, under the watchful eyes of the Nazi soldiers, the colonel led his family to the competition venue and successfully completed the choir performance. However, when the colonel saw his fellow countrymen in the audience, who showed no sorrow for their occupied country and only wanted to continue their leisurely lives, he couldn't help but sing a solo of blood and tears, trying to stir up patriotism in their hearts. Sure enough, when he sang with such emotion that he choked up and couldn't continue, everyone in the audience joined in singing. Not only that, upon learning that the captain was about to be forced to join the German Navy, the host deliberately elongated his tone when announcing the award list. When the second and third place winners went on stage to receive their awards, they tacitly spoke a few more words just to buy more time for the captain's family, who won first place, to escape. Initially, the Nazi leader in charge of surveillance didn't notice anything unusual until his subordinate hurriedly reported that the captain's entire family was missing. He then quickly led his men to the monastery. Although the captain and his family were indeed hiding there with the help of the nuns, they were fortunately not discovered. After confirming that the search team had left, the captain cautiously emerged from behind the stone wall. Unexpectedly, the telegraph boy who had joined the Nazis suddenly returned and caught him red-handed. It turned out that just moments ago, the eldest daughter saw the telegraph boy's face and in disbelief let out a gasp. Although the sound was faint, it still aroused suspicion. So, after his companions left, the telegraph boy quietly hid in the shadows, lying in wait. Unexpectedly, he indeed caught his prey. Previously, the boy had affectionately told the eldest daughter that he would protect her and not let her get hurt. But now, he had become the perpetrator. Seeing this, the captain immediately gestured for Maria to take the children and leave first. Since the Nazis target was the captain, the boy did not stop them. After the family had all left, the captain walked towards the boy, patiently saying, "I know you won't shoot me. You're still just a child. You don't belong with them. Why not leave with us?" Initially, the boy seemed to understand. So, he neither fired nor struggled when the captain took his gun. But when the captain firmly said, "You can never be one of them," the boy, feeling insecure and sensitive, thought it was a taunt and immediately cried out for help. Fortunately, the captain's car was nearby, and soon he drove away with his family into the darkness. When the Nazi soldiers prepared to drive after them, they found that the car wouldn't start. It turned out that just a minute earlier, the nuns had removed all the essential parts of the car. In this way, the captain's family successfully escaped the threat. However, due to the border being closed, they had to trek over the mountains on foot to seek a new life in a foreign land. Starring Julie Andrews and Christopher Plamer, this romantic film was released in 1965. It is based on true events with Maria's character inspired by Maria Augusta Katcara. She was born in 1905 and became a nun in Vienna, Austria. In 1926, she was sent by the convent to Salsburg to be the governness for the second daughter of the von trap family. This marked the beginning of her encounter with Captain Gayorg von Trap. In reality, Gayorg von Trap was a legendary figure. He was not only the Austrohungarian Empire's most outstanding submarine commander, but also an enviable nobleman. During World War I, he commanded submarines to sink numerous enemy ships, earning the Maria Theresa military order and becoming a hero of the Austrian Navy. After his first wife, Agatha Whitehead, passed away, he married Maria in 1927, and together they raised 10 children. Two of these children were born after their marriage in 1929. The Great Depression swept the globe, drastically reducing the Von Trap family's wealth and plunging them into financial hardship. Maria suggested forming a choir to utilize the family's singing talents to make a living. By 1930, the von trap family choir quickly rose to fame in Austria. They became the most popular performing group, touring Europe and even performing for the Pope. Their music not only sustained the family, but also became a symbol of Austrian national spirit. In 1938, Germany annexed Austria. The captain openly opposed the Nazis, putting the entire family at risk of persecution. To save their lives, they participated in a music festival and miraculously they tked over mountains from a small town on the Italian border, enduring hunger and danger to reach the United States. In America, they started from scratch, founding the Trap Family Lodge and continuing to make a living through music. During World War II, they also established the Trap Family Austrian Relief Company to aid their war torn homeland. Moreover, influenced by their father's patriotism, the sons all eagerly joined the military and bravely participated in the anti-fascist war. When Maria was 42, the captain passed away. Until she closed her eyes, she retained her Austrian citizenship. Two years after the captain's death, Maria wrote an autobiography about her life with him and published it. It quickly became a bestseller, touching and inspiring countless people. Later, after several adaptations, it became the classic film The Sound of Music. Before meeting the captain, Maria always thought her life's pursuit was to become a nun. Little did she know her direction was wrong from the start, making her always seem out of place in the convent. It wasn't until the mother superior gave her guidance that she found the right direction in life. In fact, many people like Maria are stuck in their own cognitive traps, unable to break free. Even when they feel the pain, they choose to endure it repeatedly instead of reflecting, learning, and innovating, which may lead to a life of torment. In contrast, the Baroness is very adept at assessing the situation. She will use any means necessary to achieve her goals. But when the results don't go her way, she doesn't care about sunk costs and instead decisively pulls back to cut her losses. Indeed, in life, one must have persistence. You can't just go with the flow like a drifter. You must hold on to your inner beliefs and principles. This way, life becomes more meaningful. Just like the captain who always holds on to his patriotism, this steadfastness gives him greater courage to face and solve all difficulties and challenges. Love a person, climb a mountain, follow a path, cross a stream. Every day of your life, feel with your heart. Throughout your lifetime, you will eventually find your own life. All right, that's all for today's movie sharing. Please like, comment, and share. Looking forward to our next meeting. [Music]
title: She Changed Their Lives With Music – The Sound of Music Recap

text: [Music] When you sit down to watch The Roses, you expect a dark comedy with lots of drama and a touch of romance. But by the time the credits roll, you're probably left with your jaw hanging open, asking yourself, "E, what just happened to Ivy and Theo? Did they finally get divorced? Did they reconcile? or did things end in an even darker way? This movie directed by Jay Roach and starring Olivia Coleman as Ivy and Benedict Cumberbatch as Theo takes you through a roller coaster ride of marriage, love, hate, resentment, and a shocking ending that will stay in your head for days. The movie itself is a modern reimagining of The War of the Roses, a 1989 film based on the novel of the same name. But even if you've never seen that original, The Roses works as its own story, giving viewers a bitter, funny, and heartbreaking look at what happens when love turns into resentment. Let's dive deep into the ending, break it down, and understand what it all really meant for Ivy and Theo. At the beginning of the film, Ivy and Theo look like a perfect couple. They're deeply in love, supportive, and seem to have the kind of marriage people envy. But slowly, cracks begin to show. Iivey's career starts taking off. While Theo's professional life takes a steep fall, instead of celebrating each other, the imbalance becomes poison in their relationship. Theo, once a confident and ambitious man, now feels small, overlooked, and bitter. Iivey, on the other hand, starts seeing Theo as resentful and unsupportive. What begins as little arguments grows into full blown battles. The heart of their conflict is their luxurious state of the art house designed by Theo. It isn't just a home. It's a symbol of his pride and creativity. When divorce talk enters the picture, neither of them is ready to give it up. What could have been a painful but straightforward separation instead turns into a vicious war where the house becomes their battleground. At first, their attacks are petty. They play mind games, sabotage each other's routines, and try to make life miserable. But as the story escalates, their fights become violent, destructive, and even lifethreatening. By the time the climax comes around, they've pushed each other past the point of reason. One of the cleverest details throughout the movie is Iivey's raspberry allergy. In the early days of their marriage, Theo and Ivy would handle allergic reactions together. It was almost symbolic of their partnership. But by the end, when Ivy suffers a reaction, Tio withholds the epipen. It's shocking and cruel, but also telling their marriage is at its lowest. and his willingness to watch her suffer shows just how toxic their relationship has become. Eventually, Theo does save her, but the damage to their bond feels irreversible. That moment leads into the most brutal fight of the film. Iivey pulls a gun on Theo and Theo destroys Iivey's prized possession, her beloved Julia Child. This act isn't just about smashing a household item. It's about destroying something she loves dearly. Just as their relationship has been destroyed piece by piece, the house fills with gas from the broken oven, setting the stage for the tragic ending. When Theo locks himself in the bathroom, there's a shift. For the first time in a long time, they stop fighting and actually talk. No games, no screaming, no bitterness, just raw honesty. In that quiet, vulnerable moment, they realize something important. Despite everything, they still love each other. It's bittersweet because it shows that underneath all the anger and resentment, there's still genuine affection. Theo eventually comes out and the two share Lurther, even joking about how close they came to destroying each other completely. But that reunion is cut short in the crulest way possible. The oven they fought over has leaked gas all throughout the house. When Theo lights a fire in an attempt to rekindle romance, the screen goes white. It's heavily implied that they both die in the explosion. Now, some viewers might hope they survived, but the constant camera cuts to the gas filled kitchen make it clear there's no way they made it out alive. The ending is deliberately ambiguous, but all signs point to tragedy. So, how does this compare to the War of the Roses? In the 1989 version, Oliver, Michael Douglas, and Barbara, Kathleen Turner also die, but their ending is far darker and more cynical. They fall from a chandelier, and when Oliver tries to reach out a final gesture, Barbara pushes his hand away. It's a complete rejection of love, even in their last moments. By contrast, the roses gives us something slightly more hopeful. Yes, Theo and Ivy die, but they reconcile first. Their last minutes are not filled with hate, but with laughter, forgiveness, and a rediscovery of their love. It's almost romantic in a very dark and tragic way. Viewers are left thinking that if they had survived, maybe, just maybe, they could have worked things out. The deeper meaning of the film lies in its commentary on relationships. On the surface, it's a comedy about a couple fighting over a house, but underneath, it's about how love can be eroded not by lack of affection, but by lack of communication and support. Theo felt invisible and unappreciated while Ivy felt attacked for chasing success. Neither was fully there for the others struggles. And instead of facing the issues head on, they allowed resentment to build until it consumed them. There are moments earlier in the movie that hint they could have saved themselves. They try therapy. They attempt a romantic trip, but none of it works because they never addressed the root of the problem. They stopped being partners. Instead of listening and understanding, they turned into enemies. This is why the ending, tragic as it is, feels strangely hopeful. In their final moment alive, they drop their defenses and finally see each other clearly. The film suggests that love was always there, just buried under years of bitterness. It's a bittersweet reminder that sometimes relationships end not because the love is gone, but because the people involved forget how to nurture it. So, do Ivy and Theo get divorced? The answer is no. They never finalize the divorce because their story ends much sooner with their deaths. But in a twisted way, they also never fully separate. They die together, reconciled, and in love once again. It's an ending that's dark, funny, heartbreaking, and oddly touching all at the same time. Exactly what you'd expect from a black comedy. For viewers, The Roses leaves a lot to think about. Is love worth fighting for even when it gets ugly? or is the message that unchecked resentment can kill even the strongest relationships. The film doesn't give easy answers, but it does make you reflect on the importance of communication, empathy, and support in any partnership. At the end of the day, The Roses is more than just a comedy about a bad marriage. It's a cautionary tale about what happens when love is left to wither and how even in the darkest moments connection can still shine through even if only briefly and even if tragically.
title: The Roses Ending Explained – Ivy & Theo’s Tragic Fate Revealed

text: Clark Kent / Superman stops the nation of Boravia from invading the neighboring country of Jarhanpur, and warns Boravian president Vasil Ghurkos to leave Jarhanpur alone. In Metropolis, Superman is defeated for the first time by a metahuman called the "Hammer of Boravia", and flees to his Fortress of Solitude in Antarctica with the help of Krypto, a superpowered dog. They are followed by The Engineer, an ally of billionaire Lex Luthor. Superman's robots use concentrated solar radiation to heal him and comfort Superman with a message from his birth parents who sent him to Earth to save him from the destruction of their planet Krypton. The message was damaged during the journey, so only the first half can be played. Superman returns to Metropolis and is again beaten by the Hammer, who is secretly Luthor's metahuman Ultraman. Superman agrees to be interviewed by Lois Lane, his girlfriend and colleague at the Daily Planet, leading to an argument when Lois presses him on the legal and ethical implications of his actions in Boravia. Luthor unleashes a creature on Metropolis as a distraction while he infiltrates the Fortress with Ultraman and the Engineer. They overpower the robots, capture Krypto, and discover the Kryptonian message. The Engineer is able to restore and fix the damaged portion. Superman rescues civilians while fighting the creature with the "Justice Gang", a team composed of heroes Guy Gardner, a member of the Green Lantern Corps, Mister Terrific, and Hawkgirl. Despite Superman's wanting to take the creature alive, Mister Terrific kills it. Luthor broadcasts the Kryptonian message from Superman’s parents, and Superman is shocked to hear the second half, in which his parents urge him to conquer Earth and take many wives to restore the Kryptonian race. Public opinion turns against Superman, especially when he angrily confronts Luthor looking for Krypto, which is recorded and posted online. Lois reassures Superman that she believes he is good, and he confesses his love for her before surrendering himself to the U.S. government in hopes of finding where Krypto is being held. They hand him over to Luthor for detainment and questioning inside an artificial pocket universe where Luthor secretly holds his enemies, including Krypto. Superman is imprisoned with the metahuman Metamorpho. Luthor uses Metamorpho's infant son Joey as leverage to force him to morph one of his hands into Kryptonite, rendering Superman powerless. During questioning, Luthor murders one of Superman's supporters. A horrified Metamorpho agrees to help Superman escape, and they free Joey and Krypto. Lois convinces Mister Terrific to help find Superman and they enter the pocket universe, rescuing the others. Lois takes Superman to recuperate with his adoptive parents, Jonathan and Martha Kent. Jonathan tells the demoralized Superman that his choices and actions determine who he is, not the message from his birth parents. Luthor's girlfriend Eve Teschmacher, who is obsessed with Daily Planet photographer Jimmy Olsen, provides him evidence that Luthor is aiding Boravia in return for half of Jarhanpur's territory. Luthor imprisons her and lures Superman back to Metropolis by opening an unstable portal to the pocket universe, creating a rift in reality which splits the city in half. Superman sends Guy, Hawkgirl, and Metamorpho to stop Boravia from invading Jarhanpur again. Hawkgirl kills Ghurkos and Guy invites Metamorpho to join the Justice Gang. In Metropolis, Superman and Mister Terrific fight the Engineer and Ultraman. After Superman defeats the Engineer, he learns that Ultraman is a clone of himself created by Luthor. text: Hey what's up guys. Today I'll show you a science-fiction dystopian film: "Black Mirror: White Christmas"! Spoiler ahead, watch out and take care! The movie begins where two men are stuck inside a cabin, in the middle of a snowy field during Christmas day. The charismatic man, called "Mr Geek," utters to the other alcoholic man, short-named "Mr Drunk," that it's been five years they are together in the cabin; but Mr Drunk barely speaks to him. He then encourages Mr Drunk to have a conversation with him, since it is Christmas day. To begin the conversation, he says people that end up being stuck in the cabin, must have committed a sinful act. So he asks Mr Drunk about the sinful act Mr Drunk committed outside. But Mr Drunk asks him to share first. He then shares that he ends up being in the cabin, because of an unfortunate event in his work. The scene then flashbacks to the unfortunate event that happened. Apparently, Mr Geek provides live coaching for men to seduce the woman they like. In this case, Mr Geek provides live instruction to the shy man, as he can see and hear everything the shy man perceives, through a device implanted in the shy man. He then instructs the shy man to first fix his appearance; and then he teaches the shy man how to sneak to the company Christmas party, where the shy man can find his favorite woman to date. At the party, the shy man finally finds a brunette attractive, and points it to Mr Geek. He immediately checks the identity of the brunette and the blondie, using their image. After that, he says to the shy man to give his attention to the blondie, and tell her the fake horse story, so the brunette will feel isolated. The shy man proceeds to approach the blondie; and he confidently says to her that he saw a guy with a bow, riding a horse outside. The blondie laughs; and they have a nice conversation. Apparently, Mr Geek's tactic is to deliberately let the brunette feel isolated; so she would naturally talk to the shy man, because Mr Geek believes that humans hate the feeling of being isolated. But the brunette is different; she feels content with being alone; so she leaves the conversation instead. The shy man then leaves the blondie, and heads to the restroom to pee. He tells Mr Geek not to peek at his shy sausage while he pees; but Mr Geek still takes a look. It turns out, there are also other men who are watching the shy man's point of view that night, to witness the events for the sake of entertainment. After that, Mr Geek instructs the shy man to confidently approach the brunette again. This time, the strategy is to make the brunette feel that they are two lonely people against the world. The shy man then soon eventually gains the brunette's trust, as she shares that she used to take pills, since she has a mental illness that makes her hear voices in her head. Shortly after, the brunette leaves for a while, and when she soon comes back, she sees the shy man talking to Mr Geek. The brunette then begins to believe that the shy man has made-up voices inside his mind talking to him. in reality, the voice inside the shy man's head is an actual voice coming from Mr Geek. Thinking that they share the same situation, the brunette feels instantly attracted to the shy man, and invites him to her house. Mr Geek and the watchers feel excited, since they expect that some hormone actions are about to happen between the two. But instead of hormone actions, they witness some gruesome murder action. The brunette poisons the shy man and herself to death, in the act of mercy killing. Apparently, she wants to free herself and the shy man from the voices in their head, thinking that the shy man is also mentally ill in reality like her. After witnessing that, Mr Geek immediately deletes the footage files; so he would not be involved in the shy man's death. However, his wife eventually finds out about his involvement, so she blocks him. In this new world, people on their time have a device implanted inside of them, which alters their perception. So, when his wife blocks him, they both appear censored to each other; they cannot see or hear each other. Back to the present, Mr Geek reveals to Mr Drunk that his wife eventually left him with their daughter; so he came to the cabin to avoid remembering them. To continue the conversation, Mr Geek reveals that the live coaching he provides, is a mere hobby and not his real job. He describes his real job to Mr Drunk, and the scene flashes back to when he is still working in a tech company. Apparently, their company provides a special service to clients, by making special technological assistants for them. The technological assistants are called "cookies", which provide services exactly according to the client's preferences, as cookies are the exact copy of the client's consciousness. The company installs a special bead to the client's head, and lets the bead copy the client's consciousness for days. After that, they extract the bead, which now becomes a cookie, since it now contains the copy of the client's consciousness. Because the cookie thinks like the client, its master, it is confused after the extraction, because it can see and hear everything, but it cannot feel having a body. After that, the company puts the cookie into a device, and installs it to the client's house, where it will be forced to manage the household chores. Mr Geek's job then begins, as he is the one who communicates to the cookie. Mr Geek explains to a cookie that she is only a copy of her master's consciousness; and he begins informing the cookie that her real purpose is to work, so he gives her a virtual body. In response, the cookie refuses to work, so Mr Geek lets her virtually experience six months, without anything to do inside the device. Apparently, Mr Geek can control the time inside the device. six months have already passed-by; but in reality, it is only a few minutes past. What's more, the cookie can experience mental torture, but is programmed not to mentally break down. After that punishment, the cookie begs for Mr Geek to give her work, since she experienced mental torture with nothing to do for six months inside. The cookie then starts managing the master's schedule, and preparing food for the master exactly how the master likes it. As the cookie finally starts working, Mr Geek's job is done. but before leaving, he tells the client about the fake horse story. It seems that Mr Geek's fake horse story is really effective for picking up girls, as the client starts laughing. After that, the scene moves back to the present, where it is noticeable that Mr Drunk is an alcoholic. Mr Drunk empathizes with the cookie's experience as an eternal slave, saying that it is barbaric. So, Mr Geek tells Mr Drunk that he seems to be a good guy because of his empathy. But Mr Drunk denies that he is a good guy, saying he committed horrible acts in the past. So Mr Geek manipulates him into spilling it. The scene then moves back to one Christmas day with Mr Drunk's girlfriend. During that Christmas, they seem to be happy together, before leaving the girlfriend's family house. They then attend a Christmas party together with their colleagues. At the party, the girlfriend seems obviously intimate with her colleague. Mr Drunk soon gets too drunk, and loses his temper, causing a commotion at the party. Later , Mr Drunk and his girlfriend have dinner with their colleagues, who announce they are getting married. Upon knowing this, the girlfriend's mood suddenly changes. After dinner, Mr Drunk notices that his girlfriend is silent. She then explains that she is just tired, so she proceeds to take a rest. While cleaning up their dinner mess, Mr Drunk accidentally finds a pregnancy test, indicating a positive result in the garbage bin. He then gets excited, thinking that they will have a baby. But to his disappointment, his girlfriend declares that she does not want to keep the baby. He keeps insisting on keeping it; but his girlfriend says she has already made up her mind to abort the baby. He then loses his temper, and starts cursing his girlfriend. In response, the girlfriend blocks him; and as a result, they cannot hear each other, and they appear as a silhouette to each other. This makes Mr Drunk angrier. The following day, the girlfriend decides to leave. Mr Drunk chases her, to apologize for his shitty behavior last night; but he is still blocked, so she cannot hear him. After a week, Mr Drunk decides to ask their colleagues where she is, as she still has not come back. But they say she already left, but they do not know her whereabouts. He completely misses his girlfriend; but he cannot even see her photo, as her image is also censored for him. One day, he encounters his girlfriend walking; and based on her silhouette, he figures out that she keeps the baby. So he tries to confront her about it. But she refuses to turn off the block, and shouts for help. A concerned citizen calls the police. As a result, the police legally block him. This means that the police ban him from going near to her. Meanwhile, a GPS will signal the police, if he ever goes near her, and he will instantly get arrested. This time, he does not have an option to communicate with her, but a letter. So, he keeps sending a letter to his girlfriend's house. But Sadly, he never receives a reply from her. Desperate to know about their baby, he decides to watch his girlfriend's family house from afar, hoping he can see a glimpse of their baby. The girlfriend soon arrives with their baby; but to his shock, the baby also appears as a silhouette to him. Apparently, the legal block also applies to the offspring of his girlfriend. However, this does not stop him from coming back to visit the baby from afar. Once a year, every Christmas, he visits his girlfriend's house, just to see the baby grow up. And one time, he leaves a present for the baby; and at that moment, he figures out for the first time that the child is a girl. He then thinks that he has a daughter. One day, he is watching TV, when he sees on the news that his girlfriend died from an accident, making him completely devastated. He can now see the face of his girlfriend on the TV, as the block is gone with her death. This also means that he can now finally see the child's face too. So the next Christmas, he prepares a snow globe present, and visits the child in his girlfriend's family house. To his disappointment, the child looks exactly like their colleague. At that moment, he finally realizes that his girlfriend has had a secret affair with her colleague. Filled with anger and confusion, he comes inside the house to confront the girlfriend's father. The father then reveals that he throws the letter sent by Mr Drunk, before the girlfriend can read it. Upon knowing this, Mr Drunk completely loses his mind, and smashes the father's head with the snow globe, leading to the father's death. After his murderous act, he simply leaves the house; and the police eventually pick him up. The police then inform him that the child ended up freezing to death, when she walked out of the house alone to seek help. Although he is guilty of the crime, he refuses to confess to the police. Back to the present, Mr Drunk realizes that the bird clock in the cabin, looks exactly like the father's bird clock. After Mr Drunk narrates his crime, Mr Geek asks him if he confessed, as Mr Geek puts his snow globe present to the table. Mr Drunk suddenly sees the child's dead body outside the cabin; and he tearfully says that he confesses to the crime. After that, Mr Geek suddenly celebrates, and says that he is coming out. It turns out, the cabin only has a virtual existence; and the Mr Drunk in the virtual cabin, is only a cookie extracted from the real Mr Drunk. Also, Mr Drunk's five years with Mr Geek in the cabin are just virtually produced, so as to manipulate Mr Drunk's cookie into confessing his crime; as a result, they can prove in the real world, that the real Mr Drunk is guilty of that crime. As Mr Geek successfully finishes his tasks, he comes out of the virtual cabin, and is now sent back to reality in the police station during Christmas day. The detective then goes to the real Mr Drunk, to announce that he is already proven guilty. It's then revealed that Mr Geek is also proven guilty for his illegal service, and his failure to report the murder incident. So, Mr Geek made up a deal with the detectives that he would let Mr Drunk confess, in exchange for his own freedom. He then asks the detective if he can go now. In response, the detective lets him go, but with the condition that he is forever blocked by everyone as the red-flagged target. He then walks outside; and to his shock and desperation, he sees that everyone is censored, and he is also censored from everyone. This means that although Mr Geek is set free, he will forever live isolated, as he is forbidden to talk with anyone. His Christmas is completely white, as he sees a sea of people's white silhouette outside! Meanwhile, inside the police station, an officer sets the virtual cabin's time into thousand years per minute. This means that for every minute in reality, Mr Drunk's cookie has to experience a thousand years inside the virtual cabin, while the same Christmas song plays repeatedly. The officer asks the detective if he should turn it off, but the detective says to leave the settings for an entire day, meaning that in the end, Mr Drunk's cookie will spend a gruesome million years inside the cabin, hearing the same Christmas song play over and over again! text: In 1976, an eleven-year-old Gru dreams of becoming a supervillain, assisted by the Minions, whom he has hired to work for him. Gru is ecstatic when he receives an audition invitation from the Vicious 6, a supervillain team now led by Belle Bottom, who hope to find a new member to replace their founder, the supervillain Wild Knuckles, following their betrayal and attempted murder of Knuckles during a heist to steal the Zodiac Stone – a stone connected to the Chinese zodiac. Gru's interview goes poorly but, much to the outrage of the Vicious 6, he steals the stone and escapes with Minions Kevin, Stuart, and Bob, handing it to another Minion, Otto, for safekeeping. At his basement lair, Gru is outraged that Otto has traded the zodiac stone for a pet rock, causing him to fire the Minions before going alone to find it. However, Knuckles kidnaps Gru before taking him to San Francisco and informs the Minions that if they do not give him the stone within 48 hours, Gru will be killed. Failing to locate the stone, Kevin, Stuart and Bob leave for San Francisco to rescue Gru, while Otto leaves in pursuit of a biker whom he realizes has the stone as a necklace. When they reach Knuckles' house, they are chased by his goons until Master Chow, a former Kung Fu teacher who now makes a living at an acupuncture clinic, rescues them by defeating the goons. Chow teaches the Minions Kung Fu after they beg and, ending their training prematurely, go to Knuckles' home to rescue Gru. Meanwhile, Otto catches up to and befriends the biker at Death Valley, who gives the stone back and takes him to San Francisco. Gru begins to bond with Knuckles after the latter's goons quit on him, and later saves him from being eaten by crocodiles in his pool. Teaching Gru how to be a villain, the two rob the Bank of Evil. In the meantime, the Vicious 6, having realized that Knuckles is alive, destroy his house in an attempt to find him. Failing to do so, they head towards Chinatown, with Kevin, Stuart and Bob in pursuit. Returning to his destroyed house, a distraught Knuckles laments his friends' betrayal and decides to give up villainy, sending Gru away. During a Chinese New Year parade in Chinatown, Otto and Gru find each other with the stone but are cornered by the Vicious 6, who in turn are confronted by Anti-Villain League agents. The Vicious 6 then use the stone to turn themselves into large superpowered versions of animals from the Zodiac and prepare to kill Gru by tying him to the hands of a clock tower to rip him apart. Kevin, Stuart, and Bob find Gru, but are turned into a rabbit, a rooster, and a goat. However, Knuckles returns and fights the Vicious 6 with the Minions. Encouraged by Chow's teaching, Kevin, Stuart, and Bob "find their inner beast" and battle the Vicious 6 while Otto saves Gru, but Knuckles gets badly burnt by Belle's dragon flames when trying to take the stone back. After Kevin, Stuart and Bob knock the Vicious 6 out, Gru uses the stone to turn them into rats. Congratulating the three Minions for saving his life, Gru reconciles and rehires the Minions and returns Stuart, Kevin and Bob back to normal. The Vicious 6 are arrested, except Knuckles, who is hospitalized and seemingly succumbs to his injuries, while the stone is confiscated by the Anti-Villain League. At Knuckles' funeral, Gru gives a heartfelt eulogy but is overjoyed when it is revealed Knuckles faked his death. He and Gru later drive off with the Minions. In a mid-credits scene, Gru attempts to hire Dr. Nefario in gratitude for an invention of his that helped him steal the stone. Nefario initially declines but changes his mind after Gru and the Minions beg, giving them a ride on a rocket-powered aircraft.

text: Welcome to Slash Forward. In this episode, we're going to go back and take a look at the pinnacle of zom-coms with the 2004 film Shaun of the Dead. Let's get to it. Can I get any of you [ __ ] a drink? See? He's offering to buy drinks. We learn that Shaun is stuck in a rut, desiring to spend all of his time at the Winchester, his local pub, but Liz is looking for some variety in her life. So, Shaun tries to smooth things over by making a flaccid promise to get reservations to a restaurant the next night, and then he heads home. The next morning, Shaun gets ready for work, and we learn there's a tension at home as well, as his other flatmate Pete has matured into a responsible adult right in front of their eyes, and doesn't appreciate Ed's lack of contribution to the household. They have a quick talk. Ed conveys his understanding by ripping ass, and Shaun heads out. On his way to work, we see some subtle clues of an unfolding drama in the broader world, but stay tunneled in on Shaun's narrow perspective. At work, Shaun is visited by his stepdad Philip, who reminds him of the bi-monthly visit with his mom coming up. He grabs some flowers in preparation and heads home, finding the bus ride somewhat more pestilent than normal. He runs across his ex Yvonne on the way home, and they catch up. When she inquires about Liz, he realizes that in juggling two to three responsibilities that day, he's completely forgotten to get a reservation. He tries, but is unable to secure a table, having missed the last available by a few minutes, which is a real kick in the bollocks. He breaks the sad news to Liz, but has a consolation prize all lined up, a visit to the Winchester, which she rejects outright. He tries to smooth things over, but finds David actively working against him, apparently wanting both Dianne and Liz all to himself, and Liz officially breaks up with him. He goes to the Winchester to drown his sorrows, but the environment is a bit too sad, so they take the party home, where it's crashed by Pete trying to get some sleep and feeling under the weather after being nibbled upon by a pestiferous crackhead on his way home from work. In the light of the hard truths Pete lays on him, Shaun leaves a message for his future self, waking up and finding the determination to improve his life. First stop, nibbles from the sea store. Along the way there are ample indications of drastic environmental changes overnight, but Shaun is too focused on his objective to take notice. He's not home for long before he become distracted by a girl in the garden. She's presumed drunk and mildly Randy. When she comes on too strong, Shaun gives her a firm shove with a butt-clenching oops as the result. Their manslaughter charge is quickly downgraded though when she slowly pulls herself back up. They run inside and find all the emergency numbers engaged and the news informs them the only way to remedy the situation is to remove the head or destroy the brain. Ed gets a bit of the old bloodlust so they go out to test a few small lightweight items. When these obviously fail, Shaun busts into the locked shed for some more serious implements of destruction. And when they put their shoulders into it, they find the skulls have a satisfying way of giving in like a couple of overripe cantaloupe melons. Back inside, Shaun tries to call Liz but accidentally picks up a call from his mom and finds out Philip's been bit. They develop a plan that involves picking up Barbara, killing Philip, getting Liz and holding up at the Winchester. However, things don't go to plan almost immediately when they arrive and find Barbara unwilling to leave and Philip not yet turned. Now forced to bring him along, they run out to find Ed seen to ensuring that they have to take the Jag. And they have to move quickly because some zombies shamble in and one of them peels a little flapjack off Philip's neck. At Liz's, he finds similar difficulty. First forced to climb up the facade finding them equally unwilling to leave and in greater numbers than the plan considered. He eventually convinces them and as they pass through the courtyard, they manage to get their slaughter legs beneath them. They eventually cram into the car and leave. Along the way, Philip has a touching heart-to-heart with Shaun about fatherhood before tagging out. But he's not dead for long forcing them to ditch the car. They slowly walk along the back alleys ignoring the new horrors that now represent daily life. Eventually crossing paths with Yvonne and her band of merry survivalists. Yvonne is surprised by their plan but maintains her British courtesy as they each continue on. They're briefly waylaid when Barbara investigates what she believes to be an old friend's house and Shaun is left mostly on his own to take care of it. They find the coast is far from clear so Diane leads them through some acting warm-ups as they workshop some ideas. They shamble across the expanse, but can't get in. And Shaun finds an inopportune time to gather up the courage to set Ed straight, blowing their cover. So, David breaks the window, and Shaun leads the horde around the back so the others can get in. Upon his return, they begin to realize they can't sit around in the dark with the nibbles and pig snacks forever. When the street lights come on, they recognize their current situation is fuse-related. So, Shaun goes to flip the breakers and discovers that he didn't do as good of a job slipping the horde as he thought. When the lights come back on, so does the jukebox, alerting the zombies outside to their presence. The barkeep also reveals himself, and they pummel him to the beat of a Queen song, giving up a little power in exchange for synchronicity, a risky venture. But, they manage to kill two birds with one stone. Then, they use the power of teamwork to manage their one rifle and 29 shells. After a somewhat successful first round, they fortify their base, as Shaun and the others discover Barbara was bit back in the garden. But, she didn't tell anyone until now because she didn't want to be a bother. David, acting as a proper [ __ ] sheds his pacifism and tries to make a pragmatic decision right in the middle of the emotional climax of their adventure. Dianne, distraught beyond reason, grabs a ham hock and runs out to get her vengeance. text: What's up, everybody? Welcome to FoundFlix. On this ending explain, we're checking out Hard Eyes, where a masked maniac with glowing red eyes returns every Valentine's Day to terrorize unsuspecting couples. Now, horror and romance obviously go together, but it's not as often you see a movie that really tries to go for a traditional romantic comedy plus horror. And well, that's Hard Eyes. It features so many elements plucked directly from romantic comedies, but the problem is it never successfully transcends the cliché. It also doesn't quite balance the romance and horror angles well, with the more romantic elements grinding the story repeatedly to a halt. Now, it's not all bad. Fortunately, the leading couple actually have some chemistry, and there are some quite gruesome and memorable kills. Too bad the killer itself is also pretty bland, with not much to the character at all. The director said that he was inspired by Jason Lives, and I really don't see it. It's just another mass murder with a crossbow, nothing more. I just wish it had overall found a better balance between its various subgenres. But ultimately, that is the typical feeling I have when I watch mainstream horror nowadays. It's just kind of meh. So, let's check out Hard Eyes, breaking down the story, including the killer's identity and motivation, as well as explaining the ending. Love is in the air in our opening, as a couple in a gorgeous vineyard are getting engaged. But things aren't quite so picture-perfect. The girl complains when she nearly chokes on the ring hidden in a piece of fruit. And when the guy takes a knee to go through his proposal, she mouths along with the words as though she already knows it verbatim, which makes things ring a bit false. It feels even more so when they get a ring from a photog posted in the bushes telling them that he missed the shot. So, the couple reenact the proposal to hopefully get it this time. They play act through the proposal, making it faker than ever, and check in once more. We get the photo. Before he can answer, a crossbow bolt pierces right through the shutterfly's eye. The newly minted fiance next feels the killer's wrath via another bolt through the neck. We meet these so-called hard-eyed killer, appropriately with two big heart eyes stitched into a leather mask. That's about it. Oh, and they use a crossbow featuring little hearts on the back. Cute. Killer Cupid style. She hooks it to a wine-making facility and tries to get a security guard's help, but the killer makes quick work of him. Rather than leave, she elects to hide in a giant grape crusher. Heck discovers her inside and makes the best of it by activating the machinery. The walls close in and crushes the woman into a fine paste, even popping out an eyeball. Don't get too excited because there's like three kills in the whole movie. Then, via several news reports, we learn the hard-eyed killer has been behind several killings in previous years in Boston and Philly, and on Valentine's Day, of course. To go even further, they do specifically target couples on the most romantic of days. Although, they know that they will kill anyone in their way. Oh, yeah. Stay home on Valentine's Day. It has caused a kind of panic out in the world when it comes to that day, with couples all worried they could become HEK's latest victim. A pair of detectives, played by Devon Sawa and Jordana Brewster, actually named Hobbs and Shaw, in a strange reference to the Fast and Furious franchise. Sure, why not? They arrive at the scene of the wine crushing and aren't exactly sure that it is the start of another round of murders by the hard-eyed killer. Even though there is a display left out of flowers in a heart shape with the lady's heart right in the middle. Yeah, I'm thinking that's our guy. There's some banter between the detectives regarding dating, and Brewster complains of her prospects on dating apps. There's just no good men out there. text: Steven Solderberg is back with the sexy spy thriller Black Bag. With all the deception, lies, and espionage, we break through all that to let you know exactly what happened. George, played by Michael Fazbender, works for London's National Cyber Security Center with his wife, Catherine, played by Kate Blanchett. A highly dangerous cyber weapon called Severis has been leaked, and George is tasked with finding the person who leaked it. He is given a list of names of those who may have done it. Catherine is at the top of the list. However, the list George has was a wild goose chase because the leak came from Arthur Stiglets, the top of the cyber security center. Arthur Stiglets, played by Pierce Brosman, worked with Colonel James Stokes, played by Raja Jean Paige, to leak this weapon to the Russians. They wanted to do this so the Russians would start a war that they believed would lead to Russia's destruction. George ultimately figures this out with the help of Catherine at the film's climactic ending, which takes place at a dinner party. George invites everyone on the suspect list and after dosing the food with a truth serum narcotic, the chaos begins. This is when George figures out about Stokes and Arthur. We also learn that the three other names on the list, Freddy, Zoe, and Clarissa, were not blameless, as they had unknowingly helped Arthur plant clues to make George believe it was Catherine. This dinner party ends with Stokes attempting to kill George. But when he realizes his gun has blanks in it, Catherine shoots and kills him. Knowing that Freddy, Zoe, and Clarissa were unknowingly used, he lets them live. With Stokes's body disposed of, there is only one loose end left. Catherine returns to work and confronts Arthur, telling him she knows and he needs to go. The film wraps up just as it started with George and Catherine kissing, now knowing how much they mean to each other. While the film's plot centers on espionage, the true story is about George and Catherine's marriage. This film is a test of their love and trust. My devotion to my marriage is my professional weakness. At the start of the film, that trust is felt. You can tell they have an immense amount of trust in each other. Otherwise, the black would never work. When George discovers Catherine may have betrayed that trust, his faith in their relationship is tested. The film's ending proves that their love is stronger than the external forces trying to break them apart. The film asks and answers whether you can genuinely trust someone without knowing every aspect of their lives. Soderberg is saying that true partnership requires individuality. Yes, you should allow yourself to open up, but not if that sacrifices who you are as an individual. When you do that, the love can be unbreakable. text: Did The Woman in the Yard just deliver horror's most unsettling ending, or was it all in Ramona's mind? Here's what we think. The Woman in the Yard is an allegory for grief and guilt. The movie explores this through the eerie presence of the mysterious figure outside Ramona's home. In the final haunting moments, Ramona is forced to confront the Spectre. But does this mean Ramona has finally faced her debilitating grief and overcome it? Or does this new environment indicate that she has allowed it to take her? or is the spectral woman simply just a spooky spectre? This ending is purposefully ambiguous but impactful. Throughout the movie, the lines are deliberately blurred between supernatural horror and psychological breakdown, meticulously building tension, fear, and panic. This brings Ramona's isolation and trauma front and center. The creeping figure in itself is an ominous and unnerving element, but it is more than just a terrifying presence. It symbolizes Ramona's spiraling mental state. The climax complicates the narrative brilliantly when the shrouded woman comes face tof face with Ramona. This is when things get really twisty. The woman sends Ramona's children away before helping guide Ramona to put a gun to her own head. At that point, the spectre is absorbed into Ramona's body. You may think that Ramona has made a tragic choice, but in the final shots, we see her alive and well, running to greet her children. That's not all, though. In a moment reminiscent of the spinning top in Inception, we see that Ramona's painting is mirrored. This links back to the way Ramona sees things in her dream world. This twist leaves audiences split between two compelling theories. Some interpret this scene as Ramona finally breaking free from her griefinduced paralysis, reclaiming control over her life. However, there is a much darker theory which can be backed up by the unsettling inverted shots and distorted reflections that Ramona might have actually taken her life and crossed into the next life. There is one other potential option, however, and this might make you groan. It could be a take on the age-old it was all a dream trope. If Ramona and her husband were in a car accident, could it be that she is in fact experiencing all this in a coma? This would explain why she is completely stuck in the middle of nowhere with no phone, no car, and no real escape. It would also explain Ramona's dreams and visions and why the spectre keeps telling her, "Today's the day." The endings still match with both theories above, but it paints the woman in a very different light. Either she is coming to take Ramona to the next life or coming to wake her. Both would instill fear, either from death or from having to face a real life without her husband. The Woman in the Yard stands out because it refuses to hand viewers one option for a conclusion. The ambiguous ending resonates because audiences can choose to interpret it as psychological or supernatural horror, allowing them to determine Ramona's fate. The same element suggesting recovery and closure can also symbolize her permanent departure from the real world. Thanks for watching Screen Rant.
